title: feat(plugin): Gas Town Bridge Plugin with WASM-Centric Hybrid Architecture
body:
## 🌆 Gas Town Bridge Plugin for Claude Flow V3

### Introduction

[Gas Town](https://github.com/steveyegge/gastown) is Steve Yegge's powerful multi-agent orchestrator that introduces several innovative concepts for durable workflow execution. This plugin bridges Gas Town with Claude Flow V3, enabling interoperability while leveraging WASM for 352x performance improvements on computation-heavy operations.

### Why Gas Town?

Gas Town represents a mature approach to multi-agent orchestration with battle-tested concepts:

| Concept | Description | Claude Flow Benefit |
|---------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Beads** | Git-backed issue tracking with graph semantics | Unified work tracking with AgentDB |
| **Formulas** | TOML-defined workflows (convoy, workflow, expansion, aspect) | Declarative workflow definitions |
| **Convoys** | Work-order tracking for slung work | Progress tracking across agent swarms |
| **GUPP** | Gastown Universal Propulsion Principle | Crash-resilient session persistence |
| **Molecules/Wisps** | Chained work units for durable workflows | Atomic task decomposition |

### Technical Challenge

Gas Town is written in Go (~75k lines) and **cannot compile to WASM** due to syscall dependencies:
- `syscall.Flock` - File locking
- `openInputTTY` - Terminal I/O
- tmux integration

### Solution: WASM-Centric Hybrid Architecture

We use a hybrid approach that maximizes performance:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Claude Flow V3 Plugin Host                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                      │
│  ┌─────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │    CLI Bridge       │    │         WASM Computation Layer       │ │

│  │                     │    │                                      │ │
│  │  • gt commands      │    │  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐  │ │
│  │  • bd commands      │    │  │ gastown-     │ │ ruvector-    │  │ │
│  │  • File read/write  │    │  │ formula-wasm │ │ gnn-wasm     │  │ │
│  │  • SQLite queries   │    │  │              │ │              │  │ │
│  │                     │    │  │ • TOML parse │ │ • DAG ops    │  │ │
│  │  [Node.js FFI]      │    │  │ • Variable   │ │ • Topo sort  │  │ │
│  │                     │    │  │   cooking    │ │ • Cycle      │  │ │
│  └─────────┬───────────┘    │  │ • Molecule   │ │   detection  │  │ │
│            │                │  │   generation │ │ • Critical   │  │ │
│            │                │  └──────────────┘ │   path       │  │ │
│            │                │                   └──────────────┘  │ │
│            │                │                                      │ │
│            │                │  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐  │ │

│            │                │  │ wasm         │ │ learning-wasm│  │ │
│            │                │  │              │ │              │  │ │
│            │                │  │ • Pattern    │ │ • SONA       │  │ │
│            │                │  │   search     │ │   patterns   │  │ │
│            │                │  │ • 150x-12500x│ │ • MoE routing│  │ │

│            │                              │                         │
│            └──────────────┬───────────────┘                         │
│                           │                                         │
│                           ▼                                         │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                     MCP Tool Interface                          ││
│  │                     (15 Tools + 5 WASM)                         ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### WASM Modules

| `gastown-formula-wasm` | TOML parsing, variable cooking, molecule generation | **352x vs JS** |

title: Add async hooks support for non-blocking operations (Claude Code 2.1.0+)
body:
## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive support for asynchronous hooks in Claude Code 2.1.0+, allowing hooks to run in the background without blocking execution. This is particularly useful for logging, notifications, metrics, and other side-effects that shouldn't impact performance.

## Key Changes

- **Documentation**: Added extensive "Async Hooks" section to SKILL.md with:
  - Decision table for when to use async hooks by type
  - Configuration examples for non-blocking logging and daemon startup
  - Benefits and use cases
  - Updated performance tips to reference the new `async: true` option

- **Type Definitions**: Extended `HookDefinition` interface in `src/types.ts` with:
  - `async?: boolean` - Enable asynchronous execution
  - `timeout?: number` - Maximum execution time in milliseconds
  - `once?: boolean` - Execute only once per session (Claude Code 2.1.0+)

- **Configuration**: Updated `HooksConfig` in `src/init/types.ts` with:
  - `enableAsync: boolean` - Master flag for async hook support
  - `postToolUseAsync: boolean` - Default async mode for PostToolUse hooks
  - `notificationAsync: boolean` - Default async mode for Notification hooks

- **Settings Generator**: Modified `src/init/settings-generator.ts` to:
  - Set `async: true` by default for PostToolUse hooks (logging/metrics don't need to block)
  - Set `async: true` by default for Notification hooks (pure side-effects)
  - Keep daemon start async while session-restore runs synchronously (context must load first)
  - Added inline comments explaining async behavior for each hook type

- **Defaults**: Updated both `DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS` and `MINIMAL_INIT_OPTIONS` to enable async hooks by default

## Implementation Details

The async hooks feature follows a sensible default strategy:
- **PostToolUse hooks**: Async by default (run after tool completes, don't need to block)
- **Notification hooks**: Async by default (pure side-effects, shouldn't block)
- **SessionStart hooks**: Mixed approach (daemon start is async, session-restore is sync to ensure context loads)
- **Stop/PreToolUse hooks**: Remain synchronous by default (may need to block for validation/cleanup)

All changes are backward compatible - the `async` property is optional and defaults to `false` for existing hook definitions.

title: fix(statusline): resolve character bleeding in Claude Code status line
body:
## Summary

Fixes character bleeding issue in Claude Code's statusLine where emojis and multi-line output cause terminal cursor positioning problems.

**Problem:**
- Multi-line statusline output confused terminal cursor positioning
- Emojis have inconsistent display widths (1-2 columns) across terminals
- ANSI escape codes contribute to string length but not visual width
- This caused "character bleeding" where text would overlap incorrectly

## Changes

### 1. Display Width Utilities (`statusline/index.ts`)
- `stripAnsi()`: Remove ANSI escape codes from strings
- `getDisplayWidth()`: Calculate visual width accounting for emojis (2 cols) and ANSI codes (0 cols)
- `padToWidth()`: Pad strings to target display width with alignment options
- `truncateToWidth()`: Truncate with proper width calculation

### 2. Improved Single-Line Output
- `generateSingleLine(useColor)`: Uses ASCII-only symbols by default for maximum compatibility
- `generateSingleLineWithEmoji(useColor)`: Optional emoji variant for terminals that handle them well
- `generateSingleLineAscii()`: Pure ASCII, no colors, maximum compatibility

### 3. New CLI Flags (`hooks statusline`)
- `--single-line`: ASCII-safe single-line output (recommended for Claude Code)
- `--safe`: Multi-line output with collision zone avoidance
- `--emoji`: Include emojis in single-line output (may cause display issues)

### 4. Comprehensive Tests
- Tests for display width calculation with ASCII, ANSI codes, and emojis
- Tests for single-line output format
- Tests for no-color mode

## Recommended Usage

For Claude Code's `statusLine` config in `.claude/settings.json`:


title: feat: Implement Live Operations Dashboard for Claude Flow V3
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the **Live Operations Dashboard** for Claude Flow V3, providing real-time visibility into agent activities, task progress, and system metrics.

### Features Implemented

#### 1. Dashboard Frontend (`@claude-flow/dashboard`)
- **Agent Grid** - Visual display of all agents with status indicators
- **Task Timeline/Kanban** - Track task progress with multiple view modes
- **Message Stream** - Real-time inter-agent communication log
- **Memory Log** - Track memory operations (store, retrieve, search)
- **Live Topology** - D3-powered visualization of swarm topology
- **Connection Status** - WebSocket connection indicator with auto-reconnect

#### 2. WebSocket Event Server (`@claude-flow/cli`)
- **WebSocket Server** (port 3001) - Real-time event streaming to dashboard
- **HTTP Endpoint** (port 3002) - Synchronous event posting from CLI commands
- **Channel Subscriptions** - agents, tasks, messages, memory, topology, metrics
- **Event Replay Buffer** - Last 1000 events for reconnecting clients
- **Heartbeat Mechanism** - 30-second ping/pong with dead client cleanup

#### 3. Event Emitter Bridge
- **Singleton Pattern** - Shared across CLI commands
- **Auto-connect** - Connects to HTTP endpoint automatically
- **Typed Methods** - `emitAgentStatus()`, `emitTaskUpdate()`, `emitSwarm()`, etc.
- **Event Buffering** - Queues events when server unavailable

#### 4. CLI Integration
- `event-server start/stop/status` - Manage the event server
- Agent spawn emits `agent:status` events
- Swarm init emits `swarm` and `topology:change` events

### Event Flow Architecture

```
CLI Command → HTTP POST (port 3002) → Event Server → WebSocket (port 3001) → Dashboard
```

### Event Format (WSEvent Interface)

The dashboard expects events in this format:
```typescript
interface WSEvent {
  channel: string;  // 'agents' | 'tasks' | 'messages' | 'memory'
  event: string;    // 'agent:spawned' | 'task:created' | etc.
  data: unknown;    // Event payload
}
```

### New Files
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/event-server.ts` - WebSocket + HTTP server
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/event-emitter.ts` - Event bridge singleton
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/event-server.ts` - CLI command
- `v3/@claude-flow/dashboard/` - Complete React dashboard with Tailwind CSS

### Usage

```bash
# Start the event server
npx @claude-flow/cli event-server start --port 3001

# Start the dashboard
cd v3/@claude-flow/dashboard && npm run dev

# Open http://localhost:5173

# Events will appear when you:
npx @claude-flow/cli agent spawn --type coder --name MyCoder
npx @claude-flow/cli swarm init --topology hierarchical
```

### Sending Events via HTTP

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3002/event \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "channel": "agents",
    "type": "agent:spawned",
```

title: Security: SQL injection vulnerabilities in memory-initializer.ts
body:
## Security Audit Finding

During the memory system review, 4 SQL injection vulnerabilities were identified in `memory-initializer.ts`.

### Affected File
`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/memory-initializer.ts`

### Vulnerabilities

#### 1. `listEntries()` - Lines 2132-2146
```typescript
// Vulnerable - uses string interpolation
AND namespace = '${namespace.replace(/'/g, "''")}'
LIMIT ${limit} OFFSET ${offset}
```

#### 2. `searchEntries()` - Lines 1993-1998
```typescript
// Vulnerable - same pattern
AND namespace = '${namespace.replace(/'/g, "''")}'
```

#### 3. `getEntry()` - Lines 2239-2262
```typescript
// Vulnerable in both SELECT and UPDATE
AND key = '${key.replace(/'/g, "''")}'
AND namespace = '${namespace.replace(/'/g, "''")}'
```

#### 4. `deleteEntry()` - Lines 2350-2379
```typescript
// Vulnerable - same pattern
WHERE key = '${key.replace(/'/g, "''")}'
```

### Risk Assessment

| Factor | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Attack Vector | Local (MCP/CLI input) |
| Exploitability | Low - requires specific input crafting |
| Impact | Data integrity, potential data exfiltration |
| Current Mitigation | Manual single-quote escaping |

### Recommended Fix

Use sql.js parameterized queries:

```typescript
// BEFORE (vulnerable)
db.exec(\`SELECT * FROM memory_entries WHERE namespace = '\${namespace.replace(/'/g, "''")}'\`);

// AFTER (secure)
const stmt = db.prepare('SELECT * FROM memory_entries WHERE namespace = ?');
stmt.bind([namespace]);
const result = [];
while (stmt.step()) {
  result.push(stmt.getAsObject());
}
stmt.free();
```

### Additional Recommendations

1. Add input validation using Zod schemas
2. Add path traversal protection for \`dbPath\` parameter
3. Sanitize error messages before returning to callers

### Priority

**HIGH** - Should be addressed before production use.

title: Bug: Swarm state not persisted between MCP calls
body:
# Bug: Swarm state not persisted between MCP calls

## Description

The `swarm_init` function returns success but the swarm state does not persist for subsequent MCP API calls. This causes all swarm-dependent functions (`swarm_status`, `agent_spawn`, `task_orchestrate`) to fail with "No active swarm found" errors.

## Version

- claude-flow: v3.0.0-alpha.185
- ruv-swarm MCP server

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `swarm_init` with valid parameters:
```json
{
  "topology": "mesh",
  "maxAgents": 6,
  "strategy": "specialized"
}
```

2. Receive successful response with swarm ID

3. Immediately call `swarm_status`:
```json
{"verbose": true}
```

4. **Error occurs**:
```
MCP error -32603: MCP tool error: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getGlobalMetrics')
```

5. Call `agent_spawn`:
```json
{
  "type": "coder",
  "name": "test-agent",
  "capabilities": ["typescript"]
}
```

6. **Error occurs**:
```
MCP error -32603: MCP tool error: No active swarm found. Please initialize a swarm first using swarm_init.
```

## Expected Behavior

After `swarm_init` returns success, subsequent calls to `swarm_status`, `agent_spawn`, and `task_orchestrate` should recognize the active swarm and operate normally.

## Actual Behavior

The swarm state is not persisted between MCP calls. Each call appears to be stateless, losing the swarm context.

## Root Cause Analysis

The swarm WASM module (`size: 786432 bytes`) is never actually loaded. Operations use a JavaScript fallback that doesn't maintain state between MCP calls.

**WASM Module Status**:
```json
{
  "swarm": {
    "loaded": false,
    "loading": false,
    "placeholder": false,
    "size": 786432,
    "priority": "high",
    "deps": ["core"]
  }
}
```

## Affected Functions

- `swarm_status` - Returns null pointer error
- `agent_spawn` - Returns "No active swarm found"
- `agent_list` - Likely affected
- `agent_metrics` - Likely affected
- `task_orchestrate` - Returns "No active swarm found"

## Workaround

Use the DAA (Decentralized Autonomous Agents) service instead:
```javascript
daa_init({ enableLearning: true, enableCoordination: true, persistenceMode: "memory" })
daa_agent_create({ id: "agent-name", capabilities: ["..."], cognitivePattern: "convergent" })
```

## Suggested Fix

The swarm state needs to be persisted either:
1. In memory with proper singleton pattern
2. In a file/database for cross-call persistence
3. Via proper WASM module loading

## Environment

- Platform: Windows 11
- Date: January 26-27, 2026

title: Bug: memory store/search broken — integer ID mismatch, missing value column, vector dimension hardcoded to 1536
body:
## Summary

Three bugs in `memory-initializer.js` prevent `memory store` and `memory search` from working. Embeddings are never stored or queried.

## Bug 1: `storeEntry()` — datatype mismatch on insert

The `memory_entries` table uses `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, but `storeEntry()` generates a text ID and tries to insert it:

```js
// Line ~1528
const id = `entry_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).substring(7)}`;
```

This causes: `[ERROR] datatype mismatch`

The INSERT also omits the `value` column which has a `NOT NULL` constraint, causing a secondary failure.

**Fix:** Remove `id` from the INSERT (let autoincrement handle it), add `value` to the column list, and retrieve the actual row ID after insert:

```js
db.run(`
  INSERT INTO memory_entries (
    key, value, namespace, content, type,
    embedding, embedding_dimensions, embedding_model,
    tags, metadata, created_at, updated_at, expires_at, status
  ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'semantic', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'active')
  ON CONFLICT(key, namespace) DO UPDATE SET
    value = excluded.value, content = excluded.content,
    embedding = excluded.embedding, ...
`, [key, value, namespace, value, ...]);

const idResult = db.exec(`SELECT id FROM memory_entries WHERE key = ? AND namespace = ?`, [key, namespace]);
const id = idResult[0]?.values[0]?.[0] ?? `entry_${now}`;
```

## Bug 2: `searchEntries()` — `id.substring is not a function`

Since IDs are integers from SQLite, calling `.substring()` on them crashes:

```js
// Line ~1667
id: id.substring(0, 12),        // TypeError: id.substring is not a function
key: key || id.substring(0, 15), // same
```

Same issue at line ~499 in the HNSW search path:
```js
id: entry.id.substring(0, 12),
key: entry.key || entry.id.substring(0, 15),
```

**Fix:** Wrap with `String()`:
```js
const idStr = String(id);
id: idStr.substring(0, 12),
key: key || idStr.substring(0, 15),
```

## Bug 3: RuVector PostgreSQL schema hardcodes `vector(1536)`

The `ruvector init` migration SQL creates all vector columns as `vector(1536)` (OpenAI dimensions). When using local ONNX models like `all-mpnet-base-v2` (768-dim) or `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim), inserts fail:

```
ERROR: expected 1536 dimensions, not 768
```

Affected tables and columns:
- `embeddings.embedding`
- `attention_patterns.query_embedding`, `key_embedding`, `value_embedding`
- `hyperbolic_embeddings.embedding`
- `neural_patterns.input_embedding`, `output_embedding`
- `query_cache.query_embedding`

Plus 4 HNSW indexes built on these columns.

**Fix:** The dimension should be read from `.claude-flow/embeddings.json` (or a CLI flag) during `ruvector init` / `ruvector migrate` rather than hardcoded. A manual workaround:

```sql
-- Drop HNSW indexes, alter columns, recreate indexes
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS claude_flow.idx_embeddings_vector_hnsw;
-- ... (4 indexes total)
ALTER TABLE claude_flow.embeddings ALTER COLUMN embedding TYPE vector(768);
-- ... (8 columns total across 5 tables)
CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_vector_hnsw ON claude_flow.embeddings
  USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);
-- ... (4 indexes total)
```

## Bug 4: `loadEmbeddingModel()` hardcodes `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`

The function ignores `.claude-flow/embeddings.json` and always loads `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` with 384 dimensions, regardless of what model is configured:

```js
// Line ~1166
const embedder = await pipeline('feature-extraction', 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2');
```

**Fix:** Read the model name from config:
```js
let configModel = 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2';
let configDimension = 384;
try {
    const configPath = path.join(process.cwd(), '.claude-flow', 'embeddings.json');
    if (fs.existsSync(configPath)) {
        const embConfig = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(configPath, 'utf-8'));
        if (embConfig.model) {
            configModel = embConfig.model;
            configDimension = embConfig.dimension || (configModel.includes('mpnet') ? 768 : 384);
        }
    }
} catch { /* use defaults */ }
const embedder = await pipeline('feature-extraction', `Xenova/${configModel}`);
```

## Impact

- `claude-flow memory store` silently fails on every call — no embeddings are ever persisted
- `claude-flow memory search` crashes before returning results
- `claude-flow ruvector init` creates incompatible schemas for non-OpenAI embedding models
- The embedding model config file (`.claude-flow/embeddings.json`) is decorative — never read

## Environment

- `@claude-flow/cli` version: `3.0.0-alpha.185`
- Node.js: v22
- Platform: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Embedding model: `all-mpnet-base-v2` via `@xenova/transformers`
- PostgreSQL: pgvector 0.8.1 via `ruvnet/ruvector-postgres` Docker image

title: init generates agent .md files with corrupted/unparseable frontmatter
body:
## Bug Report: Agent Parse Errors - Missing required "description" field in frontmatter

### Description

Running `claude-flow init` generates agent `.md` files that Claude Code's agent parser cannot parse, resulting in 7+ agent parse errors:

```
Agent Parse Errors
 └ Failed to parse 7 agent file(s):
   └ C:\Users\ruv\.claude\agents\specialized\mobile\spec-mobile-react-native.md: Missing required "description" field in frontmatter
   └ C:\Users\ruv\.claude\agents\architecture\system-design\arch-system-design.md: Missing required "description" field in frontmatter
   └ C:\Users\ruv\.claude\agents\development\backend\dev-backend-api.md: Missing required "description" field in frontmatter
   └ C:\Users\ruv\.claude\agents\analysis\code-review\analyze-code-quality.md: Missing required "description" field in frontmatter
   └ C:\Users\ruv\.claude\agents\documentation\api-docs\docs-api-openapi.md: Missing required "description" field in frontmatter
   └ C:\Users\ruv\.claude\agents\data\ml\data-ml-model.md: Missing required "description" field in frontmatter
   └ C:\Users\ruv\.claude\agents\devops\ci-cd\ops-cicd-github.md: Missing required "description" field in frontmatter
```

The `description` field **is present** in each file, but the YAML frontmatter is malformed in ways that cause parsers to fail silently.

### Root Cause Analysis

**All 7 failing files are in nested subdirectories** (e.g., `specialized/mobile/`, `architecture/system-design/`). These files use a complex "v1.0.0" frontmatter format that differs from the working agents.

**Working format** (e.g., `.claude/agents/core/coder.md` — ~25 lines of frontmatter):

```yaml
---
name: coder
type: developer
color: "#FF6B35"
description: Implementation specialist for writing clean, efficient code
capabilities:
  - code_generation
  - refactoring
priority: high
hooks:
  pre: |
    echo "Coder agent starting"
  post: |
    echo "Implementation complete"
---
```

**Broken format** (e.g., `specialized/mobile/spec-mobile-react-native.md` — **141 lines** of frontmatter):

```yaml
---
name: "mobile-dev"
description: "Expert agent for React Native..."
color: "teal"
type: "specialized"
version: "1.0.0"
created: "2025-07-25"
author: "Claude Code"
metadata:
  specialization: "React Native, mobile UI/UX..."
  complexity: "complex"
  autonomous: true
  ← blank line with trailing whitespace (2 spaces)
triggers:
  keywords:
    - "react native"
    ...
capabilities:
  allowed_tools:
    - Read
    - Write
    ...
constraints:
  allowed_paths:
    ...
behavior:
  error_handling: "adaptive"
  ...
hooks:
  pre_execution: |
    echo "📱 React Native Developer initializing..."
    ...multiline bash script...
  on_error: |
    echo "❌ Error: {{error_message}}"
    ...
examples:
  - trigger: "create a login screen for React Native app"
    response: "I'll create a complete login screen..."
---
```

**Identified parsing issues:**

1. **Blank lines with trailing whitespace** inside the YAML block (e.g., `  \n` at metadata boundary) — some YAML parsers interpret this incorrectly, truncating or corrupting the parsed output
2. **Extremely long frontmatter** (100-141 lines vs ~25 lines for working agents) with deeply nested structures
3. **Complex multi-line strings** in `hooks.pre_execution`, `hooks.on_error` containing bash scripts with special characters
4. **`examples` section** with nested trigger/response pairs containing embedded quotes
5. **Different key structure**: `capabilities.allowed_tools` (object) vs `capabilities: [list]` (simple array), `hooks.pre_execution` vs `hooks.pre`

### Affected Files

All in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/agents/` — these are the source templates copied by `init`:

| Nested (Broken) | Flat (Also Exists) |
|---|---|
| `specialized/mobile/spec-mobile-react-native.md` | `specialized/spec-mobile-react-native.md` |
| `architecture/system-design/arch-system-design.md` | `architecture/arch-system-design.md` |
| `development/backend/dev-backend-api.md` | `development/dev-backend-api.md` |
| `analysis/code-review/analyze-code-quality.md` | `analysis/analyze-code-quality.md` |
| `documentation/api-docs/docs-api-openapi.md` | `documentation/docs-api-openapi.md` |
| `data/ml/data-ml-model.md` | `data/data-ml-model.md` |
| `devops/ci-cd/ops-cicd-github.md` | `devops/ops-cicd-github.md` |

Note: The flat versions (also copied by init) may or may not parse correctly — they use the same complex format but with a blank line separating `author:` from `metadata:`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `npx claude-flow@v3alpha init` (or `init --all`)
2. Open Claude Code in the initialized project
3. Observe the "Agent Parse Errors" warning listing 7 files

### Expected Behavior

All agent `.md` files should be parseable by Claude Code's agent file parser without errors.

### Proposed Fix

1. **Normalize frontmatter format** in all agent template files to match the working format:
   - Use the simple `capabilities: [list]` format instead of `capabilities.allowed_tools`
   - Use `hooks.pre` / `hooks.post` instead of `hooks.pre_execution` / `hooks.post_execution`
   - Remove blank lines with trailing whitespace inside YAML frontmatter
   - Keep frontmatter under ~30 lines; move extended metadata to the markdown body
   - Remove `constraints`, `behavior`, `communication`, `integration`, `optimization`, `examples` from frontmatter (put in body if needed)

2. **Remove duplicate nested subdirectory files** — the init copies both `specialized/spec-mobile-react-native.md` and `specialized/mobile/spec-mobile-react-native.md`, which is redundant

3. **Add frontmatter validation** to the `init` command (or `doctor`) that checks all agent files parse correctly before reporting success

### Environment

- Platform: Windows (reported), also reproducible on Linux
- Claude Flow version: v3alpha
- Source: `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/agents/`
- Copy function: `copyAgents()` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/executor.ts:656-709`

### Labels

`bug`, `init`, `agents`, `v3`

title: Fix daemon busy-wait loop causing 100% CPU usage
body:
## Summary

- `processPendingWorkers()` in `worker-daemon.ts` busy-waits when a worker is deferred by `canRunWorker()` (e.g. CPU load above threshold). The deferred worker gets pushed back onto the queue and the `while` loop immediately retries, creating a tight loop that reads `/proc/loadavg` and `/proc/meminfo` millions of times per second, driving CPU to 100% and making the load condition self-sustaining.
- Added `break` when `executeWorkerWithConcurrencyControl()` returns `null` (worker deferred). The worker is already back in the queue and will be retried when the next scheduled worker completes via its `finally` block.

## Test plan

- [x] Ran `claude-flow daemon start` and confirmed CPU stays low
- [x] Triggered worker tasks and verified they still execute correctly

title: feat(memory): Use stored embeddings for semantic search in CLI
body:
## Summary

The CLI `memory search` command currently uses simple SQL `LIKE '%query%'` text matching, ignoring the `embedding` column that already exists in the database schema. This means users who generate embeddings for their memory entries get no benefit from semantic search when using the CLI.

## Current Behavior

In `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.ts`, the search handler uses text matching:

```typescript
// Simple text search (LIKE matching)
let sql = `
    SELECT key, namespace, content, created_at, access_count
    FROM memory_entries
    WHERE status = 'active' AND (
        key LIKE ? OR content LIKE ?
    )
`;
```

## Expected Behavior

When entries have stored embeddings, the search should:
1. Generate an embedding for the query
2. Compute cosine similarity against stored embeddings
3. Return results ranked by similarity score

## Proposed Solution

Check if entries have embeddings, and if so, use vector similarity search:

```typescript
// If entries have embeddings, use semantic search
const queryEmbedding = generateEmbedding(input.query);

const entries = db.query(`
    SELECT id, key, namespace, content, embedding, metadata
    FROM memory_entries
    WHERE status = 'active' AND embedding IS NOT NULL
`).all();

const results = entries
    .map(entry => ({
        ...entry,
        score: cosineSimilarity(queryEmbedding, JSON.parse(entry.embedding))
    }))
    .filter(r => r.score >= threshold)
    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
    .slice(0, limit);
```

## Benefits

- Leverages existing `embedding` column in schema
- Works with any embedding model (hash-based, neural, etc.)
- Backward compatible (falls back to text search if no embeddings)
- Significant improvement in search relevance

## Additional Context

The database schema already supports embeddings:
```sql
embedding TEXT,
embedding_model TEXT DEFAULT 'local',
embedding_dimensions INTEGER,
```

Tools like `build-embeddings` populate these columns, but the CLI search ignores them.

## Environment

- Package: @claude-flow/cli
- Version: 3.0.2
- Platform: Windows/Linux/macOS

title: Fix: Hook commands fail - stdin JSON not parsed
body:
## Summary

All Claude Code hooks generated by `claude-flow init` fail silently because they reference shell environment variables (`$TOOL_INPUT_file_path`, `$PROMPT`, `$TOOL_SUCCESS`, etc.) that Claude Code never sets. Claude Code passes hook context as **JSON via stdin**, not as environment variables.

This causes errors like:
- `UserPromptSubmit hook error`
- `PostToolUse:Bash hook error`
- `PreToolUse:Edit hook error`

Every hook that needs tool input data is affected.

## Root Cause

The `settings-generator.ts` and static `.claude/settings.json` template generate hook commands like:

```
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest hooks pre-edit --file "$TOOL_INPUT_file_path"
```

But `$TOOL_INPUT_file_path` is never set. Claude Code actually pipes JSON to stdin:

```json
{
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Edit",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.ts" }
}
```

## Fix

Introduces `.claude/hooks/hook-bridge.sh`, a bridge script that:
1. Reads the stdin JSON from Claude Code
2. Extracts relevant fields using `jq`
3. Forwards them as proper CLI arguments

All hook commands now route through the bridge:
```
.claude/hooks/hook-bridge.sh pre-edit
```

### Files changed
- **New**: `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/hooks/hook-bridge.sh` - Bridge script
- **Modified**: `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/settings-generator.ts` - Generator uses bridge
- **Modified**: `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/executor.ts` - Init copies bridge script
- **Modified**: `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/settings.json` - Static template uses bridge

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `echo '{"prompt":"test"}' | .claude/hooks/hook-bridge.sh route` works
- [ ] Verify `echo '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"/tmp/test.ts"}}' | .claude/hooks/hook-bridge.sh pre-edit` works
- [ ] Verify `echo '{}' | .claude/hooks/hook-bridge.sh pre-edit` exits cleanly (no error)
- [ ] Verify `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init --force` creates `.claude/hooks/hook-bridge.sh`
- [ ] Verify no more `UserPromptSubmit hook error` or `PostToolUse:Bash hook error` in Claude Code

## Note

Requires `jq` to be installed. This is standard on macOS (via Xcode CLI tools) and most Linux distributions. Windows users need WSL or Git Bash (which was already effectively required by the existing bash-syntax hooks).

## Summary

- Fixes bug where subcommand `--format` option was being validated against global option choices
- Example: `claude-flow process monitor` failed with "Invalid value for --format: text. Must be one of: dashboard, compact, json"

The parser applied global option defaults (`--format` defaulting to `'text'`) before command resolution. When validating, the subcommand's `--format` choices (`['dashboard', 'compact', 'json']`) were checked against the global default value (`'text'`), causing validation to fail.

title: npx @claude-flow/cli@latest fails: ETARGET on @claude-flow/memory, missing semver dependency
body:
## Summary

`npx @claude-flow/cli@latest` and `npx claude-flow@latest` both fail to execute any command. Two independent issues combine to make the CLI unusable when installed fresh via npx.

**Priority: Critical** — all fresh installations are broken.

## Issue 1: ETARGET — `@claude-flow/memory@>=3.0.0` not found

**Affects:** `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest`

### Reproduction

```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest swarm init --topology hierarchical --max-agents 6 --strategy specialized
```

### Error

```
npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
npm warn While resolving: @claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge@0.1.1
npm warn Found: peerOptional @claude-flow/memory@">=3.0.0" from the root project
npm error code ETARGET
npm error notarget No matching version found for @claude-flow/memory@>=3.0.0.
```

### Root Cause

1. `@claude-flow/cli@3.1.0-alpha.1` declares `@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge@^0.1.0` as an **optionalDependency**
2. `@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge@0.1.1` declares `@claude-flow/memory@>=3.0.0` as a **peerDependency** (marked optional)
3. `@claude-flow/memory` only has prerelease versions on npm: `3.0.0-alpha.1`, `3.0.0-alpha.2`
4. Per npm semver, `>=3.0.0` does **NOT** match `3.0.0-alpha.x` — prerelease versions require the range to include a prerelease tag (e.g., `>=3.0.0-alpha.1`)
5. npm fails with ETARGET because zero versions satisfy the constraint

Even though the peer dep is marked `optional`, npm's ETARGET error is fatal during resolution.

### Fix Options

- **Option A (recommended):** Update `@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge` peer dep to `>=3.0.0-alpha.1 || >=3.0.0`
- **Option B:** Publish `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0` (stable release)
- **Option C:** Remove `@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge` from CLI optionalDependencies until memory reaches stable

---

## Issue 2: Missing `semver` dependency — CLI crashes on startup

**Affects:** `npx claude-flow@latest` (umbrella package, which gets past ETARGET but hits this)

### Reproduction

```bash
npx claude-flow@latest swarm init --topology hierarchical --max-agents 6 --strategy specialized
```

### Error

```
Error: Cannot find package 'semver' imported from checker.js
    at legacyMainResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:204:26)
```

### Root Cause

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/update/checker.ts` has `import * as semver from 'semver'` (line 6)
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/update/validator.ts` also imports `semver` (line 6)
- `semver` is **not declared** in `@claude-flow/cli/package.json` dependencies
- It works in development (transitive dep of npm/other tools) but fails in fresh npx install

### Fix

Add `semver` to `@claude-flow/cli` dependencies:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "semver": "^7.6.0"
  }
}
```

---

## Additional Finding: `@ruvector/router` not declared

`@ruvector/router` is imported in `src/mcp-tools/hooks-tools.ts:230` but not declared in package.json. This is in a try/catch block so it doesn't crash, but should be added to `optionalDependencies` for correctness.

## Impact

**Both** `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest` and `npx claude-flow@latest` are broken for fresh installations. Users cannot run any CLI commands.

## Environment

- Node.js: v22.x
- npm: v10.x
- Package version: 3.1.0-alpha.1
- All dist-tags (latest, alpha, v3alpha) point to 3.1.0-alpha.1

## Checklist

- [ ] Fix gastown-bridge peer dep range (`>=3.0.0` → `>=3.0.0-alpha.1`)
- [ ] Add `semver` to CLI dependencies
- [ ] Add `@ruvector/router` to CLI optionalDependencies
- [ ] Publish fix: `@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge@0.1.2`
- [ ] Publish fix: `@claude-flow/cli@3.1.0-alpha.2`
- [ ] Publish fix: `claude-flow@3.1.0-alpha.2`
- [ ] Verify `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest` works
- [ ] Verify `npx claude-flow@latest` works

title: Fix statusline to show actual current model instead of hardcoded Opus 4.5
body:
## Problem

The `claude-flow hooks statusline` command was showing a hardcoded "Opus 4.5" model name regardless of which model the user was actually using in Claude Code. This caused confusion when users switched models (e.g., to Sonnet or Haiku) but the statusline continued to display "Opus 4.5".

## Root Cause

In `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hooks.ts`, the `getUserInfo()` function had:
```typescript
const modelName = 'Opus 4.5';
```

There was no detection of the actual model from Claude Code's session state.

## Solution

Updated the `getUserInfo()` function to:

1. **Read `~/.claude.json`** to find the current project's `lastModelUsage`
2. **Prefer the most specific path**: When multiple project paths match, choose the longest (most specific) one
3. **Calculate total token usage**: Include cache tokens (`cacheReadInputTokens` + `cacheCreationInputTokens`) to accurately determine the most-used model
4. **Parse model ID**: Convert model IDs like `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` to human-readable names like "Sonnet 4.5"
5. **Fallback gracefully**: Show "Unknown" if detection fails

## Changes

- Added `os` import for accessing home directory
- Replaced hardcoded `const modelName = 'Opus 4.5'` with `let modelName = 'Unknown'`
- Added model detection logic that:
  - Finds the most specific matching project path
  - Calculates total token usage including cache tokens
  - Maps model IDs to display names (Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 4, Haiku 4.5)

## Testing

Tested with:
- User switching from Opus to Sonnet → statusline correctly shows "Sonnet 4.5"
- Nested project directories → correctly prefers specific project path over parent
- Multiple models used in session → shows the most-used model by token count

## Impact

- Users will now see their actual current model in the statusline
- Works correctly across all Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku)
- Handles edge cases like nested project directories

## Screenshot

Before:
```
▊ Claude Flow V3 ● user  │  ⎇ main  │  Opus 4.5
```

After (when using Sonnet):
```
▊ Claude Flow V3 ● user  │  ⎇ main  │  Sonnet 4.5
```

title: hooks intelligence --status: TypeError on SONA display when no training data exists
body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

`claude-flow hooks intelligence --status` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')` when displaying SONA component metrics on a fresh install where no training has occurred.

### Version & Environment

- **claude-flow**: v3.1.0-alpha.3
- **Node.js**: v24.13.0
- **OS**: macOS Darwin 25.2.0 arm64
- **Install method**: `npm install -g claude-flow@alpha` (via mise)
- **Install path**: `/Users/makallen/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.0/bin/claude-flow`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh install of claude-flow v3.1.0-alpha.3
2. Initialize memory: `claude-flow memory init`
3. Run: `claude-flow hooks intelligence --status`

### Expected Behavior

Should display SONA component status with default/zero values (e.g., `0.000ms`, `0.0%`) when no training has occurred.

### Actual Behavior

```
RuVector Intelligence System

... Initializing intelligence system...
Intelligence system active

+ Intelligence Status -+
| Mode: balanced       |
| Status: active       |
| Last Training: Never |
+----------------------+

🧠 SONA (Sub-0.05ms Learning)
                                             Intelligence system error
[ERROR] Unexpected error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')
```

The command exits with code 1. Intelligence status box renders correctly, but crashes when rendering the SONA table.

### Root Cause Analysis

The crash occurs in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/hooks.js` around lines 1652-1664.

The code at line 1652 checks `result.components.sona.enabled` — this is truthy (SONA is enabled by default). It then attempts to render a table with:

```javascript
// Line 1660
{ metric: 'Learning Time', value: `${result.components.sona.learningTimeMs.toFixed(3)}ms` },
// Line 1661
{ metric: 'Adaptation Time', value: `${result.components.sona.adaptationTimeMs.toFixed(3)}ms` },
// Line 1664
{ metric: 'Avg Quality', value: `${(result.components.sona.avgQuality * 100).toFixed(1)}%` }
```

When no training has occurred, `learningTimeMs`, `adaptationTimeMs`, and/or `avgQuality` are `undefined`, causing the `.toFixed()` call to throw.

### Suggested Fix

Add null-safe defaults before calling `.toFixed()`:

```javascript
// Option A: Default to 0
{ metric: 'Learning Time', value: `${(result.components.sona.learningTimeMs ?? 0).toFixed(3)}ms` },
{ metric: 'Adaptation Time', value: `${(result.components.sona.adaptationTimeMs ?? 0).toFixed(3)}ms` },
{ metric: 'Avg Quality', value: `${((result.components.sona.avgQuality ?? 0) * 100).toFixed(1)}%` }
```

The same pattern should likely be applied to the MoE and HNSW component sections (lines 1683-1684, 1700+) as a preventive measure, since they have the same `.toFixed()` calls on properties that may be undefined when those subsystems haven't been exercised.

### Context

- All other `hooks intelligence` features work correctly (routing, explain, model-route, metrics dashboard)
- `hooks intelligence --status` is the only affected subcommand
- The issue is purely in the display formatter — the intelligence engine itself initializes fine

### Other Commands Verified Working

| Command | Status |
|---------|--------|
| `hooks route --task "..."` | ✅ Pass |
| `hooks model-route --task "..."` | ✅ Pass |
| `hooks explain --task "..."` | ✅ Pass |
| `hooks metrics --v3-dashboard` | ✅ Pass |
| `hooks model-stats` | ✅ Pass |
| `neural status` | ✅ Pass |
| `memory init / store / search` | ✅ Pass |
| `mcp status / tools / health` | ✅ Pass (200 tools) |

title: fix: daemon resource thresholds incompatible with macOS
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1077 — Daemon workers never execute on macOS due to unrealistic resource thresholds in `canRunWorker()`.

**Three issues fixed:**

1. **`maxCpuLoad: 2.0` too low for multi-core systems** — `os.loadavg()` returns system-wide load (not per-core). An 8-core Mac under normal workload reports ~8-16, far exceeding 2.0. Changed to dynamic core-aware threshold (`os.cpus().length * 3`).

2. **`minFreeMemoryPercent: 20` incompatible with macOS** — `os.freemem()` on macOS only reports truly unused RAM, excluding reclaimable cached/purgeable memory. A typical Mac shows 1-5% "free" even with plenty available. Changed default to 1%.

3. **`--quiet` flag hardcoded in background daemon spawn** — `daemon.ts` line 217 hardcoded `--quiet`, suppressing all worker event logging to the daemon log file, making diagnosis impossible.

## Changes

- `worker-daemon.ts`: Changed `maxCpuLoad` default from `2.0` to `0` (signals dynamic threshold). Updated `canRunWorker()` to compute core-aware threshold when config is 0.
- `worker-daemon.ts`: Changed `minFreeMemoryPercent` default from `20` to `1`.
- `daemon.ts`: Removed hardcoded `--quiet` flag from background process spawn.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified `map` worker executes immediately on macOS (was permanently deferred before)
- [x] Verified `audit` worker starts after 120s offset
- [x] Verified `codebase-map.json` metrics file is written
- [x] Verified daemon state file updates with `runCount > 0`
- [ ] Test on Linux to confirm behavior unchanged (load avg reporting is similar)

## Context

The combination of low thresholds + the deadlock in `processPendingWorkers()` (addressed separately in #1052) means zero workers ever execute on macOS. This PR fixes the root cause while #1052 fixes the amplification.

title: fix(windows): resolve CLI detection and process spawning on Windows
body:
## Summary

Fixes Windows compatibility issues where claude-flow fails to detect Claude Code CLI and fails to spawn processes correctly on Windows.

**Root cause:** On Windows, the `which` command doesn't exist (it's `where`), and `spawn`/`spawnSync`/`execSync` calls need `shell: true` to resolve executables from PATH.

### Changes

| File | Fix |
|------|-----|
| `hive-mind.ts` | Use `where` instead of `which` on win32 for Claude CLI detection |
| `hive-mind.ts` | Enable `shell: process.platform === 'win32'` for claude process spawn |
| `auto-install.ts` | Enable shell for npm spawnSync on Windows for PATH resolution |
| `headless-worker-executor.ts` | Enable shell for `claude --version` check and claude spawn |
| `doctor.ts` | Enable shell for `npm install` in `installClaudeCode()` |

### Additional Windows issues found (not in this PR)

During investigation, **47+ additional instances** of missing Windows compatibility were identified across the codebase:

- `statusline-generator.ts`: Unix-style `2>/dev/null` redirections, missing `shell` options
- `init.ts`: Unix-style `&` background operator, `2>/dev/null` redirections
- `security.ts`: Missing shell options for `npm audit` commands
- `browser-tools.ts`: Missing shell for `agent-browser` spawn
- `gcs.ts`: Hardcoded `/tmp` paths (should use `os.tmpdir()`)
- `container-worker-pool.ts`: Missing shell for docker spawn
- Various other files with Unix-specific shell assumptions

**Recommendation:** Consider adding a shared `shellOption()` helper:
```typescript
const shellOption = () => process.platform === 'win32';
```

### Testing

Tested on:
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Shell:** PowerShell + Git Bash
- **Node.js:** v22+ (via nvm)
- **Claude Code:** v2.1.34
- **claude-flow:** v3.1.0-alpha.3

All three core scenarios now work:
1. `claude-flow doctor` correctly detects Claude Code CLI
2. `claude-flow swarm` successfully spawns Claude instances
3. `claude-flow mcp start` auto-installs packages via npm

Closes #615

title: feat: Add --upgrade-settings flag to init upgrade command
body:
## Summary

The `npx claude-flow@v3alpha init upgrade` command currently only updates helpers and creates missing metrics files. It does **not** update `settings.json` with new features like Agent Teams configuration.

## Problem

When we add new features (like Agent Teams in v3.1.0-alpha.13), existing users who run `init upgrade` don't get the new settings. They must either:
1. Run `init --force` (destructive - loses customizations)
2. Manually add new settings to their existing settings.json

## Solution

Add an `--upgrade-settings` flag to `init upgrade` that:
1. Reads existing `.claude/settings.json`
2. Merges new settings (hooks, env vars, claudeFlow config) without losing user customizations
3. Preserves user's existing permissions, custom hooks, etc.

### New Settings to Merge (Agent Teams)

```json
{
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS": "1"
  },
  "hooks": {
    "TeammateIdle": [...],
    "TaskCompleted": [...]
  },
  "claudeFlow": {
    "agentTeams": {
      "enabled": true,
      "teammateMode": "auto",
      ...
    }
  }
}
```

## Implementation

1. Add `--upgrade-settings` flag to `upgradeCommand` in `init.ts`
2. Create `mergeSettings()` function in `executor.ts`
3. Deep merge new settings while preserving user customizations
4. Show diff of what changed

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `init upgrade --upgrade-settings` merges new settings
- [ ] Existing user hooks are preserved
- [ ] Existing user permissions are preserved
- [ ] New Agent Teams hooks are added
- [ ] New env vars are added
- [ ] claudeFlow.agentTeams config is added/updated

## Labels

`enhancement`, `v3`, `cli`, `settings`

title: BUG: in the Codex package, it seems Claude is hardcoded where Codex workers should be instantiated
body:
Where the “Codex workers” are supposed to run, Claude is run instead

In the repo, the dual-mode runner hard-codes the Codex worker command to claude.

File: v3/@claude-flow/codex/src/dual-mode/orchestrator.ts
	1.	Default command for Codex workers is claude

	•	Line 66: claudeCommand: config.claudeCommand ?? 'claude',
	•	Line 67: codexCommand: config.codexCommand ?? 'claude', // Both use claude CLI

So unless you pass codexCommand explicitly, “Codex” workers will run the same binary as Claude workers.
	2.	Even the spawned arguments are Claude-Code-specific

	•	Line 140: chooses command based on platform:
	•	const command = config.platform === 'claude' ? this.config.claudeCommand : this.config.codexCommand;
	•	Lines 145–148: builds args that assume Claude Code CLI:
	•	-p <prompt>
	•	--output-format text
	•	Lines 150–156: also assumes flags like --max-turns and --model.

That’s the smoking gun: the “codex” lane is implemented as “run claude headlessly”, not codex.

title: Bug: hook-handler.cjs never generated — blocks UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse
body:
## Summary

`npx claude-flow@v3alpha mcp start` configures `.claude/settings.json` with hooks that reference `.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs`, but **this file is never created** during setup. Three hooks lack `continueOnError: true`, so they hard-block every Claude Code session:

- `UserPromptSubmit` → blocks every prompt submission
- `PreToolUse:Bash` → blocks every shell command
- `PostToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit` → blocks every file edit

The remaining hooks (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`, `SubagentStart`) have `continueOnError: true` so they fail silently, but the three above make Claude Code unusable.

## Environment

- **claude-flow**: `v3alpha` (via `npx claude-flow@v3alpha mcp start`)
- **Node.js**: v20.20.0
- **npm**: 10.8.2
- **OS**: Linux aarch64 (OrbStack devcontainer on macOS, M4 Max)
- **Claude Code**: Latest (Opus 4.6)

## Reproduction

1. Set up a project with claude-flow V3 MCP:
   ```json
   // .claude.json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "claude-flow": {
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["claude-flow@v3alpha", "mcp", "start"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. Run `npx claude-flow@v3alpha hooks init` or let the system scaffold `.claude/settings.json`

3. The generated settings reference `hook-handler.cjs`:
   ```json
   {
     "hooks": {
       "PreToolUse": [{
         "matcher": "Bash",
         "hooks": [{
           "type": "command",
           "command": "node .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs pre-bash",
           "timeout": 5000
         }]
       }],
       "PostToolUse": [{
         "matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit",
         "hooks": [{
           "type": "command",
           "command": "node .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs post-edit",
           "timeout": 10000
         }]
       }],
       "UserPromptSubmit": [{
         "hooks": [{
           "type": "command",
           "command": "node .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs route",
           "timeout": 10000
         }]
       }]
     }
   }
   ```

4. Check if the file exists:
   ```bash
   ls .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs
   # ls: cannot access '.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs': No such file or directory
   ```

5. Files that DO exist in `.claude/helpers/`:
   ```
   auto-memory-hook.mjs
   learning-service.mjs
   metrics-db.mjs
   statusline.cjs
   # ... various .sh scripts
   # NO hook-handler.cjs
   ```

6. Submit any prompt in Claude Code → `UserPromptSubmit hook error`
7. Try any Bash command → `PreToolUse:Bash hook error`
8. Try any file edit → `PostToolUse hook error`

## Error Messages

```
⎿  UserPromptSubmit hook error
```

```
⎿  PreToolUse:Bash hook error
```

## Root Cause

The hooks scaffolding in `.claude/settings.json` references `node .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs` with subcommands (`pre-bash`, `post-edit`, `route`, `session-restore`, `session-end`, `status`) but this file is never generated during `hooks init` or any other setup step.

## Impact

- **Session-breaking**: Users cannot submit prompts, run Bash, or edit files — Claude Code is completely unusable
- **No workaround in-tool**: The errors appear before any tool can execute, so users can't self-fix from within the session
- **Silent vs loud failure inconsistency**: Some hooks have `continueOnError: true` (SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, SubagentStart) while the three most critical ones do not

## Proposed Fix

Two options (ideally both):

### Option A: Generate `hook-handler.cjs` during setup
`hooks init` should create `.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs` with working implementations for all subcommands (`pre-bash`, `post-edit`, `route`, `session-restore`, `session-end`, `status`). Even minimal stubs that exit 0 would unblock users.

### Option B: Add `continueOnError: true` to all hooks
At minimum, the scaffolded settings should include `"continueOnError": true` on every hook so a missing handler degrades gracefully instead of hard-blocking:

```json
{
  "type": "command",
  "command": "node .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs route",
  "timeout": 10000,
  "continueOnError": true
}
```

## Related Issues

- #947 — `UserPromptSubmit hook error` (same symptom, no resolution)
- #1058 — V3 MCP hook handlers are stubs that don't persist data (even if handler existed, backends are fake)
- #1084 — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks not triggered by Claude Code in some configs
- #1014 — Hooks initialization uses incorrect npm package name

## Workaround

Manually remove the three broken hook entries from `.claude/settings.json`, or add `"continueOnError": true` to each one. This loses hook functionality but unblocks Claude Code.

title: [BUG] Systematic agent termination failure: classifyHandoffIfNeeded is not defined
body:
## Bug Report: Systematic Agent Termination Failure

### Summary
Every agent spawned via the Task tool fails with `classifyHandoffIfNeeded is not defined` error during cleanup/termination, **after successfully completing their assigned work**. This is a systematic bug affecting 100% of agents tested.

### Environment
- **claude-flow version**: v3.1.0-alpha.22
- **Claude Code version**: 2.1.37
- **Platform**: Linux (OrbStack devcontainer)
- **Node.js**: 20.x
- **Install method**: Global npm install

### Reproduction Steps
1. Spawn any agent using Claude Code's Task tool with `subagent_type`
2. Agent completes its work successfully (creates files, generates output)
3. Agent attempts to terminate/handoff
4. Error occurs: `ReferenceError: classifyHandoffIfNeeded is not defined`

### Affected Agents (7/8 tested - 87.5% failure rate)

All agents completed their work successfully before failing:

| Agent ID | Type | Task | Output Size | Status |
|----------|------|------|-------------|--------|
| a9d5081 | system-architect | Queen Orchestrator (Phase 1 proposal) | 67.9k tokens | ✅ Created 60KB file, then failed |
| ac52b3f | researcher | Cross-Reference Tracker | 27.7k tokens | ✅ Created 28KB file, then failed |
| ac48b0e | pseudocode | SPARC Pseudocode documentation | 49.9k tokens | ✅ Created 59KB file, then failed |
| a5ea504 | system-architect | DDD Architect 1 (Trading + Risk domains) | 47.7k tokens | ✅ Created 2 files (29KB + domain), then failed |
| a4aa35f | system-architect | ADR Writer 2 (ADR-004, 005, 006) | 83.7k tokens | ✅ Created 3 ADRs (18KB + 25KB + domain), then failed |
| afbb1b6 | system-architect | DDD Architect 2 (Venue, Learning, Monitoring) | 74.6k tokens | ✅ Created 3 domains (22KB + 32KB + domain), then failed |
| ab8cd99 | system-architect | ADR Writer 1 (ADR-001, 002, 003) | 82.9k tokens | ✅ Created 3 ADRs (19KB + 23KB + domain), then failed |

**Agent still running**: aec3913 (expected to fail with same error)

### Error Message
```
ReferenceError: classifyHandoffIfNeeded is not defined
```

### Key Observations

1. **100% reproducible** - Every agent that completes its task hits this error
2. **Work is NOT lost** - All agents successfully create their deliverables before failing
3. **Error occurs during cleanup** - The actual agent work completes successfully
4. **Agent types don't matter** - Affects `system-architect`, `researcher`, `pseudocode` equally
5. **Task complexity doesn't matter** - Affects both simple and complex tasks

### Impact

**Severity**: Medium
- ✅ **Good**: No data loss - agents complete their work successfully
- ❌ **Bad**: Agent status shows "failed" instead of "completed"
- ❌ **Bad**: Requires manual verification that work was actually completed
- ❌ **Bad**: Breaks automated workflows relying on agent success status

**Workaround**: Check if agent's output files exist - if they do, the agent succeeded despite the error.

### Expected Behavior
Agent should complete work and terminate cleanly without errors.

### Actual Behavior
Agent completes work successfully, then fails during termination with `classifyHandoffIfNeeded is not defined`.

### Suspected Root Cause
The `classifyHandoffIfNeeded` function is likely:
1. Not imported in the agent termination code
2. Renamed/removed in a recent refactor
3. In a different module that's not being loaded

This appears to be in claude-flow's agent lifecycle management, specifically the cleanup/handoff phase after an agent completes its work.

### Additional Context

**Multi-Phase Byzantine Consensus Workflow**: We're running a complex workflow with:
- Phase 1: 1 Queen + 10 voters (Queen failed, voters succeeded)
- Phase 2: 8 parallel document creators (7/8 failed so far)
- Phases 3-5: 10 voters each (pending)

**All work is completing successfully** - we have 17/18 documents created (ADRs, DDD domains, SPARC specs) despite the errors.

### Related Issues
- #1108 (initial report from Phase 1)

### Request
Please investigate the agent termination code path and ensure `classifyHandoffIfNeeded` is properly defined/imported. This bug is preventing reliable multi-agent workflows despite the actual work completing successfully.

title: Bug: Headless workers hang indefinitely due to stdin pipe never closed
body:
## Description

All headless background workers (`audit`, `optimize`, `testgaps`) hang indefinitely when spawned via the daemon because `claude --print` blocks waiting for stdin EOF when stdin is a pipe that is never closed.

The `executeClaudeCode()` method in `headless-worker-executor.ts` spawns `claude --print` with `stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']` but **never writes to or closes `child.stdin`**. Since `claude --print` defaults to `--input-format text`, it reads from stdin even when the prompt is provided as a CLI argument. The open, unclosed pipe causes an indefinite block.

## Impact

- **100% failure rate** on all headless workers since deployment
- 4,180+ failed runs accumulated, wasting ~541 hours of process time
- Exit code 143 (SIGTERM from timeout) on every headless execution
- All result files are 363 bytes: `{ "success": false, "output": "", "error": "Process exited with code 143" }`

## Reproduction

```javascript
// test-stdin-open.mjs -- HANGS (bug reproduction)
import { spawn } from 'child_process';
const child = spawn('claude', ['--print', 'Reply with just OK'], {
  stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']  // stdin pipe created but never closed
});
// NOTE: stdin.end() NOT called - this reproduces the daemon bug
child.stdout.on('data', d => console.log('STDOUT:', d.toString()));
child.on('close', code => console.log('EXIT CODE:', code));
setTimeout(() => { console.log('TIMEOUT - killing'); child.kill('SIGTERM'); }, 15000);
```

**Result:** Hangs for 15 seconds, killed with SIGTERM (exit 143), zero stdout output.

```javascript
// test-stdio-ignore.mjs -- WORKS (fix)
import { spawn } from 'child_process';
const child = spawn('claude', ['--print', 'Reply with just OK'], {
  stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']  // stdin = /dev/null (immediate EOF)
});
child.stdout.on('data', d => console.log('STDOUT:', d.toString()));
child.on('close', code => console.log('EXIT CODE:', code));
setTimeout(() => { console.log('TIMEOUT - killing'); child.kill('SIGTERM'); }, 30000);
```

**Result:** Completes in ~8 seconds with "OK", exit code 0.

## Test Matrix

| Stdin Config | Completed? | Exit Code | Output | Duration |
|-------------|-----------|-----------|--------|----------|
| `< /dev/null` | Yes | 0 | "OK" | ~8s |
| `pipe` + `stdin.end()` | Yes | 0 | "OK" | ~8s |
| `pipe` + **no close** | **HANG** | 143 (SIGTERM) | *empty* | killed@15s |
| `'ignore'` | Yes | 0 | "OK" | ~8s |

## Root Cause

`headless-worker-executor.ts` line ~810:

```typescript
const child = spawn('claude', ['--print', prompt], {
    cwd: this.projectRoot,
    env,
    stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],  // BUG: stdin pipe opened but never closed
    windowsHide: true,
});
```

No code path in the file ever references `child.stdin`. Searching for `.stdin`, `stdin.write`, `stdin.end`, `stdin.pipe` returns zero matches in the entire services directory. The pipe was opened and never used.

## Fix

Change `stdio` from `['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']` to `['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']`:

```diff
--- a/v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/headless-worker-executor.ts
+++ b/v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/headless-worker-executor.ts
             const child = spawn('claude', ['--print', prompt], {
                 cwd: this.projectRoot,
                 env,
-                stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
+                stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
                 windowsHide: true,
             });
```

**Why `'ignore'` is correct:**
- No code ever writes to stdin — the prompt is passed entirely via CLI argument
- `'ignore'` connects stdin to `/dev/null`, providing immediate EOF
- Equivalent to `< /dev/null` which works in all tests
- Alternative fix: `child.stdin.end()` immediately after spawn (also verified working)

**Ideal future improvement:** Pipe the prompt via stdin instead of CLI argument to avoid `ARG_MAX` limits for large prompts.

## Post-Fix Verification

After applying the fix, headless workers produce real AI-powered analysis:

| Worker | Before Fix | After Fix |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| audit | 363 bytes, `success: false` | 14KB security report (13 vulnerabilities, riskScore 87) |
| optimize | 363 bytes, `success: false` | 71KB performance report (N+1 queries, cache misses) |
| testgaps | 363 bytes, `success: false` | 140KB test gap analysis with test skeletons |

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (Noble Numbat)
- **Kernel:** Linux 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64
- **CPU:** 32 cores
- **RAM:** 187 GB
- **Node.js:** v24.13.0
- **Claude Code:** v2.1.38
- **claude-flow:** v3.1.0-alpha.28

## Related Issues

- #1077 (macOS resource thresholds -- same symptom, different cause)
- #958 ("Still can't figure out how to get v3 to actually perform work")
- #510 ("Swarm Command Works But Lacks Headless/Production Support")


## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.44 through current

title: Bug: Headless worker failures silently swallowed — executeWorker never checks result.success
Bug: Worker scheduling interval mismatch — daemon runs headless workers 3-6x more frequently than intended
body:
## Description

Two independent config sources specify conflicting scheduling intervals for headless workers. The daemon's `DEFAULT_WORKERS` runs workers 3-6x more frequently than the headless executor's `HEADLESS_WORKER_CONFIGS` intended. The daemon's config is the only one that actually controls scheduling — the headless executor's `intervalMs` values are **dead code**.

## Interval Mismatch

| Worker | Daemon `DEFAULT_WORKERS` | Headless `HEADLESS_WORKER_CONFIGS` | Ratio |
|--------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|-------|
| audit | 600,000ms (**10 min**) | 1,800,000ms (**30 min**) | **3x too frequent** |
| optimize | 900,000ms (**15 min**) | 3,600,000ms (**60 min**) | **4x too frequent** |
| testgaps | 1,200,000ms (**20 min**) | 3,600,000ms (**60 min**) | **3x too frequent** |

## Impact

### API Cost

| Worker | Model | Calls/day (daemon) | Calls/day (intended) | Excess |
|--------|-------|-------------------|----------------------|--------|
| audit | haiku | 144 | 48 | 96 extra/day |
| optimize | sonnet | 96 | 24 | 72 extra/day |
| testgaps | sonnet | 72 | 24 | 48 extra/day |

Estimated: **~$520/month at daemon intervals vs ~$170/month at intended intervals** (~$350/month excess).

### Currently Masked by #1077

Issue #1077 (unrealistic resource thresholds) causes most headless executions to fail before making API calls. This has been **accidentally masking the cost exposure**. If #1077 is fixed without also fixing intervals, API costs will spike immediately.

## Root Cause

The daemon and headless executor have two separate config systems that were never unified:

```
WorkerDaemon
  └─ DEFAULT_WORKERS[] ← controls scheduling (setTimeout intervals)
       └─ For each timer fire:
            if isHeadlessWorker(type):
                headlessExecutor.execute(type)
                  └─ HEADLESS_WORKER_CONFIGS[type] ← used for prompt/model/timeout ONLY
                     └─ intervalMs field exists but NOTHING reads it for scheduling
```

**Evidence:**
1. `scheduleWorker()` (worker-daemon.ts ~line 268) uses `workerConfig.intervalMs` from `DEFAULT_WORKERS` to set `setTimeout` (line 286)
2. `execute()` (headless-worker-executor.ts ~line 416) reads `HEADLESS_WORKER_CONFIGS[workerType]` but only accesses `headless.*` properties (promptTemplate, sandbox, model, outputFormat, contextPatterns, timeoutMs)
3. No code anywhere reads `HEADLESS_WORKER_CONFIGS[type].intervalMs` for scheduling

The `DEFAULT_WORKERS` was designed for lightweight local workers (file scanning). The `HEADLESS_WORKER_CONFIGS` was designed for cost-aware API-calling workers. When headless workers were added to the daemon, they inherited the daemon's aggressive local-worker intervals.

## Fix

### Option A: Align DEFAULT_WORKERS with HEADLESS_WORKER_CONFIGS (minimal)

```diff
--- a/v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/worker-daemon.ts
+++ b/v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/worker-daemon.ts
 const DEFAULT_WORKERS = [
     { type: 'map', intervalMs: 900000, priority: 'normal', enabled: true },
-    { type: 'audit', intervalMs: 600000, priority: 'critical', enabled: true },
-    { type: 'optimize', intervalMs: 900000, priority: 'high', enabled: true },
+    { type: 'audit', intervalMs: 1800000, priority: 'critical', enabled: true },
+    { type: 'optimize', intervalMs: 3600000, priority: 'high', enabled: true },
     { type: 'consolidate', intervalMs: 1800000, priority: 'low', enabled: true },
-    { type: 'testgaps', intervalMs: 1200000, priority: 'normal', enabled: true },
+    { type: 'testgaps', intervalMs: 3600000, priority: 'normal', enabled: true },
 ];
```

### Option B: Bridge the configs (structural, preferred)

In `WorkerDaemon.start()` or `scheduleWorker()`, read the headless executor's config and override daemon intervals for headless worker types:

```typescript
scheduleWorker(workerConfig) {
    let intervalMs = workerConfig.intervalMs;
    // Use headless config intervals for API-calling workers
    if (isHeadlessWorker(workerConfig.type) && this.headlessExecutor) {
        const headlessConfig = this.headlessExecutor.getConfig(workerConfig.type);
        if (headlessConfig?.intervalMs) {
            intervalMs = headlessConfig.intervalMs;
        }
    }
    // ... use intervalMs for setTimeout
}
```

## Correct Intervals

| Worker | Current | Should Be | Rationale |
|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| map | 15 min | 15 min | Local, no API cost |
| audit | 10 min | **30 min** | Headless (haiku) |
| optimize | 15 min | **60 min** | Headless (sonnet, most expensive) |
| consolidate | 30 min | 30 min | Local, no API cost |
| testgaps | 20 min | **60 min** | Headless (sonnet) |
| document | 60 min | **120 min** | Headless (haiku, disabled by default) |

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, Kernel 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64
- **CPU:** 32 cores, **RAM:** 187 GB
- **Node.js:** v24.13.0
- **Claude Code:** v2.1.38
- **claude-flow:** v3.1.0-alpha.28

## Related Issues

- #1077 (resource thresholds masking cost exposure)


## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.44 through current

title: Bug: No log rotation — headless execution logs grow unbounded (~23 MB/day)
body:
## Description

The headless worker executor creates 2-3 log files per worker execution (prompt, result, error) but has **zero log management**. No rotation, no max file count, no TTL, no compression, no cleanup. Logs accumulate indefinitely.

## Impact

- **Growth rate:** ~75 KB per successful worker run (prompt + result logs)
- At current daemon intervals (10-20 min per worker): **~23 MB/day, ~702 MB/month**
- After 1 year: **~8.4 GB** of individual log files
- Thousands of small files can cause inode exhaustion on some filesystems
- On this system, 8,400+ files (212 MB) accumulated in 17 days before manual cleanup

## Root Cause

\`headless-worker-executor.ts\` \`logExecution()\` method (~line 985):

\`\`\`typescript
logExecution(executionId, type, content) {
    try {
        const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();
        const logFile = join(this.config.logDir, \`\${executionId}_\${type}.log\`);
        const logContent = \`[\${timestamp}] \${type.toUpperCase()}\n\${'='.repeat(60)}\n\${content}\n\`;
        writeFileSync(logFile, logContent);  // Creates new file per execution, no cleanup
    }
    catch {
        // Ignore log write errors
    }
}
\`\`\`

Each execution generates separate files with no cleanup anywhere in the codebase.

## Fix

Defect **DM-006** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch) — 3 ops targeting \`services/headless-worker-executor.js\`.

| Op | What it does |
|----|-------------|
| A | Add \`unlinkSync\` and \`statSync\` to the ESM \`fs\` import |
| B | Call \`cleanupOldLogs()\` from \`ensureLogDir()\` so cleanup runs on each execution cycle |
| C | Add \`cleanupOldLogs()\` method: removes \`.log\` files older than 7 days or beyond a 500-file cap, keeping newest first |

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, Kernel 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64
- **Node.js:** v24.13.0
- **claude-flow:** v3.1.0-alpha.28


## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.44 through current


## Related Issues

- #1171 — Multiple MCP servers start independent daemons
- #1175 — session-start ignores daemon.autoStart
- #1116 — daemon.log always 0 bytes
- #1117 — runWithTimeout doesn't kill child process

title: Bug: Multiple orphan daemon processes from subdirectory launches — no global PID registry
body:
## Description

Running `claude-flow daemon start` from subdirectories creates independent daemon processes that never detect each other. The PID check only reads `.claude-flow/daemon.pid` in the **current working directory**, so each subdirectory launch creates its own daemon with its own PID file.

## Impact

- Found **5 concurrent daemon processes** running on a single machine
- Each daemon independently spawns `claude --print` workers on its own schedule
- With 5 daemons × 3 headless workers × 10-20 min intervals = **~40 API calls/hour** (5x intended)
- Stale daemons from subdirectories operate on wrong project context
- No way to detect or clean up orphan daemons without manual `ps` inspection

## Evidence

| PID | Start Time | CWD | Status |
|---------|-------------------------|------|--------|
| 3266163 | Mon Jan 26 20:52:06 | `.../docs/data/source/resource` | Orphan |
| 3431018 | Tue Jan 27 17:11:12 | `.../docs/data/source/ontology/instances` | Orphan |
| 3442045 | Tue Jan 27 17:51:19 | `.../docs/data/source/ontology` | Orphan |
| 662692 | Wed Feb 4 00:01:09 | `/home/claude/src/gene2` | Orphan |
| 2057938 | Tue Feb 10 14:40:10 | `/home/claude/src/gene` | Legitimate |

Each orphan also created its own `.claude-flow/` directory in its CWD (238 files total in orphaned directories).

## Root Cause

`daemon.ts` line ~184 — the background spawn uses `process.cwd()` as `cwd`:

```typescript
const child = spawn(process.execPath, [cliPath, 'daemon', 'start', '--foreground', '--quiet'], {
    cwd: resolvedRoot,  // resolvedRoot = process.cwd()
    detached: true,
    // ...
});
```

The PID file is written to `{cwd}/.claude-flow/daemon.pid`. The duplicate check only reads the PID file in the current directory. No upward directory traversal, no global registry.

## Suggested Fix

Option A: Search up the directory tree for the nearest `.claude-flow/daemon.pid` before starting a new daemon.

Option B: Use a global PID registry (e.g., `~/.claude-flow/daemons/{project-hash}.pid`) that tracks all running daemons.

Option C: Lock file with project root path encoded to prevent overlapping project trees.

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, Kernel 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64
- **CPU:** 32 cores, **RAM:** 187 GB
- **Node.js:** v24.13.0
- **claude-flow:** v3.1.0-alpha.28

title: Bug: daemon.log always 0 bytes — require('fs') fails silently in ESM context
body:
## Description

The `WorkerDaemon.log()` method in `worker-daemon.ts` uses `require('fs')` inside what appears to be an ESM module context. The `require` call fails silently in the catch block, resulting in **zero daemon log output** since the daemon was first started.

## Impact

- `daemon.log` has been 0 bytes since January 24, 2026 (17 days)
- 4,180+ worker failures were completely invisible — no log output whatsoever
- Significantly delayed diagnosis of the stdin pipe hang bug
- All `this.log('info', ...)` and `this.log('warn', ...)` calls throughout the daemon are no-ops

## Root Cause

Two issues:

1. `log()` method uses `require('fs')` which is undefined in ESM modules — `appendFileSync` silently fails.
2. Path mismatch — daemon spawn writes to `.claude-flow/daemon.log` but `log()` targets `.claude-flow/logs/daemon.log`.

## Fix

Defect **DM-001** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch) — 3 ops targeting `services/worker-daemon.js` and `commands/daemon.js`.

| Op | File | What it does |
|----|------|-------------|
| A | `services/worker-daemon.js` | Add `appendFileSync` to ESM import at top of file |
| B | `services/worker-daemon.js` | Replace `require('fs').appendFileSync(...)` with the imported `appendFileSync(...)` |
| C | `commands/daemon.js` | Align spawn log path to `.claude-flow/logs/daemon.log` so daemon and spawn write to the same file |

## Evidence

```
$ ls -la .claude-flow/daemon.log
-rw-rw-r-- 1 claude claude 0 Jan 24 14:10 daemon.log
```

File created on Jan 24, still 0 bytes 17 days later despite thousands of worker executions.

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, Kernel 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64
- **CPU:** 32 cores, **RAM:** 187 GB
- **Node.js:** v24.13.0
- **claude-flow:** v3.1.0-alpha.28


## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.44 through current

title: Bug: runWithTimeout rejects promise but does not kill child process — orphan claude processes
body:
## Description

The daemon's \`runWithTimeout()\` wrapper rejects the promise after the configured timeout but does **not** kill the underlying \`claude --print\` child process. The headless executor has its own longer timeout (5-15 min vs daemon's 5 min), so child processes continue running as orphans until the executor's timeout eventually fires.

## Impact

- Workers like \`optimize\` and \`testgaps\` have 10-minute headless timeouts but the daemon wraps them in a 5-minute \`runWithTimeout\`
- After daemon timeout: promise rejected, \`failureCount++\` recorded, but \`claude --print\` process still alive
- The headless executor's timeout fires 5 minutes later, kills the orphan, and resolves a promise that nobody is listening to
- On systems with multiple workers, this can accumulate orphan processes consuming memory and API credits

## Root Cause

\`worker-daemon.ts\` has \`DEFAULT_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000\` (5 min), but the headless executor's per-worker timeouts range from 5-15 minutes (\`audit\` and \`refactor\` workers use 15 min). When the daemon timeout fires first, \`runWithTimeout\` rejects the promise but the child process keeps running.

## Fix

Defect **HW-004** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch) — 1 op targeting \`services/worker-daemon.js\`.

Raise \`DEFAULT_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS\` from 5 minutes to 16 minutes so the daemon timeout never fires before the executor's own per-worker timeout (max 15 min). The executor handles its own child process cleanup on timeout, so letting it manage the lifecycle prevents orphans.

## Note

This bug is **mitigated** by the stdin pipe fix (HW-001). Once workers complete normally (~60-120s), neither timeout fires. It only manifests when workers hang or take unusually long.

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, Kernel 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64
- **Node.js:** v24.13.0
- **claude-flow:** v3.1.0-alpha.28


## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.44 through current


## Related Issues

- #1171 — Multiple MCP servers start independent daemons
- #1175 — session-start ignores daemon.autoStart
- #1114 — No log rotation
- #1116 — daemon.log always 0 bytes
