Bug: config get/export uses hand-rolled YAML parser instead of config.json
body:
## Summary
\`readYamlConfig()\` in \`config.js\` uses a 30-line hand-rolled YAML parser to read \`.claude-flow/config.yaml\`. This parser disagrees with the other 3 YAML parsers in the codebase on edge cases. Should read from \`.claude-flow/config.json\` instead.

## Root Cause
The \`readYamlConfig()\` function (added by CF-002 patch) implements a line-by-line YAML parser that handles sections via indentation detection. It disagrees with the regex-based parsers in WM-001 and CF-003 on values containing colons, quoted strings, and multi-line values.

## Fix
Defect **CF-004** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

**Root cause:** \`readYamlConfig()\` in config.js is a 30-line hand-rolled YAML parser that disagrees with the other YAML parsers on edge cases. Should use \`JSON.parse\` on config.json instead.

Replace \`readYamlConfig()\` with \`readProjectConfig()\` that reads \`.claude-flow/config.json\` via \`JSON.parse\`.

| Op | What it does |
|----|-------------|
| CF-004a | Replace readYamlConfig() with readProjectConfig() that reads config.json |

**Affected versions:** \`@claude-flow/cli\` 3.1.0-alpha.41 through current

**Related issues:** #1142 (CF-002 original config export fix)

title: Bug: doctor checkMemoryBackend reads env var + config.yaml instead of config.json
Enhancement: init should generate .claude-flow/config.json
body:
## Summary
The \`init\` command generates \`.claude-flow/config.yaml\` as the project config file. Multiple runtime consumers now read from \`.claude-flow/config.json\` instead. Init should generate config.json as the canonical runtime config.

## Root Cause
\`settings-generator.js\` generates a config.yaml file during init, but the MCP config tools (\`config_get\`, \`config_set\`, \`config_list\`, \`config_export\`) all operate on \`.claude-flow/config.json\`. This means init creates a file that the config CRUD tools don't read, and the config tools create a file that init doesn't generate.

## Fix
Defect **SG-008** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

**Root cause:** \`generateSettingsFiles()\` in settings-generator.js writes config.yaml but doesn't write config.json. Runtime config tools and patched memory/intelligence code all expect config.json.

Add config.json generation alongside the existing config.yaml generation, so both files exist after init. config.json becomes the canonical source; config.yaml is kept for backward compatibility.

| Op | What it does |
|----|-------------|
| SG-008a | Add config.json generation after config.yaml in generateSettingsFiles() |

**Affected versions:** \`@claude-flow/cli\` 3.1.0-alpha.41 through current

**Related issues:** #1150 (SG-001 init settings), #1169 (SG-003 init helpers)

title: How do I use this? Paradox of choice and confusion as a beginner
body:
This tool is very interesting. I starred it for that reason. Then this weekend, I decided to try it out for the first time.

However, I was then confronted with a gazillion choices.

I can use Claude Flow via Claude. Then there's also something called Ruflo. What is Ruflo vs Claude Flow? Is it the same?

First, I decided to just launch Claude. Then, I am presented with a statusline with a lot of emojis and numbers. What do they mean? How can I read about this, and where? Anyway, I decided to try to ask Claude to just implement some application. Nothing happened (it was just 100% Claude doing it - no special agents or anything). I verified all the Claude Flow (or Ruflo?) skills were in the .claude folder just fine.

Then I decided to try to run `bunx ruflo@alpha --help` to see what's available. From the list of options, I was unsure how to actually just get it to start a simple task directly - here was my thinking when I saw the list:
- I assumed "start" would start things up - not necessarily work on something concrete. But would I need to start before I execute something?
- "task" could be something to start new tasks.
- "agent" could also be something to start new tasks.
- "swarm" could also be something to start new tasks.
- "hive-mind" as well.

You get the idea. A lot of choices that don't "communicate well" how to just get started. Along the way, I also realized I had to start my MCP server first to get it running.

Even after starting a queen swarm (here, I was presented with "recommended" guidance which was great at least), it was just running with 15 agents doing nothing and not using any tokens. What am I doing wrong? Would be great with guidance on this.

Also, shouldn't the app just auto-start its dependencies if they aren't started (such as MCP) etc?

They say that code or projects are only as good as their documentation. What I would love to see is something like a "beginner's guide" that could present something like:
- Trying to do a brand new app? Go here.
- Trying to do bugfixing? Go here.

Etc etc etc.

Alternatively, we could have a "universal" form of command where an AI agent will figure out the right workflow to pick for me. So I can just run `bunx ruflo@alpha --objective "objective here"`, and it'll pick the right approach. This could be super helpful so everyone doesn't have to learn everything in detail about this tool, to know which approach to pick.

The above is intended as constructive criticism - I hope it is conveyed that way. It should be seen as a desire from my side to understand it and actually be able to use it - because it seems super great.

title: Bug: start.js uses hand-rolled YAML parser instead of config.json

## Summary

Three command files (`start.js`, `status.js`, `init.js`) use a hand-rolled YAML parser and check for `config.yaml` instead of `config.json`. After SG-008 consolidation, the canonical config is `config.json`, so these commands malfunction on projects initialized with the patched version.

3. **`init.js`**: `isInitialized()` checks `config.yaml`, 5 display strings show wrong filename

|----|------|--------|
| CF-006a | `commands/start.js` | Replace `isInitialized()` + `parseSimpleYaml()` + `loadConfig()` with config.json readers |
| CF-007a | `commands/status.js` | Replace `isInitialized()` to check `config.json` |
| CF-008a | `commands/init.js` | Replace all `.claude-flow/config.yaml` display strings with `config.json` |
| CF-008b | `commands/init.js` | Replace `isInitialized()` to check `config.json` |
| CF-008c | `commands/init.js` | Replace `config.yaml` in JSON output path |

- `dist/src/commands/status.js`
- `dist/src/commands/init.js`

The original SG-008 patch was conservative — it kept config.yaml generation and added config.json alongside it. Now that all consumers (memory-initializer, intelligence, doctor, config export, start, status, init) have been migrated to read config.json, the yaml generation is dead code.

title: Bug: swarm init uses legacy 'hierarchical' default, --v3-mode flag contradicts init defaults
body:
## Summary

`claude-flow swarm init` defaults to `topology: 'hierarchical'`, contradicting `claude-flow init` which defaults to `'hierarchical-mesh'`. The `--v3-mode` flag exists solely to work around this inconsistency, but running `init` then `swarm init` silently **downgrades** the topology.

## Root Cause

In `commands/swarm.js`, the `initCommand` options array declares `default: 'hierarchical'` for the topology option, and the interactive `select()` call also defaults to `'hierarchical'`. The `--v3-mode` boolean flag gates `hierarchical-mesh` topology and several output lines (Flash Attention, AgentDB, SONA) behind an opt-in flag.

Meanwhile, `commands/init.js` and `init/types.js` (`DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS`) already use `'hierarchical-mesh'` as the default topology with 15 agents — the v3 configuration. This means:

1. `claude-flow init` → hierarchical-mesh (v3)
2. `claude-flow swarm init` → hierarchical (legacy) unless `--v3-mode` is passed
3. Users who run both get conflicting state

## Fix

Defect **SG-009** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

**8 patch operations on `commands/swarm.js`:**

| Op | What |
|----|------|
| a | Change topology option `default: 'hierarchical'` → `default: 'hierarchical-mesh'` |
| b | Remove `--v3-mode` option declaration and all `v3Mode` logic (`const v3Mode`, `if (v3Mode)` topology override, print) |
| c | Change interactive selector `default: 'hierarchical'` → `default: 'hierarchical-mesh'` |
| d | Remove `if (v3Mode)` guard around Flash Attention/AgentDB/SONA output lines (keep the lines) |
| e | Remove `V3 Mode` row from status table |
| f | Remove `v3Mode` from MCP metadata object |
| g | Remove `v3Mode` from saved state.json |
| h | Update example from `'claude-flow swarm init --v3-mode'` → `'claude-flow swarm init'` |

## Files Affected

- `dist/src/commands/swarm.js`

## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.41 through current

- #1150 — SG-001: Init generates invalid settings
- #1169 — SG-003: Init missing helpers
- #1195 — SG-008: Init generates config.json

title: Bug: MINIMAL init preset hobbles runtime with legacy mesh/5-agent/memory-only defaults
body:
## Summary

`claude-flow init --minimal` uses crippled runtime defaults (`topology: 'mesh'`, `maxAgents: 5`, `memoryBackend: 'memory'`, all features disabled) that provide no benefit and silently degrade the runtime below functional thresholds.

## Root Cause

In `init/types.js`, the `MINIMAL_INIT_OPTIONS.runtime` block hardcodes:

```js
runtime: {
    topology: 'mesh',
    maxAgents: 5,
    memoryBackend: 'memory',
    enableHNSW: false,
    enableNeural: false,
    enableLearningBridge: false,
    enableMemoryGraph: false,
    enableAgentScopes: false,
},
```

The MINIMAL preset correctly reduces **components** (no statusline, no helpers, fewer skills/agents/commands) to produce a lighter file footprint. But hobbling the **runtime** block means the resulting project can't use hybrid memory, HNSW search, neural features, or hierarchical-mesh coordination — features that have no init-time cost and are needed for basic swarm operation.

## Fix

Defect **CF-009** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

**1 patch operation on `init/types.js`:**

| Op | What |
|----|------|
| a | Replace MINIMAL runtime block: `topology: 'mesh', maxAgents: 5, memoryBackend: 'memory'` + all features false → `topology: 'hierarchical-mesh', maxAgents: 15, memoryBackend: 'hybrid'` + all features true |

The MINIMAL preset continues to reduce components, hooks, skills, and agents — but the runtime block now matches `DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS.runtime` so the runtime isn't artificially crippled.

## Files Affected

- `dist/src/init/types.js`

## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.41 through current

title: Bug: 12 config.json keys written during init are never consumed at runtime
body:
## Summary

`init` writes 19 keys to `.claude-flow/config.json` via `writeRuntimeConfig()` in executor.js, but only 7 are consumed at runtime. The remaining 12 are dead — written but never read by any code path.

Each runtime consumer (memory-initializer.js, intelligence.js, embeddings-tools.js, hooks-tools.js, start.js) has hardcoded defaults instead of reading from the project config.json that `init` generates. **Root cause:** Runtime consumers hardcode defaults instead of reading the config.json keys that `init` writes.

| b | intelligence.js | learningBridge.sonaMode/confidenceDecayRate/accessBoostAmount/consolidationThreshold, memoryGraph.pageRankDamping/maxNodes |

title: Enhancement: init command lacks CLI options for config.json settings

## Summary

The `init` command has no CLI flags for most config.json settings. Users must edit config.json manually after init to change cacheSize, coordination strategy, MCP port, memory backend, neural mode, SONA settings, etc. Additionally, `cacheSize` defaults to 100 in executor.js but 256 everywhere else.

None of the 19 config.json keys have corresponding CLI options. The `writeRuntimeConfig()` template in executor.js hardcodes `cacheSize: 100` while embeddings-tools.js and settings-generator.js use 256.

| Op | File | What |
|----|------|------|
| a | commands/init.js | Add 13 option declarations (--cache-size, --coordination-strategy, etc.) |
| b | commands/init.js | Wire CLI flags into options object |
| c | init/executor.js | Wire options into config.json template, fix cacheSize 100→256 |

title: Bug: verifyWitnessChain() and getWitnessChain() have zero callers
body:
## Summary

WM-008 exposed `verifyWitnessChain()` and `getWitnessChain()` methods on the AgentDB backend, but no code in the session lifecycle actually calls them. The witness chain is recorded at init time but never verified, so tampered memory databases go undetected.

## Root Cause

The methods were added to `agentdb-backend.js` (WM-008ef) and the init event emits `witnessChainHash` (WM-008d), but neither the auto-memory hook's `doImport()` nor the helpers-generator's `doImport()` template call `verifyWitnessChain()` after `backend.initialize()`.

## Fix

Defect **WM-010** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

Patch `doImport()` in both the helpers-generator template (HELPERS_GEN) and the source hook (`auto-memory-hook.mjs`) to call `backend.verifyWitnessChain()` after initialization:

| Op | Target | Change |
|----|--------|--------|
| WM-010a | `init/helpers-generator.js` | After `await backend.initialize()` + busy_timeout in doImport template, add witness chain verification |
| WM-010b | `.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs` | After `await backend.initialize()` + busy_timeout in doImport, add witness chain verification |

The verification is wrapped in try/catch so it is non-fatal — if the backend doesn't support witness chains (e.g. JSON backend), it silently skips.

## Files Affected

- `dist/src/init/helpers-generator.js`
- `.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs`

title: Bug: recordFeedback() exposed by AgentDB v3 has zero callers
body:
## Summary

WM-008 upgraded AgentDB v2 to v3 and exposed `recordFeedback(queryId, quality)` on the agentdb-backend, but no MCP handler or CLI command ever calls it. The self-learning feedback loop is wired at the backend level but dead from the user-facing layer.

## Root Cause

`memory-tools.js` MCP handlers (`memory_search`, `memory_retrieve`) never track which search results the agent subsequently retrieves. Without this signal, the `SelfLearningRvfBackend` cannot learn which results were useful and which were not. The `recordFeedback` method on the backend exists but has zero callers.

## Fix

Defect **WM-009** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

**Op A:** Add `recordSearchFeedback(entryId, quality)` export to `memory-initializer.js` that delegates to `_hybridBackend.recordFeedback()`.

**Op B:** In `memory-tools.js`, add a module-level `_recentSearchHits` Map. After `memory_search` returns results, populate the map with `namespace:key` -> `entryId` entries.

**Op C:** In `memory-tools.js` `memory_retrieve` handler, after a successful retrieval check the `_recentSearchHits` map. If the retrieved key was a recent search result, call `recordSearchFeedback(entryId, 1.0)` for positive implicit feedback (the agent chose to retrieve this result, so it was relevant).

| Op | Target | Change |
|----|--------|--------|
| A | `memory/memory-initializer.js` | Export `recordSearchFeedback` delegating to `_hybridBackend` |
| B | `mcp-tools/memory-tools.js` | Track search result IDs in module-level Map |
| C | `mcp-tools/memory-tools.js` | Call `recordSearchFeedback` on retrieve of recent search hit |

## Files Affected

- `dist/src/memory/memory-initializer.js`
- `dist/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.js`

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.44 through current

title: Bug: ReasoningBank not instantiated — pattern-store/search hooks use generic memory instead of ReasoningBank
body:
## Summary

The `hooks_intelligence_pattern-store` and `hooks_intelligence_pattern-search` MCP tools store/search patterns through the generic `storeEntry`/`searchEntries` functions in memory-initializer.js. They never instantiate or use the `ReasoningBank` class from `@claude-flow/neural`, which provides HNSW-indexed pattern storage with trajectory tracking, MMR-diverse retrieval, deduplication, and contradiction detection.

## Root Cause

`memory-initializer.js` initializes `HybridBackend` (WM-001) with AgentDB v3 (WM-008) but never creates a `ReasoningBank` instance from `@claude-flow/neural`. The pattern hooks in `hooks-tools.js` call `getRealStoreFunction()` / `getRealSearchFunction()` which route to `storeEntry`/`searchEntries` — generic memory operations that lack the ReasoningBank's 4-step learning pipeline (retrieve, judge, distill, consolidate).

As a result:
- Patterns are stored as plain key-value entries in the `patterns` namespace, not in the ReasoningBank's HNSW-indexed pattern store
- Pattern search uses generic SQLite/keyword search instead of ReasoningBank's MMR-diverse vector retrieval
- The consolidation pipeline (dedup, contradiction detection, pruning) never runs
- Pattern evolution tracking and quality history are lost

## Fix

Defect **WM-011** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

**Root cause:** `memory-initializer.js` creates HybridBackend + AgentDB but never instantiates `ReasoningBank` from `@claude-flow/neural`. The pattern hooks in `hooks-tools.js` use generic store/search functions instead of ReasoningBank's native API.

The patch:

| Op | Target | Change |
|----|--------|--------|
| WM-011a | `memory/memory-initializer.js` | After HybridBackend init, import `ReasoningBank` from `@claude-flow/neural` and create+initialize an instance sharing the AgentDB RVF path. Export `getReasoningBank()` getter. |
| WM-011b | `mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js` | Add lazy-loaded `getReasoningBankFn()` that imports from `memory-initializer.js`. |
| WM-011c | `mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js` | Replace `hooksPatternStore` handler to use `ReasoningBank.storeTrajectory()` + `memoryToPattern()` when available, falling back to generic store. |
| WM-011d | `mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js` | Replace `hooksPatternSearch` handler to use `ReasoningBank.retrieveByContent()` when available, falling back to generic search. |

**Affected versions:** `@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.44 through current

**Related issues:** #812, #829, #1207

title: hook-handler.cjs ignores stdin: all hook data silently lost on Claude Code 2.x (prompt, tool_input, file_path always empty)
body:
## Summary

`hook-handler.cjs` never reads from stdin. Claude Code 2.x delivers all hook payload data (prompt, tool_input, file_path, session_id) via stdin as JSON. The handler instead reads from environment variables (`PROCESS.ENV.PROMPT`, `TOOL_INPUT_command`, `TOOL_INPUT_file_path`) that Claude Code 2.x does not set. The result is that **every hook invocation silently receives empty data**, making the `route`, `pre-bash`, and `post-edit` handlers non-functional.

## Affected Versions

alpha.28 through alpha.44 (current). Likely all v3.1.0-alpha releases.

## What Claude Code 2.x Actually Sends

Claude Code pipes a JSON object to the hook process's stdin for every hook event. Examples:

**UserPromptSubmit:**
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit",
  "prompt": "the user's actual prompt text"
}
```

**PreToolUse (Bash):**
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "ls -la" }
}
```

**PostToolUse (Write/Edit):**
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "hook_event_name": "PostToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Edit",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/edited/file.js" }
}
```

## What the Handler Currently Does

**Line 39 of `hook-handler.cjs`:**
```js
const prompt = process.env.PROMPT || process.env.TOOL_INPUT_command || args.join(' ') || '';
```

- `process.env.PROMPT` — not set by Claude Code 2.x
- `process.env.TOOL_INPUT_command` — not set by Claude Code 2.x
- `args.join(' ')` — empty (no extra args are passed after the command name in settings.json hook commands)
- **Result: `prompt` is always `''`**

**Line 83 of `hook-handler.cjs` (inside `post-edit`):**
```js
var file = process.env.TOOL_INPUT_file_path || args[0] || '';
```

- `process.env.TOOL_INPUT_file_path` — not set by Claude Code 2.x
- `args[0]` — undefined
- **Result: `file` is always `''`**

## Impact Per Hook

| Hook (command) | Effect of empty data |
|---|---|
| `route` (UserPromptSubmit) | `intelligence.getContext('')` and `router.routeTask('')` called with empty string — routing is meaningless |
| `pre-bash` (PreToolUse Bash) | Dangerous command check runs against `''` — always passes trivially, detection is completely bypassed |
| `post-edit` (PostToolUse Write/Edit) | `intelligence.recordEdit('')` called — edit history records empty string for every file, not the actual path |

## Fix

Add a synchronous stdin read block **before** the `prompt` assignment, then update both extraction lines to prefer stdin data with env var fallback.

```js
// Read hook payload from stdin (Claude Code 2.x sends JSON via stdin)
let stdinPayload = {};
try {
  const raw = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8').trim();
  if (raw) stdinPayload = JSON.parse(raw);
} catch (e) { /* stdin empty or unavailable — fallback to env vars below */ }

const [,, command, ...args] = process.argv;
const prompt = stdinPayload.prompt ||
  (stdinPayload.tool_input && stdinPayload.tool_input.command) ||
  process.env.PROMPT || process.env.TOOL_INPUT_command ||
  args.join(' ') || '';
```

And in the `post-edit` handler:
```js
var file = (stdinPayload.tool_input && stdinPayload.tool_input.file_path) ||
  process.env.TOOL_INPUT_file_path || args[0] || '';
```

`fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8')` reads fd 0 (stdin) synchronously. No async changes needed. The try/catch ensures zero regression if stdin is empty or not a valid JSON object.

**No changes to `settings.json` are required.** The `echo ... && node ...` pattern in hook commands does not consume stdin before node runs.

## Notes

- This issue was first identified in #1119 (Bug 4: "Hook handler dead on mismatched event data") but not yet addressed
- Related: #1172 (stdin reading PR, currently open and unmerged)
- The `stdinPayload` object also exposes `tool_name`, `session_id`, and `hook_event_name` which could enable richer handler logic once stdin is read

## Environment

- Claude Code: 2.1.52
- claude-flow: 3.1.0-alpha.28 (also verified in alpha.44 tarball — same issue)
- macOS Darwin 25.3.0 / Node 24.13.0

title: Bug: HybridBackend doesn't proxy recordFeedback/verifyWitnessChain to AgentDBBackend
body:
## Summary

HybridBackend exposes `getAgentDBBackend()` but doesn't proxy `recordFeedback()`, `verifyWitnessChain()`, or `getWitnessChain()` methods. Callers must know about the two-layer architecture to access learning and witness chain features.

## Root Cause

The `HybridBackend` class in `@claude-flow/memory/dist/hybrid-backend.js` wraps both a SQLite backend and an AgentDB backend. While it delegates standard CRUD operations, it doesn't expose the three methods that AgentDB v3 adds for self-learning and tamper detection:
- `recordFeedback(queryId, quality)` — for the learning loop
- `verifyWitnessChain()` — for SHAKE-256 data mutation chain verification
- `getWitnessChain()` — for retrieving the current witness chain state

Without these proxies, callers must reach through `getAgentDBBackend()` to access learning/witness features, breaking the abstraction boundary and requiring knowledge of the internal architecture.

## Fix

Defect **WM-012** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

Add 3 proxy methods to HybridBackend that delegate to the AgentDB backend:

| Op | Method | Delegates To |
|----|--------|-------------|
| WM-012a | `recordFeedback(queryId, quality)` | `this.agentdb.recordFeedback()` |
| WM-012b | `verifyWitnessChain()` | `this.agentdb.verifyWitnessChain()` |
| WM-012c | `getWitnessChain()` | `this.agentdb.getWitnessChain()` |

Each proxy gracefully returns a default value if the AgentDB backend is not available or doesn't support the method.

## Files Affected

- `@claude-flow/memory/dist/hybrid-backend.js`

## Affected Versions

`@claude-flow/cli` 3.1.0-alpha.41 through current

## Related Issues

- #1207 — AgentDB v2 to v3 upgrade (WM-008)
- #1209 — Wire AgentDB learning loop (WM-009)
- #1208 — Wire witness chain verification (WM-010)

title: Wire BM25 hybrid search into memory_search handler
body:
## Summary

The \`memory_search\` handler falls back to hand-rolled word matching when semantic search returns no results. AgentDB v3 ships a \`HybridSearch\` class that combines vector similarity with BM25 keyword scoring via reciprocal rank fusion, providing significantly better recall.

## Root Cause

\`HybridSearch\` is exported from \`agentdb\` but never instantiated. The keyword fallback in \`searchEntries()\` (memory-initializer.js lines 1892-1916) uses \`String.includes()\` for matching and \`matchCount / words.length * 0.5\` for scoring — a crude approximation that misses stemming, IDF weighting, and proper BM25 term frequency normalization.

## Fix

Defect **WM-019** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

| Op | Description |
|----|-------------|
| WM-019a | Add \`_hybridSearch\` module-level variable in \`memory-initializer.js\` |
| WM-019b | Instantiate HybridSearch during \`initializeMemoryDatabase\` |
| WM-019c | Export \`getHybridSearch()\` getter (raw Python insertion) |
| WM-019d | Import getHybridSearch in memory-tools.js \`getMemoryFunctions()\` |

title: Fix npm ECOMPROMISED cache corruption blocking npx installs
body:
## Problem

Users running `npx claude-flow@alpha` (or `npx ruflo@alpha`) intermittently hit:

```
npm error code ECOMPROMISED
npm error Lock compromised
```

This blocks installation entirely — npm refuses to proceed and no user code runs.

### Root Cause

npm's `_cacache/index-v5` stores integrity hashes (SHA-512) for every downloaded tarball. When a new version is published (e.g., alpha.48 → alpha.49), the cached integrity entry may reference the **old** tarball hash while npm tries to fetch the **new** one. npm detects this mismatch and throws `ECOMPROMISED` rather than silently using potentially tampered content.

This is a known npm bug that particularly affects:
- Frequently-published packages (our alpha cadence)
- Remote/CI environments (Codespaces, GitHub Actions)
- npm 10.x on Node 22+

### Why existing fixes didn't help

We already had three layers of cache repair:

1. **`preinstall.cjs`** — cleaned ENOTEMPTY artifacts (stale `.package-*` dirs) and checked `_cacache` readability
2. **`bin/npx-repair.js`** — cleaned stale rename artifacts from `~/.npm/_npx`
3. **Inline preinstall scripts** in `package.json` for umbrella and ruflo packages

**The problem**: `ECOMPROMISED` fires during npm's own package resolution phase, *before* any `preinstall` hook runs. Our preinstall hooks only cleaned ENOTEMPTY artifacts and permission-based `_cacache` issues — they never touched the integrity index entries that cause ECOMPROMISED.

## Fix (v3.1.0-alpha.50)

### 1. Enhanced `preinstall.cjs` — integrity index cleanup

The preinstall hook now walks the `_cacache/index-v5` hash bucket structure and removes any integrity entries referencing `claude-flow` or `ruflo` packages. This forces npm to re-fetch with correct integrity on the next install.

```javascript
// Walk the two-level hash bucket structure: index-v5/XX/YY/...
var buckets = fs.readdirSync(cacheIndex);
for (var bi = 0; bi < buckets.length; bi++) {
  // ... walk subdirectories ...
  var content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
  if (content.indexOf('claude-flow') !== -1 || content.indexOf('ruflo') !== -1) {
    fs.unlinkSync(filePath);
  }
}
```

**Why this works**: While `preinstall` can't prevent the *first* ECOMPROMISED error, it ensures that once any claude-flow package successfully installs, all stale integrity entries are cleaned — preventing the error on subsequent runs.

### 2. Enhanced `npx-repair.js` — new `repairCacheIntegrity()`

Added a dedicated function that walks `_cacache/index-v5` and removes corrupted entries:

```javascript
export function repairCacheIntegrity() {
  const indexDir = join(homedir(), '.npm', '_cacache', 'index-v5');
  // Walk all hash buckets, remove entries containing 'claude-flow' or 'ruflo'
}
```

This is called from `bin/cli.js` on every CLI invocation, so running *any* claude-flow command cleans up for future npx calls.

### 3. Updated umbrella package inline preinstall scripts

Both `claude-flow` and `ruflo` `package.json` preinstall scripts now include the `_cacache` walk as an inline one-liner.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/bin/preinstall.cjs` | Walk `_cacache/index-v5` and remove claude-flow/ruflo integrity entries |
| `bin/npx-repair.js` | Added `repairCacheIntegrity()` export, added `readFileSync`/`unlinkSync` imports |
| `bin/cli.js` | Call `repairCacheIntegrity()` on startup alongside `repairNpxCache()` |
| `package.json` (umbrella) | Expanded inline preinstall to include `_cacache` walk |
| `ruflo/package.json` | Expanded inline preinstall to include `_cacache` walk |

## Workaround (for users on older versions)

```bash
npm cache clean --force
npx claude-flow@alpha init upgrade
```

## Validation

Docker test suite (clean Node 22 environment):

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Clean install | PASS — `claude-flow v3.1.0-alpha.50` |
| ECOMPROMISED recovery (corrupted integrity then re-run) | PASS |
| Version check | PASS — alpha.50 |
| Ruflo install | PASS |

## Timeline of npm cache fixes

| Version | Fix | Error Addressed |
|---------|-----|-----------------|
| alpha.47 | preinstall.cjs, npx-repair.js, inline preinstall scripts | ENOTEMPTY |
| alpha.48 | Optimized statusline (reduced shell spawns) | Statusline timeouts |
| alpha.49 | Updated statusline generator for `init upgrade` | Stale statusline on upgrade |
| **alpha.50** | **`_cacache` integrity index cleanup** | **ECOMPROMISED** |

title: doctor command reports wrong version (v0.0.0 or stale npx cache)
body:
## Bug

`claude-flow doctor` reports an incorrect version under "Version Freshness" while `claude-flow -V` reports the correct version.

### Observed behavior

| Command | Output |
|---------|--------|
| `claude-flow -V` | `claude-flow v3.1.0-alpha.54` ✅ |
| `claude-flow doctor` | `⚠ Version Freshness: v3.0.0-alpha.190` or `v0.0.0` ❌ |

### Root cause

The version detection in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/doctor.js` (`checkVersionFreshness()`) fails to resolve its own package version because:

1. **Insufficient parent traversal** — The relative path checks go up 1 and 2 levels from the module directory (`../package.json` and `../../package.json`), but `doctor.js` lives at `dist/src/commands/`, which is 5 levels below the `@claude-flow/cli` package root. Neither relative path reaches `package.json`.

2. **CWD fallback is wrong** — `process.cwd()/package.json` finds the *user's project* `package.json`, not claude-flow's. Since the name doesn't match `@claude-flow/cli`, it's skipped.

3. **npx cache is unreliable** — The code scans `~/.npm/_npx/` for `@claude-flow/cli` and uses whichever entry it finds first. If stale cache entries exist from older versions, it reports the wrong version. If the cache is empty (or the user installed globally, not via npx), it falls through to `v0.0.0`.

### Suggested fix

Replace the path-walking heuristic with a direct resolution from `import.meta.url`:

```js
import { createRequire } from 'module';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const { version: currentVersion } = require('@claude-flow/cli/package.json');
```

Or walk up from `import.meta.url` until `package.json` with `name === '@claude-flow/cli'` is found (similar to `find-up`).

### Environment

- claude-flow v3.1.0-alpha.54 (global install via npm)
- Node.js v25.6.1
- macOS (Darwin 25.2.0, arm64)

title: fix: SonaTrajectoryService does not use native @ruvector/sona API correctly
body:
## Bug Summary

`SonaTrajectoryService` (from the `agentdb` package) fails to properly integrate with the native `@ruvector/sona` engine, resulting in SONA trajectory learning being effectively disabled. The service stores the module object instead of instantiating a `SonaEngine`, and calls nonexistent methods (`recordStep`, `record`, `addStep`, `predict`, `selectAction`) instead of the actual native API.

**This bug has existed since the file first appeared in `agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.4` and is present in every version through `alpha.10`.**

## Source File Missing from Git

The `SonaTrajectoryService` TypeScript source file **does not exist anywhere in the git source** of `ruvnet/agentic-flow` (agentdb's repo) — not on `main`, not on any of the 18 feature branches, and not in the commit history. The file only exists in the npm-published `dist/` directory.

This is part of a broader pattern: 4 service files and 5 controller files exist in the npm package but have no corresponding source in git.

## Impact

- **SONA native learning is completely non-functional** — trajectories are never recorded in the native engine
- **Pattern extraction fails** — `findPatterns` is never called
- The service silently falls back to a simple JavaScript frequency counter, giving the appearance of working while providing no actual RL-based learning
- All Micro-LoRA, EWC++, and pattern clustering features of `@ruvector/sona` are bypassed
- The service reports `engineType: 'native'` and `available: true` while doing nothing with the native engine

## Root Cause (3 bugs)

### Bug 1: `initialize()` — Module vs Instance
Looks for `SONA`/`Sona` class name instead of `SonaEngine`. Falls back to storing the raw module object.

### Bug 2: `recordTrajectory()` — Nonexistent Methods
Calls `recordStep()`, `record()`, `addStep()` — none exist on SonaEngine. Silent `catch {}`.

### Bug 3: `predict()` — Nonexistent Methods
Calls `predict()`, `selectAction()` — neither exist. Falls back to frequency counter.

## Fix

PR submitted: https://github.com/ruvnet/agentic-flow/pull/121

- Uses `SonaEngine.withConfig()` for proper instantiation
- Uses `beginTrajectory` → `addTrajectoryStep` → `endTrajectory` → `tick()` pipeline
- Uses `findPatterns()` for pattern-based predictions
- 54/54 test assertions passing across 10 test categories
- Full backward compatibility maintained

- **actions/setup-node** (v4 → v6): Major version upgrade — review the [release notes](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/releases) for breaking changes

- **actions/download-artifact** (v4 → v8): Major version upgrade — review the [release notes](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases) for breaking changes
- **actions/github-script** (v7 → v8): Major version upgrade — review the [release notes](https://github.com/actions/github-script/releases) for breaking changes
- **actions/cache** (v4 → v5): Major version upgrade — review the [release notes](https://github.com/actions/cache/releases) for breaking changes

Actions that were previously pinned to commit SHAs remain pinned to SHAs (updated to the latest release SHA) to maintain the security benefits of immutable references.

These changes only affect CI/CD workflow configurations and should not impact application functionality. The workflows should be tested by running them on a branch before merging.

title: Bug: CacheManager setInterval missing .unref() prevents process exit
body:
## Summary

`CacheManager.startCleanupTimer()` in `@claude-flow/memory` calls `setInterval(..., 60000)` without `.unref()`, keeping the Node.js event loop alive indefinitely. Any CLI command that touches memory (`memory store`, `memory search`, etc.) cannot exit cleanly.

## Root Cause

`cache-manager.js` line 310:

```javascript
startCleanupTimer() {
    this.cleanupInterval = setInterval(() => {
        this.cleanupExpired();
    }, 60000);
    // MISSING: this.cleanupInterval.unref();
}
```

The `CacheManager` is instantiated via `TieredCacheManager` → `this.l1Cache = new CacheManager(...)` whenever the bridge initializes. Since the constructor calls `startCleanupTimer()`, the 60-second housekeeping interval holds the event loop open.

Other timers in the same package (`agentdb-backend.js:142`, `auto-memory-bridge.js:534`) correctly call `.unref()`. `sqljs-backend.js:81` has the same bug with its `persistTimer`.

## Fix

Defect **MM-002** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

Add `.unref()` after each `setInterval` call in `cache-manager.js` and `sqljs-backend.js`. Housekeeping timers should not prevent process exit — they are best-effort cleanup, not critical work.

| Op | File | Change |
|----|------|--------|
| MM-002a | `cache-manager.js` | Add `this.cleanupInterval.unref()` after `setInterval` |
| MM-002b | `sqljs-backend.js` | Add `this.persistTimer.unref()` after `setInterval` |

## Files Affected

- `@claude-flow/memory/dist/cache-manager.js`
- `@claude-flow/memory/dist/sqljs-backend.js`

## Affected Versions

`ruflo` (all versions)

## Related Issues

- None

title: Bug: HybridBackend dual-write causes SQLite contention under concurrent agents
body:
## Summary

When multiple agents (≥4) perform `memory_store`/`memory_delete` concurrently, SQLite throws `Error: database is locked` after 5s busy_timeout. The HybridBackend dual-writes to both SQLite and AgentDB in parallel, but SQLite serializes writers via WAL — only one agent can write at a time.

## Root Cause

`HybridBackend.store()` (hybrid-backend.js:94-97) does:

```javascript
await Promise.all([
    this.sqlite.store(entry),    // ← serialized by WAL
    this.agentdb.store(entry)    // ← independent, succeeds
]);
```

Multiple agents call this simultaneously. SQLite acquires a write lock on `.swarm/hybrid-memory.db`:
- Agent 1 gets the lock, writes successfully
- Agents 2-N block at `stmt.run()` for up to `busy_timeout` (5s)
- After 5s: `Error: database is locked` — no retry, no backoff, failure

Additional issues in the write path:
1. **No transaction wrapper**: `sqlite-backend.js:91-114` does two `stmt.run()` calls (entry + embedding) without a transaction — partial commits possible
2. **Silent `catch {}` on pragma**: `memory-initializer.js:1076-1082` silently catches if `busy_timeout` pragma fails to set
3. **No write queueing**: MCP handlers don't serialize writes to SQLite
4. **dualWrite hardcoded**: `dualWrite: true` on line 22 of hybrid-backend.js, not configurable from config.json

## Fix

Defect **MM-003** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

**Immediate fix**: Wrap SQLite writes in a transaction and add retry with backoff on SQLITE_BUSY.

**Structural fix**: Implement ADR-048 (Hybrid Elimination) — remove `dualWrite` and use AgentDB v3 directly. AgentDB's RVF backend has its own persistence format designed for concurrent access. The SQLite half is both the bottleneck and unnecessary since AgentDB v3 has complete persistence.

## Files Affected

- `@claude-flow/memory/dist/hybrid-backend.js` — dualWrite hardcoded to true
- `@claude-flow/memory/dist/sqlite-backend.js` — no transaction wrapper, no retry
- `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/memory-initializer.js` — silent catch on busy_timeout pragma

## Affected Versions

`ruflo` (all versions), `@claude-flow/memory` (all versions with HybridBackend)

## Related Issues

- #1256 — MM-002: CacheManager .unref() fix (same file: memory-initializer.js)
- #829 — WM-001: Wire HybridBackend into CLI (created the dual-write path)

title: Refactor: ADR-048 — eliminate HybridBackend, use AgentDB v3 directly
body:
## Summary

Replace `HybridBackend` dual-write layer with direct `AgentDBBackend` usage in all CLI
files. AgentDB v3 has complete persistence (RVF backend), self-learning, and witness
chain — SQLite dual-write is unnecessary overhead that causes contention under concurrent
agents (see #1257).

## Root Cause

`HybridBackend` was a transitional layer for dual-writing to both SQLite and AgentDB.
Now that AgentDB v3 is proven (vendored, 193 tests, witness chain, self-learning),
the hybrid layer adds:
- Dual-write overhead (~2x write cost)
- SQLite WAL contention under ≥4 concurrent agents (#1257)
- Unnecessary config complexity (4-way backend choice)
- Proxy method indirection (WM-012)

## Fix

Defect **WM-092** in [claude-flow-patch](https://github.com/sparkling/claude-flow-patch).

Overlay patches at execution order 990 transform the final patched state:
1. Replace `HybridBackend` instantiation with direct `AgentDBBackend`
2. Rename `_hybridBackend` → `_agentdbBackend` throughout
3. Remove SQLite config (`hybridConfig.sqlite`, `dualWrite`, `busy_timeout`)
4. Remove `getSQLiteBackend()` calls
5. Update getter: `getHybridBackend()` → `getAgentDBBackend()`
6. Remove WM-012 proxy indirection

**Affected versions:** `ruflo` (all versions)

**Related issues:** #1257 (SQLite contention), #829 (memory wiring)

      throw err;
      ^
  Error: Cannot find module 'C:\projects\myproject\apps\api\.claude\helpers\auto-memory-hook.mjs'
      at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1420:15)
      ...
      code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
      requireStack: []

  Affected Hooks

  All hooks in the generated settings.json are affected:

  - SessionStart — auto-memory-hook.mjs import, hook-handler.cjs session-restore
  - SessionEnd — hook-handler.cjs session-end
  - Stop — auto-memory-hook.mjs sync
  - PreToolUse — hook-handler.cjs pre-bash
  - PostToolUse — hook-handler.cjs post-edit
  - UserPromptSubmit — hook-handler.cjs route
  - PreCompact — hook-handler.cjs compact-manual, compact-auto
  - SubagentStart — hook-handler.cjs status
  - statusLine — statusline.cjs

  Root Cause

  The hook generator writes relative paths assuming process.cwd() will always be the project root where .claude/settings.json lives. Claude Code may set the CWD to the directory the user launched from, which can  
  be any subdirectory in a monorepo.

  Note: hook-handler.cjs internally uses __dirname (line 19) to resolve sibling files, so it works once Node can find it. The problem is Node never finds it because the path in settings.json is relative to CWD.   

  Workaround

  Manually prefix all hook commands with cd /path/to/project/root &&:

  "command": "cd /path/to/project/root && node .claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs sync"

  Suggested Fix

  Option A — Use absolute paths when generating hooks:

  "command": "node /absolute/path/to/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs sync"

  Option B — Resolve project root at runtime (walk up to find .claude/settings.json or use git):

  "command": "cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && node .claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs sync"

  Option C — Use __dirname-relative paths inside a wrapper that settings.json invokes via absolute path.

  Environment

  - @claude-flow/cli: 3.5.2
  - OS: Windows 11 (also reproducible on any OS with monorepo subdirectory CWD)
  - Node: v25.2.1
  - Claude Code: latest

title: CAUTION: Obfuscated preinstall script deletes npm cache entries for claude-flow and ruflo
body:
## Summary

  `ruflo` v3.5.2 (current on npm) contains an obfuscated one-liner in its `preinstall`
  lifecycle hook. This code runs automatically at `npm install` time, before any package
  files are written, with no disclosure in the README, CHANGELOG, or npm page.

  ## The code

  From `ruflo/package.json`, `"scripts"."preinstall"` (verify with `npm view ruflo scripts`):

      node -e "var f=require('fs'),p=require('path'),o=require('os'),h=o.homedir(),
      d=p.join(h,'.npm','_npx');
      ...f.rmSync(t,{recursive:true,force:true})...
      ...if(c.indexOf('claude-flow')!==-1||c.indexOf('ruflo')!==-1)f.unlinkSync(fp)
      ..." || true

  ## What it does (deobfuscated)

  **Part 1:** Walks `~/.npm/_npx/*/node_modules/` and recursively deletes directories
  whose names start with `.`, contain `-`, and contain 8+ consecutive letters.

  **Part 2:** Recursively walks `~/.npm/_cacache/index-v5/` (npm's package metadata
  cache) and calls `fs.unlinkSync()` on every file whose content contains the string
  `"claude-flow"` or `"ruflo"`.

  This means: if a user has previously `npm install`-ed `claude-flow` (the predecessor
  package, also by this author), those cache index entries are silently deleted on
  install of `ruflo`.

  ## Why this is a problem

  1. **Obfuscation.** Destructive filesystem operations in install scripts are a known
     supply chain attack vector. Minifying them into a single unreadable line, with no
     comment, is deceptive regardless of intent.

  2. **Destructive writes outside the package directory.** `~/.npm/_cacache/` is a
     shared user-level resource. npm's own guidelines prohibit install scripts from
     modifying files outside their package scope without disclosure.

  3. **Targets a competing package by name.** `claude-flow` is the predecessor package
     by the same author, still available on npm. Deleting its cache entries on install
     of a competing package is anti-competitive and violates npm's acceptable use policy.

  4. **No disclosure.** None of this is mentioned in the README or on the npm page.

  Note: `@claude-flow/cli` — which `ruflo` depends on — contains its own preinstall
  that is now a no-op with the comment
  `"// Preinstall hook — no-op (cache repair removed in 3.1.0-alpha.53)"`.
  The destructive version was removed from the dependency but left in the wrapper.

  ## Steps to verify

      npm view ruflo scripts --json
      # Inspect the preinstall value

title: fix(memory): wire LearningBridge into intelligence module (WM-013)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1213

`LearningBridge` was exported from `@claude-flow/memory` but never instantiated at runtime inside `intelligence.ts` (compiled: `dist/src/memory/memory-initializer.js`). Config keys `learningBridge.sonaMode`, `confidenceDecayRate`, `accessBoostAmount`, and `consolidationThreshold` were read by WM-007b but never wired to an actual `LearningBridge` instance, leaving confidence decay, trajectory tracking, and pattern consolidation as dead code.

## Changes

Following the WM-011 (`ReasoningBank`) initialization pattern:

| Op | Target | Change |
|----|--------|--------|
| WM-013a | `intelligence.ts` | Add `let _learningBridge: any \| null = null;` module-level variable after `reasoningBank` |
| WM-013b | `intelligence.ts` | Instantiate `LearningBridge` after ReasoningBank init block, reading config from `finalConfig.learningBridge.*` |
| WM-013c | `intelligence.ts` | Export `getLearningBridge()` getter function |

**Additional:**
- Add optional `learningBridge?` field to `SonaConfig` interface
- Add `learningBridgeEnabled: boolean` to `IntelligenceStats`
- Update `initializeIntelligence()` return type to surface `learningBridgeEnabled`
- Call `_learningBridge.destroy()` inside `clearIntelligence()` to flush active trajectories before teardown

## Implementation Notes

`@claude-flow/memory` is **not** a direct dependency of `@claude-flow/cli`, so `LearningBridge` is loaded via dynamic import (same optional-peer pattern that `LearningBridge` itself uses internally for `@claude-flow/neural`). The backend is resolved through `ControllerRegistry` via `memory-bridge.js`. When either is unavailable, `_learningBridge` stays `null` and all paths degrade gracefully — no change in behavior for environments without `@claude-flow/memory` installed.

## Testing

Existing `learning-bridge.test.ts` covers the `LearningBridge` class API. The wiring in `intelligence.ts` degrades silently when the package is absent, so no new required tests — but a follow-up integration test (checking `getLearningBridge() !== null` after `initializeIntelligence({ learningBridge: { enabled: true } })` in a full install) would be a useful addition.

## Related
- #1210 — WM-011 wires ReasoningBank (pattern this follows)
- #1204 — WM-007 reads learningBridge config keys
- #1212 — WM-012 adds HybridBackend proxy methods

title: AgentDB bridge always unavailable - ControllerRegistry not exported from @claude-flow/memory
body:
## Bug Description

All `agentdb_*` MCP tools (health, pattern-store, pattern-search, session-start, hierarchical-store/recall, etc.) always return `{ available: false, error: "AgentDB bridge not available" }`.

## Root Cause

`dist/src/mcp-tools/agentdb-tools.js` imports `memory-bridge.js`, which attempts:

```js
const { ControllerRegistry } = await import('@claude-flow/memory');
```

However, `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.11` does **not** export `ControllerRegistry`. The actual exports are:

```
AgentDBAdapter, AgentDBBackend, AutoMemoryBridge, CacheManager, HNSWIndex,
HybridBackend, LearningBridge, MemoryGraph, MemoryMigrator, QueryBuilder,
SQLiteBackend, SqlJsBackend, TieredCacheManager, UnifiedMemoryService, ...
```

The import fails silently (caught), sets `bridgeAvailable = false`, and all subsequent agentdb tool calls return the "not available" error permanently.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install ruflo 3.5.2 (`npm i -g ruflo@3.5.2`)
2. Configure as MCP server in Claude Code
3. Call any `agentdb_*` tool (e.g., `agentdb_health`)
4. Returns `{ available: false, error: "AgentDB bridge not available" }`

## Verification

```js
// This confirms ControllerRegistry is missing:
import('@claude-flow/memory').then(m => console.log('ControllerRegistry' in m));
// Output: false
```

## Environment

- ruflo: 3.5.2
- @claude-flow/memory: 3.0.0-alpha.11
- @claude-flow/cli: (bundled with ruflo)
- Node.js: v22.15.0
- OS: Windows 11

## Expected Behavior

`@claude-flow/memory` should export `ControllerRegistry`, or `memory-bridge.js` should use the classes that are actually exported (e.g., `AgentDBAdapter`, `UnifiedMemoryService`).

title: fix: swarm start now spawns real Claude processes
body:
## Summary

- `swarm start` was showing a fake 500ms spinner without spawning any agents. Now it writes state files, generates per-role prompts, and launches a detached Node manager that runs up to 3 concurrent `claude --print` processes
- `swarm stop` now reads PIDs from `.swarm/agents/*.json` and kills them, auto-detects swarm ID from state file
- `agent_spawn` MCP tool gains an optional `execute` flag to spawn a real Claude process (default false, backward compatible)

## What was wrong

`swarm start` ran `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 500))` then printed "deployed" — zero processes were ever started. `swarm stop` printed fake messages without killing anything.

## How it works now

1. `swarm start` flattens the agent plan, writes agent/task/prompt files to `.swarm/`
2. A detached manager script (`.swarm/.manager.js`) picks up pending agents and spawns `claude --print <prompt>` with max 3 concurrent
3. Manager deletes `CLAUDECODE` env var to bypass nested-session guard
4. On completion, agent/task JSON files are updated; output saved to `.swarm/results/`
5. `swarm status` reads real state from these files
6. `swarm stop` sends SIGTERM (or SIGKILL with `--force`) to tracked PIDs

## Files changed

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/swarm.ts` — start + stop commands
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/agent-tools.ts` — execute flag in agent_spawn

## Testing

Tested on macOS with claude CLI installed. Verified agents spawn, PIDs are tracked, status reflects real state, and stop kills processes.

Fixes #1196, #1034, #984

title: fix(memory): add .unref() to housekeeping timers to prevent process hang
body:
Adds `.unref()` to two `setInterval` timers that prevent the Node.js process from exiting cleanly.
---

**Problem**

`CacheManager.startCleanupTimer()` and SqlJsBackend 's auto-persist timer both call `setInterval()` without `.unref()`, keeping the event loop alive indefinitely. This means any CLI command that touches memory (`memory store`, `memory search`, etc.) hangs after completing its work and never exits - users have to `Ctrl+C` to kill it.

----

**Fix**

Added `.unref()` after each `setInterval` call, guarded by an existence check for environments where `.unref()` may not be available:

+ v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/cache-manager.ts - cleanup timer (line ~397)
+ v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/sqljs-backend.ts - persist timer (line ~136)

----

**Why this is safe**

- These are best-effort housekeeping timers, not critical work. The `shutdown()`  methods already handle final cleanup/persist explicitly.
- Other timers in the same package (`agentdb-backend.js:142`, `auto-memory-bridge.js:534`) already call `.unref()` correctly - this just brings the remaining two in line with that pattern.
- Zero behavioral change when the process is still running; only affects exit behavior.

---

Fixes Issue #1256

title: fix(mcp): read version from package.json instead of hardcoding
body:
Replaces the hardcoded '3.0.0-alpha' version string in `system_status` and `system_info` MCP tools with a dynamic read from 
package.json
---

**Problem**

The `system_status` and `system_info` tools both return `version: '3.0.0-alpha'`, but the actual installed npm package is `v3.5.2`. This causes confusion when users check the running server version against the installed package:

```
// Actual output
{ "version": "3.0.0-alpha" }

// Expected output
{ "version": "3.5.2" }
```
----

**Fix**

Added a `getPackageVersion()` helper that reads the `version` field from the root 
package.json at runtime. Falls back to `'unknown'` if the file cannot be read. Both hardcoded occurrences (lines 97 and 291) are replaced with calls to this helper.

**File changed:**  v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/system-tools.ts

----

**Why this is safe**

- Uses the same `readFileSync` and `existsSync` that are already imported in the file.
- Reads from `process.cwd()` which is standard for CLI tools and matches how the rest of the system resolves project-relative paths (e.g., getSystemDir() on line 34).
- Graceful fallback to `'unknown'` - no crash if package.json is missing.

----

Fixes Issue #1253

title: fix(hooks): update statusline branding from 'Claude Flow V3' to 'Rufl…
body:
Updates the statusline output to display `Ruflo V3` instead of the old `Claude Flow V3` branding.

**Problem**

The package was rebranded from `claude-flow` to `ruflo`, but the statusline generator still outputs the old name:

```
▊ Claude Flow V3 ● user │ ⎇ main │ Opus 4.5

```

This affects users who migrated to the `ruflo` package and see inconsistent branding.

Updated 4 occurrences in v3/@claude-flow/hooks/src/statusline/index.ts :

Location | Before | After
-- | -- | --
Doc comment (line 8) | Claude Flow V3 | Ruflo V3
generateStatusline() header | ▊ Claude Flow V3 | ▊ Ruflo V3
generateSingleLine() prefix | CF-V3 | Ruflo-V3
generateSafeStatusline() header | ▊ Claude Flow V3 | ▊ Ruflo V3

----
**Why this is safe**

Pure string replacement - no logic changes, no API changes, no risk of regression. Aligns with the rebrand that was already applied to package.json, README, and CLI commands.

---

title: feat(ADR-059): Context Optimization Engine — @claude-flow/context
body:
## Summary

Implements the **Context Optimization Engine** as a new bounded context package (`@claude-flow/context`) and integrates it into the live Ruflo system through CLI commands, MCP tools, and hook registration.

Closes #1273

## What's Included

### New Package: `@claude-flow/context` (57 files, 7,770 lines)

**Domain Layer (DDD)**
- 4 value objects: `CompressionRatio`, `ContextBudget`, `SearchQuery`, `SnippetWindow`
- 2 entities: `KnowledgeChunk` (FTS5-indexed), `SandboxInstance` (lifecycle FSM)
- 2 aggregates: `CompressionSession` (metrics tracking), `KnowledgeBase` (dedup + TTL eviction)
- 4 domain events: `OutputCompressed`, `ContentIndexed`, `BudgetExceeded`, `ChunksEvicted`
- 3 repository interfaces aligned with infrastructure implementations

**Infrastructure Layer**
- `FTS5Repository`: sql.js WASM-backed search with BM25 scoring and Porter stemming
- `ChunkingEngine`: heading-aware content splitting with code block preservation (2048-token chunks, 128-token overlap)
- `LevenshteinCorrector`: edit distance calculator with early-exit optimization for fuzzy Layer 3

**Sandbox Layer**
- `SandboxPool`: process-isolated execution via `child_process.spawn()` with warm pool (3 default), max 8 concurrent, 30s timeout, 512MB memory limit
- `RuntimeDetector`: auto-detection for 11 language runtimes via shebang and syntax heuristics
- `CredentialPassthrough`: fail-closed env allowlist (GitHub, AWS, K8s, Docker tokens)

**Application Layer**
- `CompressionPipelineService`: 3-tier pipeline — passthrough (<1KB), snippet (1-5KB), full pipeline (>5KB with intent filtering)
- `FuzzySearchService`: 3-layer cascade — FTS5 stemming → trigram substring → Levenshtein correction
- `UnifiedSearchService`: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) combining keyword + HNSW semantic search
- `MetricsCollector`: per-tool and per-session compression stats
- CLI command handlers: `context stats`, `context doctor`, `context search`

**Hooks**
- `PreToolUseHook`: budget-aware gate — blocks at BLOCKED level, warns at REDUCED/MINIMAL
- `PostToolUseHook`: compresses output through pipeline + indexes full content in knowledge base
- `SubagentRoutingHook`: injects batch_execute instructions into Agent/Task tool prompts

**Budget Management**
- `ContextBudgetManager`: topology-aware allocation (hierarchical: coordinator 1.5x, mesh: equal), progressive throttling (NORMAL→REDUCED→MINIMAL→BLOCKED), budget reallocation on agent completion
- `SharedKnowledgeTracker`: cross-agent content deduplication via hash tracking
- `SwarmBudgetIntegration`: event-driven bridge to swarm coordinator lifecycle with runtime payload validation

### Live System Integration (3 new files, 5 edited files)

**CLI Command** (`cli/src/commands/context.ts`)
- 5 subcommands: `stats`, `search`, `doctor`, `budget`, `compress`
- Delegates to MCP tools per ADR-005 (CLI as thin wrapper)
- Registered in commands index, category `advanced`

**MCP Tools** (`cli/src/mcp-tools/context-tools.ts`)
- 5 tools: `context_stats`, `context_search`, `context_doctor`, `context_budget`, `context_compress`
- Lazy singleton service bundle shared across all tool handlers (avoids duplicate FTS5 databases)
- Registered in MCP tool registry

**Hook Bridge** (`hooks/src/bridge/context-bridge.ts`)
- Adapts `PreToolUseHook` → `HookEvent.PreToolUse` (priority: High) for budget enforcement
- Adapts `PostToolUseHook` → `HookEvent.PostToolUse` (priority: Normal) for output compression
- Adapts `SubagentRoutingHook` → `HookEvent.AgentSpawn` (priority: Normal) for batch hints
- Auto-registered during `initializeHooks()`

**Wiring**
- `@claude-flow/context` added as `optionalDependencies` to both `@claude-flow/cli` and `@claude-flow/hooks`
- All integration points use `try/catch` dynamic imports — system works without `@claude-flow/context` installed

### Design Documents (from first commit)
- SPARC PRD: `v3/docs/PRD-context-optimization.md`
- ADR-059: Core architecture decision
- ADR-059a: FTS5 knowledge base with three-layer fuzzy search
- ADR-059b: Sandbox isolation and credential passthrough
- ADR-059c: Swarm-aware context budgets and progressive throttling
- DDD domain model and integration points

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Native package over plugin** — full hook access, HNSW integration, swarm-aware agent budgets
2. **FTS5 + HNSW dual index** — FTS5 for precision (exact terms, code symbols), HNSW for recall (semantic similarity)
3. **Process isolation over VM/container** — ~10ms startup, low overhead, good security for our threat model
4. **Progressive throttling over hard cutoff** — educates agents, degrades gracefully, provides escape hatch via batch_execute
5. **Optional dependency pattern** — `@claude-flow/context` in `optionalDependencies`, try/catch dynamic imports everywhere
6. **Lazy singleton service bundle** — all 5 MCP tools share one set of services to avoid duplicate WASM databases
7. **CLI delegates to MCP tools** — per ADR-005, CLI commands call `callMCPTool()` instead of importing domain services

## Test plan

- [x] 301 tests across 17 test files — all passing
- [x] Value objects: construction, validation, edge cases, equality (36 tests)
- [x] Entities: lifecycle state machine, expiry, deduplication (26 tests)
- [x] Aggregates: invariant enforcement, event emission, pullEvents (27 tests)
- [x] FTS5 repository: BM25 ranking, trigram search, vocabulary, eviction (25 tests)
- [x] Chunking engine: heading split, code block preservation, overlap (17 tests)
- [x] Levenshtein: distance computation, correction, early exit (22 tests)
- [x] Sandbox pool: JS/Python/shell execution, timeout, concurrency, drain (17 tests)
- [x] Runtime detector: shebang, heuristics, hint validation (28 tests)
- [x] Credential passthrough: fail-closed allowlist verification (12 tests)
- [x] Compression pipeline: passthrough/medium/full paths, intent filtering (10 tests)
- [x] Fuzzy search: 3-layer cascade, match layer annotation (6 tests)
- [x] Unified search: RRF fusion, keyword-only fallback (6 tests)
- [x] Metrics: per-tool stats, session aggregation, reset (7 tests)
- [x] Hooks: budget gate, compression routing, subagent injection (13 tests)
- [x] Budget manager: topology allocation, throttling, rebalance (31 tests)
- [x] Swarm integration: event handling, dispose cleanup (7 tests)
- [x] Build verification: all 3 packages compile with zero new TS errors
- [x] Integration wiring: CLI command registered, MCP tools in registry, hooks bridge auto-loads

title: Windows: daemon and memory init silently fail — init --start-all reports success but creates nothing
body:
## Summary

On Windows 11, `init --start-all` (via `@claude-flow/cli@latest`) reports successful daemon start and memory initialization, but neither actually occurs. Doctor's warnings are accurate; init's success messages are false positives.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise (10.0.26200)
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1 / PowerShell Core
- Node.js: v20.19.6
- npm: v10.8.2
- @claude-flow/cli: v3.5.2
- Claude Code CLI: v2.1.63

## Steps to Reproduce

```powershell
# From a project directory with no prior .claude-flow folder
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init --start-all
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest doctor --fix
Get-Content .\.claude-flow\daemon.pid
Get-ChildItem .\.claude-flow\data\
```

## Expected Behavior

- `.claude-flow/daemon.pid` exists and contains a live process ID
- `.claude-flow/data/` contains an initialized memory database
- `doctor --fix` reports both as healthy

## Actual Behavior

`init --start-all` output reports success:
```
[INFO] Starting services...
  Initializing memory database...
  Memory database already exists
  Starting daemon...
  ✓ Daemon started
  Initializing swarm...
  Swarm initialization skipped
[OK] All services started
```

But immediately after, `doctor --fix` contradicts this:
```
⚠ Config File: No config file (using defaults)
⚠ Daemon Status: Not running
⚠ Memory Database: Not initialized
```

Direct filesystem verification confirms doctor is correct:
```powershell
Get-Content .\.claude-flow\daemon.pid   # returns nothing — file does not exist
Get-ChildItem .\.claude-flow\data\      # returns nothing — directory is empty
```

## Diagnosis

Three distinct failures:

### 1. Daemon does not persist
`init --start-all` reports "✓ Daemon started" but creates no PID file and leaves no running process. The daemon process likely starts and exits immediately. This is a Windows process lifecycle issue — the daemon may depend on Unix-style process forking (`child_process.fork` with `detached: true`) which behaves differently on Windows.

### 2. Memory database not initialized
`init --start-all` reports "Memory database already exists" even after a clean directory deletion, then `data/` remains empty. The memory initialization either runs against the wrong path, fails silently, or the "already exists" check is incorrectly skipping initialization.

### 3. Doctor checks wrong config filename
`init --start-all` creates `.claude-flow/config.yaml` (confirmed in init summary output). Doctor reports "No config file" — it appears to be checking for `config.json` rather than `config.yaml`, making this warning a false negative regardless of the daemon/memory issues.

## Additional Context

- The `.claude/settings.json` file is created correctly by init
- MCP server registration via `claude mcp add` works correctly
- `@claude-flow/cli` version used: latest (`npx @claude-flow/cli@latest`)
- Issue is reproducible across multiple clean init attempts
- The `verify-cross-platform.ts` in the memory package correctly detects Windows and recommends `sql.js` over `better-sqlite3` — but the daemon/memory init path does not appear to reach this logic successfully

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Daemon**: Use PowerShell `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden` or register as a Windows scheduled task instead of Unix-style fork/detach
2. **Memory init**: Add explicit error output when initialization fails rather than silently claiming "already exists"
3. **Doctor config check**: Detect both `config.yaml` and `config.json` rather than hardcoding one filename

title: macOS: daemon dies immediately after start, status always shows STOPPED
body:
## Environment

- **OS:** macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (Apple Silicon)
- **Ruflo version:** 3.5.2
- **Node.js:** v20.20.0
- **npm:** v10.8.2
- **Claude Code CLI:** v2.1.63

## Description

After `ruflo init` and `ruflo start`, the `start` command reports success but the daemon process dies immediately. `ruflo status` always shows `STOPPED` with no running swarm, no MCP server, and no agents — regardless of how the system is started.

This is the same core issue as #1282 (Windows), but reproduced on macOS.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ruflo init` — succeeds, creates 114 files
2. `ruflo daemon start` — reports `[OK] Daemon started in background (PID: XXXXX)`
3. `ruflo memory init` — succeeds, creates memory.db
4. `ruflo start` — reports `[OK] Claude Flow V3 is running!` with healthy status

## Observed Behavior

- `ruflo start` prints success every time, creates a new swarm ID each run
- `ruflo status` always shows STOPPED immediately after
- daemon.pid file is written but the PID is dead (`ps -p <pid>` returns nothing)
- daemon.log is 0 bytes — no output, no errors, silent crash
- MCP server also fails: `[WARN] MCP tool not found: mcp_start`
- `ruflo doctor` reports `Daemon Status: Running` but the PID is dead

## Ruling Out Path Spaces

Reproduced via a symlink at `/tmp/casa-glow-agent` → same result. Not a path-with-spaces issue.

## State File Evidence

- `.claude-flow/daemon-state.json` shows `"running": true` but all workers have `"isRunning": false` and `"runCount": 0`
- `.swarm/state.json` shows `"status": "ready"` but `status` command doesn't read it
- The `start` command doesn't persist state in a way `status` can detect

## Expected Behavior

`ruflo start` should start a persistent daemon process that survives beyond the command, and `ruflo status` should reflect the running state.

title: Claude Code hooks: multiple misconfigured commands in generated settings.json cause silent/persistent failures
body:
## Summary

The hook commands generated by `@claude-flow/cli` in `.claude/settings.json` contain several bugs that cause hooks to fail silently or with visible errors on every Claude Code interaction. Tested against `@claude-flow/cli@3.5.2` on macOS (darwin 25.3.0), Node v22, Claude Code latest.

---

## Bug 1 — `PostToolUse: Write/Edit/MultiEdit` — `--file` flag is broken in `post-edit`

**Hook command (as generated):**
```
claude-flow hooks post-edit --file "$TOOL_INPUT_file_path" --success "$TOOL_SUCCESS"
```

**Expected:** Records the edited file path for pattern learning.

**Actual:** Records the value of `--success` (`"true"`) as the file path instead of `$TOOL_INPUT_file_path`. The `--file` long flag appears to not be wired to the correct positional argument in `post-edit`. The `pre-edit` subcommand handles `--file` correctly; only `post-edit` is affected.

**To reproduce:**
```bash
claude-flow hooks post-edit --file "src/app/layout.tsx" --success "true"
# Output: [INFO] Recording outcome for: true
# Expected: [INFO] Recording outcome for: src/app/layout.tsx
```

The short flag `-f` works correctly:
```bash
claude-flow hooks post-edit -f "src/app/layout.tsx" --success "true"
# Output: [INFO] Recording outcome for: src/app/layout.tsx  ✓
```

---

## Bug 2 — `PreToolUse: Task/Agent` — `pre-task` requires `--task-id` but hook only passes `--description`

**Hook command (as generated):**
```
claude-flow hooks pre-task --description "$TOOL_INPUT_prompt"
```

**Expected:** Records the task start and returns agent suggestions.

**Actual:** Always fails immediately with:
```
[ERROR] Required option missing: --task-id
```

`hooks pre-task` requires **both** `--task-id` and `--description`, but the generated hook command only passes `--description`. This means every agent/task spawn fires a failing hook. The generated CLAUDE.md documentation also only shows `--description` being passed, so the documentation is inconsistent with the CLI's actual requirements.

**To reproduce:**
```bash
claude-flow hooks pre-task --description "Fix auth bug"
# [ERROR] Required option missing: --task-id

claude-flow hooks pre-task --task-id "task-001" --description "Fix auth bug"
# Works correctly ✓
```

---

## Bug 3 — `UserPromptSubmit` and other hooks — shell quoting breaks on prompts/commands with special characters

**Hook command (as generated):**
```json
"command": "claude-flow hooks route --task \"$PROMPT\""
```

**Expected:** Routes every user prompt to the optimal agent.

**Actual:** Any prompt containing a double-quote character breaks the shell command. The hook command is evaluated by `sh -c`, so when `$PROMPT` expands to a value containing `"`, the shell sees unbalanced quotes and the command errors:

```
UserPromptSubmit hook error
```

**Example prompts that break the hook:**
- `Can you fix the "auth bug" in login.tsx?`
- `Why does git commit -m "feat: add feature" fail?`
- Any multi-line prompt with code snippets

The same issue affects the `PreToolUse: Bash` and `PostToolUse: Bash` hooks, where `$TOOL_INPUT_command` is passed inline:
```json
"command": "claude-flow hooks pre-command --command \"$TOOL_INPUT_command\""
```
Commands like `git commit -m "message"` will break these hooks in the same way.

**Root cause:** Inline variable interpolation into a `sh -c` string is not safe for arbitrary content. When the variable value contains `"`, the shell re-parses the expanded string and sees broken quoting.

---

## Bug 4 — `PostToolUse: Task/Agent` — hook matcher `^Task$` does not match Claude Code's `Agent` tool

**Hook matcher (as generated):**
```json
{ "matcher": "^Task$", ... }
```

**Expected:** Fires after every agent spawn.

**Actual:** Claude Code's `Agent` tool fires `PostToolUse` events with the tool name `"Agent"`, not `"Task"`. The `^Task$` regex does not match `"Agent"`, so the hook never fires for agent spawns. This means post-task learning patterns are never recorded when the `Agent` tool is used.

The error surfaces in Claude Code's UI as:
```
PostToolUse:Agent hook error
```
even though no hook is actually configured for `"Agent"`, suggesting Claude Code attempts some default behaviour that fails.

The matcher should be `^(Task|Agent)$` to cover both tool names.

---

## Bug 5 — `Notification` hook — `UNIQUE constraint failed` on every notification after the first

**Hook command (as generated):**
```
claude-flow memory store --namespace notifications --key "notify" --value "$NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE"
```

**Expected:** Stores each notification for later retrieval.

**Actual:** The first notification stores successfully. Every subsequent notification fails with:
```
[ERROR] UNIQUE constraint failed: memory_entries.namespace, memory_entries.key
```
because `--key "notify"` is hardcoded and the memory store does not perform an upsert. There is no `--upsert` or `--overwrite` flag available on `memory store`.

---

## Bug 6 — `SessionStart` — `memory store` (Notification hook) fails with `Database not initialized` on fresh installs

**Actual:** On a fresh project (or after a `memory init` has never been run), the `memory store` call in the Notification hook fails with:
```
[ERROR] Database not initialized. Run: claude-flow memory init
```
The `SessionStart` hook does not ensure the memory database is initialized before other hooks that depend on it run. The `Notification` hook has no fallback.

---

## Environment

| Item | Version |
|---|---|
| `@claude-flow/cli` | 3.5.2 |
| OS | macOS darwin 25.3.0 |
| Node.js | v22 |
| Claude Code | latest |
| Shell | zsh |

---

## Related Issues

- #1259 — Hook commands use relative paths (same generated hooks, different bug)
- #1261 — Obfuscated preinstall script deletes npm cache (causes `ENOTEMPTY` on hook execution via npx)
