title: Add block-no-verify to prevent AI agents from bypassing git hooks
body:
## Feature Request: Add block-no-verify to prevent AI agents from bypassing git hooks

### Problem

Ruflo is an enterprise-grade multi-agent orchestration platform with a strong security-first philosophy. The `.claude/settings.json` already has `PreToolUse` hooks for `pre-bash` handling, security scanning, and access control. One bypass vector is currently unaddressed: the git hook-skip flag.

When an AI agent (in a swarm or standalone) runs `git commit` or `git push` with the hook-bypass flag, it silently disables:
- Pre-commit hooks (linters, formatters, type-checkers)
- Commit-msg hooks (conventional commit validation)
- Pre-push hooks (test suites, CI gates)

In a 15-agent swarm context, any one agent slipping through with this flag could push unvalidated code to shared branches.

### Proposed Solution

Add `block-no-verify@1.1.2` ([github.com/tupe12334/block-no-verify](https://github.com/tupe12334/block-no-verify)) as an additional PreToolUse Bash hook entry in `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "matcher": "Bash",
  "hooks": [
    {
      "type": "command",
      "command": "npx block-no-verify@1.1.2"
    }
  ]
}
```

The package reads Claude Code's PreToolUse stdin payload, detects the hook-bypass flag across all git subcommands, and exits 2 to block. No custom scripts needed.

This closes the last git enforcement gap in an otherwise security-first hook stack.

---

_Disclosure: I am the author and maintainer of `block-no-verify`._

title: hive-mind spawn --claude prompt hardcodes wrong MCP tool prefix (mcp__claude-flow__ instead of mcp__ruflo__)
body:
## Summary

`generateHiveMindPrompt()` in `@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hive-mind.ts` hardcodes 25 MCP tool references using the legacy `mcp__claude-flow__` prefix. When Claude Code registers the ruflo MCP server, tools are exposed as `mcp__ruflo__*`. Spawned agents receive a prompt telling them to use tools that don't exist.

## Version

ruflo v3.5.41

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register the MCP server: `claude mcp add ruflo -- npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start`
2. Initialize hive-mind: `ruflo hive-mind init -t hierarchical-mesh`
3. Spawn with Claude: `ruflo hive-mind spawn -n 3 --claude -o "some task"`
4. Observe the prompt injected into the spawned Claude Code instance

## Expected Behavior

The prompt should reference `mcp__ruflo__*` tools (matching what the MCP server actually exposes to Claude Code).

## Actual Behavior

The prompt (lines 71-103 of compiled `hive-mind.js`) contains 25 hardcoded references to `mcp__claude-flow__*` tools:

```
mcp__claude-flow__hive-mind_consensus    - Democratic decision making
mcp__claude-flow__hive-mind_memory       - Share knowledge across the hive
mcp__claude-flow__task_create            - Create and delegate tasks
...
```

The spawned agent tries to call these tools but they don't exist — Claude Code only exposes `mcp__ruflo__*` tools.

## Detailed Analysis

### Wrong prefix (20 tools)

All 20 of these tools exist as `mcp__ruflo__*` but the prompt says `mcp__claude-flow__*`:

`hive-mind_consensus`, `hive-mind_memory`, `hive-mind_broadcast`, `neural_patterns`, `hive-mind_status`, `task_create`, `agent_spawn`, `agent_list`, `agent_status`, `hive-mind_join`, `hive-mind_leave`, `task_status`, `task_complete`, `workflow_create`, `memory_store`, `memory_retrieve`, `memory_search`, `neural_train`, `hooks_intelligence_pattern-store`

### Phantom tools (2 tools)

These tools are referenced in the prompt but **don't exist under any prefix**:

| Phantom tool | Closest real equivalent |
|---|---|
| `task_orchestrate` | `coordination_orchestrate` |
| `agent_metrics` | `agent_health` or `performance_metrics` |

### Duplicate

`task_create` is listed twice (sections 2 and 4 of the prompt).

### Related: `mcp-server.ts` still reports legacy name

`mcp-server.ts` (compiled `mcp-server.js` lines 255 and 333) still reports `serverInfo: { name: 'claude-flow' }` during MCP handshake. `ruflo.js` delegates MCP mode directly to `@claude-flow/cli` without overriding the server name.

## Suggested Fix

**Option A (minimal):** Replace all `mcp__claude-flow__` with `mcp__ruflo__` in the prompt template, remove phantom tools, add missing real equivalents.

**Option B (robust):** Make the prompt dynamically query available tools from the MCP server's tool registry at spawn time, instead of hardcoding tool names. This would prevent future breakage on renames.

**Option C (both):** Fix the hardcoded names now (Option A) and open a separate issue for dynamic tool discovery (Option B).

## Files to Fix

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hive-mind.ts` — `generateHiveMindPrompt()` function
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-server.ts` — `serverInfo.name` should be `'ruflo'`

title: Hive-mind worker tracking is non-functional: task lifecycle never syncs agent state
body:
## Related

Follow-up to #1391 (wrong MCP tool prefix in hive-mind prompt). This issue covers the underlying tracking pipeline that makes workers permanently show `idle` with `0` completed tasks.

## Summary

When using `hive-mind spawn --claude`, the spawned queen is instructed to coordinate virtual workers via task tools. However, **nothing connects the task system to the agent system**:

1. `task_assign` writes agent IDs to `tasks/store.json` but never updates `agents.json` → workers stay `idle` forever, `currentTask` stays `null`
2. `task_complete` marks the task done but never increments the worker's `taskCount` → `Completed` column in `rf-status` stays at `0`
3. `hive-mind_status` reports `queen.load` as `0.3 + Math.random() * 0.4` (line 266 of `hive-mind-tools.js`) — a random number, not derived from actual task state
4. `queen.tasksQueued` reads from `consensus.pending.length` instead of pending tasks

The result: `hive-mind status` always shows all workers as `idle / 0 completed` regardless of actual work done, and queen load is random noise.

## Version

ruflo v3.5.41

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
ruflo hive-mind init -t hierarchical-mesh
ruflo hive-mind spawn -n 3
# Use MCP tools:
# 1. task_create → get taskId
# 2. task_assign(taskId, [workerId])
# 3. task_complete(taskId)
# 4. Check: ruflo hive-mind status
```

## Expected Behavior

After `task_assign`, the assigned worker should show `status: active` and `currentTask: <taskId>`. After `task_complete`, the worker should return to `idle` with `taskCount` incremented. Queen load should reflect active tasks / worker count.

## Actual Behavior

Workers permanently show `idle`, `Completed: 0`, `Current Task: -`. Queen load is `Math.random()`.

## Root Cause

`task-tools.ts` and `hive-mind-tools.ts` operate on separate JSON files (`tasks/store.json` vs `agents.json`) with zero cross-references:

- `task_assign` handler (task-tools.ts ~L279-300): writes `task.assignedTo = agentIds`, saves task store. Does NOT touch agent store.
- `task_complete` handler (task-tools.ts ~L194-216): sets `task.status = 'completed'`, saves task store. Does NOT update agent `taskCount` or `status`.
- `hive-mind_status` handler (hive-mind-tools.ts ~L266): `load: 0.3 + Math.random() * 0.4`

The v2 codebase (`v2/src/hive-mind/core/HiveMind.ts`) had EventEmitter-based lifecycle events, a SwarmOrchestrator, and auto-assignment. The v3 rewrite replaced this with flat JSON CRUD that lost the cross-system linkage.

## Suggested Fix

### `task_assign` handler — sync agent state on assignment

When a task is assigned to workers:
- Set `agent.status = 'active'` and `agent.currentTask = taskId` in `agents.json`
- Auto-transition task to `in_progress` if it was `pending`
- On unassign: revert worker to `idle`

### `task_complete` handler — sync agent state on completion

When a task completes:
- Set assigned agents back to `status: 'idle'`, `currentTask: null`
- Increment `agent.taskCount`

### `hive-mind_status` handler — real metrics

Replace:
```js
load: 0.3 + Math.random() * 0.4
tasksQueued: state.consensus.pending.length
```
With:
```js
load: activeTaskCount / Math.max(1, workerCount)
tasksQueued: pendingTaskCount  // from tasks/store.json
```

### Prompt — explicit lifecycle instructions

The queen prompt (`generateHiveMindPrompt()`) should explicitly instruct: `task_create → task_assign(workerId) → [do work] → task_complete` for every subtask, with round-robin worker selection.

## Files to Fix

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/task-tools.ts` — `task_assign` and `task_complete` handlers
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/hive-mind-tools.ts` — `hive-mind_status` handler (line ~266)
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hive-mind.ts` — `generateHiveMindPrompt()` execution protocol

## Local Patch Verified

I've patched all three files locally on v3.5.41 and verified the full cycle works:
- `task_assign` → worker goes `active`, shows `currentTask`
- `task_complete` → worker returns `idle`, `Completed` increments
- Queen load shows real ratio (e.g., 33.3% = 1 active task / 3 workers)

Happy to submit a PR if the approach is acceptable.

title: [Bug] Workers always fail (stdin never closed) + daemons never terminate = kernel panic at scale
body:
#  [Bug] Workers always fail (stdin never closed) + daemons never terminate = kernel panic at scale

**Ruflo version**: 3.5.42 (latest)
**Platform**: macOS 15.7.4, Apple Silicon, 36 GB RAM
**Node.js**: 20.x

---

## Summary

Two bugs interact to cause unrecoverable memory exhaustion on machines running multiple Ruflo-enabled projects:

1. **Headless workers hang forever** — `stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']` opens stdin but never closes it; Claude Code blocks waiting for EOF until SIGTERM fires (exit 143). Every headless worker invocation fails.
2. **Daemons never terminate** — each Claude Code session spawns a new daemon with no singleton enforcement; daemons accumulate across sessions and projects.

On a 36 GB Mac with 8 Ruflo-enabled projects, this produced **9 hung `claude --print` processes at ~3 GB each + 8 daemon processes**, totalling 71 GB RSS (193% of physical RAM) and a kernel panic (`watchdog timeout: no checkins from watchdogd in 91 seconds`).

---

## Bug 1 (Critical): stdin pipe never closed — all headless workers hang forever

### Location

`headless-worker-executor.js`, line ~810

### Root cause

```js
const child = spawn('claude', ['--print', prompt], {
    cwd: this.projectRoot,
    env,
    stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],  // ← stdin opened but never written to or closed
    windowsHide: true,
});
```

`stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']` opens stdin as a writable pipe. The code never calls `child.stdin.end()` or `child.stdin.destroy()`, and never writes to it. Claude Code's `--print` mode reads stdin as part of startup and blocks waiting for EOF that never arrives.

Every invocation hangs silently until the SIGTERM timeout fires (5 min for `audit`, 10–15 min for `optimize`/`testgaps`), producing exit code 143 and empty output.

### Evidence

68 worker executions across one project, all failures:

| Worker | Runs | Successes | Failure rate | Exit code |
|--------|------|-----------|--------------|-----------|
| `audit` | 30 | 0 (0%) | 100% | 143 (SIGTERM) |
| `optimize` | 22 | 1 (5%) | 95% | 143 (SIGTERM) |
| `testgaps` | 17 | 0 (0%) | 100% | 143 (SIGTERM) |

### Fix

Change line ~810 from:
```js
stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']
```
to:
```js
stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
```

This is a one-character change. `'ignore'` closes stdin at spawn, allowing `--print` mode to proceed immediately.

---

## Bug 2 (Critical): Workers cannot run inside an active Claude Code session

### Root cause

`optimize` and `testgaps` spawn `claude --print` as a subprocess. Claude Code detects an existing session and immediately exits with:

```
Claude Code cannot be launched inside another Claude Code session.
```

Since the daemon runs while Claude Code is active (the normal use case), these workers **can never succeed during normal use** regardless of any configuration.

### Fix options

1. Use the Anthropic SDK directly for LLM calls in workers instead of spawning `claude --print`
2. Provide a `--worker` flag or `CLAUDE_FLOW_WORKER=1` env var that bypasses the nested-session check
3. At minimum: disable these workers by default and document the limitation

---

## Bug 3 (High): Daemons never terminate — accumulate across sessions and projects

### Root cause

No PID singleton enforcement. Each new Claude Code session in each project spawns a fresh daemon process. Daemons do not exit when the session ends. Over multiple sessions across multiple projects, daemons accumulate indefinitely.

**Observed**: 8 simultaneous daemon processes (one per project directory), each consuming ~650 MB. Combined with hung headless worker processes from Bug 1, total RSS reached 71 GB on a 36 GB machine.

### Fix

Standard PID-file singleton pattern:
1. On `daemon start`, check for an existing PID file
2. If the recorded PID is alive (`kill -0 $PID`), skip start
3. If dead, clean the PID file and start fresh
4. Write PID file on start; delete on clean exit

---

## Bug 4 (High): `config.yaml` silently ignored — daemon reads only `config.json`

### Root cause

`claude-flow init` generates `config.yaml`. The daemon reads only `config.json`. Projects that have `config.yaml` but no `config.json` run entirely on hardcoded defaults with no warning — `daemon.autoStart`, worker intervals, and resource thresholds are all silently bypassed.

### Fix

Either support `config.yaml` in the daemon, or emit a warning when `config.yaml` exists but `config.json` does not.

---

## Bug 5 (Medium): `memory store/search` broken — ID type mismatch and dimension mismatch

### Root cause

Two separate issues in `memory-initializer.js`:

1. **ID type mismatch**: `storeEntry()` generates text IDs for a column declared `INTEGER AUTOINCREMENT`. Downstream code calls `.substring()` on those IDs, throwing TypeError when the value is numeric.
2. **Vector dimension mismatch**: Dimensions hardcoded to 1536 (OpenAI Ada) instead of 384 (actual `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` output). Cosine similarity comparisons between mismatched vectors produce meaningless results.

### Fix

1. Remove text ID generation — let SQLite assign integer IDs via autoincrement
2. Change hardcoded 1536 to 384, or detect dimension from the loaded model at runtime

---

## Bug 6 (Medium): Orphan processes from daemon/executor timeout mismatch

### Root cause

The daemon wrapper timeout (5 min) fires before the headless executor's internal timeout (5–15 min). When the wrapper rejects the promise, the `claude --print` child process keeps running as an orphan until the executor's own timeout fires. The daemon considers the worker "done" while the process is still consuming memory.

### Fix

Either raise `DEFAULT_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS` in the wrapper to `executor_timeout + 60s`, or send SIGTERM to the child process group when the wrapper timeout fires rather than just rejecting the promise.

---

## Priority order

| # | Bug | Severity | Fix effort |
|---|-----|----------|------------|
| 1 | stdin pipe never closed | Critical | Trivial (one character) |
| 2 | Workers fail inside Claude Code session | Critical | Medium |
| 3 | Daemons never terminate | High | Low–Medium |
| 4 | config.yaml silently ignored | High | Low |
| 5 | memory store/search broken | Medium | Medium |
| 6 | Orphan processes from timeout mismatch | Medium | Low |

Bug 1 is the blocking fix — it unblocks all headless worker functionality and is a single-character change. Bugs 1 + 3 together caused the kernel panic.

title: [Maintenance] Reduce repository size by cleaning up large binary/build artifacts from git history
body:
Hi maintainers,

Thank you for the awesome work! While exploring the codebase, I noticed that the `.git` directory and some subdirectories (especially the `v2/` folder) are extremely bloated. A local analysis shows that the `.git` folder alone is close to **500MB**.

Git repositories usually shouldn't track raw executables, large binary release archives, or machine learning model files, as these exponentially increase the cloning time and bloat the `.git/objects` history for all contributors.

### Problematic files currently taking up the most space:

I ran a quick script (`git rev-list --objects --all`) to analyze the repo size. The following heavy files are found in the history and current tree that shouldn't be tracked:

**1. Compiled Binaries and Release Archives (TGZ)**
These should ideally be hosted in GitHub Releases instead of the source tree:
- `bin/claude-flow` (~84MB)
- `bin/claude-flow-node-pkg` (~46MB)
- Multiple `claude-flow-X.X.X.tgz` files (e.g., `claude-flow-2.0.0-alpha.83.tgz`, `claude-flow-1.0.70.tgz`, each around ~60MB)

**2. Machine Learning Model Weights (`v2/` dir)**
Large `.onnx` models should be hosted externally (e.g., huggingface, S3, or LFS):
- `v2/models/phi-4-mini/cpu_and_mobile/cpu-int4-rtn-block-32-acc-level-4/model.onnx` (~52MB)
- `v2/models/phi-4-mini/cpu_and_mobile/cpu-int4-rtn-block-32-acc-level-4/model.onnx.data` (~44MB)

**3. Database Backups and Memory dumps**
These data dumps update frequently and bloat history quickly:
- `v2/docs/reasoningbank/models/safla/memory.db.backup` (~10MB)
- `v2/docs/reasoningbank/models/google-research/memory.db.backup` (~9MB)
- `vendor/ruvector/.claude/intelligence/data/memory.json` (~15MB)

**4. Compiled Node/WASM extensions (`vendor/`)**
- `vendor/ruvector/npm/core/platforms/*/ruvector.node` (multiple, ~6MB each)
- `vendor/ruvector/.../ruvector_onnx_embeddings_wasm_bg.wasm` (~7MB)

### Suggested Fixes:

1. Use a tool like **`git filter-repo`** (or BFG Repo-Cleaner) to completely scrub these large files (`*.tgz`, `.onnx`, large `.bin`, database backups) from the git history. 
2. Add these file extensions/folders to the `.gitignore` to prevent them from being committed again.
3. Move binary distribution/releases to the GitHub Releases page instead of checking them into `master` / `main`. 
4. If the `.onnx` models are strictly required to be available at clone time, consider using **Git LFS**.

title: Swarm agents still do not execute work — v3.5.42 (@claude-flow/cli@latest)
body:
Swarm agents still do not execute work — v3.5.42 (@claude-flow/cli@latest)

  The state-tracking fix from this issue was correctly applied — task_assign now transitions
  tasks to in_progress. However, agents never execute the assigned work. The fundamental issue
  is that no execution engine exists: MCP tools perform JSON CRUD on registry files, but
  nothing spawns a Claude subprocess to read the task description and act on it.

  Environment

  - Package: @claude-flow/cli@latest (npm version 3.5.42, internal version string 10.8.2)
  - Platform: macOS Darwin 24.6.0
  - Client: Claude Code (Opus 4.6)
  - MCP config: autoStart: false in .mcp.json

  Test 1 — Full swarm via MCP tools (first session)

  swarm_init → topology: hierarchical, strategy: specialized, maxAgents: 8
    ✅ Success: swarm-1774027567036-4ozd3b

  agent_spawn × 7 (architect, backend, frontend, manual-qa, tester, reviewer, qa)
    ✅ All spawned, status: "idle", health: 1

  swarm_health:
    ✅ status: "healthy"
    ❌ agentCount: 0  ← agents not registered in swarm scope despite 7 spawned

  task_create (type: feature, priority: critical, assignTo: ["dashboard-map-architect"])
    ✅ taskId: task-1774027636063-dkvwp5, status: "pending"

  Poll results (every 15s for 60s):

  Poll 1 (0s):   task=pending  agent=idle  taskCount=0  currentTask=null
  Poll 2 (15s):  task=pending  agent=idle  taskCount=0  currentTask=null
  Poll 3 (30s):  task=pending  agent=idle  taskCount=0  currentTask=null
  Poll 4 (45s):  task=pending  agent=idle  taskCount=0  currentTask=null

  Stuck detected at 60s. Attempted recovery:

  task_assign(taskId, ["dashboard-map-architect"])
    ✅ Task status changed: pending → in_progress (the #1392 fix works for tracking)
    ✅ startedAt populated: 2026-03-20T17:29:12.065Z
    ❌ Agent still idle, taskCount still 0

  30s after re-assign:

  task=in_progress  progress=0  agent=idle  taskCount=0

  No files created. No reasoning happened. Aborted.

  Test 2 — CLI swarm start (same session)

  Tested the v2-documented CLI approach:

  $ claude-flow swarm start -o "write hello.txt" -s development

  [INFO] Starting swarm with objective: write hello.txt

  Agent Deployment Plan
  +-------------+-------------+-------+----------------------+
  | Role        | Type        | Count | Purpose              |
  +-------------+-------------+-------+----------------------+
  | Coordinator | coordinator |     1 | Orchestrate workflow |
  | Architect   | architect   |     1 | System design        |
  | Coder       | coder       |     3 | Implementation       |
  | Tester      | tester      |     2 | Quality assurance    |
  | Reviewer    | reviewer    |     1 | Code review          |
  +-------------+-------------+-------+----------------------+

  [OK] Swarm execution started
    Monitor: claude-flow swarm status swarm-mmz6o5ij

  $ claude-flow swarm status swarm-mmz6o5ij

  Swarm Status: swarm-mmz6o5ij
  Overall Progress: [##--------------------------------------] 5.0%

  Agents:    Active: 0  Idle: 0  Completed: 0  Total: 0
  Tasks:     Completed: 0  In Progress: 0  Pending: 0  Total: 0
  Tokens Used: 0

  Same result — agents "deployed" but 0 active, 0 tasks, 0 tokens. hello.txt never created.

  Test 3 — Fresh session POC (new Claude session, clean MCP server)

  Exited Claude entirely, started a new session to rule out stale MCP state:

  swarm_init → topology: mesh, strategy: balanced, maxAgents: 2
    ✅ swarm-1774028539625-xa6vy4

  agent_spawn (agentId: "poc-worker", type: coder, model: haiku)
    ✅ status: "spawned"

  task_create (description: "Create poc-test.txt containing 'swarm test passed'", assignTo:
  ["poc-worker"])
    ✅ taskId: task-1774028552187-3dlgkj, status: "pending"

  Immediate poll:

  task:  status=pending  progress=0  startedAt=null
  agent: status=idle  taskCount=0
  swarm: agentCount=0  ← still 0 despite agent spawned

  After 15s:

  task:  status=pending  progress=0  startedAt=null  (no change)
  agent: status=idle  taskCount=0  (no change)

  $ ls poc-test.txt
  ls: poc-test.txt: No such file or directory

  Identical behavior across fresh session. Not a caching/session issue.

  Diagnosis

  ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │           What            │  Status   │                     Detail                     │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ agent_spawn creates agent │ ✅ Works  │ Writes to agents.json                          │
  │  record                   │           │                                                │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ task_create creates task  │ ✅ Works  │ Writes to tasks/store.json                     │
  │ record                    │           │                                                │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ task_assign links task →  │ ✅ Works  │ Sets task.assignedTo, transitions to           │
  │ agent                     │           │ in_progress (#1392 fix)                        │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Agent transitions to      │ ❌ Broken │ Agent stays idle, taskCount: 0                 │
  │ active                    │           │                                                │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Swarm sees spawned agents │ ❌ Broken │ swarm_health shows agentCount: 0               │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Agent reads task and      │ ❌        │ No subprocess spawned, no file I/O, no         │
  │ executes                  │ Missing   │ reasoning                                      │
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ CLI swarm start executes  │ ❌        │ Same metadata-only pattern                     │
  │ work                      │ Missing   │                                                │
  └───────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Root cause

  The v3 rewrite replaced the v2 execution engine (SwarmOrchestrator + EventEmitter lifecycle +
   subprocess management) with flat JSON CRUD. The MCP tools manage coordination metadata but
  nothing consumes that metadata to dispatch work:

  1. agent_spawn → writes { agentId, status: "idle" } to agents.json
  2. task_create → writes { taskId, status: "pending", assignedTo } to tasks/store.json
  3. task_assign → updates both records (the #1392 fix)
  4. Missing step: nothing reads the task queue, matches assigned agents, and launches a Claude
   subprocess to execute the task description

  The v2 docs (v2/docs/reference/SWARM.md) describe claude-flow swarm execute "task" which
  presumably triggered the SwarmOrchestrator. The v3 CLI has swarm start but it only writes
  metadata — the orchestrator was not ported.

  What #1392 fixed vs what's still broken

  - Fixed: task_assign now correctly cross-references tasks/store.json ↔ agents.json (status
  transitions, startedAt population)
  - Still broken: No execution engine — agents are database rows, not running processes

  Suggestion

  The v3 MCP tools need a task consumer/dispatcher that:
  1. Watches the task store for pending/in_progress tasks with assigned agents
  2. Launches a real Claude subprocess (via claude CLI or API) with the task description as the
   prompt
  3. Updates agent status to active while the subprocess runs
  4. Captures output and marks task completed when the subprocess finishes

  Alternatively, document that the MCP tools are a coordination layer only and that execution
  must be handled externally (e.g., by Claude Code's Agent tool reading task descriptions from
  the store).

title: AgentDB bridge unavailable — traced to CLI bundling @claude-flow/memory@alpha.11 (missing ControllerRegistry)
body:
Hey — love the project and have been building heavily on claude-flow. I'm working on a multi-project knowledge management system that uses the `memory_*` tools extensively (and they work great). I'd love to get the `agentdb_*` tools working too for hierarchical recall and pattern search.

I commented on #1264 a few days ago but realized that was closed, so filing fresh with everything I've found. Happy to help test any fixes.

### What I'm trying to do

Use the `agentdb_*` MCP tools (`hierarchical-recall`, `pattern-search`, etc.) alongside the `memory_*` tools. All `agentdb_*` calls currently return `{ available: false, error: "Bridge not available" }`.

### What I've tried

1. Updated project's `@claude-flow/memory` to `3.0.0-alpha.12` (which exports `ControllerRegistry`)
2. Verified `agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.10` resolves correctly in project `node_modules`
3. Ran `doctor` — 11 passed, 3 expected warnings, no actionable items
4. Checked config, env vars, lock file, MCP server setup — all clean
5. Searched for any init flag or manual bridge activation — none exists
6. Tried direct `require()` of the controller paths from Node REPL

### What I found

The issue traces to three things, all in the published packages:

**1. CLI bundles the pre-fix memory package**

`@claude-flow/cli@3.5.42` (via npx) bundles `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.11` in its dependency tree. The bridge code in `memory-bridge.js` does:

```js
const { ControllerRegistry } = await import('@claude-flow/memory');
```

ESM resolution starts from the importer's location (the npx cache), so it resolves to the cached `alpha.11` — not the project-local `alpha.12`. Since `alpha.11` doesn't export `ControllerRegistry`, the import fails silently and the bridge never initializes.

**2. Runtime patch targets v1.x path**

`agentdb-runtime-patch.js` (in `agentic-flow`) looks for controllers at `dist/controllers/index.js`, but agentdb v3 puts them at `dist/src/controllers/index.js`. The file header references "agentdb v1.3.9" — looks like this just hasn't been updated for the v3 layout.

**3. agentdb CJS wrapper has a path issue**

`agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.10`'s `dist/src/controllers/index.cjs` does `require('./controllers/index.js')`, which resolves to `dist/src/controllers/controllers/index.js` (doesn't exist). Likely should be `require('./index.js')`.

### Suggested fix

I think the primary fix is updating the CLI's dependency on `@claude-flow/memory` to `>=3.0.0-alpha.12` and publishing a new CLI version. That would let `memory-bridge.js` find `ControllerRegistry` and initialize the bridge.

The runtime patch path (#2) and CJS wrapper (#3) would be nice to clean up but may not be blocking if #1 is resolved — the `ControllerRegistry` in alpha.12 likely handles controller loading through its own path resolution.

### Environment

- `@claude-flow/cli`: 3.5.42 (via npx)
- `@claude-flow/memory` (npx cache): 3.0.0-alpha.11
- `@claude-flow/memory` (project): 3.0.0-alpha.12
- `agentdb` (project): 3.0.0-alpha.10
- Node: v24.6.0
- macOS ARM64 (Darwin 25.3.0)

Happy to verify a fix once it's published. Thanks for all the work on this!

title: MCP tool schema: array type missing 'items' causes validation error in VSCode Copilot chat
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

Several MCP tool definitions in `ruvllm-tools.js` declare `type: 'array'` without an `items` property, which is invalid JSON Schema. VSCode Copilot chat's MCP client validates schemas strictly and rejects the entire MCP server with:

> Error al validar la herramienta mcp_ruflo_ruvllm_chat_format: Error: tool parameters array type must have items.

Claude Code's MCP client is more lenient and loads the tools fine, but VSCode Copilot chat does not.

### Affected files and lines

**`node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/ruvllm-tools.js`**

- `embedding` (line ~64): `{ type: 'array', description: 'Float array embedding vector' }` → missing `items: { type: 'number' }`
- `query` (line ~94): `{ type: 'array', description: 'Query embedding vector' }` → missing `items: { type: 'number' }`
- `messages` (line ~229): `{ type: 'array', ... }` → missing or incomplete `items`
- `stopSequences` (line ~265): `{ type: 'array', description: 'Stop sequences' }` → missing `items: { type: 'string' }`

### Fix

Add `items` to every `type: 'array'` property in all MCP tool definitions. For example:

```js
// Before
embedding: { type: 'array', description: 'Float array embedding vector' }

// After
embedding: { type: 'array', description: 'Float array embedding vector', items: { type: 'number' } }
```

### Environment

- Ruflo version: latest (npm)
- VSCode version: latest
- Platform: Windows 10

title: Hive-mind spawn uses Claude native tools instead of Ruflo MCP orchestration
body: ## Observed Behavior When running `ruflo spawn hive-mind --claude`, the spawned Claude Code session uses **Claude's native Agent/Task tools** for multi-agent orchestration instead of Ruflo's own MCP tools (`mcp__ruflo__agent_spawn`, `mcp__ruflo__task_create`, `mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_*`, etc.). ### Screenshots #### Screenshot 1: Claude native `Agent` tool spawning researchers Claude spawns 5 research agents using its built-in `Agent` tool (researcher, Explore subtypes), all "Running in the background" — none of these go through Ruflo's MCP agent orchestration. #### Screenshot 2: RuFlo V3 status bar active but tasks use Claude native tools The RuFlo V3 status bar is visible at the bottom (branch, context, model info), but the actual task breakdown (Feature 1-4, Documentation) is managed by Claude Code's native task system, not by Ruflo's `mcp__ruflo__task_create` / `mcp__ruflo__task_assign`. ## Questions / Concerns 1. **Is this by design?** When `ruflo spawn hive-mind --claude` launches a Claude Code session, does Ruflo expect Claude to use Ruflo's MCP tools for orchestration? Or is Ruflo only providing the MCP tools as *available* options that Claude may or may not choose? 2. **Tool priority conflict**: Claude Code has its own built-in `Agent` tool, `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` tools, and background agent capabilities. These overlap with Ruflo's `mcp__ruflo__agent_spawn`, `mcp__ruflo__task_create`, `mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_broadcast`, etc. Claude appears to **always prefer its native tools** over Ruflo's MCP equivalents — likely because the native tools are listed first and have tighter integration. 3. **Is Ruflo's orchestration more capable?** Ruflo's MCP tools offer features that Claude's native tools don't: - Hive-mind consensus (`mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_consensus`) - Byzantine fault tolerance - Shared memory across agents (`mcp__ruflo__memory_store/retrieve`) - Agent health monitoring (`mcp__ruflo__agent_health`) - Hierarchical-mesh topology coordination - Neural pattern learning (`mcp__ruflo__neural_*`) If these are genuinely more powerful for multi-agent coordination, they're being silently bypassed in favor of Claude's simpler native tools. 4. **Can Ruflo enforce its own tool usage?** Options: - System prompt injection that tells Claude to prefer `mcp__ruflo__*` tools for agent/task management - CLAUDE.md instructions that map operations to Ruflo MCP tools - Disabling/hiding Claude's native `Agent`/`TaskCreate` tools when Ruflo orchestration is active - Or accept that Claude's native tools are sufficient and Ruflo's MCP tools serve a different purpose (coordination metadata, memory, consensus) rather than replacing Claude's execution model ## Environment - ruflo (claude-flow) v3 via `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest` - Claude Code CLI (Opus 4.6) - MCP server registered via `claude mcp add ruflo` ## Expected Behavior Either: - Ruflo's hive-mind mode should instruct Claude to use Ruflo's MCP tools for agent spawning and task management, OR - Documentation should clarify that Ruflo's MCP tools are supplementary (memory, consensus, monitoring) while Claude's native tools handle execution

title: Add IDE integration layer and distributed memory federation for Ruflo v4
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces two major new subsystems for Ruflo v4:

1. **IDE Integration Layer** (`@claude-flow/ide`) — Integrations with Antigravity, Cursor, cloud IDEs (Gitpod/Codespaces/StackBlitz), VSCode LSP, and anti-gravity git worktrees for isolated agent workspaces.

2. **Distributed Memory Federation** (`@claude-flow/memory-federation`) — A complete federated memory system using CRDTs, gossip protocol, consistent hashing, and peer discovery for distributed AgentDB across multiple machines.

Additionally, enhancements to existing v3 modules improve embedding batching, graph caching, and neural backend GPU detection.

## Key Changes

### New Packages

**`@claude-flow/ide`** — IDE integration layer with:
- **LSP Server** (`lsp-server.ts`) — Wraps TypeScript Language Server to provide live diagnostics, hover info, and file tracking to Ruflo agents via MCP resources
- **Antigravity Integration** — Mission Control sync, MCP bridge, memory injector, guidance overlay, and worktree adapter for agent lifecycle synchronization
- **Cursor Integration** — MCP bridge for Cursor IDE configuration
- **Cloud IDE Support** — Dev container bridge for Gitpod, GitHub Codespaces, and StackBlitz
- **Workspace Management** — Worktree manager for per-agent isolated git branches and merge coordinator for conflict resolution
- **Governance** — Cursor rules generator and guidance overlay to sync Ruflo constitution with IDE configs
- **File System Watching** — Cross-platform file watcher with security and test trigger detection

**`@claude-flow/memory-federation`** — Distributed federated memory with:
- **Consistent Hashing** (`hash-ring.ts`) — FNV-1a based hash ring with virtual nodes for minimal rebalancing
- **Shard Routing** (`shard-router.ts`) — Routes reads/writes to correct peer with read-your-writes consistency via sticky sessions
- **Gossip Protocol** (`gossip-protocol.ts`) — Anti-entropy sync via UDP datagrams with version vectors and deduplication
- **Peer Discovery** — mDNS peer discovery (`mdns-peer.ts`) and STUN NAT traversal (`stun-traversal.ts`) for LAN and WAN
- **CRDTs** — LWW Register (`lww-register.ts`) with Hybrid Logical Clock and OR-Set (`or-set.ts`) for conflict-free replication
- **Version Vectors** (`version-vector.ts`) — Causal ordering and concurrency detection
- **Federation Service** (`federation-service.ts`) — Top-level orchestrator tying all components together

### Enhanced Existing Modules

**`v3/@claude-flow/memory`**:
- `batch-embedder.ts` — New batching wrapper to reduce ONNX inference overhead on bulk inserts
- `memory-graph.ts` — Added LRU cache for PageRank scores and incremental mutation support
- `hybrid-backend.ts` — Added two-phase commit coordinator with WAL (write-ahead log) for SQLite/AgentDB sync

**`v3/@claude-flow/neural`**:
- `flash-attention.ts` — New GPU backend detection for Flash Attention 2 (CUDA, Metal, WebGPU)
- `sona-integration.ts` — Integrated Flash Attention detection into SONA learning engine
- `types.ts` — Added `enableFlashAttention` config option

**`v3/@claude-flow/hooks`**:
- `event-bus.ts` — New reactive event-driven worker trigger system with fallback idle timers
- `workers/index.ts` — Exported event bus for worker event subscriptions

## Notable Implementation Details

- **LSP Server** uses JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol with request/response correlation and timeout handling
- **Gossip Protocol** uses UDP with chunking for payloads >60KB and deduplication via message IDs
- **Consistent Hash Ring** uses FNV-1a 32-bit hashing with 150 virtual

```

## Additional bugs observed in the same run

1. **ONNX model loaded twice** — `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (23MB) is downloaded and initialized twice during a single `memory init` call
2. **Broken dependency path** — on every run: `[AgentDB Patch] Controller index not found: ...agentic-flow/node_modules/agentdb/dist/controllers/index.js`
3. **1 of 5 AgentDB controllers failed to activate** — `Activated: 4  Failed: 1`

## Root cause hypothesis
ONNX Runtime spawns worker threads that are never terminated. The SQLite connection may also not be closed. The process has no explicit `process.exit()` call after completing `memory init`, so active handles keep the event loop alive.

## Workaround
`Ctrl+C` after `Synced to:` message appears — the database is fully initialized at that point.

title: Headless daemon workers use stale/nonexistent model IDs
body:
## Bug

`@claude-flow/cli@3.5.42` (ruflo 3.5.42) — the headless worker daemon has hardcoded model IDs in `headless-worker-executor.js` (line 53) that no longer exist:

```js
const MODEL_IDS = {
    sonnet: 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929',
    opus: 'claude-opus-4-6',
    haiku: 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001',
};
```

- `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` → not available on foundry deployments
- `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` → does not exist

## Impact

All 3 enabled headless workers (`audit`, `optimize`, `testgaps`) fail 100% of the time with:

```
There's an issue with the selected model (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). It may not exist or you may not have access to it.
```

Each failed run still takes ~89 seconds spawning/killing the `claude` CLI process. With default intervals (10-20 min), that's ~120 wasted process spawns per day.

The daemon has been running since Mar 24, accumulating 55 audit runs (9 fails), 40 optimize runs (7 fails), 25 testgaps runs (5 fails) — all recent runs failing since models expired.

## Expected fix

1. **Update `MODEL_IDS`** to current model IDs:
   - `sonnet` → `claude-sonnet-4-6` (or latest)
   - `haiku` → `claude-haiku-4-5` (or latest)

2. **Add config override for model IDs** — currently `daemon-state.json` only controls `enabled`/`intervalMs` per worker. There's no way to override `model` without patching `node_modules`. Suggested: allow `model` field in worker config, or read `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` env var as fallback.

3. **Consider using model aliases** (`sonnet`, `haiku`, `opus`) instead of dated snapshot IDs, so they auto-resolve to the latest version.

## Reproduction

```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest daemon start
# Wait 2 minutes for audit worker to trigger
# Check: .claude-flow/logs/headless/audit_*_result.log
```

## Environment

- ruflo: 3.5.42
- @claude-flow/cli: 3.5.42
- Claude Code: latest
- macOS Darwin 25.3.0

title: fix: close stdin pipe on headless workers and force exit after CLI commands
body:
## Summary

Two related process lifecycle bugs that cause resource exhaustion:

- **#1395 (stdin pipe never closed)**: Headless workers spawn `claude --print` with `stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']` but never write to or close stdin. Claude Code blocks waiting for EOF, causing 100% worker failure rate (exit 143 after SIGTERM timeout). Combined with no daemon singleton enforcement, this caused kernel panic on a 36 GB Mac with 8 projects.

  **Fix**: Change `'pipe'` to `'ignore'` for stdin — one-character change that provides immediate EOF.

- **#1428 (memory init hangs)**: All `memory` subcommands hang after completion because ONNX Runtime worker threads and open SQLite handles keep the Node.js event loop alive. The CLI runner only calls `process.exit()` on failure, not success.

  **Fix**: Add `process.exit(0)` after successful command execution in the CLI runner, since CLI commands are one-shot operations.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/headless-worker-executor.ts:1128` | `stdio: ['pipe'` → `['ignore'` |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/index.ts:244` | Add `process.exit(0)` after successful command |

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx ruflo memory init` should exit cleanly after "Synced to:" message
- [ ] `npx ruflo memory store -k test --value test` should exit cleanly
- [ ] `npx ruflo daemon start` → headless workers should no longer exit with code 143
- [ ] `npm run build` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/`

Closes #1395, Closes #1428

title: EPIC: Autopilot Persistent Completion Integration (ADR-072)
body:
## Epic: Autopilot Persistent Completion Integration

**ADR**: [ADR-072](../blob/feat/implement-stub-commands/v3/implementation/adrs/ADR-072-autopilot-persistent-completion.md)
**Priority**: High
**Estimated Effort**: 8-9 hours across 5 phases

## Problem

Claude Code agents and swarms routinely stop at 60-80% completion, requiring manual "continue" prompts. Complex multi-phase tasks (implement + test + docs + review) need 2-4 manual interventions to reach 100%.

## Solution

Integrate agentic-flow's **Autopilot Persistent Completion System** (ADR-058) into `@claude-flow/cli`:
- **Stop hook interception** — Detect incomplete tasks when agents try to stop
- **Re-engagement** — Re-inject remaining task context with learned patterns
- **Learning** — Record completion/failure episodes via AgentDB for predictive improvement
- **Safety limits** — Max iterations (50), timeout (4hr), stall detection, manual kill

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 5: agentic-flow Export Fix (30 min) — DO FIRST
- [ ] Re-export `AutopilotLearning` from `coordination/index.ts`
- [ ] Re-export `registerAutopilotTools` from `mcp/fastmcp/tools/index.ts`
- [ ] Re-export `handleAutopilotCommand` from `cli/index.ts`
- [ ] Add `./autopilot`, `./autopilot/cli`, `./autopilot/mcp` to package.json exports
- [ ] Publish `agentic-flow@3.0.0-alpha.3`

### Phase 1: CLI Command (2 hr)
- [ ] Create `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/autopilot.ts` with 9 subcommands
- [ ] Subcommands: `status`, `enable`, `disable`, `config`, `reset`, `log`, `learn`, `history`, `predict`
- [ ] Register in `commands/index.ts`
- [ ] Write unit tests

### Phase 2: MCP Tools (2 hr)
- [ ] Create `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/autopilot-tools.ts` with 10 tools
- [ ] Tools: `autopilot_status`, `autopilot_enable`, `autopilot_disable`, `autopilot_config`, `autopilot_reset`, `autopilot_log`, `autopilot_progress`, `autopilot_learn`, `autopilot_history`, `autopilot_predict`
- [ ] Register in `mcp-tools/index.ts` and `mcp-client.ts`
- [ ] Write unit tests

### Phase 3: Stop Hook Integration (3 hr) — CRITICAL
- [ ] Create `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/hooks/autopilot-stop-hook.ts`
- [ ] Implement 3-source task discovery (team tasks, swarm tasks, file checklist)
- [ ] Implement re-engagement prompt builder with learning context
- [ ] Implement stall detection (5 iterations no progress -> warn, 10 -> disable)
- [ ] Integrate with `AutopilotLearning` for episode recording + SONA trajectory
- [ ] Register Stop hook in settings.json via init
- [ ] Write integration tests

### Phase 4: CLAUDE.md + Init Injection (1 hr)
- [ ] Update `init/executor.ts` to inject autopilot config into `.claude/settings.json`
- [ ] Update CLAUDE.md template with autopilot behavioral instructions
- [ ] Ensure `init --wizard` offers autopilot configuration

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npx claude-flow autopilot status` returns state
- [ ] `npx claude-flow autopilot enable/disable` toggles persistent completion
- [ ] `npx claude-flow autopilot config --max-iterations 100` persists to settings
- [ ] All 10 MCP tools respond correctly via MCP client
- [ ] Stop hook intercepts agent stop and re-engages when tasks remain
- [ ] Stop hook allows stop when all tasks are complete
- [ ] Stop hook respects max iterations and timeout limits
- [ ] AgentDB learning records episodes and discovers patterns
- [ ] `npx claude-flow autopilot predict` returns actionable recommendations
- [ ] Stall detection triggers after 5 iterations with no progress
- [ ] All existing tests pass (no regressions)

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Three task sources**: Team tasks, swarm tasks, checklists
2. **Reward formula**: `(1 - iters/(iters+10)) * 0.6 + (1 - min(durationMs/3600000, 1)) * 0.4`
3. **Graceful degradation**: Works without AgentDB (no learning, still completes)
4. **Re-engagement is prompt-only**: Never executes commands, only injects continuation prompt
5. **Stall detection**: 5 iterations no progress -> warn, 10 -> auto-disable

- ADR-058: Autopilot Swarm Completion (agentic-flow)
- ADR-037: Autopilot Chat Mode (Ruflo UI)
- ADR-071: Guidance MCP Tools

title: fix(cli): process.exit at entry point to prevent ONNX event loop hang
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1428 — `ruflo memory init`, `ruflo memory stats`, and other memory subcommands hang indefinitely after completing because ONNX/WASM worker threads (from `@xenova/transformers` / `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) keep the Node.js event loop alive.

### Root cause

When any memory subcommand calls `callMCPTool()`, it triggers `ensureInitialized()` in `memory-tools.ts`, which loads the ONNX embedding model. The ONNX runtime spawns worker threads that are never terminated, preventing Node.js from exiting naturally.

### Why the fix is in `bin/cli.js` and not in `initMemoryCommand`

The original inline fix (removed in this PR) placed a `setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 500).unref()` inside `initMemoryCommand`. This was wrong for several reasons:

1. **Only fixed one command.** Every memory subcommand (`stats`, `store`, `search`, `list`, `cleanup`, `compress`, etc.) triggers the same ONNX load via `ensureInitialized()`, so every one of them hangs. Fixing them individually means 20+ call sites, each a maintenance burden and a place to forget.

2. **Commands shouldn't call `process.exit()`.** A command's `action` function is a library method — it returns a result object (`{ success, data }`) to its caller. Calling `process.exit()` inside it breaks testability (unit tests mock `process.exit` and the mock throws, failing the test) and violates separation of concerns. The command doesn't know if it's being called from a CLI binary, a test harness, or programmatic API usage.

3. **The entry point is the right place.** `bin/cli.js` is the actual process boundary — it creates the `CLI` instance, calls `cli.run()`, and is responsible for process lifecycle. Adding `.then(() => process.exit(0))` here means:
   - All commands benefit (memory, neural, or any future command that loads ONNX)
   - `CLI.run()` stays a pure library method that tests can `await` without side effects
   - The existing 32 unit tests continue to pass unchanged

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `bin/cli.js` | Added `process.exit(0)` in `.then()` after `cli.run()` resolves |
| `src/commands/memory.ts` | Removed the original inline `setTimeout/process.exit` hack from `initMemoryCommand` |

### Testing

```bash
# Before fix: hangs until killed
timeout 10 node bin/cli.js memory stats   # exit 124 (timeout)

# After fix: exits immediately
timeout 10 node bin/cli.js memory stats   # exit 0
```

Unit tests: 32 passed, 1 skipped (unchanged from baseline).

title: Windows: Daemon headless workers return empty output, breaking token optimization
body:
## Summary

RuFlo's core token optimization loop (daemon → headless workers → model routing) doesn't function on Windows because `claude -p` headless workers return empty output text. This makes the advertised 30-50% token savings unachievable on Windows installations.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- **Node.js:** v24.13.1 (installed at `C:\Program Files\nodejs\`)
- **Claude Code:** 2.1.84
- **RuFlo:** v3.5.48 (via npx)

## Issues Found

### 1. Daemon crashes on startup (ENOENT with spaced paths)

When `process.execPath` is `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`, the daemon's `spawn()` with `detached: true` fails with ENOENT because the space in "Program Files" breaks the path. The daemon log shows:

```
'C:\Program' is not recognized as an internal or external command
```

**Root cause:** `daemon.js` uses `spawn(process.execPath, args, { detached: true })` which fails on Windows when the executable path contains spaces.

**Workaround applied:** Use Windows 8.3 short path (`C:\PROGRA~1\nodejs\node.exe`) to avoid spaces entirely.

### 2. Daemon dies immediately in detached mode (event loop drain)

Even after fixing the path issue, the daemon process exits within 1-2 seconds when spawned in detached/quiet mode. The `await new Promise(() => {})` on its own does not keep the Node.js event loop alive when there's no active I/O.

**Root cause:** In `daemon.js` quiet mode branch:
```js
await startDaemon(projectRoot, config);
await new Promise(() => { }); // This alone doesn't prevent event loop exit
```

**Fix:** Add `setInterval(() => {}, 60000)` before the promise to create an active timer handle.

### 3. Headless workers return empty output (core issue)

When the daemon IS running, headless workers spawn `claude --print` but the stdout result is empty. The workers complete without error but produce no useful output. This is the blocking issue for token optimization.

**Location:** `headless-worker-executor.js` — the `spawn(claudeBin, ['--print'], ...)` with stdin pipe approach produces empty stdout on Windows even though the process exits with code 0.

### 4. `ruflo status` always shows STOPPED

The CLI `status` command calls `callMCPTool('swarm_status', ...)` through its own MCP client, which can't connect to the MCP server instance that Claude Code is using (stdio transport). So `ruflo status` always reports STOPPED even when the MCP system is fully healthy.

## Impact

The token optimization features (model routing, AgentBooster, ReasoningBank caching, batching) all depend on headless workers functioning. Without them:
- Model routing works as an MCP tool but can't automatically route tasks
- AgentBooster (skip LLM for trivial transforms) is completely non-functional
- The daemon's scheduled workers (audit, optimize, testgaps) run but produce no results

## Patches Applied

We've applied local patches to the npx cache that fix issues 1 and 2. These need to be re-applied after every `npm cache clean` or ruflo update:

- `daemon.js`: Added `setInterval` keepalive for quiet/detached mode
- `worker-daemon.js`: Allow self-PID in singleton check
- `headless-worker-executor.js`: Full `claude.cmd` path + stdin pipe + `shell: true`

Issue 3 (empty worker output) remains unresolved.

## Suggested Fixes

1. **daemon.js spawn:** Use 8.3 short path or `cmd /s /c` with proper quoting when `process.execPath` contains spaces
2. **daemon.js keepalive:** Add `setInterval` in quiet mode branch
3. **headless workers:** Investigate why `claude --print` via stdin pipe returns empty stdout on Windows — may need `--output-format json` or a different IPC approach
4. **CLI status:** Add fallback to check PID file + swarm state file when MCP client can't connect

`terminal_execute` in MCP does not execute commands; it only returns state-tracking text
body:
## Summary

The `terminal_execute` MCP tool is currently a stub in the published package I tested. It does not execute the requested command or return real stdout/stderr. Instead, it always returns a synthetic string like:

`[STATE TRACKING] Command recorded: <command>`

This makes the terminal tools unusable for actual command execution.

## Environment

- Package: `ruflo@3.5.48`
- Internal CLI package observed: `@claude-flow/cli`
- Node: `v22.22.0`
- Platform: `darwin x64`
- MCP transport: `stdio`
- Client: Codex/Windsurf MCP integration

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the MCP server with:
   `npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start`
2. Create a terminal session via MCP.
3. Call `terminal_execute` with a simple command, for example:
   `printf 'ok-from-terminal\n'`

## Actual Result

The MCP tool returns something like:

`[STATE TRACKING] Command recorded: printf 'ok-from-terminal\n'`

with exit code `0`, but no actual command output.

## Expected Result

The command should actually run and return its real stdout/stderr, or the tool should be clearly documented/renamed as a logging-only tool rather than an execution tool.

## Root Cause

In the installed package, the terminal tool appears intentionally stubbed.

Observed code in the published build:

```js
// NOTE: This is STATE TRACKING only - does not execute commands
// For real execution, use Claude Code's Bash tool
const output = `[STATE TRACKING] Command recorded: ${command}`;

File observed locally in the published package:

node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/terminal-tools.js

Impact
terminal_execute cannot be used for actual terminal automation through MCP
workflows that depend on command output break or become misleading
the tool reports success semantics that imply execution happened when it did not
Suggested Fix
One of these should happen:

Implement real command execution in terminal_execute
Rename the tool to something like terminal_record_command if it is intentionally logging-only
Return an explicit error stating execution is not supported, instead of a fake successful result

title: fix: agentic-flow missing ./embeddings export breaks ruflo embeddings init on Windows
body:
## Summary

`ruflo embeddings init --model all-MiniLM-L6-v2 --download` fails with:

```
[ERROR] Initialization failed: Package subpath './embeddings' is not defined by "exports" in
C:\...\node_modules\agentic-flow\package.json
imported from C:\...\node_modules\@claude-flow\embeddings\dist\neural-integration.js
```

## Root Cause

`@claude-flow/embeddings`'s `neural-integration.js` imports `agentic-flow/embeddings`, but `agentic-flow`'s `exports` map does not define that subpath:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/index.js",
  "./orchestration": "./dist/orchestration/index.js",
  "./sdk": "./dist/sdk/index.js",
  "./security": "./dist/security/index.js",
  "./reasoningbank": { ... },
  "./router": "./dist/router/index.js",
  "./agent-booster": "./dist/agent-booster/index.js",
  "./transport/quic": "./dist/transport/quic.js"
  // ← no "./embeddings" entry
}
```

Node.js strict ESM exports enforcement treats missing subpaths as hard errors.

## Platform

- **Windows**: Fails with the error above
- **WSL**: Works correctly (confirmed)

The difference is likely how Node.js resolves package exports in Windows vs WSL/Linux, or a different version of `agentic-flow` being resolved in each environment.

## Impact

- `ruflo embeddings init` always fails on Windows
- `ruflo init` wizard silently skips embedding initialization (catches the error and prints "Embeddings will be configured on first use")
- `ruflo memory search --query "..."` falls back to keyword matching — no semantic similarity search on Windows

## Proposed Fix

Either:

1. **Add `./embeddings` to `agentic-flow`'s exports map** pointing to the appropriate dist file
2. **Remove the `agentic-flow/embeddings` import from `@claude-flow/embeddings/neural-integration.js`** and use the main `agentic-flow` entry point or an alternative path

## Related

- Issue #1453 — `ruflo memory` subcommands hang after completion (process.exit fix)
- PR #1441 — process.exit fix for ONNX worker thread hang

title: Daemon dies immediately on Windows + Node 25 (unsettled top-level await + detached spawn)
body:
## Bug Description

The RuFlo daemon (`claude-flow daemon start`) fails to stay alive on **Windows + Node.js v25**. It reports "started" but the background process exits immediately, so `daemon status` always shows STOPPED.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 Pro (Git Bash)
- **Node.js**: v25.8.2
- **@claude-flow/cli**: v3.5.48
- **Shell**: Git Bash

## Root Cause (two bugs)

### 1. Node 25 unsettled top-level await (primary)

The daemon uses `await new Promise(() => {})` to keep the process alive ([daemon.js lines 155, 159](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/packages/claude-flow/src/commands/daemon.ts)). Node.js v25 introduced detection of "unsettled top-level await" — when a promise never resolves and nothing else keeps the event loop active, Node exits with code 13.

In quiet/background mode, there's no stdin reader or other event loop activity, so Node kills the process immediately.

### 2. Windows `detached: false` + `shell: true` (secondary)

In `startBackgroundDaemon()`, the spawn options set:
```js
detached: !isWin,  // false on Windows
...(isWin ? { shell: true, windowsHide: true } : {}),
```

- `detached: false` means the child dies when the parent npx process exits
- `shell: true` wraps node in a shell, so `child.pid` is the shell's PID, not node's — the PID file becomes stale immediately
- The comment "detached is POSIX-only" is incorrect — `detached: true` works on Windows (creates a new process group)

## Fix

### Fix 1: Keep event loop alive before the unsettled await

```js
// Before:
await new Promise(() => { }); // Keep alive

// After:
setInterval(() => { }, 2 ** 31 - 1); // Keep event loop active for Node 25+
await new Promise(() => { }); // Keep alive
```

### Fix 2: Use `detached: true` on Windows, remove `shell: true`

```js
// Before:
detached: !isWin,
...(isWin ? { shell: true, windowsHide: true } : {}),

// After:
detached: true,
...(isWin ? { windowsHide: true } : {}),
```

## Reproduction Steps

1. Install Node.js v25+ on Windows
2. Run `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest daemon start`
3. Run `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest daemon status` — shows STOPPED
4. Check `.claude-flow/daemon.log` — only shows AgentDB patch warning, no daemon output

## Verification

After applying both fixes locally to the npx cache, `daemon status` correctly shows:
```
+--------- RuFlo Daemon ---------+
| Status: ● RUNNING (background) |
| PID: 48516                     |
+--------------------------------+
```

## Additional Note

The `[AgentDB Patch] Controller index not found` warning is harmless — `agentdb@2.0.0-alpha.3.7` has a different directory structure than what the runtime patch expects. The patch gracefully returns `false` and continues. This is cosmetic only and doesn't affect daemon functionality.

title: memory_search defaults to namespace 'default', returning empty results when entries use named namespaces
body:
## Bug Description

`memory_search` returns 0 results for every query when no `namespace` parameter is provided, even though the brain has 100+ entries with valid 384-dimension HNSW embeddings.

## Root Cause

In `dist/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.js`, line 288 (and 3 other locations):

```javascript
const namespace = input.namespace || 'default';
```

When `memory_search` is called without an explicit `namespace` parameter, it defaults to `'default'`. This is passed to `bridgeSearchEntries`, which applies a SQL filter:

```sql
WHERE status = 'active' AND namespace = 'default'
```

However, entries stored via `memory_store` are typically stored under specific namespaces like `health`, `bwe`, `business`, `calendar`, etc. — NOT under `'default'`. The SQL pre-filter excludes ALL entries before the HNSW vector search even runs.

## Reproduction

```
# Store an entry with a specific namespace
memory_store({ key: "test-1", value: "Hello world", namespace: "myns" })

# Search without specifying namespace — returns 0 results
memory_search({ query: "Hello" })
# Returns: { results: [], total: 0 }

# Search with namespace: "all" — works correctly
memory_search({ query: "Hello", namespace: "all" })
# Returns: { results: [{ key: "test-1", similarity: 0.85, ... }], total: 1 }
```

## Expected Behavior

`memory_search` without a namespace should search across ALL namespaces (equivalent to `namespace: "all"`), not filter to the `'default'` namespace.

## Suggested Fix

Change line 288 (and lines 159, 225, 350) from:
```javascript
const namespace = input.namespace || 'default';
```
to:
```javascript
const namespace = input.namespace || 'all';
```

## Impact

This bug makes the MCP memory search appear completely broken. Users store entries, confirm they exist via `memory_stats` and `memory_list`, but every search query returns empty. The failure is silent — no error message, just 0 results with a valid response structure.

## Environment

- ruflo v3.5.48 / @claude-flow/cli v3.5.48
- Node.js v25.8.2 (Homebrew)
- macOS 15 (Darwin 25.4.0)

## Workaround

Always pass `namespace: "all"` explicitly when calling `memory_search`.

title: Memory SQLite database path is relative to CWD, causing data loss on MCP server restart
body:
## Bug Description

The ruflo MCP memory system stores its SQLite database at a path relative to the current working directory (`{cwd}/.swarm/memory.db`). When the MCP server restarts with a different working directory, it creates a new empty database instead of finding the existing one. Previously stored data appears to vanish.

## Root Cause

The memory bridge resolves the database path relative to `process.cwd()`. The MCP server's CWD depends on how it was launched (by Claude Code, by a LaunchAgent, manually, etc.), which can change between sessions.

## Reproduction

1. Start the MCP server from `/Users/stuart/project-a`
2. Store entries via `memory_store`
3. Verify entries exist via `memory_list` and `memory_stats`
4. Restart the MCP server (or start a new Claude Code session that launches it from a different directory)
5. Call `memory_stats` — shows 0 entries
6. The data is still in `/Users/stuart/project-a/.swarm/memory.db` but the server is now using `/Users/stuart/project-b/.swarm/memory.db`

## Expected Behavior

The memory database should be stored at a fixed, absolute path (e.g., `~/.claude-flow/memory.db` or a user-configurable path), not relative to CWD.

## Impact

Users lose access to stored knowledge between sessions. The data isn't actually deleted — it's orphaned in the old CWD's `.swarm/` directory. This makes the memory system appear unreliable.

## Suggested Fix

Use an absolute path for the database, such as:
- `~/.claude-flow/memory.db` (user home)
- Or allow configuration via an environment variable like `CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_DB`

## Environment

- ruflo v3.5.48 / @claude-flow/cli v3.5.48
- Node.js v25.8.2
- macOS 15

title: AgentDB: 4 controllers unimplemented (ContextSynthesizer, ReasoningBank, BatchOperations, CausalMemoryGraph bridge)
body:
## Environment

- ruflo@3.5.48 (npm install -g ruflo@latest)
- Node v20.19.4, Linux x64
- MCP server with `CLAUDE_FLOW_TOOL_GROUPS=memory,agentdb,embeddings,hooks`
- Database: ~/.swarm/memory.db with 1005 entries, 34 tables

## Issue

`agentdb_controllers` reports 5 controllers, 4 active. However, several MCP tools that depend on agentdb controllers return errors because the backing controllers are never registered in the controller registry.

### Working controllers (4/5)

| Controller | Status | Tools it powers |
|-----------|--------|----------------|
| hierarchicalMemory | enabled | hierarchical-store, hierarchical-recall |
| tieredCache | enabled | (internal caching) |
| memoryGraph | enabled | (registered but causal-edge still fails) |
| memoryConsolidation | enabled | session-end |

### Failing tools

| MCP Tool | Error | Expected Controller |
|----------|-------|-------------------|
| `agentdb_context-synthesize` | `"ContextSynthesizer not available"` | `contextSynthesizer` — never registered in any initializer |
| `agentdb_pattern-search` | `"controller": "unavailable"` | `reasoningBank` — registered but `enabled: false` |
| `agentdb_batch` | `"BatchOperations not available"` | Never registered |
| `agentdb_causal-edge` | `"AgentDB bridge not available"` | `memoryGraph` is registered/enabled but bridge doesn't route to it |

### Root cause analysis

1. **`contextSynthesizer`**: `memory-bridge.js:1427` calls `registry.get('contextSynthesizer')` but no code in memory-initializer.js or anywhere else ever registers this key. The ContextSynthesizer class exists in `agentdb/dist/src/controllers/ContextSynthesizer.js` but is never imported or instantiated.

2. **`reasoningBank`**: Registered at level 1 but `enabled: false`. `memory-initializer.js:1300` attempts `import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank')` — unclear if this import path resolves correctly with the current package structure.

3. **`BatchOperations`**: `memory-bridge.js:1381` returns `"BatchOperations not available"` — no controller provides this capability.

4. **`causal-edge`**: `memoryGraph` controller is registered and enabled, but `memory-bridge.js` for causal-edge falls through to the "bridge not available" error instead of routing to memoryGraph.

### Reproduction

```bash
# Install
npm install -g ruflo@3.5.48

# Start MCP and call tools
ruflo mcp start
# Via MCP client:
agentdb_controllers  # → shows 5 controllers, 4 active
agentdb_context-synthesize(query: "test")  # → ContextSynthesizer not available
agentdb_pattern-search(query: "test")  # → controller: unavailable
agentdb_batch(operation: "insert", entries: [...])  # → BatchOperations not available
agentdb_causal-edge(sourceId: "a", targetId: "b", relation: "references")  # → bridge not available
```

### Impact

These 4 tools are exposed in the MCP tool list (users see them and expect them to work) but silently fail. This blocks use cases that depend on:
- Context synthesis from stored memories
- Pattern search with confidence scoring
- Bulk memory operations
- Knowledge graph edges between entries

### Suggested fix

1. Register ContextSynthesizer from agentdb controllers package during initialization
2. Investigate why reasoningBank is disabled — enable or document requirements
3. Implement BatchOperations (or route batch calls through existing memory_store in a loop)
4. Fix causal-edge routing to use the already-registered memoryGraph controller

title: security scan prints 'The system cannot find the path specified' on Windows
body:
## Summary
On Windows, `npx @claude-flow/cli security scan --depth full` completes the scan output but then prints:

```text
The system cannot find the path specified.
```

## Reproduction
Environment used to reproduce:
- OS: Windows
- Node: v22.16.0
- npm: 10.8.3
- CLI/package version in local workspace: 3.5.48

Command:

```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli security scan --depth full
```

## Actual behavior
The scan runs and prints findings / summary, then emits an extra Windows error:

```text
The system cannot find the path specified.
```

## Expected behavior
The command should exit cleanly after printing the scan summary, without any extra shell/path error on Windows.

## Root cause
The security scan command uses POSIX shell syntax in the dependency-audit path:

```ts
npm audit --json 2>/dev/null || true
```

and in the autofix path:

```ts
npm audit fix 2>/dev/null || true
```

That works under POSIX shells, but on Windows `cmd.exe` does not understand `/dev/null`, so it surfaces `The system cannot find the path specified.`

## Suggested fix
Avoid shell redirection / `|| true` here and use a platform-safe child-process call instead, e.g. `spawnSync`/`execFile` with:
- `npm.cmd` on `win32`
- `npm` elsewhere

and parse `stdout` directly.

## Notes
I reproduced this locally and confirmed the error is tied to the `npm audit` shell invocation, not the scan itself.

title: MCP tools are not automatically used — 'just use Claude Code normally' doesn't work
body:
## Problem

The README states:

> **New to Ruflo?** You don't need to learn 310+ MCP tools or 26 CLI commands. After running init, just use Claude Code normally — the hooks system automatically routes tasks to the right agents, learns from successful patterns, and coordinates multi-agent work in the background.

This is not what happens in practice. After a full install (`--full` flag), the hooks fire and MCP tools are registered, but **Claude never actually calls any of them** unless the user explicitly tells it to.

## Root cause

1. **MCP tools are "deferred"** — Claude Code doesn't load their schemas until `ToolSearch` is explicitly called. Claude has no idea what `mcp__ruflo__memory_store` does or what parameters it takes until it actively searches for it.

2. **Hook output is passive** — The `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks inject `[INTELLIGENCE] Relevant patterns` text into system reminders, but this is just text. Claude routinely ignores system reminder text, especially when focused on the user's actual task. There is no mechanism to force Claude to invoke a tool based on hook output.

3. **No bridge between hooks and tool invocation** — The hooks can detect "this task is about swap exchange rates" and even find relevant patterns, but they can't make Claude call `mcp__ruflo__hooks_intelligence_pattern-search` to surface those patterns. The intelligence stays locked inside ruflo.

## What the user has to do instead

After discovering ruflo wasn't being used across sessions, the user had to:

1. Create `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (global instructions file) with explicit instructions telling Claude to use `ToolSearch` to load ruflo tool schemas and then call them
2. Create per-project memory files documenting this requirement
3. Manually remind Claude in-session to "use ruflo"

This defeats the purpose of "just use Claude Code normally."

## Suggested fixes

1. **Non-deferred critical tools** — Register a small set of core tools (e.g., `pattern-search`, `memory_store`, `memory_search`) as non-deferred so Claude sees their schemas immediately and can call them without `ToolSearch`.

2. **Auto-generate ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md on install** — Since this is the one file guaranteed to be read by Claude at every session start, ruflo's `init` command should write/append instructions to it automatically, telling Claude how and when to use ruflo tools.

3. **Hook output with explicit tool call suggestions** — Instead of just printing `[INTELLIGENCE] Relevant patterns: ...`, the hook could output structured text like: `[ACTION REQUIRED] Call mcp__ruflo__hooks_intelligence_pattern-search(query: "swap exchange rate") to load 3 relevant patterns before starting work.` This is more likely to trigger Claude to actually invoke the tool.

4. **Update README** — Be transparent that automatic routing requires `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` configuration, not just `init`. The current "just use it normally" claim sets wrong expectations.

## Environment

- ruflo v3.5.48
- Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.6)
- macOS
- Installed via `curl -fsSL ... | bash -s -- --full`
- MCP server configured in `~/.mcp.json`
- Hooks configured in `~/.claude/settings.json`

title: [Bug] 106 agent definitions ship by default — ~300K tokens of context bloat, most agents are non-functional
body:
## Summary

Ruflo ships **106 agent definition files** (1.19MB / ~300K tokens) in `.claude/agents/`. The majority of these agents reference MCP servers that don't exist in a standard installation, making them dead weight that inflates every conversation's context window.

When you try to use one of these agents (e.g. `frontend-design`), you get:

```
Error: Agent type 'frontend-design' not found. Available agents: general-purpose, statusline-setup, Explore, Plan, ...
```

...followed by a wall of **90+ agent names** dumped into the error message and into the system prompt. This list alone costs significant tokens on every single interaction.

## The Numbers

| Category | Files | Size | Actually functional? |
|----------|-------|------|---------------------|
| `v3/` | 16 | 238KB | Partially — references internal v3 architecture |
| `github/` | 13 | 186KB | Some work (pr-manager, issue-tracker) |
| `consensus/` | 7 | 107KB | References non-existent MCP servers |
| `optimization/` | 5 | 95KB | Generic, no project-specific value |
| `swarm/` | 3 | 88KB | Partially useful |
| `sparc/` | 4 | 70KB | SPARC methodology — niche |
| `core/` | 5 | 70KB | **Actually useful** (coder, reviewer, tester, planner, researcher) |
| `sublinear/` | 5 | 55KB | **100% non-functional** — requires `sublinear-time-solver` MCP (not installed) |
| `flow-nexus/` | 9 | 32KB | **100% non-functional** — requires `flow-nexus` MCP (not installed) |
| `hive-mind/` | 5 | 25KB | Partially useful with ruflo MCP |
| `payments/` | 1 | 5KB | **100% non-functional** — requires `agentic-payments` MCP (not installed) |
| `templates/` | 9 | 59KB | Template files, rarely used |
| Others | 24 | ~84KB | Mixed — duplicates, niche specialists |

**Total: 1,194,421 bytes (~300K tokens)** loaded or indexed per session.

## Specific Problems

### 1. Agents reference MCP servers that don't ship with Ruflo

These 15+ agents call tools from MCP servers that are never installed in a standard `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest` setup:

- **`flow-nexus/*` (9 agents)** — call `mcp__flow-nexus__*` tools. Flow Nexus is a separate SaaS platform. These agents are useless without it.
- **`sublinear/*` (5 agents)** — call `mcp__sublinear-time-solver__*` tools. This MCP server doesn't exist in any standard install.
- **`payments/agentic-payments`** — calls `mcp__agentic-payments__*` tools. Not installed.

These agents will **always fail** when spawned. They're marketing material, not functional agents.

### 2. 7 duplicate agent files

Several agents exist twice — once at the category root and once in a nested subdirectory:

```
analysis/analyze-code-quality.md          ← duplicate
analysis/code-review/analyze-code-quality.md  ← duplicate
architecture/arch-system-design.md
architecture/system-design/arch-system-design.md
development/dev-backend-api.md
development/backend/dev-backend-api.md
devops/ops-cicd-github.md
devops/ci-cd/ops-cicd-github.md
documentation/docs-api-openapi.md
documentation/api-docs/docs-api-openapi.md
specialized/spec-mobile-react-native.md
specialized/mobile/spec-mobile-react-native.md
data/data-ml-model.md
data/ml/data-ml-model.md
```

### 3. The agent list bloats every error message and system prompt

When Claude Code lists available agents (on error, or in the system prompt), it dumps all 90+ names. This is pure token waste on every single message in a conversation.

### 4. Many "agents" are just verbose prompt templates with no differentiation

Agents like `trading-predictor` (claims to "execute trades before market data physically arrives" via "temporal advantage") and `pagerank-analyzer` are marketing copy, not useful tooling. A `coder` agent with a good system prompt can do everything these claim to do.

## What's Actually Useful (from real-world usage)

From the 106 agents, roughly **10-15 are genuinely useful** for day-to-day development:

- **Core**: `coder`, `reviewer`, `tester`, `planner`, `researcher`
- **GitHub**: `pr-manager`, `issue-tracker` (maybe `code-review-swarm`)
- **Swarm**: `hierarchical-coordinator`
- **V3**: `security-auditor`, `memory-specialist` (if you use AgentDB)
- **Misc**: `sparc-coder`, `task-orchestrator`

Everything else is either non-functional (missing MCP dependencies), duplicated, or a verbose wrapper around a basic prompt that the `coder` or `planner` agent could handle.

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A: Ship a minimal core set (recommended)

Ship only the ~15 agents that work out of the box. Move everything else to an opt-in registry:

```bash
ruflo agents install flow-nexus    # only if you have Flow Nexus configured
ruflo agents install sublinear     # only if you have sublinear-time-solver
ruflo agents install github-full   # extended GitHub agents beyond pr-manager
```

### Option B: Lazy loading

Don't register agents in the system prompt until they're first used. Only load the full agent definition when `Agent(subagent_type="X")` is called.

### Option C: At minimum, remove non-functional agents

Delete agents that reference MCP servers not included in the standard install. This alone would remove 15+ agents and ~90KB of dead definitions.

### Option D: Deduplication + size audit

1. Remove the 7 duplicate files
2. Trim agent definitions to <2KB each (most are 15-35KB of verbose prompts)
3. Move detailed instructions into the agent's runtime prompt, not the static definition

## Environment

- Ruflo v3.5.x (via `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest`)
- Claude Code (Opus 4.6)
- macOS / Ubuntu 24.04

## Impact

Every conversation pays the token tax of 106 agent definitions whether or not you use agents. At ~$0.015/1K input tokens on Opus, that's roughly **$4.50 per conversation just for agent definitions** that are mostly non-functional. Over a workday of 20 conversations, that's ~$90 in wasted input tokens on agent bloat alone.

title: Plugin peer deps reject alpha versions (semver pre-release mismatch)
body:
## Bug Report

### Description
Plugin packages on npm declare peer dependencies with `>=3.0.0` ranges, but only `3.0.0-alpha.x` versions are published. npm semver treats pre-release versions as less than the release version, so `3.0.0-alpha.1` does **not** satisfy `>=3.0.0`.

### Steps to Reproduce
```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest plugins install --name @claude-flow/plugin-code-intelligence
```

### Error
```
npm error code ETARGET
npm error notarget No matching version found for @claude-flow/embeddings@>=3.0.0.
```

### Root Cause
`@claude-flow/plugin-agentic-qe@3.0.0-alpha.4` declares:
```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@claude-flow/embeddings": ">=3.0.0",
  "@claude-flow/plugins": ">=3.0.0"
}
```

But only `@claude-flow/embeddings@3.0.0-alpha.1` exists on npm. Per npm semver rules, `3.0.0-alpha.1 < 3.0.0`, so the range `>=3.0.0` rejects it.

### Affected Plugins
- `@claude-flow/plugin-code-intelligence`
- `@claude-flow/plugin-test-intelligence`
- `@claude-flow/security`
- Any plugin depending on `@claude-flow/embeddings@>=3.0.0`

### Fix
Change peer dep ranges to include pre-releases:
```json
"@claude-flow/embeddings": ">=3.0.0-0"
```
The `-0` suffix matches all pre-release versions of 3.0.0+.

### Environment
- `@claude-flow/cli@latest` (3.0.0-alpha.2)
- Node 20.19.6, npm 10.x
- Ubuntu (WSL2)
