title: Bug: claudemd-generator.ts references "Task tool" (renamed to "Agent" in Claude Code v2.1.63), missing ToolSearch/hook signal guidance
body:
## PR

#1512

## Summary

`claudemd-generator.ts` generates CLAUDE.md files with 14 references to a "Task tool" that was renamed to "Agent" in Claude Code v2.1.63. Every project running `ruflo init` gets instructions pointing to a nonexistent tool. Additionally, the generated CLAUDE.md has no guidance for ToolSearch (required for deferred MCP tools) and no instructions for acting on hook signals like `[INTELLIGENCE]`.

This was independently reported by users in #1476, #1497, and #1491 — Claude ignores or simulates ruflo features because the CLAUDE.md doesn't bridge the gap between hooks, deferred MCP tools, and Claude's actual tool surface.

## Root Cause

1. **"Task tool" naming** — inherited from v2 templates, never updated after the Claude Code v2.1.63 rename (anthropics/claude-code#29677)
2. **No ToolSearch bootstrap** — 200+ MCP tools are deferred; Claude can't call them without ToolSearch. CLAUDE.md never mentions it.
3. **No hook signal binding** — `[INTELLIGENCE]` text is injected by UserPromptSubmit hooks but CLAUDE.md never tells Claude to act on it. The signal falls into the void.
4. **`[AGENT_BOOSTER_AVAILABLE]` / `[TASK_MODEL_RECOMMENDATION]`** — referenced in CLAUDE.md but never emitted by the hook system. Only the MCP tool `hooks_pre-task` emits these, creating a circular dependency.
5. **Reference material inflates size** — CLI command tables, agent catalogs, memory command reference, intelligence system jargon (SONA, EWC++, HNSW) occupy ~60% of the file. Claude ignores all of it (#1476 user confirmed).

## Proposed Fix

Rewrite `claudemd-generator.ts` with these changes:

### Fixes
| Change | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| "Task tool" → "Agent tool" | 14 instances across `concurrencyRules()`, `swarmOrchestration()`, `autoStartProtocol()`, `executionRules()`, `setupAndBoundary()` |
| Remove `[AGENT_BOOSTER_AVAILABLE]` / `[TASK_MODEL_RECOMMENDATION]` | Phantom signals not emitted by hooks |
| Remove `TodoWrite` reference | Not a real Claude Code tool name |
| Remove `Task({prompt:..., subagent_type:...})` pseudo-code | Fabricated JS syntax; Claude already knows tool_use XML |
| Remove Project Config sub-section | Daemon runtime config (topology/HNSW/neural), not actionable by Claude |

### New sections
| Section | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| **Task Complexity** (3 lines) | When to spawn agents vs work directly |
| **MCP Tools (Deferred)** (12 lines) | ToolSearch bootstrap + 4 discovery queries + `agentdb_session-*` DO NOT CALL warning |
| **Hook Signals** (7 lines) | Before/during/after lifecycle binding for `[INTELLIGENCE]` and `[INFO]` |
| **When to Use What** (7 lines) | Decision tree: Agent tool / MCP / CLI / Skill |
| **Feature Workflow** (5 lines) | TDD checklist: test → implement → verify → commit |

### Template composition changes
- Replace `swarmOrchestration()` with `agentOrchestration()` (correct tool names)
- Replace `executionRules()` with `mcpToolDiscovery()` + `hookSignals()` + `whenToUseWhat()`
- Add `taskComplexity()` after concurrency
- Add feature workflow to `buildAndTest()`
- Remove `autoStartProtocol()`, `intelligenceSystem()`, `envVars()` from all templates

### Result
Standard template drops from ~250 lines to ~112 lines. Every line is an imperative instruction or concrete build command. Zero aspirational content.

## Proposed Template Output

Below is the exact markdown the `standard` template should produce (with `${...}` placeholders for project-specific values):

<details>
<summary>Click to expand full template (~112 lines)</summary>

$(cat /Users/henrik/source/ruflo-patch/docs/claudemd-standard-template-v2.md)

</details>

## Affected File

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/claudemd-generator.ts`

## Related Issues

- #1476 — Claude refusing to use ruflo framework ("~40% useful, ~60% boilerplate")
- #1497 — MCP tools not automatically used ("just use Claude Code normally" doesn't work)
- #1491 — Users not seeing results from framework features
- #1413 / #1422 — Hive-mind uses Claude native tools instead of ruflo MCP (fixed in v3.5.43 for hive-mind prompts, but not for CLAUDE.md generator)
- #1206 — Stale `--topology hierarchical` in CLAUDE.md templates (same class of bug, same file)

## References

- anthropics/claude-code#29677 — Task→Agent tool rename in v2.1.63
- sparkling/ruflo-patch#92 — Downstream patch implementing this fix

title: [Warning] Ruflo is 99% Theater, 1% Real — An Independent Audit of Every Tool. Don't Be Confused.
body:
## Summary

An independent technical audit of ruflo v3.5.51 reveals that **~290 out of 300+ MCP tools are stubs** — they create JSON state records but have no execution backend. Only ~10 tools (memory/HNSW, embeddings, terminal, sessions) actually compute something.

This is filed as an issue because it affects every user who installs ruflo expecting the advertised capabilities to work.

## Reproduction (anyone can verify)

```bash
# 1. Spawn an agent — check status after 5 minutes
mcp__ruflo__agent_spawn  type="coder" name="test"
mcp__ruflo__agent_status  agentId="<returned id>"
# Result: status "idle", taskCount 0 — forever

# 2. Train a neural model — check predictions
mcp__ruflo__neural_train  modelId="test" data=[[1,0],[0,1]] labels=[0,1] epochs=5
mcp__ruflo__neural_predict  modelId="test" input=[1,0]
# Result: always predicts "coder" regardless of input/training

# 3. Create a WASM agent — send it a prompt
mcp__ruflo__wasm_agent_create  name="test"
mcp__ruflo__wasm_agent_prompt  agentId="<id>" prompt="What is 2+2?"
# Result: "echo: What is 2+2?" — input echoed back

# 4. Choose any consensus type at hive-mind init — behavior is identical
# verifySignature() returns true unconditionally (source: RaftConsensus.js)
```

## Affected Components

| Component | Advertised | Actual |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| `agent_spawn` | Spawns agent with model selection | Writes `{ status: "idle" }` to a Map |
| `task_assign` | Assigns task to agent worker | Emits event to EventEmitter nobody listens to |
| `neural_train` | Trains ML model | Returns randomized accuracy, ignores data |
| `neural_predict` | Model inference | Hardcoded labels: "coder", "researcher", "reviewer" |
| `wasm_agent_prompt` | Sandboxed WASM execution | Echoes input back |
| `workflow_execute` | Runs workflow | "Workflow not found" even after creation |
| `hive-mind consensus` | Byzantine/Raft/Queen protocols | Same JSON vote-counting regardless of type |
| `coordination_*` | Distributed coordination | Config labels only |

## What Works (credit where due)

- `memory_store/search/retrieve` — Real HNSW vector search (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim)
- `embeddings_generate/compare` — Real embedding generation
- `terminal_execute` — Real shell execution
- `session_save/restore` — Real state persistence

## The Architectural Gap

The LLM provider (`AnthropicProvider` with real `fetch` to api.anthropic.com) **exists in the codebase**. The task queue exists. The agent registry exists. But the wire connecting agent_spawn → LLM provider → task execution is missing. This isn't a bug in one tool — it's a structural gap across the entire orchestration layer.

## Request

1. **Label stub tools** as `planned` or `not yet implemented` in documentation
2. **Don't expose 290 stubs** to Claude's MCP context by default — it wastes tokens and confuses users
3. **Publish a roadmap** showing which tools are being wired up

## Full Audit

📄 **Complete report with source code evidence, process traces, token cost analysis:**

👉 [Full Audit Report (GitHub Gist)](https://gist.github.com/roman-rr/ed603b676af019b8740423d2bb8e4bf6)

---

## Full Scorecard: What's Promised vs What's Real

| Category | Tools | Promised | Verdict |
|----------|-------|---------|---------|
| **Memory/HNSW** | `memory_store`, `memory_search`, `memory_retrieve`, `memory_list`, `memory_delete` | Semantic vector search with persistence | ✅ **REAL** — 384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2, HNSW index, SQLite |
| **AgentDB** | `agentdb_pattern-store`, `agentdb_pattern-search`, `agentdb_hierarchical-store/recall` | Pattern storage with vector search | ✅ **REAL** — same HNSW engine, namespace-scoped |
| **Embeddings** | `embeddings_generate`, `embeddings_compare`, `embeddings_search` | Embedding generation & similarity | ✅ **REAL** — all-MiniLM-L6-v2, cosine similarity |
| **Terminal** | `terminal_execute` | Shell command execution | ✅ **REAL** — but redundant (Claude already has Bash) |
| **Session** | `session_save`, `session_restore`, `session_list` | State persistence | ✅ **REAL** — JSON key-value store |
| **Agent** | `agent_spawn`, `agent_status`, `agent_health`, `agent_pool`, `agent_list`, `agent_terminate`, `agent_update` | Agent lifecycle with intelligent model selection | ❌ **FAKE** — JSON records in Map, status always "idle", taskCount always 0, no subprocess |
| **Task** | `task_create`, `task_assign`, `task_complete`, `task_status`, `task_list`, `task_cancel` | Task queue with worker execution | ❌ **FAKE** — EventEmitter with no listener, tasks stay "pending" forever |
| **Swarm** | `swarm_init`, `swarm_status`, `swarm_health`, `swarm_shutdown` | Multi-agent swarm coordination | ❌ **FAKE** — config storage only, `agentCount: 0` even after spawning |
| **Hive-mind** | `hive-mind_init`, `hive-mind_consensus`, `hive-mind_broadcast`, `hive-mind_spawn`, `hive-mind_join/leave` | Distributed consensus with Byzantine fault tolerance | ❌ **FAKE** — single-process JSON file, `verifySignature()` returns `true`, all consensus types run same code |
| **WASM** | `wasm_agent_create`, `wasm_agent_prompt`, `wasm_agent_tool`, `wasm_agent_files` | Sandboxed WASM agent execution | ❌ **FAKE** — echoes input back, no WASM runtime |
| **Neural** | `neural_train`, `neural_predict`, `neural_optimize`, `neural_patterns` | ML model training & inference | ❌ **FAKE** — ignores training data, returns hardcoded labels with random confidence |
| **Workflow** | `workflow_create`, `workflow_execute`, `workflow_run`, `workflow_status` | Task orchestration pipelines | ❌ **FAKE** — state machine exists, no executor behind it |
| **Coordination** | `coordination_consensus`, `coordination_sync`, `coordination_topology`, `coordination_load_balance` | Distributed node coordination | ❌ **FAKE** — labels and config objects only |
| **Claims** | `claims_claim`, `claims_handoff`, `claims_steal`, `claims_rebalance` | Distributed work claiming & locking | ❌ **FAKE** — in-memory Map, no cross-process locking |
| **DAA** | `daa_agent_create`, `daa_workflow_create`, `daa_workflow_execute` | Dynamic autonomous agents | ❌ **FAKE** — registration stubs |
| **Browser** | `browser_open`, `browser_click`, `browser_fill`, `browser_screenshot` | Web automation | ⚠️ **UNTESTED** — may work if Playwright is connected |

**Final count: ~10 real tools (3%) out of 300+ advertised.**

---

---

## Token Optimizer: "30-50% Token Reduction" — Real Infrastructure, Fake Metrics

The README advertises a Token Optimizer with impressive savings. We downloaded `@claude-flow/integration` from npm and read the source.

### The Claims vs The Code

| Component | Claimed Savings | What The Code Actually Does |
|-----------|----------------|---------------------------|
| **ReasoningBank** | -32% tokens | Real SQLite + vector retrieval exists. But the "-32%" comes from a **graph hop reduction benchmark** in agentdb simulation docs — not token measurement. The baseline is `const baseline = 1000` (hardcoded). Token "savings" = `1000 - output.length/4`. No actual token counting. |
| **Agent Booster** | -15%, "352x faster" | Real WASM engine for string-diff edits. But the "352x" benchmark does `await this.sleep(352)` as the "traditional edit baseline". It's comparing WASM speed against a **literal 352ms sleep**, not an actual LLM call. |
| **Cache** | 95% hit rate, -10% | Real `Map` with 5-min TTL. But "95% hit rate" is a marketing number — starts at 0% on fresh install. Token savings: `this.stats.totalTokensSaved += 100` — **hardcoded 100 per cache hit**, not measured. |
| **Optimal batch size** | -20% | `getOptimalConfig(agentCount)` returns `{ batchSize: 4, topology: 'hierarchical' }` regardless of input. The `agentCount` parameter is **ignored**. |
| **"30-50% combined"** | Stacks multiplicatively | No token counting code exists anywhere in the package. The percentages are individually fabricated and then summed. |

### The Smoking Gun Code

```javascript
// "352x faster" benchmark (agent-booster-migration.js:150)
await this.sleep(352);  // sleeps 352ms to simulate "traditional edit"
// Then: speedup = 352 / actualWasmMs  →  reports "352x faster"

// "Token savings" per cache hit (token-optimizer.ts:228)
this.stats.totalTokensSaved += 100;  // not measured, just += 100

// "Compact context" baseline (token-optimizer.ts:~130)
const baseline = 1000;  // hardcoded "what you would have sent"
const saved = Math.max(0, baseline - used);  // pure fiction
```

### The Real Token Cost: Ruflo INCREASES Your Token Usage

Ironically, while claiming 30-50% token reduction, ruflo **dramatically inflates** your actual token consumption:

| Source of Token Bloat | Tokens Wasted | Frequency |
|----------------------|---------------|-----------|
| **300+ MCP tool definitions** loaded into Claude's context | ~5,000-10,000 | Every session (deferred loading helps, but tool list itself is massive) |
| **`[INTELLIGENCE]` patterns** injected per message | ~150-200 | Every single message — same duplicate entry 5x |
| **Router ASCII table** with fake latency/percentages | ~100-150 | Every single message |
| **Session restore** verbose output | ~200-300 | Every session start |
| **91 agent type definitions** in Agent tool listing | ~2,000-3,000 | Every time Agent tool is invoked |
| **Estimated per-session waste** | **~15,000-25,000 tokens** | — |

**The tool that promises 30-50% token savings actually adds 15,000-25,000 tokens of noise per session.** Users are paying more, not less, for the privilege of having 290 fake tools in their context window.

---

*Filed constructively. The vision is ambitious and the memory/HNSW layer is genuinely good work. But users deserve to know what's implemented today vs what's planned.*

*Audit conducted 2026-04-04 on ruflo v3.5.51 / @claude-flow/cli@latest*

title: Bug: bare model names in init defaults cause silent fallback to mock embeddings
body:
Embedding model defaults across the CLI use bare names (e.g. `all-mpnet-base-v2`) instead of prefixed names (`Xenova/all-mpnet-base-v2`). Additionally, `ControllerRegistry` does not pass embedding config to `AgentDB`, causing it to fall back to a different default model. Both issues cause `@xenova/transformers` to silently fail, and all semantic search degrades to hash pseudo-embeddings.

## Bug 1: Bare model names in defaults

| File | Value | Should be |
|------|-------|-----------|
| `init/types.ts` FULL_INIT_OPTIONS | `all-mpnet-base-v2` | `Xenova/all-mpnet-base-v2` |
| `init/types.ts` DEFAULT/CODEX_INIT_OPTIONS | `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` |
| `commands/init.ts` wizard choices + CLI flags | bare names | prefixed names |
| `mcp-tools/embeddings-tools.ts` enum + default | bare names | prefixed names |
| `mcp-tools/hooks-tools.ts` status model | bare name | prefixed name |

## Bug 2: ControllerRegistry does not pass embedding config to AgentDB

`@claude-flow/memory/src/controller-registry.ts` line 723:

```typescript
this.agentdb = new AgentDBClass({ dbPath });  // missing embeddingModel + dimension
```

The registry reads `getEmbeddingConfig()` at line 713-715 and caches the dimension, but never passes the model to AgentDB. AgentDB falls back to its own default (MiniLM 384-dim) instead of the configured model (mpnet 768-dim). The bridge then rejects the 384-dim result because config expects 768.

## Fix

1. Prefix all bare model defaults with `Xenova/`
2. Pass `embeddingModel` and `dimension` from registry to `new AgentDBClass()`

## Verification

After fix: `memory store` writes 768-dim `Xenova/all-mpnet-base-v2` embeddings, `memory search` returns semantically relevant results.

title: Bug: intelligence.cjs graph-state.json grows to 194MB due to duplicate store entries
body:
auto-memory-store.json accumulates duplicate entries on every session (4482 entries with only 157 unique IDs). intelligence.cjs buildEdges() processes all duplicates, generating O(n^2) edges between copies of the same entry. This produces 1.3M edges (194MB graph-state.json) for just 157 unique nodes.

The cache-hit check (`graphState.nodeCount === store.length`) also never matches because it compares deduplicated node count (157) against raw store length (4482), so the graph is needlessly rebuilt on every session start.

## Fix

Deduplicate store entries by ID before building nodes and edges. Fix cache-hit check to compare against unique ID count.

Result: 194MB -> 79KB, 1,337,498 edges -> 157.

## File

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/helpers/intelligence.cjs`

title: ruvector CLI subcommands hardcode pgvector instead of detecting ruvector extension
body:
## Bug

The `ruflo ruvector status`, `ruflo ruvector benchmark`, and `ruflo ruvector optimize` subcommands assume the PostgreSQL instance uses the **pgvector** extension (`vector` type), but the official `ruvnet/ruvector-postgres` Docker image ships its own **ruvector** extension (v0.3.0) with a custom `ruvector` UDT — not pgvector's `vector` type.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Start the official ruvector-postgres image
docker run -d --name ruvector-postgres -p 5432:5432 ruvnet/ruvector-postgres:latest

# Run status — reports pgvector NOT installed (false negative)
PGPASSWORD=claude-flow-test ruflo ruvector status --verbose --database claude_flow --user claude

# Run benchmark — fails with "type vector does not exist"
PGPASSWORD=claude-flow-test ruflo ruvector benchmark --database claude_flow --user claude
```

## Expected

- `status` should detect the `ruvector` extension (not just `pgvector`)
- `benchmark` should create columns with the `ruvector` type (not `vector`)
- `optimize` should analyze indexes and types compatible with the `ruvector` extension

## Actual

- `status` reports: `pgvector extension not installed` — even though `ruvector 0.3.0` is installed and working
- `benchmark` fails: `ERROR: type "vector" does not exist`
- `optimize` was not tested independently but likely has the same hardcoded assumption

## Evidence

```sql
-- The actual extension installed:
SELECT extname, extversion FROM pg_extension;
--  ruvector | 0.3.0

-- The actual embedding column type:
SELECT udt_name FROM information_schema.columns 
WHERE table_schema='claude_flow' AND table_name='memory_entries' AND column_name='embedding';
--  ruvector

-- Data is healthy: 129 entries, 8 tables, 21 indexes (HNSW), all valid
```

## Suggested Fix

The CLI should check for **both** extensions and use whichever is present:

```sql
SELECT extname FROM pg_extension WHERE extname IN ('vector', 'ruvector');
```

Then use the detected extension's type for benchmark table creation, status reporting, and optimization analysis.

## Environment

- `ruvnet/ruvector-postgres:latest`
- `ruflo` CLI (npm, latest)
- PostgreSQL with `ruvector` extension 0.3.0
- Node v20.19.6

---
Reported from Site360 project integration testing.

title: ReasoningBank still disabled — @claude-flow/memory@alpha.12 on npm missing require('path') fix
body:
Following up from #1399 — the ControllerRegistry ESM import fix in v3.5.49 (PR #1500) landed successfully, but I believe `@claude-flow/memory` wasn't republished to npm with the updated `controller-registry.js`. ReasoningBank still shows `enabled: false` on v3.5.51.

---

### Environment cleanup

I stripped out every workaround from my earlier debugging (detailed in #1399) to make sure I'm starting clean:

- Removed `@claude-flow/memory` and `agentdb` from `package.json` dependencies
- Regenerated `package-lock.json`
- Deleted local `node_modules` copies (symlinks and barrel edits from earlier debugging)
- Removed `agentdb.rvf` and `ruvector.db` from project root
- Verified no workaround code remains in source (grep for hack/patch/workaround/barrel — zero hits)
- Confirmed no leftover `.rvf` or `ruvector.db` files outside of `.claude-flow/`

### What's working

`agentdb_controllers` returns `available: true` with 4/5 controllers active — the ControllerRegistry fix from #1399 definitely landed. `memory_store`/`memory_search` continue to work perfectly (47 entries in my project namespace).

### What I'm still seeing

```
agentdb_controllers:
  reasoningBank: enabled: false

agentdb_pattern-search:
  results: []
  controller: "unavailable"
```

### Root cause (I think)

In the npx cache, `@claude-flow/memory` still resolves to `3.0.0-alpha.12`. Line 293 of `controller-registry.js` still reads:

```js
const resolved = require('path').resolve(dbPath);
```

Since the package has `"type": "module"`, this throws a `ReferenceError` for any real `dbPath`. The `:memory:` path bypasses this line (it's inside `if (dbPath !== ':memory:')`), which is why the other controllers initialize fine.

It looks like the `require('path')` → `await import('node:path')` fix from PR #1500 landed in the CLI package but `@claude-flow/memory` wasn't republished with the change. No `alpha.13` exists on npm as far as I can tell.

I could be wrong about the publish/dependency chain — maybe the fix is delivered through a different path I'm not seeing.

### Environment

- `@claude-flow/cli`: v3.5.51 (via `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest`)
- `@claude-flow/memory`: 3.0.0-alpha.12 (resolved in CLI's dependency tree)
- npx cache hash: `85fb20e3e7e3a233`
- Node: v24.6.0
- macOS ARM64 (Darwin 25.3.0)

Happy to keep testing whenever a new version drops, and glad to submit a PR if that would be helpful. Thanks for everything you do with this project.

title: ruvector init fails: checks for pgvector instead of ruvector extension, blocks migrate
body:
## Bug

`ruflo ruvector init` fails when the `ruvector-postgres` Docker image is running because it tries `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` (pgvector), but the image ships the `ruvector` extension instead.

This cascades to `ruflo ruvector migrate`, which fails with `relation "claude_flow.migrations" does not exist` because `init` never created the migrations table.

## Reproduction

```bash
# With ruvector-postgres container running:
PGPASSWORD=claude-flow-test ruflo ruvector init \
  --host localhost --port 5432 --database claude_flow --user claude

# Output:
# ... Checking pgvector extension...  pgvector not installed, attempting to create...
#                                     Failed to create pgvector extension
# [ERROR] Please install pgvector manually

# Then migrate also fails:
PGPASSWORD=claude-flow-test ruflo ruvector migrate \
  --host localhost --port 5432 --database claude_flow --user claude

# Output:
# [ERROR] relation "claude_flow.migrations" does not exist
```

## Expected

- `init` should detect the `ruvector` extension (already installed, v0.3.0) and use `ruvector` type instead of `vector`
- `migrate` should work after a successful `init`

## Evidence

```sql
SELECT extname, extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'ruvector';
-- ruvector | 0.3.0

SELECT typname FROM pg_type WHERE typname = 'ruvector';
-- ruvector  (custom UDT exists and is functional)
```

## Related

- #1520 (same root cause for status/benchmark/optimize)

## Environment

- `ruvnet/ruvector-postgres:latest`
- `ruflo` CLI (npm, latest)
- Node v20.19.6

title: MCP Server: Memory database not initializing - memory_store fails with "Database not initialized"
body:
## Bug Description

When running ruflo as an MCP server via Claude Desktop, the memory database fails to initialize automatically, causing all `memory_store` operations to fail with error: "Database not initialized. Run: claude-flow memory init"

## Environment

- **Version**: ruflo v3.5.51
- **Platform**: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- **Node.js**: v25.8.2
- **Installation**: `npm install -g ruflo`
- **MCP Configuration**: Claude Desktop (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure ruflo as MCP server in Claude Desktop:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ruflo": {
      "command": "/opt/homebrew/bin/ruflo",
      "args": ["mcp", "start"]
    }
  }
}
```

2. Start Claude Desktop (MCP server starts automatically)

3. Attempt to store data via MCP tools:
```javascript
ruflo:memory_store({
  key: "test",
  namespace: "test",
  value: "test data",
  upsert: true
})
```

4. **Result**: Error - "Database not initialized"

## Expected Behavior

The MCP server should automatically initialize the memory database on startup, allowing `memory_store` operations to succeed without manual CLI intervention.

## Actual Behavior

- CLI command `ruflo memory init` successfully initializes database at `~/.swarm/memory.db` and `~/.claude/memory.db`
- MCP server starts successfully with all tools exposed
- `ruflo:memory_store` tool calls fail with "Database not initialized"
- `ruflo:memory_list` returns empty array even after CLI initialization
- `ruflo:embeddings_init` tool exists but fails silently when called through MCP
- `ruflo:hooks_init` succeeds, but doesn't trigger memory initialization

## What We Tried

1. **CLI initialization before MCP start**: Database initializes successfully via CLI but MCP server doesn't access it
2. **Symlinked databases**: Created symlink from `~/.claude/memory.db` → `~/.swarm/memory.db` but MCP server still reports uninitialized
3. **Wrapper script with init**: Created startup script running `ruflo memory init && ruflo mcp start` but init doesn't persist to MCP process
4. **Direct tool calls**: Called `ruflo:embeddings_init` through MCP - fails silently without error message

## Root Cause Analysis

The MCP server process appears to:
1. Start with a fresh, uninitialized in-memory database instance
2. Not persist initialization to disk properly
3. Not read existing initialized databases from `~/.swarm/` or `~/.claude/`
4. Expose initialization tools (`embeddings_init`) that fail silently when called

## Impact

**Critical**: Memory persistence and optimization features are completely non-functional when ruflo runs as an MCP server, which is the primary deployment mode for Claude.ai integration. Users experiencing token limit issues cannot leverage ruflo's advertised memory optimization capabilities.

## Workaround

Currently, only `performance_optimize` and `neural_optimize` tools work through MCP. Memory-based features require manual reactivation per conversation.

## Suggested Fix

1. Add automatic database initialization to `ruflo mcp start` command
2. Ensure MCP server reads from persistent database files (`~/.swarm/memory.db`, `~/.claude/memory.db`)
3. Fix `ruflo:embeddings_init` tool to actually initialize when called through MCP
4. Add database initialization status to MCP server startup output for debugging

## Related

- Performance optimizations (`ruflo:performance_optimize`) work correctly through MCP
- Hooks system (`ruflo:hooks_init`) initializes successfully
- Issue only affects memory/embeddings subsystem

---

**Note**: This blocks the primary use case for ruflo MCP integration - persistent context optimization across conversations to reduce token consumption.

title: feat: Intelligence ↔ Memory Bridge — connect daemon insights to ruflo memory
body:
## Summary

The ruflo daemon workers (map, audit, consolidate, testgaps, optimize) produce insights into the Intelligence Layer (`.claude-flow/data/` JSON files) but nothing flows to the ruflo memory system (`.swarm/memory.db` SQLite + HNSW). These two systems are completely disconnected.

## Problem

- `ruflo memory stats` shows 147 entries — all from interactive `mcp__claude-flow__memory_store` calls
- `.claude-flow/data/auto-memory-store.json` has 1,141 entries from daemon workers and intelligence.cjs
- `patterns` table: 0 entries, `trajectories` table: 0 entries
- The `AutoMemoryBridge` class exists in `@claude-flow/memory` but is not wired up by default

## Proposed Solution

Bridge functions that sync at session boundaries:

- **`syncToMemory()`** — pushes intelligence store entries to `memory.db` (incremental, cursor-tracked, 50/batch)
- **`importFromMemory()`** — pulls `memory.db` entries into intelligence graph (deduped by key+namespace)
- Wire into `session-end` hook (auto-sync after consolidate)
- Wire into `session-restore` hook (auto-import on startup)
- `consolidate()` triggers sync as final step

## Implementation (done in site360, proposing upstream)

- Added to `intelligence.cjs`: `syncToMemory()`, `importFromMemory()`, CLI commands `sync` and `import`
- Wired into `hook-handler.cjs` session-restore and session-end handlers
- Uses `execFileSync('sqlite3', ...)` for synchronous CJS-compatible writes (no new deps)
- Budget: <200ms sync, <100ms import

## Results

- `ruflo memory stats` went from 147 → 236 entries after initial sync
- 87 entries synced to memory.db, 28 imported back
- 54 namespaces preserved correctly

## Related

- ruvnet/ruflo#1499 (AgentDB ReasoningBank bridge bug — missing embedder param)

title: fix: auto-memory hook silently drops all session data + 4 packaging bugs
body:
## Summary

Every session's hook-written memory is silently discarded. Root cause: `AgentDBBackend` does a cross-package `import('@claude-flow/agentdb')` that fails silently in the hook subprocess. Data writes to an in-memory `Map`, lost on process exit.

Additionally: 3 CJS bugs, 2 packaging bugs, and 1 ESM extension bug — all discovered during the same investigation.

---

## ADR-0059 Fixes

### FIX-1: RvfBackend swap in `auto-memory-hook.mjs`

**Bug**: `createBackend()` instantiates `AgentDBBackend`, which does `import('@claude-flow/agentdb')`. This import fails silently because `@claude-flow/agentdb` is not a dependency of `@claude-flow/memory`. The backend degrades to an in-memory `Map` — data writes succeed but are lost on process exit. The `.rvf` file is never created.

**Fix**: Prefer `RvfBackend` (same package, atomic persist, zero native deps). Fall back to `AgentDBBackend` then `JsonFileBackend`.

### FIX-2: ID collision in `intelligence.cjs`

**Bug**: `parseMemoryDir()` ID formula `mem-${file}-${title.slice(0,30)}` produces non-unique IDs across projects. 4,482 entries collapse to 157 unique.

**Fix**: Append `-${entries.length}` index suffix.

### FIX-3: ML-006 scope in `intelligence.cjs`

**Bug**: `bootstrapFromMemoryFiles()` scans ALL subdirectories under `~/.claude/projects/` (51 dirs) instead of just the current project.

**Fix**: Compute `projectSlug` from `cwd`, scope to `~/.claude/projects/${projectSlug}/memory`.

### FIX-4: Ranked dedup in `intelligence.cjs`

**Bug**: `init()` and `consolidate()` build ranked entries from the raw store (with duplicates) instead of the deduplicated set.

**Fix**: `store.map(...)` → `deduped.map(...)` in both functions.

### FIX-5: tool_input snake_case in `hook-handler.cjs`

**Bug**: Claude Code PostToolUse sends `tool_input` (snake_case). Handler checks `toolInput` (camelCase). Every edit is recorded as `file: "unknown"`.

**Fix**: Check `hookInput.tool_input` before `hookInput.toolInput` in prompt resolution and post-edit handler.

### FIX-6: `@claude-flow/memory` optional → required in CLI

**Bug**: `@claude-flow/memory` is `optionalDependencies` in CLI. When `better-sqlite3` fails to compile, npm skips the entire memory package silently. ControllerRegistry loads with 0 controllers.

**Fix**: Move to `dependencies`. 0 controllers is not a valid state.

### FIX-7: `better-sqlite3` optional → required, pinned

**Bug**: `better-sqlite3` was `optionalDependencies` in `@claude-flow/memory`. Compile failures are silent.

**Fix**: Move to `dependencies`, pin to `11.10.0` (confirmed prebuilt binaries for darwin-arm64/x64, linux-x64 with Node 20).

### FIX-8: `github-safe.js` ESM mismatch

**Bug**: `init --full` copies `github-safe.js` which uses ESM syntax (`import`/`export`) but has a `.js` extension. `node -c` fails.

**Fix**: Rename to `github-safe.mjs`.

---

## Prerequisite Patches (included in PR)

These prior patches are prerequisites — ADR-0059 cannot work without them:

| ID | What | Why ADR-0059 needs it |
|----|------|----------------------|
| **WM-003** | `createBackend()` factory + `config.json` reader in `auto-memory-hook.mjs` | ADR-0059's RvfBackend swap is a change TO this function |
| **IN-003/IN-004** | CJS snapshot reader + signal writer in `intelligence.cjs` | Provides the intelligence pipeline ADR-0059's bug fixes target |
| **dc179d605** | Dedup guard in `intelligence.cjs` | Creates the `deduped` variable ADR-0059 references |

---

## Files Changed

| File | Lines | Content |
|------|-------|---------|
| `cli/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs` | +107 | WM-003 + FIX-1 |
| `cli/.claude/helpers/intelligence.cjs` | +157 | IN-003/IN-004 + dc179d605 + FIX-2/3/4 |
| `cli/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs` | +7 | FIX-5 |
| `cli/package.json` | +1/-1 | FIX-6 |
| `memory/package.json` | +2/-2 | FIX-7 |
| `cli/.claude/helpers/github-safe.js → .mjs` | rename | FIX-8 |

---

## Test Results

- Acceptance: **69/69** (12/12 ADR-0059 specific checks)
- Unit: 539/539
- Pipeline: 131/131

---

**PR**: #1528 (1 commit, 6 files — clean branch from upstream main)

Fixes #1526

## Summary

Audit of sparkling/ruflo and sparkling/agentic-flow forks identified 10 fix-on-fix patterns (patches that fix bugs introduced by prior fork patches), 5 upstream-already-fixed cases, and 7 stale patches.

title: Hooks causing ~20s latency on every Claude Code CLI interaction
body:
## [BUG] Hooks causing ~20s latency on every Claude Code CLI interaction

**Environment**
- OS: Ubuntu (WSL2) on Windows
- Claude Code CLI: v2.1.92
- Ruflo/Claude Flow: v3.0.0 (via settings.json)
- Node.js: v22.22.1
- Hardware: 94GB RAM, 24 cores, CUDA 13.2

**Bug Description**
Claude Code CLI becomes extremely slow (~18-21s per prompt) when running inside a project initialized with Ruflo/Claude Flow. The same CLI responds in ~4.8s outside the project directory.

**Reproduction Steps**
1. Initialize a project with Ruflo (`npx ruflo@latest init`)
2. Run `time claude --print "diga oi"` inside the project → ~18-21s, often hangs
3. Run `cd ~ && time claude --print "diga oi"` outside the project → ~4.8s, works fine

**Root Cause Analysis**
The `.claude/settings.json` generated by Ruflo registers 11+ hooks across 9 lifecycle events (SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, PreCompact, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Notification). Each hook spawns a Node.js process via `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs"`, adding cumulative startup latency.

The `SessionEnd` hook consistently fails with:
```
SessionEnd hook [node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs" session-end] failed: Hook cancelled
```

Additionally, the `SessionStart` hook spawns 3 sequential processes (session-restore, auto-memory-hook, daemon-manager with watchdog), and the daemon configuration includes 10 background workers.

**Diagnostic Evidence**
```bash
# Outside project (clean)
$ time claude --print "diga oi"
real    0m4.867s

# Inside project (with Ruflo hooks)
$ time claude --print "diga oi"
real    0m18.199s  # Had to Ctrl+C

# CLI loads instantly without hooks
$ time claude --version
real    0m0.088s

# Network is fast
$ curl -s --max-time 5 https://api.anthropic.com -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}s"
0.161694s
```

**Expected Behavior**
Hooks should not add more than 1-2s of overhead to CLI interactions.

**Suggested Fixes**
1. Run hooks in parallel instead of sequentially
2. Add lazy initialization — don't start all 10 daemon workers on every session
3. Fix the SessionEnd hook that consistently fails
4. Make hook registration opt-in rather than all-on by default
5. Add a `--lightweight` or `--no-hooks` init option for users who don't need the full orchestration stack

**Workaround**
Currently the only workaround is to manually remove or disable hooks from `.claude/settings.json`, which defeats the purpose of using Ruflo.

title: [BUG] Intelligence hooks cause indefinite hang — PageRank on 150MB JSON blocks every CLI interaction
body:
## [BUG] Intelligence hooks cause indefinite hang — PageRank on 150MB JSON blocks every CLI interaction

**Environment**
- OS: Ubuntu (WSL2) on Windows
- Claude Code CLI: v2.1.92
- Ruflo/Claude Flow: v3.0.0 (via settings.json)
- Node.js: v22.22.1
- Hardware: 94GB RAM, 24 cores, CUDA 13.2

---

**Bug Description**

Claude Code CLI hangs indefinitely when running inside a project initialized with Ruflo. The root cause is the intelligence layer (`intelligence.cjs`) performing synchronous PageRank computation on 150MB of JSON data files on every session start and end. All timings below are **minimums** — every test had to be manually killed with Ctrl+C, meaning actual completion time is unknown and potentially much longer.

---

**Root Cause: `intelligence.init()` and `intelligence.consolidate()`**

The `session-restore` hook calls `intelligence.init()` which reads and parses 150MB of JSON, builds a graph with 18,014 nodes, and computes PageRank — **synchronously, on every session start**.

The `session-end` hook calls `intelligence.consolidate()` which reconsolidates all entries, recomputes PageRank, and serializes everything back to disk — **synchronously, on every session end**.

Neither function ever completed during testing. All times below represent the moment Ctrl+C was pressed, not actual completion.

**Data files causing the bottleneck:**

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `.claude-flow/data/graph-state.json` | 94 MB |
| `.claude-flow/data/ranked-context.json` | 32 MB |
| `.claude-flow/data/auto-memory-store.json` | 23 MB |
| **Total** | **150 MB** |

---

**Diagnostic Evidence**

> ⚠️ **Important:** All timings marked "hangs" were terminated with Ctrl+C. The functions never completed on their own. Actual execution time could be significantly higher than the values shown.

### 1. Isolated hook timing (each hook tested individually)

| Hook | Time (at Ctrl+C) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `session-restore` (calls `intelligence.init()`) | **18.1s+ — killed** | CRITICAL |
| `session-end` (calls `intelligence.consolidate()`) | **12.2s+ — killed** | CRITICAL |
| `post-task` (calls `intelligence.feedback()`) | 3.5s | Slow |
| `auto-memory-hook import` | 1.2s | OK |
| `statusline` | 0.9s | OK |
| `route` | 0.05s | Fast |
| `pre-bash` | 0.04s | Fast |
| `post-edit` | 0.05s | Fast |
| `daemon-manager check` | 0.03s | Fast |
| `status` | 0.04s | Fast |
| `notify` | 0.05s | Fast |

### 2. Isolated intelligence function timing (never completed)

```bash
# intelligence.init() alone — killed with Ctrl+C after 23s, never finished
$ time node -e "const i = require('./.claude/helpers/intelligence.cjs'); i.init();"
real    0m23.236s   # MINIMUM — Ctrl+C, did not complete

# intelligence.init() + consolidate() — killed after 35s, never finished
$ time node -e "const i = require('./.claude/helpers/intelligence.cjs'); i.init(); i.consolidate();"
real    0m35.493s   # MINIMUM — Ctrl+C, did not complete
```

### 3. Module loading is instant (not the bottleneck)

```bash
$ time node -e "require('./.claude/helpers/intelligence.cjs')" 2>/dev/null
real    0m0.028s

$ time node -e "require('./.claude/helpers/learning-service.mjs')" 2>/dev/null
real    0m0.211s
```

### 4. CLI without project hooks is fast

```bash
# Outside project directory (no hooks)
$ time claude --print "diga oi"
real    0m4.867s   ✅

# Inside project directory (with Ruflo hooks)
$ time claude --print "diga oi"
real    0m18.199s  ❌ (Ctrl+C, never completed)

# CLI loads instantly
$ time claude --version
real    0m0.088s   ✅

# Network is fast
$ curl -s --max-time 5 https://api.anthropic.com -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}s"
0.161694s   ✅
```

### 5. SessionEnd hook fails 100% of the time

```
SessionEnd hook [node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs" session-end] failed: Hook cancelled
```

This appears on **every single interaction** because the hook has a 10s timeout but `intelligence.consolidate()` never completes within that window — it was still running after 35s when manually killed.

---

**Expected Behavior**

Hooks should not add more than 1-2s of overhead. The intelligence layer should handle 150MB+ datasets without hanging indefinitely.

---

**Suggested Fixes**

1. **Lazy/incremental PageRank** — Don't recompute the full graph on every session. Use incremental updates for new entries only.
2. **Async/background processing** — Move `intelligence.init()` and `intelligence.consolidate()` to the background daemon instead of running them synchronously in hooks.
3. **Data pagination/capping** — Cap the in-memory graph to the top N entries by rank instead of loading all 18,014 nodes.
4. **Binary format** — Replace 150MB of JSON with a binary format (SQLite, MessagePack, or protobuf) for faster read/write.
5. **Skip on short sessions** — For `claude --print` (single-prompt mode), skip intelligence init/consolidate entirely.
6. **Increase timeout or make it configurable** — The `session-end` hook has a 10s timeout but `consolidate()` never finishes within it, guaranteeing failure on every session end.
7. **Add a completion safeguard** — The functions appear to hang indefinitely with no progress reporting or timeout of their own. At minimum, add an internal timeout or progress logging.

---

**Workaround**

The only workaround is to manually remove `intelligence.init()` from `session-restore` and `intelligence.consolidate()` from `session-end` in `.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs`, or to run Claude Code from outside the project directory.

---

**Reproduction**

1. `npx ruflo@latest init` in any project
2. Use the project until `.claude-flow/data/` grows past ~50MB
3. Run `time claude --print "hello"` inside the project
4. Observe indefinite hang (requires Ctrl+C to exit)

**System:** 94GB RAM, 24 cores — this is not a resource-constrained environment. The functions simply never complete.

title: Bug: Global install registers MCP server without cwd, causing all file ops to fail on macOS (process.cwd() = '/')
body:
## Summary

When ruflo is installed globally via the quickstart (`curl ... | bash`) and the MCP server is registered via `claude mcp add ruflo -- ruflo mcp start`, macOS spawns the stdio process with `cwd: "/"`. All `process.cwd()`-based path resolution then targets the root filesystem, which is read-only, causing every file operation to fail silently or throw ENOENT/EACCES.

## How to reproduce

1. Run the ruflo quickstart from `~` (home directory):
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ruvnet/ruflo@main/scripts/install.sh | bash
   ```
2. The quickstart runs `claude mcp add ruflo -- ruflo mcp start` — no `cwd` or `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` is passed.
3. Claude Code launches the MCP server. On macOS, stdio processes with no `cwd` start at `/`.
4. Call `memory_store`, `swarm_init`, `agent_spawn`, or any tool that writes state — they all fail because paths resolve to `/.claude-flow/`, `/.swarm/`, etc.

## Verification

`system_info` returns `"cwd": "/"` confirming the issue:
```json
{ "cwd": "/" }
```

## Root cause

All MCP tool files use `process.cwd()` to build storage paths:
```js
function getSwarmDir() {
    return join(process.cwd(), '.claude-flow/swarm'); // → /.claude-flow/swarm — read-only!
}
```

`CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` is already checked in `hive-mind-tools.js` but is never set by the install script, and no other tool files check it.

## Fix

In the install script, when registering the MCP server, pass `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD`:

```bash
# Instead of:
claude mcp add ruflo -- ruflo mcp start

# Should be:
claude mcp add ruflo -e CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD="$HOME" -- ruflo mcp start
```

Or equivalently, add it to the registered server's env in `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```json
{
  "ruflo": {
    "command": "npx",
    "args": ["ruflo@latest", "mcp", "start"],
    "env": {
      "CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD": "/Users/<username>"
    }
  }
}
```

Additionally, all MCP tool files (`swarm-tools.js`, `agent-tools.js`, `session-tools.js`, `coordination-tools.js`, `github-tools.js`, etc.) should check `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` before falling back to `process.cwd()`, consistent with the pattern already used in `hive-mind-tools.js`.

## Impact

- All users who follow the global quickstart on macOS are affected
- `memory_store`, `swarm_init`, `agent_spawn`, `session_save`, `github_repo_analyze` and ~20 other tools silently fail or throw on first use
- Related to #1524 (memory_store fails with "Database not initialized")

## Environment

- macOS (darwin arm64)
- Node v25.6.1
- ruflo via `npx ruflo@latest`

title: fix: global install MCP server cwd resolution
body:
## fix: global install MCP server CWD resolution

Closes #1532 | Related to #1524

### Problem

When ruflo is installed globally via `npm i -g` and registered as an MCP server, macOS (and some Linux setups) spawn the stdio process at `/` (the filesystem root). Every `process.cwd()`-based file path then resolves to the read-only root filesystem, causing all storage operations to fail silently or throw `EACCES`.

### Solution

Introduced a `getBaseCwd()` helper that resolves the working directory via:

1. `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` environment variable (set by the install script or MCP server registration)
2. `process.cwd()` fallback

A console warning fires when CWD resolves to `/`, making the root-cause immediately visible in logs.

### Layers patched

| Layer | Scope | Files |
|-------|-------|-------|
| **V3 API tools** (`v3/mcp/tools/`) | 7 files — `getBaseCwd()` replaces all `process.cwd()` calls | `cwd-helper.ts` + 6 tool files |
| **CLI runtime tools** (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/`) | 17 files — same pattern | `cwd-helper.ts` + 16 tool files |
| **Memory subsystem** (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/`) | 5 files — same pattern | `cwd-helper.ts` + 4 memory files |

### Additional changes

- **`install.sh`** — Sets `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` during install so the env var is available at MCP server startup
- **`doctor.ts`** — New `checkCwd` health check: warns when CWD resolves to root, reports which source (`CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` vs `process.cwd()`) is active
- **Test** — `cwd-helper.test.ts` covers env-var override, empty-string fallback, and non-root assertion

### Verification

After rebase onto latest `main`:
- 107 `getBaseCwd` references across `v3/`
- 0 bare `process.cwd()` calls remain in `mcp-tools/` or `memory/` (outside the helper itself)
- Both `cwd-helper.ts` files emit a root-CWD console warning
- Doctor command includes the CWD check

### Credits

Thanks to @mgatof91 for reporting #1524 and guiding the fix scope across the three subsystem layers.

plugin-code-intelligence: stub implementations prevent all 5 MCP tools from returning real results
body:
## Problem

The 3 core helper functions in `v3/plugins/code-intelligence/src/mcp-tools.ts` are stubs returning empty data, which means all 5 MCP tools return structurally-correct but empty results.

### Stubs affected

| Function | Current behavior | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| `getFilesInPath()` | `return []` | Architecture analyze, split suggest get no files |
| `performSemanticSearch()` | `return results.slice(0, topK)` where results is `[]` | Semantic search always returns 0 results |
| `getAllRelatedFiles()` | `return changedFiles` (no traversal) | Refactor impact only sees directly-changed files |

Additionally, `GNNBridge.extractImports()` (gnn-bridge.ts line ~500) returns `[]`, producing dependency graphs with **zero edges**. The `buildCodeGraph` call produces nodes but no relationships.

## Root cause

The plugin references `ruvector-gnn-wasm` and `ruvector-mincut-wasm` which do not exist on npm. The actual installed packages are `ruvector-graph-transformer-wasm` (v2.0.4) and `ruvector-attention-wasm` (v0.1.32), which have different APIs. Both bridge `loadWasmModule()` methods throw `'WASM module loading not implemented'`. However, the JS fallback graph algorithms all work correctly — the only missing piece is real file data being fed into them.

## Fix (proposed — implemented locally)

Add two npm dependencies:
- `fast-glob` (already in pnpm store)
- `@claude-flow/embeddings` (already in `plugins/node_modules/`)

Then implement the three stubs:

1. **`getFilesInPath(root)`** — use `fast-glob` with `**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`, ignore node_modules/dist/build/.git/coverage/vendor/\*.min.\*, filter files >100KB via `fs.stat()`

2. **`performSemanticSearch()`** — discover files, embed query and file content (first 200 lines for semantic, 8KB for structural) using `@claude-flow/embeddings` mock provider, compute cosine similarity, threshold 0.1, sort descending, take topK

3. **`getAllRelatedFiles()`** — forward BFS (depth 3) parsing import specifiers with regex, resolve against known project files; reverse scan to find files that import any of the changed files

Additionally, add **`enrichGraphWithEdges(graph)`** — post-process `buildCodeGraph()` result by reading each node file, parsing imports, resolving to graph node IDs, and injecting `{ type: 'import', weight: 1 }` edges. Wire into the 3 tool handlers (`architecture-analyze`, `refactor-impact`, `split-suggest`) after each `buildCodeGraph()` call.

## Verified results (after fix)

- Semantic search for 'authentication middleware user role' over `apps/web/server/`: **5 ranked results** with similarity scores ~0.79
- Architecture analysis on `apps/web/server/`: **152 nodes, 393 edges** (vs 152 nodes, 0 edges before fix), health score 95.9
- All 5 MCP tools return real, non-empty data

title: plugin-code-intelligence: stub implementations prevent MCP tools from returning real results
body:
## Summary

The `@claude-flow/plugin-code-intelligence` plugin ships with 5 MCP tools that are structurally complete (types, schemas, validation, bridge integration) but return empty results because 3 core helper functions in `src/mcp-tools.ts` are stubs.

## Stubs Found

| Function | Line | Current behavior |
|----------|------|-----------------|
| `getFilesInPath(rootPath)` | ~663 | `return []` |
| `performSemanticSearch(...)` | ~647 | Returns empty array |
| `getAllRelatedFiles(changedFiles)` | ~668 | Returns input unchanged |

Additionally:
- `GNNBridge.extractImports()` (gnn-bridge.ts:500) returns `[]`, producing dependency graphs with zero edges
- Both bridge `loadWasmModule()` methods throw `'WASM module loading not implemented'`
- The plugin references non-existent packages `ruvector-gnn-wasm` / `ruvector-mincut-wasm`. The actual installed packages are `ruvector-graph-transformer-wasm` (v2.0.4) and `ruvector-attention-wasm` (v0.1.32) which have different APIs.

## Impact

All 5 MCP tools (`code/semantic-search`, `code/architecture-analyze`, `code/refactor-impact`, `code/split-suggest`, `code/learn-patterns`) return structurally correct but empty results.

## Fix Applied Locally

We wired up the 3 stubs with real implementations:

1. **`getFilesInPath`**: Uses `fast-glob` for recursive TS/JS file discovery with size filtering (100KB cap)
2. **`performSemanticSearch`**: File discovery → embedding via `@claude-flow/embeddings` (MiniLM 384-dim) → cosine similarity ranking → topK results
3. **`getAllRelatedFiles`**: Forward BFS import traversal (depth 3) + reverse dependency scan
4. **`enrichGraphWithEdges`** (new): Post-processes `buildCodeGraph()` output to inject real import edges, compensating for the `extractImports()` stub

### Results after fix:
- Semantic search: Returns ranked results with similarity scores
- Architecture analysis: 152 nodes, 393 edges (was 0), health score 95.9

### Dependencies added:
- `fast-glob` ^3.3.3
- `@claude-flow/embeddings` ^3.0.0-alpha.1

## Suggested Upstream Fix

Either:
1. Ship the stubs as real implementations (as described above)
2. Update `GNNBridge.extractImports()` to parse actual import statements
3. Update `loadWasmModule()` to reference the correct WASM packages (`ruvector-graph-transformer-wasm` instead of `ruvector-gnn-wasm`)

cleanup --force deletes entire .claude/ directory including user-owned Claude Code config (agents, skills, commands, settings.local.json, memory.db, worktrees)
body:
## Summary

`npx ruflo@latest cleanup --force` deletes the entire `.claude/` directory wholesale, including files that were never created by ruflo. This destroys user-curated Claude Code config (`settings.local.json` allow rules, custom `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/`) along with the legitimate ruflo artifacts.

The dry-run output is misleading: it shows `.claude/` as a single line item (`Claude settings, helpers, agents`), implying the whole directory belongs to ruflo. In practice, `.claude/` is **shared territory** between Claude Code's native subsystems (agents, skills, slash commands, settings, worktrees, memory.db) and ruflo's own helpers/hooks. The cleanup tool cannot tell them apart.

## Reproduction

1. Project has been used for a while with both Claude Code and ruflo:
   ```
   .claude/
   ├── agents/              ← Claude Code native (custom user agents)
   ├── skills/              ← Claude Code native (custom user skills)
   ├── commands/            ← Claude Code native (slash commands)
   ├── settings.json        ← contains BOTH ruflo hooks AND user permissions
   ├── settings.local.json  ← user's Bash allowlist (Claude Code native)
   ├── helpers/             ← ruflo hook scripts
   ├── memory.db            ← Claude Code native
   ├── launch.json          ← Claude Code native
   └── worktrees/           ← git worktrees from `git worktree add`
   ```

2. Run `npx ruflo@latest cleanup` (dry-run):
   ```
   Artifacts found:
     [would remove] dir   .claude  (549.1 MB) - Claude settings, helpers, agents
     [would remove] dir   .claude-flow  (233.5 MB)
     [would remove] dir   .swarm  (193.0 KB)
   ```

3. Running `--force` deletes the entire `.claude/` directory, taking everything with it.

## Impact

A user who installed ruflo for evaluation and decides to uninstall loses:
- All custom Claude Code agents/skills/commands they created
- Their `settings.local.json` Bash allowlist (which can take hours to curate)
- Their `memory.db` (Claude Code's local SQLite memory)
- Active `git worktrees/` (which on a multi-GB monorepo can contain in-progress work)
- Their `settings.json` permissions block (rebuilt from scratch)

This is referenced by user `JustSuperHuman` in #1159: *"pretty lame the cleanup deletes the .claude folder alltogether...."*

## Suggested fix (pick one)

**Option A — Surgical cleanup:** Only delete the specific subpaths ruflo created:
```
.claude/helpers/        (always — ruflo creates this)
.claude/settings.json   ← edit to remove `hooks` field + `claudeFlow` block,
                          NEVER delete the file
.claude-flow/           (always — ruflo's runtime data dir)
.swarm/                 (always)
.hive-mind/             (always)
data/                   (always, but check it's the ruflo `data/` not user code)
coordination/           (always)
```

Leave all other paths under `.claude/` alone.

**Option B — Manifest-based cleanup:** When `ruflo init` runs, write a manifest of every file/folder it creates to `.claude-flow/manifest.json`. The cleanup command reads the manifest and deletes only what's in it. Anything ruflo didn't create is preserved.

**Option C — Interactive prompt:** Before deleting `.claude/`, the cleanup tool should enumerate the actual contents and ask: "These items in `.claude/` were not created by ruflo: `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `settings.local.json`. Keep them? [Y/n]". The current `--force` flag should still be allowed to bypass this, but the default should be to preserve user files.

**Option D — Document the destruction loudly:** At minimum, the README and CLI help text for `cleanup --force` should warn explicitly: *"This deletes your ENTIRE `.claude/` directory, including custom agents, skills, slash commands, and Claude Code's settings.local.json. If you have any files in `.claude/` that you did not create via ruflo, back them up first."*

My vote: **Option B (manifest)** is the only correct solution long-term. Option A is the minimum acceptable fix today.

## Workaround (for users facing this now)

Don't use `cleanup --force`. Do it manually:

```bash
# Edit settings.json to remove the hooks field and claudeFlow block (preserve everything else)
python3 -c "
import json
with open('.claude/settings.json') as f: d = json.load(f)
d['hooks'] = {}
d.pop('claudeFlow', None)
with open('.claude/settings.json', 'w') as f: json.dump(d, f, indent=2)
"

# Then surgically remove only ruflo-owned paths
rm -rf .claude/helpers .claude-flow .swarm .hive-mind coordination

# npm side
npm uninstall @claude-flow/cli agentic-flow      # in projects
npm uninstall -g ruflo claude-flow @claude-flow/cli   # global
rm -rf ~/.npm/_npx
```

This preserves `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/memory.db`, `.claude/launch.json`, `.claude/worktrees/`, and everything else under `.claude/` that ruflo didn't put there.

## Environment

- Tested with: `ruflo@3.5.75`
- npm: v11.12.1
- macOS Darwin 25.1.0 (Apple Silicon)
- Claude Code: v2.1.94

title: fix: critical security & performance fixes across 6 packages
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive security hardening and performance optimization across 6 V3 packages (`cli`, `browser`, `memory`, `security`, `swarm`, `plugins`), addressing 16 vulnerabilities identified through security audit and devil's advocate review. Includes 22 automated verification tests and fixes for pre-existing test suite failures.

- **44 files changed**, 1125 insertions, 328 deletions
- **5 new files** created (utilities, configs, verification tests)
- **0 type errors** across all 5 affected packages
- **969 tests pass** across memory (353), swarm (172), security (444)

## Security Fixes

### Critical (CRIT-01 through CRIT-03)

| ID | Vulnerability | Fix | Files |
|----|--------------|-----|-------|
| CRIT-01 | SQL injection in embeddings search | Parameterized queries (`db.prepare`/`bind`) replacing string interpolation | `embeddings.ts` |
| CRIT-02 | Command injection via `execSync` template literals | `execFileSync` + input validation regex | `import.ts`, `init.ts` (×2), `agent-browser-adapter.ts` |
| CRIT-03 | Browser eval arbitrary code execution | 12 dangerous pattern blocklist + configurable 20KB length limit | `browser-tools.ts` |

### High (HIGH-01 through HIGH-05)

| ID | Vulnerability | Fix | Files |
|----|--------------|-----|-------|
| HIGH-01 | Unrestricted `child_process` imports | ESLint `no-restricted-imports` + `no-restricted-modules` rules | `.eslintrc.json` |
| HIGH-02 | Hive-mind truthiness bug (`!== false` treats undefined as truthy) | Changed to `=== true` | `hive-mind.ts` |
| HIGH-03 | Prototype pollution via `JSON.parse` on user data | `safeJsonParse` with JSON reviver stripping `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` | 3 memory backends + new `json-security.ts` |
| HIGH-04 | Plugins loaded without sandboxing silently | Added `console.warn` on unsandboxed plugin load | `manager.ts` |
| HIGH-05 | HNSW hash collisions (32-bit djb2) | Dual-hash (djb2+sdbm) producing 53-bit values with bidirectional map + linear probing | `agentdb-backend.ts` |

### Devil's Advocate Review Fixes (5 additional)

| ID | Vulnerability | Fix |
|----|--------------|-----|
| DA-CRIT-1 | Cross-package import breaks npm publish | Local `json-security.ts` in memory package |
| DA-CRIT-2 | SQL injection via PostgreSQL schema names | `validateSchemaName()` in all 6 ruvector commands via `pg-utils.ts` |
| DA-CRIT-3 | PID injection in `mcp-server.ts` | `/proc` read + `execFileSync` replacing `execSync` with PID interpolation |
| DA-HIGH-3 | SQL injection via crafted timestamps | `validateTimestamp()` with ISO 8601 regex |
| DA-HIGH-5 | ESLint rule gap (`require()` not caught) | Added `no-restricted-modules` rule |

## Performance Fixes

| ID | Optimization | Impact |
|----|-------------|--------|
| PERF-01 | `BoundedSet<T>` for gossip `seenMessages` | Map-based LRU eviction capped at 100K entries — prevents OOM |
| PERF-02 | `Promise.allSettled` for bulk operations | Batch size 50, logs partial failures instead of aborting |
| PERF-03 | CLI lazy loading | Sync imports reduced from 37 → 10 core commands; async `getCommandsByCategory()` |

## Test Suite Fixes (pre-existing failures resolved)

- **Security** (13→0 failing suites): Fixed 11 broken import paths, added missing `vitest.config.ts`, added `allowedDirectories` to test fixtures, fixed `sanitizePath` expectation
- **Memory** (5→0 failing suites): Fixed hardcoded repo path, controller test expectation, database count assertion
- **Swarm** (2→0 failing tests): Fixed sub-millisecond latency assertions for mocked operations

## New Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/ruvector/pg-utils.ts` | PostgreSQL identifier & timestamp validation |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.eslintrc.json` | `child_process` import restriction rules |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/security-verification.test.ts` | 22 automated verification tests for all scenarios |
| `v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/json-security.ts` | `safeJsonParse` — prototype pollution prevention |
| `v3/@claude-flow/security/vitest.config.ts` | Local vitest config (was missing, inheriting broken root ref) |

## Test plan

- [x] All 5 packages type-check with 0 errors (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [x] Memory: 9/9 suites, 353/353 tests pass
- [x] Swarm: 4/4 suites, 172/172 tests pass
- [x] Security: 13/13 suites, 444/444 tests pass
- [x] 22 security verification tests pass covering:
  - SQL injection prevention (parameterized queries)
  - Prototype pollution prevention (safeJsonParse with __proto__, constructor, nested)
  - Command injection prevention (container names, model names, PID)
  - Browser eval security (length limits, 12 pattern blocks)
  - BoundedSet eviction correctness
  - Bulk operation resilience (Promise.allSettled partial failure handling)
  - Schema/timestamp validation (SQL injection payloads rejected)
  - ESLint child_process restriction (import + require)
- [x] CLI `--help` displays all 35 commands across 5 categories with lazy loading

title: Bug: bare require() calls in ESM modules cause "require is not defined" on autopilot/claims commands (v3.5.75)
body:
## Summary
  `ruflo autopilot status` and `ruflo claims list` crash on a clean install of v3.5.75 with `ReferenceError: require is
  not defined`. Three source files in `@claude-flow/cli` contain bare `require()` calls inside ESM modules (`"type":
  "module"` in package.json) but do not import `createRequire` from `node:module`.

  ## Affected files
  All paths relative to `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/`:

  - `autopilot-state.ts` — uses `require('crypto')`, `require('fs')`, `require('path')` inside function bodies with no
  top-level `createRequire` setup
  - `commands/autopilot.ts` — calls into `autopilot-state.ts` and additionally has `require()` calls in the `logCommand`
   action
  - `commands/claims.ts` — uses `require('path')` in `getClaimsConfigPaths()`, `require('fs')` in `loadClaimsConfig()`,
  `require('path')` in `saveClaimsConfig()` (all with an `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires`
  comment)

  TypeScript compiles these verbatim to the `dist/` output, so the shipped
  `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/autopilot-state.js` and the two `dist/src/commands/*.js` files contain the same broken
  `require()` calls.

  ## Reproduction
  ```bash
  npm install -g ruflo@3.5.75
  ruflo autopilot status
  # → ReferenceError: require is not defined
  ruflo claims list
  # → ReferenceError: require is not defined
  ```

  Environment: macOS 15.4 (darwin 25.4.0), Apple Silicon, Node v22+, Homebrew-managed global npm.

  ## Fix
  Add to the top of each affected source file:

  ```ts
  import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
  const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);

 Or, preferred: convert the bare `require()` calls to static `import` statements at the top of the file (since
  `crypto`, `fs`, `path` have ESM equivalents — `node:crypto`, `node:fs`, `node:path`).

  ## History
  - v3.5.49 fixed an equivalent issue for AgentDB controllers by replacing `require('path')` with dynamic `import()` —
  that fix was not applied to autopilot/claims.
  - v3.5.52 (PR #1534) added `getProjectCwd()` / `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` support (closed my issue #1524). Both improvements
  are working correctly.
  - Current workaround on my machine: a `sed` patch in my `~/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` that prepends the
  `createRequire` setup on every session start because `npm install -g ruflo@latest` re-ships the unpatched files.

  ## Severity
  High for anyone using autopilot or claims. Low for MCP-only users (MCP server paths don't hit the affected modules).

title: Bug: autopilot commands fail with 'require is not defined' (CJS in ESM package)
body:
## Summary

All `autopilot` subcommands (CLI and MCP) fail immediately with `require is not defined` because `autopilot-state.js` uses CJS `require()` calls in an ESM package (`"type": "module"`).

## Version

- `@claude-flow/cli` bundled in `ruflo@3.5.70`
- Node.js v20.19.6

## Reproduction

```bash
ruflo autopilot status
# [ERROR] require is not defined

# MCP also fails:
# mcp__claude-flow__autopilot_status → MCP error -32603: require is not defined
```

## Root Cause

`dist/src/autopilot-state.js` contains 12 CJS `require()` calls that were not converted to ESM imports during compilation:

| Line | Call |
|------|------|
| 74 | `require('crypto')` |
| 88-89 | `require('fs')`, `require('path')` |
| 114-115 | `require('fs')`, `require('path')` |
| 128-129 | `require('fs')`, `require('path')` |
| + 5 more | `require('fs')`, `require('path')` |

Additionally, `dist/src/commands/autopilot.js` lines 185-186 have `require('fs')` and `require('path')` in the `log --clear` handler.

## Expected

All `require()` calls should be ESM `import` statements (or use `createRequire` from `node:module`).

## Impact

**All** autopilot functionality is broken — `status`, `enable`, `disable`, `config`, `reset`, `log`, `learn`, `history`, `predict`, `check`.

title: [Bug] `memory` commands ignore `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` — bare `process.cwd()` in `memory-bridge.js` and `memory-initializer.js` breaks MCP memory tools under Claude Desktop
body:
# [Bug] `memory` commands ignore `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` — bare `process.cwd()` in `memory-bridge.js` and `memory-initializer.js` breaks MCP memory tools under Claude Desktop

## Summary

`ruflo memory list` / `store` / `retrieve` / `init` do not honor the
`CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` environment variable that PR #1534 (v3.5.52) introduced for
project-cwd resolution. They still resolve `.swarm/memory.db` via bare
`process.cwd()`, so any caller that launches `ruflo mcp start` from a
directory other than the workspace (most notably **Claude Desktop**) gets
`Database not found` for every memory tool call — even though the workspace
env var is set correctly on the child process.

This effectively breaks `mcp__ruflo__memory_*` tools in Claude Desktop today.
`mcp__ruflo__memory_list` returns empty, `memory_store` errors with
`Database not initialized`, and the end-user sees an empty memory store even
though the real `.swarm/memory.db` is populated and persisting fine.

## Environment

- ruflo: **v3.5.75** (latest on npm as of 2026-04-08)
- Install path: `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/ruflo`
- node: v25.8.2 (Homebrew)
- macOS: 26.4 (Darwin 25.4.0), Apple Silicon
- Claude Desktop: latest, config-based MCP server (not an installed extension)
- Workspace: `/Users/mgatof/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-MSG-ENT/Claude`
  with populated `.swarm/memory.db` (372 KB, 8 entries in `user` namespace,
  entries 3–4 days old — verified persistent across sessions)

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Confirm the DB exists and has entries (run from the workspace)
cd /Users/mgatof/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-MSG-ENT/Claude
ruflo memory list --namespace user
# => Shows 8 entries, all with vector embeddings. Works as expected.

# 2. Now run the same command from any other directory,
#    explicitly passing CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD pointing back at the workspace:
cd /
CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD="/Users/mgatof/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-MSG-ENT/Claude" \
  ruflo memory list --namespace user
# => [ERROR] Failed to list: Database not found

# 3. Same thing for store:
cd /
CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD="/Users/mgatof/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-MSG-ENT/Claude" \
  ruflo memory store --key test --value test --namespace debug
# => [INFO] Storing in debug/test...
# => [ERROR] Database not initialized. Run: claude-flow memory init
```

All three should have succeeded (and steps 2 and 3 would have succeeded for
any command touched by PR #1534, e.g. `ruflo autopilot status`).

## Expected behavior

`ruflo memory *` commands should resolve the project root using the same
`getProjectCwd()` helper that PR #1534 introduced, so that setting
`CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` from a wrapper script, `launchd` plist, or Claude Desktop
MCP config entry correctly points the memory subsystem at the workspace's
`.swarm/memory.db`.

## Actual behavior

Memory commands fall back to bare `process.cwd()`, so the workspace env var
is silently ignored and the command looks for `.swarm/memory.db` relative to
whatever directory the caller happens to be in.

## Root cause (code references)

In the installed v3.5.75 dist, the memory subsystem has **at least 16 bare
`process.cwd()` call sites** that PR #1534 missed:

`src/memory/memory-bridge.js`:
```
31:    const swarmDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.swarm');
33:        return path.join(swarmDir, 'memory.db');
40:        return path.join(swarmDir, 'memory.db'); // fallback to safe default
```

`src/memory/memory-initializer.js`:
```
360:   const swarmDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.swarm');
461:   const swarmDir = path.join(process.cwd(), '.swarm');
888:   path.join(process.cwd(), 'memory.db'),
889:   path.join(process.cwd(), '.claude/memory.db'),
890:   path.join(process.cwd(), 'data/memory.db'),
891:   path.join(process.cwd(), '.claude-flow/memory.db'),
976:   const swarmDir = path.join(process.cwd(), '.swarm');
1158:  const swarmDir = path.join(process.cwd(), '.swarm');
1207:  const swarmDir = path.join(process.cwd(), '.swarm');
1697:  const swarmDir = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.swarm');
```

`src/commands/memory.js`:
```
1234:  const claudeDir = path.join(process.cwd(), '.claude');
1235:  const claudeDbPath = path.join(claudeDir, 'memory.db');
```

For comparison, grepping for `getProjectCwd` in the same dist tree shows
that the helper IS used in `mcp-tools/*.js` (hive-mind, agent, swarm,
session, terminal, performance, github, system, types) — but not in any
file under `memory/` or `commands/memory.js`. This is consistent with
PR #1534's description ("replace process.cwd() in autopilot + claims +
MCP tool registrations") — the memory path layer appears to have been
out of scope for that PR.

## Proposed fix

Replace the bare `process.cwd()` calls in `memory-bridge.js`,
`memory-initializer.js`, and `commands/memory.js` with the existing
`getProjectCwd()` helper (same pattern as PR #1534). Specifically the root
resolver at `memory-bridge.js:31` is the primary one — most other sites are
downstream of it and could be refactored to take the root as a parameter
rather than re-reading cwd.

A minimal repro-fix would be:

```js
// memory-bridge.js
import { getProjectCwd } from '../utils/project-cwd.js'; // or wherever #1534 put it
// ...
const swarmDir = path.resolve(getProjectCwd(), '.swarm');
```

## Impact / why this matters

- **Claude Desktop MCP integration is broken for memory tools.**
  Desktop spawns `ruflo mcp start` as a child process with a non-workspace
  cwd (in my case, effectively `/`), and passes `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` via the
  `env` key in `claude_desktop_config.json`. Every other ruflo MCP tool
  resolves the workspace correctly via PR #1534 — only memory tools don't.
- **Silent data-loss appearance.** End user sees "0 entries across all
  namespaces" and reasonably concludes ruflo memory isn't persisting. The
  real DB is fine and untouched; the tool just can't find it. This is a
  confusing failure mode.
- **Any launchd / systemd / wrapper setup hits this.** Not specific to
  Claude Desktop — any invocation of `ruflo mcp start` from a wrapper that
  sets `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` but doesn't `cd` first is affected.

## Workaround (current, in my setup)

Wrap `ruflo mcp start` in a shell script that does `cd "$CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD"`
before exec'ing the command. This is exactly the kind of wrapper that
PR #1534 was supposed to make unnecessary, so it's an annoying regression
against the stated goal of that PR.

## Related

- PR #1534 (v3.5.52) — "Replace process.cwd() with getProjectCwd() in 20+
  sites" — excellent fix but scoped to autopilot/claims/MCP tool
  registration, didn't cover the memory/ subtree.
- Issue #1524 (closed by #1534) — original report that motivated the
  `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` plumbing.

## Related

- **Sibling issue (also being filed today):** `ruflo autopilot` and
  `ruflo claims` fail on fresh 3.5.75 install — bare `require()` calls
  inside ESM modules (`autopilot-state.js`, `commands/autopilot.js`,
  `commands/claims.js`). Same root category (files PR #1534 didn't
  touch) — worth triaging together because both block Claude Desktop
  and fresh-install flows on 3.5.75.
- PR #1534 (v3.5.52) — "Replace process.cwd() with getProjectCwd() in 20+
  sites" — excellent fix but scoped to autopilot/claims/MCP tool
  registration, didn't cover the memory/ subtree.
- Issue #1524 (closed by #1534) — original report that motivated the
  `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` plumbing.

title: [Bug] `ruflo autopilot` and `ruflo claims` fail on fresh 3.5.75 install — bare `require()` calls inside ESM modules
body:
# [Bug] `ruflo autopilot` and `ruflo claims` fail on fresh 3.5.75 install — bare `require()` calls inside ESM modules

## Summary

On a fresh `npm install -g ruflo@latest` (currently v3.5.75), running
`ruflo autopilot status` or any `ruflo claims` subcommand fails immediately
with:

```
ERROR require is not defined
```

The cause is three compiled ESM files in `@claude-flow/cli` that contain
bare `require('crypto')`, `require('fs')`, `require('path')` calls without
the `createRequire(import.meta.url)` shim that ESM requires. The package's
`package.json` has `"type": "module"`, so Node treats these files as ESM
and `require` is not a global.

This blocks `autopilot` and `claims` completely on a clean install. I have
been working around it for weeks with a session-start hook that `sed`s the
`createRequire` import into the top of each file, but it is a regression
that should be fixed upstream so new users and new machines don't hit it.

## Environment

- ruflo: **v3.5.75** (latest on npm as of 2026-04-08)
- Install path: `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/ruflo`
- @claude-flow/cli: 3.5.75 (`"type": "module"` in its package.json)
- node: v25.8.2 (Homebrew)
- macOS: 26.4 (Darwin 25.4.0), Apple Silicon

## Reproduction

```bash
# On a machine that has never installed ruflo before:
npm install -g ruflo@latest
ruflo --version          # => v3.5.75  (fine)
ruflo doctor             # => passes (doesn't touch the broken modules)
ruflo autopilot status
# => ERROR require is not defined
ruflo claims list
# => ERROR require is not defined
```

## Expected behavior

`ruflo autopilot status` and `ruflo claims *` should run cleanly on a
fresh install with no local patching.

## Actual behavior

Both commands throw `require is not defined` at the first bare `require()`
call, because the files are loaded as ESM and do not define `require` via
`createRequire`.

## Root cause (code references)

Three files in the compiled `dist/` tree contain bare `require(...)` calls
but do **not** have `import { createRequire } from 'module'; const require =
createRequire(import.meta.url);` at the top (or the equivalent in the
TypeScript source before compilation):

`node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/autopilot-state.js`:
```
76:    const crypto = require('crypto');
90:    const fs = require('fs');
91:    const path = require('path');
116:   const fs = require('fs');
117:   const path = require('path');
...etc, multiple sites throughout the file
```

`node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/autopilot.js`:
```
187:   const fs = require('fs');
188:   const path = require('path');
```

`node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/claims.js`:
```
17:    const path = require('path');
25:    const fs = require('fs');
46:    const fs = require('fs');
47:    const path = require('path');
```

The corresponding TypeScript sources (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/
autopilot-state.ts` etc. on the `main` branch) contain the same bare
`require()` calls — this is an upstream source-level bug, not a build-step
bug.

## Proposed fix

Either:

**(a)** Add the shim at the top of each affected `.ts` source file so the
compiled `.js` inherits it:

```ts
import { createRequire } from 'module';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
```

**(b)** Replace the CommonJS `require('…')` calls with ESM dynamic or
static imports:

```ts
// top of file
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
```

Option (b) is cleaner (no CJS/ESM bridge at all) but is a larger diff.
Option (a) is a 2-line patch per file and matches the pattern already used
in other files in the same tree.

## Workaround (currently in use on my machine)

`~/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` runs a `sed` that inserts the
`createRequire` shim into each of the three files after every
`npm install -g ruflo@latest`. Rough shape:

```bash
for f in autopilot-state.js commands/autopilot.js commands/claims.js; do
  full="/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/$f"
  if ! grep -q "createRequire" "$full"; then
    sed -i '' '1i\
import { createRequire } from '"'"'module'"'"';\
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);\
' "$full"
  fi
done
```

After this patch runs, `ruflo autopilot status` and `ruflo claims list`
succeed. But the patch is overwritten every time `npm install -g ruflo`
re-runs, so it has to be re-applied on every upgrade.

## Impact

- **Breaks core commands on a clean install.** `autopilot` and `claims`
  are two of the headline v3 features, so this is the first thing a new
  user hits after `npm install`.
- **Breaks MacBook migration / new-machine setup.** I am about to migrate
  to a new Mac and had to document this as a manual post-install step so
  future-me can get ruflo working again.

## Related

- **Sibling issue (also being filed today):** `memory` commands ignore
  `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` — bare `process.cwd()` in `memory-bridge.js` and
  `memory-initializer.js`. Same root category (files PR #1534 didn't
  touch) — worth triaging together because both block Claude Desktop
  integration on a fresh 3.5.75 install.
- #1524 (closed) — my earlier `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` report that was fixed in
  PR #1534; these two remaining issues are the "missed spots" from that
  cleanup pass.

```
v3/@claude-flow/memory/benchmarks/longmemeval/
├── harness.ts                   # Main benchmark runner (4 modes)
├── types.ts                     # TypeScript interfaces
├── adapters/
