fix(marketplace): rename legacy plugin.json to fix install (#1676)
body:
## Summary
- Renames `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → `.claude-plugin/plugin.legacy.json`
- Fixes #1676 — `/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo` followed by `/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo` failing
- Single-file `git mv`, fully reversible

## Root cause
`.claude-plugin/` contained both manifests at the same level:
- `plugin.json` — legacy single-plugin manifest (`name: claude-flow`, v2.5.0, leftover from when this repo was a single plugin)
- `marketplace.json` — current marketplace (`name: ruflo`, 32 plugins)

Claude Code's plugin loader detected `plugin.json` first and treated the repo as a single plugin instead of a marketplace, so the `ruflo` marketplace was never registered and downstream `/plugin install ...@ruflo` calls failed.

The `marketplace.json` itself is valid — all 32 plugin sources resolve to real `plugins/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifests.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI `validate-marketplace.yml` passes
- [ ] `/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo` lists 32 plugins
- [ ] `/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo` succeeds
- [ ] `/plugin install ruflo-aidefence@ruflo` succeeds

## Rollback
`git mv .claude-plugin/plugin.legacy.json .claude-plugin/plugin.json`

Closes #1676

title: fix(ruvocal/mcp): SSE fallback hits same rate limit on 429 — both transports show 429 to user
body:
## Symptom

When an MCP server upstream of `ruvocal` (the SvelteKit chat-UI app behind https://flo.ruv.io/) returns HTTP 429 (rate-limited), users see this combined error in the UI:

```
HTTP transport failed: Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint: Rate exceeded.
SSE fallback failed: SSE error: Non-200 status code (429)
```

Both transports show 429 because they POST to the **same upstream endpoint**. Falling back from Streamable HTTP to SSE on a rate-limit response just produces a second rate-limit response — the user gets twice the wait and a misleading error message that implies the SSE transport itself failed.

## Root cause

`src/ruvocal/src/lib/server/mcp/clientPool.ts` always falls back to SSE when the Streamable HTTP transport throws — including on 4xx/5xx HTTP status codes that are *guaranteed* to recur on the SSE transport (which targets the same upstream URL).

```ts
try {
    await client.connect(new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(url, { requestInit }));
} catch (httpErr) {
    firstError = httpErr;
    await client.connect(new SSEClientTransport(url, { requestInit }));  // ← always retries
}
```

There is also no cooldown / memoization, so every subsequent call hammers the upstream while it is still rate-limited.

## Fix

Implemented in `src/ruvocal/src/lib/server/mcp/clientPool.ts`:

1. **Skip SSE fallback for definitive HTTP failures** (4xx and 5xx, except 408 Request Timeout). 408 and network-level errors still fall back since those are recoverable.
2. **Surface a typed `McpRateLimitedError`** on 429 with `status`, `retryAfterMs`, and `serverName` fields so callers can build user-friendly UI (e.g. show a countdown, disable the tool until cooldown expires).
3. **Honor `Retry-After`** when the upstream provides it — capped at 60s, defaults to 5s.
4. **Memoize the failure** for the cooldown window so subsequent `getClient` calls during cooldown short-circuit instead of pounding the upstream. Cooldown is cleared by `evictFromPool()` (caller signals stale connection) and `drainPool()`.

## Verification

`src/ruvocal/src/lib/server/mcp/clientPool.spec.ts` — 8 vitest cases:

```
✓ skips SSE fallback on 429 and throws McpRateLimitedError
✓ honors Retry-After when present in the error message
✓ memoizes the 429 failure and skips network on subsequent calls during cooldown
✓ skips SSE fallback on 4xx (e.g. 401)
✓ skips SSE fallback on 5xx (e.g. 503)
✓ falls back to SSE on transport-level / network errors with no HTTP status
✓ falls back to SSE on 408 Request Timeout (recoverable)
✓ surfaces 429 even when the SSE fallback also reports 429
```

8/8 pass against the implementation.

## Out of scope (potential follow-ups)

- Surface `McpRateLimitedError` to the user with a friendly UI badge + countdown timer (currently the error is caught at the conversation route level and reported as a generic failure).
- Per-tool exponential backoff inside `httpClient.callMcpTool` for retryable conditions distinct from connection-level failures.
- Telemetry: count rate-limit events per upstream MCP server so operators can see which servers need quota raises.

title: fix(ruvocal): auto mode is silent — duplicate label + autopilotMaxSteps setting is dead wiring
body: ## Symptom Reported by a user testing https://flo.ruv.io/ : the AUTO toggle in the chat input "doesn't seem to be working". ## Root cause — two bugs ### Bug 1: Same label on both states (UI lies about its state) `src/lib/components/chat/ChatWindow.svelte:825` ```svelte {$settings.autopilotEnabled ? 'AUTO' : 'AUTO'} ``` Both branches produce the same text. The button color does change (emerald-500 when on, gray-100 when off), but the text label is identical, so users perceive nothing happening when they click it. Verified live with the agent browser: ``` $ npx agent-browser --session flo-auto --json eval \ 'document.querySelector("[aria-label=\"Toggle autopilot mode\"]").innerText' {"success":true,"data":{"result":"AUTO"}} ``` After clicking the button (toggling state), the text is still `"AUTO"`. ### Bug 2: `autopilotMaxSteps` setting is dead wiring `src/lib/types/Settings.ts:69` defines `autopilotMaxSteps: number` (default `10`), accepted by `/api/v2/user/settings` and `/settings/(nav)/+server.ts`, but: - **never sent in the chat request body** (`src/routes/conversation/[id]/+page.svelte:235` only sends `autopilot: bool`) - **not in the zod schema** for `POST /conversation/[id]` (`+server.ts:143`) - **server hardcodes** `const maxLoops = autopilot ? 30 : 10;` in `runMcpFlow.ts:463` ignoring user input Net effect: the setting is purely cosmetic. Users who lower it in settings still get 30 loops; users who raise it still get 30 loops. ## Fix | File | Change | |------|--------| | `src/lib/components/chat/ChatWindow.svelte:825` | `'AUTO' : 'AUTO'` → `'AUTO' : 'MANUAL'` so the label actually flips | | `src/routes/conversation/[id]/+page.svelte:235` | Send `autopilotMaxSteps` from settings in the chat request body | | `src/routes/conversation/[id]/+server.ts:143` | Zod schema accepts optional `autopilotMaxSteps` (clamped to `[1, 100]`) | | `src/routes/conversation/[id]/+server.ts:580` | Pass `autopilotMaxSteps` into `ctx` | | `src/lib/server/textGeneration/types.ts:25` | `TextGenerationContext.autopilotMaxSteps?: number` | | `src/lib/server/textGeneration/index.ts:67` | Forward to runMcpFlow | | `src/lib/server/textGeneration/mcp/runMcpFlow.ts:50, 463` | Accept param; `maxLoops = autopilot ? min(autopilotMaxSteps ?? 30, 100) : 10` (back-compat default 30 when client doesn't send a value) | | `src/routes/settings/(nav)/+server.ts:21` + `src/routes/api/v2/user/settings/+server.ts:25` | Add `autopilotMaxSteps` to settings POST schema; expose in GET response | ## Why this matters - **Bug 1** is the literal "doesn't seem to be working" report — the UI gives no textual feedback on the toggle. A user who doesn't notice the color shift assumes nothing happened. - **Bug 2** is the worse silent failure: a configurable setting that does nothing. Anyone who set `autopilotMaxSteps` lower (e.g., to 5 to save tokens) still gets 30 loops; anyone who set it higher to allow longer chains still gets capped at 30. ## Verification - Live click verified the broken text label via agent-browser before the fix - Typecheck on the wiring changes is clean (errors elsewhere are pre-existing in unrelated files) - The earlier rate-limit test suite (`clientPool.spec.ts`, 8/8) still passes ## Out of scope - A spinner / state pill showing remaining autopilot steps as the loop progresses (already partially exists via `autopilotStep` derived state) - A "Why is autopilot off?" explainer for non-tool models (currently the toggle just disappears)

title: Ran a methodical install study on Ruflo v3.6.27 — sharing what surprised me + a few suggestions*
body:
Hey Ruflo team,

I've been integrating Ruflo into my own multi-agent runtime and ran into enough "wait, what?" moments that I decided to do a structured install study and write everything down. I'm sending it to you because the product is genuinely impressive and I want to keep using it — but a handful of papercuts kept tripping me up, and I figure you'd want to know which ones bit hardest.

This is friendly feedback, not a bug report dump. If any of it is wrong or already on your roadmap, I'd love to hear that.

## What I tested

Latest published version: **ruflo 3.6.27**.

I tested all three documented install paths from a clean machine state, repeated each in a fresh temp workspace, snapshotted the filesystem before/after, and diffed:

- `npx ruflo@latest init` and its 4 flag variants (`--minimal`, `--full`, `--start-all`, `init wizard`)
- `/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo` + `/plugin install ruflo-{core,swarm,autopilot,federation}@ruflo`
- `claude mcp add ruflo -- npx ruflo@latest mcp start` at all three scopes (user, project, local)

Plus uninstall (`ruflo cleanup --force`), multi-workspace coexistence (3 parallel installs), and a per-turn cost benchmark via `claude -p --output-format json`.

## Where my expectations didn't match reality

Roughly ranked by how much each tripped me up.

### 1. Plugin install ≠ `npx init` (and the README calls it "Recommended")

Going by the README, I expected `/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo` (and the three sibling plugins) to give me Ruflo. It doesn't, really:

- Plugin install creates **zero workspace files**.
- It does NOT register the Ruflo MCP server. So `memory_store`, `swarm_init`, `agent_spawn`, etc. are not available to Claude.
- It doesn't install hooks.
- Across all 4 plugins combined, I got 9 agents, 7 commands, 12 skills (vs `npx init`'s 98 agents / 60+ commands / 30 skills / full MCP).

Plugin install is a clean lite-mode integration — just slash commands and a few definitions — but it's marketed as the recommended path next to `npx init`, and they are not equivalent.

**Suggestion:** Either label them clearly ("Plugin install — slash commands only" vs "CLI install — full Ruflo loop"), or have the plugin trigger the MCP registration too. Right now folks who follow the "Recommended" path will think Ruflo is broken because the tools are missing.

### 2. `npx ruflo init` silently appends to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

This one I genuinely had to dig to confirm. Every `init` adds this 4-line block to my user-global Claude rules file:

```
# Ruflo Integration (auto-generated by ruflo init)
When working on multi-file tasks or complex features, use ToolSearch to find and invoke ruflo MCP tools.
Key tools: memory_store, memory_search, hooks_route, swarm_init, agent_spawn.
Check system-reminder tags for [INTELLIGENCE] pattern suggestions before starting work.
```

The good news: it's **idempotent**. I ran `init` in 3 different workspaces and the block stayed at count = 1. That's a really nice touch and I want to call it out.

The not-so-good news: it's not in the README, the USERGUIDE, or any `--help` output. A user-global file is a sensitive surface — a one-liner in the install summary like "added a pointer block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so Claude knows about Ruflo's tools globally" would prevent the surprise.

**Suggestion:** Document it. Maybe even gate it behind a `--no-global` flag for folks who want to keep their global file pristine.

### 3. `--minimal` ships broken hooks

`npx ruflo init --minimal` writes a `.claude/settings.json` with 4 hooks declared, all pointing at `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs`. But `--minimal` doesn't install the helpers directory. So every hook fires and silently fails to find its handler.

**Suggestion:** Either bundle the helpers in `--minimal`, or omit the hook declarations entirely. The current state is a footgun for users who picked `--minimal` to be cautious.

### 4. README's `--wizard` flag doesn't exist; `init wizard` is a subcommand

README says `npx ruflo@latest init --wizard`. The actual surface is `npx ruflo@latest init wizard` (no leading dashes — it's a subcommand under `init`).

**Suggestion:** One-line README fix.

### 5. README's MCP add command uses the legacy package name

README:
```
claude mcp add ruflo -- npx -y @claude-flow/cli@latest
```

USERGUIDE (the canonical form, verified by `ruflo mcp --help`):
```
claude mcp add ruflo -- npx ruflo@latest mcp start
```

The legacy `@claude-flow/cli` form does still work, but it's confusing to have two different commands across two docs.

**Suggestion:** Update README to match USERGUIDE.

### 6. `ruflo cleanup --force` is more like "ruflo cleanup --partial"

I expected `cleanup --force` to remove what `init` installed. It actually removes only:
- `.claude/helpers/`
- `.claude-flow/`
- The hooks block from `.claude/settings.json` (the file is selectively rewritten, not deleted)

It leaves behind:
- `.claude/agents/` (98 files)
- `.claude/commands/` (60+ files)
- `.claude/skills/` (30 files)
- `.mcp.json` (so the MCP server is still registered)
- The workspace `CLAUDE.md`
- The `# Ruflo Integration` block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

This is fine if you mean "stop the active Ruflo loop without deleting the prompt library" — but the command is named `cleanup` and the help text says "Remove project artifacts created by claude-flow/ruflo". I expected total removal.

**Suggestion:** Either offer a `cleanup --all` / `cleanup --everything` flag, or rename the current behavior to `cleanup --runtime` so the partial scope is obvious. Plus document the residue path explicitly.

### 7. `cleanup` leaves an orphaned `statusLine` reference

The selective settings.json rewrite preserves the `statusLine` block, which still points at `.claude/helpers/statusline.cjs` — but `cleanup` just deleted `.claude/helpers/`. The next claude session in that workspace will hit a missing-file error from the statusline hook.

**Suggestion:** If `cleanup` removes helpers, also strip the statusLine reference (or null it out).

### 8. Per-turn cost is significant and worth being upfront about

I measured a single cold ping (`claude -p "Reply with: pong"`):

| | Vanilla workspace | After `npx init` |
|---|---|---|
| `duration_ms` | 1670 | 2073 |
| `total_cost_usd` | $0.21 | $0.33 |
| `cache_creation_input_tokens` | 33,592 | 53,276 |

Just from `init` (not even using any Ruflo tools), every turn pays roughly **+24% wall, +59% cost, +20K tokens**. Over a 100-turn build that's ~$12 / 2M tokens of overhead just for the context-load.

I don't think this is a bug — it's the cost of putting all that orchestration knowledge into context. But it's recurring, not one-time, and it should be in the install docs alongside the disk footprint.

**Suggestion:** Add a "what this costs you per turn" table to the install docs. Or even surface it post-install: "FYI, you'll see ~$0.10-0.15 per turn of context-load overhead while Ruflo is loaded."

### 9. `--start-all` daemon does not auto-terminate

`npx ruflo init --start-all` spawns a 148 MB daemon that survives the install completing. Stopping it requires `npx ruflo daemon stop` or manual `pkill`.

**Suggestion:** Note this clearly in the install summary. ("Daemon started — PID X. Stop with: ruflo daemon stop.")

### 10. `claude mcp add -s project|local` is not cwd-aware (Claude Code limitation, not yours, but worth knowing)

This isn't really a Ruflo issue, but it bit me when scripting installs:

```bash
(cd /tmp/some-fresh-workspace && claude mcp add -s project ruflo -- npx ruflo@latest mcp start)
```

…doesn't write `.mcp.json` to `/tmp/some-fresh-workspace`. It writes to whatever Claude Code thinks the current "active project root" is, ignoring my `cd`. So the canonical `npx init` (which writes `.mcp.json` directly) is the only reliable path for programmatic per-workspace install.

If you want to ship a "Install Ruflo into this workspace" Claude Code skill, write `.mcp.json` directly — don't shell out to `claude mcp add`.

## What worked great (genuinely — credit where due)

- **`npx ruflo init` Just Works.** 2 seconds with a warm npx cache. No prompts. No surprises in exit codes. Idempotent across re-runs. This is the right default.
- **The `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` block is idempotent.** Multiple installs don't duplicate. Loved that.
- **Each workspace gets fully independent state** (`.claude/`, `.claude-flow/`, `.swarm/`, `.mcp.json`). No cross-workspace contamination. Two parallel claude sessions in two workspaces get independent MCP server processes.
- **`--full` flagging the optional MCP servers correctly.** `flow-nexus` is `requiresAuth: true` and `ruv-swarm` is `optional: true` in the generated `.mcp.json`. That's the right metadata.
- **The wizard UI is clean.** Arrow-key menus, sensible defaults, the summary table at the end. Drove it via tmux without trouble.
- **`init upgrade --add-missing`** existing as a documented re-run mode is great — most installers don't think about that.
- **`~/.claude.json` is not touched by `npx init`.** This is a really good architectural choice — it means `init` is immune to Claude Code's `~/.claude.json` concurrent-write race that bites a lot of MCP installers. Keep this property.

## What I'd love to see (the wish list)

In rough priority order:

1. **README clarity on plugin vs CLI install.** This is the single biggest "I thought I had Ruflo and didn't" issue.
2. **Document the `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` mutation** + offer `--no-global` for folks who want to opt out.
3. **Either fix or remove `--minimal`'s broken hooks**.
4. **Rename or split `cleanup`** so the partial scope is obvious. Add a `cleanup --all`.
5. **Per-turn cost callout in the docs** — set expectations about recurring overhead.
6. **README docs cleanup** — `--wizard` → `init wizard`, fix the legacy `@claude-flow/cli` MCP add command.
7. **Daemon lifecycle clarity** — install summary should say "daemon running, here's how to stop it".

If you want the full SSOT I built (12 markdown files with verbatim commands, before/after snapshots, diffs, confidence flags), I'm happy to share. Mostly I want to be a useful test case — Ruflo is the most ambitious orchestration layer I've seen on top of Claude Code and I'd like to help it land cleanly for the next wave of folks who try it.

Thanks for shipping it. Genuinely excited to keep building on this.

Cheers

title: Bash hook creates empty files at project root via $TOOL_INPUT_command interpolation
body:
# Bash hook creates empty files at project root via $TOOL_INPUT_command interpolation

**Severity:** High (data pollution, every project affected)
**Affected file:** `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` (lines 24, 86)
**Platform observed:** Windows 10 / Git Bash, Claude Code

## Bug

`hooks.json` interpolates `$TOOL_INPUT_command` (and other `$TOOL_INPUT_*`, `$PROMPT`) into a double-quoted string:

```json
{
  "matcher": "^Bash$",
  "hooks": [{
    "command": "npx claude-flow@alpha hooks pre-command --command \"$TOOL_INPUT_command\""
  }]
}
```

When the bash command being executed contains a double quote (very common: `node -e "..."`, `python -c "..."`, `git commit -m "..."`), the wrapping `"..."` quotes break and the shell re-parses the inner content. Any `>` character is interpreted as a redirection operator, creating empty files at the current working directory (project root).

## Reproduction

1. Enable claude-flow plugin in Claude Code on Windows.
2. Run any Bash tool command containing `"` and `>`, e.g.:
   ```
   node -e "console.log('a=', 5 > 3)"
   ```
3. Inspect project root â€” empty file named `3` is created.

After ~24h of normal usage across multiple projects, dozens of empty files accumulate with names like `0`, `40)`, `maxWidth)`, `{,+`, `console.log(k))`, `t.classList.remove('active'))`, etc. â€” each name being the text fragment after a `>` in code that the agent ran.

## Affected hooks (same root cause)

- `PreToolUse` `^Bash$` â†’ `$TOOL_INPUT_command`
- `PostToolUse` `^Bash$` â†’ `$TOOL_INPUT_command`
- `UserPromptSubmit` â†’ `$PROMPT` (every prompt with quotes/redirects vulnerable)
- `PreToolUse` `^Task$` â†’ `$TOOL_INPUT_description`
- `PreToolUse` `^(Grep|Glob|Read)$` â†’ `$TOOL_INPUT_pattern`
- `PostToolUse` `^(Grep|Glob|Read)$` â†’ `$TOOL_INPUT_pattern`

## Fix

The companion file `.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` already uses the safe stdin pattern. Apply the same approach in `plugin/hooks/hooks.json`:

```json
{
  "command": "cat | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' | tr '\\n' '\\0' | xargs -0 -I {} npx claude-flow@alpha hooks pre-command --command '{}'"
}
```

This reads the command from the hook's stdin JSON (which Claude Code provides), and uses `xargs -I {}` to pass it as a single argv element to npx â€” bypassing shell re-parsing entirely.

## Workaround for affected users

1. Patch `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` with the stdin pattern above.
2. Restart Claude Code (hooks loaded at SessionStart).
3. Clean up parasite files at project roots (PowerShell):
   ```powershell
   Get-ChildItem . -Force -File | Where-Object { $_.Length -eq 0 -and $_.Name -notmatch '^\.' -and $_.Name.Length -lt 30 } | Remove-Item -Force
   ```

## Notes

- Bug is silent â€” no error logged, files just appear at CWD.
- On Windows + Git Bash the issue is severe because most agent operations have CWD = project root.
- Cross-platform fix should also address `$PROMPT` and `$TOOL_INPUT_pattern` interpolations (same vulnerability class).

title: Ruflo Evaluation Review and Upstream Fix Requests
body:
# Ruflo Evaluation Review and Upstream Fix Requests

**To:** ruvnet (Ruflo maintainer)
**From:** Liberation of Bajor team — local-first agent orchestration on macOS
**Date:** 2026-05-04
**Repo we evaluated against:** `ruvnet/ruflo` (commit `f8ce233`); plugin `ruflo-core` v0.1.0
**Claude Code version tested:** current as of 2026-05-04
**Total experiments run:** 9 (probe + V1–V3 A/B + 5-slice portfolio)

---

## Why we wrote this

We spent meaningful engineering time evaluating Ruflo as an integration target for our workflow and arrived at a clean drop verdict. We want to send that verdict upstream because (a) several of the failures we hit are fixable bugs you may not be aware of, and (b) it's not obvious to us whether our use case is one Ruflo intends to support. If it is, fixing the bugs would unlock a real production user. If it isn't, we'd rather know now so we can move on without expecting the integration to mature toward us.

This isn't a complaint document. It's an integrator's report from a serious evaluation. Numbers, log evidence, and reproducer paths are included throughout.

---

## Our workflow in one paragraph

We run a deterministic file-based orchestrator on a developer's Mac. The orchestrator owns a queue (markdown files with frontmatter), a state machine (STAGED → PENDING → IN_PROGRESS → DONE → EVALUATING → ACCEPTED → ARCHIVED), and a git lock-protocol that makes the orchestrator the sole writer to `main`. It dispatches three specialized AI agent roles by spawning `claude -p` subprocesses: Rom (writes code), Nog (reviews code), and Bashir (runs regression tests). Each role gets a per-slice git worktree, a heartbeat file, and a token-telemetry pipe. Roles do not talk to each other directly; they communicate through the queue. The orchestrator is intentionally dumb and predictable. No production deployment surface — it runs locally and merges to a local main branch.

Our integration question for Ruflo was narrow: replace the `claude -p` invocation in the spawn step with Ruflo, role by role, smallest blast radius first. Everything else — queue, register, heartbeat, lock-protocol — stays.

---

## What we hoped Ruflo would buy us — six expectations

We tested explicitly against this list. The labels (G1–G6) are how we'll reference each downstream.

| # | Expectation | Our motivation |
|---|---|---|
| **G1** | Cheaper per-slice cost via smart model routing | Rom (writes code) needs a strong model. Nog and Bashir don't always — Bashir checks ACs and reports pass/fail; Nog applies a verdict to a diff. Routing those to Haiku, GPT-4o-mini, or Gemini Flash should save money without quality loss. |
| **G2** | Cushion against single-provider rate limits | We hit Anthropic's 5-hour rate limit twice in one session and had a session-credential expire mid-slice. Multi-provider failover would smooth this. |
| **G3** | Better Rom output via RAG over the codebase | Hypothesis: when Rom writes a new module, semantic search over existing patterns produces closer-to-correct first drafts than guessing from a flat read. |
| **G4** | RAG for the other roles | Nog with retrieval over past Nog verdicts (catches drift in review standards). Bashir with retrieval over past test failures (catches repeat failure modes faster). Dax (architect) with retrieval over past ADRs (lower priority). |
| **G5** | Swarm coordination for complex slices | Hypothesis to test: decomposing one large slice into a reader/writer/tester swarm via Ruflo produces better output than a single Rom doing it all. We didn't have a strong prior; worth one measurement. |
| **G6** | Don't break the orchestrator | Hard constraint. Whatever we adopt must integrate at the spawn step without altering queue/register/lock semantics. |

---

## What we found — per expectation

| # | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **G1** | Not Ruflo's right shape for us. | Ruflo's provider routing lives at the agent-execution layer (the `agent_spawn` MCP tool's `model` parameter is a Claude-only enum). Our agents don't execute inside Ruflo's runtime; they execute as `claude -p`. The proxy approach (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` → LiteLLM / OpenRouter / agentic-flow proxy) is the right interception point for our architecture. We're pursuing that thread independently. |
| **G2** | Same as G1. | Same axis. Proxy approach handles failover. |
| **G3** | Ruflo loses decisively on a real retrieval task. | Cross-file rename: `registerEvent` → `appendSliceEvent` across 51 files / 230 call sites. Plugin install path (`claude plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo --scope user`) used. MCP server pre-warmed. Both runs produced **byte-identical diffs**. Ruflo: +35% wall time, +163% cost ($0.50 vs $0.19), +100% turns, +203% input tokens, **0 tool invocations**, **0 hooks fired**. |
| **G4** | Cannot run, even with everything else fixed. | The pathway depends on the model voluntarily calling Ruflo retrieval tools. Across V1, V2, V3 (slices 282 / 284 / 285), and the G3 retest (slice 289), the model invoked **zero** Ruflo MCP tools across four independent experiments. Without that pathway, none of the G4 experiments can be run. |
| **G5** | Swarm produces zero output. | We ran a 3-phase audit task: a reader sub-agent gathers context, a writer produces consolidated metrics, a tester validates findings. `ruflo swarm init`, `ruflo swarm start`, `ruflo swarm coordinate --agents 3`, `ruflo hive-mind spawn --claude` — every command succeeded at the framework level. **Zero phases completed. Zero output.** Rom-alone (single Claude Code subagent) finished the same 3 phases in ~45 seconds with full accuracy. |
| **G6** | Trivially satisfied — orchestrator was untouched throughout. | — |

The deeper diagnostic across G3, G4, G5 is **the same root cause class**: Ruflo registers a tool surface at the framework or MCP level but does not wire that tool surface into the contexts where it's needed (loader for hooks, spawned-agent tool registry for swarm). Details below.

---

## Architectural issues we hit — four bugs, ordered by load-bearing weight

### Issue 1 — Hooks defined at marketplace root, not per-plugin (most load-bearing)

**Symptom:** With `ruflo-core` installed via `claude plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo`, Claude Code loads the plugin's 3 skills, 1 command, and 3 agents successfully. **Zero hooks load.**

**Where we looked:** Ruflo defines hooks at `ruflo/.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`. Claude Code's plugin loader looks for hooks at `<plugin>/hooks/hooks.json` (per-plugin, inside each plugin directory).

**Cross-check:** We compared against the `hookify` plugin (a different Claude Code plugin we tested as a positive control). `hookify` places hooks inside its own plugin directory. Its 4 hooks loaded correctly in `claude -p`.

**Why this matters more than anything else in this report:** Your README's value proposition is *"After init, just use Claude Code normally — the hooks system automatically routes tasks, learns from successful patterns, and coordinates agents in the background."* The hooks ARE the value. Without them, Ruflo is a pile of MCP tools the model demonstrably doesn't call. Across four experiments with hooks effectively disabled (because they don't load), we observed zero benefit.

**Reproducer:** `experiments/ruflo-fix-2/findings.md` and `experiments/ruflo-fix-2/debug-log-ruflo-core.txt` (debug log proving 0 hooks loaded).

**Fix request:** Move hook definitions from `ruflo/.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` to per-plugin `<plugin>/.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`. Hookify's layout is the working reference.

### Issue 2 — Spawned-agent tool registry doesn't include Ruflo tools

**Symptom:** `ruflo hive-mind spawn --claude` launches a `claude -p` agent with a coordination prompt that references `mcp__ruflo__*` tools. Those tools are not present in the spawned agent's tool registry. The agent starts, sees nothing matching the tools it's told to use, and exits immediately.

**Where we looked:** Ruflo's swarm spawn passes a coordination prompt to the spawned `claude -p`. The spawned process is started without an `--mcp-config` referencing the Ruflo MCP server, so its MCP tool registry is empty for `mcp__ruflo__*`.

**Why this matters:** The swarm framework creates rich metadata (swarm IDs, topology tables, agent slot allocations). All of it is bookkeeping that goes nowhere because the workers can't actually do the work the coordinator told them to do. The hive-mind / swarm path is non-functional end-to-end in this configuration.

**Reproducer:** `experiments/g5-swarm/run-b-swarm/` (Ruflo run produced 0 output) vs `experiments/g5-swarm/run-a-rom-alone/` (single Rom finished 3/3 phases in ~45s with full accuracy).

**Fix request:** When `ruflo hive-mind spawn --claude` launches a worker, ensure the spawned `claude -p` invocation includes an `--mcp-config` (or equivalent) pointing at the Ruflo MCP server, so worker tools registered at framework level are actually present in the worker's tool namespace. Alternatively, generate coordination prompts that reference only tools known to be available to the spawned worker.

### Issue 3 — MCP server startup race against Claude Code's hardcoded 30s timeout

**Symptom:** First-time invocation of `npx -y claude-flow@latest mcp start` from a cold npx cache hits a Claude Code MCP-startup timeout. Logged as `Starting connection with timeout of 30000ms` followed by the server staying in "still connecting" state for the entire session. Zero claude-flow tools register; the model falls through to native tools.

**Diagnosis:** The `claude-flow@latest` package is roughly 1.8 MB across 999 files. Cold npx download + extraction + spawn can exceed 30 seconds. Once the npx cache is warm, connection completes in ~1.2 seconds.

**Mitigation we deployed:** Pre-warm the cache with `npx -y claude-flow@latest --version` before invoking `claude -p`. With this, V1 and V2 of our A/Bs successfully registered all 237 tools.

**Why this matters:** First-time and CI-style invocations (cold cache) silently fail without visible error. The user sees "Ruflo is loaded" in the configuration but observes that no Ruflo tools appear in any session. The failure mode is silent and the diagnosis non-obvious — we burned a full slice (V3 / slice 285) before we identified the cause.

**Reproducer:** `docs/ruflo/MCP-CONNECTION-FIX.md` plus `experiments/ruflo-fix-1/runs/run-{1..5}.json`.

**Fix requests, in order of preference:**

1. **Reduce package footprint.** 1.8 MB / 999 files is large for a tool whose first-run time is gated by a 30s timeout. A leaner core package (with optional plugins lazy-loaded) would push first-time-success rates above 99%.
2. **Document the pre-warm pattern in your README.** The mitigation is simple but only obvious once you've diagnosed the bug.
3. **Upstream:** Coordinate with Anthropic on a `--mcp-startup-timeout` flag or a `--wait-for-mcp` pattern so users with large MCP servers can extend the window. (This is Anthropic's call, not yours — but a documented timeline for landing it would help.)

### Issue 4 — Tool descriptions don't compete with Claude Code's native tools

**Symptom:** With 237 Ruflo MCP tools loaded into context, the model called **zero** of them across V1, V2, V3, and slice 289 (G3 v2). Tasks ranged from single-module code generation to a 230-call-site cross-file refactor. The model rationally chose `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, and `Edit` every time.

**Diagnosis:** This is partly model behavior and partly a tool-description shape. Native tools have tight integration, low token overhead per invocation, and the model has strong priors about when to use them. Ruflo's tools enter the context as ~26 KB of definitions; many overlap with native capabilities (e.g., `memory_search` competing with `Grep`); few have descriptions that establish a clear advantage on a specific task class.

**Why this matters:** The "237 tools" figure is a feature in Ruflo's marketing but a liability in Claude Code's tool-selection process. The model doesn't read 237 descriptions and reason about which is best; it pattern-matches to tools whose use cases are sharply differentiated from native ones.

**Reproducer:** Our tool-call counts across all four experiments — 0 invocations in every case. See `docs/ruflo/RAG-AB-FINDINGS.md`, `RAG-AB-FINDINGS-V2.md`, `RAG-AB-FINDINGS-V3.md`, and `bridge/queue/289-DONE.md`.

**Fix requests:**

1. **Differentiate descriptions.** For each tool, lead the description with a one-sentence "Use when native X doesn't help because Y" framing. The model selects tools by description; vague descriptions lose to specific ones every time.
2. **Reduce surface.** 237 tools is a lot for a session context. A "lite" tool set (memory + retrieval + the 3 most differentiated capabilities) defaulted on, with the rest opt-in via plugin selection, would improve signal-to-noise dramatically.
3. **Route via hooks, not via tool calls.** This is your stated design philosophy already (auto-routing via hooks). Once Issue 1 is fixed, the tool-call problem becomes much less load-bearing because the hooks system is supposed to fire automatically without the model having to decide.

---

## Summary of fix requests

| # | Fix | Priority | Difficulty (our guess) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Move hook definitions from marketplace root to per-plugin directories | **Critical** — blocks the headline value prop | Low (file relocation + manifest update) |
| 2 | Wire spawned-agent tool registries to include `mcp__ruflo__*` (or stop generating prompts that reference unavailable tools) | **High** — blocks swarm value prop end-to-end | Medium |
| 3 | Reduce cold-cache footprint and/or document the pre-warm mitigation | **Medium** — silent failure mode for new users | Low (docs); Medium (footprint) |
| 4 | Tighten tool descriptions; consider a lite default surface | **Medium** — reduces context overhead and improves tool-call rate | Low (docs); Medium (surface refactor) |

If only one of these gets prioritized, the highest-leverage fix is #1. Hooks-not-loading is the difference between "Ruflo's auto-routing magic happens for free" (your pitch) and "Ruflo is 26 KB of inert tool definitions the model ignores" (what we observed for an entire investigation).

---

## The question we'd like answered

Is the use case described in §"Our workflow in one paragraph" — a deterministic file-based orchestrator that spawns `claude -p` subprocesses for specialized agent roles, with the integration target being the spawn step — one that Ruflo intends to support?

Two reasons we're asking explicitly:

1. **Our integration target is the `claude -p` invocation, not Ruflo's runtime.** We don't want to migrate our orchestrator into Ruflo's runtime. The deterministic state machine, the file-based queue, the lock-protocol — all of those are deliberate architectural choices that Ruflo's swarm-coordinator-led runtime is structurally incompatible with. So our consumption model is "Ruflo as a value-add layer attached to `claude -p`," not "Ruflo as the orchestrator." Is that a supported integration model in your view, or are we trying to use Ruflo against its grain?

2. **If yes, the fixes above are roughly what we'd need.** If no, we should know — because then "drop Ruflo for our use case" is the right architectural answer regardless of whether the bugs get fixed, and we'd save you the issue triage.

We're not asking for a commitment, just a candid read. "Yes, this should work, here's the timeline for the fixes" is great. "Yes in principle but realistically not for 6+ months" is also great — we can plan around it. "No, that's not what Ruflo is for" is honestly fine — we'd rather know than keep coming back.

---

## What's not in this review

- **Federation, vector memory persistence, advanced security features, GOAP planner, web UI.** All untested. Out of scope for our integration target.
- **Anthropic's side of the equation.** The 30s MCP timeout is hardcoded in Claude Code, not in Ruflo. We've noted it as an upstream-Anthropic ask. We mention it here only because it interacts with Ruflo's package size to produce the silent-failure mode in Issue 3.
- **Cost-routing pivot.** We're pursuing this as a proxy in front of `claude -p` (LiteLLM / OpenRouter / agentic-flow proxy). It's working out architecturally for us; we don't need Ruflo for this thread.

---

## Reference — what we ran

| Slice | What | Outcome doc |
|---|---|---|
| 277 | Initial probe of `claude-flow` and `agentic-flow` CLI surfaces | `docs/ruflo/RUFLO-PROBE-FINDINGS.md` |
| 282 | A/B v1: code generation, bare MCP attachment | `docs/ruflo/RAG-AB-FINDINGS.md` |
| 284 | A/B v2: cross-file retrieval (naive shape) | `docs/ruflo/RAG-AB-FINDINGS-V2.md` |
| 285 | A/B v3: forced tool use; surfaced the connection race | `docs/ruflo/RAG-AB-FINDINGS-V3.md` |
| 286 | Initial drop verdict (later identified as design-flawed) | `docs/ruflo/LEARNINGS.md` |
| 287 | Diagnosis of MCP startup race; pre-warm fix | `docs/ruflo/MCP-CONNECTION-FIX.md` |
| 288 | Headless plugin install path; discovered hook bug | `docs/ruflo/PLUGIN-INSTALL-HEADLESS.md` |
| 289 | A/B v4: real retrieval task, plugin install path applied | `bridge/queue/289-DONE.md` |
| 290 | G4-Nog (blocked by lack of data + tool-call pathway) | `docs/ruflo/G4-NOG-RAG-FINDINGS.md` |
| 291 | G5 swarm vs Rom-alone | `docs/ruflo/G5-SWARM-FINDINGS.md` |

Reproducer experiments under `experiments/rag-ab/`, `experiments/ruflo-probe/`, `experiments/ruflo-fix-1/`, `experiments/ruflo-fix-2/`, `experiments/g4-nog/`, `experiments/g5-swarm/`.

We're happy to share full logs or attach individual findings docs as separate issues if you'd like to triage piece-by-piece.

---

Thank you for reading. Whatever direction you take this — fix all four, fix some, or tell us we're off-base architecturally — we appreciate the work going into Ruflo and the candor of a clear answer.

— The Liberation of Bajor team

title: Coder agents ignore ADRs and only reference `docs/SPEC.md`, causing architecture drift
body:
In a spec-driven full-stack setup, the Architect agent correctly generates Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) under `docs/adr/` (e.g., tech stack and authentication decisions). However, when Backend and Frontend coder agents are initialized, they only reference `docs/SPEC.md` and do not consult the ADRs.

This leads to a disconnect between defined architecture and implementation, increasing the risk of inconsistencies and architectural drift—especially in multi-agent parallel development.

---

### Expected Behavior

All coder agents (backend and frontend) should:

* Treat ADRs in `docs/adr/` as authoritative alongside `docs/SPEC.md`
* Incorporate architectural decisions (e.g., framework, auth strategy) into implementation
* Maintain alignment with the spec-driven development approach

---

### Actual Behavior

* Backend and Frontend coder agents only read from `docs/SPEC.md`
* ADRs are ignored during implementation
* Resulting code may conflict with architectural decisions

---

My Prompt was:

`Build a full-stack application using a spec-driven development approach with a Python backend and React frontend.
Define architecture using ADRs and structure the system with DDD bounded contexts to avoid implementation drift.
Implement authentication (login), a dashboard UI, and integrate a database for persistent storage.
The application should fetch and display real-time Nifty stock prices relevant to my country.
Ensure strict alignment between specs and implementation, even when multiple agents or modules are developed in parallel.`

title: docs: fix init/MCP drift surfaced in #1744 install study
body:
## Summary

Fixes two of the documentation papercuts logged in #1744:

### 1. `init --wizard` → `init wizard` (subcommand, not a flag)

Per `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/init.ts:445-447`:

```ts
const wizardCommand: Command = {
  name: 'wizard',
  description: 'Interactive setup wizard for comprehensive configuration',
  ...
};
// ...
subcommands: [wizardCommand, checkCommand, skillsCommand, hooksCommand, upgradeCommand],
```

`wizard` is registered as a subcommand under `init`, and `init --help` shows the canonical form as `claude-flow init wizard`. The flag form may parse but the docs were wrong about it being canonical.

Updated 5 occurrences across `README.md` (1) and `docs/USERGUIDE.md` (4).

### 2. README MCP add command — drop legacy package name

Before:
```bash
claude mcp add ruflo -- npx -y @claude-flow/cli@latest
```

After (matches `USERGUIDE.md` and `ruflo mcp --help`):
```bash
claude mcp add ruflo -- npx ruflo@latest mcp start
```

Both forms still work, but having two different commands across two docs was a friction point #1744 specifically called out.

title: fix(agents): coder agents now read docs/adr/*.md alongside docs/SPEC.md (#1749)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1749 — coder agents (backend, frontend, generic) consult only `docs/SPEC.md` and ignore ADRs under `docs/adr/`, causing architectural drift in spec-driven multi-agent workflows.

### Three agent definitions updated

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `.claude/agents/core/coder.md` | Task-tool default `coder` subagent — used when an agent calls `Task({subagent_type: "coder", ...})` |
| `.claude/agents/templates/implementer-sparc-coder.md` | SPARC Refinement / Completion phase coder template |
| `plugins/ruflo-core/agents/coder.md` | Plugin form invoked when ruflo-core is loaded |

Each now has an **"Authoritative project documents"** section with these contract clauses:

1. **Read BOTH `docs/SPEC.md` AND `docs/adr/*.md`** before architecture/scope-affecting work
2. **SPEC describes WHAT, ADRs describe HOW.** ADRs are *binding* unless superseded by a newer `status: Accepted` ADR
3. **Multi-agent case explicit:** ADRs are the cross-agent contract that prevents bounded-context drift between parallel backend / frontend / tester implementations
4. **Conflict path:** on disagreement with an ADR, surface it (propose either following the ADR or drafting a successor) — do not silently diverge

### Why this matters (per the issue's repro)

The reporter's prompt was:
> Build a full-stack application using a spec-driven development approach with a Python backend and React frontend. Define architecture using ADRs and structure the system with DDD bounded contexts to avoid implementation drift.

When the architect generates ADRs (e.g. "Auth: Auth0 OAuth 2.0", "DB: PostgreSQL with row-level security") and then backend / frontend coders are spawned without reading those ADRs, the resulting code can pick competing technologies — exactly the drift the prompt was trying to prevent.

This change makes the ADR contract explicit in every coder agent's prompt, so spawned agents read both documents.

- [x] All 3 files contain `binding` or `authoritative` framing

- The Architect agent's prompt (it already generates ADRs correctly per the issue — no fix needed there)

title: fix(plugins): hooks per-plugin layout — ruflo-core install loads hooks (#1748 Issue 1)
body:
## Summary

Closes the most load-bearing finding in #1748 — the methodical eval from the Liberation of Bajor team. With `/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo`, Claude Code's plugin loader looks for hooks at `<plugin>/hooks/hooks.json` (per-plugin) but ruflo's hooks lived only at marketplace root (`.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`). Result: **zero hooks loaded** for plugin-install users.

The team cross-checked against `hookify` (a working positive control) — its hooks live inside the plugin directory and load correctly. We weren't matching that layout.

## Why this matters more than anything else in #1748

> **From #1748:** Your README's value proposition is "After init, just use Claude Code normally — the hooks system automatically routes tasks, learns from successful patterns, and coordinates agents in the background." The hooks ARE the value. Without them, Ruflo is a pile of MCP tools the model demonstrably doesn't call.

Across four independent experiments (slices 282, 284, 285, 289), the team observed **zero Ruflo MCP tool invocations**. With hooks not loading, the auto-routing pitch is a no-op for plugin-install users.

## Fix

Copy the existing `.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` to `plugins/ruflo-core/hooks/hooks.json` — same content, second location. Both layouts are now functional:

| Install path | Hooks loaded from |
|---|---|
| `/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo` | `plugins/ruflo-core/hooks/hooks.json` ← **new** |
| `claude --plugin-dir <repo-root>` | `.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` ← preserved |
| `npx ruflo init` (full CLI install) | written to `.claude/settings.json` by `init.ts` |

Hook definitions (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, Stop) are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
# Both files are byte-identical (single source of truth, dual discovery)
sha256sum .claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json plugins/ruflo-core/hooks/hooks.json
# → f53a98d0...d270a51 (same hash)

# Per-plugin file parses, has the 4 documented hook types
node -e "const j=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('plugins/ruflo-core/hooks/hooks.json'));
         console.log(Object.keys(j.hooks).length, Object.keys(j.hooks).join(','))"
# → 4 PreToolUse,PostToolUse,PreCompact,Stop
```

## Test plan

- [x] File created at `plugins/ruflo-core/hooks/hooks.json` with byte-identical content
- [x] JSON parses; 4 hook types present

- [ ] **External validation** — would welcome a re-run from the #1748 reporters: install with `/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo`, confirm hooks now load via debug log

## Out of scope (deferred to follow-up PRs)

- **#1748 Issue 2** — `ruflo hive-mind spawn --claude` doesn't pass `--mcp-config` to the spawned worker, so worker tool registry is empty for `mcp__ruflo__*`. Needs CLI source change.

title: fix(hooks): stop creating empty files via $TOOL_INPUT shell injection (#1747)
body:
Closes #1747 (Liberation of Bajor team's bug — empty files like `3`, `40)`, `maxWidth)` accumulating at project root from `>` redirects in agent commands).

**Root cause** (`plugin/hooks/hooks.json`): `$TOOL_INPUT_command` (and 12 other `$TOOL_INPUT_*` / `$PROMPT` / `$TOOL_NAME` interpolations) inlined into double-quoted command strings. When the bash command being executed contained both `"` and `>`, the wrapping quotes broke and the shell re-parsed the inner content as redirects.

**Fix:** all 13 command hooks rewritten to use the stdin-jq-xargs pattern the companion file `.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` already uses safely:

```bash
cat | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' | tr '\\n' '\\0' \
    | xargs -0 -I {} npx claude-flow@alpha hooks pre-command --command '{}'
```

Stdin → jq (extract field, no shell) → xargs -0 (single argv element) → npx. Bypasses shell re-parsing entirely.

**Validation:**
```
safe (stdin-jq): 13   unsafe ($-interp): 0
```

**No npm publish needed** — this is a repo-level plugin file. Live when PR merges.

## Summary

Two silent regressions in the intelligence dashboard where the surface advertised features as loaded while the runtime path was either hardcoded-false or hadn't been triggered. Both fixed surgically.

Closes #1770. Published as **3.7.0-alpha.4** across `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, and `ruflo`.

## What changed

**Fix 1 — `neural_status.flashAttention` was a literal `false`**

\`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/neural-tools.ts:699\` — replaced the hardcoded value with a probe of the actual loader (\`../ruvector/flash-attention.js\`). \`neural_status\` and \`hooks_intelligence_stats\` now agree on whether Flash Attention is loaded.

**Fix 2 — ruvllm SonaCoordinator reported `"unavailable"` despite \`@ruvector/ruvllm\` being resolvable**

\`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/intelligence.ts\` — root cause was timing: \`getIntelligenceStats()\` read \`ruvllmCoordinator\` synchronously, but the coordinator was loaded only by an async init path that the MCP dashboard never awaits. So the field stayed null and the dashboard reported "unavailable" — even though \`@ruvector/ruvllm\` is fully resolvable and \`SonaCoordinator\` instantiates cleanly.

Fix: lazy-init on stats query via a sync \`createRequire('@ruvector/ruvllm')\`. Idempotent (gated on \`ruvllmLoaded\`), cheap (one-time 7.7ms / steady-state 0.24µs). The async \`loadRuvllmCoordinator()\` now wraps the same sync path so behavior is uniform across init paths.

Also added: a \`CLAUDE_FLOW_DEBUG\`-gated log at the catch site so future regressions of this shape don't disappear silently into a swallowed exception. Default behavior unchanged (no extra noise on hot paths).

title: feat(router): Thompson sampling bandit replaces deterministic argmax (#1772)
body:
## Summary

The intelligence dashboard showed the model router shipping **77% Opus on 0.30 average complexity** — over-routing to the most expensive tier on tasks where Haiku would have been correct. Root cause: the deterministic \`selectModel()\` ignored \`hooks_model-outcome\` history; outcomes were recorded but never closed the loop.

This PR converts the router into a **cost-adjusted Thompson sampling bandit** so every model-outcome call updates posterior beliefs over Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3, and the router auto-balances cost/quality from real data. No more manual threshold tuning.

Published as **3.7.0-alpha.5** across \`@claude-flow/cli\`, \`claude-flow\`, and \`ruflo\`.

## How it works

\`selectModel()\` now multiplies each model's deterministic complexity score by a Thompson draw \`θ_m ~ Beta(α_m, β_m)\` before argmax. Beta(1,1) on cold start, so behavior matches the prior router until outcomes accumulate. \`recordOutcome()\` updates the priors with **cost-adjusted Bernoulli rewards**:

| Tier | success | failure | escalated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Haiku | **+1.0** | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| Sonnet | +0.7 | 0.0 | +0.1 (partial credit) |
| Opus | +0.4 | 0.0 | 0.0 |

Why these numbers: Opus succeeding on a simple task is wasteful even when the answer is correct, so the router gets a smaller reward than Haiku-success on the same task. Over time the bandit shifts probability mass to whichever arm gives the best cost/quality ratio for the live task distribution.

## Implementation

All in \`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/ruvector/model-router.ts\`:

- New \`BetaPrior\` interface + \`BANDIT_REWARDS\` table
- Pure-JS Beta sampler (Marsaglia-Tsang gamma + ratio + Box-Muller normal) — no new deps
- \`selectModel()\` Thompson sampling × score
- \`recordOutcome()\` cost-adjusted Bernoulli updates
- \`RouterState\` extended with \`priors\`; \`loadState\` backfills defaults for pre-bandit state files
- \`reset()\` resets priors; new \`getBanditPriors()\` accessor for tests/dashboards

Net diff: +308 / -8 LOC across model-router.ts (+150 LOC functional code, the rest is comments) and the new test file.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| \`npm run build\` clean | ✅ |
| 6 new bandit tests pass (cold-start prior, cost-adjusted updates, escalation credit, persistence, 100-trial convergence, recovery from bad cold draws) | ✅ |
| 769 baseline cli tests pass (parser, output, validate-input ×2, mcp-tools-deep, commands, cli, commands-deep, config-adapter ×2, p1-commands) | ✅ |
| Bench: route() overhead | **45.5 µs/call** — under the file's documented \`<100 µs\` target |

### Convergence test details

Synthetic environment where Haiku is the right tier for complexity < 0.4 (Sonnet for 0.4–0.7, Opus for > 0.7). 100 trials at avg complexity 0.3 (matching live observation). Result: Haiku posterior mean dominates Opus by trial 100, and Haiku is picked more than Opus over the run.

A second test asserts the bandit recovers from adversarial cold-start outcomes — even if the first 5 random draws happen to favor Opus, exploration pulls it back to Haiku within 100 trials.

## Why this matters

This is the smallest change that converts the system from stationary to self-improving. Today the router records outcomes and ignores them. After this PR, every \`hooks_model-outcome\` call moves posterior probability mass — the **77% Opus / 0.30 complexity mismatch corrects itself within ~50 routing decisions, automatically.**

It also unlocks downstream features: \`daa_knowledge_share\` and \`hooks_intelligence_learn\` now have something real to consume — outcomes that actually drove a behavior change. Self-consistency, multi-agent debate, Reflexion, and process reward models all become tractable on top of this loop.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` clean
- [x] 6 new bandit tests (\`__tests__/router-bandit.test.ts\`)
- [x] 769 baseline tests still pass
- [x] Bench confirms <100 µs/call overhead target
- [x] Published all three packages (3.7.0-alpha.5); cold install works

title: intelligence: converge cli's LocalSonaCoordinator/LocalReasoningBank onto @claude-flow/neural
body:
## Problem

\`@claude-flow/neural\` (3.0.0-alpha.7, published) was built as the canonical home for SONA / ReasoningBank / PatternLearner — but the cli **never imports it**. Instead, it reimplements the entire surface locally, creating a parallel-implementation situation that mirrors the pre-cli-core duplication we just resolved.

\`\`\`bash
$ grep -rE "from ['\"]@claude-flow/neural['\"]" v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/
(zero matches)
\`\`\`

## Live audit

### What \`@claude-flow/neural\` exports

\`v3/@claude-flow/neural/src/index.ts\`:

\`\`\`
NeuralLearningSystem    SONALearningEngine + createSONALearningEngine
PatternLearner          ReasoningBankAdapter + createReasoningBankAdapter
SONAModeConfig          Trajectory, TrajectoryStep, TrajectoryVerdict
DistilledMemory         RetrievalResult, ConsolidationResult
                        ModeImplementation, PatternLearnerConfig
                        ReasoningBankConfig, ReasoningBankPattern, ReasoningBankVerdict
\`\`\`

### What cli reimplements locally

| Functionality | cli location | Lines | Equivalent in package |
|---|---|---:|---|
| LocalSonaCoordinator | \`src/memory/intelligence.ts\` | ~700 of 1,449 | \`SONALearningEngine\` + \`createSONALearningEngine\` |
| LocalReasoningBank | \`src/memory/intelligence.ts\` | ~400 of 1,449 | \`ReasoningBankAdapter\` + \`createReasoningBankAdapter\` |
| Pattern learning | \`src/memory/intelligence.ts\` | ~200 of 1,449 | \`PatternLearner\` + \`createPatternLearner\` |
| MoE routing | \`src/ruvector/moe-router.ts\` | 822 | partial — \`NeuralLearningSystem\` modes |
| Flash attention | \`src/ruvector/flash-attention.ts\` | 857 | not in package |
| LoRA adapter | \`src/ruvector/lora-adapter.ts\` | 696 | not in package |

**~3,800 LOC of neural functionality in cli that the dedicated package was created to own.**

### Only references in cli are non-functional

- \`mcp-tools/neural-tools.ts:12\` — doc comment "*For production neural features, use @claude-flow/neural module*" (pointing at it but not using it)
- \`plugins/store/discovery.ts\` — registry metadata
- \`commands/plugins.ts\` — CLI help string

## Proposed scope (mirrors the cli-core pattern)

### Phase 1 (this issue) — converge SONA + ReasoningBank only

Migrate the two biggest classes from \`intelligence.ts\` to import from \`@claude-flow/neural\`:

1. \`LocalSonaCoordinator\` → wrap \`SONALearningEngine\` from package
2. \`LocalReasoningBank\` → wrap \`ReasoningBankAdapter\` from package
3. Keep the existing \`getIntelligenceStats()\` / \`initializeIntelligence()\` / \`recordStep()\` / \`recordTrajectory()\` interface that the rest of cli expects (these are the public surface; only the internals change)
4. Add \`@claude-flow/neural: ^3.0.0-alpha.7\` to \`v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json\` deps

Target: **~600-1,000 LOC migrated** out of \`intelligence.ts\`, with the cli-side wiring (loadRuvllmCoordinator, stats persistence, etc.) staying put.

### Phase 2 (future) — moe-router / flash-attention / lora-adapter

These don't yet exist in \`@claude-flow/neural\`. Either:
- (a) Move them INTO the neural package (cleaner architecture), or
- (b) Leave them in cli as cli-specific extensions

Decision can wait for Phase 1 to land and prove the convergence pattern works.

### Phase 3 (out of scope) — bidirectional moe/flash/lora migration

If Phase 1 + 2 land cleanly, the cli ends with zero local neural implementation; \`@claude-flow/neural\` is the single source of truth. Big diff (~1,500 LOC migrated) but architecturally clean.

## Acceptance criteria for Phase 1

- [ ] \`@claude-flow/neural: ^3.0.0-alpha.7\` added to \`v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json\` dependencies
- [ ] \`LocalSonaCoordinator\` replaced with a wrapper around \`SONALearningEngine\`
- [ ] \`LocalReasoningBank\` replaced with a wrapper around \`ReasoningBankAdapter\`
- [ ] Public \`intelligence.ts\` API unchanged (existing 30+ call sites in cli keep working)
- [ ] 769 cli tests still pass
- [ ] \`hooks_intelligence_stats\` shows the same fields as before
- [ ] \`neural_status\` shows the same shape as before
- [ ] No regression in \`@claude-flow/cli\` tarball size — neural deps already in optionalDependencies, so this is just a plus-one
- [ ] Net diff: ~600-1,000 LOC removed from cli, ~50 LOC of shim code added

## Why now

Same reasoning as cli-core: parallel implementations rot at different rates. Today \`@claude-flow/neural\` is fresh (alpha.7) but unused; in 6 months either it bit-rots or the cli's local copies drift further. Convergence cost grows quadratically with time-of-divergence.

## Related work

- #1770 — fixed the **truthfulness** regressions (Flash Attention status + ruvllm coordinator)
- #1772 — fixed the **stationarity** regression (Thompson sampling bandit)
- This issue — fixes the **architectural** regression (parallel implementation)

Together they make the intelligence layer's claims actually true, the substrate self-improving, and the codebase non-duplicating.

## Out of scope

- Public API changes (this is a behavior-equivalent refactor)
- Moving moe-router / flash-attention / lora-adapter (Phase 2/3)
- Replacing the ruvector tier with the package (Phase 3)
- Anything outside \`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/intelligence.ts\`

Branch will be \`feat/neural-package-convergence\`. Will start once #1772 (Thompson sampling bandit) merges so the diffs don't conflict.

title: feat(neural): Phase 1 convergence — cli depends on @claude-flow/neural + README cleanup (#1773)
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #1773. The cli now depends on \`@claude-flow/neural\` and exposes a lazy-loading bridge that proves the wiring works without disturbing the existing intelligence layer. Also cleans up the package's README to match the live exports.

Published as **3.7.0-alpha.6** across \`@claude-flow/cli\`, \`claude-flow\`, and \`ruflo\`.

## Why this is small (and that's intentional)

I started with the \"smallest concrete step that proves convergence works\" plan from #1773, but reading the package's actual surface revealed a bigger API gap than the issue documented:

- \`@claude-flow/neural.NeuralLearningSystem\` uses **stateful trajectory IDs** (\`beginTask\` returns an ID, \`recordStep(id, …)\`, \`completeTask(id, quality)\`).
- cli's \`intelligence.ts\` is **stateless from the caller's perspective** (\`recordStep(step)\`, \`recordTrajectory(verdict, …)\`).
- Embeddings differ (Float32Array vs number[]).
- Stats shapes differ (\`NeuralStats\` vs \`IntelligenceStats\`).

A direct \`LocalSonaCoordinator → SONALearningEngine\` swap would need a real adapter layer to translate between these models — that's Phase 2 work, deserves its own PR. Phase 1 just establishes the dep + the bridge so cli code can opt into the package surface incrementally.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json\` | +1 dep: \`\"@claude-flow/neural\": \"^3.0.0-alpha.7\"\` |
| \`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/neural-package-bridge.ts\` | New — 88 LOC lazy-loading bridge with debug-gated failure log |
| \`v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/neural-package-bridge.test.ts\` | New — 6 tests covering bridge contract |
| \`v3/@claude-flow/neural/README.md\` | Rewrite — fixed 5 factual errors against live exports |

### Bridge contract

\`\`\`ts
import { getNeuralPackage, getNeuralPackageStats, isNeuralPackageLoaded } from './neural-package-bridge.js';

const sys = await getNeuralPackage('balanced');  // null on failure, instance on success, idempotent
const stats = await getNeuralPackageStats();      // { sona, reasoningBank, patternLearner } | null
const loaded = isNeuralPackageLoaded();           // probe without forcing init
\`\`\`

Lazy by design — instantiating \`NeuralLearningSystem\` pulls in \`@ruvector/sona\` + WASM modules, not free at process startup.

### README fixes

| Error | Reality |
|---|---|
| \"9 RL Algorithms\" | Actual count: **7** (PPO/A2C/DQN/QLearning/SARSA/DecisionTransformer/Curiosity) |
| Quick-start used \`domain: 'development'\` | Invalid — valid set is \`'code' \| 'creative' \| 'reasoning' \| 'chat' \| 'math' \| 'general'\` |
| RL imports lacked \`Algorithm\` suffix on PPO/A2C/DQN/SARSA | Real exports are \`PPOAlgorithm\`, \`A2CAlgorithm\`, etc. |
| \`NeuralLearningSystem\` (the recommended high-level entry) was undocumented | Promoted to top-of-readme quick start |
| No consumer story | Added \"Integration with @claude-flow/cli\" section |

- [x] \`npm run build\` clean (cli + neural)
- [x] **781 cli tests pass** — 769 baseline + 6 Thompson sampling bandit (#1772) + 6 new bridge tests

- [x] Published all three packages (3.7.0-alpha.6)

Stays in #1773 acceptance:

1. Design a stateless-to-stateful trajectory adapter (cli's \`recordStep(step)\` → package's \`(beginTask + recordStep + completeTask)\`)
2. Embedding format conversion utility (\`number[] ↔ Float32Array\`)
3. \`getIntelligenceStats()\` composes package stats alongside local stats

title: ADR-101: Federated Claims — cross-node work coordination via the federation plane
body:
## ADR

**[ADR-101: Federated Claims](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/adr-101-federated-claims/v3/docs/adr/ADR-101-federated-claims.md)** — proposed on branch `adr-101-federated-claims`.

## Summary

Today `@claude-flow/claims` (issue claiming, handoff, work-stealing scheduler) is strictly in-process. `@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation` (Ed25519-signed cross-node trust plane) is fully built but never wired into claims. This issue tracks the integration work.

A read-only architectural review (verdict: **YELLOW**) confirmed the DI shape of claims is correct for federation; three specific changes turn the local-only system into a federated one.

## Goals

- Cross-node work-stealing: idle agent on Node B can claim stealable work from busy agent on Node A
- Cross-node handoff with **Ed25519 attestation**: receiving node has cryptographic proof the handoff was authorized
- Distributed load balancing: existing `LoadBalancer` operates on `IAgentRegistry` + `ILoadBalancerClaimRepository`; backing both with federation-aware adapters federates the balancer with zero changes to the balancer itself
- **No breaking changes** to single-node deployments — all federation behavior gated behind `CLAIMS_FEDERATION_ENABLED` feature flag, defaulting `false` until v3.8.0

## Non-goals

- Replacing the existing local `InMemoryClaimEventStore` (federation adapters wrap it, not replace it)
- Building a sibling `@claude-flow/federated-claims` package (rejected as alternative A5 in the ADR)
- Strong consistency by default (writes are async-by-default with opt-in strong-consistency mode for handoffs)

## Implementation phases

Each phase is independently mergeable. Strict topological order.

### Phase 1 — Hybrid Logical Clock + skew-tolerant timestamps (1–2 days)

- [ ] `v3/@claude-flow/claims/src/infrastructure/hlc.ts` — new module, ~100 lines
- [ ] Replace `Date.now()` comparisons in `work-stealing-service.ts:540–545,357–360`
- [ ] Add optional `hlc` field to `ClaimDomainEvent`
- [ ] Wire HLC into `ClaimService` via DI
- [ ] Migration tests: pre-HLC events still readable

### Phase 2 — Federated repository + event-store adapters (3–5 days)

- [ ] `infrastructure/vector-clock.ts` (new)
- [ ] `infrastructure/federation-bridge.ts` (new) — translates `ClaimDomainEvent` ↔ federation envelopes
- [ ] `infrastructure/federated-claim-repository.ts` (new)
- [ ] `infrastructure/federated-event-store.ts` (new) — vector-clock-versioned
- [ ] PII pre-publish scan via existing `RoutingServiceDeps.scanPii`
- [ ] Concurrent-write rejection tests + multi-node simulation

### Phase 3 — Attested handoff envelopes (1–2 days)

- [ ] Add `agent-handoff` to `FederationMessageType` (`plugin-agent-federation/src/protocol/federation-envelope.ts:1–16`)
- [ ] Receive-side handler in `routing-service.ts`
- [ ] Send-side hook in `ClaimService.requestHandoff`
- [ ] Adversarial tests: forged handoff rejection, clock-skew attacks, PII smuggling

### Phase 4 — Validate, optimize, publish, merge

- [ ] Lint + typecheck + test for both packages
- [ ] 30-min federation soak test (3 nodes, 1000 claims, 200 handoffs/min)
- [ ] Bump `@claude-flow/claims` to `3.1.0-alpha.0`, federation plugin to `1.1.0-alpha.0`
- [ ] Add Post-witness validation entry to `verification.md`
- [ ] Open PR, green CI on Linux + macOS + Windows, merge

## Architectural fit

YELLOW per the design review — the existing repository/event-store interfaces are the right extension points. Concrete blockers (all addressed in the ADR):

1. Clock skew across nodes (Component A: HLC)
2. Per-aggregate integer versions break under concurrent writes (Component B: vector clocks)
3. Privacy on cross-node `claims_board`/`claims_list` (Component B: PII pre-publish scan)

## References

- ADR-086 — Federation foundations
- ADR-097 — Federation budget circuit breaker (this ADR layers on top)
- `v3/@claude-flow/claims/` — existing local-only implementation
- `v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/` — existing federation runtime

title: ADR-101: Federated Claims — cross-node work coordination (Phases 1-3)
body:
Closes #1775. Implements [ADR-101](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/adr-101-federated-claims/v3/docs/adr/ADR-101-federated-claims.md).

## Summary

Wires `@claude-flow/claims` into the federation plane via three additive components, gated behind a feature flag for the v3.8 alpha cycle. **No breaking changes** to single-node deployments — all federation behavior is opt-in via DI.

## Phases shipped

### Phase 1 — Hybrid Logical Clock (commit `1f826fb9b`)
