## Background

YC Lightcone podcast (2026-05-08, [*Tokenmaxxing*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=57lDpTwiW6g)) mentions two emerging tools alongside Claude Code:

- **GStack** — described as 'accidental product emergence' / 'emerging framework/tool'
- **OpenClaw** — labeled as 'agent framework'

Both are unverified. If either is a thin-harness + skill-marketplace architecture, they directly compete with Ruflo's positioning.

See: [docs/COMPETITIVE_NOTES.md](../blob/main/docs/COMPETITIVE_NOTES.md) for full context.

## Investigation Tasks

### Discovery
- [ ] \`gh search repos \"gstack\" --language=typescript\`
- [ ] \`gh search repos \"openclaw\"\`
- [ ] npm search for both names
- [ ] Twitter / HN search for project announcements
- [ ] YC batch lookups (Lightcone hosts often surface YC-portfolio tools)

### If found, capture per project
- [ ] Repository / organization
- [ ] Stars, contributors, commit frequency
- [ ] Architecture: thin-harness vs framework vs SaaS
- [ ] Skill / plugin model (if any)
- [ ] Memory layer (do they have anything like AgentDB + HNSW?)
- [ ] Multi-agent coordination model
- [ ] License & funding
- [ ] Differentiation vs Ruflo

### Output
- [ ] Append findings to \`docs/COMPETITIVE_NOTES.md\` using the existing template
- [ ] If either project is a direct competitor, flag with risk assessment and recommended Ruflo response

## Suggested Swarm

\`\`\`javascript
mcp__ruv-swarm__swarm_init({ topology: \"mesh\", maxAgents: 3, strategy: \"balanced\" })

Task({ name: \"gstack-scout\",  subagent_type: \"researcher\", run_in_background: true,
       prompt: \"Locate GStack: github + npm + twitter + HN. Report architecture, license, traction. Compare to Ruflo's thin-harness + fat-skills model.\" })

Task({ name: \"openclaw-scout\", subagent_type: \"researcher\", run_in_background: true,
       prompt: \"Locate OpenClaw: github + npm + twitter. Report architecture, agent model, traction. Compare to Ruflo's swarm + dual-mode coordination.\" })

Task({ name: \"synthesizer\", subagent_type: \"reviewer\", run_in_background: true,
       prompt: \"Wait for both scouts. Append findings to docs/COMPETITIVE_NOTES.md. Flag direct competitors with risk + recommended Ruflo response.\" })
\`\`\`

## Effort

~30 minutes for discovery if projects are public; up to 2 hours if deeper analysis needed.

## Priority

Medium — YC backing means rapid traction is possible. Worth knowing before they show up in customer comparisons.

title: agentdb_pattern-store writes to bridge-fallback; agentdb_pattern-search reads from reasoningBank → silent zero results
body:
## Summary

`agentdb_pattern-store` and `agentdb_pattern-search` use **different controllers**, so patterns stored never appear in search.

## Repro

```jsonc
// 1. Store a pattern
agentdb_pattern-store({
  pattern: "Billing/financial code numeric type rules. ALWAYS use decimal for prices/costs/balances; double for percentages...",
  type: "type-safety-billing",
  confidence: 0.95
})
// → { success: true, patternId: "entry_1778426551908_12072bc5d7457b95", controller: "bridge-fallback" }

// 2. Search for it (any reasonable query)
agentdb_pattern-search({ query: "decimal billing precision", topK: 3, minConfidence: 0 })
// → { results: [], controller: "reasoningBank" }   ← empty
```

I stored 8 distinct patterns this way (different `type` and `confidence`), all returned `controller: "bridge-fallback"` from the store call. Every subsequent search call returns `results: []` with `controller: "reasoningBank"`.

## Expected

Patterns stored via `agentdb_pattern-store` should be retrievable by `agentdb_pattern-search`. Either:
- both use the same controller, OR
- search falls through to bridge-fallback when reasoningBank has no results, OR
- store hits both controllers when reasoningBank is the primary.

## Actual

- `pattern-store` → `bridge-fallback`
- `pattern-search` → `reasoningBank` (always empty)
- Patterns are silently dropped from the user's POV.

## Workaround

Patterns are still retrievable via `embeddings_rabitq_search` if they were also imported via `memory_import_claude` (which I did). But for greenfield pattern-store calls without that bridge step, patterns are effectively write-only.

## Environment

- Plugin: ruflo-core (and ruflo-rag-memory) installed user-scope from `ruvnet/ruflo` marketplace
- Discovered: 2026-05-10 while curating a ChatOOH agent-memory pattern corpus

## Related

- #812 (MCP memory tools don't use ReasoningBank)
- #1492 (4 controllers unimplemented — closed)
- #1499, #1521 (ReasoningBank disabled history)

Looks like `pattern-search` is querying ReasoningBank which appears to still be empty/disabled in the bundled CLI, while `pattern-store` correctly falls back to bridge.

title: feat(federation): ADR-111 Phases 1-3 — opt-in WireGuard mesh layer
body:
## Summary

Implements Phases 1-3 of [ADR-111 — Federation network mesh via WireGuard](v3/docs/adr/ADR-111-federation-wg-mesh.md), tracked in #1879. Closes the federation-trust ↔ packet-layer-reachability gap: when the breaker SUSPENDs or EVICTs a peer, the same transition propagates to WG `AllowedIPs` — a peer the trust layer just blocked can't reach the rest of the mesh at L3 either.

**OPT-IN.** Default tailnet+ws path stays untouched; new behavior only activates when `integrations.wgMesh` is wired. No new runtime dependencies — X25519 keygen uses Node's core crypto.

## Phase 1 — Manifest extension + key generation
`v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/src/domain/value-objects/wg-config.ts` (new)
- `WgManifestSection` (`publicKey`, `endpoint`, `meshIP`), `WgLocalKey`
- `generateWgKeyPair()` — X25519 via Node `generateKeyPairSync`, extracts raw 32-byte key from PKCS8/SPKI DER → base64 (the WG wire format)
- `deriveMeshIP(nodeId, subnet, usedIPs)` — sha256(nodeId) → host octets, clamps `.0`/`.255`, rotates hash input on `usedIPs` hit (bounded 1024 probes)
- `FederationManifest.wg?` extension — Ed25519 manifest signature already covers it since it's part of `Omit<FM, 'signature'>`

## Phase 2 — `WgMeshService`
`v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/src/domain/services/wg-mesh-service.ts` (new)
- `WG_NETWORK_GATES`: trust-level → port-rule table from the ADR
- `buildInterfaceConfig(peers)` — pure-projection `wg-quick`-compatible config. **Service never shells out** — emits config + commands; operator runs them, per CLAUDE.md destructive-actions guidance
- Breaker hooks: `removeAllowedIPs` (soft-block via empty `AllowedIPs`), `restoreAllowedIPs` (`set-allowed-ips`), `removePeer` (terminal)
- Defense-in-depth: `formatCmd` regex-validates every arg before shell splicing — refuses anything with metachars
- `summarize()` for the eventual `federation_wg_status` MCP tool (Phase 6)

## Phase 3 — Coordinator/breaker wiring
- `FederationCoordinatorIntegrations` gains `wgMesh` + `wgCommandSink`
- `evictPeer()` after successful evict → `wgMesh.removePeer()` + audit
- `reactivatePeer()` after successful reactivate → `wgMesh.restoreAllowedIPs()` + audit
- `FederationBreakerService` gains optional `BreakerTransitionListener` 3rd constructor arg, fires post-transition (`apply` mode only); errors swallowed so failing WG propagation can't unwind a successful entity transition
- No-op for peers without `metadata.wgPublicKey` / `metadata.wgMeshIP` — mixed-deployment safety preserved

## ADR doc fixes (the 3 review nits)
- Status: `Proposed` → `Accepted` (Phases 1-3 Implemented)
- Phase 4 firewall: inconsistent "Phase 2 add" → "Phase 4 add"
- Subnet rationale: documented 10.50.0.0/16 choice vs Tailscale's 100.64.0.0/10, birthday-collision thresholds, and collision-handling probe loop. Also notes 10.50.0.0/12 jump for larger deployments

## Tests

**513/513 pre-existing pass + 33 new tests across 3 files, all green.**

- `__tests__/unit/wg-config.test.ts` (10 tests) — keygen format/uniqueness, IP determinism, `.0`/`.255` clamping, custom subnets, collision handling, error paths
- `__tests__/unit/wg-mesh-service.test.ts` (16 tests) — config generation, trust filtering, suspend/restore/evict commands, shell-injection rejection, `summarize()`
- `__tests__/unit/wg-coordinator-integration.test.ts` (5 tests) — `evictPeer`/`reactivatePeer` emit WG commands; no-op for peers without wg metadata; breaker `onTransition` listener fires on successful transition

## Not in this PR (separate phases — sub-issues to file under #1879)
- Phase 4 — trust-graded firewall (nftables/pf projection)
- Phase 5 — witness attestation chain for mesh changes
- Phase 6 — operator MCP tools (`federation_wg_status` / `_attest` / `_keyrotate`)
- Phase 7 — cross-OS validation (mac↔ruvultra), federation alpha bump

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Existing federation-coordinator-breaker tests still pass (verifies no regression in the breaker public contract)
- [ ] Doc preview renders cleanly

Tracks #1879

title: feat(federation): ADR-111 Phases 4-6 — firewall projection + witness chain + MCP tools
body:
## Summary Lands Phases 4-6 of [ADR-111](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-111-federation-wg-mesh.md) on top of the alpha.14 Phases 1-3 release. Tracking issue [#1879](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/1879). | Phase | What | Where | |---|---|---| | 4 | Trust-graded firewall projection — `nftables` (linux) + `pf` (macOS) | `domain/services/wg-firewall-service.ts` | | 5 | Witness attestation chain — Ed25519-signed append-only log | `domain/services/wg-witness-service.ts` | | 6 | Operator MCP tools: `federation_wg_status` / `_attest` / `_keyrotate` | `mcp-tools.ts` | Phase 7 (real WG mesh bringup over Tailscale) is **operator-mediated and outside this PR** per CLAUDE.md destructive-actions guidance — Phase 1-6 emits configs + commands; Phase 7 is the human running them. ## Phase 4 — `WgFirewallService` Two backends with platform auto-detection: **linux-nftables** — atomic `nft -f`, table `inet ruflo_fed`, default `policy drop`, input chain scoped to the WG interface name. Rules of shape `ip saddr tcp dport accept` per `WG_NETWORK_GATES` entry. **darwin-pf** — anchor-scoped (`pfctl -a ruflo-fed -f`) so the operator's main pf ruleset stays untouched. Rules of shape `pass in on ruflo-fed proto tcp from to any port

keep state`. Defense-in-depth: every spliced value (interface name, pf anchor, mesh IP) goes through a regex filter before reaching a rule line. UNTRUSTED peers excluded (no mesh IP); peers without `wgMeshIP` skipped. Service never shells out — returns rule string + the `nft -f` / `pfctl -f` command. ## Phase 5 — `WgWitnessService` Append-only Ed25519-signed chain. Each entry has: - `content`: `{ version, type, timestamp, nodeId, peerPublicKey?, meshIP?, wgCommand?, rationale, prevHash }` - `hash`: `sha256(canonicalize(content))` — sorted keys, no whitespace, omitted-on-undefined - `signature`: operator's Ed25519 sig over the canonical bytes `prevHash` chains entries: tampering with history requires forging a signature chain with the operator's key. `verifyWitnessChain` walks the chain end-to-end and reports `failedAt` + reason (`broken-chain-link` | `invalid-signature-or-hash`). `attestWgCommand` adapter maps `WgCommand.verb` → event type so the breaker-side path from Phase 3 (`removeAllowedIPs`/`restoreAllowedIPs`/`removePeer`) auto-produces witness entries. ## Phase 6 — Three new MCP tools | Tool | Purpose | Destructive | |---|---|---| | `federation_wg_status` | Per-peer mesh state — trust, meshIP, AllowedIPs, suspended/evicted flags | No | | `federation_wg_attest` | Operator-signed witness chain entry | No | | `federation_wg_keyrotate` | Rotate local WG keypair + emit upgrade checklist | **Yes** (`confirm: true` required; drops tunnels until peers fetch updated manifest) | Also: - `createMcpTools` gains an optional `getWgMesh` getter (additive, no breaking change) - `FederationCoordinator.listPeers()` public accessor for the discovery peer set ## Tests **543/543 pass** (was 513 before this PR, +27 new + 3 plugin-test assertions for the new MCP tool names). ``` ✓ wg-config.test.ts 12 tests (Phase 1) ✓ wg-mesh-service.test.ts 16 tests (Phase 2) ✓ wg-coordinator-integration.test.ts 5 tests (Phase 3) ✓ wg-firewall-service.test.ts 16 tests (Phase 4) NEW ✓ wg-witness-service.test.ts 11 tests (Phase 5) NEW ✓ plugin.test.ts 61 tests (Phase 6 — 3 added) ``` ## Not in this PR (Phase 7 — separate operator-mediated work) - Stage WG configs on mac mini + ruvultra (via Tailscale ssh) - Operator-approved `wg-quick up ruflo-fed` on both hosts - Federation envelopes ride over `10.50.0.x:9101` - SUSPEND a peer → confirm L3 isolation → reactivate restores - Witness-verify the change log - Bump federation to `1.0.0-alpha.15` and publish This work happens in a follow-up since bringing up a kernel WG interface modifies host networking + requires root + interactive operator approval. ## Test plan - [ ] CI green - [ ] Existing federation-coordinator-breaker tests still pass (verifies no regression in the core breaker contract) - [ ] Phase 7 staging (separate operator-mediated session) Tracks #1879 🤖 Generated with [RuFlo](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo)

title: External audit (AlphaSignal AI, May 2026): independent review of v3.6.30 functional gaps
body:
> External audit published by [AlphaSignal AI](https://alphasignalai.substack.com/p/how-ruflo-turns-claude-code-into) (May 7, 2026, targeting v3.6.30). Filing as a tracking issue so the gaps named publicly can be triaged against our own [ADR-095 (April audit framework)](v3/docs/adr/ADR-095-architectural-gaps-from-april-audit.md), confirmed/refuted against current main (now v3.7.0-alpha.21 + federation alpha.15), and either closed or rolled into existing issues.

## Article's framing

> "Ruflo is usable today for memory, embeddings, task, and claims management on top of Claude Code, though the multi-agent swarm runtime its README describes does not yet execute end-to-end."

That's the headline. The article is fair on what works and specific on what doesn't.

## What the article says works

- Memory + embeddings (HNSW + 384-dim ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
- Task tools (TaskCreate/Get/List/Update)
- Claims tools
- Workflow scheduling (not execution)
- Session save/restore
- ~195 of ~240 MCP tools verified real

## What the article says doesn't work (mapped to ADR-095 G-rows)

### G1 — Agent execution
> "`agent_spawn` writes a JSON record into an in-memory Map. No subprocess — provider classes exist but agent/task/swarm code paths don't import them."

**Spot-check on current main:** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/agent-tools.ts` line 182+ — `agent_spawn` writes to `loadAgentStore()`-backed in-memory record. No subprocess. **Claim still holds.**

### G2 — Hive-Mind transport
> "EventEmitter-based, no inter-node transport. Single-process per ADR-095 G2, so cross-machine swarm coordination does not yet work."

**Spot-check:** This is the gap that ADR-104 transport + ADR-109 inbound dispatcher closed for the federation plugin specifically (alpha.13+). Whether hive-mind itself uses that transport is a separate question — likely still open.

### G3 — Workflow runtime
> "`workflow_execute` returns 'Workflow not found' even with valid stored workflows. No executor walks the dependency graph."

**Spot-check on current main:** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/workflow-tools.ts` — 4 occurrences of `'Workflow not found'` in the execute path. **Claim still holds.**

### G4 — WASM agent
> "Returns the input prefixed with 'echo:' — no LLM call, no runtime."

Worth verifying against current WASM plugin path.

### G6 — Auto-memory bloat
> "Injects ~5,706 entries with ~20 unique into every Claude message. Uses Trigram Jaccard graph instead of the 384-dim embeddings used elsewhere. PageRank uniform across nodes, meaningless at the graph's density."

The 5,706-entries-per-message claim is severe — would be a 10x+ context-window tax on every turn. Needs immediate verification + fix or refutation with evidence.

## What the article calls out as separate issues

### Tool discoverability (#1748 #4)
> "237 of 300 descriptions don't tell Claude when to use Ruflo's version over native (Bash, Read, Grep, Glob). 230 fall through to native, so Ruflo's tools fire less often than install suggests."

This is a documented issue already; the article amplifies its visibility.

### Benchmark integrity
> "`simulate_benchmarks.py` generates results with `random.uniform(-0.05, 0.05)`. Ruflo does not appear on the official SWE-bench leaderboard. Claims of '84.8% on SWE-bench' are synthesized, not verified."

This is the most reputationally damaging finding. If `simulate_benchmarks.py` exists in tree and produces fake numbers that downstream marketing materials use, it must be (a) deleted, (b) replaced with a real benchmark run, or (c) clearly labeled as a simulator in the same file + every downstream consumer.

## What's changed since the article (v3.6.30 → v3.7.0-alpha.21)

The article snapshots v3.6.30 (May 5). Since then:
- `@claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.21` published (memory_import_claude fixes #1883/#1884, archive trim #1882)
- `@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@1.0.0-alpha.15` published (ADR-111 Phases 1-6 — opt-in WG mesh layer with breaker propagation, firewall projection, witness chain, MCP tools)
- ADR-097 federation breaker + ADR-104 transport + ADR-109 inbound dispatcher with Ed25519 sig verify + ADR-107 TLS pinning + ADR-110 MemorySpendReporter
- Witness manifest (ADR-103) — cryptographic attestation that documented fixes are present in dist (99 fixes verified end-to-end as of yesterday)
- 6/6 documented user-reported bugs closed in the last 24h (#1859 #1862 #1874 #1881 #1882 #1883 #1884)

None of those directly address G1/G3/G4/G6. The federation work is parallel to the swarm-runtime gap.

## Action items (proposed — not yet decisions)

- [ ] **G6 verify-or-fix** — measure actual auto-memory injection volume on a real session. If 5,706/20 unique is accurate, fix before the next user-visible release.
- [ ] **G1 reality check** — either ship the agent-spawn → real-subprocess wire (ADR-095 G1 work) OR change `agent_spawn`'s description to explicitly state it's a tracking record, not an executor.
- [ ] **G3 reality check** — same: either implement the dependency-graph walker or change `workflow_execute`'s description.
- [ ] **G4 reality check** — verify WASM agent claim against current main.
- [ ] **Benchmark integrity** — locate `simulate_benchmarks.py`, either delete or guard. Run an actual SWE-bench batch and publish either a real number or a "no current score" disclaimer.
- [ ] **Tool discoverability (#1748)** — audit pass on the 237 descriptions called out.
- [ ] **External-audit response** — consider a public reply explaining what's true, what's stale relative to v3.7.0-alpha, and the timeline for the remaining gaps.

## Related

- [ADR-095 — Architectural Gaps From April 2026 Audit](v3/docs/adr/ADR-095-architectural-gaps-from-april-audit.md) (currently Proposed/tracking-only — this issue argues for upgrading rows G1/G3/G4/G6 to Accepted with concrete owners)
- [#1700 — 5 'real-implementations' features broken or cosmetic end-to-end](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/1700) (already closed but covers overlapping territory; cross-reference)
- [#1748 — tool description audit](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/1748)
- [Public audit gist (April)](https://gist.github.com/roman-rr/ed603b676af019b8740423d2bb8e4bf6)

title: feat(mcp): ADR-112 — 285/285 tool descriptions have 'Use when …' guidance + CI guard + #1892 statusline
body:
**Scope expanded from the original docs-only update.** This PR now covers the whole #1896 audit response + #1748 tool discoverability + #1892 statusline + the new ADR-112 CI guard.

## What this PR does

### ADR-112 — MCP tool discoverability (closes #1748)

External audit ([AlphaSignal AI, May 7](https://alphasignalai.substack.com/p/how-ruflo-turns-claude-code-into)) measured 237/300 MCP tool descriptions lacked guidance for when Claude should pick Ruflo's tool over native (Bash/Read/Grep/Glob/Task/TodoWrite). Re-measurement on current main was actually worse: **279/285**. Now: **0/285**.

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tools with "Use when …" guidance | 6/285 (2%) | **285/285 (100%)** |
| Tools < 80 chars | (not measured) | **0** |
| Duplicate descriptions | (not measured) | **0** |

The rule (in `v3/docs/adr/ADR-112-mcp-tool-discoverability.md`): every description must name the native overlap (or state "no native equivalent"), state when to use Ruflo's version because of concrete value-add (cost attribution / learning persistence / coordination / witness chain / sandbox isolation), and honestly say when native is fine.

### CI guard (every tool checked)

- `scripts/audit-tool-descriptions.mjs` — scans every `MCPTool` definition and enforces:
  1. "Use when …" guidance present
  2. Description length ≥ 80 chars
  3. Description unique across all tools
- Baseline at `verification/mcp-tool-baseline.json` — monotone-decreasing across all three counts.
- New `tool-descriptions-audit` job in `v3-ci.yml`, wired into `witness-verify` needs[] so the release pipeline gates on it.

### #1892 — UI version mismatch (closes #1892)

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/helpers/statusline.js` hardcoded `RuFlo V3.5`. Now `resolveBannerVersion()` reads from the installed `@claude-flow/cli` `package.json` so UI matches `ruflo doctor`. Resolves across local-checkout, npm-installed, and globally-installed layouts.

### Witness manifest

`verification/witness-fixes.json` adds ADR-111, ADR-112, #1892 markers. `verification/macos/manifest.md.json` regen'd — **102/102 fixes verified, Ed25519 signature valid**.

### ADR-095 status update (the original scope of this PR)

Records that 5 of 7 originally-named gaps have been quietly fixed by the v3.7.0-alpha work — see #1896 for the per-gap measurement evidence.

## Tests + verification

- `1963 / 1963 federation+cli tests pass` on this branch
- Build clean
- `node scripts/audit-tool-descriptions.mjs` reports `285 tools, 285 with guidance, all gates pass`

## What this PR does NOT do

- Doesn't ship runtime tests for each of the 285 tools (the gate is static analysis of descriptions). That would be a separate per-tool integration test undertaking.
- Doesn't restructure the tool taxonomy. Some tool name prefixes are inconsistent (e.g. `analyze_` vs `analyze-`); fix in a follow-up.

## Related

- Closes #1748 (tool discoverability — 237/300 → 0/285)
- Closes #1892 (UI version mismatch)
- Tracks #1896 (external audit response)
- References ADR-095 (gap framework), ADR-111 (federation WG mesh — independent work)

title: Stop hook ETIMEDOUT: npx downloads claude-flow@alpha on every response
body:
## Problem

The `ruflo-core` plugin registers a Stop hook that runs on every assistant response:

```sh
npx claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end --generate-summary true --persist-state true --export-metrics true
```

Because `npx` always checks npm registry for `claude-flow@alpha` before running (even if the package is cached), the hook fails with `ETIMEDOUT` on any brief network interruption:

```
Stop hook error: Failed with non-blocking status code: npm warn exec The following package was not found and
will be installed: claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.22
npm error code ETIMEDOUT
npm error syscall read
npm error errno -60
npm error network read ETIMEDOUT
```

## Reproduction

1. Install `ruflo-core` plugin in Claude Code
2. Have any brief network interruption (e.g. VPN reconnect, interface flap)
3. Observe stop hook error at the end of next assistant response

## Expected behavior

Hook should either:
- Use a locally installed binary (`claude-flow`) instead of `npx`, or
- Add `--prefer-offline` / `--no-install` flag so npx uses cached version without hitting registry, or
- Handle network errors gracefully (exit 0) so the error doesn't surface to users

## Suggested fix

Replace `npx claude-flow@alpha` with one of:
```sh
# Option 1: prefer offline cache
npx --prefer-offline claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end ...

# Option 2: use globally installed binary if available
$(npm bin -g)/claude-flow hooks session-end ... 2>/dev/null || true

# Option 3: silent failure
npx claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end ... 2>/dev/null || true
```

## Environment

- Claude Code with ruflo-core v0.2.1
- macOS Darwin 25.3.0
- npm 10.x

title: Stop hook uses outdated package name claude-flow@alpha instead of ruflo
body:
## Problem

The stop hook registered by `ruflo-core` plugin still references the old package name `claude-flow@alpha`:

```sh
# hooks/hooks.json — Stop hook
npx claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end --generate-summary true --persist-state true --export-metrics true
```

Since **ruflo is the rebranding of claude-flow**, this hook should reference `ruflo` (or the equivalent ruflo CLI package), not the legacy `claude-flow@alpha` name.

As a result, every time a Claude Code session ends, `npx` attempts to download the old `claude-flow` package from npm. This causes:
- Unnecessary network requests on every response
- `ETIMEDOUT` errors on any brief network interruption (VPN reconnect, interface flap, etc.)
- The error surfaces visibly to users even though it's non-blocking

```
Stop hook error: Failed with non-blocking status code: npm warn exec The following package was not found and
will be installed: claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.22
npm error code ETIMEDOUT
```

## Expected behavior

The stop hook should use the `ruflo` package name, consistent with the rebranding:

```sh
npx ruflo hooks session-end --generate-summary true --persist-state true --export-metrics true
```

Or reference the appropriate ruflo CLI entrypoint so users don't see errors related to the old `claude-flow` package.

## Environment

- ruflo-core v0.2.1
- Claude Code on macOS Darwin 25.3.0

title: feat: ruflo-rtk plugin — integrate RTK token compression without hook conflicts
body:
## Problem

[RTK (Rust Token Killer)](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) reduces LLM token consumption by **60–90%** by intercepting Bash tool calls and compressing shell output (git, ls, grep, test runners) before it reaches the LLM context.

RTK installs its own `PreToolUse/Bash` hook via `rtk init -g`, writing to `.claude/settings.json`. Ruflo also manages `settings.json` (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, hooks pipeline). **Conflict**: when either tool updates, it can clobber the other's hooks entry.

Ruflo's own Token Optimizer achieves 30–50% savings at the context/caching level. RTK operates at the shell output level (60–90%). Together they stack — but only if the integration is conflict-free.

## Proposed Solution: `ruflo-rtk` plugin

A thin adapter plugin that:

1. Places the RTK hook script under `.claude/plugins/ruflo-rtk/` — a directory Ruflo's updater never touches
2. Registers the hook in `settings.local.json` — which Ruflo never writes to (`settings.json` only)
3. Chains cleanly: RTK compresses stdout first, then Ruflo's post-bash hook records the result

### Architecture

```
PreToolUse/Bash pipeline:
  1. settings.local.json → .claude/plugins/ruflo-rtk/rtk-pre-bash.sh  (RTK rewrite)
  2. settings.json       → .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs pre-bash    (Ruflo safety check)

PostToolUse/Bash:
  → hook-handler.cjs post-bash  (Ruflo learning + metrics, already compressed input)
```

### Combined savings

| Layer | Savings | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| RTK (shell output) | 60–90% | stdout filter per Bash call |
| Ruflo Token Optimizer | 30–50% | context caching + smart routing |
| Combined (typical session) | ~85–90% | stack multiplicatively |

## Implementation

### `.claude/plugins/ruflo-rtk/rtk-pre-bash.sh`

Thin delegating hook — all rewrite logic lives in `rtk rewrite` (Rust binary). Hook uses the `hookSpecificOutput` protocol to transparently rewrite commands:

```bash
INPUT=$(cat)
CMD=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' <<<"$INPUT")
[ -z "$CMD" ] && exit 0

REWRITTEN=$(rtk rewrite "$CMD" 2>/dev/null)
case $? in
  0) jq -c --arg cmd "$REWRITTEN" '.tool_input.command = $cmd | {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"allow",permissionDecisionReason:"RTK auto-rewrite",updatedInput:.tool_input}}' <<<"$INPUT" ;;
  3) jq -c --arg cmd "$REWRITTEN" '.tool_input.command = $cmd | {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",updatedInput:.tool_input}}' <<<"$INPUT" ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
```

### `settings.local.json` registration

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Bash",
        "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "sh -c '~/.claude/plugins/ruflo-rtk/rtk-pre-bash.sh'", "timeout": 3000 }]
      }
    ]
  },
  "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(rtk *)"] }
}
```

## Why `settings.local.json`?

- Ruflo's `init` and plugin installer write only to `settings.json`
- Claude Code merges both files — hooks from `settings.local.json` run alongside those in `settings.json`  
- `settings.local.json` is user-local and not committed (no merge conflicts on team repos)
- Plugin files under `.claude/plugins/ruflo-rtk/` are in a path Ruflo's updater skips

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/plugin install ruflo-rtk@ruflo` registers the hook in `settings.local.json`
- [ ] `rtk gain` shows savings accumulating through Ruflo sessions
- [ ] Ruflo update (`npx ruflo@latest update`) does not remove the RTK hook
- [ ] `ruflo doctor` reports RTK version and hook status
- [ ] If RTK is not installed, hook exits 0 silently (no disruption)

title: plugin-agentic-qe@3.0.0-alpha.4 declares peer-deps `>=3.0.0` blocking npm install in plugin store
body:
## Summary

`@claude-flow/plugin-agentic-qe@3.0.0-alpha.4` declares two `peerDependencies` with constraints `>=3.0.0` (without `-alpha` qualifier) for packages that have **never been published as stable** (only prereleases exist on the registry). This blocks `npm install` of any other `@claude-flow/*` plugin in the same store with `ETARGET` / `E404`.

## Affected peer-deps (verified via `npm view`)

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@claude-flow/memory": ">=3.0.0",
  "@claude-flow/plugins": ">=3.0.0"
}
```

Registry reality (empirical):
- `@claude-flow/memory` published versions: only `3.0.0-alpha.{11..15}`. **No `3.0.0` stable exists.**
- `@claude-flow/plugins` published version: only `3.0.0-alpha.1`. **No `3.0.0` stable exists.**

semver semantics: `>=3.0.0` **excludes prereleases** by design, so the constraint never matches.

## Repro

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/cf-repro && cd /tmp/cf-repro
npm init -y >/dev/null
npm install '@claude-flow/plugin-agentic-qe@3.0.0-alpha.4' --no-fund --no-audit
npm install '@claude-flow/neural@latest' --no-fund --no-audit
# → npm error code ETARGET
# → No matching version found for @claude-flow/memory@>=3.0.0
```

## Impact

Anyone with `plugin-agentic-qe` in their plugin store cannot install `@claude-flow/neural`, `@claude-flow/plugins`, or several `@claude-flow/plugin-*` packages until this is fixed. `--legacy-peer-deps`, `--omit=peer`, and `--force` all fail to bypass because npm validates the consolidated tree before any mutation.

## Proposed fix

Change the constraints to include the `-alpha` prerelease range:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@claude-flow/memory": ">=3.0.0-alpha.1",
  "@claude-flow/plugins": ">=3.0.0-alpha.1"
}
```

## Workaround

`npm overrides` in the plugin store's `package.json`:

```json
"overrides": { "@claude-flow/memory": "3.0.0-alpha.15" }
```

Plus install via `npm install <pkg> --save` (positional package args degrade the blocker to peer-optional warning).

---
Reported by independent integrator running ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.22 + @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.22 on Linux aarch64.
Source files: `v3/plugins/agentic-qe/package.json` peer-deps section.

title: Peer-dep `@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream` referenced by 3 plugins but never published to npm registry (404)
body:
## Summary

Three published plugins declare `peerDependencies` on `@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream`, but **this package has never been published to the npm registry** (`npm view` returns 404). This blocks `npm install` of these plugins and any dependent install paths.

## Affected plugins (verified via `npm view`)

| Plugin | Version | Peer constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `@claude-flow/plugin-legal-contracts` | 3.0.0-alpha.1 | `>=3.0.0-alpha.1` |
| `@claude-flow/plugin-healthcare-clinical` | 3.0.0-alpha.1 | `>=3.0.0-alpha.1` |
| `@claude-flow/plugin-perf-optimizer` | 3.0.0-alpha.1 | `>=3.0.0-alpha.1` |

## Repro

```bash
npm view '@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream'
# → npm error 404 Not Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@claude-flow%2fruvector-upstream
```

```bash
npm install '@claude-flow/plugin-legal-contracts@latest' --no-fund --no-audit
# → npm error code E404
# → '@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream@^0.1.0' could not be found
```

## Code-side analysis

Source usage in compiled dist (extracted from tarball):

- `plugin-legal-contracts/dist/bridges/attention-bridge.js:35,212` — only string reference inside comment ("In production, this would load from @claude-flow/ruvector-upstream")
- `plugin-perf-optimizer/dist/bridges/sparse-bridge.js:43` — `const modulePath = '@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream'` (dynamic load pattern)
- `plugin-healthcare-clinical` — only declared in `package.json`, no `require`/`import` in dist

The runtime usage is **optional/dynamic** but the `peerDependencies` declaration is strict and breaks install.

## Proposed fix (pick one)

1. **Publish `@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream`** to the registry pointing at the real package (likely `ruvector@^0.2.0` standalone exists at https://npmjs.com/package/ruvector).
2. **Replace the peer-dep target** in the 3 plugins with the existing standalone: `"ruvector": "^0.2.0"`.
3. **Demote to `peerDependenciesMeta.optional: true`** so npm doesn't fail when absent.

## Local workaround (validated)

Stub package re-exporting standalone `ruvector@0.2.25` (174 exports surface) installed at `<plugin-store>/node_modules/@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream/`:

```json
{ "name": "@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream", "version": "3.0.0-alpha.1",
  "main": "index.js", "private": true }
```

```js
module.exports = require('ruvector');
```

After stub: all 3 affected plugins import correctly via `await import()` from inside the plugin store.

---
Reported by independent integrator running ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.22 + @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.22 on Linux aarch64.
Affected directories: `v3/plugins/legal-contracts`, `v3/plugins/healthcare-clinical`, `v3/plugins/perf-optimizer`.

title: plugin-gastown-bridge@0.1.3 declares `exports.import → ./dist/index.mjs` but tarball contains only `.cjs`
body:
## Summary

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/cf-gast && cd /tmp/cf-gast
npm init -y >/dev/null
npm install '@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge@0.1.3' --no-fund --no-audit
cat > test.mjs <<'EOM'
const m = await import('@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge');
console.log(Object.keys(m).length);
EOM
node test.mjs
# → ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
# → Cannot find module '.../@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge/dist/index.mjs'
```

## Proposed fix (pick one)

1. **Include `.mjs` builds** in `prepublishOnly` (e.g. `tsup`/`unbuild` dual-format), then republish.
2. **Remove the `import` branch** from `exports` (CJS-only delivery — the `.cjs` is fully working).
3. **Point `import` at `.cjs`** (works because Node treats `.cjs` as CommonJS regardless of `exports.import` branch).

## Local workaround (validated)

Patch `package.json` exports to point `.import` at the existing `.cjs`:

```diff
-  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", ... }
+  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.cjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", ... }
```

After patch: `await import('@claude-flow/plugin-gastown-bridge')` yields 196 exports.

---
Reported by independent integrator running ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.22 + @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.22 on Linux aarch64.
Source path: `v3/plugins/gastown-bridge/package.json` exports field + `v3/plugins/gastown-bridge/tsup.config.{ts,js}` (suspected source of mjs/cjs build skew).

title: feat(swarm): ADR-095 G2 — pluggable ConsensusTransport + Ed25519 message signing (step 1)
body:
First concrete piece of [ADR-095 G2](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-095-architectural-gaps-from-april-audit.md) — making hive-mind consensus multi-process. Tracks #1872.

## The gap

The consensus protocols (raft/byzantine/gossip in `@claude-flow/swarm`) used a local `EventEmitter` for *everything* — observability events AND inter-node messages. The inter-node side never crossed a process boundary: a node "sent" a message by `emit`ting it locally and synthesizing the peer's reply inline. `byzantine-coordinator.ts`'s `verifySignature()` returned `true` unconditionally. That's the single-process limitation #G2 names.

## What this PR lands

`v3/@claude-flow/swarm/src/consensus/transport.ts`:
- **`ConsensusTransport` interface** — `send` (request-response), `broadcast`, `onMessage`, `peers`, `close`. Separates the inter-node-message dimension from observability events (events stay on each protocol's own EventEmitter).
- **`LocalTransport` + `LocalTransportRegistry`** — in-process registry, the default. Matches current single-process behavior so nothing breaks. Supports optional Ed25519 signing + per-sender monotonic-`seq` replay defense.
- **Real Ed25519 helpers** via Node's built-in `crypto` (no new deps): `generateNodeKeyPair`, `signMessage`, `verifyMessage`, `canonicalizeForSigning` (deep-sorted-key JSON — cross-host deterministic), `messageDigest`.
- Exported from `consensus/index.ts`.

## CI guard

`plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/test-consensus-transport.mjs`, wired into the `mcp-roundtrip-smoke` job:
- Static: required exports present; **no `return true` signature-stub regression** (the original #G2 bug).
- Behavioral: `LocalTransport` round-trip; Ed25519 verify is real (true for right key; false for wrong key / tampered payload / missing sig). 30s watchdog.

## Tests

14 new tests in `__tests__/consensus-transport.test.ts`. **186/186 swarm suite passes.** Build clean.

## Remaining for G2 (subsequent PRs on this branch)

- `FederationTransport` adapter — wraps the federation plugin's WS transport (ADR-104, `agentic-flow/transport/loader`)
- Wire raft/byzantine/gossip to accept an injected `ConsensusTransport` instead of hard-depending on the EventEmitter for messaging
- Replace `byzantine-coordinator.ts`'s `verifySignature() → true` with the real `verifyMessage`
- Per-strategy correctness: BFT vote counting tolerant of f<n/3; Raft term/log replication
- Failure-injection tests (f<n/3, f<n/2)
- Cross-host validation (mac ↔ ruvultra over tailscale)

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green (incl. the new `consensus-transport` step)
- [ ] Swarm test suite still 186/186
- [ ] Cross-host validation in a follow-up once `FederationTransport` lands

title: fix(#1906): agent_execute model aliases → current Claude 4.x ids
body:
`agent_execute` failed with HTTP 404 on every call: `MODEL_MAP` mapped `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`/`inherit` to `claude-3-5-haiku-latest` / `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest` / `claude-3-opus-latest` — ids the Anthropic API no longer serves. (Same path the WASM agent's LLM fallback uses via `resolveAnthropicModel`, so that failed too.)

## Fix

| alias | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `haiku` | `claude-3-5-haiku-latest` (404) | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` |
| `sonnet` | `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest` (404) | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| `opus` | `claude-3-opus-latest` (404) | `claude-opus-4-7` |
| `inherit` | `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` (= new `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) |

Also replaced 4 other hardcoded `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest` defaults (the `callAnthropicMessages` fallback, `resolveAnthropicModel`'s no-input case, `executeAgentTask`'s fallback, the doc-comment example) with `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`.

## CI coverage

1. **Unit test** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/agent-execute-models.test.ts` (8 tests) — picked up by the cli package's vitest run in CI. Includes a regression-class assertion: *no alias resolves to a `claude-3.x` id*.
2. **Witness marker** `#1906` — `claude-sonnet-4-6` must be present in `agent-execute-core.js` dist; `witness-verify` fails on regression. 104/104 fixes verified.

## Related

- Closes #1906
- Related to #1863 — that issue's comment pointed users at `agent_execute` as the path that actually runs agents; this makes it work.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green (incl. the new model-aliases test + witness-verify with the #1906 marker)
- [ ] Reporter @Jordo960 confirms `agent_execute` no longer 404s with a valid key

title: bug: claude-flow MCP transport closes during broad tool smoke test
body:
## Summary

A broad smoke test of the `claude-flow` MCP server in Codex validated many tools successfully, but the MCP transport closed during the hooks batch. After that point, every subsequent `mcp__claude_flow__.*` call in the Codex session failed with `Transport closed`, including `mcp_status`. A standalone `npx claude-flow mcp start --test` still starts a stdio server, so the failure appears to break the active MCP transport/session rather than making the CLI unable to start.

## Environment

- Date: 2026-05-11
- Repo: `ruvnet/ruflo`
- CWD: `/Users/cohen/Projects/ruflo`
- Git HEAD: `b0793ab73`
- Version: `ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.24`
- Node: `v22.22.1`
- npm: `10.9.4`
- Codex MCP registration: `claude-flow  npx claude-flow mcp start  enabled`
- MCP transport before failure: `running: true`, `transport: stdio`, `pid: 68818`
- `gh` auth: logged in as `ruvnet`

## Trigger

The crash happened while invoking a hooks smoke batch after a successful `hooks_pre_task` call. `hooks_pre_task` returned normally, but these calls in the same batch returned MCP tool errors with `Caused by: Transport closed`:

- `hooks_route`
- `hooks_model_route`
- `hooks_explain`
- `hooks_pre_command`
- `hooks_post_command`
- `hooks_pre_edit`
- `hooks_post_edit`
- `hooks_list`
- `hooks_worker_detect`

Afterward, even `mcp_status` returned `Transport closed`.

## Reproduction Outline

1. Register/use Codex MCP server: `npx claude-flow mcp start`.
2. Run a broad MCP smoke test using test-only keys/agents.
3. Invoke `hooks_pre_task` with a simple payload.
4. Invoke the hook-related MCP tools above, especially in a batch/parallel call.
5. Observe the active MCP transport closes.
6. Try `mcp_status`; it also fails with `Transport closed`.
7. Run `npx claude-flow mcp start --test`; it still prints `Starting in stdio mode`, showing the CLI can start a new server even though the active session is broken.

## Tools Successfully Exercised Before Transport Failure

### Server / memory / embeddings

- `mcp_status`: pass before crash; reported stdio transport.
- `memory_store`: pass; stored `mcp-smoke-20260511-1512-memory` with 384-dim embedding.
- `memory_list`: pass.
- `memory_retrieve`: pass.
- `memory_search`: pass.
- `memory_search_unified`: pass, returned score `0.8002408964323315`.
- `memory_stats`: pass; reported `203` total entries and 100% embedding coverage.
- `memory_bridge_status`: pass.
- `memory_import_claude`: pass; imported 6 entries into `claude-memories-mcp-smoke`.
- `memory_migrate`: pass; `No legacy data to migrate`.
- `memory_delete`: pass for the test key.
- `embeddings_search`: pass; returned HNSW/hyperbolic metadata.

### Config / guidance / AgentDB status

- `config_list`: pass.
- `config_export`: pass.
- `config_set`: pass for `mcp.smoke.validation`.
- `config_get`: returned the just-set key, but suspiciously reported `source: default`.
- `config_reset`: pass for only `mcp.smoke.validation`.
- `guidance_capabilities`: pass.
- `guidance_recommend`: pass.
- `guidance_workflow`: pass.
- `agentdb_controllers`: pass; reported `reasoningBank` and `vectorBackend` disabled, 4/6 active.
- `agentdb_health`: pass.

### Swarm / agents / tasks / sessions

- `swarm_init`: pass; created `swarm-1778512302629-lpk3xy`.
- `swarm_status`: pass.
- `swarm_health`: pass.
- `swarm_shutdown`: pass.
- `agent_spawn`: pass; created `mcp-smoke-agent-1512`.
- `agent_list`: pass.
- `agent_status`: pass.
- `agent_health`: pass.
- `agent_update`: pass.
- `agent_execute`: expected guarded failure: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set in environment`.
- `agent_terminate`: pass.
- `task_create`: pass.
- `task_assign`: pass.
- `task_update`: pass.
- `task_status`: pass.
- `task_list`: pass.
- `task_summary`: pass.
- `task_complete`: pass.
- `task_cancel`: pass.
- `session_save`: pass; created `session-1778512302763-boe128`.
- `session_list`: pass.
- `session_info`: pass.
- `session_restore`: pass.
- `session_delete`: pass.

### Hive mind / DAA

- `hive_mind_init`: pass; created `hive-1778512302767-vcz4yv`.
- `hive_mind_status`: pass, but ID shown as `hive-1778512302767` while init returned `hive-1778512302767-vcz4yv` (possible ID truncation/inconsistency).
- `hive_mind_join`: pass.
- `hive_mind_spawn`: pass.
- `hive_mind_memory`: pass for `set`, `get`, `list`, and `delete`.
- `hive_mind_broadcast`: pass.
- `hive_mind_consensus`: pass for propose/list/vote/status after using term 2; term 1 correctly reported an existing pending proposal.
- `hive_mind_leave`: pass.
- `hive_mind_shutdown`: expected guarded failure with graceful shutdown because there were pending consensus items.
- `daa_agent_create`: pass.
- `daa_learning_status`: pass.
- `daa_agent_adapt`: pass.
- `daa_cognitive_pattern`: pass.
- `daa_performance_metrics`: pass.
- `daa_knowledge_share`: pass.
- `daa_workflow_create`: pass.
- `daa_workflow_execute`: pass, but explicitly notes steps are tracked and not auto-executed.

### Hooks

- `hooks_pre_task`: pass.
- Subsequent hook tools listed in the Trigger section failed with `Transport closed`.

## Ambiguous / Suspicious Results

1. `config_get` for a key written by `config_set` returned `exists: true` but `source: default`, which is probably misleading.
2. `agentdb_feedback` returned `success: true` with `controller: none` and `updated: 0`; this looks like a false-positive success response.
3. `hive_mind_status` returned a shortened hive ID compared with `hive_mind_init`.
4. `hive_mind_status` included old workers/shared memory from previous runs after initializing a new hive, which may indicate global state bleed between test hives.
5. `swarm_status` for a newly initialized swarm reported `agentCount: 0` even though a test agent was spawned separately. This may be expected if agents are not auto-associated without explicit swarm config, but it is worth clarifying.

## MCP Tools Not Reached Because Transport Closed

The transport failure prevented testing the rest of the discovered MCP surface in the same session, including but not limited to:

- Remaining hooks/intelligence tools: `hooks_post_task`, `hooks_notify`, `hooks_worker_dispatch`, `hooks_worker_list`, `hooks_worker_status`, `hooks_worker_cancel`, `hooks_metrics`, `hooks_intelligence`, `hooks_intelligence_stats`, `hooks_intelligence_learn`, `hooks_intelligence_reset`, `hooks_intelligence_trajectory_start`, `hooks_intelligence_trajectory_step`, `hooks_intelligence_pattern_store`, `hooks_intelligence_pattern_search`, `hooks_model_outcome`, `hooks_model_stats`, `hooks_session_restore`, `hooks_transfer`, `hooks_build_agents`, `hooks_init`.
- AgentDB mutating/advanced tools: `agentdb_batch`, `agentdb_hierarchical_store`, `agentdb_hierarchical_recall`, `agentdb_hierarchical_delete`, `agentdb_consolidate`, `agentdb_causal_edge`, `agentdb_causal_edge_delete`, `agentdb_causal_node_delete`, `agentdb_context_synthesize`, `agentdb_pattern_store`, `agentdb_pattern_search`, `agentdb_route`, `agentdb_semantic_route`, `agentdb_session_start`, `agentdb_session_end`.
- Performance tools: `performance_metrics`, `performance_report`, `performance_bottleneck`, `performance_profile`, `performance_benchmark`, `performance_optimize`.
- GitHub MCP tools: `github_repo_analyze`, `github_metrics`, `github_workflow`, `github_issue_track`, `github_pr_manage`.
- WASM/RuVLLM/tools: `wasm_gallery_list`, `wasm_gallery_search`, `wasm_gallery_create`, `wasm_agent_create`, `wasm_agent_files`, `wasm_agent_tool`, `wasm_agent_export`, `ruvllm_generate_config`, `ruvllm_hnsw_create`.
- Other discovered tools: `aidefence_is_safe`, `analyze_file_risk`, `transfer_store_search`, `transfer_plugin_search`, `embeddings_neural`, `embeddings_rabitq_build`, `coordination_topology`, `guidance_discover`, `config_import`, full `config_reset` (intentionally avoided to protect user/project config).

## Cleanup Performed

- Deleted test memory key `mcp-smoke-20260511-1512-memory`.
- Reset test config key `mcp.smoke.validation`.
- Terminated test agent `mcp-smoke-agent-1512`.
- Shut down test swarm `swarm-1778512302629-lpk3xy`.
- Deleted test session `session-1778512302763-boe128`.
- Deleted test hive memory key `mcp-smoke-key-1512`.
- Removed explicit joined hive test agent `mcp-smoke-hive-agent-1512`.

Note: graceful hive shutdown was rejected because existing pending consensus items were present; I did not force shutdown because that could affect pre-existing hive workers/state.

## Expected Behavior

A failing MCP tool should return a structured tool error without closing the active stdio transport. After an individual hook/tool failure, `mcp_status` and unrelated tools should remain callable.

## Actual Behavior

After the hook batch, all subsequent MCP tool calls failed with `Transport closed`, including `mcp_status`.

## Severity

High for Codex/Claude MCP users: one tool batch can make the entire `claude-flow` MCP server unusable for the rest of the active session, preventing diagnostics and cleanup through MCP.

title: feat(codex): finish Codex ↔ Ruflo integration — real `codex exec`, `dual run --worker`, tests, CI guard (#1909)
body:
Finishes the Codex ↔ Ruflo integration so "dual-mode" actually uses the OpenAI Codex CLI (not two Claude instances), the `claude-flow-codex` CLI matches its docs, the codex surface is test- and CI-guarded, and the config it generates is correct.

Closes #1909. Context / deep review: #1910 (the MCP-stdout bug surfaced during the smoke test of this work is being fixed separately on its own branch).

## What changed

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **MCP backend** | `npx @openai/codex mcp serve` — `codex mcp` has no `serve` subcommand → backend never started | `npx @openai/codex mcp-server` (the real "start as MCP server" command), in both `ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/index.js` and `ruflo/src/ruvocal/mcp-bridge/index.js` |
| **Dual-mode orchestrator** | `codexCommand` defaulted to `'claude'` ("Both use claude CLI"); every worker launched with Claude-only flags (`-p`, `--output-format text`, `--max-turns`) | `codexCommand` → `'codex'`; platform-specific args — claude: `-p <prompt> --output-format text [--max-turns N] [--model M]`; codex: `exec --sandbox workspace-write --skip-git-repo-check [-m M] <prompt>` |
| **Dual-mode agent defs** | `codex-worker.md` / `codex-coordinator.md` spawned workers with `claude -p "<task>" --session-id <id>` | rewritten to `codex exec --sandbox <workspace-write\|read-only> --skip-git-repo-check "<prompt>"`; CLI/MCP-tool refs → `ruflo` |
| **`dual run` CLI** | only `--template <name>` / `--config <path>` — the documented `--worker "claude:architect:…"` syntax didn't exist; `dual run feature` silently no-op'd | `dual run [template]` positional + repeatable `-w, --worker "<platform>:<role>:<prompt>"` (sequential chaining unless `--parallel-workers`); `parseWorkerSpecs()` exported |
| **CLI ref** | `npx claude-flow@alpha …`; `codex mcp add claude-flow -- npx claude-flow mcp start`; `args = ["-y","@claude-flow/cli@latest"]` (no `mcp start`!) | `npx ruflo@alpha …`; `codex mcp add ruflo -- npx ruflo mcp start`; **config.toml default MCP server** = `{ name: 'ruflo', args: ['-y','ruflo@latest','mcp','start'] }` |
| **Generated `SKILL.md`** | only `name` + `description` → `validate` flagged 3 missing-field warnings/skill | frontmatter now emits `version` / `author` / `tags` → `validate` clean |
| **`@claude-flow/codex` version** | `VERSION` const `3.0.0-alpha.8` while `package.json` `3.0.0-alpha.9` | synced |
| **package.json** | `files: ["dist","templates"]` (no `templates/` dir); `repository`/`homepage`/`bugs` → `ruvnet/claude-flow` | `files: ["dist"]`; URLs → `ruvnet/ruflo`; same for `PACKAGE_INFO.repository` + generated doc URLs |
| **New** | — | `claude-flow-codex loop` runner — Codex-native `/loop` equivalent (`loop run`/`status`/`stop`, `.codex/loop/<name>.json` state, `./loop` package export, README docs) |

## Tests & CI
- `tests/dual-mode.test.ts` — 18 new tests: `parseWorkerSpecs` (incl. 3 error paths), `CollaborationTemplates`, `dual` command wiring, `DualModeOrchestrator.buildDependencyLevels` (linear / fan-in / circular).
- `scripts/audit-codex-integration.mjs` + `.github/workflows/codex-integration-audit.yml` — pure-Node static guard (no install) for all the invariants above; runs on PRs/pushes touching the codex package, mcp-bridge, dual-mode agents, or the script.

## Verification
- `cd v3/@claude-flow/codex && npm run build` → ✓
- `npx vitest run` → **184/184 pass** (162 prior + 18 dual-mode + 4 loop)
- `node scripts/audit-codex-integration.mjs` → ✓
- `git diff --check` → clean

## Out of scope / follow-ups
- Full `CodexInitializer.initialize()` integration test — it shells out `codex mcp add`, which would mutate the user's real `~/.codex/config.toml`; needs a `child_process` mock first.
- The repo's *committed* `.agents/AGENTS.md` / `.agents/config.toml` still carry old `ruvnet/claude-flow` URLs — generated artifacts; the generators are now fixed so re-init produces `ruvnet/ruflo`.

Ruflo hive task assignment does not execute workers; hive workers are stored separately from agent tooling and agent_logs handler is missing
body:
# Ruflo hive task assignment does not execute workers; hive workers are stored separately from agent tooling and `agent_logs` handler is missing

## Environment

- Package: `ruflo`
- Version: `3.7.0-alpha.23`
- Platform: Windows 10
- Node package execution: local project install via `npx --no-install ruflo`
- MCP config: `npx -y ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.23 mcp start`
- Repo-local compatibility runtime: not used
- `node_modules` patch: not used

## Expected Behavior

After `hive-mind init`, `hive-mind spawn`, `task create`, and `task assign`:

- Assigned hive worker should receive and execute the task.
- Task should progress beyond `0`.
- Task should eventually become `completed` or `failed`.
- Hive metrics should update `completedTasks` or `failedTasks`.
- `agent status <hive-worker-id>` should resolve the same worker visible in `hive-mind status`.
- `agent logs <hive-worker-id>` should return logs or a supported empty-log response.

## Actual Behavior

- `hive-mind init` works.
- `hive-mind spawn` works and lists workers in hive status.
- `task create` works.
- `task assign` works only as a state transition and returns `in_progress`.
- After bounded polling, task remains `in_progress`, `progress: 0`, `completedAt: null`, `result: null`.
- Hive metrics remain `completedTasks: 0`.
- Hive workers remain `idle`, with `currentTask: null` and `tasksCompleted: 0`.
- `agent status <hive-worker-id>` returns `status: not_found`, `error: Agent not found`.
- `agent logs <hive-worker-id>` fails with `MCP tool not found: agent_logs`.

## Minimal Reproduction Steps

Use a fresh project directory or remove previous `.claude-flow`, `.swarm`, `.hive-mind`, `.claude/memory.db`, and `ruvector.db` artifacts first.

```powershell
$nonce = "UPSTREAM-RUFLO-ISSUE-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS"
npx --no-install ruflo --version
npx --no-install ruflo hive-mind init --topology mesh --format json
npx --no-install ruflo hive-mind spawn --count 4 --role worker --type worker --prefix "upstream-issue-$nonce" --format json
npx --no-install ruflo task create --type review --description "Upstream issue reproduction $nonce" --priority normal --format json
npx --no-install ruflo task assign <task-id> --agent <first-hive-worker-id> --format json
```

Poll for a bounded time:

```powershell
npx --no-install ruflo hive-mind status --format json
npx --no-install ruflo task status <task-id> --format json
npx --no-install ruflo agent status <first-hive-worker-id> --format json
npx --no-install ruflo agent logs <first-hive-worker-id> --format json
```

Optional command that is fixed only for submission:

```powershell
npx --no-install ruflo hive-mind task --description "Upstream issue hive submission $nonce" --priority normal --format json
```

## Observed Output Summary

From reproduction nonce `UPSTREAM-RUFLO-ISSUE-20260511-185113`:

- `ruflo --version`: `ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.23`.
- `hive-mind spawn`: returned `success: true`, `spawned: 4`.
- `task assign`: returned `status: in_progress`.
- `hive-mind status`: workers listed, each with `status: idle`, `currentTask: null`, `tasksCompleted: 0`.
- `hive-mind status`: `metrics.completedTasks: 0`, `metrics.activeTasks: 1`.
- `task status`: `status: in_progress`, `progress: 0`, `completedAt: null`, `result: null`.
- `agent status`: `status: not_found`, `error: Agent not found`.
- `agent logs`: `MCP tool not found: agent_logs`.

## Source-Level Suspected Root Cause

- `hive-mind_spawn` writes hive workers to `.claude-flow/agents.json`.
- `agent_status`, `agent_list`, and `agent_spawn` use `.claude-flow/agents/store.json`.
- `task_assign` writes `.claude-flow/tasks/store.json`, then tries to sync assigned agents only through `.claude-flow/agents/store.json`.
- `task_assign` transitions tasks to `in_progress` but does not call `agent_execute`, does not enqueue work, and does not run a worker.
- `task_complete` is the only inspected path that sets `completed`, `progress: 100`, and `completedAt`, but assignment does not invoke it.
- `worker-daemon.js` default workers are maintenance workers (`map`, `audit`, `optimize`, `consolidate`, `testgaps`) and do not consume `.claude-flow/tasks/store.json` assignments.
- `agent_logs` is referenced by guidance/CLI surfaces but no registered MCP handler is available.

## Suggested Fix

1. Normalize hive worker persistence so hive-spawned workers are written to the same store consumed by `agent_status`, `agent_list`, `task_assign`, and execution tooling.
2. Make `agent_status` and `agent_list` resolve hive-spawned workers, either by using the unified store or by merging hive and agent stores consistently.
3. Add an official task queue consumer for `.claude-flow/tasks/store.json` or make `task_assign` dispatch to an official executor.
4. Ensure execution updates task `progress`, terminal status, `completedAt`, `result`, hive completed/failed metrics, and worker `taskCount`.
5. Register an `agent_logs` MCP handler or remove the public CLI/logs surface until it is implemented.
6. Add tests covering pending -> in_progress -> completed/failed lifecycle, no false completed count, hive worker resolvability through agent status, and log retrieval.

## Impact

Users can create official hive workers and assign official tasks, but the workflow can appear active while no worker executes. This creates false confidence in multi-agent execution, prevents official log evidence, and makes `completedTasks` stay at `0`.

## Related Positive Result

In `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.23`, official AgentDB memory store/search/retrieve/list works with a fresh nonce, and `hive-mind task` submission no longer fails with the old missing `hive-mind_task` handler.

## Local Evidence Files

Prepared evidence file names in the downstream project:

- `official-version-and-config.md`
- `agentdb-fixed-evidence.md`
- `task-execution-failure-evidence.md`
- `source-level-root-cause.md`
- `official-patch-plan.md`

These names are included only as local evidence references; no private absolute paths or secrets are attached.

## Sensitive Data

No secrets, credentials, tokens, cookies, phone numbers, OTPs, customer data, or production/staging data are included in this report.

title: fix(#1914): daemon start only reaps daemons in the current workspace
body:
## Summary
- `daemon start` previously SIGTERM'd **every** process whose command line contained `daemon start --foreground` — so starting the daemon in workspace B killed workspace A's daemon. That violates ADR-014's per-workspace daemon scope (#1914).
- The forked daemon's argv is now stamped with `--workspace <root>` (kept as the last argv entry), and `killStaleDaemonsPosix` / `killStaleDaemonsWindows` only reap daemons whose command line ends with `--workspace <thisRoot>` — an exact trailing match, never a bare path-prefix match, so `/a/proj` can't reap `/a/proj-other`'s daemon.
- Pre-#1914 daemons (no `--workspace` stamp) are intentionally left for `daemon stop` to handle via the PID file rather than being globally reaped.
- `resolveWorkspaceFlag` rejects shell metacharacters / null bytes (defence-in-depth — the value lands in a forked child's argv and is later compared against `ps` / `tasklist` output).

## CI guard
- New `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/daemon-workspace-scope.test.ts` — 12 cases covering cross-workspace isolation, path-prefix siblings, legacy (no-stamp) lines, Windows `tasklist` CSV rows, extra flags before `--workspace`, and space-containing workspace paths. Auto-discovered by `vitest run` in the `Test V3 Packages` job.
- Witness marker added for `#1914` (`daemonCommandLineBelongsToWorkspace` in `dist/src/commands/daemon.js`) — manifest regenerated, `ruflo verify` reports `pass: 105, regressed: 0`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` (cli) — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/daemon-workspace-scope.test.ts` — 12/12 pass
- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/services/worker-daemon-resource-thresholds.test.ts __tests__/commands.test.ts` — pass
- [x] `node scripts/regen-witness.mjs` + `ruflo verify` — 105 verified, 0 regressed
- [ ] CI green on PR

title: fix(plugins): #1902/#1903/#1904 install-safety + plugin-package CI guard
body:
> Stacked on #1917 (`fix/1914-daemon-workspace-scope`) — GitHub will retarget this to `main` when #1917 merges. The witness manifest in this branch references #1914's marker, so it must sit on top of that branch.

## Summary
Fixes the matheusassali0-wq plugin-packaging cluster — all three break `npm install` of an affected plugin.

- **#1903** — `plugin-legal-contracts` / `plugin-healthcare-clinical` / `plugin-perf-optimizer` published tarballs declared `@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream` (a package that was never published) as a hard `dependencies` entry (legal-contracts) or a strict `peerDependencies` entry (the other two), so `npm install` E404'd. The repo source was already clean — the runtime does `await import('@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream').catch(() => null)` and falls back — so the fix is a **republish** plus a CI guard.
- **#1902** — `plugin-agentic-qe`'s published peer ranges (`">=3.0.0"`) can't resolve *any* `@claude-flow` publish since they're all `3.x` prereleases. Repo source already uses `">=3.0.0-0"` + `peerDependenciesMeta.optional`; fix is a **republish** (the repo version was also stale at `3.5.59` while npm is on `3.0.0-alpha.4`).
- **#1904** — `plugin-gastown-bridge`'s `exports` advertised `./dist/index.mjs` plus `./formula` and `./convoy` subpaths the build never emitted, so those import specifiers 404'd in the published tarball. `tsup.config.ts` now builds the `formula`/`convoy` entries (previously commented out) and `package.json` `exports`/`main`/`module` point at the actually-emitted `.js`/`.cjs` filenames.

## CI guard (the "add cases to ci guard" part)
`scripts/audit-plugin-packages.mjs` scans every `v3/plugins/*/package.json` and fails on:
- **(A)** an unpublished `@claude-flow/*` package as a hard dep or non-optional peer — catches the #1903 class
- **(B)** a bare-stable peer range (`>=X.Y.Z`, `^X.Y.Z`, …) for a `@claude-flow/*` target — catches #1902
- **(C)** a `main`/`module`/`exports` path not covered by `files`
- **(D)** post-build, a `main`/`module`/`exports` path that doesn't exist on disk — catches #1904

Wired into `v3-ci.yml` as the `plugin-package-audit` job (builds the plugins first so check D is live) and added to `witness-verify`'s `needs[]`. Witness markers added for `#1902-#1903-guard` and `#1904`; `ruflo verify` → `pass: 107, regressed: 0`.

## Republish (done out-of-band with the merge)
Version bumps in this PR: `legal-contracts`/`healthcare-clinical`/`perf-optimizer` `3.0.0-alpha.1`→`3.0.0-alpha.2`, `agentic-qe` `3.5.59`→`3.0.0-alpha.5`, `gastown-bridge` `0.1.3`→`0.1.4`. These were published to npm (`v3alpha`/`latest`/`alpha` dist-tags updated) and the IPFS plugin registry CID was bumped — see the issue threads.

## Summary
New ADR (status: **proposed**) recording the decision to adopt [`ruvnet/dspy.ts`](https://github.com/ruvnet/dspy.ts) (TS port of Stanford DSPy) as an optional `@claude-flow/plugin-dspy`:

- **Boundary recorded**: DSPy = compile-time, task-scoped prompt+demo optimization (output is a reusable artifact); ruflo intelligence = run-time, cross-task ambient pattern learning. The plugin must not re-implement the intelligence pipeline, must not be a hard dep of any core package, and must pass `scripts/audit-plugin-packages.mjs`.

Registered in AgentDB (`adr-ADR-114`, semantic tier) and the `adr-patterns` namespace. Related: ADR-026, ADR-098, ADR-112, ADR-G008 (optimizer promotion rule — reuse for "when does a compiled module replace the current one"), ADR-G009 (headless eval harness).

This is a decision record only — no code. Implementation would be a follow-up PR.

title: [BUG] hooks.json refs `claude-flow@alpha` → npm `Invalid Version` on PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hook fire (3.7.0-alpha.18 → .24)
body:
## Summary

  Every hook defined in `.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` invokes `npx claude-flow@alpha …`, and `claude-flow@alpha` currently resolves to
  `3.7.0-alpha.24` (and previously `.18`, `.20` — same failure on each). Installing that version via `npx` fails with `npm error Invalid Version: `
  (trailing empty version), so **every Stop/PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook fires an error inside Claude Code on every turn**.

  This is a re-occurrence of the failure class previously reported in #1147 (which referenced `@claude-flow/cli@3.1.0-alpha.39`).

  ## Affected file

  https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json

  5 hook commands reference `claude-flow@alpha`:

  | Line | Hook | Command |
  |------|------|---------|
  | 9 | PreToolUse `Bash` | `cat \| npx claude-flow@alpha hooks modify-bash` |
  | 18 | PreToolUse `Write\|Edit\|MultiEdit` | `cat \| npx claude-flow@alpha hooks modify-file` |
  | 29 | PostToolUse `Bash` | `… \| xargs -0 -I {} npx claude-flow@alpha hooks post-command …` |
  | 38 | PostToolUse `Write\|Edit\|MultiEdit` | `… \| xargs -0 -I {} npx claude-flow@alpha hooks post-edit …` |
  | 68 | **Stop** | `npx claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end --generate-summary true --persist-state true --export-metrics true` |

  The Stop hook is the one users see surface in Claude Code as `Stop hook error: Failed with non-blocking status code` after every assistant turn. The
  other four fail silently per-tool-use.

  ## Reproduction

  Minimal repro, no Claude Code needed:

  ```bash
  mkdir -p /tmp/cf-repro && cd /tmp/cf-repro
  echo "{}" > package.json
  npx --yes claude-flow@alpha --version
  ```

  Result:

  ```
  npm warn exec The following package was not found and will be installed:
  claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.24
  npm error Invalid Version:
  ```

  Exit code 1.

  ## Root cause

  `claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.24`'s own `package.json` is valid:

  ```json
  {
    "version": "3.7.0-alpha.24",
    "dependencies": {
      "@claude-flow/cli-core":  "^3.7.0-alpha.5",
      "@claude-flow/mcp":       "^3.0.0-alpha.8",
      "@claude-flow/neural":    "^3.0.0-alpha.8",
      "@claude-flow/shared":    "^3.0.0-alpha.7",
      "@noble/ed25519":         "^2.1.0",
      "@ruvector/rabitq-wasm":  "^0.1.0",
      "semver":                 "^7.6.0",
      "zod":                    "^3.22.4"
    }
  }
  ```

  The `Invalid Version: ` error fires inside `@npmcli/arborist`'s **dedupe** phase, comparing semver strings deep in a transitive `@opentelemetry/*`
  subtree. From the npm trace just before the crash:

  ```
  80 placeDep node_modules/@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc
     @grpc/grpc-js@1.14.3 OK for: @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1
  81 placeDep ROOT @opentelemetry/core@1.25.1 OK for: @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1
  82 TypeError: Invalid Version:
         at new SemVer (.../semver/classes/semver.js:38:13)
         at compare (.../semver/functions/compare.js:3:32)
         at Object.gte (.../semver/functions/gte.js:2:30)
         at Node.canDedupe (.../arborist/lib/node.js:1081:32)
         at PlaceDep.pruneDedupable (.../arborist/lib/place-dep.js:426:14)
         at #buildDepStep (.../arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:917:18)
  ```

  The empty string in `Invalid Version: ` indicates a package in the resolved tree exposes an empty `version` field, which `Node.canDedupe →
  semver.gte("", "1.25.1")` then chokes on.

  The OTEL deps are pulled in transitively (most likely via `@claude-flow/mcp`), so the malformed `version` field is somewhere downstream of
  `claude-flow` itself — not in `claude-flow`'s own manifest.

  ## Scope

  - `claude-flow@alpha`  → `3.7.0-alpha.24` ❌ fails
  - `claude-flow@latest` → `3.7.0-alpha.24` ❌ fails
  - `ruflo@alpha`        → `3.7.0-alpha.24` ❌ fails (alias)
  - `ruflo@latest`       → `3.7.0-alpha.24` ❌ fails (alias)

  `alpha-v2` (2.0.0-alpha.2) and earlier 3.6.x versions install cleanly. Confirmed `3.7.0-alpha.18`, `3.7.0-alpha.20`, and `3.7.0-alpha.24` all hit the
   same crash — so this is a regression introduced somewhere in the 3.7.0 alpha line.

  ## Impact

  Every Claude Code session that has `ruflo-core` plugin installed surfaces a visible `Stop hook error` to the user after every assistant turn, plus
  four silent PreToolUse/PostToolUse failures per tool call. Because npm has to attempt the install from cold cache each time (the install fails before
   package contents are cached), it also adds ~7s of wasted registry traffic per turn.

  ## Environment

  - npm: `10.8.2`
  - node: `v20.20.0`
  - platform: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (Debian 12, devcontainer)
  - claude-code: `2.1.137`
  - ruflo-core plugin: `0.2.0`

  ## Prior art

  - #1147 — `@claude-flow/cli@3.1.0-alpha.39 fails with 'Invalid Version' npm error` (closed; same error class)
  - #1595 — `npm error: Invalid Version in koa-router@14.0.0 dependency tree` (closed)
  - #1688 — `@claude-flow/cli install: broken @ruvector/ruvllm native binary chain (Invalid Version)` (closed)

  Same failure shape recurring on a different version.

title: fix(security): plugin registry signature verification is a no-op (CWE-347)
fix(#1921): plugin hooks use a resilient shim, not bare `npx @alpha` per fire
body:
## Summary
Closes the user-visible part of #1921 — every `ruflo-core`-plugin user was seeing a `Stop hook error` after every assistant turn (plus 4 silent Pre/PostToolUse failures per tool call), because each hook ran `npx <pkg>@alpha hooks …`, which re-resolves the dist-tag and re-installs from cold cache on every fire — and when that install crashes (arborist `Invalid Version` on npm 10.8.x, deep in a transitive OTEL/grpc subtree) the failure surfaces in Claude Code, plus ~7s of wasted registry traffic per turn.

**Fix:** each plugin (`.claude-plugin/`, `plugin/`, `plugins/ruflo-core/`) ships `scripts/ruflo-hook.sh` — prefers an already-installed `ruflo`/`claude-flow` binary, falls back to `npx --prefer-offline --yes ruflo@alpha`, and **always exits 0**. `hooks.json` invokes `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ruflo-hook.sh" … || true` (the `|| true` covers the unset-`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` case → silent no-op). stdin (the hook event JSON) passes through unchanged; the stdin-jq-xargs shell-injection-safety pattern in `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` (#1747) is preserved.

> This does **not** fix the underlying arborist crash — that needs the offending empty-`version` transitive package pinned via `overrides` once it's identified on `npm@10.8.2` (see the issue thread; asked the reporter for the `~/.npm/_logs/*-debug-0.log`). This PR makes a CLI/install failure *invisible and cheap* instead of a visible error every turn, and uses the local binary / npx cache when available so most users pay zero per-turn cost.

## CI guard ("update ci guard")
- `scripts/audit-hook-commands.mjs` — fails CI if any hook `command` uses `npx` without `--prefer-offline`, or invokes the CLI without a non-fatal guard (`|| true` / `continueOnError`). Negative-tested.
- Wired into `v3-ci.yml` as `hook-command-audit` (also `bash -n`-lints each `ruflo-hook.sh` and asserts it exits 0 with an empty PATH) + added to `witness-verify` `needs[]`. Path triggers extended to `**/hooks/hooks.json`, `**/scripts/ruflo-hook.sh`, `scripts/**`.
- Witness markers for `#1921` + `#1921-shim`; `#1862`'s marker updated to track the shim-relocated invocation. `ruflo verify` → `pass: 106, regressed: 0`.

## Verification
- Shim exits 0 in every failure mode: failing `npx`, missing `npx` (empty PATH), failing local binary, working local binary (uses it). ✅
- All 3 `hooks.json` parse as valid JSON. ✅
- `node scripts/audit-hook-commands.mjs` PASS; negative test (reintroduce bare `npx ...@alpha`) → exit 1. ✅
- `node scripts/regen-witness.mjs` + `ruflo verify --manifest verification/macos/manifest.md.json` → 106 verified, 0 regressed. ✅
- [ ] CI green (`hook-command-audit` job)

## Test plan
- [x] Shim behavior unit-probed (success/failure/no-CLI/no-npx)
- [x] hook-command audit + negative test
- [x] witness regen + verify
- [ ] CI green

title: fix(#1916): register agent_logs + hive worker resolution + all 20 dangling CLI↔MCP tools — published 3.7.0-alpha.26
body:
## Summary
Addresses the two clearly-bounded pieces of #1916 (the headline "hive workers don't execute" piece is a separate, larger change — see below).

- **`agent_logs` MCP tool was never registered.** `ruflo agent logs <id>` (and the guidance surface) called `callMCPTool('agent_logs', …)` → `MCP tool not found: agent_logs`. Now registered in `agent-tools.ts`. Today it returns the agent's `createdAt` + `lastResult` as synthetic entries, with the documented shape `{ agentId, entries: [{timestamp, level, message, context?}], total }` — full per-agent activity logging lands with the hive-worker execution wiring (#1916 items 3/4).
- **Hive-spawned workers were invisible to `agent_status` / `agent_list`.** `hive-mind_spawn` writes workers to `.claude-flow/agents.json`; `agent_status`/`agent_list`/`agent_logs` read `.claude-flow/agents/store.json` — different files — so `agent status <hive-worker-id>` returned `not_found`. Added `loadAllAgents()` (canonical store ∪ hive store, canonical wins on id collision) and routed those three tools through it.

### Not in this PR
- **Task-execution dispatch** (#1916 items 3/4): `task_assign` transitions a task to `in_progress` but doesn't enqueue work or run a worker; hive `completedTasks` stays `0`. Wiring this needs a design decision (which executor — `agent_execute`? the worker daemon? a new `.claude-flow/tasks/store.json` consumer?) and is a separate change. Left as a tracked follow-up; happy to do it next if you want to pick the executor.

## CI guard ("make sure the ci guard catches this type of error")
`scripts/audit-cli-mcp-tools.mjs` scans every `callMCPTool('<name>', …)` reference in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/*.ts` and fails if `<name>` isn't registered by an MCPTool definition in `src/mcp-tools/*.ts` — i.e. the exact `MCP tool not found` class. **It surfaced 20 *other* CLI subcommands with the same bug** (`memory export`, `memory import`, `memory cleanup`, `memory compress`, `task retry`, `workflow validate`, `workflow stop`, `session export`, `session import`, `session current`, `swarm stop`, `mcp start`, `mcp stop`, `hive-mind optimize-memory`, the `hooks coverage-*` / `hooks teammate-idle` / `hooks task-completed` ones, `memory detailed-stats`) — those are carried in a monotone-decreasing baseline at `verification/cli-mcp-tool-baseline.json` (same pattern as `audit-tool-descriptions.mjs`); the audit fails on any *new* dangling reference and the count can only go down. Wired into the `tool-descriptions-audit` CI job (already in `witness-verify` `needs[]`).

Behavioral guard: `__tests__/agent-logs-hive-resolution.test.ts` (6 cases — `agent_logs` registered, unknown-agent shape, hive worker resolved by `agent_status`/`agent_list`/`agent_logs`, canonical-store-wins-on-collision). Witness markers for `#1916` + `#1916-guard`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` (cli) — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/agent-logs-hive-resolution.test.ts` — 6/6 pass
- [x] `npx vitest run __tests__/commands.test.ts __tests__/agentdb-delete-tools.test.ts` — pass
- [x] `node scripts/audit-cli-mcp-tools.mjs` PASS at baseline 20; negative test (add a fake dangling ref) → exit 1

title: [BUG] ruflo-cost-tracker: encodeProjectPath fails on Windows (no \ or : handling)
body:
## Summary

`plugins/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/track.mjs` cannot locate Claude Code session jsonl files on Windows because `encodeProjectPath()` only handles forward slashes — Windows paths contain `\` and `:`.

## Repro

```bash
# On Windows, in any project, e.g. D:\project\Subcloudy
node node_modules/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/track.mjs
```

Output:
```
cost-track: no Claude Code project dir for cwd=D:\project\Subcloudy
looked under C:\Users\<user>\.claude\projects/D:\project\Subcloudy
```

Note the corrupt path in the "looked under" line — `D:\project\Subcloudy` was passed through `cwd.replace(/\//g, '-')` which is a no-op on Windows. The real folder is `C:\Users\<user>\.claude\projects\D--project-Subcloudy\` (Claude Code on Windows encodes `:` and `\` as `-`).

**Workaround:** `TRACK_CWD="D//project/Subcloudy" node track.mjs` (manually construct a path that becomes the right folder after the `/` → `-` replace).

## Suggested fix

In `track.mjs` (line ~48):

```javascript
function encodeProjectPath(cwd) {
  // Claude Code encodes absolute path by replacing path separators AND
  // the Windows drive colon with `-`. E.g. on Windows
  //   D:\project\Subcloudy  →  D--project-Subcloudy
  // On POSIX
  //   /home/user/proj       →  -home-user-proj
  return cwd.replace(/[\/\]/g, '-').replace(/:/g, '-');
}
```

## Related issue (secondary)

After working around the path bug, `Persisted: FAILED (exit null)` on long sessions. `spawnSync('npx', ['claude-flow', 'memory', 'store', '--value', JSON.stringify(summary)])` exceeds the Windows `CreateProcess` argv limit (~32K for cmd.exe, smaller via `npx`) when `summary` includes large byModel breakdowns. Markdown output to stdout still works fine.

Possible fix: write `summary` to a temp file and use `--value-file` (if `memory store` supports it) or stream via stdin.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (10.0.26200), PowerShell
- Node v24.12.0, npm v11.6.2
- ruflo-cost-tracker 0.16.1
- @claude-flow/cli 3.7.0-alpha.26
- Claude Code v2.1.139

## Impact

`cost-report` skill is unusable on Windows out of the box — every Claude Code user on Windows hits this on first try with no obvious fix path (the error message tells them a directory doesn't exist, but the directory the script is looking for is itself wrong).

🤖 Filed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) on behalf of a Windows user

title: fix(#1927): ruflo-cost-tracker encodeProjectPath handles Windows backslash + drive colon
