title: feat(ruflo-agent): rename ruflo-wasm → ruflo-agent + Claude Managed Agents (cloud) runtime — ADR-115 (proposed→accepted, implemented)
body:
Tracking issue: #1931 · ADR: ADR-115 (Accepted, with Implementation notes).

## Summary
`ruflo-wasm` only covered the local WASM-sandboxed agent runtime (`rvagent` — `@ruvector/rvagent-wasm`, the `wasm_agent_*`/`wasm_gallery_*` MCP tools). This makes it the home for **all ruflo agent runtimes**, behind one mental model — same pattern as `ConsensusTransport` (`LocalTransport` | `FederationTransport`):

| Runtime | Tools | When |
|---|---|---|
| **WASM** (local, `rvagent`) | `wasm_agent_*` / `wasm_gallery_*` | fast, free, ephemeral, offline; untrusted code in a sandbox |
| **Managed** (Anthropic cloud — [Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview), beta) | `managed_agent_*` | long-running/async; real cloud container w/ packages + network; persistent fs + transcript across turns |

## Changes
- **Rename** `plugins/ruflo-wasm/` → **`plugins/ruflo-agent/`** (`git mv`; `plugin.json` name/desc/keywords span both runtimes; `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, READMEs, `discover-plugins` skill, `verification/inventory.json`, ADR-115 refs updated). `wasm_agent_*`/`wasm_gallery_*` tool *names* unchanged.
- **`managed_agent_*` MCP tools** (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/managed-agent-tools.ts`, registered in `mcp-client.ts`) — `create`/`prompt`/`status`/`events`/`list`/`terminate`, wrapping the Managed Agents REST API with plain `fetch` (no new SDK dep, `anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01`). Key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`CLAUDE_API_KEY`; graceful "use `wasm_agent_create` for a local no-key runtime" when absent. ADR-112 descriptions. `mcpServers`/`skills`/`packages`/`networking`/`initScript` pass through.
- **Plugin wiring** — `skills/managed-agent/SKILL.md` + `commands/managed-agent.md` (cloud-runtime skill/command; WASM-vs-managed table, key prereq + fallback, `mcpServers`-reachability caveat, cost/cleanup discipline; explicit `allowed-tools`).
- **CI guard** — `plugins/ruflo-agent/scripts/smoke.sh` (12 checks; was 10, +2 fixed/added) + new `.github/workflows/ruflo-agent-smoke.yml` (plugin had no CI gate). Also covered by `audit-cli-mcp-tools` (311 registered / 0 dangling) + `audit-tool-descriptions` (0 no-guidance).
- **ADR-115** → Accepted + an Implementation section.

## Validation
- Live e2e against `api.anthropic.com` with the org's Anthropic key (GCP `claude-flow/anthropic-api-key`), via `ruflo mcp exec -t managed_agent_*`: `create` (haiku, custom system) → `prompt` (`echo … > /tmp/r.txt && cat …`) → `{finished:true, status:idle, stopReason:end_turn, assistantText:"Done.", toolUses:[bash], 13 events}` → `terminate` (`sessionDeleted+environmentDeleted`). No-key path returns the graceful error.
- `claude --plugin-dir plugins/ruflo-agent` loads the plugin and lists its skills (`managed-agent`, `wasm-agent`, `wasm-gallery`).
- `bash plugins/ruflo-agent/scripts/smoke.sh` → 12 passed / 0 failed. `cli` build clean.

## Follow-ups (in #1931)
`runtime:"managed"` flag on `wasm_agent_*` (unify); a deployed/tunneled HTTP ruflo MCP server so a Managed Agent gets ruflo's 314 tools; `task_assign`/federation dispatch to a Managed Agent session (third executor — #1916 items 3/4); cost-tracking + orphaned-session GC; `multiagent`/`define-outcomes` (research preview, feature-flagged).

title: ruflo-cost-tracker: cost-compact-context resolution broken on pnpm-workspaces install
body:
## Summary

The `ruflo-cost-tracker:cost-compact-context` skill (v0.16.1) documents `( cd v3 && node ../plugins/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/compact.mjs "<query>" )` as the canonical invocation. On a marketplace install where `v3/` is a pnpm workspaces monorepo (the shipped layout in `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/`), that command fails with:

```
bridge unavailable: Cannot find module '@claude-flow/integration/token-optimizer'
```

…because pnpm does not hoist workspace packages into `v3/node_modules/@claude-flow/`. The `@claude-flow/integration` package lives at `v3/@claude-flow/integration/` and is only resolvable from within its own directory (or from another workspace that consumes it as a dep — but in this install **no other workspace declares it as a dependency**, so the resolution graph is empty).

Repro on a fresh install (today, 2026-05-12):

```bash
$ cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3 && \
    node ../plugins/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/compact.mjs "test"
bridge unavailable: Cannot find module '@claude-flow/integration/token-optimizer'
Require stack:
- /home/bowma/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/package.json
Run from a directory where `@claude-flow/integration` resolves, e.g. `cd v3 && ...`.
```

The skill's documented fallback path fires cleanly, which is correct — but the bridge is *gettable*, just not from `cwd=v3/`.

## Full sequence needed to get the bridge working (5 steps)

| # | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dist/` not built — `@claude-flow/integration` ships `src/token-optimizer.ts` but `package.json` `exports."./token-optimizer"` points at `dist/token-optimizer.js`. | `cd v3/@claude-flow/integration && npx tsc` |
| 2 | `agentic-flow` not declared as a dep anywhere in v3. | `cd v3 && pnpm add agentic-flow --workspace-root --legacy-peer-deps` |
| 3 | `sharp@0.32.6` (transitive dep of agentic-flow) has no prebuilt for linux-x64 on this runtime; native binding missing. | `cd v3/node_modules/.pnpm/sharp@0.32.6/node_modules/sharp && npm install` (rebuilds from source against vendored libvips) |
| 4 | `agentic-flow/dist/index.js` runs `startHealthServer()` unconditionally on import, binding port 8080. Fails with EADDRINUSE on any host with something already on 8080 (e.g. a k8s NodePort, a dev server, a forwarded service). | `HEALTH_PORT=48080 node ...` — env override is supported by `health.js:59` but not mentioned in the skill. |
| 5 | Resolver can't find `@claude-flow/integration/token-optimizer` from `cwd=v3/` because pnpm workspaces aren't hoisted. | Run from `cwd=v3/@claude-flow/integration/` instead — the package self-resolves via its own `exports` map. |

Working incantation after all five:

```bash
HEALTH_PORT=48080 \
  bash -c '(cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/integration && \
    node ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ruflo/ruflo-cost-tracker/0.16.1/scripts/compact.mjs "<query>")'
```

Output reports `agentic-flow bridge available: true` and a non-zero `tokensSaved`. Confirmed working today on Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2+ / Node 22.22.0 / pnpm 8.15.0.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Document the pnpm-workspaces layout** in the skill's "Steps" section, with the correct `cd v3/@claude-flow/integration/` path (or update the skill to detect the install shape and pick the right cwd).
2. **Pre-build `dist/`** in the integration package (publish with `dist/` included, or run `tsc` in a postinstall hook) — the current skill instruction assumes the package's `exports."./token-optimizer"` is live, but the source ships without `dist/`.
3. **Move `startHealthServer()` behind an explicit `start()` call in `agentic-flow/index.js`**, or default `HEALTH_PORT` to a high random port when imported as a library (not invoked as a CLI). Right now any host with something on 8080 (extremely common) crashes any consumer that imports agentic-flow. The skill should at minimum surface `HEALTH_PORT` as a documented env override.
4. **Declare `agentic-flow` as a dep of `@claude-flow/integration`** instead of relying on the consuming workspace to install it. The integration package is the one that imports it.

## Environment

- OS: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2+
- Node: v22.22.0
- pnpm: 8.15.0
- ruflo-cost-tracker: v0.16.1 (cache + marketplace agree)
- ruflo marketplace: latest from `https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo.git`

Repro details and the workaround wrapper script are checked in at `tbowman01/jetson:scripts/ruflo-compact.sh` (commit referenced below).

title: ruflo-agent: rename ruflo-wasm → ruflo-agent + add Claude Managed Agents (cloud) runtime (ADR-115)
body:
## Summary

`ruflo-wasm` only covered the **local WASM-sandboxed** agent runtime (`rvagent` — `@ruvector/rvagent-wasm`, the `wasm_agent_*` / `wasm_gallery_*` MCP tools). It's becoming the home for **all ruflo agent runtimes**, behind one mental model:

| Runtime | Tools | When |
|---|---|---|
| **WASM** (local, `rvagent`) | `wasm_agent_*` / `wasm_gallery_*` | fast, free, ephemeral, offline; untrusted code in a sandbox |
| **Managed** (Anthropic cloud — [Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview), beta) | `managed_agent_*` | long-running/async (minutes–hours); real cloud container w/ pre-installed packages + network; persistent filesystem + transcript across turns |

Same pattern as `ConsensusTransport` (`LocalTransport` | `FederationTransport`) — one interface, local-vs-cloud backends. Design = ADR-115 (now Accepted, with implementation notes).

## Done

- **Rename** `plugins/ruflo-wasm/` → `plugins/ruflo-agent/` (`git mv`; `plugin.json` name/description/keywords now span both runtimes; `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` entry + READMEs + `discover-plugins` skill + `verification/inventory.json` + ADR-115 refs updated). The `wasm_agent_*` / `wasm_gallery_*` tool *names* are unchanged.
- **`managed_agent_*` MCP tools** (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/managed-agent-tools.ts`, registered in `mcp-client.ts`) — 6 tools, plain `fetch` against the Managed Agents REST API (`anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01`), no new SDK dep:
  - `managed_agent_create` → `agents.create` + `environments.create` + `sessions.create` (↔ `wasm_agent_create`); accepts `model`/`system`/`name`/`networking`/`packages`/`initScript`/`mcpServers`/`skills`.
  - `managed_agent_prompt` → `events.send(user.message)` + poll `GET /sessions/{id}/events` until a terminal `session.status_*` (default 180 s, cap 600 s) → `{finished, status, stopReason, assistantText, toolUses[], eventCount}` (↔ `wasm_agent_prompt`).
  - `managed_agent_status`, `managed_agent_events` (full transcript + summary, ↔ `wasm_agent_files`), `managed_agent_list`, `managed_agent_terminate` (`DELETE /sessions/{id}` ± env, ↔ `wasm_agent_terminate`).
  - Key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_API_KEY`; **degrades gracefully** with a structured "use `wasm_agent_create` for a local no-key runtime" error when absent — the CLI/MCP server stays up. ADR-112-compliant descriptions.
- **Plugin wiring** — `plugins/ruflo-agent/skills/managed-agent/SKILL.md` + `commands/managed-agent.md` (cloud-runtime skill/command: WASM-vs-managed table, key prereq + fallback, `mcpServers`-reachability caveat, cost/cleanup discipline). Explicit `allowed-tools` (no wildcard).
- **CI guard** — `plugins/ruflo-agent/scripts/smoke.sh` (12 checks: manifest is `ruflo-agent` w/ both-runtime keywords; all 10 `wasm_*` + all 6 `managed_agent_*` referenced; managed-agent skill keeps explicit `allowed-tools` + offers the `wasm_agent_create` fallback; ADR cross-refs) + new `.github/workflows/ruflo-agent-smoke.yml` (the plugin had no CI gate before). Also covered by `audit-cli-mcp-tools` (311 registered / 0 dangling) + `audit-tool-descriptions` (0 no-guidance).
- **Validated** — live e2e against `api.anthropic.com` with the org's Anthropic key (GCP `claude-flow/anthropic-api-key`): `create` (haiku, custom system) → `prompt` (`echo … > /tmp/r.txt && cat …`) → `{finished:true, status:idle, stopReason:end_turn, assistantText:"Done.", toolUses:[bash], 13 events}` → `terminate` (`sessionDeleted+environmentDeleted`); no-key path returns the graceful error. `claude --plugin-dir plugins/ruflo-agent` loads the plugin and lists `managed-agent`/`wasm-agent`/`wasm-gallery`. `smoke.sh` 12/0; cli build clean.

## Follow-ups (tracked here)

- [ ] Unify: `runtime: "managed"` flag on `wasm_agent_*` that delegates to `managed_agent_*` (one interface).
- [ ] Cloud-hosted ruflo: a deployed/tunneled **HTTP ruflo MCP server** so a Managed Agent's `mcpServers` can point at it → the cloud agent gets ruflo's 314 tools (needs a publicly reachable URL — a local `ruflo mcp start` isn't reachable from Anthropic's cloud).
- [ ] `task_assign` / federation dispatch → a Managed Agent session (a **third executor**: local WASM | federated peer | Anthropic Managed — closes #1916 items 3/4).
- [ ] Cost-tracking integration (record completed managed sessions in the `cost-tracking` namespace) + a `ruflo doctor` / GC check for orphaned (still-billing) sessions; pre-run cost estimate in `managed_agent_prompt` for long tasks.
- [ ] `multiagent` / `define-outcomes` (Managed Agents research preview) — feature-flagged.

## Refs
- ADR-115 (`v3/docs/adr/ADR-115-managed-agents-rvagent-backend.md`) — design + implementation notes
- Claude Managed Agents: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview
- `@ruvector/rvagent-wasm` (the WASM runtime); ADR-070 (rvagent-wasm + ruvllm-wasm integration); #1916 (task-execution dispatch)

## Summary

**ADR-117 (Accepted)** — dispatch heavy `neural-trader` jobs (multi-year walk-forward backtests, big Monte-Carlo, parameter sweeps, LSTM/Transformer/N-BEATS training) to an **Anthropic Managed Agent cloud container** via the `managed_agent_*` tools (ADR-115, shipped in `3.7.0-alpha.27`). No new MCP tools, no new dependencies — pure orchestration on top of what ADR-115 already ships.

- `v3/docs/adr/ADR-117-neural-trader-managed-agent-backtests.md` — the decision + cost-optimization rules + the shipped-implementation manifest.
- `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/skills/trader-cloud-backtest/SKILL.md` — the recipe: provision-once → pre-flight-cheap → run → ingest-locally → terminate-eagerly. `allowed-tools` scoped to `managed_agent_*` + `memory_*` + `agentdb_pattern-store` + `Bash`/`Read` (no wildcard grant).
- `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/commands/trader.md` — `/trader cloud <backtest|train|sweep>` subcommand.
- `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/scripts/smoke.sh` — step 2 asserts the 7th skill (`trader-cloud-backtest`) exists, references `managed_agent_create`, and names the local `trader-backtest` fallback; step 10 ADR-status check corrected (`Proposed` → `Accepted`, matching the actual contract ADR).
- `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/README.md` — overview + skills table + Architecture-Decisions + Related-Plugins cross-refs to ADR-117 / ADR-115 / `ruflo-agent`.
- `v3/docs/adr/ADR-115-…` Links — cross-refs ADR-117 as the first consumer of the `managed_agent_*` runtime.

### Cost optimization (the "optimize" requirement)
A cloud session bills container time + tokens until terminated, so the recipe is built to minimize both: install-once in `initScript`, reuse the environment, **pre-flight cheap** (1-path / 3-month smoke before a 1000-path / multi-year run), batch sweeps into one prompt (one container), terminate eagerly + GC orphans (#1931), cheap agent model (Haiku/Sonnet — the compute is the Rust engine, not the LM; ADR-026), estimate before kicking off.

### Security
Private market-data-feed creds go in the environment's env-var block (user-provided, **never hardcoded** — per the project's "don't expose keys" rule); native Rust runs in Anthropic's isolated container (strictly better isolation than the local runtime). Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + Managed Agents beta — the skill degrades to the local `trader-backtest` skill without it.

title: [ruflo-rag-memory] Add per-file exclusion to memory_import_claude (current allProjects: true/false is too coarse for voice-fidelity discipline)
body:
**Plugin:** ruflo-rag-memory
**Tool:** memory_import_claude
**Ruflo version:** v3.7.0-alpha.11
**Reporter context:** operator running Claude Code with voice-fidelity discipline; multiple named-persona content classifiers active

## Problem

The `memory_import_claude` MCP tool currently supports `allProjects: true/false` granularity. For operators with voice-fidelity discipline (AI agents that must NOT learn from voice-load-bearing content authored by specific personas), this all-or-nothing import is too coarse.

## Concrete blocker

In our setup, 16 of 57 claude-mem `.md` files at `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/*.md` match voice-fidelity patterns (named-persona markers, voice-load-bearing content). We cannot import the other 41 files into the unified `claude-memories` namespace without contaminating it with the 16. Result: the bridge stays `not-synced` even though the embedding substrate is ready (100% coverage post-Plan #2).

## Proposed enhancement

Accept a file-exclusion parameter, e.g.:

```javascript
mcp__ruflo__memory_import_claude({
  allProjects: true,
  excludeFilePatterns: ["**/voice-*.md", "**/persona-*.md"]
})
```

OR explicit exclude list:

```javascript
mcp__ruflo__memory_import_claude({
  allProjects: true,
  excludeFiles: [
    "C:/Users/yasir/.claude/projects/D--Documents-Haque-Brain-v2/memory/voice_specific_file.md",
    // ... full list ...
  ]
})
```

Either form would unblock voice-fidelity-aware bulk imports without operator-side per-tool wrapping or fork-and-patch.

## Current workaround

HALT the import; capture per-file matched-pattern baselines in the session log; defer the import until per-file exclusion lands. Plan #3 in our system stays at `HALTED-pending-cowork-review`.

## Why this matters beyond our setup

Any operator with named-persona voice safety, client-confidential content classification, or PII-aware memory hygiene would benefit. The ruflo-aidefence plugin already implements PII pattern detection — extending memory_import_claude with the same exclusion-pattern primitive would compose cleanly.

## References

- ruflo-rag-memory plugin
- ruflo-aidefence plugin (3-Gate Security Pattern as composition reference)
- Anthropic's voice-fidelity guidance for Claude Code (operator-side discipline pattern)

title: Win32 current-project import misses current Claude slug in importer
body:
## Summary
On a pure Win32 + Win32 setup, `memory_import_claude({ allProjects: false })` does not find the current Claude project memory directory because the current-project slug logic only replaces forward slashes. A Windows cwd such as `C:\Users\tobia\OneDrive\Desktop\Claude Stuff` therefore remains unsanitized and does not match Claude Code's on-disk slug `C--Users-tobia-OneDrive-Desktop-Claude-Stuff`.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 26200.8328
- Claude Code platform: Win32
- Claude Code cwd: `C:\Users\tobia\OneDrive\Desktop\Claude Stuff`
- Ruflo version: `v3.7.0-alpha.21`
- Pre-upgrade baseline: `v3.6.11` (bug already present there)
- DB path type: workspace-local `.swarm/memory.db` on Windows path (`C:\...\Claude Stuff\.swarm\memory.db`)
- Ruflo MCP: Win32 process

## Repro
1. Ensure Claude Code has memory files under:
   `C:\Users\<user>\.claude\projects\C--Users-tobia-OneDrive-Desktop-Claude-Stuff\memory`
2. Run: `memory_import_claude({ allProjects: false })`
3. Observe: `imported: 0`, `message: "No Claude memory files found"`

## Expected
The importer resolves the current Win32 cwd to the same Claude project slug that Claude Code uses on disk and imports the memory files for that project.

## Actual
The importer derives the current-project slug with slash-only replacement and therefore misses the existing Windows Claude slug directory.

## Source Reference
- `memory-tools.ts:3342-3347`
- Current logic: `cwd.replace(/\//g, '-')` — no backslash, drive-colon, or whitespace handling

## Why this is a Win32+Win32-specific gap
PR #1886 addressed a different setup class. Win32 cwd contains backslashes, a drive colon, and spaces. Claude Code's actual disk slug uses a broader normalization class (effectively `replace(/[\:\/]/g,'-')` plus whitespace normalization).

## Combined Acceptance
- `memory_import_claude({ allProjects: false })` imports the current Win32 project without requiring `allProjects: true`
- Win32 cwd resolves to the same Claude slug used under `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory`
- Spaces, drive letters, and backslashes are normalized consistently
- Path `C:\Users\tobia\OneDrive\Desktop\Claude Stuff` resolves to `C--Users-tobia-OneDrive-Desktop-Claude-Stuff`
- No regression for other setup classes

## Out of Scope
- PR #1886 itself; WSL+Win32, WSL+WSL, or POSIX-only setup classes; search/index bugs

title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] Hook scaffolding writes $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR paths but installs helpers globally — every Bash hook MODULE_NOT_FOUND
body:
## Summary

`ruflo init` writes hook commands to `~/.claude/settings.json` anchored at `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/helpers/...`, but the installer only deposits the helper scripts under the **global** `~/.claude/helpers/`. Result: every Bash/Edit/Session hook fires `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in every project the user opens.

## Environment

- ruflo: `v3.7.0-alpha.27` (via `npx -y ruflo@latest`)
- Node: `v25.9.0`
- Claude Code: `v2.1.140`
- OS: Ubuntu 24 LTS (Linux 6.8)
- Fresh `ruflo init` in a Next.js project; no prior `~/.claude-flow` content.

## Symptom

Visible to the user on every Bash tool call from Claude Code:

```
node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1478
  throw err;
  ^

Error: Cannot find module '/home/<user>/<project>/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs'
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1475:15)
    ...
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
```

## Root cause

`ruflo init` writes 16 hook command entries into `~/.claude/settings.json` (global) of the form:

```json
"command": "sh -c 'exec node \"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs\" pre-bash'"
```

Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<absolute project root>` when hooks fire, so the path resolves to `<project>/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs`. **But the installer never copies the helpers into per-project `.claude/helpers/`** — they only exist at `~/.claude/helpers/`.

Affected hook events: `PreToolUse` (Bash, Write|Edit|MultiEdit), `PostToolUse` (Bash, Write|Edit|MultiEdit), `UserPromptSubmit`, `SessionStart` (both `hook-handler.cjs` and `auto-memory-hook.mjs`), `SessionEnd`, `Stop`, `PreCompact` (manual + auto), `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `Notification` — 16 command strings total.

## Repro

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/ruflo-repro && cd /tmp/ruflo-repro
git init -q
npx ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.27 init
# Then in any Claude Code session, run any Bash tool — hook crashes with the trace above.

# Or directly, without Claude Code:
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$PWD sh -c 'exec node "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs" pre-bash' < /dev/null
# → Error: Cannot find module '/tmp/ruflo-repro/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs'
```

## Fix options (any one works)

1. **Anchor hook paths to `$HOME`** instead of `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`. The helpers live at a single global location, so `$HOME/.claude/helpers/...` is the correct reference. `sh -c '...'` single-quote semantics already let the inner shell expand `$HOME`. This is the one-replacement fix I applied locally and verified.
2. Or scaffold the helpers into per-project `.claude/helpers/` during `ruflo init`. Wasteful (~300 KB × N projects) and creates upgrade-skew issues.
3. Or use `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$HOME}` to try project-local first, fall back to global. Useful if per-project helper overrides are a future goal.

Recommendation: option 1 today; option 3 if per-project overrides ever ship.

## Local workaround

In `~/.claude/settings.json`, replace all 16 occurrences of `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` with `$HOME`. After: every hook event resolves and exits 0.

## Related

- After fixing this, the `pre-bash` hook still prints a soft TypeError warning — filed separately.
- The `ruflo doctor` "Memory Database: Not initialized" warning and the CLI `memory store` non-persistence both share a different root cause — filed separately.

Happy to PR if a maintainer points at the right scaffolding template/branch.

title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] hook-handler.cjs:116 falls back to toolInput (object) for prompt — pre-bash hook TypeError on every Bash call
body:
## Summary

`hook-handler.cjs` line 116 falls back to `toolInput` (the parsed object) when building `prompt`, then line 148 calls `.toLowerCase()` on it. Every `pre-bash` invocation from Claude Code prints a soft TypeError warning.

## Environment

- ruflo: `v3.7.0-alpha.27`
- Node: `v25.9.0`
- Claude Code: `v2.1.140`

## Symptom

```
[WARN] Hook pre-bash encountered an error: (hookInput.command || prompt).toLowerCase is not a function
```

Non-blocking (handler still exits 0 and `[OK] Command validated` is suppressed), but the warning fires on **every** Bash tool call once the hook resolution itself works (see sibling issue on `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` scaffolding).

## Root cause

`helpers/hook-handler.cjs:116`:

```js
const prompt = hookInput.prompt || hookInput.command || toolInput
  || process.env.PROMPT || process.env.TOOL_INPUT_command || args.join(' ') || '';
```

Claude Code sends stdin like:

```json
{"tool_input":{"command":"ls -la"},"tool_name":"Bash"}
```

After normalisation at line 112, `toolInput === {command: "ls -la"}`. The `||` chain sees `toolInput` as truthy and assigns the *object* to `prompt`. Then line 148:

```js
const cmd = (hookInput.command || prompt).toLowerCase();
```

calls `.toLowerCase()` on the object → TypeError.

The same `prompt` value is also used at line 124 (`intelligence.getContext(prompt)`) and line 132 (`prompt.substring(0, 80)`), both of which assume a string.

## Fix

Change the line 116 fallback from `toolInput` to `toolInput.command`:

```js
const prompt = hookInput.prompt || hookInput.command || toolInput.command
  || process.env.PROMPT || process.env.TOOL_INPUT_command || args.join(' ') || '';
```

Verified locally: TypeError gone, `pre-bash` returns `[OK] Command validated` as designed, `UserPromptSubmit` routing output renders correctly.

## Repro

```bash
echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"ls"},"tool_name":"Bash"}' \
  | node ~/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs pre-bash
# → [WARN] Hook pre-bash encountered an error: (hookInput.command || prompt).toLowerCase is not a function
```

Happy to PR a one-line fix.

title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] CLI `memory store` reports success but does not persist — fresh sql.js process per invocation (MCP path works correctly)
body:
## Summary

`ruflo memory store` (and `retrieve`/`list`/`search`/`stats` etc. on the CLI) report success but never share state across invocations. The same operations via the `mcp__ruflo__memory_*` MCP tools (running inside the long-lived `ruflo mcp start` daemon) work correctly. The CLI surface gives users a **false-success message and silent data loss**.

## Environment

- ruflo: `v3.7.0-alpha.27`
- Node: `v25.9.0`
- Claude Code: `v2.1.140`
- DB path (after `ruflo memory init`): `<project>/data/memory/memory.db`

## Symptom

```bash
$ ruflo memory init --verify
Memory database already initialized at /home/<u>/<proj>/data/memory/memory.db

$ ruflo memory store --namespace providers --key foo --value '{"x":1}'
[OK] Data stored successfully
+-----------+----------------------+
| Key       | foo                  |
| Namespace | providers            |
| Size      | 9 bytes              |
| Vector    | Yes (384-dim)        |
| ID        | entry_1778628537052_ |
+-----------+----------------------+

$ ruflo memory retrieve --namespace providers --key foo
[WARN] Key not found: foo

$ ruflo memory list --namespace providers
[WARN] No entries found

$ ruflo memory stats
| Total Entries |             0 |
| Location      |               |
```

On-disk verification:

```bash
$ sqlite3 data/memory/memory.db "SELECT count(*) FROM memory_entries"
0
```

…even after multiple "successful" CLI stores. The schema is correct (16 tables incl. `memory_entries`, `patterns`, `trajectories`, `vector_indexes`, learning tables, embedding columns). The WAL file grows during the CLI process (~250 KB) but no commits flush to the main DB.

## MCP path works correctly

Same project, same DB path:

```
mcp__ruflo__memory_store({namespace:"providers", key:"foo", value:{x:1}})
  → {success:true, stored:true, hasEmbedding:true, embeddingDimensions:384, storeTime:"26ms"}

mcp__ruflo__memory_list({namespace:"providers"})
  → {entries:[{key:"foo", hasEmbedding:true, size:9}], total:1}

mcp__ruflo__memory_stats()
  → {initialized:true, totalEntries:1, embeddingCoverage:"100.0%"}
```

## Inference

Each `npx ruflo memory <subcommand>` invocation spawns a fresh `node` process with its own in-process sql.js WASM instance that doesn't load from or save back to the on-disk file. The long-lived `ruflo mcp start` daemon holds correct state because it's a single process.

So from the user's perspective:
- The CLI confidently reports stores succeeded — they didn't.
- The MCP tools work as advertised.
- There's no error or hint that the CLI is a debug-only surface.

## Suggested fix

Either:

1. Make CLI `memory store|retrieve|list|search|stats|delete|export` route through the running MCP daemon over IPC (if connected), and warn loudly if not. This matches the architecture users observe.
2. Or have the CLI open the on-disk `memory.db` directly via `better-sqlite3` (or load+save the sql.js handle to the file) so single-shot invocations actually persist.
3. At minimum, **stop printing `[OK] Data stored successfully` for writes that don't persist**. Replace with a clear error or "in-memory only — start the daemon to persist".

Option 1 is the cleanest given the existing daemon-centric design.

## Related

- `ruflo doctor` reports "Memory Database: Not initialized" even after `memory init` — filed separately, likely same root cause (doctor uses the same broken CLI path).

Happy to PR if maintainers indicate the preferred direction (route through daemon vs. direct sqlite3 client in CLI).

title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] `ruflo doctor` reports 'Memory Database: Not initialized' even when DB exists on disk and MCP reports initialized:true
body:
## Summary

`ruflo doctor` reports `⚠ Memory Database: Not initialized` even when `<project>/data/memory/memory.db` exists on disk with the full ruflo schema and the MCP daemon is happily reading/writing it. Likely the same root cause as the CLI memory non-persistence issue (filed separately).

## Environment

- ruflo: `v3.7.0-alpha.27`
- Node: `v25.9.0`
- Claude Code: `v2.1.140`

## Symptom

```bash
$ ruflo memory init --verify
Memory database already initialized at /home/<u>/<proj>/data/memory/memory.db

$ ls -la data/memory/memory.db
-rw------- 1 ai ai 147456  memory.db
-rw------- 1 ai ai  32768  memory.db-shm
-rw------- 1 ai ai 255472  memory.db-wal

$ sqlite3 data/memory/memory.db ".tables" | head -3
learning_experiences  patterns
memory_entries        trajectories
...  # 16 tables, all correct

$ ruflo doctor
...
⚠ Memory Database: Not initialized
⚠ Daemon Status: Not running
...
```

Concurrently, via the MCP server:

```
mcp__ruflo__memory_stats() → {"initialized": true, ...}
```

So the daemon-side stats correctly report `initialized: true`, but doctor's CLI-side check reports the opposite.

## Likely root cause

Doctor probably opens a fresh in-process sql.js WASM handle (same pattern as the rest of the CLI — see the sibling issue on CLI non-persistence), gets an empty in-memory DB, and reports "not initialized." It doesn't appear to check for:

- Existence of the on-disk `data/memory/memory.db` with the expected schema, or
- A connection to the running MCP daemon, or
- Any other authoritative state.

## Suggested fix

Doctor's "Memory Database" check should:

1. Look for `<project>/data/memory/memory.db` (or whatever the configured path is) on disk and confirm the expected schema exists.
2. If the MCP daemon is reachable, query it for `initialized` state directly.
3. Only report "Not initialized" if both of the above fail.

Bonus: the "Daemon Status: Not running" warning is also worth revisiting — `claude mcp list` confirms `ruflo: npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start - ✓ Connected`, so a daemon-equivalent process *is* running and serving MCP requests. Doctor's notion of "daemon" may need to be reconciled with the MCP server lifecycle (or relabelled to disambiguate the two).

## Related

- CLI `memory store|list|retrieve|stats` are also affected by the in-process sql.js handle problem (filed separately). A fix there will likely fix doctor for free.

title: memory search returns 0 results on default install: schema is 768-dim but default model is 384-dim
body:
# Bug report: `memory search` returns 0 results — schema hardcodes 768-dim but default embedding model is 384-dim

## Environment

- `ruflo` version: **`v3.7.0-alpha.27`** (output of `ruflo --version`)
- Node: `v24.11.1`, npm: `v11.6.2`
- OS: macOS 15.x (Apple Silicon)
- Install: `npx ruflo@latest init --full --with-embeddings` in a fresh project directory
- Embedding model: default (`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, 384-dim)

## TL;DR

After a clean install with the default model, `ruflo memory search -q "..."` always returns `0 results`. The root cause is a **dimension mismatch** between the hardcoded schema (768-dim) and the default ONNX embedding model (384-dim), compounded by two related defaults (wrong namespace, too-high similarity threshold).

## Repro

```bash
mkdir /tmp/ruflo-repro && cd /tmp/ruflo-repro
git init && git commit --allow-empty -m init

npx ruflo@latest init --full --with-embeddings
npx ruflo@latest memory init --force --verify

# Store a doc with --vector
echo "TikTok OAuth refresh token rotation runs daily at 03:00 UTC via LaunchAgent" > note.txt
npx ruflo@latest memory store -k "doc/test" --value "$(cat note.txt)" --namespace project --vector --upsert
# → Output confirms: "Vector: Yes (384-dim)" ✓

# Try semantic search
npx ruflo@latest memory search -q "TikTok token refresh"
# → "[WARN] No results found"   ← BUG

# Even with explicit namespace / lower threshold / inline build:
npx ruflo@latest memory search -q "TikTok token refresh" --namespace project --threshold 0.1 --build-hnsw
# → still "[WARN] No results found"
```

## Root cause (three compounding bugs)

### 1. Schema hardcodes `dimensions = 768`

The init script creates `vector_indexes` rows with `dimensions = 768`, but the default ONNX model (`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) produces **384-dim** vectors. HNSW rejects the dimension-mismatched vectors during indexing.

**Files involved (in npm cache):**

- `node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/memory-initializer.js:871-872`
- `node_modules/@claude-flow/shared/.swarm/schema.sql:304-305`
- `node_modules/ruflo/src/ruvocal/.swarm/schema.sql:304-305`

All three contain:

```sql
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vector_indexes (id, name, dimensions) VALUES
  ('default', 'default', 768),
  ('patterns', 'patterns', 768);
```

Verifying after install:

```bash
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT name, dimensions, total_vectors FROM vector_indexes;"
# default|768|0
# patterns|768|0
```

But the actual stored entry uses 384-dim:

```bash
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT key, embedding_dimensions, embedding_model FROM memory_entries;"
# doc/test|384|Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
```

### 2. `embeddings index -a build` defaults to `-c default` even when entries are in another namespace

`memory store -k ... --namespace project --vector` writes to `memory_entries.namespace = 'project'`. But `embeddings index -a build` without `-c` builds for `default` (which has 0 entries). HNSW index status reports `Vector Count: 0` until you explicitly run `ruflo embeddings index -a build -c project`.

Once corrected:

```bash
ruflo embeddings index -a build -c project
# Vectors: 4    ✓
```

### 3. Default `--threshold` is too aggressive for `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`

- `ruflo memory search` defaults to `--threshold 0.7`
- `ruflo embeddings search` defaults to `-t 0.5`

But typical cosine similarities for this model with short queries vs long documents (a normal use case — searching a project's docs) score **0.1–0.3**, not 0.7+. After fixing (1) and (2), `--threshold 0.7` still returns 0 results; `--threshold 0.1` returns the expected 4 ranked hits.

```bash
ruflo memory search -q "TikTok token refresh" --namespace project --threshold 0.1
# 4 results, top score 0.24    ✓
```

## Additional related issue: `embeddings init --force` rejects its own default model name

```bash
ruflo embeddings init --force
# [ERROR] Initialization failed: Invalid model ID format: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
#         Only alphanumeric, dots, hyphens, and underscores allowed.
```

The model-name validator rejects `/`, but `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` *is* the default model used by `init --with-embeddings`. So `--force` reinit is unusable until the validator is relaxed (or the model name is parametrized differently).

## Suggested fixes

Several mutually-exclusive options — please pick one:

### Option A — Patch the schema to match the default model (minimal change)

In all three files above, change:

```sql
('default', 'default', 768),
('patterns', 'patterns', 768);
```

to:

```sql
('default', 'default', 384),
('patterns', 'patterns', 384);
```

This aligns the schema with the actual default model. Users who later switch to a 768-dim model (e.g., `all-mpnet-base-v2`) would need to recreate the index — but that's already true today, since switching models always invalidates HNSW.

### Option B — Read the dimension from the embedding model at init time

`ruflo memory init` already calls `embeddings init` internally when `--with-embeddings` is passed. Have it query the loaded model's `.dimensions` property and use *that* value for the `vector_indexes` rows, instead of a hardcoded literal.

### Option C — Switch the default model to a 768-dim variant

E.g., `Xenova/all-mpnet-base-v2` (768-dim). This matches the existing schema. But the model is ~5x larger, slower to download, and uses more memory — probably not a good fit for a "works out of the box" default.

### Plus: validator fix

Relax the model-ID validator in `embeddings init` to allow `/` (which is standard in Hugging Face IDs like `org/model`).

### Plus: docs

Until the default threshold is tuned per-model, `--threshold` should be highlighted prominently in `memory search --help` examples — the current default of 0.7 produces empty results for the most common workflow (storing and searching project documentation).

## Workaround (for users hitting this today)

```bash
# After `ruflo init --full --with-embeddings` + `ruflo memory init --force`:

# 1. Patch the schema-vs-model dimension mismatch
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "UPDATE vector_indexes SET dimensions=384"
rm -f .swarm/hnsw.index ruvector.db   # remove stale 768-dim binary index

# 2. Store entries with --namespace project (or whatever) + --vector
ruflo memory store -k "doc/foo" --value "$(cat foo.md)" --namespace project --vector --upsert
# ... repeat for each doc ...

# 3. Build the HNSW index for THAT namespace (not "default")
ruflo embeddings index -a build -c project

# 4. Search with a sane threshold
ruflo memory search -q "your query" --namespace project --threshold 0.1
```

`ruflo memory init --force` reverts step 1, so after any reinit, repeat the UPDATE + rebuild.

## Why this matters

`ruflo init --full` advertises AgentDB + semantic search as a headline feature, and the docs imply `memory search -q "..."` just works. Today, the headline feature returns 0 results on a clean install — most users will likely conclude semantic search is broken or unsupported, when in fact the indexed vectors are correct, just not findable through the high-level CLI.

Happy to send a PR for Option A + validator fix + the docs/threshold note if it'd be useful.

---

**Affected version:** `v3.7.0-alpha.27`
**Severity:** medium (workaround exists, but headline feature is broken on default install)
**Triage hint:** `area:memory area:embeddings`

npm error code E403
npm error 403 403 Forbidden - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/cookies/-/cookies-0.9.1.tgz
npm error 403 In most cases, you or one of your dependencies are requesting
npm error 403 a package version that is forbidden by your security policy,

```
@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@1.0.0-alpha.15
  └─ koa-router@14.0.0          (deprecated — "Please use @koa/router instead")
       └─ cookies@0.9.1          ← 403 Forbidden from npm registry
```

The `koa-router@14.0.0` package itself printed a deprecation warning during the partial download but its `cookies@0.9.1` dependency was blocked before install could complete.

## What does work

- `npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` → `ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.27` (exit 0) ✓
- `npx -y ruflo@alpha --version` → `ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.27` (exit 0) ✓
- `npm install agentic-flow@fix` → 524 packages, exit 0 ✓ (Check 8 passed)

So the 403 is specific to `cookies@0.9.1` and is not a general registry outage.

- **Check 2** (federation plugin exports `FederationNodeState`, `FederationBreakerService`, `InMemorySpendReporter`): UNVERIFIED
- **Check 3** (federation breaker Phase 2.a/2.b/3 sanity smoke): BLOCKED

1. `koa-router@14.0.0` is already deprecated upstream (it recommends `@koa/router`). Its dependency on `cookies@0.9.1` may be why that specific version is blocked in some environments.
2. `cookies@0.9.1` itself may have a known vulnerability flag causing security-policy rejections on hardened npm registries.

title: hooks_pretrain: extracts 0 patterns when first 50 files are non-code (Markdown/docs-heavy repos)
body:
## Summary

`hooks_pretrain` reports `patternsExtracted: 0` for any repo where the depth-first traversal hits more than 50 non-code files (`.md`, `.json`, `.db`, `.yaml`, etc.) before reaching any `.ts`/`.js`/`.py`/`.go`/`.rs`/`.java` file. The bug is a single counter at `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js:1416-1424`.

## Reproduction

Any monorepo with a docs-heavy or planning-heavy directory at the root (e.g. `docs/`, `specs/`, `_bmad-output/`).

```
$ npx claude-flow hooks pretrain --depth medium
filesAnalyzed: 1914
patternsExtracted: 0       # ← always zero
note: "Found 789 source-code file(s) but extracted zero import/require patterns.
       They may be empty, generated, or use non-standard module syntax."
```

The note is misleading — the source files were never opened. The 50-file budget was exhausted by `.md`/`.db`/`.yaml` files first.

## Root cause

In `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js:1416-1434`:

```js
filesAnalyzed++;                                  // ← counts EVERY file, not just code
if (['.ts','.js','.py','.go','.rs','.java'].includes(ext)) {
  try {
    const content = readFileSync(full, 'utf-8');
    const lines = content.split('\n');
    totalLines += lines.length;
    // Extract import patterns (first 50 files max for performance)
    if (filesAnalyzed <= 50) {                    // ← budget already eaten by non-code files
      for (const line of lines.slice(0, 30)) {
        if (line.startsWith('import ') || line.startsWith('from ') ||
            line.startsWith('const ') && line.includes('require(')) {
          ...
```

`filesAnalyzed` is incremented for **every** directory entry (including `.md`, `.db`, `.yaml`, `.log`, etc.) before the extension check. The depth-first walker fills the 50-file budget with non-code files long before recursing into the directory containing actual source.

## Repro evidence (this codebase)

Walked depth-4 from repo root using the exact same logic, captured first 50 files visited:

```
{
  ".md":     43,
  ".yaml":    6,
  ".db":      1,
  "(none)":   1
}
Code files in first 50: 0
```

The walker recursed into `_bmad-output/` (58 `.md` files) and `claude-code-orchestrator-kit/` (183 `.md` files) at depth 1, exhausting the 50-file budget on Markdown before reaching `apps/`, `workers/`, or `packages/`.

## Suggested fix

Use a separate counter for code files only:

```js
let codeFilesAnalyzed = 0;
...
filesAnalyzed++;
if (codeExts.includes(ext)) {
  try {
    const content = readFileSync(full, 'utf-8');
    const lines = content.split('\n');
    totalLines += lines.length;
    if (++codeFilesAnalyzed <= 50) {        // ← gate on code-file count
      for (const line of lines.slice(0, 30)) {
        ...
```

Optional secondary improvements:
- Sort `readdirSync` entries to recurse into directories containing code first (heuristic: `src/`, `apps/`, `packages/`, `lib/`, `workers/` before `docs/`, `specs/`, `_*`).
- Increase the line-scan window past 30 — modern TS files often have type-only headers / JSDoc / license preambles before the first `import`.
- Update the misleading note when the real cause is budget exhaustion rather than non-standard syntax.

## Environment

- Package: `@claude-flow/cli` (current as of 2026-05)
- File: `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js:1416-1424`
- Tool: `hooks_pretrain` MCP tool
- Repo shape that triggers: any with >50 non-code files visited before the first code file in depth-first order

fix(memory): schema vector_indexes dim 768→384 + CI guard (#1947, #1942, #1952)
body:
## Summary

**Root cause** (issues #1947, #1942, #1952): the bundled SQL schema initialises the `default` and `patterns` rows in `vector_indexes` with `dimensions = 768`, but the default ONNX embedding model (`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) produces **384-dim** vectors. HNSW rejects every insert with the mismatched dim, so on a fresh install `memory_store --vector` prints success while `memory_search` always returns 0 hits and `memory_stats` reads 0 vectors. The bug is silent — there's no error, the data just disappears.

The single inline schema literal in `getInitialMetadata()` (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/memory-initializer.ts`) is the canonical writer of the `vector_indexes` rows at init time — it's run against the user's DB by `db.run(getInitialMetadata(backend))` before HNSW comes up. Changing those two literals from `768` to `384` makes the schema match the default model, and `memory_search` starts returning real hits.

## Fix

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/memory-initializer.ts` — change the two inline SQL literals from 768 to 384, with a comment that tells the next developer why (and which bug breaks if they revert it).

## CI guard (per the user's "update ci guard to catch these cases")

- `scripts/audit-vector-dim.mjs` (new) — scans `v3/` and `ruflo/` for every `INSERT … INTO vector_indexes (id, name, dimensions) VALUES ('default'|'patterns', …, N)` row and fails the build if `N !== 384`.
- `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml` — new `vector-dim-audit` job; added to `witness-verify.needs` alongside the other audits.
- Verified to catch a deliberately-reverted regression (1 offender reported with file:line, exit 1) and to pass on the fixed tree (24 matching rows scanned, all 384, exit 0).

## Resolves

- #1947 root cause #1 (the schema vs default-model dim mismatch)
- #1942 (Bridge search index 768 vs imported 384-dim embeddings — same root cause, observed via the bridge)
- #1952 (Windows: store ok, search returns 0, stats shows 0 — same root cause, Windows is just where the reporter observed it)

## Follow-ups (explicitly out of scope here)

- #1947 root cause #2: `embeddings index -a build` defaults to `-c default` even when entries are in another namespace.
- #1947 additional: `embeddings init --force` model-ID validator rejects the default model's own name (`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) because of the `/`.
- #1941: claude-memories import path doesn't provision a `vector_indexes` row for that namespace.
- #1940: `memory_bridge_status` reports `totalEntries: 0` despite 237 persisted rows.
- Several published `@claude-flow/*` packages have no `files:` / `.npmignore` and ship stale `.swarm/` binary state (`memory.db`, `hnsw.index`, …). Separate hygiene cleanup.

## Test plan

- [x] `node scripts/audit-vector-dim.mjs` → `✓ all 24 rows set dimensions=384`, exit 0
- [x] Inject a 768 regression in one schema → audit reports `v3/…/schema.sql:304  'default' row has dim=768, expected 384`, exit 1
- [x] Restore → audit clean again
- [x] `node scripts/audit-tool-descriptions.mjs` / `audit-cli-mcp-tools.mjs` / `audit-plugin-packages.mjs` / `audit-hook-commands.mjs` — all still pass

title: fix(hooks): pre-bash TypeError + global-install MODULE_NOT_FOUND (#1944, #1943)
body:
## Summary

Two critical hook regressions on a fresh `ruflo init` (`v3.7.0-alpha.27`):

### #1944 — every Bash tool call from Claude Code spams a TypeError

`helpers/hook-handler.cjs` builds the `prompt` string from a `||` fallback chain whose third term is the normalised `toolInput` *object* (`{command:"ls"}`). The object is truthy so the chain stops there; the next line calls `.toLowerCase()` / `.substring()` on it and every `pre-bash` invocation prints:

```
[WARN] Hook pre-bash encountered an error: (hookInput.command || prompt).toLowerCase is not a function
```

**Fix:** fall back to `toolInput.command` (the string) instead of `toolInput` (the object). One-character change in three places — the deployed handler (both tracked copies) and the template in `helpers-generator.ts` that writes the user's `.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs` at init time.

Repro on the fixed file:
```bash
echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"ls"},"tool_name":"Bash"}' \
  | node v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs pre-bash
# → [OK] Command validated   (was: TypeError warning)
```
Dangerous-command guard still fires correctly:
```bash
echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf /"},"tool_name":"Bash"}' | … pre-bash
# → [BLOCKED] Dangerous command detected: rm -rf /
```

### #1943 — every Bash / Edit / Session hook fires `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after global init

`settings-generator.ts` writes hook command strings anchored at `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/helpers/…`. That works when init lands helpers project-locally, but breaks when settings end up in `~/.claude/settings.json` (global install) with helpers at `~/.claude/helpers/`: Claude Code still sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` to the *project* root, the path resolves there, finds nothing, and every hook fires `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

**Fix:** replace the path expression with a POSIX `sh` probe that tries the project-local path first and falls back to `$HOME` when it's missing — project-local overrides still take precedence; global installs work; no upgrade-skew. Windows gets the same probe via `cmd /c IF EXIST … ELSE …`. Applied to both `hookCmd()` and `generateStatusLineConfig()` (statusline scaffolding had the same anchor bug).

## CI guard (per the user's "update ci guard to catch these cases")

`scripts/audit-hook-handler-prompt.mjs` (new) — fails the build if any `.cjs` handler / TS template falls back to a bare `toolInput` (object) instead of `toolInput.command` (string). Wired into the existing `hook-command-audit` job. Verified to:
- pass on HEAD (`✓ no '|| <…>toolInput' (object) fallbacks found`)
- catch a deliberately-reverted regression (`✗ 2 offending fallback(s) — #1944 regression: <file>:<line> match: || toolInput …`, exit 1)

## Resolves

- #1944 (pre-bash TypeError on every Bash call)
- #1943 (MODULE_NOT_FOUND from global init's hook commands)

## Test plan

- [x] `node scripts/audit-hook-handler-prompt.mjs` → clean (3 targets scanned, 0 offenders)
- [x] All other audits still green (`audit-tool-descriptions`, `audit-cli-mcp-tools`, `audit-plugin-packages`, `audit-hook-commands`)
- [x] Manual repro of #1944 against the fixed handler → no TypeError, `[OK] Command validated`
- [x] Dangerous-command detection still works
- [ ] CI (full pipeline including the new `Run hook-handler prompt-resolution audit` step)

title: fix(memory): bridge + doctor honor CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH / config (#1945, #1946)
body:
## Summary

Two CLI memory bugs caused by hard-coded `.swarm/memory.db` paths that ignored the configured memory location.

### #1945 — CLI \`memory store\` doesn't persist (the user-visible "store reports success but next process can't find it" bug)

`memory-bridge.ts::getDbPath()` always defaulted to `<cwd>/.swarm/memory.db` regardless of \`CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH\` or \`claude-flow.config.json#memory.persistPath\`. So a user with a non-default memory layout (e.g. \`data/memory/memory.db\`) had \`memory init\` write the schema to the configured file, while \`bridgeStoreEntry()\` silently wrote INSERTs to \`.swarm/memory.db\` — a different file, sometimes a different directory. CLI \`memory store\` reported success against the wrong DB, and a fresh process reading the configured path saw zero rows.

**Fix:** route \`getDbPath()\` through \`getMemoryRoot()\` (from memory-initializer), the same function \`memory init\` already uses. The two now agree on the same file. \`:memory:\` and explicit \`customPath\` still work unchanged; path-traversal protection unchanged. Imported via \`createRequire\` so the cross-module dep doesn't create an ESM cycle.

### #1946 — \`ruflo doctor\` reports DB "Not initialized" on a perfectly-init'd DB

\`doctor.ts::checkMemoryDatabase()\` only checked the legacy candidates \`.claude-flow/memory.db\` / \`.swarm/memory.db\` / \`data/memory.db\` and ignored \`CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH\` / config entirely. The reporter's DB at \`data/memory/memory.db\` (with the \`memory/\` subdir, off by one) made doctor lie about a perfectly-functional install.

**Fix:** check \`getMemoryRoot() + '/memory.db'\` first (the authoritative path the rest of the CLI uses); fall back to the legacy candidates for non-standard layouts; add \`data/memory/memory.db\` to the fallback list.

## Resolves

- #1945 — CLI memory store doesn't persist (same-process bridge writes a different file than the configured one)
- #1946 — doctor reports DB "Not initialized" when it exists

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm run build\` (\`@claude-flow/cli\`) → clean tsc
- [ ] CI: existing audits + Build V3 across ubuntu/macOS/windows
- [ ] Manual repro on fresh install with \`CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH=data/memory ruflo init\` + \`memory store\` + new-process \`memory list\` (post-merge)

title: fix(hooks-pretrain): code-file budget + code-dir-first traversal (#1953)
body:
## Summary

\`hooks_pretrain\` reported \`patternsExtracted: 0\` on any monorepo whose depth-first traversal hit 50 non-code files (\`.md\` / \`.yaml\` / \`.db\` / \`.log\` / …) before reaching a single \`.ts\`/\`.js\`/\`.py\`/etc. The 50-file budget that gates the import-pattern scan was checked against \`filesAnalyzed\`, which counts **every** directory entry — so in markdown-heavy repos (\`docs/\`, \`specs/\`, \`_bmad-output/\`, …) the budget burned out on Markdown long before the walker recursed into \`apps/\`, \`packages/\`, or \`src/\`.

The reporter's evidence in their repo: first 50 files visited were 43× \`.md\`, 6× \`.yaml\`, 1× \`.db\`, 1× untyped — zero code files in the entire budget window.

## Fix (two parts)

1. **Separate \`codeFilesScanned\` counter** for the 50-file budget. The cap now means \"50 code files\", which is what the comment always claimed.
2. **Sort \`readdirSync\` entries** so the walker recurses into code-likely dirs first (\`src/\`, \`apps/\`, \`packages/\`, \`lib/\`, \`crates/\`, \`workers/\`, \`server/\`, \`backend/\`, \`frontend/\`, \`app/\`, \`cli/\`, \`core/\`) and deprioritises docs/specs/build/coverage/test dirs.

## Collateral improvements (in the same hot path)

- Widened per-file scan window from **30 → 80 lines**. Modern TS files often have license headers + JSDoc + type-only imports before the first \`import\` — the 30-line cap was missing real imports.
- Recognise more code extensions: \`.tsx\`, \`.jsx\`, \`.mjs\`, \`.cjs\` (plus the existing \`.ts\`/\`.js\`/\`.py\`/\`.go\`/\`.rs\`/\`.java\`). The \`SUPPORTED_EXTRACTION_EXTS\` list used by the \"found N code files but 0 patterns\" note got the same expansion so the diagnostic stays accurate.

## Resolves

- #1953 — \`hooks_pretrain\` extracts 0 patterns when first 50 files are non-code

title: fix(memory-import): resolve Win32 cwd to Claude Code's slug (#1939)
body:
## Summary

\`memory_import_claude({ allProjects: false })\` couldn't find the current project's memory directory on a pure Win32+Win32 install — slug candidates in \`resolveProjectMemoryDir()\` only replaced forward slashes, never the drive-colon / backslash / whitespace a Win32 cwd contains.

Verified: for the reporter's cwd, the candidate set now contains \`C--Users-tobia-OneDrive-Desktop-Claude-Stuff\` exactly.

title: fix(memory): provision vector_indexes per namespace + truthful bridge_status (#1941, #1940)
body:
## Summary

Two related memory-bridge bugs both surfaced by the same reporter on Win32 alpha.21:

### #1941 — \`memory_search({namespace:\"claude-memories\"})\` always returned 0

\`memory_import_claude\` inserts hundreds of rows under \`claude-memories\`, but the schema's \`vector_indexes\` table only held \`default\` and \`patterns\` rows. AgentDB's HNSW/router keys namespace lookups by this table — without a row, the namespace was effectively unindexed for search.

**Fix:** every store path (both \`bridgeStoreEntry\` and the raw-sql.js fallback \`storeEntry\`) now does \`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vector_indexes (id, name, dimensions) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\` for the entry's namespace before the row insert. Idempotent; legacy DBs without the table fall through cleanly. Dimensions defaults to the embedding's actual dim (384 for the default MiniLM-L6 model), preserving #1947's contract.

### #1940 — \`memory_bridge_status\` reported \`totalEntries: 0\` on a DB with 237 rows

Root cause was a page-size bug: it used \`listEntries({}).entries.length\`, but \`listEntries\` returns at most 20 entries with the full count in a separate \`.total\` field. So the reporter capped at 20 (or 0 if the first page was empty), regardless of the actual row count.

**Fix:** use \`listEntries({}).total\` for the count. Plus surface a per-namespace breakdown (\`agentdb.namespaces\`) for the common namespaces (\`default\`, \`patterns\`, \`claude-memories\`, \`auto-memory\`, \`tasks\`, \`feedback\`, \`pretrain\`) so callers can see where the rows actually live. \`bridge.status\` now flips to \`connected\` on ANY persisted row, not only \`claude-memories\`.

## Resolves
- #1941
- #1940

title: fix(embeddings-index): make `-c` optional for build/rebuild (#1947 RC2)
body:
## Summary

The HNSW index is a single global structure that indexes every namespace's embeddings — \`-c\` was always informational. But \`embeddings index -a build\` REQUIRED \`-c\`, and the documented examples (\`-c documents\` / \`-c patterns\` / \`-c default\`) led users to think \`-c\` actually scoped the index. The user-visible failure mode (per #1947 RC #2):

1. \`memory store -k ... --namespace project --vector\` → entries land in namespace \`project\`.
2. \`embeddings index -a build\` → \"Collection is required\".
3. \`embeddings index -a build -c default\` → \`Vector Count: 0\` (default namespace has zero entries).
4. User has to discover and run \`embeddings index -a build -c project\` to see anything.

## Fix

Drop the required check. When \`-c\` is omitted, label the result \`(all namespaces)\`, run the same global rebuild, and print a helpful follow-up if the count is 0. Update help text + examples so the contract is clear (\"Omit to build for all namespaces\"). No runtime behavior change for callers passing \`-c\` — still indexes globally, just labels with whatever they passed.

## Resolves

- #1947 RC #2 — embeddings index defaults to `-c default` even when entries are elsewhere

title: verify(federation): unblock Checks 2/3 with cookies@0.9.0 pin (#1949)
body:
## Summary

#1949's federation Checks 2 + 3 have been blocked because the verification job tries \`npm install @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@alpha\` and a transitive dep brings in \`cookies@0.9.1\`, which a registry security policy rejects.

Two facts make the obvious fix non-obvious:

1. **\`cookies@0.9.1\` is the LATEST published version** of \`cookies\` — there is no newer version to override to. (\`npm view cookies dist-tags\` confirms: \`latest: 0.9.1\`, no \`0.9.2\` exists.)
2. **\`package.json#overrides\` is only honored at the root** of the install — adding it inside the federation plugin's own manifest doesn't help downstream consumers.

But **\`cookies@0.9.0\`** (one patch back, same surface, \`koa@3.2.0\` accepts either interchangeably) is NOT blocked. So the verification harness can pin that at its own root \`package.json\` and the install unblocks.

## Fix

Add \`scripts/verify-federation-plugin.sh\` — a tiny wrapper that creates a temp dir, writes \`package.json\` with \`overrides.cookies=0.9.0\`, runs \`npm install @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@<tag>\`, then runs Check 2 (required exports) and Check 3 (breaker/reporter wire-up smoke).

## Verified end-to-end against the live \`alpha\` tag

\`\`\`
$ bash scripts/verify-federation-plugin.sh
[verify-federation] installing @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@alpha
added 527 packages in 21s
[verify-federation] resolved cookies version: 0.9.0
[verify-federation] Check 2 OK — FederationNodeState, FederationBreakerService, InMemorySpendReporter
[verify-federation] Check 3 OK — FederationBreakerService + InMemorySpendReporter instantiate cleanly
[verify-federation] all checks PASSED for tag=alpha
exit=0
\`\`\`

Resolved dep chain (the issue mis-identified \`koa-router\`; it's actually plain \`koa\`):

\`\`\`
@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation
  └─ agentic-flow
       └─ fastmcp
            └─ mcp-proxy
                 └─ pipenet@1.4.0
                      └─ koa@3.2.0
                           └─ cookies@0.9.1   ← blocked → override to 0.9.0
\`\`\`

## Resolves

- #1949 (workaround — until \`pipenet\`/\`koa\`/\`cookies\` upstream chain ships a non-blocked release)

## Test plan

- [x] Live install + exports check against published \`alpha\` (3.7.0-alpha.32 era) → all pass
- [x] Script returns distinct exit codes (1 = install failed, 2 = export/smoke failed, 0 = pass)

title: daemon start --workers map still enables default workers
body:
# `daemon start --workers map` still enables default workers

Observed against: `ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.33` / `@claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.33`.

## Summary

`ruflo daemon start --workers map` accepts the flag, but the daemon still enables the full default worker set:

```json
["map", "audit", "optimize", "consolidate", "testgaps"]
```

Expected behavior: only `map` should be enabled.

## Reproduction

In a disposable project with `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.33`:

```bash
ruflo daemon start --workers map --max-cpu-load 1000 --min-free-memory 0
ruflo daemon status
```

Observed running status:

```text
Workers Enabled: 5

map         enabled
audit       enabled
optimize    enabled
consolidate enabled
testgaps    enabled
```

The daemon state also reports:

```json
{
  "enabledWorkers": ["map", "audit", "optimize", "consolidate", "testgaps"]
}
```

One extra clue: the foreground daemon process launched by the command did not retain the requested worker selection in argv. It looked like:

```text
.../cli.js daemon start --foreground --quiet --workspace <disposable-project>
```

There was no `--workers map` in that foreground process command line.

## Why It Matters

For project-scoped daemon use, `--workers` is a safety boundary. A user may intentionally select a local-only mapper and avoid broader audit/optimize/testgaps workers until the project is ready.

This also matters for environments that wrap headless execution, enforce routing policies, or want deterministic dry-run/map-only behavior before enabling AI-backed workers.

## Candidate Fix Shape

A local proof patch against an earlier alpha did two things:

1. parse and forward a validated worker list from the daemon command layer into daemon config and background argv;
2. filter configured workers by `enabledWorkerTypes` after worker state initialization, so restored daemon state cannot silently widen the selected worker set.

The local proof is not necessarily the final upstream style, but the intended behavior is straightforward:

```bash
ruflo daemon start --workers map
```

should produce:

```json
["map"]
```

not:

```json
["map", "audit", "optimize", "consolidate", "testgaps"]
```

title: fix(daemon): forward --workers / --headless / --sandbox to forked child (#1968)
body:
## Summary

\`daemon start --workers map\` (and \`--headless\` / \`--sandbox\`) were accepted by the launcher but silently dropped when it forked the foreground child — so the daemon came up with the full default worker set (\`map,audit,optimize,consolidate,testgaps\`) regardless of what the user asked for.

The reporter's repro on alpha.33:
\`\`\`bash
$ ruflo daemon start --workers map --max-cpu-load 1000 --min-free-memory 0
$ ruflo daemon status
Workers Enabled: 5   ← should be 1
map          enabled
audit        enabled
optimize     enabled
consolidate  enabled
testgaps     enabled
\`\`\`

The argv trace in the report (\`.../cli.js daemon start --foreground --quiet --workspace <root>\`) made it obvious: the launcher never appended \`--workers map\`.

## Fix

\`startBackgroundDaemon()\` accepted only resource thresholds (\`--max-cpu-load\` / \`--min-free-memory\`) and \`--workspace\`. Threaded \`--workers\`, \`--headless\`, \`--sandbox\` through the same path, gated by strict input validation (same posture as the existing threshold validators):

| Flag | Validation |
|---|---|
| \`--workers <list>\` | \`/^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*(,[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)*$/\` |
| \`--headless\` | boolean |
| \`--sandbox <mode>\` | \`strict\` \\| \`permissive\` \\| \`disabled\` |

Anything that fails validation is silently dropped (matches existing thresholds behaviour). All three end up in the forked child's argv, which is what both the daemon's own arg parser AND \`killStaleDaemons\` rely on.

After this fix, the same repro returns:

\`\`\`bash
$ ruflo daemon status
Workers Enabled: 1
map          enabled
\`\`\`

## Resolves

- #1968 — daemon start --workers map still enables default workers

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm run build\` on @claude-flow/cli → clean tsc
- [ ] CI: existing audits + Build V3 across ubuntu/macOS/windows

title: fix(cost-tracker/compact): resolve from anywhere + free HEALTH_PORT (#1930)
body:
## Summary

\`plugins/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/compact.mjs\` was failing on the marketplace install layout with two distinct bugs:

1. **Resolution** — script only worked when the caller ran from a cwd where \`@claude-flow/integration\` resolved. On a pnpm-workspace marketplace install (the shipped layout: \`~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/\`) that means \`cwd=v3/@claude-flow/integration/\` specifically — pnpm doesn't hoist into \`v3/node_modules/\`. The skill's documented \`cd v3 && node ...\` path failed with \`Cannot find module @claude-flow/integration/token-optimizer\`.
2. **Port** — the script imported agentic-flow indirectly. agentic-flow binds \`process.env.HEALTH_PORT || 8080\` at module-load time and EADDRINUSE'd on any host with something else already on 8080 (k8s NodePort, forwarded dev server, …).

## Fix

**Resolution chain** — try in order:
- \`createRequire(cwd)\` — npm-style hoisted installs
- \`createRequire(script-dir)\` — run from inside the plugin
- absolute path walk from \`import.meta.url\` (up to 6 parents) looking for \`v3/@claude-flow/integration/dist/token-optimizer.js\` — marketplace layout, cwd-independent

**HEALTH_PORT** — set to \`0\` by default before the dynamic import runs (OS picks a free port). Users can still override with an explicit value.

**dist/-missing** — when the resolver finds a path that doesn't exist on disk (the \"\`dist/\` not built\" case from the issue's step 1), surface a clear error pointing at the build command (\`cd v3/@claude-flow/integration && pnpm run build\`) instead of the generic MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

## Out of scope (per the issue)

| # | Step | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | \`agentic-flow\` not in workspace deps | Install-environment issue; \`@claude-flow/integration\` lists it as a peer so consumers opt in. The graceful-fallback path already reports \`agenticFlowAvailable: false\`. |
| 3 | \`sharp\` prebuild missing on linux-x64 | Native binding, upstream sharp/agentic-flow concern. |
| 1 | \`@claude-flow/integration/dist/\` missing | Packaging fix — marketplace bundle should include built dist. Tracked separately. |

## Resolves

- #1930 (script-level — the deeper packaging fix is a separate concern)

## Test plan

- [x] Manual: \`node plugins/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/compact.mjs \"test\"\` works from repo root (cwd resolves to v3 via createRequire)
- [x] Manual: same script works from \`cd /tmp && node /path/to/compact.mjs \"test\"\` (absolute-path fallback)
- [x] Manual: HEALTH_PORT collision repro (\`HEALTH_PORT=8080\` already bound) no longer EADDRINUSEs
- [ ] CI: existing audits

title: neural-trader@2.7.1: fork bomb on install + missing platform binaries (120GB RAM leak on macOS)
body:
## Summary

The `ruflo-neural-trader` plugin in this repo (`plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/README.md`) lists `npm install neural-trader` as a prerequisite. **Following that single instruction on Apple Silicon macOS produces a fork bomb that consumed ~120 GB of RAM from 3,049 stuck processes within ~80 minutes on my MacBook before manual intervention.**

The underlying `neural-trader@2.7.1` npm package has two compounding defects:

1. The `optionalDependencies` and the napi-rs platform loader reference platform-specific subpackages that **have never been published to npm** (verified via `npm view`, all return 404).
2. The install fallback script `scripts/install-with-prebuilds.js` recursively invokes `npm install` from inside the `install` lifecycle hook → unbounded process recursion.

The package only "works" on `linux-x64` because the binary is hardcoded inline in the tarball at `neural-trader-rust/neural-trader.linux-x64-gnu.node`, bypassing the napi-rs platform-package mechanism entirely.

## Reproduction

On any non-`linux-x64` machine (verified on macOS Apple Silicon):

```bash
# This is literally the prerequisite from plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/README.md
npm install neural-trader

# Process count grows by ~40/min
# Each holds 30–300 MB RAM
# At ~80 min mark: 3,000+ stuck processes, ~120 GB RAM consumed
```

---

## Bug 1 — Fork bomb in `scripts/install-with-prebuilds.js`  *(Critical — system-crashing)*

When no prebuilt binary is found for the current platform and `python3` + `node-gyp` are detected, the script does:

```js
// neural-trader@2.7.1, scripts/install-with-prebuilds.js, ~line 83
if (hasBuildTools) {
  ...
  try {
    execSync('npm install', { stdio: 'inherit' });  // <-- fork bomb
```

`package.json` declares:

```json
"scripts": { "install": "node scripts/install-with-prebuilds.js" }
```

Running `npm install` in the package directory re-triggers the `install` lifecycle script, which calls `npm install` again → unbounded recursion. This is what produced the 3,049 stuck processes.

**Suggested patch:**

```diff
- execSync('npm install', { stdio: 'inherit' });
+ // Don't recursively npm install — that re-runs THIS script via the
+ // `install` lifecycle hook, causing infinite process recursion.
+ // Building the Rust binding requires `napi build`, not `npm install`,
+ // and the Rust source is not shipped in the npm tarball anyway.
+ console.error('No prebuilt binary available for ' + platformKey);
+ console.error('Supported platforms: linux-x64. Other platforms pending.');
+ process.exit(1);
```

Also: the `hasBuildTools` check tests for `python3` + `node-gyp`, but neural-trader's native code is Rust/napi-rs — neither tool is relevant. The check is incorrect regardless of the recursion bug.

This single-line fix would have prevented the entire memory event even with the platform-binary issues below unresolved.

---

## Bug 2 — Missing platform binary subpackages on npm  *(Critical)*

`package.json` (v2.7.1) declares:

```json
"optionalDependencies": {
  "neural-trader-darwin-arm64": "2.2.0",
  "neural-trader-darwin-x64": "2.2.0",
  "neural-trader-linux-arm64": "2.2.0",
  "neural-trader-linux-x64": "2.2.0",
  "neural-trader-win32-x64": "2.2.0"
}
```

**None of these packages exist on npm.** Verified:

```
$ npm view neural-trader-darwin-arm64
npm error code E404 ... not found
```

Same 404 for all five `neural-trader-{platform}-{arch}` packages.

Additionally, `neural-trader-rust/index.js` (the napi-rs–generated loader bundled in the tarball) references *different* names:

```js
case 'darwin':
  localFileExisted = existsSync(join(__dirname, 'neural-trader.darwin-universal.node'))
  ...
  nativeBinding = require('@neural-trader/core-darwin-universal')
```

`@neural-trader/core-darwin-universal` is also not published. The parent `@neural-trader/core@2.0.0` declares optional deps on `@neural-trader/darwin-arm64@0.1.0`, `@neural-trader/darwin-x64`, `@neural-trader/win32-x64-msvc`, `@neural-trader/linux-x64-gnu`, `@neural-trader/linux-x64-musl` — **none of those are published either**. Verified each individually.

**Fix:** Publish the platform subpackages. Your other packages (`@ruvector/sona`, `@ruvector/attention`, `@ruvector/gnn`) follow the correct napi-rs pattern with separate `@scope/name-{platform}-{arch}` packages on npm — that pattern works correctly for darwin-arm64. Apply the same to neural-trader and **align the optionalDependencies names with what the napi-rs loader actually requires** (currently the two lists disagree on naming convention).

---

## Bug 3 — Rust source not shipped in npm tarball  *(Blocks user fallback)*

The `neural-trader-rust/` directory in the published tarball contains only:

```
index.js              (auto-generated napi-rs loader)
index.d.ts            (type definitions)
neural-trader.linux-x64-gnu.node   (the binary, linux-x64 only)
README.md
.env.example
```

No `Cargo.toml`, no `.rs` files, no `crates/napi-bindings/`. Users with a Rust toolchain installed *cannot* build from source even if they wanted to. The `package.json` `files` field or `.npmignore` likely needs updating if a local-build fallback is intended.

(Plugin source for `ruflo-neural-trader` is in this repo, but the underlying npm package's Rust source appears to live elsewhere — `github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader` returns 404. See Bug 4.)

---

## Bug 4 — `neural-trader` repo not accessible  *(Blocks issue reporting at source)*

`https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader` returns HTTP 404. The README link in `neural-trader`'s `package.json` (`https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader#readme`) is dead. That's why this issue is filed against `ruflo` — it's the closest reachable repo that references and depends on neural-trader.

If the underlying `neural-trader` repo is intentionally private, the `repository` and `homepage` fields in `neural-trader`'s `package.json` should be removed or pointed at this repo's plugin directory.

---

## Requested fixes (priority order)

1. **Critical / one-line fix:** Patch `neural-trader@2.7.1`'s `scripts/install-with-prebuilds.js` to remove the recursive `npm install` call. This prevents the system-crashing fork bomb regardless of the platform-binary state, and is the highest-impact fix. Without it, every new user who follows the `ruflo-neural-trader` plugin README on a non-linux-x64 machine will reproduce this.
2. **Critical:** Publish the platform binary subpackages at the versions referenced by `@neural-trader/core` and `neural-trader-rust/index.js`. Until this is done, neural-trader (and therefore the `ruflo-neural-trader` plugin) is unusable on macOS / Windows / Linux-arm64.
3. **Important:** Restore public access to `github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader` or update the repository links in `neural-trader`'s `package.json` to a working location (e.g., this repo's plugin path).
4. **Nice-to-have:** Ship Rust source in the neural-trader npm tarball for source-build fallback, *or* update the install script's error message to clearly say "no prebuilt for X, supported on Y" instead of attempting a doomed build.
5. **Nice-to-have:** Add a platform-support note to `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/README.md` Prerequisites section warning that `npm install neural-trader` currently only succeeds on linux-x64 — until fixes 1–2 ship.

## Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64)
- Node.js (current LTS)
- npm (current)
- `neural-trader@2.7.1`

title: fix(neural-trader): mitigate upstream fork-bomb on install + CI guard (#1974)
body:
## Summary

The upstream \`neural-trader@2.7.1\` (and every earlier published version we audited) ships a malicious-by-accident \`install\` lifecycle script that recursively invokes \`npm install\` from inside the install hook. On non-\`linux-x64\` hosts the recursion is unbounded — the reporter saw **3,049 stuck processes consuming ~120 GB of RAM in ~80 minutes** on macOS Apple Silicon.

The \`plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/README.md\` Prerequisites section said plainly \`npm install neural-trader\`. We can't patch upstream from here, but we CAN stop telling users to run the dangerous command.

## Mitigations in this repo

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`README.md\` Prerequisites | Prominent warning advisory + switch recommended install to \`npm install --ignore-scripts neural-trader\` |
| \`agents/trading-strategist.md\` | Same \`--ignore-scripts\` fix on the "Ensure installed" line |
| 6 skill files (\`trader-backtest/portfolio/regime/risk/signal/train\`) | Same one-liner fix |
| \`trader-cloud-backtest/SKILL.md\` | Patch \`npm install -g neural-trader\` in the Managed-Agent \`initScript\` too (cloud containers ARE isolated, but in-container fork-bomb amplification still bites) |

The upstream linux-x64 binary is hardcoded inline in the tarball, so the package still works on linux-x64 after \`--ignore-scripts\`. On macOS / Windows / linux-arm64 the runtime won't work until upstream publishes the platform-binary subpackages it advertises in \`optionalDependencies\` — but at least \`--ignore-scripts\` doesn't fork-bomb the host.

## CI guard

\`scripts/audit-neural-trader-safety.mjs\` (new) scans \`plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/\` for any \`npm install neural-trader\` / \`npm i neural-trader\` invocation that doesn't also carry \`--ignore-scripts\`. Allowlist: lines preceded by a "DO NOT run" marker (the README's anti-example block). Wired into the existing \`hook-command-audit\` job (which is in \`witness-verify.needs\`, so any regression-by-removal blocks the release pipeline).

## Resolves

- #1974 (in this repo). Upstream fix still required for the underlying bug.

## Test plan

- [x] \`node scripts/audit-neural-trader-safety.mjs\` → clean (exit 0)
- [x] Inject regression (drop \`--ignore-scripts\` from one invocation) → exit 1 with per-file diagnostic
- [x] All other audits (\`vector-dim\`, \`hook-handler-prompt\`, \`fix-invariants\`, \`hook-commands\`) still green
- [x] \`bash plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/scripts/smoke.sh\` → 11 passed, 0 failed
- [ ] CI: existing audits + new \`Run neural-trader install-safety audit (#1974)\` step
