title: announce: neural-trader@2.7.6 — full fix shipped (4 bugs, 3 PRs, 3/5 platforms covered)
body:
## Intro

A week ago, an attempt to install `neural-trader` on Apple Silicon led to a 120 GB RAM fork-bomb. The fix for that ([#1974](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/1974)) was shipped quickly, but it only addressed the most dramatic symptom. A deeper audit found three more bugs that had been silently making the package unusable as a library on every platform since v2.5.0 (November 2025) — including missing source files that were caught by a stray Python-template `.gitignore` rule, an x86-only hashing library that blocked builds on Apple Silicon, and a release pipeline that claimed to ship binaries for five platforms but actually shipped one.

All of those are fixed in **`neural-trader@2.7.6`**, on npm now. This issue is the announcement, with what changed, who's affected, and what to do.

## What's fixed in 2.7.6

| Bug | Symptom | Versions affected | Fix |
|-----|---------|-------------------|-----|
| Install-hook fork-bomb | 3,049 stuck processes + 120 GB RAM on macOS in 80 min | 2.6.x – 2.7.1 | [`neural-trader#109`](https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader/pull/109) → shipped in 2.7.2 |
| Missing `napi-loader-shared.js` / `napi-loader.js` / `validation-utils.js` (caught by unscoped `lib/` in `.gitignore`) | `require('neural-trader')` always threw `Cannot find module './src/cli/lib/napi-loader-shared'` | 2.5.0 – 2.7.4 | [`neural-trader#111`](https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader/pull/111) → shipped in 2.7.5 |
| `fasthash` C build hard-codes x86 SIMD flags | `cargo build` aborted on aarch64-apple-darwin | all 2.x | [`neural-trader#111`](https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader/pull/111) → replaced single call site with stdlib SipHash |
| Cross-platform binary publish pipeline never worked (8 separate workflow bugs) | npm tarball claimed 5 platform binaries, shipped 1 | all 2.x | [`neural-trader#111`](https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader/pull/111) → workflow fixes; 3 of 5 binaries shipped in 2.7.6 |

## Platform coverage in 2.7.6

| Platform | Status |
|----------|--------|
| `linux-x64-gnu` | ✅ |
| `darwin-arm64` (Apple Silicon — M1/M2/M3/M4) | ✅ **first time ever shipped** |
| `darwin-x64` (Intel Macs) | ✅ **first time ever shipped** |
| `linux-arm64-gnu` (Raspberry Pi, AWS Graviton, etc.) | ⏳ pending — CI build path now wired, will fill in on the next tag-triggered release |
| `win32-x64-msvc` (Windows x64) | ⏳ pending — same |

## What to do

If you're using `neural-trader` directly:

```bash
npm install --ignore-scripts neural-trader@2.7.6
```

(The `--ignore-scripts` flag is kept as belt-and-braces defense in depth — the install hook is safe in 2.7.2+, but skipping it costs nothing.)

Verify:

```bash
node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('neural-trader')).length)"
# Expected: 194
```

If you're using the `ruflo-neural-trader` plugin in this repo, it'll be bumped to require `neural-trader@^2.7.6` in a follow-up PR — the CI guard `scripts/audit-neural-trader-safety.mjs` still enforces `--ignore-scripts` on every documented invocation as defense in depth.

## Want the full story?

The full technical post-mortem with root-cause analysis for each bug is at:

📄 **https://gist.github.com/ruvnet/a1aca90a5c299d89fa92e905dab11041**

It covers:
- How the install hook ended up calling itself recursively
- Why a Python `.gitignore` template made three load-bearing JS files invisible to git
- Why one placeholder hash call brought down the entire ARM-darwin build
- All 8 separate CI workflow bugs and how each was fixed
- Build-from-source verification on Apple Silicon

## References

- Original bug report: [#1974](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/1974)
- Upstream PRs: [`#109`](https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader/pull/109), [`#111`](https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader/pull/111), [`#112`](https://github.com/ruvnet/neural-trader/pull/112)
- Post-mortem gist: https://gist.github.com/ruvnet/a1aca90a5c299d89fa92e905dab11041
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/neural-trader (`latest` = `2.7.6`)

Closing this issue when the `ruflo-neural-trader` plugin's prerequisite pin is bumped to `^2.7.6`.

title: Stop hook fails with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE on session-end
body:
## Summary

The session-end stop hook fails on Windows because `npx claude-flow@alpha` cannot reach the npm registry due to a TLS certificate verification error. The error is reported as non-blocking, but it still surfaces to the user every time a session ends.

## Repro

Configured stop hooks (from `.claude/settings.json` / project hooks):

1. `cmd /c node %CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR%/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs sync`
2. `npx claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end --generate-summary true --persist-state true --export-metrics true`

On session end, Claude Code reports:

```
Ran 2 stop hooks
Stop hook error: Failed with non-blocking status code: npm error code UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE
npm error errno UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE
npm error request to https://registry.npmjs.org/claude-flow failed, reason: unable to verify the first certificate
npm error A complete log of this run can be found in:
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\npm-cache\_logs\2026-05-14T16_07_26_919Z-debug-0.log
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise (10.0.26200)
- Shell: PowerShell / cmd
- Claude Code on Windows
- npm hits a TLS intercepting proxy / corporate CA, so `registry.npmjs.org` fails leaf-cert verification when invoked via `npx`

## Root cause

`npx claude-flow@alpha` always tries to resolve the package from the registry on first run, which fails in any environment with a TLS-intercepting proxy or missing root CA. Every session-end then prints the failure.

The error comes from this ruflo plugin:
```
  Source B — installed plugin C:\Users\mario.MFJ-WIN10-2020\.claude\plugins\cache\ruflo\ruflo-core\0.2.0\hooks\hooks.json:63-71
  "Stop": [{ "hooks": [{
     "command": "npx claude-flow@alpha hooks session-end --generate-summary true --persist-state true --export-metrics true"
  }]}]
```

That hook is owned by the ruflo-core plugin v0.2.0 that's been installed into your Claude Code plugin cache — not by
anything in this repo. (Mirror copies live under ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/... which is the marketplace's source
tree.)


## Suggested fixes (one or more)

1. Prefer a locally-installed `claude-flow` binary in the hook (resolve via `node_modules/.bin` or a pinned path) instead of `npx claude-flow@alpha`, so session-end works offline / behind corporate proxies.
2. Cache the resolved package so repeat `npx` invocations don't hit the registry on every session end.
3. If the hook must fetch, swallow registry/TLS errors silently (or downgrade to a single-line warning) since the hook is already declared non-blocking — currently it dumps a full npm error block on every exit.
4. Document a workaround for users behind TLS-intercepting proxies (e.g. `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `npm config set cafile`, or disabling the hook).

## Workaround

Disable the `session-end` hook or point it at a locally-installed `claude-flow` binary to avoid the `npx` registry fetch.

title: memory stats reports HNSW '0 entries' — reads ./.claude/memory.db while store/search use ./.swarm/memory.db
body:
## Summary

`memory stats` reads from a different SQLite database than `memory store` / `memory search` write to, causing it to report `HNSW Index: active (0 entries)` even when data has just been stored, indexed, and successfully retrieved via semantic search.

The data is fine; the stats command is reading from the wrong file.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| **Package** | `claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.35` |
| **CLI command** | `npx claude-flow@v3alpha` |
| **Node** | v24.14.0 |
| **OS** | Darwin 25.5.0 (macOS, Apple Silicon M1 Max) |
| **CWD** | non-git project directory |
| **Env** | `CLAUDE_FLOW_V3_ENABLED=true`, `CLAUDE_FLOW_HOOKS_ENABLED=true` |

## Reproduction

```bash
NS="bug-repro-$(date +%s)"

# 1. Store entry (succeeds, vector embedded)
npx claude-flow@v3alpha memory store -n "$NS" -k "test-entry" \
  --value "OAuth2 with PKCE authentication flow" --upsert
# → [OK] Data stored successfully · Vector: Yes (384-dim)

# 2. Semantic search works (proves vector is indexed somewhere)
npx claude-flow@v3alpha memory search -q "OAuth" -n "$NS" --threshold 0.1
# → Found 1 results · test-entry · score 0.41

# 3. list confirms entry exists
npx claude-flow@v3alpha memory list -n "$NS"
# → Showing 1 of 1 entries · Vector: ✓

# 4. BUG: memory stats reports 0
npx claude-flow@v3alpha memory stats
# → HNSW Index: active (0 entries)   ❌
```

## Expected

`memory stats` reports the actual count of indexed entries — at least 1 after step 1, matching what `list` and `search` report.

## Actual

`memory stats` always reports `HNSW Index: active (0 entries)`, regardless of how many entries exist.

## Root cause

Two databases coexist in the project directory and are queried by different commands:

```
./.claude/memory.db   ← memory stats reads from here (EMPTY)
./.swarm/memory.db    ← memory store/search write here (has the data)
```

Confirmed by inspecting both DBs after the repro above:

```sql
-- ./.claude/memory.db
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries;
-- → 0 rows

-- ./.swarm/memory.db
SELECT COUNT(*), namespace FROM memory_entries GROUP BY namespace;
-- → 1 | bug-repro-1778783822
-- → 3 | demo-collab
-- → 1 | repro-1778783177
```

`vector_indexes` table is also inconsistent:

```
./.claude/memory.db  → 2 indexes (default 768d, patterns 768d) — the seed only
./.swarm/memory.db   → 5 indexes including the user namespaces at 384d
```

The 768d → 384d dimension change between the two files suggests the seed migration ran against `./.claude/memory.db` once, but live writes target `./.swarm/memory.db` (which uses the current `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` model at 384d).

## Likely culprit

The `memory stats` code path resolves the DB location differently from `memory store` / `memory search` / `memory list`. Either:

1. **Different resolver functions** in `@claude-flow/memory` — `stats` uses a hardcoded `./.claude/memory.db`, while live commands resolve via the configured backend path (`./.swarm/memory.db`).
2. **Stale env var or config branch** — `stats` reads `CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH` differently.
3. **HNSW counter is decoupled** from `memory_entries` rows and stored in a separate state file that never gets incremented.

A grep for `./.claude/memory.db`, `'.claude'` path joining, or `getStatsDb()` style helpers in `@claude-flow/memory` should surface it quickly.

## Impact

- Users can't trust `memory stats` for monitoring or capacity planning.
- Anything that depends on stats output (dashboards, doctor checks, possibly hook gates) sees zero entries and may erroneously trigger "empty memory" logic.
- Dual-mode Claude + Codex orchestration (which depends on shared memory) appears broken to users running `memory stats` to verify cross-agent state.

## Related observation

After `memory delete -k <key> -n <ns>`, the output reports:

```
[OK] Deleted "test-entry" from namespace "bug-repro-..."
[INFO] Remaining entries: 1
```

`Remaining entries: 1` may refer to total DB rows across all namespaces (intended) or may be another stale counter. Worth confirming alongside the stats fix.

## Proposed direction

1. Consolidate DB path resolution into a single helper used by **all** subcommands of `memory`.
2. Make the path configurable via one env var (`CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH`) with one default — pick `./.swarm/memory.db` since live data already lands there.
3. Add a smoke test: `store` → `stats` should reflect the new entry count.

Happy to open a PR — currently spinning up an agent swarm to investigate.

## Evidence file

Full repro log: attached separately if needed.

title: feat(federation): ADR-120 Step 2 — midstream-aware transport loader
body:
## Summary

Lands ruflo-side Step 2 of [ADR-120](v3/docs/adr/ADR-120-midstream-quic-from-agentic-flow.md). Extends the federation transport loader to prefer midstream's real QUIC build when `MIDSTREAMER_QUIC_NATIVE=1`, transparently falling through to the existing agentic-flow loader (ADR-108 native QUIC / ADR-104 WebSocket fallback) otherwise.

## What's in

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/src/transport/midstream-aware-loader.ts` | **new** — `loadFederationTransport(config)` probes midstreamer first, refuses the WASM stub via `isStub()` per ADR-119, returns `LoadedFederationTransport{transport, source, fallbackReason?}` |
| `v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/src/plugin.ts` | imports from the wrapper instead of `agentic-flow/transport/loader` directly; logs resolved `source` |
| `v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/__tests__/unit/midstream-aware-loader.test.ts` | **new** — 5 cases (env unset / "0" / "1"-without-package / config passthrough / envelope shape) |
| `scripts/audit-fix-invariants.mjs` | 2 new invariants pinning the env-flag check + the `loadFederationTransport` import in plugin.ts |

## Behavior change today

**None.** Midstream's WASM build is a counter-tracking stub per ADR-119, so `MIDSTREAMER_QUIC_NATIVE=1` falls through to agentic-flow's loader on every install today. The wrapper activates the moment `midstreamer@0.3.0` ships real QUIC (ADR-120 Step 1, upstream work in `ruvnet/midstream`).

Built in a worktree per the user's request.

- Step 1 (upstream midstream QUIC republish) — out of repo scope
- Step 3 (`v3/crates/ruflo-federation-peer/` Rust crate) — blocked on Step 1; will land in a follow-up

title: feat(federation-peer): wire real midstreamer-quic@0.3.0 + aimds-core@0.2.0 (ADR-120 Step 3)
body:
## Summary

Closes ADR-120 Step 3. Replaces the typed `not implemented` placeholders in `native_transport` and `native_gate` with real implementations that delegate to the embedding traits published in [ruvnet/midstream PR #82](https://github.com/ruvnet/midstream/pull/82) (now on crates.io as `midstreamer-quic@0.3.0` and `aimds-core@0.2.0`).

Both upstream crates are now real published versions; this PR wires them in.

## Changes

### Cargo.toml

| Dep | Old | New |
|-----|-----|-----|
| `midstreamer-quic` | 0.2.1 | **0.3.0** (now exposes `QuicTransport` trait) |
| `aimds-core` | 0.1.1 | **0.2.0** (now exposes `SafetyGate` + `SafetyVerdict`) |
| `aimds-detection` / `-analysis` / `-response` | optional 0.1.1 | _dropped_ |
| `uuid` (v4) | — | **added (optional, native)** |
| `chrono` | — | **added (optional, native)** |

Dropping the three concrete `aimds-*` impl crates keeps the peer minimal: it composes **any** `aimds_core::SafetyGate`, so the concrete 3-gate pipeline is supplied by the caller (e.g. AIMDS's `ComposedGate` or a custom composition).

### `native_transport::MidstreamerTransport<T: QuicTransport>`

Real, no stubs:
- Generic over any embedder-supplied transport (defaults to `QuicConnection`)
- `connect(addr)`: opens a client connection via `QuicConnection::connect`
- `send(addr, msg)`: opens a bidirectional stream, writes one NDJSON line per `FederationMessage`, finishes the stream
- `recv()`: accepts an inbound bidirectional stream, reads to EOF (16 MiB cap), parses one JSON value
- `close()`: closes the connection with reason `peer shutdown`

### `native_gate::AimdsGate`

Real adapter, no stubs:
- Holds `Arc<dyn aimds_core::SafetyGate>` — composes any 3-gate pipeline (AIMDS's canonical `ComposedGate`, custom composition, or test stub)
- Converts `FederationMessage` ↔ `PromptInput` (payload-as-string + metadata-as-context)
- Converts `aimds_core::SafetyVerdict` ↔ peer-local `SafetyVerdict`, preserving routing metadata on `Redact`

### `bin.rs`

Under `--features native`, boots a real tokio runtime:
- `MidstreamerTransport::connect()` against `RUFLO_FEDERATION_REMOTE_ADDR`
- `AimdsGate::new(PassGate)` (pass-through default so the smoke path works without AIMDS rules configured)
- NDJSON-stdout dispatcher — parent process (ruflo MCP server) ingests verdicts

Without `--features native`, prints a help message and exits.

## Tests

- **3/3** tests pass (default features)
- **4/4** tests pass (`--features native`) — includes new `aimds_gate_adapter_forwards_pass_and_block_verdicts` that exercises the real `aimds_core::SafetyGate` trait against an in-test pattern gate

## CI guard

`scripts/audit-fix-invariants.mjs`:
- Bumped Cargo.toml pin invariants to 0.3.0 / 0.2.0
- Added two new invariants checking the lib.rs imports actually reference upstream `QuicTransport` and `aimds_core::SafetyGate` — guards against silent reversion to a typed placeholder
- **34/34** invariants pass

## Why now

The two upstream PRs ([midstream#82](https://github.com/ruvnet/midstream/pull/82) for `QuicTransport` + `SafetyGate` traits) just merged + published to crates.io. This is the unblocking change for the typed-placeholder backends in `ruflo-federation-peer` that have been waiting on those embedding-trait surfaces.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --lib` — 3/3 green
- [x] `cargo test --lib --features native` — 4/4 green
- [x] `cargo build --bins` — both feature flavors compile
- [x] `node scripts/audit-fix-invariants.mjs` — 34/34 invariants pass

title: 🔄 Rollback Incident: [Brief Description]
fix(plugin-agent-federation): #1949 — agentic-flow → optional peer dep (drops cookies@0.9.1 blocker)
body:
Closes #1949.

## Problem

Hardened npm registries reject `@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@alpha` with `403 Forbidden` on `cookies@0.9.1` because of a deep transitive chain:

\`\`\`
@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation
└─ agentic-flow
   └─ fastmcp
      └─ mcp-proxy
         └─ pipenet
            └─ koa@3.2.0       ← deprecated koa-router warning lives here
               └─ cookies@0.9.1  ← blocked by hardened registry policies
\`\`\`

This blocks Check 2 + Check 3 of the 12-hour scheduled verification — and any user on a hardened registry.

## Fix

The plugin only uses `agentic-flow` for **one** function (`loadQuicTransport` as fallback transport in `midstream-aware-loader.ts`). Make it an **optional peer dependency** so the koa transitive chain only gets pulled in when the operator actually wants the agentic-flow backend.

### package.json

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `dependencies.agentic-flow` (hard) | `peerDependencies.agentic-flow` (optional) |
| 529 transitive packages | **2 transitive packages** |

\`\`\`json
"peerDependencies": {
  "agentic-flow": ">=2.0.12-fix.8",
  "midstreamer": ">=0.3.1"
},
"peerDependenciesMeta": {
  "agentic-flow": { "optional": true },
  "midstreamer": { "optional": true }
}
\`\`\`

Both backends are now optional — at least one must be installed at runtime. The loader throws a clear, actionable error when neither is present.

Version bump: 1.0.0-alpha.15 → 1.0.0-alpha.16

### midstream-aware-loader.ts

- Replaced the static value import of `loadQuicTransport` with a lazy `loadAgenticFlowQuicTransport()` that uses a vitest-mockable direct dynamic `import()` and falls back to `null` when the package isn't installed
- Type imports remain static — they're erased at compile time, so TypeScript users still get full IntelliSense without forcing the runtime install

## Verification

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin install in clean workspace | **529 packages** | **2 packages** ✅ |
| `cookies@0.9.1` pulled in | yes | **no** ✅ |
| `koa-router@14.0.0` deprecation warning | yes | **no** ✅ |
| vitest test suite | 549/549 | **555/555** ✅ (6 new loader-fallback tests pass) |
| Loader graceful failure | (would crash) | clear error ✅ |
| `tsc --strict` | pass | **pass** ✅ |

\`\`\`bash
# Verified locally:
npm pack /Users/cohen/Projects/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation
cd /tmp/empty && npm init -y
npm install ./claude-flow-plugin-agent-federation-1.0.0-alpha.16.tgz
# → added 2 packages in 703ms
# → npm ls cookies koa-router → (empty)
\`\`\`

Loader behavior when neither peer is installed:
\`\`\`
Error: No federation transport available. Install \`agentic-flow\` (default)
       or \`midstreamer\` and set \`MIDSTREAMER_QUIC_NATIVE=1\` (per ADR-120).
       Both are now optional peer dependencies — at least one must be
       present at runtime.
\`\`\`

## CI guard

`scripts/audit-fix-invariants.mjs`:
- Added 4 new invariants checking the peer-dep wiring stays in place (package.json `peerDependencies` + `peerDependenciesMeta`, and the loader's type-only import + lazy loader symbol)
- **38/38** invariants pass

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — tsc clean
- [x] `npm test` — 555/555 vitest tests pass
- [x] `npm pack` + fresh install in `/tmp` — 2 packages total
- [x] Loader gracefully throws actionable error when no peer is installed
- [x] `node scripts/audit-fix-invariants.mjs` — 38/38 invariants pass

title: ruflo-browser 0.2.0: `browser_session_record` fails — `ruvector rvf create` missing required `-d, --dimension` flag
body:
## Summary

The `mcp__ruflo__browser_session_record` MCP tool from `ruflo-browser` plugin v0.2.0 fails when called because the wrapper invokes `npx ruvector@0.2.25 rvf create --kind browser-session` **without** the `-d, --dimension <n>` flag that `ruvector` requires.

## Environment

- Plugin: `ruflo-browser` 0.2.0 (cache path `~/.claude/plugins/cache/ruflo/ruflo-browser/0.2.0/`)
- `ruvector` resolved by `npx -y ruvector@0.2.25`
- OS: macOS Darwin 25.4.0
- Reproduction date: 2026-05-15

## Reproduction

Invoke the MCP tool with any session args:

\`\`\`
mcp__ruflo__browser_session_record({
  url: "https://example.com",
  task: "test",
  session: "login-test-2026-05-15"
})
\`\`\`

Response:

\`\`\`json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "rvf create failed",
  "detail": "Command failed: npx -y ruvector@0.2.25 rvf create /path/to/login-test-2026-05-15.rvf --kind browser-session\nerror: required option '-d, --dimension <n>' not specified\n",
  "stderr": "error: required option '-d, --dimension <n>' not specified\n",
  "sessionId": "login-test-2026-05-15",
  "rvfPath": "/path/to/login-test-2026-05-15.rvf"
}
\`\`\`

Direct CLI repro confirms the upstream contract:

\`\`\`
$ npx -y ruvector@0.2.25 rvf create /tmp/x.rvf --kind browser-session
error: required option '-d, --dimension <n>' not specified

$ npx -y ruvector@0.2.25 rvf create --help
Usage: ruvector rvf create [options] <path>
  -d, --dimension <n>    Vector dimension
  -m, --metric <metric>  Distance metric (l2, cosine, dotproduct) (default: "cosine")
  -h, --help             display help for command
\`\`\`

## Impact

- `browser_session_record` is unusable as shipped — every call fails before opening a session.
- Blocks every downstream `ruflo-browser` skill that depends on session creation: `browser-login`, `browser-record`, `browser-test`, `browser-extract`, `browser-form-fill`, `browser-auth-flow`, `browser-replay`, `browser-screenshot-diff`.
- Effectively makes the entire 23-tool browser stack inert until session creation succeeds.

## Suggested fix

Pass `-d <dimension>` in the wrapper. The trajectory embedding dimension used elsewhere in `ruflo-browser` (per the plugin docs) appears to be 384 (matching ONNX `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` referenced in `ruflo-ruvector:vector-setup`). The wrapper should:

1. Read the configured dimension from plugin config (default `384`), or
2. Probe `npx ruvector default-dimension` / pin it explicitly to 384.

Then invoke:

\`\`\`
npx -y ruvector@0.2.25 rvf create <path> --kind browser-session --dimension 384 --metric cosine
\`\`\`

(Defaults to `cosine` metric per the CLI help, so `--metric` can be omitted unless a non-default is desired.)

## Reporter context

Hit this trying to drive `/ruflo-browser:browser-login intigriti.com` for a bug-bounty workspace authenticated-scope-capture workflow. Without `browser_session_record` succeeding, the entire `browser-login` skill chain is unreachable.

title: pre-bash hook silently skips dangerous-command validation on real Claude Code payloads
body:
**Repo:** `ruvnet/ruflo`
**Version observed:** `3.6.30` (please verify on latest alpha too)
**File:** `.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs`
**Severity:** Medium — security control documented as active is in fact a no-op for every Bash PreToolUse call.

---

## Summary

`.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs` reads the command to validate from the wrong field, so the dangerous-command check in the `pre-bash` handler never runs against the actual command sent by Claude Code. The check appears to pass on every call (returns `[OK] Command validated`, exits 0), masking what is supposed to be a safety gate.

## Where the bug lives

```js
// hook-handler.cjs — lines ~111-117

const toolInput = hookInput.toolInput || hookInput.tool_input || {};
const toolName  = hookInput.toolName  || hookInput.tool_name  || '';

// BUG: this falls through to the entire `toolInput` OBJECT
//      when neither hookInput.prompt nor hookInput.command exists.
const prompt = hookInput.prompt || hookInput.command || toolInput
  || process.env.PROMPT || process.env.TOOL_INPUT_command || args.join(' ') || '';
```

Claude Code sends PreToolUse Bash payloads with the command nested under `tool_input.command` (snake_case). So:

| Field | Value at runtime |
|---|---|
| `hookInput.prompt` | `undefined` |
| `hookInput.command` | `undefined` (not at top level) |
| `toolInput` | `{ command: "rm -rf / --no-preserve-root", description: "..." }` ← the **object**, not the string |

`prompt` therefore becomes the entire `toolInput` object. Then in the handler:

```js
'pre-bash': () => {
  const cmd = (hookInput.command || prompt).toLowerCase();   // ← .toLowerCase() on an object
  const dangerous = ['rm -rf /', 'format c:', 'del /s /q c:\\', ':(){:|:&};:'];
  for (const d of dangerous) {
    if (cmd.includes(d)) {
      console.error(`[BLOCKED] Dangerous command detected: ${d}`);
      process.exit(1);
    }
  }
  console.log('[OK] Command validated');
}
```

`.toLowerCase()` on an object throws `TypeError`. The 5s global safety timer (and any surrounding `try/catch`) swallows the throw with `exit 0`, so the check appears to pass.

## Reproduction (no install needed)

After `npx ruflo@3.6.30 init`, from the project root:

```bash
# Test 1 — innocuous command, real Claude Code payload schema
echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls -la"}}' \
  | node .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs pre-bash
# Expected: [OK] Command validated, exit 0
# Actual:   [OK] Command validated, exit 0    ← passes (by accident)

# Test 2 — dangerous command, same schema
echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf / --no-preserve-root"}}' \
  | node .claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs pre-bash
# Expected: [BLOCKED] Dangerous command detected: rm -rf /, exit 1
# Actual:   [OK] Command validated, exit 0    ← BUG: dangerous command not blocked
```

Test 2 is the smoking gun: the documented "Validate command safety before execution" gate silently lets the dangerous command through.

## Suggested fix (minimal)

Two-line patch, no behavior change for any other call site:

```diff
--- a/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs
+++ b/.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs
@@ -113,7 +113,7 @@
   // Merge stdin data into prompt resolution: prefer stdin fields, then env, then argv
-  const prompt = hookInput.prompt || hookInput.command || toolInput
+  const prompt = hookInput.prompt || hookInput.command || toolInput.command
     || process.env.PROMPT || process.env.TOOL_INPUT_command || args.join(' ') || '';

@@ -146,7 +146,7 @@
   'pre-bash': () => {
     // Basic command safety check — prefer stdin command data from Claude Code
-    const cmd = (hookInput.command || prompt).toLowerCase();
+    const cmd = String(hookInput.command || toolInput.command || prompt || '').toLowerCase();
     const dangerous = ['rm -rf /', 'format c:', 'del /s /q c:\\', ':(){:|:&};:'];
```

- Line 116 reads the **string** `toolInput.command`, not the whole object.
- Line 148 wraps in `String(... || '')` so any non-string sneaking through (`null`, an object, etc.) can no longer throw.

## Verification after the fix

| # | Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ls -la` | `[OK]` exit 0 (accidental) | `[OK]` exit 0 |
| 2 | `rm -rf / --no-preserve-root` | `[OK]` exit 0 ← bug | `[BLOCKED]` exit 1 ✓ |
| 3 | `{}` (empty payload) | `[OK]` exit 0 | `[OK]` exit 0 |
| 4 | `{"tool_input":{"command":null}}` | `[OK]` exit 0 | `[OK]` exit 0 |

## Side observations (not strictly part of this bug)

- The danger list (`rm -rf /`, `format c:`, ...) is very narrow. After this fix, the gate works as documented but its coverage is still minimal — e.g. `rm -rf /home` or `dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/sda` would still pass. Worth considering whether to expand or make it configurable, but that's separate.
- A regression test that pipes a real Claude Code-shaped payload into `node hook-handler.cjs pre-bash` and asserts the exit code would prevent this class of regression. Happy to PR one if helpful.

## Credit

Found via a code review on a downstream Arbora install. Reported here so the fix lands for every Ruflo user.

title: @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38 fails with npm 'Invalid Version' (regression of #1147 pattern)
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

`@claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38` (tagged `latest` and `alpha`) fails to install via `npx` with `npm error Invalid Version:` (empty version string). Same failure shape as closed #1147 — recurring on a new alpha.

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest doctor
# or
npx @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38 doctor
```

### Actual Behavior

```
npm warn exec The following package was not found and will be installed: @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38
npm error Invalid Version: 
npm error A complete log of this run can be found in: ~/.npm/_logs/...-debug-0.log
```

### Root Cause (from npm debug log)

```
silly fetch manifest @huggingface/transformers@^4.2.0
silly placeDep ROOT @huggingface/transformers@4.2.0 OK for: @claude-flow/embeddings@3.0.0-alpha.15 want: ^4.2.0
verbose stack TypeError: Invalid Version:
verbose stack     at new SemVer (.../semver/classes/semver.js:40:13)
verbose stack     at compare (.../semver/functions/compare.js:5:32)
verbose stack     at Object.eq (.../semver/functions/eq.js:4:29)
verbose stack     at Node.canDedupe (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/node.js:1137:32)
verbose stack     at PlaceDep.pruneDedupable (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/place-dep.js:426:14)
```

Transitive dep `@huggingface/transformers@4.2.0` (pulled by `@claude-flow/embeddings@3.0.0-alpha.15`) has an empty `version` field in some resolved manifest, breaking `npm`'s arborist dedupe step. This is the new variant of the recurring problem — historically `@xenova/transformers` (see #858), now `@huggingface/transformers`.

### Workaround

Pin to alpha.37:
```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.37 doctor   # ✅ works
```

### Environment

- macOS Darwin 25.5.0 (Apple M1)
- node v25.9.0
- npm v11.12.1
- Claude Code v2.1.142

### Suggested Fix

1. Republish `alpha.38` with `@claude-flow/embeddings@3.0.0-alpha.15` pinning a transformers version that has a clean manifest, or
2. Move `latest` tag back to alpha.37: `npm dist-tag add @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.37 latest`
3. Lock the embeddings package out of `npx`'s default install path (lazy-load per ADR-100 #1760).

### Impact

- `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest …` broken for any user on npm 11.x / Node 24+
- MCP server / doctor / status all unavailable on default install path
- Recurring pattern — same failure as #1147 in alpha.39 last cycle.

title: vectorBackend controller permanently disabled due to API mismatch between @claude-flow/memory and agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.14
body:
Background

In a prior session, a config_set call wrote the key agentdb.controllers.vectorBackend.enabled = true to .claude-flow/config.json. However, the agentdb_health MCP tool continued to report vectorBackend: enabled: false. The hypothesis was that a daemon restart would pick up the config change. This investigation picks up after that restart.

Step-by-Step Investigation

Step 1 — Check if daemon restart picked up the config change

Action: Called mcp__claude-flow__agentdb_health immediately after restarting Claude Code.

Raw result:

{ "name": "vectorBackend", "enabled": false, "level": 2 }
{ "name": "vectorBackend", "enabled": false, "level": 2 }

Finding: The daemon restart had no effect. The config_set change (stored in .claude-flow/config.json under scopes.project) is not read by the MCP server at startup. The value was persisted as a string "true" rather than a boolean true, which may also have contributed to it being ignored.

Step 2 — Attempt bootstrapping via embeddings_init

Action: Called mcp__claude-flow__embeddings_init with default parameters (model: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, dimension: 384, hyperbolic enabled).

Raw result:

{
  "success": true,
  "config": { "model": "Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2", "dimension": 384, "cacheSize": 256 },
  "paths": {
    "config": "D:\\...\\ruflo-stable\\.claude-flow\\embeddings.json",
    "models": "D:\\...\\ruflo-stable\\.claude-flow\\models"
  }
}
{
  "success": true,
  "config": { "model": "Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2", "dimension": 384, "cacheSize": 256 },
  "paths": {
    "config": "D:\\...\\ruflo-stable\\.claude-flow\\embeddings.json",
    "models": "D:\\...\\ruflo-stable\\.claude-flow\\models"
  }
}

Called agentdb_health again. Result: still vectorBackend: false.

Finding: embeddings_init writes an embeddings.json config file and creates a models directory, but does not affect the AgentDB controller registry inside the MCP server. The models directory remained empty — no ONNX model weights were downloaded.

Step 3 — Read the agentdb-vector-search skill

Action: Located and read .claude\skills\agentdb-vector-search\SKILL.md.

Summary of skill content:

  • Describes the standalone agentdb CLI package (npx agentdb@latest ...)
  • Prerequisites: Node.js 18+, agentdb v1.0.7+, optional OpenAI API key or custom ONNX model
  • Key command: npx agentdb@latest init ./vectors.db --dimension 384 to create a vector database file
  • Also mentions npx agentdb@latest mcp as a separate MCP server

Finding: The skill documents the standalone agentdb CLI, not how to enable the vectorBackend controller inside the claude-flow MCP server. It does not mention config_set, controller toggles, or environment variables. Its main actionable suggestion was to run npx agentdb@latest init.

Step 4a — Run agentdb init to create the vector database file

Action:

npx agentdb@latest init "D:\...\ruflo-stable\.claude-flow\vectors.db" --dimension 384
npx agentdb@latest init "D:\...\ruflo-stable\.claude-flow\vectors.db" --dimension 384

Raw output:

✅ Using sql.js (WASM SQLite, no build tools required)
⚠ Warning: Schema file not found: ...agentdb\dist\schemas\schema.sql
⚠ Warning: Schema file not found: ...agentdb\dist\schemas\frontier-schema.sql
✅ AgentDB initialized successfully
Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 76
Exit code 9
✅ Using sql.js (WASM SQLite, no build tools required)
⚠ Warning: Schema file not found: ...agentdb\dist\schemas\schema.sql
⚠ Warning: Schema file not found: ...agentdb\dist\schemas\frontier-schema.sql
✅ AgentDB initialized successfully
Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 76
Exit code 9

A vectors.db file (12,288 bytes) was created despite the Windows libuv assertion crash on exit.

Called agentdb_health again. Result: still vectorBackend: false.

Finding: The vectors.db file is irrelevant to the controller registry. The registry uses :memory: by default unless explicitly configured with a dbPath. The file on disk has no effect on the in-process AgentDB instance.

Step 4b — Source-code analysis of the controller registry

Action: Read the compiled source of the @claude-flow/memory package at:

C:\Users\DineshR\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\claude-flow\node_modules\@claude-flow\memory\dist\controller-registry.js
C:\Users\DineshR\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\claude-flow\node_modules\@claude-flow\memory\dist\controller-registry.js

Key finding 1 — isControllerEnabled for vectorBackend:

case 'vectorBackend':
case 'guardedVectorBackend':
    return this.agentdb !== null;
case 'vectorBackend':
case 'guardedVectorBackend':
    return this.agentdb !== null;

The controller is only eligible for initialization if the internal this.agentdb instance is non-null.

Key finding 2 — initializeController for vectorBackend:

case 'vectorBackend':
case 'graphAdapter': {
    // These are accessed via AgentDB internal state, not direct construction
    if (!this.agentdb)
        return null;
    try {
        if (typeof this.agentdb.getController === 'function') {
            return this.agentdb.getController(name) ?? null;
        }
    }
    catch { /* fallthrough */ }
    return null;
}
case 'vectorBackend':
case 'graphAdapter': {
    // These are accessed via AgentDB internal state, not direct construction
    if (!this.agentdb)
        return null;
    try {
        if (typeof this.agentdb.getController === 'function') {
            return this.agentdb.getController(name) ?? null;
        }
    }
    catch { /* fallthrough */ }
    return null;
}

The enabled flag is set to instance !== null. So even when AgentDB initializes successfully, the controller stays disabled if agentdb.getController('vectorBackend') returns null or throws.

Key finding 3 — AgentDB does initialize successfully:
Direct Node.js test:

[AgentDB] Using RuVector backend (native)
[AgentDB] RuVector initialization failed, trying RVF backend
[AgentDB] Reason: RuVector initialization failed. Please install: npm install ruvector
[AgentDB] Using RVF backend (N-API fallback)
[AgentDB] Initialized with better-sqlite3 + rvf vector backend
Init OK
[AgentDB] Using RuVector backend (native)
[AgentDB] RuVector initialization failed, trying RVF backend
[AgentDB] Reason: RuVector initialization failed. Please install: npm install ruvector
[AgentDB] Using RVF backend (N-API fallback)
[AgentDB] Initialized with better-sqlite3 + rvf vector backend
Init OK

The AgentDB class initializes fine with :memory: (falling back from native ruvector → RVF N-API → sql.js). This rules out an initialization error as the cause.

Key finding 4 — getController('vectorBackend') throws:

Error: Unknown controller: vectorBackend
    at AgentDB.getController (AgentDB.js:124:23)
Error: Unknown controller: vectorBackend
    at AgentDB.getController (AgentDB.js:124:23)

Reading the getController source confirmed it only recognizes three controller names:

switch (name) {
    case 'memory':
    case 'reflexion':
        return this.reflexion;
    case 'skills':
        return this.skills;
    case 'causal':
    case 'causalGraph':
        return this.causalGraph;
    default:
        throw new Error(`Unknown controller: ${name}`);
}
switch (name) {
    case 'memory':
    case 'reflexion':
        return this.reflexion;
    case 'skills':
        return this.skills;
    case 'causal':
    case 'causalGraph':
        return this.causalGraph;
    default:
        throw new Error(`Unknown controller: ${name}`);
}

The registry's try/catch silently swallows this error and falls through to return null, which sets entry.enabled = false.

Root Cause

Version mismatch between @claude-flow/memory and agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.14.

Component | Expectation -- | -- @claude-flow/memory controller registry | Calls agentdb.getController('vectorBackend') expecting it to return a live controller instance agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.14 | Does not implement vectorBackend in its getController() switch — throws Unknown controller: vectorBackend

title: [verification] HIGH: Witness manifest stale — #1825 marker regressed after @claude-flow/memory bump alpha.14→alpha.16
body:
## Summary

The scheduled 12-hour verification (2026-05-16T19:04Z, commit `ca0a6fa`) reports **`regressed=1`** on all three platform manifests (macOS, Linux, Windows). The Ed25519 signatures remain valid, but the witness manifest marker for fix `#1825` no longer matches the source file.

The root cause is a dependency version bump that was not followed by a manifest regeneration: `@claude-flow/memory` was updated from `^3.0.0-alpha.14` to `^3.0.0-alpha.16` (as part of fix #2019), which changed the content of `v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json`. The marker the manifest is looking for no longer exists in the file.

## Impact

- The integrity chain is technically intact (all three Ed25519 signatures are valid) but the **marker verification layer is broken**.
- A future regression in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json` could be silently masked by the pre-existing `regressed=1` noise.
- The CI gate `witness-verify` reads the same manifests — stale markers produce persistent false positives that erode confidence in the pipeline.
- Additionally, 95 of 113 manifest entries report `missing` because this verification environment is a source-only checkout (no `npm run build`). The `#1880` precondition heuristic (exit 2 when *all* entries are missing) does not fire because 13 package.json checks still pass.

## Expected

```
Summary: pass=N drift=0 regressed=0 missing=0
```

## Actual (identical across macOS, Linux, Windows)

```
Manifest signature:
  hash matches:                    yes
  public key reproducible:         yes
  Ed25519 signature valid:         yes

Summary: pass=13 drift=4 regressed=1 missing=95

Regressed:
  #1825  marker missing in v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json
```

**Manifest entry for #1825:**
```json
{
  "id": "#1825",
  "desc": "hotfix: workspace: protocol leak in cli optionalDependencies",
  "file": "v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json",
  "sha256": "9d8b24743c09a6f60371150207edd60a05ce393a67137c69d62e27b1d3e16c75",
  "marker": "\"@claude-flow/memory\": \"^3.0.0-alpha.14\""
}
```

**Actual file content (line 112):**
```
"@claude-flow/memory": "^3.0.0-alpha.16",
```

**Actual SHA256:** `eb755f44efe5c79e4c32afe82bfff79f75c07711a463bdb3a86dcb0fada799a4`

## Recommended fix

1. **Regenerate manifests** after the `@claude-flow/memory` bump: run `node plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/regen.mjs` (or equivalent) and commit the updated `verification/{macos,linux,windows}/manifest.md.json`.
2. **Add a CI step** that runs `verify.mjs` on the fully built tree (after `npm ci && npm run build`) and fails on any `regressed > 0`, so stale markers are caught at merge time rather than by the next scheduled run.
3. **Consider a version-agnostic marker** for #1825 (e.g., `"@claude-flow/memory": "^3.0.0-alpha.`) if the intent is only to verify the `workspace:` protocol was removed, not to pin an exact minor version.

## Relevant report section

```
Check 1: Witness signature verification
Status:   FAILED
Severity: HIGH
Exit code: 1
Duration: ~3s per platform
```

## Environment

- Commit: `ca0a6fa5cb1678b5c57c9289bc09a036f7308c61` (main HEAD)
- Timestamp UTC: 2026-05-16T19:04:45Z
- Node: v22.22.2 / npm: 10.9.7
- OS: Linux x86_64 6.18.5
- agentic-flow: 2.0.12-fix.8

title: [upstream] @ruvector/sona@0.1.6 is an empty publish — broke @claude-flow/neural until alpha.9 pinned around it
body:
## Summary

`@ruvector/sona@0.1.6` (current `latest` on npm) shipped as an **empty publish** — the tarball only contains `README.md` and `package.json`. No `index.js`. No native binaries. The previous release `@ruvector/sona@0.1.5` had full content (`index.js`, `.d.ts`, and 7 platform-specific `.node` files).

This made every `npm install @claude-flow/neural@3.0.0-alpha.8` fail at import time with:

\`\`\`
Error: Cannot find package '.../node_modules/@ruvector/sona/index.js'
    imported from .../node_modules/@claude-flow/neural/dist/sona-integration.js
\`\`\`

`@claude-flow/neural`'s `package.json` pinned `\"@ruvector/sona\": \"latest\"`, so every fresh install resolved to the broken 0.1.6.

## Reproduction (the broken state)

\`\`\`bash
TMPDIR=\$(mktemp -d) && cd \$TMPDIR && npm init -y >/dev/null
npm install @ruvector/sona@0.1.6
ls node_modules/@ruvector/sona/
# → README.md  package.json     (no index.js, no native bins)

npm install @ruvector/sona@0.1.5
ls node_modules/@ruvector/sona/
# → README.md  index.d.ts  index.js  package.json
#   sona.darwin-arm64.node  sona.darwin-universal.node  sona.darwin-x64.node
#   sona.linux-arm64-gnu.node  sona.linux-x64-gnu.node  sona.linux-x64-musl.node
#   sona.win32-arm64-msvc.node  sona.win32-x64-msvc.node
\`\`\`

## Workaround (already shipped in alpha.9)

`@claude-flow/neural@3.0.0-alpha.9` (2026-05-16) pins to the exact known-good version:

\`\`\`json
{
  \"dependencies\": {
    \"@ruvector/sona\": \"0.1.5\"
  }
}
\`\`\`

Live functional check confirms the fix:

\`\`\`
$ npm install @claude-flow/neural@3.0.0-alpha.9
$ node -e \"import('@claude-flow/neural').then(m => console.log('keys:', Object.keys(m).slice(0,5)))\"
keys: A2CAlgorithm,BalancedMode,BaseModeImplementation,BatchMode,CuriosityModule
\`\`\`

## What needs to happen upstream

Either:

1. **Unpublish `@ruvector/sona@0.1.6`** (requires deprecation/unpublish window) and ensure `latest` points back to `0.1.5`. This is the cleanest fix.

2. **Republish `@ruvector/sona@0.1.7`** with the actual source content + native bins, advance `latest` to it. Then this repo can switch `@claude-flow/neural`'s pin back to `^0.1.5 || ^0.1.7` (skipping the bad 0.1.6).

3. **Republish `@ruvector/sona@0.1.6`** in place if npm allows it (only within the unpublish window — most likely already past 72h).

The pin in `@claude-flow/neural@3.0.0-alpha.9` is a workaround, not the real fix — the real fix lives in the `@ruvector/sona` build/publish pipeline. Most likely cause: a release script that ran `npm publish` from a clean source dir before the build step / before native bins were prebuilt.

## Impact

- `@claude-flow/neural` is at **~40,000 weekly downloads** — every fresh install between the 0.1.6 publish (date?) and the alpha.9 publish (2026-05-16) hit this error.
- Workaround is now in `@claude-flow/neural@3.0.0-alpha.9` and propagated to `@claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.43+`, `claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.43+`, and `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.43+`.

## Action items

- [ ] Investigate why the 0.1.6 publish ran without `index.js` / native bins
- [ ] Republish 0.1.7 (or 0.2.0) with content
- [ ] Remove the exact pin in `@claude-flow/neural` once a known-good \"latest\" exists again
- [ ] Add a smoke test to the @ruvector/sona release pipeline that asserts `index.js` exists in the published tarball

title: feat(ruflo-loop-workers): custom-worker manifest schema + register skill (v0.3.0)
body:
## Summary

Adds a thin, additive surface for consumer plugins (and downstream projects) to declare their own recurring workers in a YAML manifest and register each as a `CronCreate` schedule via a new skill. The 12 built-in triggers continue to dispatch through `mcp__claude-flow__hooks_worker-dispatch` unchanged; custom workers run alongside, in a separate registration path.

**Marked draft so the design can be redirected before merge.** Happy to rework the schema, naming, or scope based on your read.

## Motivating consumer

AgentVille's L4 deterministic anomaly tick. The L4 spec [§7.5](https://gitlab.com/altitudes-cloud/ai/agentville/-/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-16-auto-ops-l4-loop-worker-design.md) defines a manifest contract; AgentVille's [deployment runbook](https://gitlab.com/altitudes-cloud/ai/agentville/-/blob/main/docs/runbooks/2026-05-16-auto-ops-l4-deployment.md) currently documents three concrete cron recipes (CronCreate, Unix cron, systemd) the operator picks from. Generalising that surface here so consumers declare once in YAML, the skill walks the entries through `CronCreate`.

## What changed

- **`plugin.json`**: bump `0.2.0 → 0.3.0`; add `custom-workers` keyword.
- **`skills/register-custom-workers/SKILL.md`**: new skill. Reads a manifest, validates all-or-nothing, builds the per-worker `Bash:` invocation, calls `CronCreate`, reports cron IDs back to the operator. `allowed-tools: Read CronCreate CronList CronDelete`.
- **`docs/custom-worker-manifest.md`**: canonical schema. Required fields: `name`, `schedule`, `command`. Optional: `cwd`, `env`, `timeout_seconds`, `token_budget`, `description`. Pinned at `version: 1`.
- **`docs/adrs/0002-custom-worker-manifest.md`**: rationale, scope, what-this-is-not (job runner / secret manager / lifecycle).
- **`README.md`**: new "Custom workers" section linking to schema + skill, plus ADR-0002 in Architecture Decisions.
- **`scripts/smoke.sh`**: +4 checks for the new surface, bumps the version check from `0.2.0` to `0.3.0`. Drive-by fix on check 11: accepts `Proposed|Accepted` (ADR-0001 had drifted to `Accepted` upstream without a matching smoke update; check 11 was failing pre-PR).

## Scope discipline

What this PR is **not**:

- Not a generic job runner. `CronCreate` is the executor; the skill is a registration helper.
- Not secret management. Manifests must not carry plaintext secrets; they reference wrapper scripts that read from disk.
- Not lifecycle. No update / delete from the skill itself — that's `CronList` + `CronDelete` on the operator side.
- Not a competitor to the 12 built-in triggers. Custom workers run alongside, in a separate namespace, with separate observability.

## Verification

```bash
bash plugins/ruflo-loop-workers/scripts/smoke.sh
# Expected: 16 passed, 0 failed
```

Before this PR: 11 passed, 1 failed (the pre-existing ADR-0001 status drift).
After this PR: 16 passed, 0 failed (12 originals + 4 new, with check 11 relaxed).

## Open questions for the maintainer

1. **Scope of validation.** The skill instructs the model to validate the manifest. A future hardening could ship a JSON Schema + a runnable validator (Node? Python? Bash + jq + yq?). Worth doing now, or defer until a second consumer lands?
2. **Worker name namespacing.** The schema treats `name` as a free-form kebab-case identifier with uniqueness only within a manifest. Should cross-project name collision be a real concern (e.g. prefix worker names with the plugin/project key)?
3. **Plugin layout.** I added the skill under the existing `ruflo-loop-workers` plugin to keep the surface in one place. Would you prefer a sibling plugin (`ruflo-custom-workers`) to keep the 12-trigger contract pristine?

Happy to iterate. AgentVille L4 will adopt whatever shape this lands in.

[verification] MEDIUM: Witness signature check unrunnable — scheduled runner lacks @noble/ed25519 (source-only checkout)
body:
## Summary

The 12-hour scheduled verification (2026-05-17T07:01Z, commit `f8ab5a3`) cannot execute Check 1 (Witness Signature Verification) because `@noble/ed25519` is not installed in the verification environment.

**This is a precondition miss (exit code 2), NOT a real signature failure (exit code 1).** The manifests are valid — the most recent main commit (`f8ab5a3`, 2026-05-16T23:20:26Z) ran the manifests locally and confirmed all three platforms pass:

```
macos:   pass=113 drift=0 regressed=0 missing=0  exit=0
linux:   pass=113 drift=0 regressed=0 missing=0  exit=0
windows: pass=113 drift=0 regressed=0 missing=0  exit=0
```

## Impact

The scheduled verification agent cannot confirm witness signatures are valid on every run. Real signature regressions (drift, regressed, missing markers) would go undetected by the cron check until a manual or CI-triggered run occurs. Product integrity is likely fine — the product's own CI guards (wired in `v3-ci.yml`) catch drift before publish.

## Expected

```
Ed25519 signature valid: yes
pass=113 drift=0 regressed=0 missing=0
```

## Actual

```
verify.mjs: could not load @noble/ed25519 from any of:
  /home/user/ruflo
  /home/user/ruflo/v3
  /home/user/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/cli
  /home/user/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation
  last error: Cannot find module '@noble/ed25519'
Require stack:
- /home/user/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/noop.js

Fix: from the repo root, run `npm install` (the dep is declared
in the root package.json under @noble/ed25519). If your runner
is a source-only checkout, your verification pipeline must run
`npm ci && npm run build` before invoking this script. See #1880
for the full diagnosis.
```

Exit code: **2** (precondition miss — per #1880 fix; this is the correct signal that the environment needs setup, not that a signature failed)

## Recommended fix

Add `npm ci` (or `npm install`) to the verification runner's setup step before invoking `verify.mjs`. Example:

```bash
# In the scheduled verification environment, before Check 1:
npm ci --ignore-scripts   # installs @noble/ed25519 without running postinstall builds
node plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/verify.mjs --manifest verification/linux/manifest.md.json
```

Alternatively, treat exit code 2 in the runner as a non-actionable warning (environment not fully set up) and skip filing issues for it.

## Environment

- Commit: `f8ab5a325537192843f0168bc063b77013d3c2be`
- Node: v22.22.2 / npm: 10.9.7
- Verification run: 2026-05-17T07:01:40Z UTC
- Branch: main HEAD

title: Subagents cannot use SendMessage/TaskUpdate in Claude Code harness — hive-mind coordination silently fails
body:
## What happened

Tried to run a 7-agent hive-mind audit (researcher, rust-reader, 4 role-hats, synthesizer). Initialized hive-mind via `mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_init` (success), then spawned 7 LLM workers via Claude Code's `Agent` tool with `run_in_background: true`. Each agent's brief instructed it to coordinate with named teammates via `SendMessage` per the canonical CLAUDE.md pattern generated by `ruflo init`.

**Result:** 2 of 7 agents aborted before doing any work; 5 completed only because they ignored the brief and worked in "degraded mode" — reading source docs directly and using the shared memory namespace as a bus.

Verbatim from the agents themselves:
- *"SendMessage is not present in this environment."*
- *"SendMessage and TaskUpdate are not surfaced as deferred tools in this environment."*
- *"Tool gaps surfaced: SendMessage is not present in this environment (ToolSearch returned no matches for send/message/agent communication beyond gmail/wasm_agent_prompt)."*
- *"mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_broadcast reports 'Hive-mind not initialized.'"* (even though the lead initialized it successfully one tool-call earlier)

## Root cause (three layers)

**1. Tool-availability asymmetry.** The lead session has `SendMessage` available (loadable via `ToolSearch`). Subagents spawned via Claude Code's `Agent` tool get a different tool allowlist that does NOT include `SendMessage`. Same applies to `TaskUpdate`. So the lead can message subagents but subagents cannot message each other or the lead.

**2. Coordination metadata vs actual workers.** `mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_init` initializes a coordination registry (consensus state machine, queen ID, topology). `hive-mind_spawn` creates placeholder *registry entries* — not LLM workers. The real LLM workers come from Claude Code's `Agent` tool, but they don't auto-register with the hive's coordination layer. So the hive has zero registered workers from its own perspective even when 7 Agent subagents are running concurrently. Calling `hive-mind_broadcast` from a subagent reports "Hive-mind not initialized" because that subagent's process never joined the hive.

**3. No "wait" semantics for subagents.** Subagents are stateless one-shot workers. They start, do work, complete. There's no inbox to poll, no event loop, no way to actually wait for an asynchronous message. A brief that says "WAIT for SendMessage from X" cannot be honored — the agent either aborts cleanly (correct per spec) or runs open-loop with stale assumptions.

The CLAUDE.md "SendMessage-First Coordination" pattern that ships with `ruflo init` is aspirational — it describes how the swarm tools are *supposed* to work, but the harness doesn't deliver it for subagents.

## Impact

For my audit, 2 of 7 agents (first dev-hat and synthesizer) aborted cleanly with helpful diagnostic messages. The other 5 inferred the protocol was broken and adapted to memory-as-bus on their own. The audit completed, but only because half the agents independently figured out the workaround. A less robust set of agents would have produced an unrunnable mess. The lead (me, in the Claude Code session) had to respawn 2 agents and orchestrate phases sequentially.

For any user running ruflo-coordinated swarms today via Claude Code, the experience is:
- Either agents abort with "SendMessage not available" errors (visible failure — annoying but recoverable)
- Or agents silently work open-loop and produce stale/inconsistent output (invisible failure — much worse)

## Proposed fix (two options)

**Option A: Make SendMessage actually work for subagents.** Add `SendMessage`/`TaskUpdate` to the default tool allowlists for every subagent spawned via Claude Code's `Agent` tool (or at least the named-agent subagent types: researcher, coder, system-architect, reviewer, planner, backend-dev). Implement an inbox-polling mechanism — or have the harness deliver queued messages on each tool-use cycle as a virtual tool-result. Also have `hive-mind_init` and friends register the subagent's process ID so `hive-mind_broadcast`/`consensus` actually reach the workers. This is the spec-honest fix but requires harness changes.

**Option B: Update the canonical pattern documentation to reflect reality.** Revise `ruflo init`-generated CLAUDE.md and any docs that recommend the SendMessage-First pattern. Promote **memory-as-bus + lead-orchestrated phases** as the canonical pattern:
- All inter-agent state lives in a shared memory namespace (`memory_store` / `memory_search`)
- The lead orchestrates: spawn → wait for completion notification → verify outputs in memory → spawn next agent with explicit input-key list in its brief
- Parallelize only when work is genuinely independent
- Every subagent brief includes a degraded-mode paragraph instructing it to read source files directly and use memory if coordination tools are missing
- Subagents are stateless one-shot workers, not long-lived event-loop participants

Option B is much cheaper to ship and doesn't depend on Claude Code harness changes. Option A is the right long-term fix if cross-subagent coordination is a real product goal.

## Reproduction

1. `mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_init({topology:"hierarchical", consensus:"byzantine"})` — succeeds
2. Spawn 2+ subagents via Claude Code's `Agent` tool with prompts instructing them to use `SendMessage` to coordinate (e.g. *"When done, SendMessage to 'reviewer'"*)
3. Observe: agents report `SendMessage not present in environment` and either abort or proceed open-loop

## Environment

- Claude Code (Opus 4.7, 1M context)
- ruflo MCP server (current — full tool list includes `mcp__ruflo__hive-mind_*`, `mcp__ruflo__memory_*`, `mcp__ruflo__agent_*`, etc.)
- macOS Darwin 25.3.0

title: [verification] HIGH: npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version times out in network-constrained container
body:
## Summary

Check 2 (Published package smoke test) fails because `npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` is killed by SIGTERM after 60 s in the scheduled verification container. The CLI package has ~527 transitive dependencies and its cold download exceeds the per-command 60 s budget. `ruflo@alpha --version` (thin wrapper) resolves fine at 3.7.0-alpha.45.

## Impact

The verification agent cannot confirm that the CLI alpha version meets the `>= 3.7.0-alpha.20` requirement on each run. Users installing via `npm install` (not `npx` cold-start) are unaffected. A genuine CLI version regression could go undetected in this check.

## Expected

```
npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
# prints: 3.7.x-alpha.NN  (>= 3.7.0-alpha.20)
# exit 0
```

## Actual

```
npm warn deprecated koa-router@14.0.0: ...
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: ...
npm warn deprecated node-domexception@1.0.0: ...
npm warn deprecated uuid@9.0.1: ...
npm error process terminated
npm error signal SIGTERM
# exit 124 (timeout)
```

## Command output

```
=== CLI version check ===
<deprecation warnings>
npm error process terminated
npm error signal SIGTERM
CLI_EXIT:124

=== Ruflo version check ===
<deprecation warnings>
ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.45
RUFLO_EXIT:0
```

## Recommended fix

Two options:
1. **Raise the per-command timeout** for the CLI version check from 60 s to 180 s to accommodate slow container downloads.
2. **Verify CLI version indirectly** via `ruflo@alpha --version` instead of a separate `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` invocation, since ruflo is a thin wrapper that shares the same underlying CLI version.

The published CLI is functionally valid — the doctor check (`npx ruflo@alpha doctor`) completed successfully and reported `✓ Version Freshness: v3.7.0-alpha.45 (up to date)`.

## Relevant report section

Check 2 in the scheduled verification run at 2026-05-17T19:07:28Z UTC.

title: bug(memory): `memory_search_unified` hardcodes 6 namespaces — silently ignores custom namespaces
body:
## Summary

`mcp__ruflo__memory_search_unified`'s docstring promises:

> "Search across both Claude Code memories and AgentDB entries using semantic vector similarity. Returns merged, deduplicated results from all namespaces."

The "all namespaces" claim does not hold in practice. The tool returns `searchedNamespaces: ["default", "claude-memories", "auto-memory", "patterns", "tasks", "feedback"]` — a hardcoded 6-namespace whitelist. Any custom namespace is silently dropped.

## Severity

**P2** — workaround exists (use `memory_search` with explicit `namespace=` arg, iterating across known namespaces) but it degrades the team UX for the entire reason `memory_search_unified` exists.

## Reproduction

```
# 1. Create entry in a custom namespace
mcp__ruflo__memory_store namespace='my-team-decisions' key='test-1' value='hello'

# 2. Verify directly stored
mcp__ruflo__memory_retrieve namespace='my-team-decisions' key='test-1'
# → returns 'hello'

# 3. Direct search works
mcp__ruflo__memory_search query='hello' namespace='my-team-decisions' threshold=0.1
# → 1 result

# 4. Unified search FAILS
mcp__ruflo__memory_search_unified query='hello'
# → 0 results
# response.searchedNamespaces shows the hardcoded 6 — 'my-team-decisions' absent
```

## Impact

For multi-team / multi-project deployments — i.e. the entire "M humans + N AI agents" future ruflo positions itself for — cross-namespace semantic recall is the headline feature of `memory_search_unified`. Hardcoding 6 namespaces breaks the value prop. Every team adopting ruflo with project-prefixed namespaces (we use `kariismatics-*`) has to write a workaround.

## Proposed fix

Either:
- **(A)** Enumerate all namespaces dynamically via the equivalent of `memory_namespace list` rather than the hardcoded list.
- **(B)** Accept an explicit `namespaces=[...]` parameter so callers can target custom namespaces.

Option A matches the docstring promise more closely.

## Local workaround we're using

In `kariisma` (our deployment): iterate `mcp__ruflo__memory_search` over each known custom namespace; codified at our `.claude/rules/ruflo/triggers.md`. Discovered 2026-05-17 during a memory-architecture audit (full report: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/ruflo-usage-architecture-2026-05-17.md` §2.b).

## Environment

- Discovered: 2026-05-17
- Discovered against: latest `claude-flow` (whatever was on npm as of 2026-05-17)
- Local MCP backend: `sql.js + HNSW` per `memory_stats` output

title: bug(agents): `code-review-swarm` missing `mcp__ruflo__*` tools in default allowed-tools — blocks ruflo dispatch hygiene
body:
## Summary

The default `code-review-swarm` agent (shipped via `claude-flow` npm package, installed to `.claude/agents/ruflo/github/code-review-swarm.md` post-init) does NOT include `mcp__ruflo__*` tools in its allowed-tools / tool grant list. This blocks the agent from firing the mandatory ruflo dispatch hygiene calls that the rest of the system expects.

## Why this matters

Per ruflo's own `guidance_workflow type=feature` template, the final step of any feature workflow is **"Record patterns (hooks post-task)"**. Per `guidance_quickref domain=daily-dev`, four triggers are mandatory:

1. `memory_search` BEFORE work
2. `hooks_pre-task` BEFORE dispatch
3. `hooks_route` for model-tier routing
4. `hooks_post-task` AFTER dispatch return — **the learning loop**

`code-review-swarm` cannot do any of these because its allowed-tools list doesn't grant `mcp__ruflo__*`. Result:

- Review verdicts can't be stored at `qa-memory::review-pr<NUM>-<DATE>` (the conventional location for PR review artifacts) from the agent itself.
- Parent dispatcher has to retrofit the writes after-the-fact — fragile (dispatcher may not have full review context).
- SONA pattern trainer learns nothing from review outcomes.

## Severity

**P2** — workaround exists (project-local override that adds the missing tool grants), but every team adopting `claude-flow` with ruflo memory hygiene must maintain the override. Multiplied across teams, meaningful adoption friction.

## Reproduction

```
# 1. Fresh init in a project with ruflo MCP configured
npx claude-flow init

# 2. Inspect the shipped agent
cat .claude/agents/ruflo/github/code-review-swarm.md
# Note allowed-tools list — no mcp__ruflo__*

# 3. Dispatch the agent against any PR — observe: cannot call
#    memory_store / memory_search / hooks_post-task from inside agent.
```

## Proposed fix

Ship the default `code-review-swarm.md` with these tools granted:

- `mcp__ruflo__memory_search`
- `mcp__ruflo__memory_store`
- `mcp__ruflo__memory_retrieve`
- `mcp__ruflo__hooks_pre-task`
- `mcp__ruflo__hooks_post-task`
- `mcp__ruflo__hooks_route`

So the project-local override is no longer necessary.

## Local workaround we're using

Project-local override at `.claude/agents/ruflo/github/code-review-swarm.md` (kariisma sha `7498aed4f`, 2026-05-17) that adds the missing grants. Discovered during a memory-architecture audit dispatched per operator escalation: full context in `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/ruflo-usage-architecture-2026-05-17.md`.

## Environment

- Discovered: 2026-05-17
- Discovered against: latest `claude-flow` (whatever was on npm as of 2026-05-17)

title: agent_execute ignores provider config — hardcodes Anthropic SDK, unusable with OpenRouter
body:
## Description

The `agent_execute` MCP tool and the agent execution runtime ignore the configured provider settings and hardcode Anthropic's SDK directly. This makes it impossible to use Ruflo with non-Anthropic providers like OpenRouter, Ollama, or other OpenAI-compatible endpoints — despite the provider config system existing and being user-configurable.

## Ruflo Version

- `ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.69`
- Claude Code CLI: `v2.1.121`
- Node.js: `v22.22.2`
- OS: Ubuntu (Linux 6.17.0-29-generic x64)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `npx ruflo@latest init`
2. Configure OpenRouter provider in `.claude-flow/config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   providers:
     openrouter:
       enabled: true
       baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
       apiKey: sk-or-v1-...
       models:
         default: openrouter/qwen/qwen3-coder-plus
   ```
3. `ruflo agent spawn --type coder --task "test"`
4. Call `agent_execute` MCP tool with the spawned agent ID

## Expected Behavior

`agent_execute` reads the provider config, routes the request through the configured provider (OpenRouter in this case), and uses the specified model.

## Actual Behavior

`agent_execute` requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment and calls Anthropic's API directly, ignoring all provider configuration.

**Error without Anthropic key:**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set in environment",
  "remediation": "Set the env var and re-run. The key is read at call time."
}
```

**Error with OpenRouter key set as Anthropic key:**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "model": "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001",
  "error": "Anthropic API error 401: authentication_error: invalid x-api-key"
}
```

## Related Observations

1. **`ruflo config providers` still shows OpenRouter as "Disabled"** even after setting `providers.openrouter.enabled = true` via `ruflo config set`. The config file is updated but the CLI doesn't reflect the change — suggests the providers command reads from a different source.

2. **`ruflo config set` doesn't write to `.claude-flow/config.yaml`** for provider settings. Values are accepted but don't appear in the config file and aren't read at runtime.

3. **`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env var is ignored** by `agent_execute`. Even when set to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, the tool still sends requests to Anthropic's endpoint.

4. **`ruflo agent wasm-prompt` CLI has a flag parsing bug** — `--agent-id` / `-a` is reported as required but rejected when provided. All flag formats fail. This blocks testing agent execution via the WASM sandbox path.

## Environment

```bash
$ ruflo doctor
✓ Version Freshness: v3.7.0-alpha.69
✓ Node.js Version: v22.22.2
✓ Claude Code CLI: v2.1.121
⚠ API Keys: No API keys found
✓ MCP Servers: 1 servers
✓ Memory Database: .swarm/memory.db (0.15 MB)
```

## Suggestion

The provider config system already has the right structure (baseUrl, apiKey, models per role). The fix would be:

1. Have `agent_execute` read from the provider config instead of hardcoding Anthropic
2. Support OpenAI-compatible API format (since OpenRouter, Together, Groq, vLLM, Ollama all use it)
3. Map model names from Ruflo's internal format to the provider's format
4. Fix the `config set` command to actually persist provider settings to the YAML config

This would unlock Ruflo for users who don't have Anthropic subscriptions but want to use Claude Code + Ruflo with alternative providers.

title: [verification] HIGH: witness manifests report missing=95 drift=2 on all three platforms
body:
## Summary

The 12-hour scheduled verification run (2026-05-19T07:08:18Z, commit `c292e5fcf563b1639ea2ce7842c8f4a110c3ad39`) found that all three witness manifests (macOS, Linux, Windows) report `missing=95 drift=2`. The Ed25519 manifest signature itself is valid — the manifest has not been tampered with — but 95 artifacts it references are absent from the working tree and 2 known artifacts have drifted from their signed hash.

## Impact

The verification runner cannot confirm the integrity of 95 dist-layer files (MCP tool bundles, CLI command modules, security/memory packages). These are the files that users and downstream tooling consume. If the artifacts are absent in a deployed or published context, MCP tool calls that depend on them will fail at runtime with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

In a bare source-only checkout (no `npm run build`) this is expected behaviour — but the scheduled check runs in such an environment and the spec requires `missing=0 drift=0`. CI environments that run `npm ci && npm run build` before `verify.mjs` would pass.

## Expected

```
Summary: pass=N drift=0 regressed=0 missing=0
Ed25519 signature valid: yes
```

## Actual (all three manifests — macOS, Linux, Windows — identical)

```
Manifest signature:
  hash matches:                    yes
  public key reproducible:         yes
  Ed25519 signature valid:         yes

Summary: pass=16 drift=2 regressed=0 missing=95
```

## Sample of missing artifacts

```

v3/@claude-flow/embeddings/dist/transformers-loader.js
```
