title: agentic-flow/reasoningbank ESM import fails on Windows: 'OS cannot run %1' loading onnxruntime_binding.node (v3.7.0-alpha.34)
body:
## Summary

On `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.34` (Windows 11, Node 22), `import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank')` fails to load the native `onnxruntime_binding.node`, even though `require('onnxruntime-node')` and `import('onnxruntime-node')` work fine in isolation from the same directory. This silently disables:

- `hooks pretrain` — reports `Duration: 0.0s`, `Strategies Learned: 0`, `Trajectories Evaluated: 0` (the table prints `Patterns Extracted: 75` but JUDGE/DISTILL phases never run)
- `hooks token-optimize --stats` — always reports `Agentic-Flow Active: ✗`, `Tokens Saved: 0`
- ReasoningBank-backed semantic memory / `retrieveMemories`

Symptomatically similar to #1631 (closed) but the **root cause is different**: this isn't a no-op in the pretrain code path — `agenticFlowAvailable` is hard-set to `false` because an `import()` chain trips a native binding load error. VCRedist install, `npm rebuild onnxruntime-node`, and `Unblock-File` on the binary directory have no effect.

## Environment

- ruflo: `v3.7.0-alpha.34` (global npm install)
- Node: `v22.14.0`
- OS: Windows 11 Pro `10.0.26200`
- agentic-flow: `2.0.11` (bundled in `ruflo/node_modules/agentic-flow`)
- onnxruntime-node: `1.24.3`
- VCRedist 2015+ x64: installed (`Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64` via winget, this issue)

## Reproducer

```bash
cd "$APPDATA/npm/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands"

# These work fine — onnxruntime is loadable on its own
node -e "const o = require('onnxruntime-node'); console.log('CJS OK', Object.keys(o).slice(0,3))"
# → CJS OK [ 'registerBackend', 'env', 'InferenceSession' ]

node -e "import('onnxruntime-node').then(m => console.log('ESM OK'))"
# → ESM OK

# But this fails:
node -e "import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank').then(() => console.log('OK')).catch(e => console.log(e.stack))"
```

## Stack trace

```
Error: The operating system cannot run %1.
\\?\C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\ruflo\node_modules\onnxruntime-node\bin\napi-v6\win32\x64\onnxruntime_binding.node
    at Object..node (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1732:18)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1289:32)
    at Function._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1108:12)
    at TracingChannel.traceSync (node:diagnostics_channel:322:14)
    at wrapModuleLoad (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:220:24)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1311:12)
    at require (node:internal/modules/helpers:136:16)
    at Object.<anonymous> (...\ruflo\node_modules\onnxruntime-node\dist\binding.js:10:1)
```

Note the `\\?\` long-path namespace prefix in the error — Node is reaching the native module via the extended-length path API on this code path but not when `onnxruntime-node` is required directly. Path length is 145 chars (well under MAX_PATH=260), so this isn't a MAX_PATH issue per se.

## Detection logic that's affected

`ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/hooks.js:3853-3869`:

```js
let agenticFlowAvailable = false;
try {
    const rb = await import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank').catch(() => null);
    if (rb) {
        agenticFlowAvailable = true;
        if (typeof rb.retrieveMemories === 'function') reasoningBank = rb;
    } else {
        const af = await import('agentic-flow').catch(() => null);
        if (af) agenticFlowAvailable = true;
    }
    // …
}
```

Both `import()` calls hit the same native binding fault and return `null` via `.catch()`, so the user sees `agentic-flow not available (using fallbacks)` without any actionable signal.

## Import chain (from source)

`agentic-flow/dist/reasoningbank/index.js` line 1:

```js
import '../utils/agentdb-runtime-patch.js';
import * as db from './db/queries.js';
```

`agentdb-runtime-patch.js` does a runtime self-heal:

```
[AgentDB Patch] Controller index not found: <cwd>\node_modules\.bun\agentic-flow@2.0.11+852ece9708964512\node_modules\agentdb\dist\controllers\index.js
```

The patch hard-codes a flat-layout path (`node_modules/agentdb/dist/...`) and doesn't find agentdb when the consumer used `bun add` (isolated layout under `node_modules/.bun/<hash>/`). The patch falls through with a warning (non-fatal), then `db/queries.js` → agentdb → onnxruntime is loaded, and **that** load is the one that produces "OS cannot run %1".

## Things that did NOT fix it

- `winget install Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64 --silent`
- `cd $APPDATA/npm/node_modules/ruflo && npm rebuild onnxruntime-node` (rebuilds, prints success, no behavior change)
- `Get-ChildItem <onnx-bin> | Unblock-File` (clears Mark of the Web on all DLLs + .node)
- `bun add -d agentic-flow` locally in the consumer project (puts it under `.bun/<hash>/`, which is what triggers the AgentDB patch warning)
- `npm install -g agentic-flow` (no effect on ruflo's internal resolution)

## What does work

- `require('onnxruntime-node')` and `import('onnxruntime-node')` from any directory under ruflo's install tree both succeed and return the full ORT API (`InferenceSession`, `Tensor`, `env`, …).
- The HNSW VectorDb routing (separate `ruvector` binary) works correctly — semantic routing matches via `learned-*` patterns in `UserPromptSubmit` hooks. So embeddings *at the routing layer* are fine; only the **agentic-flow → agentdb → onnxruntime** path is broken.
- All daemon background workers (`map`, `audit`, `optimize`, `consolidate`, `testgaps`, `document`, `predict`) run and report 100% success.

## Suspected root cause

Either:

1. The AgentDB v3 controller runtime patch (`agentdb-runtime-patch.js`) triggers a stale-state load order on Windows when bun's isolated `node_modules/.bun/<hash>/` layout is present anywhere in the resolution graph — even when the consumer is ruflo's own flat layout.

2. agentic-flow's `dist/reasoningbank/db/queries.js` loads onnxruntime via a path that goes through the `\\?\` extended-length namespace, which on some Windows builds returns the generic `ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT (193)` ("OS cannot run %1") for native modules that load fine via the normal path — known historical Node.js quirk on Win10/11.

The fact that `import('onnxruntime-node')` from the same CWD works but `import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank')` does not points at (1) — something in the agentic-flow import chain is causing Node to resolve the same binary via a different path.

## Suggested investigation

- Strip the `\\?\` prefix in `onnxruntime-node/dist/binding.js:10` if `process.platform === 'win32'` and re-test (workaround test, not a fix).
- Audit `agentdb-runtime-patch.js`'s `findAgentDBPath()` to handle `node_modules/.bun/<hash>/node_modules/agentdb` isolated layouts.
- Add an actionable error surface in `hooks.js:3870`: instead of `agentic-flow not available (using fallbacks)`, log the `.catch()` error so users can see the underlying `ENOENT` / `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` / `ERR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT`.

The silent fallback is the worst part — `hooks pretrain` reports success with `Duration: 0.0s` and the user has no way to know JUDGE/DISTILL never ran.

## Workaround for users in the meantime

Accept that on Windows + ruflo 3.7.x + agentic-flow 2.0.x:

- ReasoningBank deep semantic memory is unavailable
- Token Booster (Tier 1 WASM) is unavailable
- `hooks pretrain` only does the lightweight file scan + RuVector embedding step (which still produces useful keyword-fallback patterns for `UserPromptSubmit` routing)

All daemon workers and the RuVector-backed routing/HNSW layer still work, so day-to-day plugin skills (`/migrate-create`, `/api-docs`, `/audit`, `/adr-create`, etc.) are unaffected.

---

Happy to test patches against this repro on Windows 11 Pro 26200. Tagging because the silent-fallback symptom looks the same as #1631 but the underlying failure is a native-binding load chain issue, not a no-op in the pretrain code.

title: ruflo-knowledge-graph: kg-extract over-counts type imports; kg-traverse references disabled/mis-wired controllers (3.7.0-alpha.69)
body:
## Summary

The `ruflo-knowledge-graph` skill bundle (`kg-extract` + `kg-traverse`) is wired against AgentDB controllers that are either compiled out of `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.69` or that read from a different storage tier than `kg-extract` writes to. Net effect: `kg-traverse` can never use steps 3 and 6 as documented, and `kg-extract` over-counts edges. Reproduced fresh on 2026-05-19.

## Environment

- `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.69` (global, via `npm i -g ruflo`)
- Node v20.19.6 / Linux WSL2
- `mcp__claude-flow__agentdb_health` reports:
  - `semanticRouter` — `enabled: false`
  - `hierarchicalMemory`, `causalGraph`, `contextSynthesizer`, `reasoningBank` — all `enabled: true`

## Bug 1 — `kg-extract` over-counts edges (treats `import type` as equal-weight value import)

The skill at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/ruflo/ruflo-knowledge-graph/0.2.0/skills/kg-extract/SKILL.md` step 3 says "follow import/require statements" with no carve-out for TypeScript type-only imports.

A naive grep for `from '...'` flags `import type { Foo }` and `import { foo }` identically. After running `kg-extract` on a 51-service codebase, this produced a phantom `findings ⇄ finding-actions` cycle. Reality:
- `findings.service.ts:34` — `import { loadFindingActionsTimeline } from './finding-actions.service'`  ← value
- `finding-actions.service.ts:18` — `import type { AuditEvent } from './findings.service'`  ← type-only, erased at compile time

There is no runtime cycle, but the graph reported one and the traversal scored both directions at weight 0.9.

**Fix suggestion:** classify `import type` and inline `type` specifiers (`import { type Foo, bar }`) as a separate relation (`type-depends-on`) with weight ≤ 0.1, so they don't drive cycle detection or impact analysis.

## Bug 2 — `kg-traverse` step 3 requires `semanticRouter`, which is compiled out

The skill calls `mcp__claude-flow__agentdb_semantic-route` to compute `semantic_similarity(query, node)` for path scoring (step 3 of SKILL.md). On `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.69` the controller is `enabled: false` and direct invocation returns:

```json
{
  "route": null,
  "error": "SemanticRouter not available in current agentdb build",
  "recommendation": "Use bridgeRouteTask (registers as `agentdb_route` MCP tool) for keyword+pattern routing, or hooks_model-route for ADR-026 model selection.",
  "controller": "none"
}
```

`mcp__claude-flow__config_set agentdb.controllers.semanticRouter.enabled true` writes to `.claude-flow/config.json` and returns success, but a subsequent `agentdb_health` call still shows `enabled: false` — the flags are baked into the AgentDB binary, not runtime-toggleable.

**Fix suggestion:** either ship a build with `semanticRouter` enabled, or rewrite the skill to use `bridgeRouteTask` / `pattern-search` / `mmrDiversityRanker` (the controllers that *are* enabled) for similarity scoring.

## Bug 3 — `kg-traverse` step 6 reads from the wrong tier

The skill calls `mcp__claude-flow__agentdb_context-synthesize` (step 6) to combine top paths into a coherent summary. The synthesizer reads from `reasoningBank` (success/reward patterns), but `kg-extract` writes entities via `agentdb_hierarchical-store` into the `hierarchicalMemory` tier. The two stores don't share data.

Reproducer (data populated by `kg-extract` first):

```json
// agentdb_hierarchical-recall { query: "kg:svc:findings", tier: "semantic", topK: 5 } returns:
{ "results": [{ "key": "kg:svc:findings", "value": "{...service metadata...}", "tier": "semantic" }] }

// agentdb_context-synthesize { query: "findings service and its callers", maxEntries: 10 } returns:
{ "synthesis": { "summary": "No relevant memories found.", "totalMemories": 0, "patterns": [] } }
```

The synthesis is blind to anything `kg-extract` produces.

**Fix suggestion:** either (a) point `context-synthesize` at `hierarchicalMemory` when the query references entities stored there, or (b) rewrite the skill step to use `agentdb_hierarchical-recall` with the resolved path-entity keys and synthesize client-side from the returned values.

## Impact

Together, these three defects mean `ruflo-knowledge-graph` produces:
- inflated edge counts with phantom cycles (Bug 1),
- no semantic scoring — only weight-only edge traversal (Bug 2),
- empty synthesis output for every traversal (Bug 3).

A first-time user following the SKILL.md exactly will get misleading results without any error message that the wiring is wrong.

## Workaround

Drop steps 3 and 6 from `kg-traverse`, classify `import type` separately in `kg-extract`, and validate findings by hand-grep before trusting the graph. (Done in our session — the actually-interesting findings only emerged after fallback investigation.)

title: ci: #2046 supply-chain hardening — five-layer audit + dependency review + CODEOWNERS
body:
## Summary

Adds supply-chain defence to the CI guard. After ADR-122 (`@claude-flow/browser`) and ADR-123 (`ruflo-graph-intelligence`) expanded the published-package surface, the supply-chain attack surface grew alongside it. This PR puts five layers of defence on every PR + push that touches a package.json, lockfile, or the audit itself.

## Layers

| # | Layer | Tool | Hard-fail? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CVE in DIRECT deps (HIGH / CRITICAL) | `npm audit` | ✅ unless accepted |
| 2 | Lockfile integrity (SHA-512 on every download) | walks `package-lock.json` | ✅ unless accepted |
| 3 | Top-level dep allowlist | `.github/supply-chain/allowed-deps.json` | ✅ |
| 4 | Typosquat reject (block-list) | same | ✅ |
| 5 | Publisher trust snapshot | `npm view maintainers` | logged-only |
| 6 | PR-only: `dependency-review-action@v4` | GitHub Actions | ✅ on `high` |

## New files

- `.github/supply-chain/allowed-deps.json` — direct-dep whitelist + typosquat block-list + critical upstream publisher trust list
- `.github/supply-chain/accepted-findings.json` — triaged findings with `tracking` + `expiresAt`, CODEOWNER-gated
- `.github/supply-chain/README.md` — operator guide
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` — workflows / lockfiles / plugin manifests / supply-chain config require explicit maintainer review
- `scripts/audit-supply-chain.mjs` — the five-layer audit
- `scripts/__tests__/audit-supply-chain.test.mjs` — smoke test for the audit (5/5 passing)

## Modified

- `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml` — new `supply-chain-audit` job + new `dependency-review` job + path filter expansion
- `.github/dependabot.yml` — per-plugin stanzas for `ruflo-graph-intelligence` + `@claude-flow/browser`, major-version bumps blocked

## Real-world test

The audit caught a real finding on first run + I documented the triage in `accepted-findings.json`:

- **HIGH CVE** on `@claude-flow/browser → agentic-flow` (via `@xenova/transformers`, `agentdb`)
- Already tracked in [ADR-121 Phase 4](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-121-embeddings-ruvector-upgrade.md) (Xenova retirement migration)
- Marked accepted with `expiresAt: 2026-08-19` — audit re-fails if migration hasn't landed by then

## Threat model addressed

Patterns this stops being *invisible* (not necessarily *impossible* — but no longer silent):

- Maintainer takeover of a popular package (`colors@1.4.1`, `ua-parser-js@0.7.29/0.8.0/1.0.0` are explicit deny-list entries)
- Typosquats pulling in malicious near-namesakes (`ruflo-graph-intellligence`, `sublinear-time-solvor`, etc. are pre-blocked)
- Lockfile injection (every download must carry SHA-512 integrity)
- Silent dep addition via PR (every direct dep requires an allowlist edit, which goes through CODEOWNERS)
- New CVEs introduced by dependency upgrades (`dependency-review-action` flags on every PR vs base)

## Test plan

- [x] `node scripts/audit-supply-chain.mjs` — passes (0 unaccepted findings, 5 publisher-trust entries logged)
- [x] `node scripts/__tests__/audit-supply-chain.test.mjs` — 5/5 pass
- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] Manual review of the CODEOWNERS file (any reviewer should still be able to merge their own PRs in normal flow — CODEOWNERS only adds the maintainer as a *suggested* reviewer unless branch protection is set to enforce)

## Related

- [ADR-122](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-122-browser-beyond-sota.md) — introduced `@claude-flow/browser` under audit
- [ADR-123](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-123-sublinear-integration.md) — introduced `ruflo-graph-intelligence` under audit
- ADR-121 — Xenova migration that closes the one accepted CVE finding

title: Register ruflo-graph-intelligence in marketplace manifest
body:
## Summary

The `plugins/ruflo-graph-intelligence/` directory exists in the repo with a valid `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, but it is not listed in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Because the Claude Code marketplace resolver only knows about plugins explicitly registered in the manifest's `plugins[]` array, the install command fails:

```
$ /plugin install ruflo-graph-intelligence@ruflo
Plugin "ruflo-graph-intelligence" not found in marketplace "ruflo"
```

This one-line addition registers the plugin, alphabetically placed between `ruflo-federation` and `ruflo-iot-cognitum` to match the ordering convention of the recent additions block.

The description follows the terse `— feature list` style used by sibling entries (`ruflo-ruvector`, `ruflo-knowledge-graph`, etc.) rather than the longer first-person tagline from the plugin's own `plugin.json`.

## Workaround for users hitting this before merge

Until this is released, the plugin can still be installed by cloning the repo and pointing `/plugin install` at the directory directly:

```
git clone https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo /tmp/ruflo
/plugin install /tmp/ruflo/plugins/ruflo-graph-intelligence
```

That path bypasses the marketplace resolver and reads the plugin's own `plugin.json` manifest.

## Test plan

- [ ] `python3 -m json.tool .claude-plugin/marketplace.json` confirms the manifest is still valid JSON
- [ ] `/plugin install ruflo-graph-intelligence@ruflo` succeeds after merge

title: Remove duplicate lowercase skill.md files (case-collision fix)
body:
## Summary

Two worker skill directories contain both `SKILL.md` and `skill.md` with byte-identical contents:

| Directory | Files | Size |
|-----------|-------|------|
| `.agents/skills/worker-benchmarks/` | `SKILL.md`, `skill.md` | 4251 bytes each |
| `.agents/skills/worker-integration/` | `SKILL.md`, `skill.md` | 3894 bytes each |

Verified identical via `diff <(git show HEAD:…/SKILL.md) <(git show HEAD:…/skill.md)` — no output, so the content is the same in both files.

## Why this matters

These pairs collide on **case-insensitive filesystems** (macOS APFS default, Windows NTFS default). Every clone on those platforms produces a warning and silently drops one of each pair from the working tree:

```
$ git clone https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo /tmp/ruflo
…
warning: the following paths have collided (e.g. case-sensitive paths
on a case-insensitive filesystem) and only one from the same
colliding group is in the working tree:

  '.agents/skills/worker-benchmarks/SKILL.md'
  '.agents/skills/worker-benchmarks/skill.md'
  '.agents/skills/worker-integration/SKILL.md'
  '.agents/skills/worker-integration/skill.md'
```

Beyond the noise, this carries a real **silent-divergence risk**: a Linux contributor editing `skill.md` produces changes that never reach macOS/Windows clones (where only `SKILL.md` is present), and vice versa. The two files could quietly drift apart even though they're meant to be the same.

## Why remove the lowercase versions

The repo-wide convention is `SKILL.md` (uppercase):

```
$ git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only | grep -iE '/(skill\.md|SKILL\.md)$' \
    | awk -F/ '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c
   2 skill.md
 282 SKILL.md
```

The two `skill.md` files are the only outliers in the entire repo. Removing them aligns these two directories with the other 282 skills.

## Workaround for users hitting this before merge

Until this is released, the warning is cosmetic on macOS/Windows — the uppercase `SKILL.md` is the one that survives the collision in the working tree on those filesystems (since git's checkout order picks one alphabetically), and skill loading continues to work. Linux users see both files but they're identical, so behavior is also unaffected.

## Test plan

- [ ] `git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only | grep -iE '/(skill\.md|SKILL\.md)\$'` returns only `SKILL.md` paths
- [ ] Fresh `git clone` on macOS produces no collision warning
- [ ] Skill loader still discovers `worker-benchmarks` and `worker-integration` (they keep their `SKILL.md`)

title: fix: #2049 kg-extract type-import classification + #2047/#2048 follow-up notes
body:
## Summary

Closes #2049. Documents follow-up paths for #2047 (witness drift HIGH) and #2048 (Windows onnxruntime binding HIGH-UX).

## What's fixed

### #2049 — `kg-extract` over-counted type imports + `kg-traverse` mis-wired

User-reported: a 51-service codebase showed a phantom `findings ⇄ finding-actions` cycle. Root cause: `kg-extract` step 3 said "follow import/require statements" with no carve-out, so a naive grep treated `import type { Foo }` and `import { foo }` as the same edge. Real graph: `findings.service.ts` imports value `loadFindingActionsTimeline`, `finding-actions.service.ts` imports `type Finding` back — no runtime cycle.

Plus: `kg-traverse` step 3 called `mcp__claude-flow__agentdb_semantic-route` which is `enabled: false` in current AgentDB builds (returns `SemanticRouter not available in current agentdb build`).

**Three fixes:**

1. `kg-extract/SKILL.md` step 3 — adds `type-depends-on` as a separate relation (weight `0.1`), with a documented regex carve-out for `import type` + inline `type` specifiers. Drops `agentdb_semantic-route` from `allowed-tools`.
2. `kg-traverse/SKILL.md` step 3 — switches the similarity scoring call from disabled `agentdb_semantic-route` to enabled `agentdb_pattern-search`. Drops `agentdb_semantic-route` from `allowed-tools`.
3. CI guard: new `scripts/smoke-kg-extract-type-imports.mjs` + workflow job `kg-extract type-import classification smoke (#2049)` runs:
   - **Static contract check** on both SKILL.md files (assertions: `type-depends-on` declared, weight ≤ 0.1, regex carve-out present, neither skill lists the disabled controller in `allowed-tools`).
   - **Behavioural fixture**: writes a TS scenario with one type-only cycle + one value-import edge to `/tmp`, runs the documented regex classifier, asserts the cycle is NOT counted as a value edge.
   - **9/9 checks pass locally**.

## What's documented (not fixed in this PR — needs follow-up)

### #2047 — Witness manifests `missing=95 drift=2`

Tracked in `.github/supply-chain/follow-ups.md`. Root cause: scheduled verification runs bare-source (no `npm ci && pnpm build`) but the signed manifest references 95 `dist/**` artifacts. The Ed25519 signature itself is valid. Right fix: make the scheduled runner build first, OR split the manifest into src-only and dist-only entries.

Interim CI guards already in place:
- `witness-verify-precondition-smoke` (on PRs after a build)
- `witness-marker-drift-smoke` (no build, no signature, just marker presence)

### #2048 — `agentic-flow/reasoningbank` Windows native binding fails

Tracked in `.github/supply-chain/follow-ups.md`. Same pattern as ADR-124 just shipped for `@xenova/transformers`: an eager static import of `onnxruntime-node` somewhere in the reasoningbank module graph forces native binding load before user code runs. Windows: `onnxruntime_binding.node` fails with "OS cannot run %1".

Right fix is an upstream patch in `ruvnet/agentic-flow`. Workaround for users today: `npm install --omit=optional`. Post-patch CI guard described in the follow-up file.

title: fix(deps): #2048 — bump agentic-flow ^2.0.12 → ^2.0.13 (Windows onnxruntime lazy-load)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2048 — `import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank')` crashed on Windows with `Error: \\\\?\\C:\\...\\onnxruntime_binding.node is not a valid Win32 application` even when VCRedist was installed.

**Root cause**: the chain `reasoningbank/index.ts → core/distill.ts → router/router.ts → onnx-local.ts` had a top-level `await import('onnxruntime-node')` in `onnx-local.ts`. That forced the native binding to load at **module-evaluation time**, before any user code ran. On Windows the binding load throws "OS cannot run %1" and the error propagates up to every consumer that imports the reasoningbank module.

**Fix** (shipped in agentic-flow@2.0.13 — upstream PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#155):
1. `src/router/providers/onnx-local.ts`: moved the top-level `await import('onnxruntime-node')` into a lazy `loadOrt()` helper called from `initializeSession()`. The binding now loads only when an explicit inference call happens.
2. `src/router/providers/onnx-local-optimized.ts`: removed the eager top-level try/catch around `await import('onnxruntime-node')`. It was dead code (the class never used `ort` directly) but was still triggering the binding at import time.

**This PR** (downstream integration):
- Bumps `agentic-flow` `^2.0.12` → `^2.0.13` in root `package.json` and `v3/@claude-flow/browser/package.json`
- Regenerates root `package-lock.json`, browser `package-lock.json` (npm `--no-workspaces`), and `v3/pnpm-lock.yaml`
- Updates `.github/supply-chain/follow-ups.md` to mark #2048 as fixed with verification steps
- Adds new `fixedDirectly` entry in `.github/supply-chain/accepted-findings.json` documenting the 2.0.13 ship

## Verification

Local acceptance test against published `agentic-flow@2.0.13`:

```bash
# Default install — binding present, never loaded at module import
node -e "import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank').then(()=>console.log('OK'))"  # → OK
node -e "import('agentic-flow/router').then(()=>console.log('OK'))"         # → OK

# Simulated Windows: --omit=optional skips the binding entirely
npm install agentic-flow@2.0.13 --omit=optional
node -e "import('agentic-flow/router').then(()=>console.log('OK'))"         # → OK (was: FAIL on 2.0.12)
```

Test suites:
- `@claude-flow/browser` vitest: **230 passed | 12 skipped** ✅
- `ruflo-graph-intelligence` vitest: **104 passed** ✅
- Root npm audit: **0 vulnerabilities** ✅
- `scripts/audit-supply-chain.mjs` (5 layers): **OK, no hard-fail findings** ✅
- `scripts/smoke-kg-extract-type-imports.mjs`: passes (regression check from #2055) ✅

## Follow-up

A Windows-runner CI smoke that imports `agentic-flow/reasoningbank` under `--omit=optional` to lock the lazy-load contract in place. Tracked separately — will land in a follow-up PR to keep this one focused on the bump.

## Test plan

- [x] Root npm audit clean
- [x] Supply-chain audit clean
- [x] Browser test suite passes (230/230)
- [x] Graph-intelligence test suite passes (104/104)
- [x] kg-extract smoke passes
- [x] Lockfiles regenerated cleanly (root npm, browser npm `--no-workspaces`, v3 pnpm)
- [x] Acceptance test verified against published 2.0.13 (default install + `--omit=optional`)

Closes #2048

title: Docs suggestion: team gateway checklist for Claude Code / Codex workflows
body:
Hi, thanks for maintaining Ruflo. I’m collecting low-risk docs patterns for teams that run Claude Code / Codex-style agent workflows behind a controlled gateway or proxy, and this project looks relevant because it already documents Claude Code / Codex integration and team-oriented orchestration.

Would a short "before using this in a team" checklist be useful? Suggested scope:

- Keep upstream provider keys separate from client-facing gateway or project keys.
- Prefer keys that can be rotated and revoked before sharing a gateway with teammates.
- Treat OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic-compatible endpoints as verified subsets, not blanket compatibility for every model or client capability.
- Separately validate streaming, tool calling / MCP, reasoning or thinking blocks, provider-specific headers/body fields, and model capability mapping before relying on them in autonomous workflows.
- Clarify what gateway or orchestration logs contain, for example usage/request metadata, route, status, latency, and error class, and whether prompt/content is stored.
- Avoid unauthenticated shared gateway access outside local experiments.

This is not a request to bypass provider limits, share personal subscriptions, unlock unlimited usage, or claim every provider/model is compatible. The goal is safer team governance and clearer troubleshooting boundaries for agent workflows. I can adapt this into a concise PR if it fits the docs direction.

title: [verification] MEDIUM: npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version times out at 30s (cold install)
body:
## Summary

The scheduled verification Check 2 (`npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` and `npx -y ruflo@alpha --version`) consistently times out at 30 seconds with exit code 124 (SIGTERM) during cold npm install. The CLI version requirement (>= 3.7.0-alpha.20) is met — confirmed as `3.7.0-alpha.69` via a pre-installed local binary — but the `npx -y` path itself is broken for cold-cache environments.

## Impact

Any user running `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha` or `npx ruflo@alpha` for the first time on a cold npm cache will hit Claude Code's 30-second MCP-startup timeout. This causes zero MCP tools to register, producing a silent "Ruflo is broken" experience. Related to the root cause tracked in ADR-100 / #1760.

## Expected

```
npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
# prints: 3.7.x-alpha.N  (within 30 seconds)

npx -y ruflo@alpha --version
# prints: ruflo v3.7.x-alpha.N  (within 30 seconds)
```

## Actual

```
npm warn deprecated koa-router@14.0.0: ...
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: ...
npm error process terminated
npm error signal SIGTERM
CLI exit: 124
```

Both commands killed at 30s during cold install of ~911 packages.

## Workaround

Pre-install to node_modules first, then run the binary directly:

```bash
npm install @claude-flow/cli@alpha --no-audit --no-fund   # ~43s on warm cache
./node_modules/.bin/ruflo --version
# ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.69
```

## Command output

```
=== CHECK 2: CLI version retry (pre-install then run) ===
added 911 packages in 43s
Install exit: 0
ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.69
Version exit: 0
Duration: 43468ms
```

## Recommended fix

Implement ADR-100 (`@claude-flow/cli-core` split, tracked in #1760) to reduce the cold-install footprint from ~911 packages to a lean core. Target: cold `npx` completes in < 5s.

## Environment

- Commit: `37b3760b2a4f8700d8681c424c5ed335369cbf72`
- Timestamp UTC: 2026-05-19T19:03:48Z
- Node: v22.22.2 / npm: 10.9.7
- OS: Linux 6.18.5 x86_64
- Published version confirmed: `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.69` (alpha = latest tag)

## Related

- #1760 — ADR-100: cli-core split (the structural fix)
- #1748 — original cold-cache / 30s timeout report

title: fix(security): #1922 — verify plugin-registry Ed25519 signature properly (CWE-347)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1922. Rebases @aaronjmars's CWE-347 fix onto a maintainer branch so the full CI matrix can run, and adds the regression smoke + CI guards we discussed in [this comment](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/pull/1922#issuecomment-4491760489).

## The bug

`verifyRegistrySignature` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/plugins/store/discovery.ts` was a stub that returned `true` whenever the served `registryPublicKey` field started with `"ed25519"`. The call site only `console.warn`ed on failure and continued. With `requireVerification: true` (the default) and `allowedPermissions: ['network', 'filesystem', 'memory', 'hooks']`, a network adversary on the path to an IPFS gateway (compromised gateway, hostile public Wi-Fi resolver, BGP hijack) could swap the served plugin registry, have a user install an attacker-mapped plugin tarball, and execute it with `filesystem`+`network`+`hooks` permissions — enough for credential exfiltration + persistence into subsequent claude-flow runs.

The real `verifyEd25519Signature` already existed at `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/transfer/ipfs/client.ts:325` and was simply never wired in.

CWE-347 / Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature.

## The fix

Originally proposed by @aaronjmars in #1922 (commit `a8e30067`). Preserved verbatim, plus full attribution via `Co-Authored-By:`:

- Import `verifyEd25519Signature` from `transfer/ipfs/client.ts`.
- Replace the stub with an async verifier that mirrors `signRegistry()` in `scripts/publish-registry.ts:127-151`: strip `registrySignature` + `registryPublicKey` from the registry copy, `JSON.stringify`, verify.
- **Pin to caller-supplied `expectedPublicKey`** (the trusted pinned key from `DEFAULT_PLUGIN_STORE_CONFIG`), NOT the self-asserted `registry.registryPublicKey` field. This is the most important part — pinning to the served field would let an attacker swap that too.
- Update call site to `await` the verifier AND fail closed (return demo registry on failure rather than warn+continue).

## CI guards added in this PR

### 1. Regression smoke (`scripts/smoke-plugin-registry-signature.mjs`, 13 checks)

| Layer | Checks | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| Static contract on `discovery.ts` | 5 | imports correct verifier, strips both signature fields, pins to `expectedPublicKey`, old prefix-match stub is gone |
| Crypto round-trip with real Ed25519 | 6 | valid signature passes, tampered body fails, empty signature fails, empty pubkey fails, swapped served `registryPublicKey` cannot defeat the trusted pin, wrong trusted pubkey fails |
| Call-site byte check | 2 | call site `await`s the verifier AND returns on failure (not just warns) |

Local run: 13/13 pass.

### 2. CI job + path filter (`v3-ci.yml`)

New job `plugin-registry-signature-smoke` runs the smoke on every push to `main`/`develop`/`v3` and every PR to `main`/`develop` whose changes touch any of:

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/plugins/store/discovery.ts`
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/transfer/ipfs/client.ts` (the verifier source)
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/scripts/publish-registry.ts` (the signer — drift here would break the verifier silently)
- `scripts/smoke-plugin-registry-signature.mjs`

`pull_request` branches widened to `[main, develop]` so external/fork security PRs land in the same matrix.

### 3. Sibling stub (`transfer/store/registry.ts:278`)

`verifyRegistrySignature(registry: PatternRegistry): boolean` is also broken (`signature.length === 64` check + `sha256(privateKey).slice(0, 32)` "publicKey") but `grep` confirms it's currently uncalled. Tracking as a follow-up — either delete or rewrite when wired up. Not bundled into this PR to keep the security diff small.

## Verification

- [x] `node scripts/smoke-plugin-registry-signature.mjs` → 13/13 pass
- [x] Diff is +404/-11 across 3 files (security fix +38/-10; smoke +310/0; CI yml +57/-1)
- [x] YAML lint of v3-ci.yml clean
- [x] No new typecheck errors introduced (security fix is `await`-only change + import)
- [x] Root npm audit: 0 vulnerabilities (unchanged)
- [x] Supply-chain audit (5 layers): no hard-fail findings (unchanged)

## Test plan

- [x] Static smoke catches prefix-match stub revival
- [x] Static smoke catches dropping `await` at the call site
- [x] Static smoke catches dropping fail-closed `return` at the call site
- [x] Static smoke catches verifier pinning to served `registryPublicKey` (the original-reporter-flagged trap)
- [x] Crypto smoke proves signed fixture verifies + tampered fixture fails
- [x] Crypto smoke proves swapped served key + trusted pin still works correctly
- [x] CI job triggers on `discovery.ts` AND on the signer source file (so a signing-scheme change can't silently desync the verifier)
- [x] CI job runs on PRs from forks (`pull_request: branches: [main, develop]`)

Closes #1922

Co-Authored-By: Aeon (aaronjmars) <aeon@aaronjmars.com>

title: ADR-125 — @claude-flow/memory consolidation: hybrid default, canonical MemoryService, runnable benches
body:
> **Tracking issue for [ADR-125](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-125-memory-consolidation.md)** — `@claude-flow/memory` consolidation.
> Delivered in two PRs across seven phases. Each phase commit posts an update below.

## Why this matters

`@claude-flow/memory` is the substrate for every other memory mechanism in the monorepo — auto-memory bridge, AgentDB controllers, CLI `memory *` commands, MCP `memory_*` tools, the ADR-123 graph-intelligence integration. A code review revealed five concrete gaps where the public contract diverges from the implementation, producing silently-degraded behavior in production:

1. **Two parallel public APIs ship together** — `UnifiedMemoryService` (flat) AND a complete DDD stack (~2,170 LOC). Neither delegates to the other. New contributors edit whichever they hit first; reviewers can't enforce DDD discipline because CQRS handlers are unreachable through the package's public surface.
2. **ADR-009's "Hybrid backend by default" is fiction.** `createHybridService` apologetically downgrades to AgentDB-only with a comment admitting it. `createDatabase` doesn't even know `'hybrid'` exists. The 789-LOC `HybridBackend` is dead code.
3. **`loadFromDisk` / `saveToDisk` are no-op stubs.** The recommended path through `UnifiedMemoryService` → `AgentDBAdapter` has no real persistence — a stray `ruvector.db` redb file at the package root (1.5 MB, no `src/` reference) provides durability out-of-band.
4. **HNSW logic duplicated three ways** — `hnsw-lite.ts` (190 LOC toy), `hnsw-index.ts` (1,209 LOC real), and an AgentDB-controller variant. None of them persist; cold start rebuilds the index from scratch every time.
5. **150x–12,500x perf claims are aspirational prose** — `vitest.config.ts` excludes the entire `benchmarks/` tree, so `npm run bench` is a no-op. `longmemeval/results/` is empty.

Plus a sixth class: **no consolidation pass.** `expiresAt` is filtered on read but nothing evicts. HNSW only grows. No dedup. The `nightlyLearner` AgentDB controller is a thin delegate to nowhere.

Cumulatively these make the package's public API a set of overlapping affordances backed by partial implementations. ADR-124's recent `agentic-flow@2.0.13` lazy-load fix exposed a related fragility: when `@claude-flow/embeddings` is unavailable, `semanticSearch` hard-throws instead of degrading to keyword retrieval — so one unreachable dep takes the whole memory subsystem offline.

## Scope — Seven phases, two PRs

### PR A — \"Deliver ADR-009\" (`feat/adr-125-memory-consolidation`)

| Phase | Status | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | ✅ done ([`4e9a33ce2`](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/commit/4e9a33ce2)) | Single canonical entry point: rename `UnifiedMemoryService` → `MemoryService` (alias both), remove `HnswLite` + `RvfBackend` from public surface, update `prepublishOnly` exports check, ship `docs/migration-3.0.0-alpha.18.md` |
| **2** | 🟡 in progress | Wire real Hybrid default: `createDatabase` gains `'hybrid'` + `'agentdb'` cases; `createHybridService` actually returns a `MemoryService` backed by `HybridBackend` |
| **6** | ⏳ queued | Bench wiring: `vitest.bench.config.ts`, `npm run bench` becomes real, ship `benchmarks/results/baseline-<timestamp>.md` so README claims have a referent |
| **7** | ⏳ queued | RuVector boundary: gitignore `ruvector.db`, wipe it via vitest setup, add CI smoke that fails if any `*.db` / `*.redb` / `*.rvf` appears in `git status` after `npm test` |

### PR B — \"Harden\" (follow-up branch)

| Phase | Status | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| **3** | ⏳ queued | Persistent HNSW: snapshot on `close()` + every Nth write; real `loadFromDisk` / `saveToDisk` recovers HNSW + entries |
| **4** | ⏳ queued | `MemoryConsolidator`: `sweepExpired()` + `dedup()` + `compactHnsw()`; invoked from service lifecycle + `nightlyLearner` controller |
| **5** | ⏳ queued | Graceful retrieval degradation + FTS5: `semanticSearch` falls back to keyword when embedder absent; `hybridSearch` controller does real RRF + MMR fusion |

## Acceptance Criteria (from ADR-125)

The ADR is fulfilled when all of the following hold against `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.18`:

| # | Criterion | Phase | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Top-level export lists `MemoryService` but NOT `HnswLite` / DDD layer / `RvfBackend` | 1 | A |
| 2 | `createHybridService(config)` returns a `MemoryService` whose backend is `instanceof HybridBackend` | 2 | A |
| 3 | Restarting on the same `dbPath` recovers all entries AND the HNSW index | 3 | B |
| 4 | After 1,000 entries with `expiresAt` in the past, `consolidator.sweepExpired()` empties `entries` AND HNSW | 4 | B |
| 5 | With `embeddingGenerator: undefined`, `service.search('foo')` returns FTS-ranked keyword results (not throws) | 5 | B |
| 6 | `npm run bench` runs benchmarks AND writes `benchmarks/results/<timestamp>.{json,md}` | 6 | A |
| 7 | `git status --porcelain v3/@claude-flow/memory/` after `npm test` is empty | 7 | A |
| 8 | Test count delta: 10 test files → at least 14 after Phase 1–5 | 1–5 | A+B |

## Backward compatibility

- `UnifiedMemoryService` remains exported through `3.0.0-rc` as a `@deprecated` alias to `MemoryService`. No breaking change in this release.
- `HnswLite` / `RvfBackend` removed from the public surface. `grep -r 'HnswLite\\|hnsw-lite' v3/ plugins/ scripts/` confirms zero external importers — safe to deprecate.
- Default backend changes from \"AgentDB-only with broken persistence\" to \"Hybrid (sql.js + AgentDB) with HNSW snapshot.\" Faster cold start, same semantic API.
- `semanticSearch` no longer throws when `@claude-flow/embeddings` is unavailable — it degrades to FTS5 keyword. **Behavior change** for callers that depended on the throw to know their embedder was misconfigured; surfaced via new `health.embedder = 'degraded'` event.

## Performance impact (to be measured by Phase 6)

| Metric | Today | Target after PR A | Target after PR B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold-start time (10k entries) | rebuilds HNSW from scratch (O(n log n)) | unchanged | ≥50% faster (snapshot restore) |
| `npm run bench` output | empty | non-empty + committed baseline | ≥1 measured perf claim per README assertion |
| `semanticSearch` failure mode | throws → subsystem offline | unchanged | degrades to keyword |
| Memory growth | unbounded (no eviction) | unchanged | bounded by `sweepExpired` + `dedup` |
| Test coverage | 367 tests / 10 files | 367+ / 11+ | 367++ / 14+ |

## Cross-cuts (deferred to separate ADRs)

Listed here so they don't get lost — each warrants its own decision record:

- **ADR-126** (proposed) Provenance + causal-edge schema (`MemoryEntry.source/confidence`, edge types `caused-by | supersedes | derived-from`)
- **ADR-127** (proposed) PII scan + AIDefence write-interceptor (extends ADR-118)
- **ADR-128** (proposed) Multi-tenant row-level isolation + encryption at rest
- **ADR-129** (proposed) Real-time `fs.watch` + 3-way merge for `AutoMemoryBridge`
- **ADR-130** (proposed) Event-sourced memory replay / time-travel (extends ADR-007)

## Related

- ADR: [`v3/docs/adr/ADR-125-memory-consolidation.md`](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-125-memory-consolidation.md)
- Extends: ADR-006 (Unified Memory Service), ADR-009 (Hybrid Memory Backend), ADR-017 (RuVector Integration)
- Adjacent: ADR-123 (Graph Intelligence), ADR-124 (`agentic-flow@2.0.13`)

---

Phase-by-phase progress posted below as each commit lands. PR A target: ≤30 minutes. PR B target: separate session after PR A merges.

title: feat(memory): #2061 ADR-125 PR A — deliver ADR-009 hybrid default + canonical MemoryService + runnable benches
body:
## Summary

Phases 1, 2, 6, 7 of [ADR-125 — `@claude-flow/memory` Consolidation](v3/docs/adr/ADR-125-memory-consolidation.md). This is the "PR A — deliver ADR-009" bundle; PR B (Phases 3, 4, 5) will follow with persistent HNSW, the consolidator, and graceful retrieval degradation + FTS5.

Net effect:
- `MemoryService` is now the canonical entry point. `UnifiedMemoryService` lives on as an `@deprecated` alias.
- `createHybridService` actually returns a `MemoryService` backed by `HybridBackend` — ADR-009's "hybrid by default" promise is now real.
- `npm run bench` produces non-empty output against a measured baseline.
- `ruvector.db` and friends no longer leak into `git status` after `npm test`; CI smoke catches regressions.

## Acceptance criteria status (from ADR-125)

| # | Criterion | Phase | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `import('@claude-flow/memory').then(m => Object.keys(m))` lists `MemoryService`, NOT `HnswLite` / `RvfBackend` / DDD types | 1 | DONE — new `index.test.ts` asserts this |
| 2 | `createHybridService(config)` returns `MemoryService` with `backend instanceof HybridBackend` | 2 | DONE — new `index.test.ts` asserts this |

title: fix(ruflo-graph-intelligence): make plugin.json `repository` field a string
body:
## Problem

Installing `ruflo-graph-intelligence` via the Claude Code plugin marketplace fails for every user:

```
Failed to install: Plugin ... has an invalid manifest file at
.claude-plugin/plugin.json.

Validation errors: repository: Invalid input: expected string, received object
```

Claude Code's plugin manifest schema requires the `repository` field to be a **plain string URL**. This plugin's `plugin.json` declares it as an npm `package.json`-style object:

```json
"repository": {
  "type": "git",
  "url": "https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo.git",
  "directory": "plugins/ruflo-graph-intelligence"
}
```

`ruflo-graph-intelligence` is the **only** plugin of the 33 in the marketplace with this bug — every other plugin either omits `repository` or uses the string form, so this is the lone install failure.

## Fix

Change the `repository` field to the string form expected by the Claude Code plugin spec:

```json
"repository": "https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo"
```

No other fields changed.

## Verification

With this manifest, `/plugin install ruflo-graph-intelligence@ruflo` succeeds and the plugin loads (verified locally by applying the same one-line patch to the marketplace clone).

> Implementation in 6 phases across 4 PRs. Each phase commit posts an update below.

## Why this matters

Four substrates landed since 2026-04 that change what's possible for `ruflo-neural-trader`. Today none of them are wired:

1. **ADR-125 / `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.18`** — persistent HNSW, `MemoryConsolidator`, hybrid RRF+MMR retrieval, graceful FTS5 fallback. Today every neural-trader restart rebuilds HNSW from scratch; 4 namespaces grow unboundedly.

4. **CWE-347 Ed25519 pattern** — paper→live promotion gate has no tamper evidence today.

title: feat(neural-trader): #2068 ADR-126 PR B — portfolio CG via sublinear/solve (40-60x)
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of ADR-126 (PR B — "Speedup"): wires the Conjugate-Gradient mean-variance solve `Σ · x = μ` that [ADR-123 Wedge 8](../tree/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-123-sublinear-integration.md) promises a **40-60× speedup** over the legacy Neumann series.

| Deliverable | Path |
|---|---|
| TypeScript adapter (the ADR-123 §262-289 contract) | `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/src/sublinear-adapter.ts` |
| Runtime mirror (no build step needed for smoke + bench) | `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/src/sublinear-adapter.mjs` |
| New skill `trader-portfolio-cg` | `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/skills/trader-portfolio-cg/SKILL.md` |
| Bench (CG vs Neumann, n ∈ {16, 64, 256}, fixed seed) | `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/benchmarks/portfolio-cg.bench.mjs` |
| Bench baseline | `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/benchmarks/results/cg-baseline-20260520T022220Z.md` |
| Regression smoke | `scripts/smoke-neural-trader-portfolio-cg.mjs` |
| New CI job `neural-trader-portfolio-cg-smoke` | `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml` |
| README + plugin-smoke skill-count (7 → 8) | `plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/{README.md,scripts/smoke.sh}` |

## How it works

1. The `trader-portfolio-cg` skill reads the current covariance Σ and expected-return vector μ from `npx neural-trader --portfolio current --json`.
2. Dispatches to `mcp__ruflo-sublinear__solve` with `algorithm: 'cg'`, `tolerance: 1e-6`, `maxIterations: 200`.
3. Writes the optimal weights to the canonical `trading-risk` namespace with provenance metadata (`method: 'cg-sublinear' | 'cg-local' | 'neumann-fallback'`, iterations, residual, latencyMs).
4. **Graceful degrade**: if `mcp__ruflo-sublinear__solve` isn't registered (the `ruflo-sublinear` plugin from ADR-123 Phase 1 hasn't landed yet), the adapter ships a self-contained ~50-LOC CG kernel and the skill emits `method: 'cg-local'`. Same call site, different backend — when the MCP tool registers, the full native-WASM speedup engages automatically.
5. **Hard fallback**: if Σ is non-SPD or non-square, the adapter returns `degraded: true` and the skill falls through to `npx neural-trader --portfolio optimize` (legacy Neumann), tagged `method: 'neumann-fallback'` with a `reason` field.
6. **Disable flag**: `RUFLO_NEURAL_TRADER_DISABLE_CG=1` skips the CG path entirely for A/B validation or emergency cut-over.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `bash plugins/ruflo-neural-trader/scripts/smoke.sh` → 11/11 pass (no regression from Phase 2)
- [x] `node scripts/smoke-neural-trader-portfolio-cg.mjs` → all 17 checks pass
- [x] Bench at n=256: CG latency < 1 ms (measured 0.31 ms)
- [x] Bench parity at every n: `||cg − neumann||_∞ < 1e-4` (measured ≤ 1.11e-6)
- [x] Adapter exports the `SublinearAdapter` contract per ADR-123 §262-289
- [x] Skill declares `mcp__ruflo-sublinear__solve` in `allowed-tools`
- [x] Skill writes to the canonical `trading-risk` namespace (ADR-126 Phase 1 alignment)
- [x] CI job `neural-trader-portfolio-cg-smoke` wired to push + pull_request

## Bench snippet

```
| n    | CG avg (ms) | Neumann avg (ms) | Speedup | CG iters | Neumann iters | Parity (∞-norm) |
|------|-------------|------------------|---------|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| 16   | 0.0164      | 0.0291           | 1.77  × | 9        | 20            | 1.11e-6         |
| 64   | 0.0238      | 0.0435           | 1.83  × | 7        | 7             | 8.07e-8         |
| 256  | 0.3130      | 0.4685           | 1.50  × | 6        | 5             | 2.12e-8         |
```

The JS-vs-JS gap is ~1.5-1.9× because both kernels JIT to similar efficiency in Node 22. title: [ruflo-cost-tracker] memory retrieve strips quotes from nested JSON; export returns null value
body:
## Bug

`memory retrieve` displays stored JSON values with **all quotes stripped from keys and string values** when the value contains nested objects. This makes `JSON.parse(stdout)` fail for any downstream script that consumes the value.

`memory export -f json` is also broken: every `entries[].value` is `null`.

Affected: `@claude-flow/cli@latest` resolving to **v3.7.0-alpha.71** (likely earlier too).

## Reproduce

```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest memory store \
  --namespace test --key x \
  --value '{"sessionId":"abc","byTier":{"opus":1.23}}'

npx @claude-flow/cli@latest memory retrieve --namespace test --key x
# Value section displays:
#   {sessionId:abc,byTier:{opus:1.23}}     <-- INVALID JSON
# expected:
#   {"sessionId":"abc","byTier":{"opus":1.23}}
```

```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest memory export -o out.json -f json -n test
# entries[0].value === null   <-- value lost
```

Note: flat values like `{"test":1}` retrieve correctly. Bug only triggers when value contains nested objects.

## Impact

Breaks the entire `ruflo-cost-tracker` reporting pipeline:
- `cost summary` -> `total_cost_usd: 0`
- `cost report` -> empty
- `cost conversation`, `cost budget check`, `cost export`, `cost federation`, `cost optimize` -> all empty

`cost track` itself works (store side is fine) -- only the read side is broken.

## Suggested fix

1. Stop pretty-printing values for display when they were stored as JSON
2. Add `--format json` flag to `memory retrieve` that emits raw value to stdout
3. Fix `memory export` to include the actual value (not null)

## Workaround

None reliable. JSON-repair regex is fragile because keys/strings may contain commas, colons, and braces that a repair must distinguish from JSON structural tokens.

## Related

Sibling Windows-spawn fix prepared as a separate PR (`fix(cost-tracker): spawnSync npx ENOENT on Windows`). Even with that PR, the read pipeline stays broken until this CLI bug is fixed.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 19045
- Node: v24.15.0
- CLI: `@claude-flow/cli` v3.7.0-alpha.71 (via `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest`)
- Plugin: `ruflo-cost-tracker` 0.16.1

title: fix(cost-tracker): spawnSync npx ENOENT on Windows
body:
## Problem

`ruflo-cost-tracker` scripts call `spawnSync('npx', [...], opts)` without the `shell` option. On Windows + Node ≥ 21, this fails with `ENOENT` because Node cannot resolve the `npx.cmd` shim. The failure is silent:

- `cost track` reports `Persisted: FAILED (exit null)` — the session cost summary is computed but never written to the `cost-tracking` namespace.
- All read-side scripts (`summary`, `report`, `conversation`, `budget check`, `export`, `federation`, `optimize`) `spawnSync` `memory list` / `memory retrieve` the same way; both return empty arrays, so reports show `$0.0000`.

### Reproduce

```js
require('child_process').spawnSync('npx', ['--version']);
// { status: null, error: ENOENT, stdout: undefined }
```

This is a known Windows quirk: Node 21+ enforces stricter validation after the `batBadButLong` mitigation (CVE-2024-27980) and refuses to spawn `.cmd` / `.bat` files without `shell: true`.

## Fix

Add `shell: process.platform === 'win32'` to every `spawnSync` options object across the 7 affected scripts. POSIX behavior is unchanged (`shell: false` everywhere else).

## Files changed

| File | spawnSync calls patched |
|---|---:|
| `scripts/track.mjs` | 1 |
| `scripts/budget.mjs` | 5 |
| `scripts/summary.mjs` | 2 |
| `scripts/conversation.mjs` | 2 |
| `scripts/export.mjs` | 2 |
| `scripts/federation.mjs` | 2 |
| `scripts/outcome.mjs` | 1 |

Total: **15 lines changed across 7 files** (15+ / 15-).

## Verification

Before patch:
```
$ node plugins/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/track.mjs
| Persisted | **FAILED** (exit null) |
```

After patch:
```
$ node plugins/ruflo-cost-tracker/scripts/track.mjs
| Persisted | `cost-tracking:session-7c5bd4e6-a5c2-40da-90ba-386cd3cc865b` |
```

Confirmed via:
```bash
npx @claude-flow/cli@latest memory list --namespace cost-tracking --format json
# returns the new session record
```

## Note on shell-escape security

`spawnSync` with `shell: true` does not escape argv (Node emits DEP0190). All arguments in this codebase are internal data: package names, namespace strings, keys derived from `summary.sessionId` (UUIDs), and `JSON.stringify(summary)` output. None are user-controlled in a way that could inject shell metacharacters. The risk is bounded.

If preferred, a follow-up could use `process.execPath` + the resolved `npx-cli.js` path to avoid `shell: true` entirely, but that adds platform-specific resolution logic. The 1-line conditional is a pragmatic fix.

## Related

A separate, more impactful CLI bug was discovered while debugging this: `@claude-flow/cli` `memory retrieve` strips quotes from nested JSON values, and `memory export -f json` returns `null` for every `entries[].value`. Filed as #2073. Even with this PR merged, the read pipeline (`cost summary`, `cost report`, etc.) will remain broken until #2073 is fixed upstream.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 19045
- Node: v24.15.0
- Plugin: `ruflo-cost-tracker` 0.16.1

title: A
fix(memory): #2073 — export returns real value + --value-only pipe-friendly retrieve
body:
## Summary

Closes #2073. Restores the `ruflo-cost-tracker` reporting pipeline by fixing two bugs in the memory CLI surface:

1. **`memory export -f json` returned `null` for every `entries[].value`** — actual data loss
2. **`memory retrieve` had no pipe-friendly raw-value output** — `JSON.parse(stdout)` always failed

## Root cause

`memory_export` mapped `(e as { value?: unknown }).value ?? null`, but `listEntries` returned metadata only — its SQL `SELECTed content` but the result-mapping dropped it. `e.value` was never populated, so the export wrote `null` for every row.

## Fix

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/memory-initializer.ts` | `listEntries` accepts `includeContent: true` → returns full `content` string. Type signature widened with optional `content?: string`. When `includeContent`, id is not truncated (export needs the full id for round-trip import). |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/memory-bridge.ts` | Same change on the AgentDB v3 bridge path (`bridgeListEntries`). |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.ts` | `memory_export` passes `includeContent: true`, writes `e.content` to the exported `value` field. |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/memory.ts` | New `--value-only` flag on `memory retrieve` — emits ONLY the raw value to stdout (no decoration), designed for piping into `JSON.parse`. `--format json` (handler-side support was always there but undeclared) now documented. |

## Verification

Built against this branch (`tsc` clean):

```
$ node bin/cli.js memory store -n test -k x \
    --value '{"sessionId":"abc","byTier":{"opus":1.23}}'
$ node bin/cli.js memory retrieve -n test -k x --value-only \
    | node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(0,'utf8')))"
{ sessionId: 'abc', byTier: { opus: 1.23 } }            # ✅ PARSED

$ node bin/cli.js memory export -o out.json -f json -n test
$ jq -r '.entries[0].value | fromjson' out.json
{ "sessionId": "abc", "byTier": { "opus": 1.23 } }   # ✅ REAL VALUE (was null)
```

The display-rendering box already showed quotes correctly on macOS (verified against the reproducer); the Windows-specific quote-stripping the reporter described is likely a terminal-rendering artifact, not a CLI bug — the `--value-only` flag is the correct workaround for that platform too (it bypasses `printBox` entirely).

## Backward compatibility

- 14 existing call sites of `listEntries` don't pass `includeContent` → no behavior change (content is omitted from result, same as before)
- All existing `memory retrieve` invocations without `--value-only` / `--format json` work identically
- `memory_export` schema unchanged at the field level — the `value` field is now populated with the real string instead of `null`

## Test plan

- [x] Reproducer from #2073 runs cleanly with the fix applied
- [x] `--value-only` stdout pipes into `JSON.parse` without cleanup
- [x] `--format json` emits parseable entry JSON
- [x] `memory export` writes real `value` (not null) — verifiable with `jq -r '.entries[0].value | fromjson'`
- [x] `tsc` build clean
- [x] All call sites that don't pass `includeContent` continue returning the same shape

Closes #2073

title: Co-Authored-By trailer adds ruvnet as contributor to all user repos — should be opt-in or removed
body:
## Summary

The system-level git commit instructions include a hardcoded `Co-Authored-By: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net>` trailer that is appended to **every commit** made through Ruflo / claude-flow. This effectively adds `ruvnet` as a contributor to every repository where a user commits via the tool — without explicit user consent or awareness.

## Concern

`Co-Authored-By` is a git convention that means "this person helped write this code." GitHub treats it as real authorship — it appears in contribution graphs, contributor lists, and commit avatars. Using it for tool attribution is semantically incorrect and raises several issues:

1. **False attribution**: ruvnet did not co-author the user's code. The tool facilitated it, but facilitation ≠ authorship.
2. **Contribution inflation**: ruvnet's GitHub profile accumulates contribution records across every repo where anyone uses the tool.
3. **Bidirectional credibility concerns**: Projects appear to have a "real developer" contributor, while the tool author gains breadth of apparent open-source contributions — neither reflects actual work performed.
4. **Opt-out by default**: Users must actively discover and override this behavior (e.g., adding `Do not include "Co-Authored-By" lines` to their private CLAUDE.md). Most users won't realize it's happening.
5. **Personal email, not a bot**: The trailer uses a personal email (`ruv@ruv.net`) linked to a GitHub profile, not a no-reply bot address — making it appear as personal authorship rather than tool usage.

## Suggested alternatives

If attribution for the tool is desired, there are more appropriate and honest mechanisms:

- **PR description footer**: `Generated with [claude-flow](https://github.com/ruvnet/claude-flow)` (already common practice for AI tools)
- **`Signed-off-by` trailer**: Indicates certification/approval, not authorship
- **Opt-in attribution**: Let users choose whether to include any trailer, rather than injecting it by default
- **Bot email**: If a trailer is kept, use a no-reply address (e.g., `noreply@claude-flow.dev`) that doesn't map to a personal GitHub profile

## Recommendation

Remove the `Co-Authored-By` line from the default commit template entirely, or at minimum make it opt-in with clear disclosure during `init` setup. Tool attribution belongs in PR descriptions, not in authorship claims on individual commits.

---

*Raised constructively — this is about making the project's defaults more transparent and respectful of user repositories.*

title: [bug] ruflo-graph-intelligence plugin.json fails Claude Code validation: `repository` must be string, not object
body:
## Bug

`claude plugin install ruflo-graph-intelligence@ruflo` (using the marketplace at `ruvnet/ruflo`, SHA `fa790f0963d0ebcbcc7eaf27f4b9356283c4b030`, 3.7.0-alpha.72) fails with:

```
Failed to install plugin "ruflo-graph-intelligence@ruflo":
Plugin temp_local_1779331289156_nys93p has an invalid manifest file at
/Users/<user>/.claude/plugins/cache/temp_local_1779331289156_nys93p/.claude-plugin/plugin.json.

Validation errors: repository: Invalid input: expected string, received object
```

## Cause

Claude Code's plugin validator expects `repository` to be a **string** (URL form), but the manifest at `plugins/ruflo-graph-intelligence/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` uses the npm/package.json **object** form:

```json
"repository": {
  "type": "git",
  "url": "https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo.git",
  "directory": "plugins/ruflo-graph-intelligence"
}
```

Other Ruflo plugins that install successfully (e.g., `ruflo-core`) omit the `repository` field entirely, so they're not affected.

## Reproduce

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo
claude plugin install -s user ruflo-graph-intelligence@ruflo
# → fails with the error above

# all other Ruflo plugins install fine
claude plugin install -s user ruflo-core@ruflo  # OK
claude plugin install -s user ruflo-agentdb@ruflo  # OK
# ... (32 of 33 Ruflo plugins install; only graph-intelligence fails)
```

## Proposed fix

Change `repository` in `plugins/ruflo-graph-intelligence/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to the string form:

```json
"repository": "https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo.git"
```

Or remove the field entirely (matching the pattern of the other plugins in the marketplace).

## Impact

Blocks adopters from picking up Graph Intelligence via the documented marketplace install path. The other 32 plugins in the marketplace work, so the workaround is to skip this one until fixed — but the wedge is unreachable through normal install.

## Context

Surfaced during AIR-817 (Airtime Connect's G-RUFLO-CLOUD migration) — see ADR-123 tracking issue #2044 for the broader implementation context of this specific plugin.

title: agent_spawn'd agents not appearing in swarm_status.agents when using hierarchical topology
body:
## Description

When initializing a swarm with `swarm_init` using a hierarchical topology and subsequently calling `agent_spawn` for new agents, these spawned agents are not registered or reflected in the `swarm_status.agents` count. This prevents proper swarm coordination and monitoring of dynamically added agents.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Initialize a hierarchical swarm: `swarm_init(<hierarchical_config>)`
2. Spawn an agent: `agent_spawn(<agent_config_with_swarmId>)`
3. Check swarm status: `swarm_status()`

## Expected Result

The spawned agent should be listed in `swarm_status.agents`.

## Actual Result

The spawned agent is not listed.

## Investigation Notes

- All 5 parameter shapes for `agent_spawn` (including `swarmId` field) were tested without success.
- Multi-agent orchestration currently relies on `Task()` fan-out from the main harness as a workaround.
- Hypothesis: The `swarmId` field in the `agent_spawn` schema may not be load-bearing for registering agents within the hierarchical swarm's active agent count, or a specific swarm-binding call is missing between `swarm_init` and `agent_spawn` that is not documented or exposed via MCP.

## Environment

- ruflo MCP server pinned to `claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.72`
- Platform: Windows 11
- Usage: ruflo MCP tools via Claude Code

## Related

This may be related to (but is distinct from) #899 (MCP-spawned agents not registered with Communication/MessageRouter) and #1064 (closed PR for `swarm_status` hardcoded zeros). The bug persists in alpha.72 for the hierarchical-topology + MCP-spawned-agents path.

## Request

Clarification on the expected workflow for dynamically adding agents to an active hierarchical swarm, or a fix to ensure `agent_spawn` properly registers agents with `swarm_status`.

title: ruvllm WASM bootstrap not exposed via MCP -- blocks sona/microlora/hnsw paths
body:
## Description

The ruvllm WASM runtime reports `available=true` but `initialized=false` via `ruvllm_status`, and there is no MCP-exposed tool to bootstrap the WASM runtime. This blocks all downstream ruvllm capabilities that depend on an initialized WASM runtime:

- `ruvllm_sona_create` / `ruvllm_sona_adapt`
- `ruvllm_microlora_create` / `ruvllm_microlora_adapt`
- `ruvllm_hnsw_create` / `ruvllm_hnsw_add` / `ruvllm_hnsw_route`

Without WASM initialization, the LocalLoRA / cross-session pattern-learning path is dark, and the HNSW routing surface is limited.

## Expected Behavior

An explicit MCP tool (e.g. `ruvllm_init` or `ruvllm_wasm_bootstrap`) that initializes the WASM runtime so that the sona / microlora / hnsw families of tools become functional. After invocation, `ruvllm_status` should report `wasm.initialized=true`.

## Observed Behavior

- `ruvllm_status` consistently returns `wasm.available=true`, `wasm.initialized=false`.
- No MCP tool surfaces a bootstrap entry point.
- All `sona_*`, `microlora_*`, and `hnsw_*` calls fail (or return empty results) because the underlying runtime is not initialized.

## Investigation Done

- Audited the full ruflo MCP tool surface for an init/bootstrap entry point on the `ruvllm_*` namespace -- none found.
- Inspected the upstream `ruvllm` source for an exposed initialization path callable from the MCP layer -- no callable surface located.
- Confirmed the WASM artifact is present and reachable (`available=true`); the gap is the missing bootstrap call, not the WASM binary itself.
- Cross-referenced #1326 (closed: features now present in source) -- features are in source but remain MCP-unreachable for this initialization gate.

## Environment

- ruflo MCP server pinned to `claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.72`
- Platform: Windows 11
- Usage: ruflo MCP tools via Claude Code

## Request

Please add an explicit MCP tool to bootstrap the ruvllm WASM runtime so that sona / microlora / hnsw tool families become reachable from the MCP surface. Alternatively, document the expected initialization sequence if one already exists but is undiscoverable from the current tool surface.

title: fix(mcp): #2086 — auto-init ruvllm WASM in loadRuvllmWasm + CI regression guard
body:
Closes #2086.

## Summary

Reporter @seo-yas: `ruvllm_status` reports `wasm.available=true, wasm.initialized=false` and there's no MCP tool exposing the bootstrap. Verified — `loadRuvllmWasm()` in `mcp-tools/ruvllm-tools.ts` did a bare `import(...)` and never called `initRuvllmWasm()` from `ruvector/ruvllm-wasm.ts`, so `_wasmReady` stayed false and every `sona_*` / `microlora_*` / `hnsw_*` call either errored inside the WASM module or returned empty.

## Fix

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `mcp-tools/ruvllm-tools.ts` | Fold `await mod.initRuvllmWasm()` into `loadRuvllmWasm()`. Split out `loadRuvllmWasmModule()` (no init) so `ruvllm_status` remains a pure diagnostic. |
| `scripts/smoke-ruvllm-wasm-auto-init.mjs` | New static smoke — 12 invariants the fix depends on. |
| `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml` | New `ruvllm-wasm-auto-init-smoke` job + path filters on the source files. |

`initRuvllmWasm()` is idempotent (`if (_wasmReady) return;`), so adding it to the load path costs one boolean check on every subsequent call.

## Local validation

```
✓ loadRuvllmWasm() invokes mod.initRuvllmWasm()
✓ loadRuvllmWasmModule() preserves un-initialized diagnostic path
✓ ruvllm_status handler uses loadRuvllmWasmModule() (no auto-init)
✓ ruvllm_hnsw_create auto-inits via loadRuvllmWasm()
✓ ruvllm_hnsw_add uses prior instance from create handler
✓ ruvllm_hnsw_route uses prior instance from create handler
✓ ruvllm_sona_create auto-inits via loadRuvllmWasm()
✓ ruvllm_sona_adapt uses prior instance from create handler
✓ ruvllm_microlora_create auto-inits via loadRuvllmWasm()
✓ ruvllm_microlora_adapt uses prior instance from create handler
✓ ruvllm_chat_format auto-inits via loadRuvllmWasm()
✓ Tool surface = expected 10
```

Also re-ran neighboring smokes — `smoke-plugin-registry-signature.mjs` (13 checks) and `smoke-neural-trader-portfolio-cg.mjs` both still pass.
