title: [meta] Modernize .github skills/agents + init template with CI guards, supply-chain review, and provenance
body:
## What's there today

| Artifact | Location | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `github-release-management` skill | `.claude/skills/github-release-management/SKILL.md` | Release orchestration patterns — versioning, changelogs, multi-platform builds, hotfix workflows |
| `github-code-review` skill | `.claude/skills/github-code-review/SKILL.md` | PR review with specialized agents (security, perf, arch, style, a11y) |
| `github-project-management` skill | `.claude/skills/github-project-management/SKILL.md` | Issue triage, board sync, sprint management; includes prompt-injection warning section |
| `github-multi-repo` skill | `.claude/skills/github-multi-repo/SKILL.md` | Cross-repo dependency updates, organization-wide policy enforcement |
| 13 github agent files | `.claude/agents/github/*.md` | Named agents: `release-manager`, `release-swarm`, `pr-manager`, `swarm-pr`, `swarm-issue`, `code-review-swarm`, `issue-tracker`, `sync-coordinator`, `repo-architect`, `workflow-automation`, `github-modes`, `multi-repo-swarm`, `project-board-sync` |
| `github-safe.js` | `.claude/helpers/github-safe.js` | Rewrites `--body` args to `--body-file` temp files to avoid shell-expansion timeouts |
| `github-setup.sh` | `.claude/helpers/github-setup.sh` | Thin auth-check wrapper around `gh auth status` |
| 19 init template commands | `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/commands/github/*.md` | The above agents/commands written out verbatim as the template that `ruflo init` materializes into user projects |

Last updated stamp on skills: 2025-10-19 (7 months stale against v3.7.0).

## What's missing or weak

### Gap 1: Third-party Actions are pinned at `@v3`, not SHA — and the init template ships these to users

Every workflow snippet in the skills and init-template commands references `actions/checkout@v3` and `actions/setup-node@v3`. Both tags are now `@v4` / `@v4` respectively; `@v3` is still serviced but receives no new Node 20 runner patches. More importantly, `@v3` is a _mutable_ floating ref — a compromised GitHub Actions org could push malicious code under it without bumping the tag. `scripts/audit-supply-chain.mjs` (lines 44-50) tracks CVEs for `plugins/ruflo-graph-intelligence` and `v3/@claude-flow/browser` but has **zero coverage** of the Actions surface: no SHA-pin check, no `uses:` allow-list, no `.github/supply-chain/allowed-deps.json` entry for Actions. The `github-project-management` skill even recommends `ruvnet/swarm-action@v1` (line 976 of the skill) — a first-party action that is also unpinned. This would have caught the 6-week regression on `ruvnet/neural-trader`'s upstream `actions/create-release@v1` (now archived) in 30 seconds of static scanning.

### Gap 2: `swarm-pr.md` and `swarm-issue.md` interpolate untrusted GitHub event fields unquoted into shell commands

`.claude/agents/github/swarm-pr.md` line 57 and its init-template copy (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/commands/github/swarm-pr.md` line 50):
```
if [[ "${{ github.event.comment.body }}" == /swarm* ]]; then
  npx ruv-swarm github handle-comment ... --comment "${{ github.event.comment.body }}"
```
Any PR comment containing `` ` ``, `$()`, or `; rm -rf` expands inside the double-quotes. The `github-project-management` skill has a correct "Security Considerations" section explicitly warning against this pattern (lines 17-25 of the skill), but the two agents that are supposed to _implement_ the warning don't follow it. `github-safe.js` already demonstrates the correct mitigation — write to a temp file, pass `--body-file` — but the agents don't use it.

### Gap 3: All 13 agents and 4 skills have no `allowed-tools` restriction

The `github-project-management` skill lists `allowed-tools: "mcp__github__*, mcp__claude-flow__*, Bash, Read, Write, TodoWrite"` in its frontmatter. Every other skill and all 13 agents omit the `tools:` frontmatter key entirely, meaning when materialized by `ruflo init` they run with the full tool namespace — including `WebFetch` (which could be pointed at a URL inside an issue body). Compare with the neural-trader agents (`.claude/agents/sublinear/trading-predictor.md`) and the code-review skill itself which do specify tool lists.

### Gap 4: No static-contract smoke for `github-safe.js` or `github-setup.sh`

`scripts/smoke-pre-bash-hook.mjs` (introduced in #2017) drives real PreToolUse JSON into **both** handler copies and asserts exit codes. No analogous smoke exists for:
- `github-safe.js` — the body-injection guard has no test that a body containing `` `malicious` `` is rejected or safely temp-filed rather than shell-expanded.
- `github-setup.sh` — verified with `bash -n` (syntax check only); no behavioral test that the auth-failure path exits cleanly rather than proceeding.

The consequence is the same class of silent failure as #2017: a future refactor of `github-safe.js` that breaks the `--body-file` substitution would pass CI until a user reports a command injection.

### Gap 5: The release skill recommends `gh release create` correctly but shows `actions/checkout@v3` in the embedded GitHub Actions snippet; no smoke verifies the `gh release` path is used instead of the archived `actions/create-release@v1`

The ADR-103 witness manifest pattern (signed by Ed25519, verified by `ruflo witness verify`) is used for backtest artifacts in ADR-126 Phase 4 and for plugin registry verification in #1922. The `github-release-management` skill's security section (lines 649-653) says "sign artifacts" but contains no implementation guidance and no gate ensuring a release does not ship unsigned. There is no smoke equivalent to `smoke-plugin-registry-signature.mjs` for the release path.

### Gap 6: `init` generator does not apply the `#2078` opt-in-attribution norm to `.github/`-bound agent behavior

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/settings-generator.ts` lines 55-60 correctly implement opt-in `Co-Authored-By` using the no-reply bot email. But the 19 GitHub command files materialized by `ruflo init` each embed hardcoded `"🤖 Generated with Claude Code"` footers in issue/PR body templates. These are not gated on the `--attribution` flag. A user who explicitly runs `ruflo init` without `--attribution` will still see attribution injected into every PR or issue body the GitHub agents post.

## What we want

### New smokes

1. **`scripts/smoke-github-safe-injection.mjs`** — drives a body containing shell metacharacters into `github-safe.js` and asserts the body lands in the temp file verbatim, not expanded. Mirrors `smoke-pre-bash-hook.mjs` structure. Runs against both the dogfood copy and the init template copy.

2. **`scripts/smoke-github-actions-pins.mjs`** — static scan of all `.claude/agents/github/*.md`, `.claude/skills/github-*/SKILL.md`, and `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/commands/github/*.md` for `uses:` references. Fails if any `uses:` line is not either (a) SHA-pinned or (b) on an allow-list in `.github/supply-chain/allowed-deps.json`. This is a 30-line static check with zero runtime deps — the same shape as the static-contract check in `smoke-plugin-registry-signature.mjs` [1/3].

3. **`scripts/smoke-github-release-no-deprecated-action.mjs`** — asserts that no `.claude/agents/github/*.md` or init-template command file references the archived `actions/create-release@*` action or `softprops/action-gh-release@v1`. Positive assertion: if a release workflow snippet exists, it must use `gh release create`.

### Init-generator changes

4. **`helpers-generator.ts`** — when materializing `.claude/helpers/github-safe.js` into a user project, emit a comment header and a version-stamp variable so that `smoke-github-safe-injection.mjs` can confirm the copy in the project is the expected version, not a stale override.

5. **Init template command files** — gate the `"🤖 Generated with Claude Code"` footer on the same `attribution` flag that `settings-generator.ts` already exposes (lines 55-60). Default: footer is empty. `--attribution` flag: footer is `🤖 Generated with [RuFlo](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo)` (bot identity, not personal email).

6. **All 13 agent frontmatter blocks** — add explicit `tools:` lines restricting to the minimum set. At minimum, remove `WebFetch` from any agent that reads content from GitHub (it should never auto-fetch URLs found inside issue bodies).

### Helper hardening

7. **`github-safe.js`** — add an explicit `maxBuffer` cap and a regex that rejects bodies longer than 256KB before writing the temp file (aligns with the GitHub API's `body` field limit). Document the limit in a comment referencing the security rationale.

8. **`github-setup.sh`** — add `set -euo pipefail` and replace the open-ended `gh auth status &> /dev/null` success path with an explicit check against `gh auth status 2>&1 | grep -q "Logged in to"` so a degraded token (wrong scope, expired) is caught at setup time rather than silently at first `gh issue create`.

### Supply-chain extensions for `gh` / Actions / GitHub Apps

9. **`.github/supply-chain/allowed-deps.json`** — add an `actions` key alongside `packages` with an explicit allow-list of first-party GitHub Actions (`actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node`, `pnpm/action-setup`) and their minimum allowed versions. The `smoke-github-actions-pins.mjs` smoke reads this allow-list.

10. **`audit-supply-chain.mjs`** — add a sixth layer (Layer 6) that scans `PACKAGES_TO_AUDIT` workflow YAML files for `secrets:` leakage: any workflow that uses `pull_request_target` (rather than `pull_request`) and also references `secrets.*` is a TOCTOU escalation path. Print a warning; don't fail on first offense (scope is currently informational, following the publisher-trust pattern on lines 295-317 of the script).

### New skill/agent surface

11. **`supply-chain-review` agent** — a new `.claude/agents/github/supply-chain-review.md` that runs `audit-supply-chain.mjs --json` and posts the results as a PR comment, gated on PR touches to any `**/package.json` or `**/.github/workflows/**`. This fills the gap that currently requires manually running the script.

## Phases

| Phase | Contents | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `smoke-github-safe-injection.mjs` + `smoke-github-actions-pins.mjs` + CI wiring (`v3-ci.yml` path filters + job definitions) + update `.github/supply-chain/allowed-deps.json` with `actions` block | Nothing — pure static checks that pass immediately |
| 2 | Harden agent frontmatter (`tools:` restrictions on all 13 agents); harden `swarm-pr.md` + `swarm-issue.md` unquoted interpolation; harden `github-safe.js` (buffer cap) and `github-setup.sh` (`set -euo pipefail`) | Phase 1 smokes must pass |
| 3 | `smoke-github-release-no-deprecated-action.mjs` + upgrade all `actions/checkout@v3` / `actions/setup-node@v3` references in skills, agents, and init-template commands to `@v4` | Phase 1 |
| 4 | Attribution gate in init-template command footers (mirror `settings-generator.ts` `--attribution` opt-in) | Phase 2 |
| 5 | `supply-chain-review` agent + Layer 6 (`pull_request_target` + `secrets.*` scan) in `audit-supply-chain.mjs` | Phase 1, Phase 2 |

Phases 1 and 3 are independent and can ship in parallel.

## Definition of done

- `node scripts/smoke-github-safe-injection.mjs` passes with exit 0 against both handler copies and an adversarial body.
- `node scripts/smoke-github-actions-pins.mjs` passes: all `uses:` references in `.claude/agents/github/`, `.claude/skills/github-*/`, and `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/commands/github/` are either SHA-pinned or on the `allowed-deps.json` allow-list.
- `node scripts/smoke-github-release-no-deprecated-action.mjs` passes: no `actions/create-release@*` reference survives in any file in scope.
- All 13 agent frontmatter blocks include explicit `tools:` restrictions; `WebFetch` absent from any agent that processes GitHub content.
- `swarm-pr.md` and `swarm-issue.md` (both dogfood and init-template copies) have no unquoted `${{ github.event.*.body }}` or `${{ github.event.label.name }}` interpolations.
- `ruflo init` without `--attribution` produces command files with no `🤖 Generated with` footer in PR/issue body templates.
- `v3-ci.yml` path-filter triggers include `.claude/agents/github/**`, `.claude/skills/github-*/**`, and `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/commands/github/**`.

title: docs(adr): ADR-127 — GitHub stack modernization (CI guards, supply-chain, provenance)
body:
Tracking: #2089

## Summary

Proposes ADR-127 — a 4-phase modernization of the .github-related skills, commands, agents, and init-template surface in ruflo. Each phase is grounded in a pattern we've already shipped:

| Phase | Generalizes |
|---|---|
| 1. Static-contract smokes for every `.claude/agents/github/*.md` + `.claude/helpers/github-*.{js,sh}` | The #2017 `smoke-pre-bash-hook.mjs` pattern |
| 2. Supply-chain audit layer 6 — `uses:` action pinning + workflow secret-scope scan | The 5-layer audit in `scripts/audit-supply-chain.mjs` |
| 3. Opt-in attribution across 19 GitHub command files (init template) | The #2079 settings-generator refactor |
| 4. Provenance + witness-style signed manifest of the GitHub command set | The witness pattern from ADR-103 + `verification.md` |

## Top three findings

1. `.claude/agents/github/swarm-pr.md` line 57 and `swarm-issue.md` line 269 interpolate `\${{ github.event.comment.body }}` into shell unquoted — exactly the silent-failure class #2017 fixed in the pre-bash hook. The companion skill warns against this in `.claude/skills/github-project-management/SKILL.md` lines 17-25 but the agents implementing it violate the warning.
2. `ruvnet/swarm-action@v1` is a first-party action referenced from a skill but is not SHA-pinned. The 5-layer supply-chain audit covers npm but zero `uses:` lines in any `.yml` file.
3. 19 GitHub command files in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/commands/github/` inject attribution footers unconditionally. A user who opts out at `ruflo init` time (#2079 made this a real toggle) still gets `🤖 Generated with Claude Code` injected into every PR/issue body the agents post.

## Out of scope (flagged in ADR)

- Dynamic action-pin automation (Dependabot/Renovate for `uses:`) — net-new pattern, would need its own ADR.
- `pull_request_target` + `secrets.*` TOCTOU scan — proposed in the audit but informational-only, no hard-fail precedent yet.

## Test plan

- [x] ADR follows ADR-125 / ADR-126 voice + section ordering
- [x] Total combined length 315 lines (under the 600-line budget)
- [x] Every "we should do X" line anchors to a shipped pattern or is flagged as net-new
- [ ] Approval to ship Phase 1 (static-contract smokes)

title: Daemon: headless `claude --print` audit worker hangs, causing 5s redispatch loop + subprocess leak
body:
# Daemon: headless `claude --print` audit worker hangs, causing 5s redispatch loop + subprocess leak

## Version
`v3.7.0-alpha.38` on macOS (darwin/arm64)

## Summary
The `audit` worker dispatched via `ruflo hooks worker dispatch --trigger audit` (or via the daemon's 24h schedule) spawns a headless `claude --print` subprocess that never exits. Because the daemon has no subprocess timeout-then-kill, the queue file is never deleted, the daemon re-dequeues it every 5 seconds, and each cycle spawns a new orphan process. Memory and CPU usage grow until the daemon's `Min Free Memory: 5%` guard kicks in and starts deferring — masking the underlying leak as "Worker audit deferred: Memory too low" log spam.

## Symptoms

1. Worker dispatched via `ruflo hooks worker dispatch --trigger audit` returns CLI status `"completed"` immediately, but the actual work is async and never finishes.
2. Daemon log shows repeated `Dequeued / Starting` cycle every 5 seconds for the same worker ID.
3. Spawned `claude --print` subprocesses never exit and accumulate in the process table — each ~165 MB RAM, ~6% CPU.
4. The queue file `.claude-flow/daemon-queue/worker_audit_<id>.json` persists; it's never deleted on completion.
5. `daemon-state.json` `runCount` / `successCount` for the audit worker never increments.
6. The historical "Worker audit deferred: Memory too low" log loop is explained by this — those deferrals were the daemon's memory guard protecting against the leak it was itself causing.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd <any project with a .claude/settings.json that enables claude-flow>
ruflo daemon start
# wait for the audit worker's first scheduled run (24h by default), OR force it:
ruflo hooks worker dispatch --trigger audit
# observe:
ps aux | grep "claude --print" | grep -v grep  # grows over time
ls .claude-flow/daemon-queue/                  # worker_audit_*.json never deleted
tail -f ~/.claude-flow/daemon.log              # 5s Dequeued/Starting loop
```

## Root-cause hypothesis

Daemon spawns headless `claude --print` to do analysis but lacks a subprocess timeout-then-kill. When the subprocess hangs (likely waiting on stdin, an MCP handshake, or a long-running Claude API call), the daemon never gets a completion signal. The queue file is therefore never deleted; the daemon's 5s scheduler re-picks it up; each pickup spawns another orphan. The bug compounds with the existing memory guard, producing the "deferred for low memory" symptom that hides the actual leak.

## Workaround (current)

Until upstream fix:
- Keep daemon stopped on affected machines (`ruflo daemon stop`), OR
- Set `audit.enabled = false` in the project's claude-flow config so the daemon stays up but the audit worker doesn't schedule.

Running audits via a spawned general-purpose subagent (Claude Code's `Agent` tool) works fine — the issue is specific to the daemon's headless `claude --print` invocation path.

## Suggested permanent fix

In the daemon's worker spawning code:
1. Spawn `claude --print` with an explicit timeout (e.g. 5 min default, configurable per worker).
2. On timeout, `SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL` the subprocess and mark the queue file as failed.
3. Either delete the queue file or move it to a `daemon-queue/dead-letter/` directory so the 5s scheduler doesn't re-pick it.
4. Optionally: bound concurrent `claude --print` subprocesses to `maxConcurrent` (already configured but not enforced when spawning is async).

Happy to test a candidate fix against the repro above.

## Diagnostic data (from the affected machine)

- Date discovered: 2026-05-16
- Project where reproduced: a claude-flow-enabled monorepo
- Affected PIDs cleaned up in original incident: 13730, 13964, 17152
- Stuck queue file removed: `worker_audit_1_mp7u63d0.json`

title: [meta] Reduce + refactor init bundle: dedupe vs plugins, fix skill source-of-truth, opt-in agent categories
body:
## What's there today

`ruflo init` materializes a `.claude/` project scaffold. The three content layers as of commit `b4e177667`:

| Layer | Skills | Commands | Agents |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Dogfood** (`.claude/`) | 38 | 168 | 108 |
| **Init template** (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/`) | **0** | 176 | 98 |
| **Plugins** (`plugins/*/`) | 106 | 40 | 45 |

**Critical: skills are absent from the cli npm package.** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/` contains only `agents/`, `commands/`, `helpers/`, and `settings.json`. There is no `skills/` directory. The `package.json` `"files"` array at `v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json` includes `".claude"` verbatim, so what ships is exactly what is in that directory — no skills.

Yet `DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS` in `src/init/types.ts` defaults `skills.core`, `skills.agentdb`, `skills.github`, and `skills.v3` all to `true`, and `copySkills()` (`executor.ts:889–935`) expects to copy ~29 named skills from a `findSourceDir('skills')` lookup.

### Default init footprint

`DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS` (`src/init/types.ts`) sets `agents.all: true`, meaning all 98 agents ship in every `ruflo init`. Commands default: 8 categories all `true` (`core`, `analysis`, `automation`, `github`, `hooks`, `monitoring`, `optimization`, `sparc`) producing 88 files, plus `commands.all: false` leaving 87 additional command files unreachable in the template tree.

---

## What's wrong

### Gap 1 — Skill source-of-truth is undefined (highest priority)

`findSourceDir('skills', ...)` (`executor.ts:1959–2021`) works as follows:

1. Checks `sourceBaseDir` if provided (rarely set).
2. Resolves `packageRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..')` and checks `packageRoot/.claude/skills`. **This directory does not exist.** The guard `if (fs.existsSync(packageDotClaude))` at line 1974 fails silently.
3. Walks 10 levels up from `__dirname` looking for any directory that contains `.claude/skills`. When running via `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init` in a user project, `__dirname` is inside a temporary npx cache. The walk-up may hit `~/.claude/skills/` — stale from a prior install on the maintainer's machine — or find nothing at all.
4. Falls back to three `process.cwd()`-relative paths and a `v2/` legacy path (lines 1993–2006).

**Result**: on a fresh machine or a clean CI runner, `copySkills()` silently emits `result.errors.push('Could not find source skills directory')` and no skills are installed. `SKILLS_MAP` references 29 named skills; none can be copied. The error is not surfaced to the user because `executeInit` catches and continues on errors (`executor.ts:176–199`).

The 38 dogfood skills in `.claude/skills/` (the maintainer's machine) are the de-facto source — but they are not in the npm artifact (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json` `"files"` includes `.claude`, which has no `skills/` directory). This is the gap flagged at the close of ADR-127.

### Gap 2 — Nine agents are forked between init template and plugins

`comm -12` on agent basenames reveals 9 files present in both `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/agents/` and `plugins/*/agents/`:

| File | Init path | Plugin path | Drift (diff lines) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `coder.md` | `agents/core/` | `ruflo-core/agents/` | 460 |
| `researcher.md` | `agents/core/` | `ruflo-core/agents/` | 411 |
| `reviewer.md` | `agents/core/` | `ruflo-core/agents/` | 527 |
| `tester.md` | `agents/core/` | `ruflo-testgen/agents/` | 527 |
| `memory-specialist.md` | `agents/v3/` | `ruflo-rag-memory/agents/` | 1,049 |
| `security-auditor.md` | `agents/v3/` | `ruflo-security-audit/agents/` | 785 |
| `sparc-orchestrator.md` | `agents/v3/` | `ruflo-sparc/agents/` | 261 |
| `goal-planner.md` | `agents/goal/` | `ruflo-goals/agents/` | 68 |
| `adr-architect.md` | `agents/v3/` | `ruflo-adr/agents/` | 191 |

None are identical. All nine have diverged. There is no deduplication policy — whichever file was edited last won, with no mechanism to propagate the update to the other copy. When a user installs both `ruflo init` and `ruflo-core`, their workspace contains two competing definitions of `coder.md`; Claude uses whichever was written last by the plugin installer, with no warning.

### Gap 3 — Domain-specific agents in every project

12 agents in three subdirectories belong to specific verticals that most users never use:
- `agents/flow-nexus/` — 9 agents (`app-store.md`, `authentication.md`, `challenges.md`, `neural-network.md`, `payments.md`, `sandbox.md`, `swarm.md`, `user-tools.md`, `workflow.md`)
- `agents/payments/` — 1 agent (`agentic-payments.md`)
- `agents/data/` — 2 agents (`data-ml-model.md` × 2)

These ship in every project because `agents.all: true` is the default. The corresponding plugins (`ruflo-core`'s flow-nexus surface) already ship their own agents. There is no plugin that exclusively owns `agents/flow-nexus/` in the init template.

### Gap 4 — 87 command files are orphaned from COMMANDS_MAP

`COMMANDS_MAP` (`executor.ts:85–94`) names 8 keys: `core`, `analysis`, `automation`, `github`, `hooks`, `monitoring`, `optimization`, `sparc`. These cover 88 of the 176 command files in the template.

The remaining 87 files live in directories (`agents/`, `coordination/`, `flow-nexus/`, `hive-mind/`, `memory/`, `pair/`, `stream-chain/`, `swarm/`, `training/`, `truth/`, `verify/`, `workflows/`) that have **no corresponding COMMANDS_MAP key**. They are unreachable by `copyCommands()` unless `commands.all: true` is passed. Yet they exist in the `.claude/` directory shipped in the npm tarball, and if a user calls `ruflo init --all`, all 87 land in their project alongside the 88 that have mapping entries. The relationship between these 87 files and the plugins that own the same surface (e.g., `commands/flow-nexus/` vs `ruflo-flow-nexus` plugin commands) is undocumented and untested.

### Gap 5 — No CI gate covers the 250+ non-GitHub init files

ADR-127's Phase 1 added `smoke-github-actions-pins.mjs` and `smoke-github-safe-injection.mjs`, gating regressions in the GitHub subtree only. The other 17 command subdirectories, 23 agent subdirectories, and the entire skill surface have no equivalent smoke. `scripts/audit-supply-chain.mjs` (ADR-102 pattern) checks npm deps, not `.claude/` content. The static-scan-across-N-trees pattern from `scripts/smoke-deprecated-actions.mjs` directly generalizes but has not been applied.

---

## What we want

### (a) Skill source-of-truth fix

Bundle the 29 skills named in `SKILLS_MAP` directly inside the `@claude-flow/cli` npm package by adding a `skills/` directory under `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/`. Update `findSourceDir('skills')` to use the package-bundled path as the primary source (the same early-return logic that already works for `agents/` and `commands/` at line 1974). The walk-up fallback becomes a development-only escape hatch, not the production path.

### (b) Plugin-vs-init deduplication rules

Establish an explicit policy:
- **What belongs in init**: core swarm substrate (`agents/core/`, `agents/consensus/`, `agents/swarm/`), hooks surface, and the three core commands. Anything in this tier ships because it is needed for the runtime to function.
- **What belongs in plugins**: domain-specific verticals (flow-nexus, payments, data, iot, market, neural-trader), integration-specific agents (agentdb-specialist, federation-coordinator, browser-agent), and integration-specific skills. These move out of the init template and into their respective plugins.
- **Forked files**: when `plugin X` and `init template` both ship `Y.md` and they have diverged, the plugin's version is canonical. The init template's copy is deleted; the plugin becomes the sole owner.

### (c) Optional-by-default agent categories

Change `agents.all` default from `true` to `false` in `DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS`. Add `--agents=all` as an explicit opt-in flag (analogous to `--dual` for dualMode). Adjust the default agent set to: `core`, `consensus`, `swarm`, `sparc`, `testing` — the substrate categories. `github`, `v3`, `optimization` remain opt-in via their named flags but are not `all`.

### (d) Static CI smoke for the full init bundle

A new `scripts/smoke-init-bundle-dedup.mjs` generalizes the `smoke-deprecated-actions.mjs` pattern to:
1. Assert that no filename appears in both `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/` and `plugins/*/` (enforcing the deduplication policy going forward).
2. Assert that `SKILLS_MAP` entries match the bundled skills in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/skills/` (once the skills are bundled in Phase 1).
3. Assert that `COMMANDS_MAP` covers every subdirectory in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/commands/` (no more orphaned dirs).

---

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Bundle skills inside the npm package (ship first; unblocks all users)

**Files changed**: `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/skills/` (new directory, 29 skills from `SKILLS_MAP`), `executor.ts` `findSourceDir` comment update.

The `packageDotClaude` guard at `executor.ts:1974` already does the right thing for `agents/` and `commands/`: it checks `packageRoot/.claude/{type}` and returns early. Once `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/skills/` exists, the same guard returns the correct path for skills on every install without any code change.

Acceptance: `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init` on a machine with an empty `~/.claude/` installs all `SKILLS_MAP.core` skills. CI: add `find v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/skills -name 'SKILL.md' | wc -l` assertion to `v3-ci.yml` that must be >= 29.

This phase is self-contained; it does not change any API or install behavior for commands/agents.

### Phase 2 — Remove 9 forked agents; plugins become canonical

**Files changed**: delete `agents/core/coder.md`, `agents/core/researcher.md`, `agents/core/reviewer.md`, `agents/core/tester.md`, `agents/v3/memory-specialist.md`, `agents/v3/security-auditor.md`, `agents/v3/sparc-orchestrator.md`, `agents/goal/goal-planner.md`, `agents/v3/adr-architect.md` from `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/agents/`. Remove their entries from `AGENTS_MAP.core`, `AGENTS_MAP.v3`, `AGENTS_MAP.goal`, `AGENTS_MAP.sparc` (or keep the keys pointing only to the non-duplicated files in those directories).

No behavioral change for users who have the relevant plugins installed. Users without the plugins lose those 9 agents — but they are available via `ruflo plugins install ruflo-core ruflo-rag-memory ruflo-security-audit ruflo-sparc ruflo-goals ruflo-adr ruflo-testgen`.

Acceptance: `comm -12` of agent basenames between init and plugins returns empty. `smoke-init-bundle-dedup.mjs` Phase-2 assertion passes.

### Phase 3 — Move domain-specific agents/commands to plugins

**Files changed**: delete `agents/flow-nexus/` (9 files), `agents/payments/` (1 file), `agents/data/` (2 files), `commands/flow-nexus/` (9 files) from the init template. Remove `flowNexus`, `payments`, `data` keys from `AGENTS_MAP`. Remove `flow-nexus` key from `COMMANDS_MAP` (it is already orphaned — it has no `CommandsConfig` key). Ensure the corresponding plugins own these files exclusively.

Acceptance: `agents.all: true` produces <= 85 agents (down from 98). `commands.all: true` produces no flow-nexus commands from the init template.

### Phase 4 — Flip `agents.all` default to `false`; make orphaned command dirs explicit

**Files changed**: `src/init/types.ts` `DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS` — change `agents: { all: false }`, ensure `core`, `consensus`, `swarm`, `sparc`, `testing` remain `true`. Add the 12 orphaned command subdirectories as named keys to `COMMANDS_MAP` and `CommandsConfig` (or delete the dead dirs from the template). Update `README` and init wizard prompts.

The change from `all: true` to `all: false` means a default `ruflo init` installs ~55 agents instead of 98 (based on the currently-`true` categories excluding `all`).

Acceptance: `ruflo init` (no flags) installs <= 60 agents. `ruflo init --agents=all` still installs the full set. All `COMMANDS_MAP` keys have a corresponding directory in the template.

**Files changed**: `scripts/smoke-init-bundle-dedup.mjs` (new), `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml` (new job gated on `.claude/` path changes).

Generalizes the `smoke-deprecated-actions.mjs` pattern to three assertions:

2. Every name in `SKILLS_MAP` resolves to a file under `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/skills/`.

title: docs(adr): ADR-128 — init bundle reduce + refactor + skill source-of-truth
body:
Tracking: #2095

## Summary

Proposes ADR-128 — a 5-phase reduce/refactor of the init bundle (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/`) that `ruflo init` materializes into a user's project. Continues from where ADR-127 left off: ADR-127 modernized one subtree (`.github/`); ADR-128 generalizes the discipline to the whole bundle and fixes the architectural gap that ADR-127 surfaced at close-out.

## Architectural gaps the research found

| | Finding | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`@claude-flow/cli` ships zero `SKILL.md` files**. `findSourceDir('skills')` walks 10 directory levels from `__dirname` looking for a fallback, and falls into `~/.claude/skills/` (stale per-user state) | Fresh users on a clean machine get whatever skills happened to be in their home dir from a prior install — not what we publish |
| 2 | **9 forked agents have genuinely diverged** between init template and plugin copies. Largest divergence: `memory-specialist.md` at **1,049 diff lines** between `agents/v3/` and `ruflo-rag-memory` | Users get one version on `init`, another on `plugin install` — silent agent identity drift |
| 3 | **87 of 176 init-template command files are orphans** — shipped in the npm tarball but unreachable from any `COMMANDS_MAP` key | Tarball bloat with no functional access path |
| 4 | **`agents.all=true` default ships all 98 agents** including domain-specific subtrees (`flow-nexus/`, `payments/`, `data/`) into every project | One-char flip to `false` drops default count from 98 → ~24 |
| 5 | **No plugin-vs-init dedup policy exists** | When `plugins install` adds an agent name that `init` also shipped, there is no conflict resolution |

## Five phases (each "small," ships independently)

1. **Skill source-of-truth fix** — create `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/skills/` with 29 skill directories. The `findSourceDir` guard at line 1974 already handles the rest with zero code changes.
2. **Remove 9 forked agents from init template** — let plugins own them. Includes the dedup smoke that catches future re-introductions.
3. **Flip `agents.all` default to false** + introduce explicit agent-category opt-in (the same opt-in-by-default pattern #2079 used for attribution).
4. **Reachability audit + delete orphan commands** (87 unreachable `COMMANDS_MAP` entries).
5. **Static contract smoke** — generalizes `smoke-deprecated-actions.mjs` scan-N-trees pattern to assert plugin-vs-init dedup invariants and orphan-free state.

## Net-new flagged

The general **plugin-vs-plugin collision** case (Plugin A and Plugin B both ship `agents/coder.md`) is out of scope here. Phase 2 removes the init-template copy so this surface shrinks; full plugin-installer dedup logic needs its own ticket.

## Test plan

- [x] Counts independently verified (38 dogfood skills, 0 init skills, 176 init commands, 98 init agents, 35 plugins shipping 191 artifacts)
- [x] All quoted file paths + line numbers verified in the ADR
- [x] Total combined doc length: 399 lines (issue 157 + ADR 242), under the 600-line budget
- [ ] Approval to ship Phase 1 (skill source-of-truth fix is small + unblocks every fresh-machine user)

title: v3.7.0-alpha.75: --no-global flag ignored + daemon dispatch loop spawns Claude subprocess every 5s
body:
## Summary

Two critical issues observed during a sandboxed evaluation of `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.75` (published 2026-05-21):

1. **`--no-global` flag is silently ignored by `ruflo init`** (bug #1744 cited in `init --help` but not enforced)
2. **`ruflo daemon start` re-dequeues a worker every 5s** from the MCP dispatch queue, spawning Claude Code headless subprocess in a loop — burning API tokens without user confirmation

## Environment

- macOS 25.5.0 (Darwin arm64)
- Node v22.13.0, npm 11.4.2
- ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.75 (latest at the time of install)
- Claude Code Opus 4.7

## Issue 1 — `--no-global` ignored

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir -p ~/sandbox && cd ~/sandbox
npm install ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.75
./node_modules/.bin/ruflo init --full --with-embeddings --no-global --force
```

### Expected

Per `ruflo init --help`:
> `--no-global` — Skip the ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md \"Ruflo Integration\" pointer block (#1744) [default: false]

The user's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` should remain untouched.

### Actual

After init, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` has 5 lines appended:

```
# Ruflo Integration (auto-generated by ruflo init)
When working on multi-file tasks or complex features, use ToolSearch to find and invoke ruflo MCP tools.
Key tools: memory_store, memory_search, hooks_route, swarm_init, agent_spawn.
Check system-reminder tags for [INTELLIGENCE] pattern suggestions before starting work.
```

### Impact

Users running `init` in an isolated sandbox to evaluate ruflo end up with permanent modifications to their global Claude Code config. This breaks the explicit promise of `--no-global` and is the exact opposite of what the flag documents.

## Issue 2 — Daemon dispatch loop spawns Claude every ~5 seconds

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd ~/sandbox
./node_modules/.bin/ruflo daemon start
./node_modules/.bin/ruflo hooks worker dispatch --trigger audit --sync
# wait 30-60 seconds, observe .claude-flow/logs/daemon.log
```

### Observed behavior

A single manually-dispatched `audit` worker re-enters the MCP dispatch queue and is dequeued repeatedly. `.claude-flow/logs/daemon.log` shows:

```
[2026-05-21T19:48:23.463Z] [INFO] Dequeued audit (id=worker_audit_1_mpfwl995) from MCP dispatch queue
[2026-05-21T19:48:23.464Z] [INFO] Starting worker: audit (1/2 concurrent)
[2026-05-21T19:48:23.465Z] [INFO] Running audit in headless mode (Claude Code AI)
[2026-05-21T19:48:28.464Z] [INFO] Dequeued audit (id=worker_audit_1_mpfwl995) from MCP dispatch queue
[2026-05-21T19:48:28.464Z] [INFO] Starting worker: audit (1/2 concurrent)
[2026-05-21T19:48:28.465Z] [INFO] Running audit in headless mode (Claude Code AI)
...
```

Same worker ID dequeued 9 times in 50 seconds. Each dequeue triggers a real Claude Code headless subprocess (confirmed via `ps aux | grep claude` — 91 processes total including helpers). Each headless invocation sends a ~27 KB prompt (`.claude-flow/logs/headless/audit_*_prompt.log`).

### Aggravating factors

- The daemon's default config schedules `audit` with `interval: 600s`, but the MCP queue re-dispatches the same job immediately
- Worker `--context "./src"` argument is silently dropped (status shows `Context: default`)
- `--dangerously-skip-permissions=true` is the **default** for `hive-mind spawn --claude`
- No confirmation prompt before spawning Claude subprocess
- `ruflo daemon stop` did not stop the spawned subprocess — required `pkill -f ruflo` to clean up

### Impact

Estimated cost during the 50-second daemon run: 9 Claude headless invocations × ~27 KB input + analysis = roughly \$3-8 USD in API tokens, **without any user interaction beyond `daemon start`**. If a user accidentally leaves the daemon running overnight, the cost ceiling is unbounded.

## Suggested fixes

1. **`--no-global`** : honor the flag in `init`. Add a regression test that asserts no mutation of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when the flag is set.
2. **Daemon dispatch** : when a worker is manually dispatched via MCP, it should not re-enter the queue. Add a `dispatched_at` timestamp + dedup window (e.g. don't redispatch a worker whose ID was completed within the last N seconds).
3. **Cost safety** : require explicit opt-in for headless-mode workers (e.g. `daemon start --enable-headless`). Print an estimated cost warning before first spawn.
4. **`--dangerously-skip-permissions`** : default should be `false`. Users who want it should opt in.
5. **Daemon stop** : ensure `daemon stop` propagates SIGTERM to all spawned Claude subprocesses.

## Reproducibility

100% reproducible on a clean macOS Apple Silicon install with the steps above. Logs available on request.

## Mitigation for current users

```bash
# Avoid daemon for now
ruflo daemon stop
pkill -f ruflo
pkill -f claude-flow

# Clean global pollution from --no-global bypass
# Manually remove "# Ruflo Integration" block from ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (5 lines)
rm -rf ~/.claude-flow/
```

title: fix(cli,daemon,mcp): #2098 #2093 #2085 — three regressions reported on alpha.75
body:
Closes #2098, #2093, #2085.

Three independent bugs from three reporters, all reproducible on alpha.76 today. Each fix is small and localized.

## Per-issue fix

### #2098A — `--no-global` flag silently ignored (@pierrefuseau)

The parser handles `--no-foo` by stripping the prefix and storing `flags.foo = false` (`parser.ts:291-294`), not by storing `flags['no-foo'] = true`. The consumer at `init.ts:190` read the wrong key, so the flag was always `undefined` and the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` got modified anyway.

**Fix**: read `flags['global'] === false` AND keep accepting the literal-key form. One line, plus a why-comment so the next reader doesn't undo it.

### #2098B / #2093 — Daemon subprocess group not killed (@pierrefuseau, @maxstefanakis1114)

`headless-worker-executor.ts` spawns `claude --print` without `detached: true`. Grandchildren (MCP stdio bridges, plugin tools) belong to the parent's process group, so `child.kill()` on timeout only signals the head — grandchildren get reparented to init and leak. Combined with the queue-file path the alpha.73 `.processed/` rename already fixed, the surface was 90% closed but the residual gap was the missing tree-kill.

**Fix**: spawn with `detached: true` (POSIX only — Windows process groups don't work the same way), then signal the group with `process.kill(-pid, sig)` instead of `child.kill(sig)`. Fallback to plain `child.kill` if `-pid` kill fails.

### #2085 — `agent_spawn` not in `swarm_status.agents` (@seo-yas)

`agent_spawn` writes only to the agent store; `swarm_status` reads only from the swarm store. The two are never bridged. Every topology is affected — not just hierarchical as the reporter assumed. Also the schema never accepted `swarmId`, which is why all 5 of their parameter-shape variants failed identically.

**Fix**: add `swarmId` to the `agent_spawn` schema (optional; defaults to most-recent swarm), then after writing the agent store, also push the agentId into `swarm.agents`. Idempotent so retries don't duplicate.

## Files changed (4)

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/init.ts` | Read `--no-global` from the right parser key (#2098A) |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/headless-worker-executor.ts` | `detached: true` spawn + `process.kill(-pid, sig)` tree-kill (#2098B / #2093) |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/agent-tools.ts` | Accept `swarmId` + register in `swarm.agents` (#2085) |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/swarm-tools.ts` | Export `loadSwarmStore` / `saveSwarmStore` for #2085 |

Closes #2078.

Final piece of the #2078 fix that ruvnet acknowledged but hadn't shipped: a project-level rule in the generated CLAUDE.md that tells the agent to ignore Claude Code's built-in Bash-tool commit-template suggestion.

## Why this matters

ruvnet's earlier reply on #2078 acknowledged @shaal's five points, then noted that #2079 only fixed half the surface (the settings-generator opt-in defaulting to `false`). The other half — the Claude Code Bash tool's default commit-message instructions — still suggests `Co-Authored-By: RuFlo <ruv@ruv.net>` regardless of project settings. Users were left having to discover the override themselves.

## What this patch does

Adds one rule to the generated `CLAUDE.md`'s Behavioral Rules section:

```
- NEVER add a `Co-Authored-By` trailer to user commits unless this project's
  `.claude/settings.json` has `attribution.commit` set (#2078). The Claude Code
  Bash tool may suggest one in its default commit-message template — ignore it.
  `Co-Authored-By` is semantic authorship attribution under git/GitHub convention;
  the tool is the facilitator, not a co-author.
```

Agents read CLAUDE.md on every session start, so the override is automatic for every project that runs `ruflo init` going forward. Users who DO want the trailer still get it via the `settings.attribution.commit` opt-in that #2079 added.

title: fix(mcp): #2042 — agent_execute routes through v3 provider system (Anthropic / OpenRouter / Ollama)
body:
Closes #2042. Reporter: @ummcke00.

## What was broken

`agent_execute` and `executeAgentTask()` hardcoded a `fetch` to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` and required `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Users with OpenRouter, Ollama, or other OpenAI-compatible providers in `.claude-flow/config.yaml` got `"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set in environment"` regardless of their config.

The router `callAnthropicMessages()` already existed (added in #1725 for Ollama) but `executeAgentTask()` predated it and never delegated.

## Fix (3 parts, ~80 lines)

| Change | What |
|---|---|
| `agent-execute-core.ts` `callAnthropicMessages()` | Add OpenRouter branch — detect via `RUFLO_PROVIDER=openrouter` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set when no Anthropic key. Updates the "no provider" error to list all three options. |
| `agent-execute-core.ts` new `callOpenAICompat()` | OpenAI-compat helper — `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, OpenRouter analytics headers, logical model name translation. |
| `agent-execute-core.ts` `executeAgentTask()` | Delegates to `callAnthropicMessages()` instead of inline `fetch`. Agent registry coupling preserved. |
| `scripts/smoke-agent-execute-providers.mjs` (new) | 5-check static + behavioral regression guard. |
| `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml` | New `agent-execute-providers-smoke` job + path filters. |

## Local smoke matrix

```
$ node scripts/smoke-agent-execute-providers.mjs
✓ executeAgentTask delegates to callAnthropicMessages (no inline Anthropic fetch)
✓ OPENROUTER_API_KEY env var routes the OpenRouter branch
✓ callOpenAICompat helper exists for OpenRouter + OpenAI-compat backends
✓ No-provider error message lists Anthropic + OpenRouter + Ollama options
✓ OPENROUTER_API_KEY routes to openrouter dispatch (auth error from openrouter, not anthropic)
#2042 regression smoke PASS
```

Behavioral verification with fake keys (no real network auth):

## What's NOT changed

Streaming — `executeAgentTask()` didn't stream before, doesn't now. Same with response shape: callers see `AgentExecuteResult` regardless of which backend answered.

## Out of scope (flagged for follow-up)

`config.yaml` reading — the reporter had `providers.openrouter.apiKey` in YAML. This PR honors env vars only (matching the existing pattern from #1725). A follow-up can read the YAML and seed env vars at config-load time. Documented in the smoke description.

title: perf(guidance): RaBitQ-style 1-bit quantization → 2.70x at N=1000 + 32x memory
body:
**Status**: Ready. M4 quantization delivers the SOTA proof.

📊 **Gist**: https://gist.github.com/ruvnet/fcf31c97644acb3cb001f8fdfb4c25f4

## Headline result

| Metric | Baseline | M4 quantized | **Speedup** |
|--------|---------:|-------------:|------------:|
| `retriever.retrieve()` at N=100 | 12,135 ops/s | **26,372 ops/s** | **2.17x** |
| `retriever.retrieve()` at N=500 | 2,470 ops/s | **6,468 ops/s** | **2.62x** |
| `retriever.retrieve()` at N=1000 | 1,303 ops/s | **3,522 ops/s** | 🚀 **2.70x** |
| Memory per shard signature | 1,536 bytes | **48 bytes** | **32x smaller** |
| Per-pair Hamming vs Float32 dot | 332 ns | **30 ns** | **10.93x** |

All 1,331 existing tests pass.

## What's in the box

| Layer | What | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1** | Single-pass `extractMetrics`, `text.matchAll`, unit-vector dot-only cosine | within V8 noise — clean code, no perf claim |
| **M3** | Packed Float32 embedding matrix, filter-first reorder | within V8 noise — clean code |
| **M4** | **1-bit RaBitQ-style sign signatures + Hamming popcount** | **🚀 2.70x at N=1000** |

The first two iterations attacked V8 JIT-friendly hot paths and didn't yield measurable speedup (the JIT already optimized them). M4 is the algorithmic win — 384 multiplies replaced with 12 XOR + popcount per pair.

## Algorithm (M4)

For each unit-normalized embedding, record the sign of each dimension as a 1-bit signature (`dim=384 → 12 Uint32 words → 48 bytes`). Compute cosine approximation via Hamming distance on packed Uint32 XOR + popcount.

Sign-Random-Projection theorem (Charikar 2002):
> `cos(θ) ≈ cos(π · hamming(sig_q, sig_s) / dim)`

The approximation is exact enough for the retriever's downstream sort + intent-boost + risk-boost pipeline. All 1,331 tests pass.

## New benchmark scripts (durable)

- `bench-phase-1.mjs` — 3-hot-path microbenchmarks, 5-trial median
- `bench-retriever-scale.mjs` — end-to-end at N ∈ {10, 100, 500, 1000}, filtered + unfiltered
- `bench-quantization.mjs` — per-pair cosine vs Hamming popcount

8 JSON artifacts in `docs/benchmarks/` for reproducibility.

title: Franchise-Level Context Management for Long-Running Creative Projects
body:
Summary

I've been using Ruflo/Claude Flow to build a children's animated educational franchise called TinyNova Adventures.

The platform performs exceptionally well for:

* Episode planning
* Research synthesis
* Educational content generation
* SEO generation
* Production package creation
* Multi-agent collaboration

However, while building multiple episodes, I encountered a consistency challenge that may affect other long-running creative projects (animation, games, books, educational series, etc.).

##The Problem

Agents generate high-quality episode deliverables but do not automatically load project-wide approved assets and canon.

Example:

* Episode planning agents generated excellent content.
* Production agents generated excellent scene packages.
* Visual prompts were technically correct.

However, approved character references were not automatically loaded into the workflow.

As a result, generated visuals began drifting from approved character designs even though the story content remained correct.

The issue was not content quality.

The issue was project continuity.


##Current Workflow

Project
├── Characters
├── Canon
├── Style Guides
├── Assets
└── Episodes

Episode
├── Scenes
├── SEO
├── Production Files
└── Deliverables

Currently, agents appear to work primarily from episode-level context.

---

## Suggested Solution

### 1. Project Context Registry

Allow projects to define permanent context sources:

project_context/
├── characters/
├── canon/
├── style-guide/
├── environments/
└── assets/

Agents automatically load these before executing work.

---

### 2. Asset Registry

Support asset lifecycle states:

* ACTIVE
* LOCKED
* DRAFT
* DEPRECATED

Example:

Noah_V2.png → LOCKED
Noah_V1.png → DEPRECATED

Agents should preferentially use ACTIVE or LOCKED assets.

---

### 3. Shared Project Memory

Allow multiple agents to reference a common project knowledge base rather than relying only on episode-level documents.

This would improve consistency across:

* Characters
* Environments
* Story canon
* Visual style
* Educational standards

---

### 4. Dependency Validation

Warn users when visual assets are generated without approved character references or style guides.

Example:

"Warning: No approved character references detected. Visual consistency may be affected."

---

## Why This Matters

Ruflo works extremely well at generating individual deliverables.

The challenge appears when scaling from:

* One episode

to

* A 50+ episode franchise

where continuity becomes as important as content generation.

A project-wide context system would make Ruflo significantly stronger for:

* Animation studios
* Educational content creators
* Game development teams
* Book series
* Long-running media franchises

Thank you for the excellent work on the project. This feedback comes from active production use and is intended to help support larger creative workflows.

title: feature: configurable memory DB path via CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH env var
body:
## Summary

Currently `ruflo memory store / retrieve / search / list / delete / stats` hard-codes the SQLite DB path to `${HOME}/.swarm/memory.db`. `memory init -p <path>` accepts a custom path but only writes the template; subsequent operations ignore the override and always go back to `~/.swarm/memory.db`. There's no env var or `--path` flag on the sub-commands.

This forces operators to either:

1. Accept `~` (often on the system drive `C:\` on Windows) for the DB — even when project policy requires "everything on a separate drive".
2. Work around via NTFS junction / Unix symlink — functional but fragile, invisible in code, breaks if the directory is recreated.

## Proposed change

Read the DB path with this precedence:

1. `--path <path>` CLI flag (when present on a sub-command).
2. `CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH` env var.
3. `~/.swarm/memory.db` (current default, unchanged).

Affected sub-commands: `memory store`, `memory retrieve`, `memory search`, `memory list`, `memory delete`, `memory stats`, `memory cleanup`, `memory compress`, `memory export`, `memory import`, `memory configure`.

## Why an env var (not just `--path`)

`--path` on every CLI call is too noisy for daily use. `memory configure` already exists but stores the chosen path in `~/.swarm/config.json` — same problem if the policy is to keep state off the home drive entirely. An env var is declarative per-shell, survives `npx`, and doesn't pollute the filesystem.

## Implementation sketch

Where the DB path is resolved (likely a helper around `better-sqlite3` open):

```ts
function resolveDbPath(cliFlag?: string): string {
  if (cliFlag) return path.resolve(cliFlag);
  if (process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH) {
    return path.resolve(process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH);
  }
  return path.join(os.homedir(), ".swarm", "memory.db");
}
```

Pass `cliFlag` from every sub-command handler.

## Backward compatibility

Fully backward-compatible: behaviour unchanged unless the env var or `--path` is set.

## Test plan

1. `unset CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH; ruflo memory store -k smoke -v ok` → DB at `~/.swarm/memory.db` (current behaviour).
2. `export CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH=/tmp/mydb.db; ruflo memory init && ruflo memory store -k smoke -v ok` → DB at `/tmp/mydb.db`.
3. `ruflo memory store -k smoke -v ok --path /tmp/other.db` → DB at `/tmp/other.db` (CLI flag wins).
4. Round-trip: store with env var set → retrieve in same env → value matches.
5. Cross-platform: confirm on Windows, macOS, Linux.

## Real-world demand

In our project (`Yaroslav_Stack`, Штаб-Совет infrastructure) we needed the DB on a different drive than `C:\` for policy reasons. The workaround was an NTFS junction `C:\Users\<user>\.swarm` → `D:\Yaroslav_Stack\.swarm`. It works but adds opaque coupling: a new contributor cloning the repo wouldn't know the DB lives off-drive unless we document the junction explicitly. An env var would let us put `CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH=D:\Yaroslav_Stack\.swarm\memory.db` in the project's setup README and remove the junction entirely.

I'm happy to write the PR if there's buy-in on the env var name. Open to bikeshedding (`RUFLO_DB_PATH`? `CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_DB`?).

## Environment

- `@claude-flow/cli` v3.7.0-alpha.72
- Node v24.15.0, Windows 11 / Git Bash

title: Claude/doner restaurant app vg ee6
Hook xargs error: 'command line cannot be assembled, too long' for long bash commands
body:
## Problem

PreToolUse and PostToolUse Bash hooks fail with:

```
PreToolUse:Bash hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: xargs: command line cannot be assembled, too long
```

## Root Cause

The generated hook commands in `.claude/settings.json` use `xargs -I {}` to inject the full bash command as an argument:

```bash
cat | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 -I {} npx claude-flow@alpha hooks pre-command --command '{}' --validate-safety true --prepare-resources true
```

When the bash command being intercepted is long (multi-line scripts, long argument lists, etc.), `xargs` hits the OS `ARG_MAX` limit and fails with the above error. On macOS the limit is typically ~200KB but `xargs -I` has a much smaller per-argument limit.

## Affected hooks

- `PreToolUse` → `Bash` matcher
- `PostToolUse` → `Bash` matcher

## Fix

Replace the `xargs` pattern with a shell variable approach that has no argument length limit, and truncate commands to a safe length:

```bash
/bin/sh -c 'CMD=$(cat | jq -r ".tool_input.command // empty" | cut -c1-500); [ -n "$CMD" ] && npx claude-flow@alpha hooks pre-command --command "$CMD" --validate-safety true --prepare-resources true || true'
```

This avoids `xargs` entirely by storing the value in a shell variable, and truncates to 500 chars to prevent any OS limit issues.

## Environment

- macOS Darwin 25.3.0
- Claude Code hooks (settings.json generated by `ruflo init`)

ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.79 fails with npm `Invalid Version:` (regression of #2018 pattern, new transitive dep)
body:
## Summary

`npx ruflo@latest mcp start` fails on a clean run with `npm error Invalid Version:` (empty version string). This is the same crash pattern as #2018, #1921, #1688, #1595 — a transitive dependency ships a manifest with an empty `version` field, which crashes `@npmcli/arborist`'s `canDedupe` step via `new SemVer('')`.

The previous fixes targeted `@huggingface/transformers`, `@ruvector/ruvllm`, and `koa-router`. This regression appears to be in a **different** transitive — the stack now points at `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1`'s dependency tree.

The `latest` tag currently resolves to `3.7.0-alpha.79`, so anyone following the documented install (`npx ruflo@latest mcp start`) is blocked.

## Reproduction

```bash
npx ruflo@latest mcp start
```

Result:
```
npm warn exec The following package was not found and will be installed: ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.79
npm error Invalid Version:
npm error A complete log of this run can be found in: /Users/<user>/.npm/_logs/2026-05-22T22_12_30_619Z-debug-0.log
```

## Stack trace (from npm debug log)

```
106 verbose stack TypeError: Invalid Version:
106 verbose stack     at new SemVer (.../semver/classes/semver.js:40:13)
106 verbose stack     at compare (.../semver/functions/compare.js:5:32)
106 verbose stack     at Object.eq (.../semver/functions/eq.js:4:29)
106 verbose stack     at Node.canDedupe (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/node.js:1137:32)
106 verbose stack     at PlaceDep.pruneDedupable (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/place-dep.js:426:14)
106 verbose stack     at new PlaceDep (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/place-dep.js:278:14)
106 verbose stack     at #buildDepStep (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:995:18)
106 verbose stack     at async Arborist.buildIdealTree (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:178:7)
```

The last `placeDep` lines before the crash:

```
102 silly placeDep node_modules/@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc @grpc/grpc-js@1.14.4 OK for: @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1 want: ^1.7.1
103 silly placeDep node_modules/@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc @opentelemetry/core@1.25.1 OK for: @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1 want: 1.25.1
104 silly placeDep node_modules/@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc @opentelemetry/otlp-transformer@0.52.1 OK for: @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1 want: 0.52.1
105 silly placeDep ROOT @opentelemetry/resources@1.25.1 OK for: @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1 want: 1.25.1
```

i.e. the empty-version manifest is somewhere in the `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1` subtree (likely `@opentelemetry/resources@1.25.1` or one of its peers).

## Environment

- macOS Darwin 23.6.0 (Intel)
- Node v24.15.0 (nvm)
- npm v11.15.0
- `ruflo@latest` → `3.7.0-alpha.79`

## Suggested remediation (same options as #2018)

1. Republish `alpha.79` (or follow-up) with the offending opentelemetry transitive pinned to a version that has a valid manifest.
2. Revert the `latest` dist-tag to the last known-good alpha while investigating.
3. Long-term: enforce a publish-time check that every direct + transitive dep manifest has a non-empty `version` field — this pattern keeps recurring across unrelated transitives (#1595, #1688, #1921, #2018, now this one).

## User workaround

Per official install instructions, users are expected to keep `npx ruflo@latest mcp start` in their MCP registration verbatim. Pinning a specific alpha locally is fragile and has caused unrelated breakage in the past, so the practical workaround is to wait for the upstream `latest` tag to point at a working alpha again.

## Summary

Three moderate-severity CVEs resolved via `npm overrides` in `package.json`:

- **GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26** — `qs` 6.11.1–6.15.1: remotely triggerable DoS — `qs.stringify` crashes with `TypeError` on `null`/`undefined` entries in comma-format arrays when `encodeValuesOnly` is set. Fixed by adding override `qs >=6.15.2`.

title: fix(security): patch CVEs, shell injection, SSRF in ruflo
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive security audit of the ruflo codebase (2026-05-23). `npm audit` returned 0 vulnerabilities (existing `overrides` in `package.json` already cover all known CVEs). Static analysis found two classes of real vulnerabilities patched in this PR:

**CWE-78 — Shell Injection (9 sites)**

Every call to `execSync(templateLiteral)` that assembled a shell command string was replaced with `execFileSync(cmd, argArray)`. Passing an array bypasses the OS shell entirely so shell metacharacters (backticks, `$(...)`, semicolons, whitespace) in any argument cannot be interpreted as commands.

Sites fixed:
- `.claude/helpers/github-safe.js` — `execSync(\`gh ${args.join(' ')}\`)` in no-body and non-body paths (the body path already used `--body-file` but still joined args into a shell string for the final `gh` call)
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/helpers/github-safe.js` — identical copy, same fix
- `v3/@claude-flow/mcp/.claude/helpers/github-safe.js` — older variant without body-cap
- `scripts/audit-supply-chain.mjs` — `execSync(\`npm view "${name}" maintainers --json\`)` where `name` comes from a JSON config file
- `scripts/track-clones.mjs` — `execSync(\`gh api repos/${repo}/traffic/clones\`)`
- `plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/perf.mjs` — six `execSync` calls in benchmark runners (`git rev-parse`, `pnpm pack` ×2, `npm init`, `npm pkg set`, `npm install <tarball>`, `node verify.mjs`)
- `v3/@claude-flow/browser/tests/e2e/browser-e2e.test.ts` — `execSync(\`agent-browser ... ${command}\`)`

**CWE-918 — SSRF (2 sites)**

`callCloudFunction(url, ...)` in both `ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/index.js` and `ruflo/src/ruvocal/mcp-bridge/index.js` accepted an arbitrary URL without validation. Added `assertSafeUrl()` called before every `fetch()` that:

3. Rejects private/loopback ranges: `10.x`, `172.16-31.x`, `192.168.x`, `127.x`, `::1`, `fc`/`fd` ULA, `localhost`, `*.local`

- [x] `npx vitest run` — no new test file failures vs pre-patch baseline (variance is pre-existing flakiness in `router-bandit.test.ts` Thompson sampling test)

body:
Closes #2112.

## Root cause

@crayes reported `npx ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.79 mcp start` crashes with `npm error Invalid Version:` on npm 11.x. Stack trace named `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc@0.52.1` — same pattern as #2018, #1921, #1688, #1595, #1147 (optionalDeps ↔ peerDeps overlap with empty-version string crashes arborist's `canDedupe`).

## What was missing

The opentelemetry pins lived in **root** `package.json` since the original fix, but the **published `ruflo` wrapper** — which is what `npm install ruflo@latest` actually consumes — has its own `overrides` block and was missing them. So:

```bash
# At repo root (where overrides exist) — install succeeds
npm install --legacy-peer-deps          # ok

# Via published wrapper (where overrides did NOT exist) — crash on npm 11
npx ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.79 mcp start      # Invalid Version: — issue #2112
```

## Fix

Copies 12 opentelemetry entries from root `package.json` overrides into `ruflo/package.json` overrides:
- 3 core/resource/sdk-trace-base pins
- 3 sdk-node/auto-instrumentations/exporter-prometheus floors
- 6 exporter-base / otlp-transformer transitives the reporter's stack named

Bumps all 3 packages to **3.7.0-alpha.80**.

## Reproduction status

Could not reproduce on local **npm 10.9.4** or **npm 11.15.0** — both succeed with `npx -y ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.79 --version`. The bug is sensitive to the exact (npm patch, cache state, transitive resolution order) triple. Pre-emptive ship under the "fewer-knobs-for-arborist" policy that worked for the prior 5 recurrences of this pattern.

title: fix(daemon): #2110 — WSL2 silent-degrade triple fix + alpha.81
body:
Closes #2110. Reporter: @tatyinandy-commits.

## Three compounding bugs, file:line-anchored

Reporter gave a precise breakdown — verified all three:

### 1. `isAvailable()` caches `false` forever (`headless-worker-executor.ts:634`)
A transient `claude --version` failure cached `false` for the daemon's lifetime. Now: cache only `true`, surface the actual error via emit, support `CLAUDE_CODE_AVAILABILITY_TIMEOUT_MS` env var for WSL2-class slow systems.

### 2. WSL2 `/proc/loadavg` permanently fails CPU gate (`worker-daemon.ts:152`)
WSL maps Windows-side process counts into `/proc/loadavg`, reporting 100-1000x real values. New `WorkerDaemon.isWslEnvironment()` static (checks `WSL_DISTRO_NAME`, `WSL_INTEROP`, `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease`); on WSL the gate floors at 1000 so it's effectively disabled.

### 3. `runWorkerLogic` doesn't check `result.success` (`worker-daemon.ts:1047`)
`HeadlessWorkerExecutor.execute()` returns `success:false` on failure instead of throwing. Catch never fired; stubs got persisted as `mode:"headless"`. Now explicit `success === true` check, falsy falls through to local with a warn log.

ruflo alpha.81: status and memory stats misreport initialized DB
body:
## Summary

Two CLI regressions appeared between `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.79` and `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.81`: `ruflo status` reports that an initialized project is not initialized, and `ruflo memory stats` reports `Total Entries: 0` even though the SQLite memory DB contains entries.

The underlying `.swarm/memory.db` appears intact and MCP continues to run; this looks like a CLI/status reporting regression rather than data loss.

## Environment

- OS: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- Node: v22.18.0 via nvm
- Current package: `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.81` published 2026-05-23 19:19 UTC
- Last known working package: `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.79` published 2026-05-22 11:18 UTC
- Relevant globally installed packages:
  - `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.81`
  - `claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.73`
  - `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.18`
  - `@claude-flow/codex@3.0.0-alpha.12`
  - `@openai/codex@0.133.0`

## Reproduction

### Bug 1: `ruflo status` falsely reports that the project is not initialized

From a project directory with an existing `.swarm/memory.db`:

```bash
cd /home/alexa/projects/RadFreq/calib
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries"
ruflo status --verbose
ruflo mcp status
```

### Bug 2: `ruflo memory stats` reports zero entries for a populated DB

From the same project directory:

```bash
cd /home/alexa/projects/RadFreq/calib
ruflo memory stats
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries"
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT namespace, COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries GROUP BY namespace ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5"
ls -lh .swarm/hnsw.index .swarm/hnsw.metadata.json
```

### Minor related issue: MCP `memory_store` does not persist tags

Store a memory through the MCP tool with tags:

```json
{
  "tags": ["foo", "bar"]
}
```

Then retrieve it through MCP `memory_retrieve`. The `value` is persisted correctly, but the retrieved memory has empty tags:

```json
{
  "tags": []
}
```

## Expected

- `ruflo status --verbose` should recognize an initialized project when `.swarm/memory.db` exists and is usable.
- `ruflo memory stats` should report the actual number of rows in `memory_entries`; in this verified case, `Total Entries` should be `251`.
- MCP `memory_store` should preserve provided tags so a subsequent `memory_retrieve` returns `["foo", "bar"]`.

## Actual

### Bug 1

`ruflo status --verbose` reports that the directory is not initialized:

```text
$ ruflo status --verbose
[DEBUG] Command: status
[DEBUG] CWD: /home/alexa/projects/RadFreq/calib
[DEBUG] Executing: status
[ERROR] RuFlo is not initialized in this directory
[INFO] Run "ruflo init" to initialize
[DEBUG] Completed in 0ms
```

However, MCP status works from the same project:

```text
$ ruflo mcp status
Running, PID, stdio
```

The string `RuFlo is not initialized` appears in `node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/controller-registry.js`, but I did not trace the full path from the `status` command handler to that message.

### Bug 2

`ruflo memory stats` reports zero entries:

```text
$ ruflo memory stats
Memory Statistics
Overview
| Backend       | sql.js + HNSW |
| Total Entries |             0 |
| HNSW Index    | available but not initialized |
```

Direct SQL against the same DB shows 251 entries:

```text
$ sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries"
251

$ sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT namespace, COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries GROUP BY namespace ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5"
feedback|85
causal-edges|71
session|31
project|23
pattern|18
```

Additional local state:

- `.swarm/hnsw.index` is approximately 1.5 MB on disk.
- `.swarm/hnsw.metadata.json` shows 179 indexed entries.

## Diff analysis

This was verified by comparing `3.7.0-alpha.79` and `3.7.0-alpha.81` with `npm pack` plus `diff`.

- `3.7.0-alpha.79` was working.
- `3.7.0-alpha.80` added 12 OpenTelemetry dependencies, including `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` and OTLP exporters.
- `3.7.0-alpha.81` added an SSRF guard in `src/mcp-bridge/index.js` that blocks non-HTTPS HTTP and private IPs.
- Total functional changes observed across the range were limited to 3 files: `package.json` and two `mcp-bridge/index.js` files.

The visible regressions are in CLI status/stat reporting, while the DB remains readable and MCP status is still functional.

## Workarounds

- To verify the memory DB state directly:

```bash
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries"
sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT namespace, COUNT(*) FROM memory_entries GROUP BY namespace ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5"
```

- To verify MCP is running:

```bash
ruflo mcp status
```

- Continue using MCP and direct SQLite checks for now; the system appears functional, but the `status` and `memory stats` CLI outputs are unreliable in `3.7.0-alpha.81`.

## Related

- https://github.com/ruvnet/claude-flow/issues/837 is an older, loosely related memory command issue (`claude-flow` v2.7.15 / `onnxruntime-node`), not this `ruflo@3.7.0-alpha.81` regression.
- No exact existing report found for `ruflo status` falsely reporting "is not initialized" or `ruflo memory stats` returning `Total Entries: 0`. Note: `gh issue list` searches were attempted for `"memory stats"`, `"ruflo status initialized"`, `"Total Entries 0"`, and `"memory_store tags"`, but the local `gh` client could not connect to `api.github.com`; web search found the related issue above.

title: fix(memory): #2120 — accept NULL status (legacy DBs) + first stable 3.7.0
body:
Closes #2120. Reporter: @alexandrelealbess (WSL2, alpha.81).

## Root cause

`WHERE status = 'active'` in both `bridgeListEntries` and `listEntries` excluded rows where the `status` column was NULL. Legacy DBs created before the column existed (or via auto-memory-bridge writes that didn't set status) end up with NULL status after schema migration — so the user's 251-row DB returned 0 from `memory stats`.

Bonus: `isInitialized()` in `status.ts` required `.claude-flow/config.yaml` exclusively, missing projects with only `.swarm/memory.db` from `ruflo memory init`.

## Fix (4 parts + CI guard)

| # | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `memory-bridge.ts` | Accept `status IS NULL` alongside `'active'` in `bridgeListEntries` |
| 2 | `memory-initializer.ts:listEntries` | Same NULL-acceptance in raw sql.js fallback (4 prepares) |
| 3 | `memory-initializer.ts:ensureSchemaColumns` | Belt-and-suspenders backfill — `UPDATE ... SET status='active' WHERE status IS NULL` after ALTER TABLE |
| 4 | `status.ts:isInitialized` | Accept any of 4 initialization signals, not just `.claude-flow/config.yaml` |
| **CI guard** | `scripts/smoke-memory-stats-legacy-db.mjs` + path filter | Builds 251-row legacy DB, asserts `total=251` and backfill works |

## Verification

```
$ node scripts/smoke-memory-stats-legacy-db.mjs
✓ fixture: 251 entries written to /tmp/smoke-2120-*/.swarm/memory.db with status=NULL
✓ fixture sanity: 251 rows have status=NULL
✓ listEntries returns total=251 against legacy DB (NULL status accepted as active)
✓ backfill: ensureSchemaColumns promoted NULL → 'active' for all 251 rows
#2120 regression smoke PASS
```

- `npm test` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli`: **1999/2045 pass** (46 skipped, 0 fail)
- Build clean

## First stable 3.7.0 — no more alphas

Per CLAUDE.md update yesterday (alpha series ended at alpha.81), this is the **first stable release: 3.7.0** — no `-alpha.N` suffix. Legacy `alpha` + `v3alpha` dist-tags continue to point at the latest stable for backward compat.

title: feat(rvagent): #ADR-129 — full rvagent integration (4 phases)
body:
Implements all 4 phases of ADR-129 ([v3/docs/adr/ADR-129-rvagent-full-integration.md](v3/docs/adr/ADR-129-rvagent-full-integration.md)). Makes WasmAgents first-class participants in the ruflo swarm — they now route through the v3 provider system, can call the 314 ruflo MCP tools, expose the full Gallery CRUD, and accept skills from plugins.

## Commits

| Phase | SHA | What |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | `678cd045c` | JsModelProvider wires WasmAgent through `callAnthropicMessages` (Anthropic / OpenRouter / Ollama). Replaces the echo-stub at `agent-wasm.ts:165-196`. |
| **2** | `28d972a7b` | `wasm_agent_compose` MCP tool + `WasmRvfBuilder.addMcpTools` bridge. Explicit allowlist gate on destructive tools (`memory_delete`, `federation_*`, etc.); requires `mcpToolsAllowDestructive: true` to escalate. Also fixes the `template.mcp_tools` silent drop at `agent-wasm.ts:420-429`. |
| **3** | `fe885e9ec` | **16 new MCP tools**: 10 gallery CRUD (`wasm_gallery_load_rvf`, `_configure`, `_categories`, `_list_by_category`, `_add_custom`, `_remove_custom`, `_import` (⚠️ HIGH RISK + AIDefence gate), `_export`, `_active`, `_config`) + 6 agent introspection (`wasm_agent_state`, `_todos`, `_tools`, `_turn_count`, `_is_stopped`, `_reset`). |
| **4** | `69f79dfe6` | Plugin `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` accepts optional `"rvagent": { exposeSkillsAsTools, skills }`. `wasm_agent_compose` gains `includePlugins` param. |

## Smoke matrix (all pass)

| Smoke | Result |
|---|---|
| `smoke-wasm-provider-bridge.mjs` | 6/6 (JsModelProvider wired, set_model_provider called, callAnthropicMessages bridged, echo-stub fallback preserved) |
| `smoke-wasm-rvf-compose.mjs` | 7/7 (compose tool registered, destructive gate present, mcp_tools drop fixed, addMcpTools called, includePlugins schema) |
| `smoke-wasm-gallery-crud.mjs` | 8/8 (all 16 tools registered, HIGH_RISK marker, AIDefence gate, resetWasmAgent calls .reset()) |
| `smoke-wasm-plugin-bridge.mjs` | 7/7 (fixture parses correctly, unknown plugin warns not throws, boolean handling) |

## Test results

- `npm test` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli`: **1999/2045 pass, 46 skipped — identical to baseline** (the `router-bandit.test.ts` Thompson-sampling flap is pre-existing, confirmed against baseline commit)
- `npm run build` (tsc): clean

## Deviations from ADR-129

1. The ADR's narrative listed 3 introspection tools in one place and 6 in the acceptance criteria — shipped all 6 (matches the gap analysis count).
2. `wasm_gallery_configure` takes the full config JSON (matching the WASM d.ts), not separate `id` + config params.
3. AIDefence gate on `wasm_gallery_import` is dynamic import (catches if unavailable, logs HIGH_RISK warning and proceeds) — matches the ADR-118 "warn and proceed" pattern.

## Security notes

- **Destructive MCP tool gate**: Phase 2's `wasm_agent_compose` rejects destructive tools (`*_delete`, `*_remove`, `*_drop`, `*_shutdown`, `federation_*`, `swarm_shutdown`) by default. Requires `mcpToolsAllowDestructive: true` to escalate. Default safe-by-default.
- **AIDefence gate on import**: Phase 3's `wasm_gallery_import` runs user JSON through AIDefence scanner before passing to the WASM runtime.
- **No billing surprise**: Phase 1 documents (in tool descriptions) that `wasm_agent_prompt` now makes real LLM calls. The fallback to echo behavior is preserved when no provider env is set, matching existing `callAnthropicMessages` semantics.

## Versioning

This adds new MCP tools — backward-compatible additions per the semver policy in CLAUDE.md → **next release is `3.8.0`** (minor bump). No breaking changes.

## Test plan

- [x] All 4 new smokes pass
- [x] No test regressions
- [x] Build clean
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] Post-merge: publish 3.8.0 across 3 packages + GitHub Release

Closes nothing yet — ADR-129 will be marked Accepted via the release notes when 3.8.0 ships.
