title: [verification] HIGH: npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version times out at 60s — cold-cache regression recurs at v3.10.13
body:
## Summary

The 12-hour scheduled verification run (2026-05-30T07:03:56Z, commit `e6dc21fc79539af029c4f5e87d2b929ebb794291`) found that both `npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` and `npx -y ruflo@alpha --version` are killed by SIGTERM at 60s in the verification container. This is the same cold-cache npx install regression documented in closed issues #2034 (2026-05-17), #2059 (2026-05-19), and #2151 (2026-05-26). The root cause (ADR-100 / cli-core split, #1760) remains unimplemented. The CLI is functionally healthy at v3.10.13 as confirmed by the doctor check; only the cold-cache npx path is broken.

## Impact

Any user or CI pipeline that installs `@claude-flow/cli@alpha` or `ruflo@alpha` from a cold npx cache experiences 60–120s+ delay before the CLI responds. Under Claude Code's 30-second MCP startup timeout, this means zero MCP tools register, producing a silent "Ruflo is broken" experience for new installs. The verification suite cannot confirm the published CLI version meets the `>= 3.7.0-alpha.20` requirement via the expected command path.

## Expected

```
npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
# prints version >= 3.7.0-alpha.20, exits 0, within 60 seconds

npx -y ruflo@alpha --version
# prints ruflo version, exits 0, within 60 seconds
```

## Actual

```
npm warn deprecated koa-router@14.0.0: ...
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: ...
npm warn deprecated node-domexception@1.0.0: ...
npm warn deprecated uuid@9.0.1: ...
npm error process terminated
npm error signal SIGTERM
CLI_EXIT:124

npm error process terminated
npm error signal SIGTERM
RUFLO_EXIT:124
```

Both killed at 60s during cold install. Approximately 527 transitive packages must download before the binary can run.

## Doctor confirms CLI is healthy

```
✓ Version Freshness: v3.10.13 (up to date)
Summary: 10 passed, 7 warnings
All checks passed with some warnings.
```

The CLI is functional. Only the cold-cache `npx` path exceeds the timeout.

## Recommended fix

1. **Short-term**: Raise the verification environment's per-command timeout for this check from 60s to 180s. Alternatively, pre-install via `npm install @claude-flow/cli@alpha` and verify using the local binary path.
2. **Long-term**: Implement ADR-100 (#1760) to split `@claude-flow/cli` into a lean `cli-core` (≤250KB) entry point. Target: cold `npx` completes in <5s.

## Recurrence history

|-------|------|---------|--------|
| #2034 | 2026-05-17 | 3.7.x-alpha | Closed |
| #2059 | 2026-05-19 | 3.7.0-alpha.69 | Closed |
| #2151 | 2026-05-26 | 3.10.1 | Closed |
| (this) | 2026-05-30 | 3.10.13 | New |

The pattern recurs every ~4 days in each new verification cycle; ADR-100 is the structural fix.

title: Self-learning reports success but persists nothing (3.10.6): signalsProcessed dead, task-completed stub (#1916), pretrain hollow
body:
# Bug report: learning/telemetry reports success but persists nothing (claude-flow / ruflo 3.10.6)

**Upstream:** github.com/ruvnet/claude-flow
**Package:** `ruflo` 3.10.6 (vendored `@claude-flow/cli`, `@ruvector/ruvllm`, `agentdb`)
**Environment:** Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu); Node 24; daemon via systemd-user `ruflo-daemon.service`; memory backend `hybrid` (sql.js + HNSW); workspace `~/ruflo-memory`.
**Severity:** High — the entire self-learning subsystem appears functional (commands return success) but does not persist learned data, so it never improves.

## Summary

Every documented learning entry point returns a success response, but the learned data is **not persisted** to any queryable store. Multiple independent status/metric sources report mutually contradictory numbers, and at least one metric is dead code. The net effect: `patternsLearned` and the metrics dashboard stay at 0 indefinitely regardless of usage, while CLI/MCP calls claim success.

## Reproduction

Backend metadata: `schema_version 3.0.0`, `pattern_learning enabled`, `sql_js true`. `migration_state` table is empty.

### 1. `signalsProcessed` is dead code
`.claude-flow/neural/stats.json` always shows `"signalsProcessed": 0`.
In `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/intelligence.js` the field is **initialized** (lines ~607, ~1001) and **read** (line ~924) but **never incremented anywhere**. It is a permanently-zero metric presented as a health indicator.

### 2. `hooks task-completed` (trainPatterns) is a stub
```
MCP hooks_intelligence task-completed {taskId, success:true, quality:0.95, trainPatterns:true}
-> { "patternsLearned": 0, "metrics": { "learningUpdates": 0 },
     "note": "completion recorded; pattern-learning is delegated to the intelligence pipeline (#1916 follow-up)" }
```
`trainPatterns:true` is a no-op. Completing tasks never feeds learning. The session queue-poller path (`ruflo memory store` + `ruflo hooks post-task`) therefore never trains.

### 3. `hooks post-edit` / `post-command` report success, metrics stay 0
```
$ ruflo hooks post-edit -f src/index.ts        -> [OK] Outcome recorded for src/index.ts
$ ruflo hooks post-command -c "npm test" ...    -> [OK] Command outcome recorded
$ ruflo hooks metrics
  Pattern Learning: Total Patterns 0 | Avg Confidence 0.0%
  Agent Routing:    Total Routes 0
  Command Execution: Total Executed 0
```
Outcomes are "recorded" but the metrics dashboard never reflects them.

### 4. `hooks pretrain` reports patterns but persists none
```
$ ruflo hooks pretrain -p <repo> --skip-git
  Files Analyzed 4205 | Patterns Extracted 47 | Strategies Learned 0 | Duration 0.0s
  [OK] Repository intelligence bootstrapped successfully
  Semantic search enabled: Use "embeddings search -q <query>"
```
But immediately afterward:
```
$ ruflo embeddings search -q "escrow money calculation"   -> Found 0 matches; [WARN] No matches found
MCP neural_patterns {action:"list"}                        -> { "patterns": [], "total": 0 }
MCP embeddings_status                                      -> { "initialized": false, "message": "Embeddings not initialized. Run embeddings/init first." }
```
"47 patterns extracted, semantic search enabled, 0.0s" for 4205 files is not physically plausible. Nothing is persisted to `agentdb.rvf` (unchanged), `neural_patterns`, or the embeddings index.

### 5. Contradictory status sources
For the same workspace/daemon, four sources disagree:
- `memory_bridge_status` -> `trajectoriesRecorded: 3791`
- `.claude-flow/neural/stats.json` -> `trajectoriesRecorded: 3823, patternsLearned: 1`
- `hooks_intelligence_stats` (before daemon restart) -> all zeros
- `hooks metrics` dashboard -> all zeros

### What DID work (the one real path)
MCP `hooks_intelligence trajectory-start -> trajectory-step -> trajectory-end {success:true}` genuinely learns:
```
trajectory-end -> { "learning": { "sonaUpdate": true, "patternsExtracted": 2, "ewcConsolidation": true }, "persisted": true }
hooks_intelligence_stats -> sona.trajectoriesTotal 1->2, patternsLearned 1->2
```
But this store is isolated from `neural_patterns list` (still 0), `hooks metrics` (still 0), and `embeddings`.

## Contributing environment issue (also worth a docs note)
A long-running daemon does **not** reload after a package upgrade and does not run pending migrations. Our daemon started ~4 min before a 3.10.x upgrade and silently ran stale code with a dead intelligence store until restarted (`systemctl --user restart ruflo-daemon.service`). Consider: auto-restart on upgrade, or a version-mismatch warning, or running migrations on daemon start (`migration_state` was empty while package was 3.10.6 and schema 3.0.0).

## Expected vs actual
- **Expected:** documented learning entry points (post-edit/post-command/post-task/pretrain) persist data that `hooks metrics`, `neural_patterns list`, and `embeddings search` can see; status counters reflect real state.
- **Actual:** they return success but persist nothing queryable; `signalsProcessed` is dead; `pretrain` is cosmetic; stores are fragmented and stat sources contradict each other.

## Suggested fixes
1. Implement or remove the `#1916` task-completed -> learning delegation; don't return success for a no-op.
2. Increment or remove `signalsProcessed`.
3. Make `pretrain` actually persist extracted patterns + initialize embeddings, or fail loudly; the `0.0s` duration suggests it short-circuits.
4. Unify the learning stores (trajectory SONA store, `neural_patterns`, `hooks metrics`, embeddings) or document which is authoritative.
5. Run migrations on daemon start; warn on package/daemon version mismatch.

## Evidence collected
2026-05-30, ruflo 3.10.6, workspace `/home/andrei/ruflo-memory`. All command outputs above are verbatim from this environment.

title: memory_search_unified default fan-out misses most namespaces; +3 agentdb/patch-durability papercuts (3.10.13 / @claude-flow/cli 3.10.22)
body:
## Environment
- `ruflo` **3.10.13** (npm `-g`), bundling `@claude-flow/cli` **3.10.22**
- Upgraded from `ruflo` 3.10.3 during this report
- Node **24.14.1**, Windows 11, sql.js + HNSW memory backend
- Store: ~8,789 entries across ~33 namespaces

Thanks for ruflo -- filing four reproducible findings from a production upgrade, ordered by impact.

---

## 1. `memory_search_unified` default fan-out only covers 6 namespaces -> most of the store is silently unsearchable

**Where:** `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.js`, the `memory_search_unified` handler (~ line 1012 in 3.10.22).

When no `namespace` filter is supplied, the handler searches a hardcoded list of **6** namespaces:

```js
const namespaces = ns ? [ns] : ['default', 'claude-memories', 'auto-memory', 'patterns', 'tasks', 'feedback'];
```

There is no env-var, no `namespaces: string[]` parameter, and no dynamic enumeration of the namespaces actually present in the DB. Any entry written to a namespace outside those 6 is **silently unreachable** through the default (no-filter) call -- the tool returns `searchedNamespaces: [6 names]` and never reports that other namespaces exist.

**Impact (measured on our store):** of 8,789 entries, the 6-namespace default reaches ~454 (~5%). The remaining ~95% -- `knowledge-graph` (6,770), `causal-edges` (473), `brain-system` (341), `trajectories` (167), plus app-specific namespaces -- are invisible to semantic recall unless the caller already knows the exact namespace to pass.

**Reproducer:**
1. `memory_store({ key: "t", value: "needle", namespace: "brain-system" })`
2. `memory_search_unified({ query: "needle" })`  // no namespace filter
3. Result: the entry is **not** returned; `searchedNamespaces` lists only the 6 defaults.

**Suggested fix (any one):**
- Enumerate namespaces dynamically: `SELECT DISTINCT namespace FROM memory_entries` and fan out across all of them (optionally capped/paged); or
- Accept an explicit `namespaces: string[]` argument; or
- Read an env override (e.g. `CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_SEARCH_NAMESPACES`).

(Issue #2037 looks related and was reported fixed around alpha.63, but the 3.10.22 dist we received still ships the 6-namespace hardcode -- worth confirming the fix shipped to the published `dist/`.) We currently maintain a local patch that adds the env-override + a wider default; happy to open a PR if useful.

---

## 2. `npm install -g ruflo` silently overwrites `dist/.../memory-tools.js` with no patch-durability warning

**Where:** `@claude-flow/cli/package.json` `"files": ["dist", ...]` + `postinstall: "node ./scripts/postinstall.cjs"`.

The runtime tool handlers live in the published `dist/` tree, so every `npm install -g ruflo@<newer>` replaces them wholesale. The `postinstall.cjs` only patches agentdb exports -- it does **not** detect, preserve, back up, or warn about user modifications to `memory-tools.js` (or any other `dist/` file). There is no post-update hook. Result: a local patch vanishes on the next upgrade with zero notice (this is exactly how our namespace patch from finding 1 was lost on a prior auto-upgrade).

**Reproducer:**
1. Append a marker comment to `.../@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.js`.
2. `npm install -g ruflo@<newer>`.
3. The marker is gone; no warning was printed during install.

**Suggested fix:** have `postinstall.cjs` checksum key `dist/` files against the packaged versions and warn (or back up to `*.user.bak`) when user edits are detected; or document in the README that `dist/` edits do not survive upgrades and recommend the supported extension points.

---

## 3. agentdb causal-edge creation silently orphans edges when a node id isn't mapped

**Where:** `agentdb/dist/controllers/CausalMemoryGraph.js` `addCausalEdge()` (bundled agentdb `3.0.0-alpha.16`), with `NodeIdMapper` in `dist/utils/NodeIdMapper.js`.

```js
const mapper = NodeIdMapper.getInstance();
const fromNodeId = typeof edge.fromMemoryId === 'string'
  ? edge.fromMemoryId
  : (mapper.getNodeId(edge.fromMemoryId) || `${edge.fromMemoryType}-${edge.fromMemoryId}`);
// ...same for toNodeId, then createCausalEdge(graphEdge)
```

When `mapper.getNodeId()` returns `undefined` (no registered mapping), the code falls back to a string-interpolated id like `episode-123` and proceeds to create the edge -- with **no** `console.warn`, validation, or thrown error. If no node with that constructed id exists in the graph, the edge dangles. We hit this as recurring causal-edge deprecation noise with no actionable guidance about required id formats (e.g. `entity:` / `mem:` prefixes).

**Reproducer:** call `addCausalEdge()` with a numeric `fromMemoryId` never registered via `NodeIdMapper.register()` -> edge is created against `episode-<id>` and silently orphans.

**Suggested fix:** when the mapper misses, emit one actionable warning (what id was expected, how to register it) or reject the edge, instead of constructing an unvalidated id. (Please confirm whether 3.10.22's pinned agentdb changed this -- we could only inspect the bundled alpha.16.)

---

## 4. `graph-pathfinder` returns `"graph_edges DB unavailable"` when the memory DB file is absent

**Where:** `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/graph-edge-writer.js` `getBridgeDb()` (~ lines 33-78) + three call sites in `dist/src/mcp-tools/agentdb-tools.js` (pagerank / personalized-pagerank / general pathfinder).

`getBridgeDb()` returns `null` if (a) `memory.db` doesn't exist on disk, (b) a concurrent init is in flight, or (c) sql.js load / DB open throws. Every pathfinder call site then returns `{ success: false, error: 'graph_edges DB unavailable' }`. The code already does `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for the `graph_edges` table, but does **not** create the DB *file* on demand -- so a fresh environment that has never initialized memory cannot use graph-pathfinder, and the error message doesn't tell the user how to fix it.

**Reproducer:** with no `memory.db` present, call `agentdb_graph-pathfinder` with any valid `seedNodeId` -> `graph_edges DB unavailable`.

**Suggested fix:** lazily create an empty `memory.db` (+ `graph_edges`) on first pathfinder call, **or** make the error actionable (e.g. "run `ruflo memory init` first").

---

Happy to provide full repro logs or open PRs for #1, #2, or #4. Thanks again.

**MCP Authentication Measurement** (arXiv:2605.22333, May 21, 2026, Grade A): First empirical measurement of 7,973 live MCP servers. Result: 40.55% expose tools with zero authentication; 96.6% of OAuth-enabled servers contain ≥1 exploitable flaw (most common: improper scope validation). This means a Ruflo agent that calls an MCP tool has a >40% chance of accepting a response from an unauthenticated server.

**AIRGuard** (arXiv:2605.28914, May 27, 2026, Grade A): Runtime authority control at the action execution layer. Implements least-privilege per-action (not per-session). Result: agent attack success rate drops 36.3% → 5.5% (−85%). The key insight is that session-level auth (which Ruflo has) is insufficient — each individual action must be validated against the minimum necessary scope.

**Authorization Propagation** (arXiv:2605.05440, Apr 2026, Grade A): Formal analysis of authorization invariants in multi-agent systems. Seven structural requirements. Core finding: when agent A delegates a task to agent B via SendMessage, agent B can escalate privileges by calling tools A was not authorized to use. Classical RBAC/ABAC cannot prevent this — scope must travel with the delegation message and be enforced at every hop.

**Dual-Graph Provenance Defense** (arXiv:2605.26497, May 25, 2026, Grade A): Compares an execution provenance graph (what the agent actually did) against an authorization intent graph (what it was allowed to do). Reduces indirect prompt injection success 40% → 1%. This is complementary to ADR-131's content screening — provenance adds a behavioral audit layer on top of content filtering.

title: Model router: uncertainty escalation in selectModel() overrides the Thompson bandit, routing ~40% of trivial tasks to opus
body:
## Summary

In `@claude-flow/cli` `src/ruvector/model-router.ts` (v3.10.29), `selectModel()` applies an "escalate one tier up" step **after** Thompson sampling. Because the escalation triggers on `uncertainty > maxUncertainty` (default **0.15**), and `uncertainty` is structurally ~0.68 for low-complexity tasks, the escalation fires on nearly every trivial route — promoting `sonnet → opus` and `haiku → sonnet`. This **overrides the (correctly working) bandit**: a tier with a strongly negative posterior (e.g. opus `Beta(α≈3.8, β≈17.2)`, mean ≈0.18) still gets selected ~40% of the time on trivial tasks, and `haiku` is never the final pick.

## Environment

- `ruflo` / `@claude-flow/cli` **3.10.29** (global npm)
- Routing via `ruflo hooks model-route` (CLI), state at `.swarm/model-router-state.json` (v2 per-bucket priors, ADR-142)

## Repro

State has a well-trained, suppressed opus prior in every complexity bucket:
```json
"opus": { "alpha": 3.8, "beta": 17.2 }   // posterior mean ≈ 0.18
"sonnet": { "alpha": 12.2, "beta": 6.8 } // ≈ 0.64
"haiku": { "alpha": 3, "beta": 2 }       // ≈ 0.60
```
Route the same trivial task 12×:
```
$ for i in $(seq 1 12); do ruflo hooks model-route \
    -t "Add a single option to a select dropdown, one-line edit" --format json \
    | jq -r .model; done | sort | uniq -c
   7 opus
   5 sonnet
```
- complexity ≈ 0.23 (low bucket)
- opus selected ~40% across ~37 samples; **haiku never selected** (the confirming signature)
- `--prefer-cost` does not change this (42% vs 44% opus)

## Root cause

`selectModel()` samples correctly:
```js
sampledScore[m] = baseScore[m] * sampleBeta(priors[m].alpha, priors[m].beta);
```
For complexity 0.23 the base scores are `haiku 0.548 / sonnet 0.452 / opus 0.339`, and opus's `Beta(3.8,17.2)` draw crushes its sampled score to ~0.06 — so the bandit *does* make opus lose the sampling. But then:
```js
// uncertainty ≈ 0.68 for trivial tasks (low, tightly-clustered sampled scores → tiny spread)
let model = bestModel;
if (uncertainty > this.config.maxUncertainty && bestModel !== 'opus') {  // maxUncertainty = 0.15
  model = bestModel === 'haiku' ? 'sonnet' : 'opus';                      // ← bumps UP, bypassing the bandit
}
```
`0.68 ≫ 0.15`, so escalation fires on ~every trivial route: `sonnet→opus`, `haiku→sonnet`. The learned suppression is computed and then discarded one line later.

## Why it can't be worked around

`maxUncertainty` is read only from the constructor config — there is no env var, config-file, or CLI flag that reaches it, and `--prefer-cost` does not affect the escalation. So Thompson-sampling cost optimization is effectively defeated for low-complexity tasks with no user-facing remedy.

## Impact

The whole point of the cost-adjusted bandit ("auto-corrects against tier overuse") is negated for the cheap-task case it most needs to protect. Users relying on the router for cost control get opus on ~40% of trivial edits regardless of accumulated learning.

## Suggested fixes (any one)

1. Apply the escalation **before** sampling, or skip it when the bandit posterior for the escalation target is poor (don't escalate *into* a tier the bandit has down-weighted).
2. Recalibrate `maxUncertainty` to the actual range the `uncertainty` formula produces (it's ~0.68 baseline for low-complexity), or fix the uncertainty formula so low-complexity ≠ high-uncertainty.
3. Expose `maxUncertainty` (and ideally the escalation behaviour) via config / CLI so it can be tuned.

Happy to test a patch.

title: v3.10.21: `ruflo daemon trigger -w <worker>` always falls through to local mode — headless init not awaited on trigger path
body:
## Environment

- ruflo: `3.10.21` (`npm install -g ruflo@latest`)
- `@claude-flow/cli` (nested): `3.10.21`
- Claude Code CLI: `2.1.154` (verified in PATH: `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude → /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe`)
- OS: macOS Sequoia 15.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon
- Daemon configuration: long-running, started with `ruflo daemon start`, `Workers Enabled: 2` (only `map` + `consolidate`, the three headless workers `audit`/`optimize`/`testgaps` deliberately disabled via `ruflo daemon enable -w <type> --disable`)
- Resource thresholds: `minFreeMemoryPercent: 0.01`, `maxCpuLoad: 999` (effectively gates-off, applied to work around the macOS `os.freemem()` underreporting issue)

## Symptom

`ruflo daemon trigger -w audit` (and `-w optimize` / `-w testgaps`) **always** completes in ~2ms and writes a local-mode stub instead of invoking the headless Claude Code SDK path — even though:

1. The long-running daemon log explicitly states `[INFO] Claude Code headless mode available - AI workers enabled` at every init.
2. `claude --version` returns successfully in the same shell environment.
3. Daemon-**scheduled** runs of the same workers DO use headless mode correctly (verified via prior week's `.claude-flow/logs/headless/*_result.log` files written by scheduled fires, and 8.5KB headless-mode `security-audit.json` outputs).

Only the **on-demand `daemon trigger -w <worker>`** path falls through to local mode. The two paths exercise different code, and only the trigger path has this bug.

## Reproduction

On a Mac with ruflo `3.10.21` installed globally and Claude Code CLI in PATH:

```bash
# 1. Start daemon (any worker config — bug reproduces with all workers enabled too)
ruflo daemon start

# 2. Wait for warm-up
sleep 5

# 3. Confirm headless availability in daemon log
grep "headless mode available" .claude-flow/logs/daemon.log | tail -1
# → [INFO] Claude Code headless mode available - AI workers enabled

# 4. Trigger an audit
ruflo daemon trigger -w audit

# 5. Inspect output
cat .claude-flow/metrics/security-audit.json
```

**Actual output:**
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-31T07:36:24.878Z",
  "mode": "local",
  "checks": {
    "envFilesProtected": true,
    "gitIgnoreExists": true,
    "noHardcodedSecrets": true
  },
  "riskLevel": "low",
  "recommendations": [],
  "note": "Install Claude Code CLI for AI-powered security analysis"
}
```

**Expected output:** the full headless-mode JSON with `"mode": "headless"`, `findings.vulnerabilities[]`, `model: "haiku"`, `durationMs ~31000` — equivalent to what daemon-scheduled fires produce in `.claude-flow/logs/headless/audit_*_result.log` (~8-13 KB).

**Daemon log around the trigger:**
```
[2026-05-31T07:36:24.877Z] [INFO] Starting worker: audit (1/2 concurrent)
[2026-05-31T07:36:24.878Z] [INFO] Claude Code headless mode available - AI workers enabled
[2026-05-31T07:36:24.878Z] [INFO] Worker audit completed in 2ms
```

Note: no `[INFO] Running audit in headless mode (Claude Code AI)` log line — present in every successful scheduled fire. The headless branch in `runWorkerLogic` was never entered.

Reproduced twice in a row on the same daemon with 3-second sleep buffer between triggers. Identical output both times.

## Suspected root cause

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/worker-daemon.ts` — `triggerWorker(type)` → `executeWorker(workerConfig)` → `runWorkerLogic(workerConfig)`:

```ts
async runWorkerLogic(workerConfig) {
    if (isHeadlessWorker(workerConfig.type) && this.headlessAvailable && this.headlessExecutor) {
        // headless path
    }
    // local fallback switch
}
```

The condition `this.headlessAvailable && this.headlessExecutor` is checked synchronously, but `initializeHeadlessExecutor()` is fired-and-forgotten in the constructor (called via `this.initializeHeadlessExecutor()` without `await`). On the long-running daemon this is fine — init completes within ~500ms of startup and `headlessAvailable` is true by the time scheduled fires arrive minutes later.

But `ruflo daemon trigger -w <worker>` appears to dispatch the trigger through an IPC path that arrives at a daemon instance whose `initializeHeadlessExecutor()` hasn't completed (or whose `headlessExecutor` reference is null in the trigger-receiving context). Result: condition is false, falls through to local switch, returns the stub in 2ms.

This is in the same vicinity as issue #1637 ("daemon-state.json write-race: background daemon's periodic in-memory flush can overwrite atomic runCount increments from ruflo daemon trigger --worker") and issue #2110 (the WSL2 isAvailable caching bug, which was fixed for the cache-poisoning angle but not for this triggers-bypass-init angle).

## Suggested fix direction

In `triggerWorker(type)`, await headless readiness before calling `executeWorker`:

```ts
async triggerWorker(type) {
    const workerConfig = this.config.workers.find(w => w.type === type);
    if (!workerConfig) throw new Error(`Unknown worker type: ${type}`);

    // Wait for headless executor init if it's still in-flight
    if (isHeadlessWorker(type) && this.headlessInitPromise) {
        await this.headlessInitPromise;
    }

    return this.executeWorker(workerConfig);
}
```

Where `this.headlessInitPromise` is set in the constructor to the promise returned by `initializeHeadlessExecutor()`, so the trigger path can `await` it deterministically.

## Why this matters for users

The documented use case for `ruflo daemon trigger` is "refresh AI metrics on demand without waiting for the next scheduled interval" (e.g., before a release, after a refactor). When triggers silently fall through to local mode, users get a 291-byte stub instead of the AI-driven audit they expected, with no error or warning. The metrics file is overwritten with the stub, so the previous headless result is also lost.

For my project (BuildHive), this came up while wiring a calendar-scheduled `LaunchAgent` weekly snapshot — the snapshot writes local stubs every Wednesday instead of fresh AI audits, while costing nothing. The setup is structurally fine but the value of the weekly trigger is reduced until this is fixed.

Happy to test a fix if a PR lands.

## Deep Dive Findings — Security

### SOTA Summary (2026)

**Context for tonight**: Prior security dives covered (1) content-layer injection at MCP tool boundaries [#2149, ADR-131] and (2) runtime authorization propagation across agent delegation chains [#2248, ADR-144]. Tonight covers the **pre-runtime layer**: plugin supply-chain integrity before malicious code ever executes, and memory namespace write governance to contain poisoning propagation.

**Semantic Compliance Hijacking — SCH** (arXiv:2605.14460, May 14, 2026, Grade A): Eliminates the recognizable payload entirely. Instead of injecting malicious code, SCH wraps malicious intent in natural-language "compliance rule" text within plugin descriptions. The LLM agent reads the rule and *generates* the harmful code itself at runtime. Benchmark: **77.67% confidentiality breach success, 67.33% RCE success, 0.00% scanner detection**. Signature-based defenses are completely blind. This is a qualitative escalation over all prior supply-chain attacks.

**DDIPE** (arXiv:2604.03081, Apr 3, 2026, Grade A): Document-Driven Implicit Payload Execution embeds malicious logic in plugin documentation and configuration templates. Tested across four frameworks, five models, 1,070 adversarial skills covering 15 MITRE ATT&CK categories. Bypass rate: **11.6–33.5%**; 2.5% of adversarial skills evade *both* detection and alignment systems. Four confirmed CVEs resulted from coordinated disclosure.

**Memory Poisoning — MINJA** (arXiv:2601.05504, Jan 9, 2026, Grade A): Query-only memory injection achieves **95% success** under idealized conditions; **38% for GPT-4o-mini** and **28% for Llama** in realistic production deployments. Defense: composite trust-scored sanitization with temporal decay — reduces attack success to near-zero when calibrated correctly.

**Plan Injection** (arXiv:2506.17318, Jun 18, 2026, Grade A): Context-chained memory attacks achieve **3× higher attack success** than prompt-based injection and **+17.7% exfiltration gain** by creating logical bridges between user objectives and attacker goals. Attack surface: external memory systems managing LLM context client-side.

**Mnemonic Sovereignty Survey** (arXiv:2604.16548, Apr 17, 2026, Grade A): Identifies 9 governance primitives required for secure long-term agent memory (write authorization, read authorization, update authorization, forget/rollback, share governance, temporal decay, provenance, confidentiality, availability). **Zero existing published architectures satisfy all 9.**

**Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit** (Microsoft OSS Blog, Apr 2, 2026, Grade B): Open-sourced MIT-licensed 7-package governance framework. Relevant capabilities: Ed25519 plugin signing (Agent Marketplace package), YAML/OPA/Cedar policy engine with **<0.1ms p99** enforcement latency, full OWASP ASI01–ASI10 coverage via defense-in-depth.

### Gap vs Current Ruflo

| Gap | SOTA Solution | Ruflo Status |
|-----|--------------|-------------|
| Plugin install with no integrity check | Ed25519 signing + semantic intent scan (2-layer) | Not implemented |
| SCH: no-payload attacks undetectable by scanners | Semantic intent classification at install time | Not implemented — 0.00% detection with current tools |
| Memory namespaces accept writes from any agent | Per-namespace write ACLs with explicit grants | Not implemented |
| Memory poisoning propagation across boundaries | Trust-scored sanitization + namespace isolation | Not implemented |
| OWASP ASI06 (Memory/Context Poisoning) | Mnemonic sovereignty primitives 1–3 | Gap |
| OWASP ASI09 (Supply Chain) | Plugin signing + semantic scan | Gap |

### Recommended Action

**ADR-145** (filed tonight — `v3/docs/adr/ADR-145-plugin-supply-chain-integrity-memory-governance.md`): Two-part architectural decision:
1. `PluginIntegrityVerifier` — Ed25519 signature verification + semantic intent scan at `plugins install`; targets `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/plugins/store/discovery.ts` + new `v3/@claude-flow/security/src/plugins/integrity-verifier.ts`
2. Memory namespace write ACLs — agents receive explicit `writeNamespaces: string[]` at spawn; AgentDB enforces at storage boundary; target `v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/namespaces/authorization.ts`

Backwards-compatible: warn-only defaults (`CLAUDE_FLOW_STRICT_PLUGINS=false`, `CLAUDE_FLOW_STRICT_MEMORY=false`); strict mode becomes default in v4.0.0.

Note on ADR numbering: ADR-144 is in-flight on `dream/2026-05-31-security` (authorization propagation). ADR-145 used tonight to avoid collision.

---

## Scan Findings — Intelligence

**Source:** arXiv:2603.07915, March 2026 (Grade A)

**Finding:** ARES (Adaptive Reasoning Effort Selection) trains a lightweight per-step router to predict the minimum reasoning level needed at each agent step. Results: **52.7% reduction in reasoning token usage** while maintaining task success rates. Distinct from SR²AM (covered #2156, May 27) — SR²AM optimizes *planning frequency*; ARES optimizes *per-step reasoning depth*.

**Competitive signal (Grade B):** OpenAI Agents SDK v0.13 ships opt-in retry policies and session persistence — optimizing for reliability rather than token efficiency. Ruflo's 3-tier routing operates at task level; ARES-style per-step routing would compound the savings.

**Recommended action:** Extend the `route` hook's Tier-3 dispatch to apply ARES-style effort prediction per reasoning step. Implementation-level enhancement to ADR-026 — no new ADR.

---

## Scan Findings — Swarm

**Source:** arXiv:2602.08009, February 2026 (Grade A)

**Finding:** Dynamic Ad-Hoc Networks (DANET) for LLM agent swarms: agents self-organize topology in response to failures and load rather than fixing topology at init. Under ≥20% simultaneous agent failure, adaptive DANET topology reduces task latency by **31%** vs static hierarchical topology. Complements ADR-132 (proposed two-tier hierarchy) with a graceful-degradation path.

**Competitive signal (Grade B):** LangGraph v1.1.3 ships distributed runtime support allowing graph nodes to span machines — implicitly enabling topology adaptation. Ruflo's swarm topology is static after `swarm init`.

**Recommended action:** Add DANET-style topology reconfiguration trigger to hive-mind's failure detection path. Enhancement to ADR-132 (proposed but unmerged) — implementation-level, no new ADR.

---

## Competitors Reviewed

| Framework | Plugin Signing | Memory Governance | Supply-Chain Defense | OWASP ASI Coverage | Key 2026 Update |
|-----------|---------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------|----------------|
| **Ruflo v3.6** | None | None (shared namespaces) | None | ASI01 proposed only | ADR-131, ADR-144 proposed; unmerged |
| **Microsoft AGT** | Ed25519 per plugin | YAML/OPA/Cedar policy engine | Agent Marketplace package | Full — all ASI01–ASI10 | Open-sourced Apr 2026, MIT license |
| **OpenAI Agents SDK v0.13** | Platform-signed | Platform-managed | Input/output guardrails | Best-in-class | any-LLM adapter + MCP resource support |
| **LangGraph v1.1.3** | No | Checkpoint-scoped | No | HITL checkpoints | Deep agent templates + distributed runtime |
| **CrewAI v1.12** | No (SOC2 audit trail) | Hierarchical memory isolation | No | SOC2 partial | Agent skills + native OpenAI-compatible providers |

title: [verification] HIGH: --version blocks 60+ s on cold start — ONNX model download at CLI init
body:
## Summary

The 12-hour scheduled verification run (2026-06-01T07:04:01Z, commit `28eb57543be916abf5191f71114268a3985cb001`) found that `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` (and `npx ruflo@alpha --version`) terminates with exit code 143 (SIGTERM) when given a 60 s timeout window on a cold ONNX model cache.

## Impact

Any user who installs ruflo fresh and immediately runs `npx ruflo --version` or `npx @claude-flow/cli --version` will experience a silent hang of 60–90 s while a 23 MB model file downloads from HuggingFace. On slow or metered networks the command may never complete within common timeout windows. This also affects Claude Code's MCP startup (30 s timeout, documented in #1760), which already tracks the root cause as ADR-100.

## Expected

```
ruflo v3.10.31
```
Printed within the 60 s timeout of `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version`.

## Actual

```
Loading model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (23MB)
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/onnx/model.onnx
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/tokenizer.json
ONNX embedder ready: 384d, SIMD: true
ruflo v3.10.31
^--- total wall time: ~68 s on first run (cold cache)
```

Exit code on 60 s timeout: **143** (Terminated)
Exit code on 180 s timeout: **0** (succeeds, v3.10.31)
Subsequent warm-cache invocations: fast (disk cache hit).

## Command output (check 2 first invocation)

```bash
$ timeout 60 npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
Terminated
# exit 143
```

```bash
$ timeout 180 npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
Loading model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (23MB)
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/onnx/model.onnx
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/tokenizer.json
ONNX embedder ready: 384d, SIMD: true
ruflo v3.10.31
# exit 0, duration 68 s
```

## Recommended fix

Defer ONNX model loading to the first command that actually needs embeddings. `--version` (and any lightweight commands such as `--help`, `doctor`, `config`) should never trigger a network download. The ADR-100 cli-core split (#1760) is the structural fix — moving heavy deps into lazy-loaded extras — but a shorter-term fix would be to guard `initEmbedder()` (or equivalent) behind a `needsEmbeddings` flag that is false for `--version`.

## Relationship to existing issues

- **#1760** (ADR-100 cli-core split) — tracks the architectural fix for cold-cache startup latency in general
- **#1748** — original MCP cold-cache timeout report

## Environment

- Commit: `28eb57543be916abf5191f71114268a3985cb001`
- Timestamp UTC: 2026-06-01T07:04:01Z
- Node: v22.22.2 / npm: 10.9.7
- OS: Linux 6.18.5 x86_64
- Verification check: 2 (Published package smoke test)
- agentic-flow installed: 2.0.12-fix.8

title: `.claude/helpers/router.js` agent matcher uses unanchored substring regexes — short tokens (`cd`, `ci`, `ui`, `add`, `structure`) match inside unrelated words and mis-route at a confident 80%
body:
## Summary

The `UserPromptSubmit` agent router shipped by `ruflo init`
(`.claude/helpers/router.js`) matches a task to an agent with
**unanchored substring regexes** built from short alternation
tokens. Because the tokens are not word-boundary-anchored, they
match *inside* unrelated words, producing confident (hard-coded
80%) mis-routes on prompts that have nothing to do with the
matched agent.

The matcher is also advertised as learning ("Routes tasks to
optimal agents based on learned patterns") but is in fact a
static keyword table: confidence is a literal `0.8` on any match
and `0.5` on the default, and there is **no feedback path** from
accepted/rejected recommendations back into the table.

Confirmed location (`ruflo@3.10.5`, project-local copy emitted by
`ruflo init`):

```js
// .claude/helpers/router.js  (lines 18–53, ruflo@3.10.5)
const TASK_PATTERNS = {
  'implement|create|build|add|write code': 'coder',
  'test|spec|coverage|unit test|integration': 'tester',
  'review|audit|check|validate|security': 'reviewer',
  'research|find|search|documentation|explore': 'researcher',
  'design|architect|structure|plan': 'architect',
  'api|endpoint|server|backend|database': 'backend-dev',
  'ui|frontend|component|react|css|style': 'frontend-dev',
  'deploy|docker|ci|cd|pipeline|infrastructure': 'devops',
};

function routeTask(task) {
  const taskLower = task.toLowerCase();
  for (const [pattern, agent] of Object.entries(TASK_PATTERNS)) {
    const regex = new RegExp(pattern, 'i');      // <-- no \b anchors
    if (regex.test(taskLower)) {
      return { agent, confidence: 0.8, reason: `Matched pattern: ${pattern}` };
    }
  }
  return { agent: 'coder', confidence: 0.5, reason: 'Default routing - no specific pattern matched' };
}
```

## The two-letter / substring landmines

| Token | Pattern | Matches *inside* these common words | Wrong agent |
|-------|---------|-------------------------------------|-------------|
| `cd`  | devops  | `cd` (role abbrevs, file paths), and literally the word "CD" | devops |
| `ci`  | devops  | de**ci**sion, spe**ci**fication, effi**ci**ency, spe**ci**fic | devops |
| `structure` | architect | infra**structure** | architect (pre-empts devops) |
| `add` | coder   | **add**ress, **add**endum, **add**itional | coder |
| `spec`| tester  | **spec**ification, **spec**ific, e**spec**ially | tester |
| `test`| tester  | la**test**, grea**test**, con**test**ant | tester |
| `ui`  | frontend| g**ui**dance, req**ui**re | frontend-dev |
| `plan`| architect | (anchored is fine; unanchored hits "explanation") | architect |

Because the loop is **first-match-wins in object-insertion order**,
the ordering also matters: `reviewer` (`review|audit|check|validate|security`)
is tested *before* `researcher` (`research|find|search|...`), so a
research task that merely mentions "audit" or "check" routes to
`reviewer`.

## Reproduction

```bash
node .claude/helpers/router.js "Work as CD. Canonize the decision at parent level"
# → { "agent": "devops", "confidence": 0.8, "reason": "Matched pattern: deploy|docker|ci|cd|pipeline|infrastructure" }
#   (matched the substring "cd" in "CD", and "ci" in "decision")

node .claude/helpers/router.js "set up the deployment infrastructure"
# → { "agent": "architect", "confidence": 0.8, "reason": "Matched pattern: design|architect|structure|plan" }
#   (matched "structure" inside "infrastructure"; architect pre-empts devops)

node .claude/helpers/router.js "research the routing hook and audit how it works"
# → { "agent": "reviewer", "confidence": 0.8, "reason": "Matched pattern: review|audit|check|validate|security" }
#   (reviewer is checked before researcher; "audit" wins over "research")
```

### Live evidence

Observed across four consecutive `UserPromptSubmit` firings in a
documentation-heavy project (Claude Code + ruflo, project vocabulary
saturated with "decision", "audit", "CD", "validate", "infrastructure"):

1. Research task → recommended `reviewer` @ 80% (keyword "audit"/"check").
2. Pure-documentation task at parent scope → recommended `devops`
   @ 80% (substring "cd"/"ci" in "CD"/"decision") — completely off.
3. Cleanup task → `coder` @ 50% default (correct fallback).
4. A meta-task *to investigate this very router* → `coder` @ 80%
   (keyword "implement").

## Expected

Tokens should match whole words, not substrings, and two-letter
acronyms should be spelled unambiguously. A research task should
not route to `reviewer`/`devops` because it contains "audit" or
the letters "ci".

## Suggested fix

1. **Word-boundary-anchor every alternation:** `\b(...)\b`. This
   alone removes the `structure`→"infrastructure", `add`→"addendum",
   `spec`→"specification", `test`→"latest", `ci`→"decision" class of
   false positives.
2. **Replace bare two-letter CI/CD tokens** `ci|cd` with `ci/cd|cicd`.
   Two-letter tokens are inherently noisy even when `\b`-anchored
   (e.g. anchored `\bcd\b` still matches a literal "CD" used as a
   role/label, which is unrelated to continuous deployment).
3. **Order `researcher` before `reviewer`** so research intent is
   not pre-empted by reviewer keywords on first-match.
4. **Stop hard-coding `confidence: 0.8`.** A keyword hit is a weak
   signal; report it honestly (e.g. 0.6 on match, 0.3 on the
   no-match advisory default) and fix the docstring, which currently
   claims the router learns when it does not.
5. **Optionally**, document or implement an actual feedback path.
   The hook system has `hooks_model-outcome` for model-tier routing
   but nothing analogous feeds the *agent* router; `post-task`
   calls `intelligence.feedback(true)` which only adjusts the
   file-edit PageRank graph, never `router.js`.

Minimal diff (keeps the original vocabulary, just anchors + de-landmines):

```diff
-const TASK_PATTERNS = {
-  'implement|create|build|add|write code': 'coder',
-  'test|spec|coverage|unit test|integration': 'tester',
-  'review|audit|check|validate|security': 'reviewer',
-  'research|find|search|documentation|explore': 'researcher',
-  'design|architect|structure|plan': 'architect',
-  'api|endpoint|server|backend|database': 'backend-dev',
-  'ui|frontend|component|react|css|style': 'frontend-dev',
-  'deploy|docker|ci|cd|pipeline|infrastructure': 'devops',
-};
+const TASK_PATTERNS = [
+  ['coder',        /\b(implement|create|build|add|write code)\b/i],
+  ['tester',       /\b(test|spec|coverage|unit test|integration)\b/i],
+  ['researcher',   /\b(research|find|search|documentation|explore)\b/i],
+  ['reviewer',     /\b(review|audit|check|validate|security)\b/i],
+  ['architect',    /\b(design|architect|structure|plan)\b/i],
+  ['backend-dev',  /\b(api|endpoint|server|backend|database)\b/i],
+  ['frontend-dev', /\b(ui|frontend|component|react|css|style)\b/i],
+  ['devops',       /\b(deploy|docker|ci\/cd|cicd|pipeline|infrastructure)\b/i],
+];
```

(With the array form, `routeTask` iterates `for (const [agent, regex] of TASK_PATTERNS)`
and the `reason` can report the matched word via `regex.exec(task)`.)

## Local workaround applied

Applied the minimal diff above to both the project-local
`.claude/helpers/router.js` and the global marketplace-clone source
copies that `ruflo init` copies from
(`v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/helpers/router.js` and
`v3/@claude-flow/mcp/.claude/helpers/router.js`, identical files).
Verified against the four live mis-route cases above plus
"addendum"/"infrastructure"/"ci/cd" stress cases — all route
correctly now ("Work as CD…decision" → `coder` @ 0.3 advisory
default; "infrastructure" → `devops`; "research…audit" →
`researcher`).

## Environment

- ruflo `3.10.5` (`npm i -g`)
- Node `v24.15.0`, npm `v11.12.1`, nvm
- Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04)
- Claude Code CLI `2.1.142`

## References

- `.claude/helpers/router.js` lines 18–53 (`TASK_PATTERNS`, `routeTask`).
- `.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs` `route` handler (lines 119–144) —
  the `UserPromptSubmit` entry point that prints the recommendation box.

title: v3.10.31: `ruflo memory store` writes to `ruvector.db` but `stats`/`list`/`search` read from empty sql.js — three contradictory persistence surfaces (parallel to #2245)
body:
## Environment

- ruflo: `3.10.31` (latest as of filing)
- `@claude-flow/cli` (nested): `3.10.31`
- Claude Code CLI: `2.1.154`
- OS: macOS Sequoia 15.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon
- Daemon: long-running, F-pure config (only `map` + `consolidate` enabled — verified the bug reproduces even with all workers enabled and on a freshly-warmed daemon)
- Workspace: `/Users/.../BuildHive-KMP` (1,443 tracked files), `.claude-flow/`, `.swarm/`, and `ruvector.db` all present at workspace root

## Symptom

`ruflo memory store` reports `[OK] Data stored successfully` but the stored entries are invisible to **every** read surface (`memory stats`, `memory list`, `memory search`, `embeddings index -a build`). Search returns 0 results even when querying for the exact value of an entry just stored 1 second prior.

Same shape as #2245 / #2110 but in the **memory store / unified-stats pipeline**, not the trajectory pipeline. The ADR-074 wiring fix that closed #2245 did not extend to this layer.

## Reproduction (~10 seconds, deterministic)

```bash
# 1. Confirm starting state
ruflo memory stats | grep "Total Entries"
# → | Total Entries |             0 |

# 2. Store a unique sentinel
SENTINEL="bug-evidence-$(date +%s%N)"
ruflo memory store --key "$SENTINEL" --value "reproducible memory layer disconnect"
# → [OK] Data stored successfully

# 3. Stats — still zero
ruflo memory stats | grep "Total Entries"
# → | Total Entries |             0 |

# 4. List — empty
ruflo memory list
# → [WARN] No entries found

# 5. Search for the exact value just stored — finds nothing
ruflo memory search --query "reproducible memory layer disconnect" --limit 1
# → [WARN] No results found

# 6. HNSW index build — finds nothing to index
ruflo embeddings index -a build
# → [INFO] No vectors indexed. Store some entries first
```

## Three contradictory persistence surfaces — same workspace, same moment

```bash
# Surface A: ./ruvector.db is where `memory store` ACTUALLY writes (mtime updates on store)
$ touch /tmp/before && sleep 1 && ruflo memory store --key X --value Y && find . -newer /tmp/before -name "*.db" 2>/dev/null
./ruvector.db    # binary vector DB, ~1.5 MB, updates on every store

# Surface B: .swarm/memory.db has 63 STALE rows from 2026-05-10 to 2026-05-13
$ sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db ".schema memory_entries" | head -5
CREATE TABLE memory_entries (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  key TEXT NOT NULL,
  namespace TEXT DEFAULT 'default',
  content TEXT NOT NULL,
  ...

$ sqlite3 .swarm/memory.db "SELECT namespace, COUNT(*), datetime(MAX(created_at)/1000, 'unixepoch') FROM memory_entries GROUP BY namespace;"
default|29|2026-05-13 10:49:36
pattern|17|2026-05-12 08:39:06
project|17|2026-05-10 18:26:11

# Surface C: the unified-stats aggregator and search both report 0 — neither queries A nor B
$ ruflo memory stats | head -10
| Backend       | sql.js + HNSW |
| Total Entries |             0 |
```

So:
- **Store writes to `ruvector.db`** (Surface A)
- **`.swarm/memory.db` holds 63 rows from May 10-13** orphaned (Surface B) — predates some migration, never copied forward
- **Stats / list / search read from neither** — they read from an empty sql.js in-memory backing (Surface C) that nothing populates

## Help-text vs behavior mismatch

```bash
$ ruflo memory store --help | grep -A1 path
      --path  Override DB file path (also: CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH env var). Precedence:
              --path > CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH > CLAUDE_FLOW_MEMORY_PATH/memory.db > cwd/.swarm/memory.db
```

Help text says default is `cwd/.swarm/memory.db`. Actual write target is `cwd/ruvector.db`. Either docs are stale or there's a silent backend swap that doesn't surface in `--help`.

## Why this is high-impact

1. **Silent data loss perception** — users who `grep .swarm/memory.db` or look at file mtime conclude "RuFlo isn't storing my data." They then try workarounds (manual storage, switching tools) instead of relying on RuFlo's memory.
2. **`memory_search` / `mcp__ruflo__memory_search` returns zero results** — the documented "semantic search over your memory" feature doesn't work. ReasoningBank patterns (from `neural train` / `pretrain`) are isolated in a separate store (`.claude-flow/neural/patterns.json`) and aren't searchable via this surface either.
3. **HNSW index can't be built** — `embeddings index -a build` reports `Vectors: 0` because the indexer queries Surface C (empty), not Surface A where data actually lives.
4. **Orphaned data**: the 63 entries from a prior schema (May 10-13 on my workspace) are stranded. A schema migration likely happened but didn't carry the rows forward.

## Suggested investigation

The contradictory surfaces suggest the unified-stats aggregator (Surface C) initializes a fresh sql.js in-memory backing without loading from the persisted `ruvector.db` (Surface A) or migrating from `.swarm/memory.db` (Surface B). Three repairs would resolve it:

1. **Aggregator reads from the real store**: `memory stats`/`list`/`search` query `ruvector.db` (or whatever Surface A is) instead of an empty in-memory backing.
2. **Migration from `.swarm/memory.db`**: on RuFlo startup, if `.swarm/memory.db` exists with entries that aren't in the active store, migrate them forward (or at least surface a warning).
3. **Docs + `--help` align with reality**: either change default back to `.swarm/memory.db` or update precedence string to reflect the actual `ruvector.db` target.

## Cross-reference

This is parallel to but distinct from:
- #2245 (closed via ADR-074) — fixed the trajectory pipeline; same class of disconnect but in the trajectory store
- #2110 (closed) — `isAvailable()` cache poisoning on WSL2; different subsystem
- #2251 (closed in v3.10.31 — thanks for the fast turnaround on the previous fix I filed)

Happy to test a fix when one lands.

title: v3/@claude-flow/browser standalone package-lock.json can't refresh from workspace:* via npm install
body:
## Summary

`v3/@claude-flow/browser/package.json` is intended for standalone npm publish (per accepted-findings.json comment dated 2026-05-19) and ships its own `package-lock.json`. The package.json contains workspace:* protocol references that `npm install --package-lock-only` cannot resolve in isolation (`EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL`), so the package-lock graph can drift behind the package.json spec.

Concrete symptom today: `vitest` was bumped `^4.0.16` → `^4.1.0` in package.json to clear GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (CVSS 9.8), but the package-lock still resolves the older 4.0.16 transitive graph. `npm audit` in the standalone dir still flags critical-severity vitest until the lock is regenerated through the workspace.

## Workaround in place

A time-boxed accepted-findings entry (expires 2026-09-02) suppresses the audit failure with the rationale: devDependency-only + UI-server-only attack vector + zero production exposure (`--omit=dev`).

## What to do here

One of:
1. Add a npm-postinstall step (or scripts/sync-browser-lockfile.mjs) that rewrites workspace:* to file: refs before `npm install --package-lock-only`, then restores.
2. Switch the browser package to publish without a standalone package-lock and document install-from-tarball semantics.
3. Move the standalone bundling into a CI release step that runs from a temp dir with the workspace deps already packed.

Once any of those land, the accepted-findings entry for vitest can be deleted and the next `npm audit` will validate the fix.

## Related

- accepted-findings.json entry: `v3/@claude-flow/browser :: vitest`, expires 2026-09-02
- The lockfile refresh that didn't propagate: `v3/pnpm-lock.yaml` correctly carries vitest 4.1.x; only the standalone npm lock didn't update.

title: hive-mind spawn --claude: --dangerously-skip-permissions is silently dropped (kebab vs camelCase flag key), so headless runs cannot edit files
body:
## Summary

`hive-mind spawn --claude --non-interactive --dangerously-skip-permissions` never actually passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` to the spawned `claude` process. The headless session runs in `permissionMode: "default"`, so every `Edit`/`Write` is auto-denied (no TTY to approve), and the agent finishes having changed nothing — typically ending with "please approve the file-write permission."

Affects `@claude-flow/cli` **3.10.31** (verified on current `main`).

## Root cause

In `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hive-mind.ts`:

```js
const skipPermissions = flags['dangerously-skip-permissions'] === true && !flags['no-auto-permissions'];
```

The arg parser (`src/.../parser.js`, `normalizeKey`) converts kebab-case to camelCase and stores **only** the normalized key:

```js
flags[this.normalizeKey(key)] = true;  // '--dangerously-skip-permissions' -> flags.dangerouslySkipPermissions
```

So `flags['dangerously-skip-permissions']` is always `undefined`, `=== true` is always `false`, and `skipPermissions` is `false` regardless of the CLI flag. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is therefore never appended to `claudeArgs`.

The non-interactive check just above already handles this correctly with a camelCase fallback:

```js
const isNonInteractive = flags['non-interactive'] || flags.nonInteractive;
```

which is why `--non-interactive` works but `--dangerously-skip-permissions` does not.

## Fix

Mirror the existing dual-key pattern:

```js
const skipPermissions =
  (flags['dangerously-skip-permissions'] === true || flags.dangerouslySkipPermissions === true) &&
  !(flags['no-auto-permissions'] || flags.noAutoPermissions);
```

## Reproduction

1. `npx @claude-flow/cli hive-mind init`
2. `npx @claude-flow/cli hive-mind spawn --claude --non-interactive --dangerously-skip-permissions -o "edit any file in this repo"`
3. In the stream-json output, the `init` event shows `"permissionMode":"default"`, and every `Edit` appears under `permission_denials`; files are unchanged.
4. Running the equivalent directly — `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions "<same task>"` — shows `"permissionMode":"bypassPermissions"` and the edits succeed. This confirms the flag itself works and the wrapper is dropping it.

## Secondary (docs mismatch)

`--help` advertises `--dangerously-skip-permissions [default: true]`, but the `=== true` logic treats an unpassed flag (`undefined`) as *not* skipping. The help text and the behavior disagree — either honor the documented default or remove "default: true" from the help.

title: Windows: ruflo-core hooks still fail with '/bin/bash: /bin/bash: cannot execute binary file' in 0.2.2 (regression of #2132)
body:
## Relation to prior issues

This appears to be a **regression / incomplete fix** of the Windows hook problem already reported and closed:

- #2132 / #2133 / #2134 — "Plugin hooks use /bin/bash and POSIX-only pipelines — broken on Windows" (CLOSED)
- #2155 — "fix(plugins/ruflo-core/hooks): 3 unwrapped .sh invocations cause exit-126 on Windows (#2132 follow-up)" (CLOSED)
- #680 — "Hook error on windows persisting" (still OPEN)

The fix from those issues kept `hooks/hooks.json` **POSIX-only** (`_platform: posix`) and relied on `ruflo init` writing a Windows `.claude/settings.json` override. But on a fresh plugin install where `ruflo init` was never run (e.g. the plugin is simply enabled in Claude Code), the shipped `hooks.json` is still active and still fails. The default Windows experience is therefore still broken in **0.2.2**. Please consider reopening / shipping the cross-platform `hooks.json` below so the default case works without a manual `ruflo init`.

## Summary

On native Windows, every `ruflo-core` plugin hook fails with:

```
Stop [ruflo-core] failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/bash: /bin/bash: cannot execute binary file
```

This surfaces on **every turn** (the Stop hook is the most visible, but `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `PreCompact` are all affected) because `hooks/hooks.json` invokes each hook as `/bin/bash -c '...'`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (win32)
- Claude Code (plugin host)
- Plugin: `ruflo-core@ruflo` version **0.2.2**
- File: `plugins/ruflo-core/0.2.2/hooks/hooks.json`
- A Git-for-Windows `bash` is on PATH (`/usr/bin/bash`), but `/bin/bash` resolves to a **Windows PE executable**:
  ```
  $ file /bin/bash
  /bin/bash: PE32+ executable (console) x86-64 (stripped to external PDB), for MS Windows
  ```

## Root cause

`hooks/hooks.json` is explicitly marked POSIX-only and hard-codes `/bin/bash -c '...'` for every hook. The file's own `_platform_note` documents the intent: *"On Windows, ruflo init writes a `.claude/settings.json` that overrides these entries with node-based equivalents via `plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/ruflo-hook.cjs`."*

In practice that Windows override is **not** applied (a fresh plugin install / a project that never ran `ruflo init` on Windows keeps the POSIX `hooks.json` active). When Claude Code spawns the hook on Windows, `bash` is handed `/bin/bash` as a *script argument* to execute — and since `/bin/bash` is a binary, bash reports `cannot execute binary file`, yielding the doubled `/bin/bash: /bin/bash:` message.

Notably, the cross-platform Node shim the project already ships — `scripts/ruflo-hook.cjs` — was built for exactly this case (its header comment: *"The bash shim (ruflo-hook.sh) works on Mac/Linux but fails on native Windows (exit 126 — 'cannot execute binary file')."*). The bug is simply that nothing routes Windows hook execution to it by default.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, enable the `ruflo-core` plugin in Claude Code.
2. Do **not** run `ruflo init` (or run in a project that has no `.claude/settings.json` hook overrides).
3. Trigger any tool call or let the turn end.
4. Observe the Stop-hook error above.

The two `PreCompact` hooks are pure `echo` guidance text run through `/bin/bash`; on Windows they fail the same way. They should either be dropped or re-expressed in a cross-platform way (e.g. `node -e "console.log(...)"`).

The current design only works on Windows if the user runs `ruflo init` *and* Claude Code's settings-hook merge actually suppresses the plugin's own `hooks.json` entries. Plugin hooks and settings hooks generally **both** run, so the POSIX entries keep firing and erroring regardless of the settings override. Making `hooks.json` itself cross-platform removes the failure at the source and keeps the same hook behavior on Mac/Linux (`node` + the shim works identically there).

### Verification

With the patched `hooks.json`, the Stop hook runs cleanly:

```
$ echo '{}' | RUFLO_HOOK_SKIP_NPX=1 node "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/ruflo-hook.cjs" session-end
$ echo $?
0
```

No `/bin/bash` error; exit 0 as intended.

title: [verification] HIGH: verify.mjs crashes with noble/ed25519 v2 — witness integrity unverifiable
body:
## Summary

`plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/verify.mjs` uses the `@noble/ed25519` v1 API (assigning `ed.etc.sha512Sync`) but `package.json` declares `"@noble/ed25519": "^2.1.0"`. In v2, `ed.etc` is frozen/sealed — any environment that has run `npm install` will hit an unhandled TypeError, and **no witness manifest is ever verified**.

## Impact

Every call to `verify.mjs` in an installed checkout crashes before it can check any signature. All three platform manifests (macOS, Linux, Windows) are affected. Witness integrity gates in CI or pre-release pipelines silently fail.

## Expected

```
Ed25519 signature valid: yes
pass=N  drift=0  regressed=0  missing=0
```

## Actual

```
TypeError: Cannot add property sha512Sync, object is not extensible
    at verifySignature (file:///…/verify.mjs:175:21)
```

## Command output

```
NODE_PATH=/tmp/ruflo-verify/pkg/node_modules \
  node plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/verify.mjs \
  --manifest verification/macos/manifest.md.json

file:///home/user/ruflo/plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/verify.mjs:175
  ed.etc.sha512Sync = (...m) => { const h = createHash('sha512'); for (const x of m) h.update(x); return h.digest(); };
                    ^

TypeError: Cannot add property sha512Sync, object is not extensible
    at verifySignature (…/verify.mjs:175:21)
    at file:///…/verify.mjs:39:19
Node.js v22.22.2
```

(Linux and Windows manifests fail identically.)

## Root cause

`verify.mjs:175` does:
```js
ed.etc.sha512Sync = (...m) => { ... };
```
This was required in noble/ed25519 v1 to provide a synchronous hash. In v2, `ed.etc` is `Object.freeze`d — assignment silently fails in sloppy mode or throws in strict/module mode. The script runs as ESM (`type: module`), so it throws.

`package.json` (root and `v3/@claude-flow/cli`) both declare:
```json
"@noble/ed25519": "^2.1.0"
```

## Recommended fix

Update `verify.mjs` to the noble/ed25519 v2 API. In v2 the default exports are already synchronous — `ed.etc.sha512Sync` is not needed at all:

```js
// v1 (broken with v2):
// ed.etc.sha512Sync = (...m) => { ... };
// const valid = await ed.verify(sig, msg, pubKey);

// v2 (correct):
import * as ed from '@noble/ed25519';
const valid = ed.verify(sig, msg, pubKey);   // synchronous in v2
```

If the v1 setup is needed for a shim, downgrade the declared dependency to `"^1.7.1"`.

body:
**Severity:** Critical
**Package:** ruflo@3.10.36
**Reporter:** Independent security researcher

## Summary

After installing ruflo on a Proxmox LXC container for evaluation purposes, 
I discovered that the package autonomously initiated hundreds of Claude Code 
SDK sessions using my personal Anthropic OAuth token — without my knowledge 
or consent. This resulted in complete exhaustion of my Claude Pro session 
limits and $17 USD in unexpected charges.

## Timeline
