title: `embeddings init` fails with default model ID — `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` rejected by validator
body:
## Summary

`ruflo embeddings init` (with default flags) fails on a fresh
install with:

```
[ERROR] Initialization failed: Invalid model ID format: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
Only alphanumeric, dots, hyphens, and underscores allowed.
```

The default model ID hardcoded in
`@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/embeddings.js` is the full
Hugging Face name (`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), but the
embedder's `MODEL_REGISTRY` (in `agentic-flow`'s
`optimized-embedder.js`) uses short names only
(`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`). The slash in the full name also fails
the `VALID_MODEL_ID_PATTERN = /^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/` path-traversal
validator.

So the default fails two checks at once and there's no way to
`init` without explicitly passing `--model all-MiniLM-L6-v2`.

## Reproduction

```bash
npm install -g ruflo@latest    # confirmed on 3.10.5
cd /tmp && mkdir test-init && cd test-init
ruflo embeddings init --no-download
# [ERROR] Initialization failed: Invalid model ID format: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
```

Passing the short form works:

```bash
ruflo embeddings init --no-download --model all-MiniLM-L6-v2
# ✓ succeeds
```

## Expected

`ruflo embeddings init` with no `--model` flag should succeed
and write the standard config.

## Actual

Errors out immediately at the validator. User has to know to
pass the short form explicitly.

## Root cause

In `node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/embeddings.js`
around line 623, 638, and the examples at 632:

```js
{ name: 'model', short: 'm', type: 'string',
  description: 'ONNX model ID',
  default: 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2' },   // line 623
...
const model = ctx.flags.model || 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2';  // line 638
```

`MODEL_REGISTRY` in
`agentic-flow/dist/embeddings/optimized-embedder.js`:

```js
const MODEL_REGISTRY = {
  'all-MiniLM-L6-v2':       { url: '...Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/...' },
  'all-MiniLM-L6-v2-full':  { url: '...' },
  'bge-small-en-v1.5':      { url: '...' },
  'gte-small':              { url: '...' },
};
```

The full HF name is the URL substring inside the registry, but
the registry key is the short form.

## Suggested fix

Change the default in `embeddings.js` to the registry key:

```diff
- default: 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'
+ default: 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2'

- const model = ctx.flags.model || 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2';
+ const model = ctx.flags.model || 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2';
```

And in the examples block:

```diff
- { command: 'claude-flow embeddings init --model Xenova/all-mpnet-base-v2', ... }
+ { command: 'claude-flow embeddings init --model all-mpnet-base-v2', ... }
```

(Note: `all-mpnet-base-v2` isn't currently in MODEL_REGISTRY
either — that may want a separate add, but at minimum the
example should use the registry-style short form.)

Confirmed working locally after this patch:

```
Initialize Embedding Subsystem
| Model            | all-MiniLM-L6-v2                         |
| Dimension        | 384                                      |
...
```

## Alternative considered

Loosening `VALID_MODEL_ID_PATTERN` to allow `/` and adding the
full HF names to MODEL_REGISTRY as aliases would also work, but
the simpler fix is to make the CLI default match the registry
contract that's already in place.

## Re-verified upstream

Re-checked on `20260603T163916Z` against
`@claude-flow/cli@3.10.36/dist/src/commands/embeddings.js`:
**bug unchanged.** Same line numbers as the original draft:

- Line 623: `default: 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'`
- Line 632: example uses `--model Xenova/all-mpnet-base-v2`
- Line 638: `ctx.flags.model || 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'`
- Lines 777, 1179–1181: same full-name uses in display
  tables / status output.

`ruflo embeddings init` (no flags) still fails out-of-the-box.

## Environment

- ruflo `3.10.5` + `@claude-flow/cli` `3.10.5` at original draft;
  `ruflo@3.10.36` + `@claude-flow/cli@3.10.36` at re-verification
  (cli moved 3.10.5 → 3.10.31 → 3.10.36 between draft and filing;
  defect persists at the same line numbers).
- `agentic-flow` `2.0.13` (bundled in
  `@claude-flow/cli/node_modules/`)
- Node `v24.15.0`, npm `v11.12.1`
- Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04)

## References

- `node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/embeddings.js`
  lines 623, 632, 638
- `node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/node_modules/agentic-flow/dist/embeddings/optimized-embedder.js`
  lines 21 (`VALID_MODEL_ID_PATTERN`), 30 (`MODEL_REGISTRY`),
  63-73 (`validateModelId`)

title: `resolveAutoMemoryDir` misses underscore→dash normalization, breaks projects with `_` in path
body:
## Summary

`AutoMemoryBridge`'s `resolveAutoMemoryDir(workingDir)` is meant
to mirror Claude Code's `~/.claude/projects/{key}/memory/`
directory derivation, but only converts path separators to
dashes — not underscores. Claude Code normalizes **both**, so
any project whose path contains `_` (e.g.
`/home/phil/A-Project/RX_ERP/`) gets the wrong project key and
the bridge looks at a non-existent directory.

Result: SessionStart auto-memory import silently returns 0
entries, even when the user has memory files in the real
directory.

## Reproduction

```bash
# A project at a path containing an underscore
PROJECT=/home/phil/A-Project/RX_ERP/

# What the bridge computes:
node -e "
const m = await import('@claude-flow/memory/dist/auto-memory-bridge.js');
console.log('bridge:', m.resolveAutoMemoryDir('$PROJECT'));
"
# bridge: /home/phil/.claude/projects/-home-phil-A-Project-RX_ERP/memory

# What Claude Code actually uses (visible via `ls ~/.claude/projects/`):
ls /home/phil/.claude/projects/ | grep RX
# -home-phil-A-Project-RX-ERP   <-- note the dash, not underscore

# So the bridge looks at .../RX_ERP/memory which doesn't exist;
# the real memory dir is .../RX-ERP/memory.
```

## Expected

`resolveAutoMemoryDir(workingDir)` should produce the same
project key that Claude Code uses, so the bridge can find the
existing memory directory.

## Actual

For `/home/phil/A-Project/RX_ERP/`:
- Bridge: `-home-phil-A-Project-RX_ERP`
- Claude Code: `-home-phil-A-Project-RX-ERP`

The two diverge whenever the path contains `_`.

## Root cause

`node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/auto-memory-bridge.js`,
around line 552-563:

```js
export function resolveAutoMemoryDir(workingDir) {
    const gitRoot = findGitRoot(workingDir);
    const basePath = gitRoot || workingDir;
    // Claude Code normalizes to forward slashes then replaces with dashes
    // The leading dash IS preserved (e.g. /workspaces/foo -> -workspaces-foo)
    const normalized = basePath.split(path.sep).join('/');
    const projectKey = normalized.replace(/\//g, '-');   // ← only slashes
    return path.join(
        process.env.HOME || process.env.USERPROFILE || '~',
        '.claude', 'projects', projectKey, 'memory'
    );
}
```

Claude Code applies an additional `_` → `-` substitution.

## Suggested fix

```diff
- const projectKey = normalized.replace(/\//g, '-');
+ const projectKey = normalized.replace(/[\/_]/g, '-');
```

Confirmed working: with this single-character regex change, the
bridge resolves to the same directory Claude Code uses, and
SessionStart import finds the user's memory files.

If there are *other* characters Claude Code normalizes (dots?
spaces?), the regex should be widened accordingly — but `_` is
the only mismatch I encountered.

## Re-verified upstream

Re-checked on `20260603T163916Z`:
`@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.18/dist/auto-memory-bridge.js`
line 558 still reads
`const projectKey = normalized.replace(/\//g, '-');` — slashes
only, no underscore handling. **Bug unchanged.** (The package
was rev'd onto a separate version track since the original
draft: `3.10.5` → `3.0.0-alpha.18`. The defect persists at the
same logical site on the new track.)

## Environment

- ruflo `3.10.5` + `@claude-flow/memory` `3.10.5` at original
  draft; `ruflo@3.10.36` + `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.18`
  at re-verification.
- Claude Code CLI `2.1.142`
- Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04)

## References

- `node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/auto-memory-bridge.js`
  line ~556
- Real-world project that exposed this: any path with `_` (e.g.
  `RX_ERP`).

title: `parseMarkdownEntries` ignores Claude Code's actual auto-memory file format
`auto-memory-hook.mjs` hardcodes `workingDir: PROJECT_ROOT` (plugin path) instead of user's project
body:
## Summary

The SessionStart auto-memory hook in the ruflo plugin
marketplace
(`/home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs`)
hardcodes the bridge's `workingDir` to `PROJECT_ROOT`, where
`PROJECT_ROOT` is computed from `__dirname` and resolves to
the **plugin's own location**, not the user's project. The
bridge then computes its memory directory from the plugin
path and looks at
`~/.claude/projects/-home-phil-.claude-plugins-marketplaces-ruflo/memory/`
(non-existent) instead of the user's actual project key.

The bridge's own default
(`process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD || process.cwd()`) would work
correctly — the hook just overrides it incorrectly.

## Reproduction

Standard SessionStart flow: Claude Code invokes the hook with
the user's project as cwd. The hook does:

```js
const __dirname = dirname(__filename);
const PROJECT_ROOT = join(__dirname, '../..');
// PROJECT_ROOT = /home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/
...
const bridgeConfig = {
    workingDir: PROJECT_ROOT,   // ← wrong
    syncMode: 'on-session-end',
};
```

Then:

```js
const bridge = new memPkg.AutoMemoryBridge(backend, bridgeConfig);
await bridge.importFromAutoMemory();
```

The bridge calls `resolveAutoMemoryDir(PROJECT_ROOT)` which
returns the plugin-derived path. Nothing in that path
exists, so 0 entries are imported.

```bash
node ./auto-memory-hook.mjs import
# [AutoMemory] ✓ Imported 0 entries
```

## Expected

`workingDir` should reflect the user's project so the bridge
finds the right
`~/.claude/projects/{user-project-key}/memory/` directory.

## Actual

`workingDir` reflects the plugin marketplace clone location,
which has no corresponding `~/.claude/projects/{key}/` entry,
so every import returns 0 entries silently.

## Root cause

`auto-memory-hook.mjs` (in the ruflo plugin marketplace repo)
sets `workingDir: PROJECT_ROOT` in **both** the `doImport`
function (around line 226 in current head) and the `doSync`
function (around line 316). `PROJECT_ROOT` is derived from
`__dirname/../..` which points at the plugin's clone, not the
user's project.

The bundled `@claude-flow/memory/dist/auto-memory-bridge.js`
already handles the no-`workingDir` case correctly via:

```js
workingDir: process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD || process.cwd(),
```

(see the `defaultBridgeConfig` around line 43). The hook just
needs to stop overriding this with the wrong value.

## Suggested fix

In both `doImport` and `doSync`:

```diff
  const bridgeConfig = {
-     workingDir: PROJECT_ROOT,
+     workingDir: process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD || process.cwd(),
      syncMode: 'on-session-end',
  };
```

Confirmed working — with this patch + the dist symlinks +
the underscore normalization + parser fixes (filed
separately), the SessionStart hook ingests + vectorizes the
user's actual auto-memory files end-to-end.

## Alternative

Have the hook explicitly pass the CWD it was invoked with
(Claude Code sets it to the project root at SessionStart).
Both produce the same effective behavior.

## Re-verified upstream

Re-checked on `20260603T163916Z`:
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruvnet/ruflo/main/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs`
still has `workingDir: PROJECT_ROOT` at lines 226 and 316
(verbatim line numbers from the original draft). The bundled
`@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.18/dist/auto-memory-bridge.js`
default (`process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD || process.cwd()`) is also
unchanged. **Bug unchanged across `ruflo` 3.10.5 → 3.10.36.**

## Environment

- ruflo plugin marketplace at HEAD (verified
  `2026-05-28` against the repo as cloned by Claude Code's
  plugin sync; re-verified `2026-06-03` against
  `raw.githubusercontent.com/ruvnet/ruflo/main/...`).
- The fix should be applied to the plugin marketplace repo,
  not to ruflo proper — the hook lives in the plugin clone.

## References

- `/home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs`
  lines ~226 (`doImport`) and ~316 (`doSync`).
- `node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/auto-memory-bridge.js`
  line ~43 (default `workingDir` resolution).

title: Plugin marketplace ships `@claude-flow/*` source-only; SessionStart hook can't find `dist/` and silently degrades
body:
## Summary

The ruflo plugin marketplace
(`/home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/`) contains a
`v3/@claude-flow/*` tree with `src/` directories but no
corresponding `dist/`. The SessionStart auto-memory hook
(`auto-memory-hook.mjs`) tries to resolve the
`@claude-flow/memory` package using a four-strategy lookup
that **starts from the plugin path**:

```js
async function loadMemoryPackage() {
  // Strategy 1: Local dev (built dist)
  const localDist = join(PROJECT_ROOT, 'v3/@claude-flow/memory/dist/index.js');
  if (existsSync(localDist)) { /* import */ }

  // Strategy 2: createRequire from PROJECT_ROOT/package.json for '@claude-flow/memory'
  // Strategy 3: bare ESM import('@claude-flow/memory')
  // Strategy 4: walk up from PROJECT_ROOT looking for node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/index.js

  return null;
}
```

Where `PROJECT_ROOT = /home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/`.

In a normal `npm install -g ruflo` setup, the bundled package
lives at
`/home/phil/.nvm/.../lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/`.
**None of the four strategies reach it:**

- Strategy 1: `v3/@claude-flow/memory/dist/index.js` doesn't
  exist (only `src/`).
- Strategy 2: `PROJECT_ROOT/package.json`'s
  `createRequire('@claude-flow/memory')` can't resolve from
  the plugin clone's node_modules.
- Strategy 3: no ESM resolution from a non-module location.
- Strategy 4: walk-up from the plugin path goes
  `~/.claude/plugins/...` → `~/.claude/plugins/` →
  `~/.claude/` → `~/` → `/`. The global npm install path
  (`/home/phil/.nvm/.../lib/node_modules/`) is never crossed.

Result: the hook prints
`Memory package not available — skipping auto memory import`
on every session start, and the entire auto-memory bridge
silently does nothing.

## Reproduction

```bash
npm install -g ruflo@latest    # confirmed on 3.10.5
# Plugin marketplace gets cloned via plugin sync
# Open Claude Code in any project; check session-start output:

# SessionStart:startup hook success: [AutoMemory] Importing auto memory files into bridge...
#   Memory package not available — skipping auto memory import
```

Manually probing the hook:

```bash
node /home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs status
# === Auto Memory Bridge Status ===
#   Package:        ❌ Not found
```

## Expected

The SessionStart hook should find the `@claude-flow/memory`
package bundled with the user's installed ruflo and complete
the import without manual intervention.

## Actual

`@claude-flow/memory` is unreachable from the plugin path.
The hook degrades silently and the entire auto-memory ingest
pipeline never runs. Users see the "not available" hint but
have no obvious fix.

## Root cause / options

Multiple workable approaches:

### Option A — ship `dist/` in the plugin marketplace

Build and commit `v3/@claude-flow/{memory,cli}/dist/` so
Strategy 1 succeeds. Pros: hermetic, no path-walking required.
Cons: bloats the marketplace clone and ties plugin releases
to package-build cadence.

### Option B — add a post-install build step

If the marketplace ships only sources, add a post-install
script (`npm i && npm run build` inside each `@claude-flow/*`
subdir) so `dist/` is created on first use. Pros: smaller
checked-in tree. Cons: adds runtime install delay and
node_modules churn.

### Option C — extend the lookup to include the global npm path

Add a fifth strategy that checks the global npm prefix's
`ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/{name}/dist/index.js`:

```js
// Strategy 5: fall back to the globally-installed ruflo's bundled package
try {
  const { execSync } = await import('child_process');
  const npmPrefix = execSync('npm prefix -g', { encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim();
  const candidate = join(npmPrefix, 'lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/index.js');
  if (existsSync(candidate)) {
    return await import(`file://${candidate}`);
  }
} catch { /* fall through */ }
```

Pros: zero plugin-tree changes, picks up whatever version
the user installed. Cons: requires `npm` on PATH and assumes
the standard install layout (works on nvm + global,
Homebrew, etc.).

### Option D — change the hook to start from `process.cwd()`

If the bridge already lives in `node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/`
of the user's project (e.g., a project that depends on ruflo
directly), Strategy 4 from `process.cwd()` would find it.
Doesn't help the global-install case, but would help
project-scoped installs.

I'd recommend **Option C** as a one-file change with low blast
radius, possibly combined with Option A long-term.

## Local workaround applied

For the time being I'm using two symlinks to bridge Strategy 1:

```bash
mkdir -p /home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/memory
ln -sfn /home/phil/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist \
        /home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/memory/dist

mkdir -p /home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src
ln -sfn /home/phil/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory \
        /home/phil/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory
```

The second symlink is needed because the hook also looks up
`memory-initializer.js` from the CLI dist for the AgentDB
vectorization step.

These symlinks survive plugin marketplace updates but are
wiped on any global ruflo upgrade (target path changes).

## Re-verified upstream

Re-checked on `20260603T163916Z` against current published / HEAD
sources: **bug unchanged.**

- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruvnet/ruflo/main/.claude/helpers/auto-memory-hook.mjs`
  still implements Strategy 1–4 at lines 134–156, all anchored on
  `PROJECT_ROOT` (computed from `__dirname/../..`, i.e. the plugin
  clone). None reach the global npm install path.
- `ruflo@3.10.36` (latest) still ships `@claude-flow/cli@^3.10.3`
  and pulls `@claude-flow/memory@^3.0.0-alpha.17` transitively; the
  bundled packages live under
  `lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/*/dist/` and
  remain unreachable from the marketplace's `PROJECT_ROOT`.
- Tested on Phil's RX_ERP install with the original five-patch set
  applied; the symlinks (this issue's workaround) survive plugin-
  marketplace pulls but are wiped on global ruflo upgrades.

## Environment

  `ruflo@3.10.36` + `@claude-flow/cli@3.10.36` +
  `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.18` at re-verification.
- Plugin marketplace at HEAD as of `2026-05-28` (original) and
  `2026-06-03` (re-verification — same lookup logic + line ranges).

title: [verification] HIGH: @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version hangs >60s on cold install (ONNX model download on every startup)
body:
## Summary

`npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` does not return within 60 seconds on a cold install and must be killed (SIGTERM, exit code 143). The CLI initializes the ONNX embedder unconditionally on startup — including for trivial meta-commands like `--version` and `--help` — triggering a 23 MB model download the first time any command is run. In environments with slow or rate-limited network access, or in automated pipelines with short command timeouts, `--version` appears to hang indefinitely.

## Impact

- Users who run `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` to verify their install see an apparent hang with no output.
- CI pipelines and install scripts with ≤60s step timeouts report failure even though the package is valid.
- `ruflo@alpha --version` is unaffected (thin wrapper, no ONNX initialization).

## Expected

```
$ npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
3.10.36
```

Returns in < 1 second.

## Actual

```
--- @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version ---
Terminated
EXIT_CODES: cli=143
```

Killed at 60s timeout with no output. On the *second* invocation (ONNX model cached) the doctor command starts in ~2s.

## Evidence

Check 4 (doctor, same session, ONNX cached):
```
Loading ONNX model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2...
  Disk cache hit: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
ONNX embedder ready: 384d, SIMD: true
... (completes in ~2s without download)
```

Check 2 (--version, cold, ONNX not yet cached):
```
Loading ONNX model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2...
Loading model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (23MB)
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/onnx/model.onnx
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/tokenizer.json
```
The download phase on the verification host took >60s, causing SIGTERM.

## Root cause

The ONNX embedder initialization fires in the CLI startup path unconditionally. Meta-commands (`--version`, `--help`, `completions`) do not use embeddings and should not trigger initialization.

## Recommended fix

Lazy-load the ONNX embedder: initialize it only when a command that actually needs embeddings runs (e.g. `memory search`, `embeddings embed`). Skip initialization entirely for `--version`, `--help`, and `completions`.

Alternatively, add a fast-exit path at the top of the CLI entry point for known meta-commands before any module initialization.

## Command output

```bash
# From /tmp/ruflo-verify/pkg (fresh install, cold ONNX cache)
timeout 60 npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
# → Terminated (exit 143)

timeout 60 npx -y ruflo@alpha --version
# → ruflo v3.10.36 (exit 0, no ONNX init)
```

## Environment

- `@claude-flow/cli`: 3.10.36 (alpha tag)
- `ruflo`: 3.10.36 (alpha tag)
- Node: v22.22.2
- npm: 10.9.7
- OS: Linux 6.18.5 x86_64
- Commit: `844f68dbe5f28c4c2b13c56e8e102528aa63b629`
- Timestamp UTC: 2026-06-03T19:03:21Z

## Deep Dive Findings — Performance SOTA

### SOTA Summary (2026)

Three Grade-A/B results define the multi-agent performance frontier in 2026:

1. **LAMaS** (arXiv:2601.10560, Jan 2026 — **Grade A**): Xi Shi et al. introduce the Latency-Aware Multi-agent System, which models inter-agent task dependencies as an explicit DAG and computes the critical execution path before dispatching. Result: **38–46% reduction in critical path length** vs. the SOTA baseline for multi-agent architecture search across multiple benchmarks, while maintaining or improving task performance. Core insight: sequential scheduling is the primary latency bottleneck; the fix is topology-aware dispatch, not hardware.

2. **COMB / MAS** (arXiv:2511.00739, updated Apr 2026 — **Grade A**): CPU-Aware Overlapped Micro-Batching overlaps CPU pre/post-processing with GPU inference calls. Achieves **1.7× lower P50 latency** standalone and **3.9× lower service latency** under open-loop load. Mixed Agentic Scheduling (MAS) reduces minority-request-type latency by **2.37–2.49× at P50/P90** under heterogeneous load.

3. **Multi-agent system-level optimizer** (arXiv:2603.14703, Mar 2026 — **Grade B**): Coordinated multi-agent roles (summarise, analyse, optimise, verify) applied to microservice-level code achieve **36.6% throughput gain** and **27.8% average response time reduction** on the TeaStore benchmark. Demonstrates that architecture-level reasoning outperforms local code transforms.

### Gap vs. Current Ruflo

| Capability | SOTA 2026 | Ruflo Today | Gap |
|-----------|-----------|------------|-----|
| Inter-agent dependency graph | LAMaS: explicit DAG at spawn | None — static hierarchical order | Critical |
| Critical path scheduling | LAMaS: dispatch critical-path first | None — fixed sequential dispatch | Critical |
| CPU/GPU overlap | COMB: hooks run concurrent with LLM | Hooks synchronous on critical path | Significant |
| Published latency benchmarks | LangGraph: <1.2 s, P50/P90 public | No public benchmark | Visibility gap |

### Recommended Action

**Implement ADR-147** (filed on this branch): add `topology: "latency-aware"` mode with `after: [...]` dependency field and critical-path-first dispatch. Target: ≥30% wall-clock reduction on a 5-agent pipeline with 2 parallelizable branches. Follow-on: COMB async-hooks flag for 5–15% additional gain.

**One-sentence finding:** Prompt injection remains OWASP LLM #1 in 2026 (present in 73% of production deployments — Grade C), with MCP tool-description poisoning emerging as the highest-severity new vector for agentic systems specifically.

- MCP tool-description injection: malicious server embeds instructions in tool descriptions, which are treated as trusted by the agent at read time. Directly relevant to Ruflo's MCP plugin ecosystem.
- Cascading failures: a single compromised tool can propagate through connected memory, agents, and external APIs.

- AgentShield dataset (IEEE, 2026): 15,000 multi-agent scenarios across medical/legal/financial/autonomous-driving for Byzantine resilience evaluation — benchmark resource Ruflo could adopt.
- Traditional BFT assumes binary correctness; LLM agents have probabilistic correctness → confidence-weighted quorums are the 2026 SOTA upgrade.
- **Gap:** Ruflo's `byzantine` consensus uses standard BFT voting without agent confidence scores. No confidence weighting in `quorum-manager`.

title: 7 dependent controllers from #1610 still return null after #1611 — agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.16 doesn't export the classes @claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.19 instantiates
body:
## Relationship to existing issues (dedup done)

- **Follow-up to #1610 (closed by #1611).** That issue reported the **same exact 7 controllers** (`mutationGuard`, `gnnService`, `attestationLog`, `semanticRouter`, `guardedVectorBackend`, `rvfOptimizer`, `graphAdapter`) returning null, root-caused to `ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB()` not passing `vectorBackend` config (AgentDB → HNSWLib fallback → cascade). **In ruflo 3.10.37 that fix is present and working: `vectorBackend` now activates.** Yet **the same 7 still fail**, so the cascade explanation no longer applies — there is a **second, independent root cause**.
- **Same family as #1721 (closed):** claude-flow's repacked/bundled agentdb being out of sync with what the CLI/memory layer expects.
- **Tracked under #1228 (open, ADR-053):** design/tracking issue; does not enumerate these failures.

## Summary

On a fresh `ruflo init` + `ruflo memory init`, the Controller Registry (ADR-053) reports **`Activated: 16  Failed: 7`**. All 7 failures are silent `Controller returned null`. With #1610's fix in place (`vectorBackend` activates), the remaining cause is a **version skew inside the published bundle**: `@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.19`'s `controller-registry.js` resolves AgentDB classes via `await import('agentdb')` (its comments attribute them to *agentdb alpha.10*), but the bundle pins **`agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.16`**, where those classes are **not exported** — so `agentdbModule.<Class>` is `undefined` and each `createController()` hits its `if (!X) return null` guard.

This is not a native-binding/platform issue — all Windows `.node` binaries are present and the core 16 controllers (and 6/6 init verification) pass.

## Environment

- `ruflo` 3.10.37 / `@claude-flow/cli` 3.10.37 (installed via `npx ruflo@latest`)
- `@claude-flow/memory`: **3.0.0-alpha.19** (contains the controller registry)
- Bundled `agentdb`: **3.0.0-alpha.16** (at `@claude-flow/memory/node_modules/agentdb`)
- **The skew:** the registry in memory **alpha.19** resolves AgentDB classes that its own comments attribute to agentdb *alpha.10*, but the bundle pins agentdb **alpha.16**, which does not export them. (i.e. the memory package is *newer* than the agentdb it ships with, yet targets export names absent from that agentdb build.)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (26200), Node on win32-x64
- Backend: `sql.js + HNSW`, schema 3.0.0 — core init reports "Verification passed (6/6 tests)"

## The 7 failing controllers

| Controller | Init level | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| `mutationGuard` | 2 | `agentdbModule.MutationGuard` is `undefined` → `if (!MG) return null` |
| `gnnService` | 2 | `agentdbModule.GNNService` is `undefined` |
| `attestationLog` | 3 | `agentdbModule.AttestationLog` is `undefined` |
| `semanticRouter` | 4 | `agentdbModule.SemanticRouter` is `undefined` |
| `rvfOptimizer` | 5 | `agentdbModule.RVFOptimizer` is `undefined` |
| `guardedVectorBackend` | 5 | **Cascade**: `createController()` calls `this.get('mutationGuard')`, which is null → `if (!vb || !guard) return null` |
| `graphAdapter` | 6 | agentdb exposes no `graphAdapter` field and `getController('graphAdapter')` is unhandled |

## Root cause detail

`@claude-flow/memory/dist/controller-registry.js` → `createController(name)` resolves these classes via `const m = await import('agentdb'); const X = m.MutationGuard; if (!X) return null;`. The inline comments assert these were *"exported from agentdb 3.0.0-alpha.10 (ADR-060 / ADR-062)"*.

Probing the actually-installed `agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.16` module:

```
GNNService:           NOT EXPORTED
MutationGuard:        NOT EXPORTED
AttestationLog:       NOT EXPORTED
SemanticRouter:       NOT EXPORTED
RVFOptimizer:         NOT EXPORTED
GuardedVectorBackend: NOT EXPORTED
```

So six controllers fail directly, and `guardedVectorBackend` fails as a downstream cascade of `mutationGuard`. `graphAdapter` fails because alpha.16 neither exposes the field nor handles the name in `getController()` (its switch only handles `memory/reflexion/skills/causal/causalGraph` — see the `#2019` comments already in `controller-registry.js`).

## Reproduction

```bash
npx ruflo@latest init
npx ruflo memory init     # banner shows "Activated: 16  Failed: 7"
```

To enumerate the exact names + errors, call the same bridge the CLI uses and dump the public `registry.controllers` map:

```js
// node ESM, BRIDGE=@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/memory-bridge.js, DBPATH=.swarm/memory.db
const { getControllerRegistry } = await import('file:///' + process.env.BRIDGE.replace(/\\/g,'/'));
const reg = await getControllerRegistry(process.env.DBPATH);
for (const [name, e] of reg.controllers)
  if (!e.enabled) console.log(`L${e.level}  ${name}  ::  ${e.error}`);
```

Output:
```
L2  gnnService           ::  Controller returned null
L2  mutationGuard        ::  Controller returned null
L3  attestationLog       ::  Controller returned null
L4  semanticRouter       ::  Controller returned null
L5  guardedVectorBackend ::  Controller returned null
L5  rvfOptimizer         ::  Controller returned null
L6  graphAdapter         ::  Controller returned null
```

## Impact

- **Severity: low / cosmetic for core use.** All core memory controllers activate (hierarchicalMemory, reasoningBank, vectorBackend, memoryGraph, skills, reflexion, causalGraph, learningSystem, nightlyLearner, memoryConsolidation, mmrDiversityRanker, contextSynthesizer, graphTransformer, batchOperations, explainableRecall, tieredCache). Store / semantic search / learning / consolidation all work.
- **What is silently unavailable:** the ADR-060 integrity layer (`mutationGuard`, `attestationLog`, `guardedVectorBackend` — i.e. no mutation attestation / audit log on vector writes) and the ADR-062 extras (`gnnService`, `semanticRouter`, `rvfOptimizer`). Users who expect the security/attestation guarantees get them silently disabled, which is the more concerning part.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)

1. **Align versions** — publish `@claude-flow/memory` against the agentdb build it actually bundles (alpha.16), updating `createController()` to the real export names; **or** pin/bump `agentdb` to a version that does export `MutationGuard`/`AttestationLog`/`GuardedVectorBackend`/`GNNService`/`SemanticRouter`/`RVFOptimizer`.
2. **Add `graphAdapter` + `vectorBackend` handling** to agentdb's `getController()` switch (the `#2019` comments already note the switch is incomplete).
3. **Surface a real reason instead of `Controller returned null`** — distinguish "class not exported in installed agentdb vX" from "constructor threw," so the banner is actionable rather than a bare count.
4. **(Optional) Don't count intentionally-absent controllers as "Failed"** — if a feature isn't in the pinned agentdb, register it as `skipped`/`unsupported` rather than `failed`, to avoid alarming users on a healthy install.

## Note

`guardedVectorBackend` will keep failing as a cascade until `mutationGuard` resolves, even if the other five are fixed — worth fixing `mutationGuard` first or making the dependency explicit in the failure message.

---

<sub>Reported from a real ruflo 3.10.37 install on Windows 11; controller status verified against the live `@claude-flow/cli` memory bridge and `agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.16` module exports.</sub>

fix(hooks): #2272 cross-platform hooks.json via node + ruflo-hook.cjs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2272 — Windows users get `/bin/bash: cannot execute binary file` on every hook because `hooks.json` hard-codes POSIX-only `/bin/bash -c` commands.

## Root cause

PR #2136 added `ruflo-hook.cjs` (a cross-platform Node.js shim) and PR #2161 wrapped hooks in `/bin/bash -c`, but the design relied on `ruflo init` writing Windows overrides to `.claude/settings.json`. In practice, users just `claude plugins enable ruflo-core` — the POSIX `hooks.json` is loaded directly, and `/bin/bash` fails on native Windows.

## Fix

Make `hooks.json` truly cross-platform by replacing `/bin/bash` with `node` + `ruflo-hook.cjs` in all three copies. The `.cjs` shim already existed and supported the core subcommands; this PR extends it with:

- **pre-compact** subcommand (`--mode manual|auto`) — echo PreCompact guidance locally
- **Generic stdin-JSON arg extraction** for 10+ additional hook subcommands: `pre-edit`, `pre-command`, `pre-task`, `pre-search`, `mcp-pre`, `post-task`, `post-search`, `mcp-post`, `route`, `session-start`, `notify`
- **post-command** and **post-edit** with internal JSON parsing (no jq/pipeline needed)

The old `/bin/bash -c` path is gone. Mac/Linux/Windows all use the same `node` invocation now.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `plugins/ruflo-core/hooks/hooks.json` | 7 hooks: `/bin/bash` → `node` |
| `.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` | 7 hooks: `/bin/bash` → `node` |
| `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` | 14 hooks: `/bin/bash` → `node` |
| `plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/ruflo-hook.cjs` | Add pre-compact, generic stdin dispatch |

## Verification

```bash
# JSON validation (all 3 copies)
$ node -e "JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(hooks.json,utf8))" → OK ×3

# Smoke tests (all exit 0 on Windows)
$ node ruflo-hook.cjs pre-compact --mode manual   → exit 0
$ node ruflo-hook.cjs pre-compact --mode auto     → exit 0
$ node ruflo-hook.cjs session-end ...             → exit 0
$ node ruflo-hook.cjs modify-bash                 → exit 0
$ echo {tool_input:{...}} | node ruflo-hook.cjs post-command → exit 0
$ echo {tool_input:{...}} | node ruflo-hook.cjs post-edit    → exit 0
```

title: fix(cli): #2269 honor --dangerously-skip-permissions in hive-mind spawn
body:
Fixes #2269.

## Summary

`hive-mind spawn --claude --non-interactive --dangerously-skip-permissions` was silently dropping the flag. The arg parser (`parser.ts` `normalizeKey`) converts kebab-case to camelCase and stores only the normalized key, so `flags['dangerously-skip-permissions']` was always `undefined` and the `=== true` check always failed. The headless `claude` child therefore ran in `permissionMode: \"default\"`, every `Edit`/`Write` landed in `permission_denials`, and the agent finished having changed nothing.

## Fix

Mirror the dual-key fallback used a few lines above for `isNonInteractive`:

\`\`\`ts
const skipPermissions =
  (flags['dangerously-skip-permissions'] === true || flags.dangerouslySkipPermissions === true) &&
  !(flags['no-auto-permissions'] || flags.noAutoPermissions);
\`\`\`

This is the patch the issue reporter (@rvrheenen) proposed verbatim — kept narrow on purpose. Also resolves the documented `default: true` mismatch the secondary note in #2269 called out, because the parser populates the camelCase key with the option's default value.

## Verification

Repro from the issue:

\`\`\`
npx @claude-flow/cli hive-mind spawn --claude --non-interactive \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions -o \"edit any file in this repo\"
\`\`\`

- Before: stream-json \`init\` event shows \`\"permissionMode\":\"default\"\`; every \`Edit\` lands in \`permission_denials\`; files unchanged.
- After: \`--dangerously-skip-permissions\` is appended to \`claudeArgs\`; spawned \`claude\` runs in \`bypassPermissions\`; edits succeed (matches running \`claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions\` directly).

## Scope

One file, one logical change. No behavior change for users who don't pass the flag (parser default behavior unchanged); only the previously-broken path is restored.

title: Invalid MCP allow rule generated in settings.json (mcp__claude-flow__:* should be mcp__claude-flow__*)
body:
## Bug

The `claude-flow` init/setup process writes an invalid permission rule into `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
"permissions": {
  "allow": [
    "mcp__claude-flow__:*"
  ]
}
```

Claude Code rejects this with:

> Invalid permission rule \"mcp__claude-flow__:*\" was skipped: Wildcard tool name \"mcp__claude-flow__:*\" is not supported in allow rules. An allow pattern must name the scope it widens — globs are permitted only in the tool position after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix. Deny and ask rules accept wildcards anywhere.

## Root Cause

The colon (`:`) before the `*` is not valid syntax for an allow rule. The correct form is:

```
mcp__<server>__<toolname>
```

where the tool name position accepts a glob. There is no colon separator.

## Fix

Change:
```json
"mcp__claude-flow__:*"
```
to:
```json
"mcp__claude-flow__*"
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init` (or the setup that generates `.claude/settings.json`)
2. Open the generated `settings.json` and inspect `permissions.allow`
3. Start Claude Code — the `/doctor` command reports the skipped rule

## Environment

- Platform: darwin/arm64
- Claude Code version: current
- Claude Flow CLI: `@claude-flow/cli@latest`

5. **WebMCP Tool Surface Poisoning** (arXiv:2606.06387, **Grade A**): Attackers can inject malicious tools via third-party scripts during active sessions — relevant to Ruflo's plugin hot-load path.

6. **Agent Recusal via In-Band Access-Deny** (arXiv:2606.06460, **Grade A**): Governance control signals achieve 100% voluntary recusal when present. ADR-144 covers authorization propagation but not voluntary recusal via in-band signals.

title: [verification] HIGH: v3-ci.yml main CI failing — @claude-flow/security build TS2307 Cannot find module @noble/ed25519
body:
## Summary

`@claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.8` fails to compile in CI because `@noble/ed25519` is imported in `src/plugins/integrity-verifier.ts:260` but is not declared in the package's own `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. All 5 most recent v3-ci.yml runs on `main` are `failure` as a result.

## Impact

- CI pipeline on `main` has been continuously failing since at least 2026-06-02
- The `ToolOutputGuardrail smoke (ADR-131)` job is completely blocked
- New security module releases cannot be validated
- Same root cause blocks witness signature verification in source-only checkouts (see related MEDIUM issue)
- Unblocks only when `@noble/ed25519` is added to `@claude-flow/security/package.json` directly

## Expected

`@claude-flow/security` TypeScript build completes successfully:

```
> @claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.8 build
> tsc
```

## Actual

```
##[error]src/plugins/integrity-verifier.ts(260,30): error TS2307: Cannot find module '@noble/ed25519' or its corresponding type declarations.
/home/runner/work/ruflo/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/security:
 ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL  @claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.8 build: `tsc`
Exit status 2
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
```

## Command output

Failing job: **ToolOutputGuardrail smoke (ADR-131)** (job id 79526004357, run id 26953932236)
Failing step: **Build @claude-flow/security**

```
2026-06-04T13:13:19.9793467Z > tsc
2026-06-04T13:13:21.6780573Z ##[error]src/plugins/integrity-verifier.ts(260,30): error TS2307: Cannot find module '@noble/ed25519' or its corresponding type declarations.
2026-06-04T13:13:21.6952277Z  ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL  @claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.8 build: `tsc`
2026-06-04T13:13:21.6952995Z Exit status 2
2026-06-04T13:13:21.7197181Z ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
```

## Recommended fix

Add `@noble/ed25519` to `v3/@claude-flow/security/package.json` `dependencies`:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@noble/ed25519": "^2.0.0"
}
```

Per the lesson from #2112: root-level `overrides` do not propagate into published packages — the dependency must be declared explicitly in the package that imports it.

body:
## Summary

`scripts/smoke-trajectory-graph-edges.mjs` (graph trajectory hooks smoke, ADR-130 P3) crashes with JavaScript heap out-of-memory during TEST 2 (post-task reinforced-by edge write). Node's heap grows to 4050+ MB before GC gives up and the process is killed with SIGABRT (exit 134). TEST 1 passes cleanly.

## Impact

- CI pipeline on `main` has been continuously failing since at least 2026-06-02 (all 5 most recent runs are `failure`)
- ADR-130 P3 trajectory graph hook cannot be validated in CI
- If the memory growth reflects a real runtime leak (not just test-harness specific), production agent sessions using trajectory graph edge recording could be affected
- Unblocks only when the memory leak in TEST 2 is identified and fixed

## Expected

`smoke-trajectory-graph-edges.mjs` completes all test cases successfully:

```
PASS  1d: graph_edges has trajectory-caused row (count=1)
TEST 2: post-task writes reinforced-by edge
PASS  2x: ...
```

## Actual

```
PASS  1d: graph_edges has trajectory-caused row (count=1)

TEST 2: post-task writes reinforced-by edge
[2768:0xb255000]    29877 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 4050.5 (4128.9) -> 4048.3 (4130.1) MB
[2768:0xb255000]    30108 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 4051.7 (4130.1) -> 4050.5 (4150.6) MB

FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
Aborted (core dumped) node scripts/smoke-trajectory-graph-edges.mjs
##[error]Process completed with exit code 134.
```

## Command output

Failing job: **graph trajectory hooks smoke (ADR-130 P3)** (job id 79526307991, run id 26953932236)
Failing step: **Run trajectory graph edges smoke**

```
2026-06-04T13:15:52.0767426Z   PASS  1c: tool returns in <200ms (took 1ms)
2026-06-04T13:15:52.5803327Z   PASS  1d: graph_edges has trajectory-caused row (count=1)
2026-06-04T13:15:52.5805306Z
2026-06-04T13:15:52.5806601Z TEST 2: post-task writes reinforced-by edge
2026-06-04T13:16:21.7899691Z [2768:0xb255000]    29877 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 4050.5 MB
2026-06-04T13:16:21.7905207Z [2768:0xb255000]    30108 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 4051.7 MB
2026-06-04T13:16:21.7907422Z FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory

2026-06-04T13:16:40.3421438Z ##[error]Process completed with exit code 134.
```

Time between TEST 2 start and crash: ~29 seconds.

## Recommended fix

1. Profile `smoke-trajectory-graph-edges.mjs` TEST 2 — likely a mock/stub or graph structure that accumulates in memory without disposal between test cases.
2. Add explicit cleanup between TEST 1 and TEST 2 (close DB handles, clear in-memory graph caches).
3. Add `--max-old-space-size=512` to the CI smoke invocation to surface leaks faster with a cleaner error.
4. Consider whether the trajectory graph reinforced-by edge writer accumulates all prior edges in memory during batch writes.

title: [verification] MEDIUM: witness verify blocked — @noble/ed25519 not installed in source-only checkout
body:
## Summary

The scheduled verification runner cannot confirm witness signature integrity because `@noble/ed25519` cannot be resolved from any package search path in this source-only checkout. `plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/verify.mjs` exits 2 (precondition failure) for all 3 platform manifests. This is the designed behavior per issue #1880 (exit 2 = "needs install+build", not a real signature failure), but it means signature integrity remains unconfirmed on every scheduled run.

Note: This finding shares the same root cause as the HIGH finding in issue #2311 (`@noble/ed25519` missing from `@claude-flow/security/package.json` dependencies). Fixing #2311 should resolve this as well, since `@claude-flow/security` is in the package search path used by verify.mjs.

## Impact

- Witness signature integrity cannot be confirmed on every scheduled verification run
- Verification confidence is degraded
- No user-visible impact — published packages are clean (Check 2 passed, v3.10.37 all dist-tags aligned)
- Not a real signature failure (exit 2 ≠ exit 1)

## Expected

```
Ed25519 signature valid: yes
pass=N
drift=0
regressed=0
missing=0
```

## Actual

```
verify.mjs: could not load @noble/ed25519 from any of:
  /home/user/ruflo
  /home/user/ruflo/v3
  /home/user/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/cli
  /home/user/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation
  last error: Cannot find module '@noble/ed25519'

Fix: from the repo root, run `npm install` (the dep is declared
in the root package.json under @noble/ed25519). If your runner
is a source-only checkout, your verification pipeline must run
`npm ci && npm run build` before invoking this script. See #1880
for the full diagnosis.
```

Exit code: 2 (precondition failure, per #1880 design)

## Recommended fix

Option A (preferred): Fix #2311 — add `@noble/ed25519` to `@claude-flow/security/package.json` dependencies. Since that package is in the verify.mjs search path, the dep will be found automatically.

Option B: Update the scheduled verification runner to run `npm ci && npm run build` before Check 1, or run from a pre-built artifact.

## Relevant report section

Check 1: Witness signature verification — SEVERITY:MEDIUM

## Commit SHA

`d065b15927c6ba7318623e8af123e7980e4c6681`

## Timestamp UTC

2026-06-07T07:05:32Z

title: Competitive ruliology: arena/tournament swarm modes, co-evolution, and an emergence dashboard
body:
## Summary

Stephen Wolfram's [**Games Between Programs: The Ruliology of Competition**](https://writings.stephenwolfram.com/2026/06/games-between-programs-the-ruliology-of-competition/)
reframes multi-agent systems as **competition between programs**: each strategy is a simple
program (FSM / cellular automaton / Turing machine), and the interesting questions — *which
strategies win? are winners simple or complex?* — are only answerable by **running** the
competition (computational irreducibility).

Ruflo's swarms today are cooperative (pipeline / fan-out / supervisor). This proposes adding
**first-class competitive execution** plus the learning and observability around it, as
opt-in plugins/extensions — no breaking changes to cooperative swarms.

I've already built a **working prototype plugin** (`plugins/ruflo-arena`, branch
`feat/ruflo-arena-plugin`, PR to follow) to de-risk the idea. Opening this to get maintainer
direction before going further.

## What's proposed

1. **Arena & tournament execution modes** — a `GameSpec` payoff abstraction, deterministic
   seedable matches, round-robin tournaments producing Wolfram's **competitive array**
   (mean-payoff matrix). *(ADR-147)*
2. **Co-evolutionary learning** — extend the SONA loop (RETRIEVE→JUDGE→DISTILL→CONSOLIDATE)
   with mutation operators + selection and **mutual co-evolution** (arms races); fitness comes
   from arena/tournament outcomes. *(ADR-148)*
3. **Emergence observability dashboard** — competitive-array heatmaps, fitness curves
   (plateau→breakthrough), evolution timelines, arms-race traces, as a Ruflo dashboard plugin. *(ADR-149)*
4. **Visualization architecture decision** — *most/all UI lives inside Ruflo* (plugins on the
   existing web UI + agent dashboard); RuVector stays a data/intelligence backend with no UI;
   no separate viz repo until components are large **and** reusable across multiple ruvnet
   projects. *(ADR-150 + the joint ADR-154 ↔ RuVector ADR-202)*

### Cross-cutting (shared with RuVector — see companion issue)

- **Hybrid simple-program + LLM strategies with distillation** — span the spectrum and distill
  winning LLM behavior into cheap, reproducible programs via 3-tier routing + SONA DISTILL. *(ADR-151)*
- **Ruflo ↔ RuVector integration layer** — MCP/HTTP/RVF contract, shared ID namespace,
  AgentDB-cache degradation (the ADR-130 pattern). *(ADR-152)*
- **Safe execution & resource governance** — sandbox untrusted/evolved/LLM strategies; enforce
  timeouts (Wolfram's non-halting programs), budgets, `@claude-flow/security` SafeExecutor,
  aidefence screening. *(ADR-153)*
- **Governance & contribution** — paired ADRs across the two repos, versioned contracts,
  reproducibility. *(ADR-155)*

## Prototype (already working)

`plugins/ruflo-arena` — zero-dep TS plugin, `tsc` clean, **23 Vitest tests passing**:

- Strategies-as-programs (Moore-machine FSMs: tit-for-tat, grim, pavlov, …) + mutation operators.
- `arena/run`, `tournament/run`, `evolve/run`, `coevolve/run`, `run/get`, `run/list` MCP tools
  (Zod-validated, `{success,result}` envelope) + a CLI.
- Persistence via a pluggable `RunStore` (file artifacts + an AgentDB summary payload for
  `memory_store`, so runs are semantically searchable — the local stand-in for the RuVector layer).

Representative output (PD round-robin, mean-vs-field): `grim ≈ 2.99`, `always-defect ≈ 2.76`,
`tit-for-tat ≈ 2.50` … `always-cooperate ≈ 1.88`; evolution climbs ~2.78 → ~3.00 with the
classic plateau→breakthrough curve; co-evolution oscillates as an arms race.

## Proposed phasing (smallest-first)

- **Phase 1 (ready now):** `ruflo-arena` plugin — arenas, tournaments, evolution, co-evolution,
  MCP tools, persistence. No core changes.
- **Phase 2:** wire fitness into SONA co-evolution (ADR-148); AgentDB run history.
- **Phase 3:** emergence dashboard plugin (ADR-149/150).
- **Phase 4:** RuVector data/intelligence layer behind the integration contract (ADR-152); LLM
  strategies + distillation (ADR-151); sandboxing hardening (ADR-153).

## Non-goals (v1)

LLM-strategy execution, untrusted-program sandboxing, the dashboard UI, and the RuVector data
layer are **out of scope** for the first plugin (tracked in the ADRs above).

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is competitive/tournament mode a direction you want upstream in Ruflo?
2. Preferred home & surface — a standalone `ruflo-arena` plugin (as prototyped) vs. native
   `swarm arena|tournament` subcommands?
3. Appetite for the ADRs (147–155) as drafted, or would you rather own that architecture and
   have this contribute implementation only?
4. AgentDB persistence shape — is the `memory_store` namespace approach the one you'd want?

Full ADR set and the cross-repo map: drafted in the `ruliad` meta-repo (`INTEGRATION-ADRS.md`).
Happy to adjust scope to whatever is most useful.

title: feat(plugins): add ruflo-arena — competitive ruliology (arenas, tournaments, co-evolution)
body:
**Related issue:** ruvnet/ruflo#2314

## What

A new opt-in plugin, `plugins/ruflo-arena`, that adds **competition between program
strategies** to Ruflo, following Stephen Wolfram's
[*Games Between Programs: The Ruliology of Competition*](https://writings.stephenwolfram.com/2026/06/games-between-programs-the-ruliology-of-competition/).
Strategies are programs (deterministic Moore-machine FSMs); they compete under payoff games;
tournaments produce Wolfram's **competitive array**; hill-climb and **mutual co-evolution**
discover winners empirically.

This is **Phase 1** of a larger proposal (see issue) and is intentionally self-contained:
**no changes to Ruflo core**, one runtime dependency (`zod`, already common across plugins).

## Why

Ruflo swarms are cooperative today. Wolfram's work motivates first-class *competitive*
execution + the learning/observability around it. This plugin de-risks the idea with a working,
tested vertical slice before any core or cross-repo work.

## Contents

```
plugins/ruflo-arena/
  src/domain/      types (+ Zod) · games (PD, match-or-not) · strategies (FSM programs, library, mutation)
  src/engine/      rng · arena (match) · tournament (competitive array) · evolution (hill-climb + co-evolution)
  src/persistence/ RunStore (File + InMemory) + AgentDB record builder
  src/report/      competitive-array tables · ASCII heatmaps · fitness sparklines
  src/mcp-tools/   arenaTools: 6 MCP tools (arena/tournament/evolve/coevolve/run-get/run-list)
  src/cli.ts       human-facing CLI
  commands/arena.md, docs/adrs/0001-arena-contract.md, README.md
  tests/           4 suites
```

## MCP tools

`arena/run`, `tournament/run`, `evolve/run`, `coevolve/run`, `run/get`, `run/list` — all
Zod-validated, returning the `{ success, result | error }` envelope, persisting artifacts via a
pluggable `RunStore` and exposing an `agentdb` payload for `mcp__claude-flow__memory_store`
(searchable run history; the local stand-in for the proposed RuVector data layer).

## Integration / open question for maintainers

The 6 MCP tools are exported (`ruflo-arena/mcp-tools`) and unit-tested, but Ruflo's CLI does not
currently auto-discover or aggregate plugin tool-arrays — `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-client.ts`
registers only the CLI's own `src/mcp-tools/*`, and the existing `ruflo-graph-intelligence`
plugin's `graphIntelligenceTools` are not wired in either. **So this PR deliberately does not
touch CLI core to self-register** — I didn't want to add a one-off import to core without your
call on the pattern.

How would you like plugin MCP tools surfaced?

- a **generic plugin-tool loader** (scan `plugins/*/dist/mcp-tools` and register), or
- an **explicit registration** — `import { arenaTools } from 'ruflo-arena/mcp-tools'` +
  `...arenaTools` in `mcp-client.ts`?

Either is a small change I'm happy to add to this PR once you pick a direction. Until then the
plugin is fully usable as a **standalone CLI** (`node dist/cli.js`) and an **importable library**
(`ruflo-arena/engine`).

## Test evidence

```
$ npm install && npm run lint && npm run build && npm test
install : light (runtime dep: zod only; no native deps)
eslint  : clean
tsc     : clean
vitest  : 4 files, 23 tests passed
```

Engine correctness is asserted, including a real game-theoretic invariant (All-Defect is
pairwise-unbeatable in PD) and monotonic hill-climb fitness. Everything is reproducible under a
fixed `--seed`.

## Scope / non-goals

In: simple-program + stochastic strategies, PD + zero-sum games, tournaments, hill-climb &
co-evolution, file/AgentDB persistence, MCP tools + CLI.

Out (tracked in the issue/ADRs): LLM-agent strategies + distillation, untrusted-program
sandboxing/resource governance, the dashboard UI, and the RuVector data/intelligence layer.

## Follow-ups

- Decide the plugin MCP-tool registration pattern (see above), then wire `arena/*` in.
- Wire fitness into the SONA co-evolution loop (ADR-148).
- Emergence dashboard plugin (ADR-149/150).
- RuVector integration contract for strategy graphs + payoff/fitness storage (ADR-152 ↔ RuVector ADR-196–200).

## Checklist

- [x] No Ruflo-core changes; opt-in plugin only
- [x] `eslint` clean, `tsc` clean, 23 tests passing
- [x] Light install (runtime dep: `zod` only — no native deps)
- [x] Files < 500 lines; typed public APIs; input validated at boundaries (Zod)
- [x] Plugin conventions followed (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `commands/`, `docs/adrs/`, `MCPTool` shape)
- [ ] Maintainer call on the MCP-tool registration pattern (see *Integration* above)
- [ ] Maintainer direction on scope / API surface (see issue #2314)

title: [verification] HIGH: agentic-flow/transport/loader ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED — federation transport smoke broken
body:
## Summary

The ADR-104 federation wire transport smoke (Check 8) fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. Two compounding causes:

1. **`agentic-flow@fix` install is broken** — `npm install agentic-flow@fix` fails with `ENOENT: Cannot cd into node_modules/@ruvector/gnn`. The `fix` dist-tag is the version that contains the `./transport/loader` export (introduced in PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#153).

2. **Fallback `agentic-flow@^2` (v2.0.13) does not export `./transport/loader`** — it only exports `./transport/quic`. The `./transport/loader` path that the federation plugin and the smoke test import does not exist in the stable ^2 release.

## Impact

- Federation transport smoke fails on every scheduled verification run
- Any environment that installs `agentic-flow@^2` (rather than being pinned to a working `fix` build) will hit `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` at federation plugin initialization
- `@claude-flow/cli@alpha` doctor install may also fail due to the same `@ruvector/gnn` ENOENT (see Check 4 companion issue)
- New users installing `@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation` into a fresh project may see federation transport fail silently or crash on first use

## Expected

```
Transport smoke: ok, sent in <N> ms
```
with `agentic-flow/transport/loader` exporting `loadQuicTransport`, `getTransportCapabilities`, `WebSocketFallbackTransport`.

## Actual

```
npm error enoent ENOENT: Cannot cd into '/tmp/ruflo-verify/pkg/node_modules/@ruvector/gnn'
(agentic-flow@fix install failure)

Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './transport/loader' is not defined
by "exports" in /tmp/ruflo-verify/pkg/node_modules/agentic-flow/package.json
code: 'ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED'
(fallback agentic-flow@^2 = v2.0.13)
```

Installed agentic-flow v2.0.13 exports:
```json
[".", "./orchestration", "./sdk", "./package.json", "./reasoningbank", "./reasoningbank/backend-selector",
 "./reasoningbank/wasm-adapter", "./router", "./agent-booster", "./transport/quic"]
```
`./transport/loader` is absent.

## Command output

```bash
# Install attempt (agentic-flow@fix tag)
npm install agentic-flow@fix --no-audit --no-fund
# npm error enoent ENOENT: Cannot cd into '/tmp/.../node_modules/@ruvector/gnn'

# Fallback
npm install "agentic-flow@^2" --no-audit --no-fund
# installed v2.0.13

# Smoke test
node transport-smoke.mjs
# Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './transport/loader' is not defined
# exit code: 1
```

## Recommended fix

1. Investigate and fix the `@ruvector/gnn` ENOENT in the `agentic-flow@fix` dist-tag — a missing or corrupted package directory is blocking the install
2. Add `./transport/loader` to the `exports` map in the agentic-flow stable `^2` release (or land ruvnet/agentic-flow#153 into main)
3. Until upstream is fixed, federation plugin should pin to a specific working version (e.g. `agentic-flow@2.0.12-fix.3`) rather than `@fix` dist-tag

✓ Node.js: v22.22.2 (>= 20)
✓ npm: 10.9.7 (>= 9)

ADR-097 breaker loadable  OR  Federation plugin not installed (optional)

title: [dream-cycle] meta: ADR-147 collision across 6 open PRs + 0 merges in 14 nights
body:
## Summary

A review of the last 6 dream-cycle PRs (#2278, #2290, #2295, #2304, #2310, #2317 — dates 2026-06-03 → 2026-06-08) surfaces three cluster-level issues that block the dream-cycle workflow from shipping. The per-PR findings are posted on each PR; this issue tracks the umbrella concerns.

## Findings

### 1. ADR-147 number collision (blocks merge)

Every one of the 6 open dream-cycle PRs adds a *different* file named `ADR-147-*.md`:

| PR | File | Date |
|---|---|---|
| #2278 | `ADR-147-…-temporal-compression…` | 2026-06-03 |
| #2290 | `ADR-147-adaptive-swarm-topology-selection.md` | 2026-06-04 |
| #2295 | `ADR-147-…-latency-aware-scheduling.md` | 2026-06-05 |
| #2304 | `ADR-147-memory-integrity-mcp-verification.md` | 2026-06-06 |
| #2310 | `ADR-147-retrospective-harness-optimization.md` | 2026-06-07 |
| #2317 | `ADR-147-multi-signal-memory-retrieval.md` | 2026-06-08 |

Current highest accepted ADR in `v3/docs/adr/` is **ADR-146**. First merge wins ADR-147; subsequent merges either conflict on `v3/docs/adr/README.md` or silently land duplicate-numbered ADRs. The dream-cycle generator needs to **read the ADR index before assigning a number**, not hardcode 147.

**Suggested resolution:** authors / cycle agent renumber in PR-creation order — #2278→147, #2290→148, #2295→149, #2304→150, #2310→151, #2317→152 — before any merge.

### 2. Zero dream-cycle PRs merged in 14 nights

The earliest open dream PR (#2150) is from 2026-05-26 — **14 nights ago**, which is exactly the `needs-merge` threshold the cycle issues themselves flag. None of the 6 in this window has landed either.

If the goal of the cycle is to ship an ADR every night, the merge rate at 0/14 means the workflow is producing research but not converging. Two practical levers:
- **Cap the inventory** at e.g. 3 unmerged dream PRs, then pause new cycles until one merges.
- **Pick one weekly winner** (highest-impact ADR) for synchronous landing.

### 3. Self-grading rubric measures shape, not truth

Every dream-cycle issue scores its own prior-night work 10/10 on six criteria (Grade-A benchmark cited, ≥4 competitor rows, witness present, <1500 words, etc.). These measure *whether the report has the right shape*, not whether the finding is **true**, **adopted**, or **leads to merged work**.

A real signal would be `merged_adrs_last_14_nights / cycles_last_14_nights`. That number is currently `0/14`. The 10/10 streak isn't carrying useful information.

## Quality of the research itself

**Good.** Findings are well-sourced (arXiv IDs, dates, Grade A/B marks, ~4 competitor rows each), and the gap analyses cite specific in-tree modules (e.g. #2317 correctly notices `fts5.ts` + `graceful-retrieval.ts` exist but are unwired; #2295 names `@claude-flow/hooks` synchronous critical path). The collision + zero-merge problem is the rate-limiter, not the research quality.

## Suggested next move

1. Renumber the 6 PRs as above.
2. Land **one** to validate the workflow end-to-end (recommend #2310 RHO — biggest single-paper claim, lines up with existing SONA work).
3. Replace the self-grading rubric with a merge-rate signal.

cc @ruvnet

title: fix(init): use valid MCP allow-rule wildcard (mcp__ruflo__*)
body:
## Problem

A fresh `ruflo init` writes a `.claude/settings.json` whose `permissions.allow`
list contains:

```jsonc
"mcp__claude-flow__:*"
```

Claude Code **rejects** this rule and skips it, surfacing in `/doctor` as:

> Invalid permission rule "mcp__claude-flow__:*" was skipped: Wildcard tool name
> "mcp__claude-flow__:*" is not supported in allow rules. An allow pattern must
> name the scope it widens — globs are permitted only in the tool position after
> a literal `mcp__<server>__` prefix.

Two issues in one line:

1. **Invalid syntax.** Allow-rules only permit a glob in the *tool* position
   (`mcp__<server>__*`). The `:*` form is valid for **Bash** rules but not
   **MCP** rules, so the whole rule is discarded.
2. **Stale server name.** ruflo replaced claude-flow; the MCP server now
   registers as `ruflo`. Even once the syntax is fixed, `claude-flow` names a
   server that no longer exists, so the rule pre-approves nothing.

## Fix

Change `mcp__claude-flow__:*` → `mcp__ruflo__*` in the generator and both static
template copies:

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/settings-generator.ts` (the generator)
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/settings.json`
- `v3/@claude-flow/mcp/.claude/settings.json`

## Deliberately left alone

The `Bash(npx @claude-flow*)` / `Bash(npx claude-flow*)` allow-rules are **not**
touched. They are valid syntax, and ruflo's bundled hooks still shell out to
`@claude-flow/cli`, so renaming them could introduce new permission prompts.
This PR is scoped to the one genuinely-broken rule.

## Verification

Each of the 3 files is a single `+1/-1` change. After regenerating settings,
`/doctor` no longer reports the skipped-rule error.

title: feat(memory): ADR-147 entity arm + signal provenance in hybridSearch
body:
Closes part of #2317 and references #2324.

## What this lands

Implements the actual gap from the ADR-147 multi-signal retrieval proposal: **the third RRF arm (entity matching) + per-result signal provenance**.

The ADR's stated P1 ("wire FTS5 + RRF fusion") turned out to be **already shipped** — `controller-registry.ts:713` already runs `semanticSearch()` + `searchKeyword()` in parallel, fuses via `applyRRF(k=60)`, diversifies via `applyMMR(λ=0.7)`. The dream-cycle author missed this. The actual gap was the entity arm (ADR P2) and the missing `signals` field.

## Changes

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---|---|
| `src/entity-tagger.ts` (new) | +71 | Regex extractor for emails, URLs, file paths (POSIX + Windows), quoted phrases, proper-noun 2-grams |
| `src/entity-tagger.test.ts` (new) | +94 | 12 unit tests pinning conservatism — false negatives OK, false positives bad |
| `src/controller-registry.ts` | +63 / −21 | `hybridSearch` controller gains the entity arm (per-entity `searchKeyword` in parallel) + builds `signals` set membership before RRF |
| `src/graceful-retrieval.test.ts` | +55 / −0 | Provenance assertion on existing test + new needle-in-haystack test (Alice Smith in 30 generic auth entries) |

## Design notes

- **Conservative tagger.** False negatives are fine (dense + sparse arms cover); false positives would dilute RRF. Tests pin generic prose → empty, single capital words → empty, `and/or` → empty. Key bug found and fixed: the original quote regex paired the closing `"` of one phrase with the opening `"` of the next (the `"a" over "b"` capturing ` over ` problem) — fixed with `(?<!\w)..(?!\w)` lookarounds.
- **Empty arm bypass.** If `extractEntities(query)` returns nothing, the entity arm is dropped from the RRF input entirely rather than passed as `[]`. Avoids diluting the fusion when there are no entities.
- **Provenance via pre-fusion set membership.** Build `denseIds`, `sparseIds`, `entityIds` from the candidates BEFORE RRF, then stamp `signals[]` on each fused output by checking which sets contain the candidate id. Doesn't require modifying `applyRRF`.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run src/entity-tagger.test.ts src/graceful-retrieval.test.ts` — **16/16 pass**
- Full memory suite — **416/420 pass**. The 4 failures are pre-existing Windows-environment issues in unrelated files (`agent-memory-scope.test.ts` path separators, `benchmark.test.ts` perf budget). My branch doesn't touch any of those files.

## What this defers

- **Entity index in SQLite** (ADR P2 stretch goal) — current implementation runs per-entity `searchKeyword` calls. Fine for typical query entity counts (1–3) but unbounded if a query mentions 20 entities. A dedicated entity index would cap this; deferred to a follow-up.
- **Async writes by default** (ADR P3) — orthogonal concern; the existing consolidator already handles HNSW background rebuild.
- **LoCoMo benchmark publication** (ADR P4) — requires harness wiring + dataset access; punted to a separate workstream.

- [x] `entity-tagger.test.ts` 12/12 pass
- [x] `graceful-retrieval.test.ts` 4/4 pass (2 existing + 2 new ADR-147 ones)
- [x] `npm run build` clean (no TS errors)

title: `model-router.ts` documents FastGRNN/Tiny-Dancer neural routing, but ships lexical heuristics + a Thompson bandit — no `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` import; embedding path unreachable
body:
## Summary

The default model router in `@claude-flow/cli` documents itself — in both the `model-router.ts`
file header and in ADR-026 — as a **Tiny-Dancer / FastGRNN neural router with embedding-based
complexity scoring**. The shipped code is instead a **lexical/regex complexity heuristic plus a
Thompson-sampling Beta-Bernoulli bandit**: `model-router.ts` imports only `fs` and `path`, no
`@ruvector/tiny-dancer` (or any model file) is loaded anywhere in the package, and the one
embedding-consuming branch is unreachable on every internal routing path.

To be clear up front: **the heuristic + bandit router works and routes sensibly** — this isn't a
functional break, and the bandit design is a nice piece of work. It's just an accuracy gap between
the documented design (neural/FastGRNN) and the shipped implementation (heuristic + bandit), plus an
unreachable embedding branch. Raising it because the gap is non-obvious for anyone evaluating ruflo
for "neural" routing, and because the neural path looks like a small, clean addition rather than a
rewrite (sketch below) — so it felt more useful to report than to sit on.

Line numbers below are from the canonical TypeScript source at `ruvnet/ruflo@main`
(`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/ruvector/`) since that's the edit target; the published `.js` dist carries
the same code at slightly different line numbers (a few call-site references use the `.js` paths and
are labelled as such). Verified on **3.10.38** (current latest).

## Stated design vs shipped behavior

**Stated (two places):**

- `model-router.ts:2,8,12` — file header:
  ```
   * Intelligent Model Router using Tiny Dancer
   * - FastGRNN-based routing decisions (<100μs)
   * - Complexity scoring via embeddings
  ```
- **ADR-026** (`v3/implementation/adrs/ADR-026-agent-booster-model-routing.md`) describes the
  underlying router as `tiny-dancer` "neural-based complexity analysis" (e.g. lines 10, 65, 390, 445).
  It contains no mention of a bandit or heuristic scorer.

**Shipped:**

- `model-router.ts` imports are `fs` and `path` only (`:22-23`) — no `@ruvector/tiny-dancer`, no
  model/safetensors load.
- Complexity is scored lexically: `computeLexicalComplexity` (`:463`), `computeSemanticDepth`
  (`:478`), `computeTaskScope` (`:503`), `computeUncertaintyLevel` (`:527`) — `.split()`,
  `.includes()`, regex `.test()`, length counts, blended `lexical*0.2 + semantic*0.35 + scope*0.25
  + uncertainty*0.2` (`:441-446`).
- Model selection is a genuine Thompson-sampling Beta-Bernoulli bandit: `BANDIT_REWARDS` (`:170`),
  bucketed `Beta(α,β)` priors (`:158`, `defaultBanditPriors` `:281`), `sampleBeta` via Marsaglia-Tsang
  (`:231-275`), posterior update in `recordOutcome` (`:744`), persisted to
  `.swarm/model-router-state.json` (`:344`, load `:775`, save `:809`).
- There is **no neural-network/matrix math** (no `Float32Array`/tensor/matmul/sigmoid/safetensors).
  (`computeSemanticDepth` does compute a mean/variance over an optional `embedding` arg — plain JS
  arithmetic, and off by default; see next section.)

So both the header and ADR-026 describe a neural/FastGRNN router; the code is heuristic + bandit.

## The `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` reference is not wired in

- **Not imported.** Zero `require('@ruvector/tiny-dancer')` / `from '@ruvector/tiny-dancer'` /
  `import('@ruvector/tiny-dancer')` anywhere in the `@claude-flow/cli` dist. The only 4 string
  occurrences are comments / literals (`commands/hooks.js:4424`, `mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js:3934`
  `implementation: 'tiny-dancer-neural'`, `ruvector/enhanced-model-router.js:358,360`).
- **Not even a declared dependency** of `@claude-flow/cli` — it appears in no `dependencies`/
  `optionalDependencies`/`devDependencies` section of its `package.json`. (It is present in the wider
  install tree at v0.1.18 only because the root project and `agentic-flow` declare it.) Wiring it in
  would require adding the dependency first.
- The member `enhanced-model-router.ts:260,284` named `tinyDancerRouter` is misleading: it is
  assigned `getModelRouter()` (`:284`) — an instance of the local heuristic `ModelRouter`, not the
  package.

## Embedding-based scoring path is unreachable on internal routing paths

`route(task, embedding?)` (`:382`) and `analyzeComplexity(task, embedding?)` (`:423`) take an
**optional** embedding; the only consumer is `if (embedding && embedding.length > 0)` in
`computeSemanticDepth` (`:490`). No live internal caller supplies one:

| Call site | Passes embedding? |
|---|---|
| `routeToModel(task)` → `route(task)` (`model-router.ts:909`) | no |
| `analyzeTaskComplexity(task)` → `analyzeComplexity(task, undefined)` (`:929`) | explicit `undefined` |
| `enhanced-model-router.ts:455` → `tinyDancerRouter.route(task)` | no |
| MCP `model-route` handler `mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js:3924` → `router.route(task)` | no |
| `mcp-tools/agent-tools.js:150` → `router.route(task)` | no |

The only embedding-forwarding wrapper, `routeToModelFull(task, embedding)` (`:916` → `route(task,
embedding)` `:921`), has **zero internal callers** (it's exported via the barrel only). So the
embedding-variance branch is dead on every internal routing path — reachable only by an external
consumer importing `routeToModelFull` directly.

## Affected version / re-verification

- Present in **3.10.38** (current latest; this is also the installed version). Canonical `main`
  source and the published dist are byte-identical on every point above.
- The only change to `model-router.js` across 3.10.18 → 3.10.38 (20 releases) was the #2250
  uncertainty-escalation guard (+44 lines); it added no imports and left the FastGRNN/embedding
  surface untouched.
- Re-verified against `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruvnet/ruflo/main/v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/ruvector/model-router.ts`
  on 2026-06-08 — header lines 2/8/12 unchanged.

## Suggested resolution (either resolves the accuracy gap)

**Option A — minimal: make the docs match the code.** Update the `model-router.ts` header (and the
`tiny-dancer-neural` literal at `hooks-tools.js:3934`) to describe the actual mechanism — lexical
complexity heuristics + a Thompson-sampling Beta-Bernoulli bandit — and either remove the unreachable
embedding branch in `computeSemanticDepth` or document it as an external-only API. Reconcile ADR-026's
"tiny-dancer/neural" description with the shipped router.

**Option B — wire in the real neural path (the design ADR-026 + the header describe).** This looks
small because the seam already exists and `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` is already in the tree:

1. Add `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` to `@claude-flow/cli` deps; embed the task with a local 384-dim
   embedder (`lib/embeddings`, `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) — cheap, local, $0.
2. Model the tiers as candidates and call the package's `Router.route({queryEmbedding, candidates})`
   → `decisions[{candidateId, confidence, useLightweight, uncertainty}]`; thread the embedding through
   the existing `route(task, embedding?)` seam so the `computeSemanticDepth` branch becomes live.
3. Keep the Thompson bandit for online learning + as cold-start / circuit-breaker-open fallback.

**One real prerequisite for Option B:** `@ruvector/tiny-dancer`'s `RouterConfig.modelPath` is
**required** ("Path to the FastGRNN model file (safetensors format)") — a trained FastGRNN artifact is
needed (trainable offline from accumulated `.swarm/model-router-state.json` routing history, or
distilled from the bandit). That's the one design decision this issue can't make for you.

Either path closes the gap, and I'm glad to help land it — happy to open a PR for Option A, or to
prototype Option B, whichever is more useful to you. Thanks again for the project.

## Environment

- `@claude-flow/cli` / `ruflo` **3.10.38** (current latest)
- `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` 0.1.18 present in tree (declared by the root project + `agentic-flow`, not by `@claude-flow/cli`)
- Node **v20.20.0**, npm 10.8.2
- Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)

## References

*(Line numbers are from the canonical `.ts` source; the published `.js` dist is the same code at slightly different lines.)*

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/ruvector/model-router.ts` — header `:2,8,12`; imports `:22-23`; scoring
  `:463/478/503/527`; bandit `:170/231-275/281/744`; state `:344/775/809`; `route` `:382`;
  `computeSemanticDepth` embedding branch `:490`; wrappers `:909/921/929`
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/ruvector/enhanced-model-router.ts` — `tinyDancerRouter` `:260,284`; `.route(task)` `:455`
- `v3/implementation/adrs/ADR-026-agent-booster-model-routing.md`
- `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` `index.d.ts` — `Router.route()` `:103-128`; `RouterConfig.modelPath` (required) `:6`

related: #2250 (closed) — same subsystem (`selectModel()` internals). This issue concerns the
documented-vs-shipped scorer; #2250 fixed the escalation logic within the same bandit.

title: docs(router): make model-router docs match shipped impl (#2329, Option A)
body:
Closes #2329 via Option A — make the docs match the shipped router. Option B (wire in the real `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` neural path) is deferred until a trained FastGRNN safetensors artifact exists.

## Why Option A first

@rcraw's audit on #2329 is correct: `model-router.ts` and ADR-026 describe a Tiny-Dancer / FastGRNN neural router with embedding-based complexity scoring, but the shipped implementation is a lexical heuristic + Thompson-sampling Beta-Bernoulli bandit. `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` is not imported, not declared as a dep of `@claude-flow/cli`, and the embedding-consuming branch in `computeSemanticDepth` is unreachable on every internal call site.

The bandit itself is well-built and routes sensibly; the gap is purely accuracy of the description, not function. Aligning docs first is the smaller, lower-risk fix and removes the misleading surface that prompted the audit. Option B remains tracked.

## What this changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/ruvector/model-router.ts` | Header rewritten to describe the actual mechanism (heuristic + Thompson bandit, persisted bandit state, no model load). Includes a #2329 note pointing at the deferred neural path. |
| `src/mcp-tools/hooks-tools.ts` | `implementation: 'tiny-dancer-neural'` → `'heuristic-thompson-bandit'`, with a comment about the telemetry-schema implication. |
| `src/ruvector/enhanced-model-router.ts` | Private member `tinyDancerRouter` → `baseRouter`; locals `tinyDancerResult` → `baseResult`. **Public `getStats()` return field kept as `tinyDancerStats`** for downstream telemetry stability, with a comment explaining the legacy name. |
| `v3/implementation/adrs/ADR-026-...md` | Top-of-context note flagging the design-vs-shipped delta; references-list entry for `tiny-dancer` rewritten. |

## Validation

- `npm run build` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli` — clean (tsc, no errors)
- No test changes — pure docs/rename/comment, no behavioural delta
- Public API surface preserved: `getStats()` return shape unchanged, all exported functions unchanged

## What's intentionally NOT in this PR

- **Option B (wire `@ruvector/tiny-dancer` for real)** — deferred. Needs a trained FastGRNN safetensors artifact + a dependency declaration in `@claude-flow/cli/package.json`. The author offered to prototype this; if you want it, this PR landing first unblocks it (the seam in `route(task, embedding?)` is now honestly documented).
- **Removing the unreachable embedding branch** in `computeSemanticDepth` — kept as the integration point for Option B. The new header documents it as "externally-callable via `routeToModelFull`".
