Implementation note: the issue predicted **3** silent literal-key traps; building it surfaced **8**, one of which (`getBanditPriors`) was caught *by the new regression test during development*. P3 (gated escalation) + P4 (criticality/credit pool) await your design sign-off — draft **ADR-148** at the bottom of this issue. 3. ⏰ **Mind the June 22 window** — alias + tier MVP landed before the cutoff means every Max user seeds Fable priors/ROI data for free; after the 22nd it's metered (which is what §7's Credit Sommelier is for). 4. Optional: §8 one-liner; and if useful, add `claude-fable-5` to the `bench:capability` matrix so the Frontier-ROI ledger starts from measured capability data. ### 📋 Implementation tracker (check off as merged) - [ ] **Finding A — `temperature` 400 fix** → [PR #2358](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/pull/2358) (+17/−1 src + 13-case regression, before/after dist proof) - [ ] **ADR-148 P1 — alias + pass-through** → in [PR #2359](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/pull/2359) (`MODEL_MAP.fable`, 3× `ClaudeModel` unions) - [ ] **ADR-148 P2 — first-class tier** → in [PR #2359](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/pull/2359) (capabilities, bandit rewards/priors, defensive `clonePriors` + forward-migration, `getBanditPriors` hardening, explicit `agent_spawn`) - [ ] **ADR-148 P3 — gated `opus → fable` escalation rung** (`allowFrontier` / `CLAUDE_FLOW_ALLOW_FABLE`) — awaiting design sign-off; diff sketch in §5 - [ ] **ADR-148 P4 — `criticality` signal + regret gate + Credit Sommelier pool** (§7 · Central Bank + Blueprint 3) — awaiting design sign-off - [ ] Adopt/renumber **ADR-148** into `v3/docs/adr/` - [ ] Optional: `claude-fable-5` in the `bench:capability` matrix - [ ] Optional: §8 OpenRouter retired-default one-liner Everything here is cited and verified — pull whatever's useful. 🙏 --- # 🚀 Innovation track — from catalog to blueprints: the next three builds, the worked economics, and the research horizon > §7 above is the **what** — fourteen institutions. This section is the **how**: the three highest-leverage builds specified to near-PR depth (tools, state shapes, failure modes, test plans, metrics), the regret math worked on real task archetypes, and the research program that falls out of the telemetry for free. Everything here composes machinery that already ships in this repo — nothing assumes a primitive ruflo doesn't have. --- ## 🏗️ Blueprint 1 — The Sovereign Court (`frontier-court`) *Builds §7 #1. The judiciary with compounding economics: every ruling makes the next one free.*
Full spec — tools · state · flow · failure modes · tests · metrics **New MCP surface** ```ts court_file({ disputeId, trigger, contested, evidence: Evidence[] }) // queen-only; auto-filed on triggers court_precedents({ query, k = 5, minSimilarity = 0.82 }) // HNSW over the precedent namespace, $0 court_verdict({ disputeId }) // status + ruling + signature ``` **Config** ```jsonc "court": { "enabled": false, // opt-in, like everything frontier "triggers": ["quorum_deadlock", "irreversible_op", "goal_mutation", "budget_breach"], "precedentThreshold": 0.82, // similarity above which precedent applies without a ruling "maxRulingsPerDay": 5 // hard backstop, draws from the Sommelier's court envelope } ``` **Precedent record** (ReasoningBank namespace `court-precedents`, embedding-indexed) ```ts interface Precedent { id: string; // prec_... trigger: CourtTrigger; contestedDigest: string; // normalized statement of the dispute, NOT the whole task ruling: string; // the holding rationale: string; // why — this is what makes precedents reusable citations: string[]; // prior precedent ids this ruling relied on repoEpoch: string; // HEAD sha window — staleness guard signature: string; // Ed25519 via the witness chain (ADR-103) createdAt: string; } ``` **Flow** 1. Hive-mind detects a trigger (e.g. byzantine quorum split twice on the same question). 2. `court_precedents` retrieval — **the $0 path**: similarity ≥ threshold → apply ruling, emit `precedent_hit`, done. *Court never convenes.* 3. Novel dispute → one Fable adjudication: the contested delta + evidence + the top-k *near* precedents (so rulings stay mutually consistent — the court reads its own case law before ruling). 4. Verdict Ed25519-signed into the witness manifest; stored as a new precedent; `hooks_explain` narrates the ruling to the swarm. **Failure modes → mitigations** | Failure | Mitigation | |---|---| | Stale precedent (codebase moved on) | `repoEpoch` window + similarity decay with age; expired precedents become *persuasive*, not binding (retrieved as context, never auto-applied) | | Contradictory precedents accumulate | Periodic **en-banc review**: one Fable pass consolidates/supersedes; superseded records keep their signatures (history is never rewritten — the witness chain forbids it) | | Threshold too loose → bad auto-applies | Judge-of-Judges (§7 #3) samples `precedent_hit` events and audits them — the court audits its own clerks | **Test plan** — deadlock fixture files exactly once · identical dispute second time = `precedent_hit` at $0 · signature verifies against the manifest · en-banc supersession leaves an auditable chain · per-day cap enforced. **Metrics** — precedent hit-rate (should climb monotonically), $/dispute (should fall), time-to-resolution vs unresolved-deadlock baseline.
**Effort:** M · **Depends on:** #2359 merged, witness plugin · **The compounding asset:** a 6-month-old install has a body of case law a fresh install doesn't — the first ruflo feature whose value is purely a function of *institutional age*. --- ## 🏗️ Blueprint 2 — The Dream Cycle (worker: `dream`) *Builds §7 #6. The label has existed in this repo all along — this is its feature.*
Full spec — schedule · prompt contract · verification · failure modes · tests · metrics **Worker config** (13th background worker, beside `ultralearn`/`consolidate`) ```jsonc "dream": { "schedule": "02:00", "maxTrajectories": 20, "nightlyBudget": 3.00, // drawn from the Sommelier's dream envelope "source": { "verdicts": ["failure", "low_confidence"], "window": "24h" }, "clusterFirst": true // embed → cluster → ONE exemplar per failure-class per night } ``` **The nightly pass** ```text 02:00 collect today's failed / low-confidence trajectories (ReasoningBank) 02:02 cluster by embedding — don't re-dream the same failure class twenty times 02:05 per exemplar, one Fable call: "Here is what the swarm did, and how it went wrong. Write (a) the counterfactual trajectory that would have succeeded, (b) the ONE-SENTENCE principle distinguishing them, (c) your confidence." 02:40 VERIFY before believing: where the task is executable (code), replay the counterfactual's decision fork in a WASM sandbox / arena harness; where it isn't, gate on JUDGE ≥ threshold 02:55 DISTILL surviving patterns tagged source:dream → EWC++ consolidation (the anti-forgetting machinery — already shipped — is what makes nightly learning safe) 08:00 morning report via hooks_notify: "while you slept, the swarm learned: …" ``` **The eval design that makes this publishable, not vibes:** hold out half the failure clusters each night as a **control group**. If dreamed classes don't out-improve held-out classes on next-day success rate, the cycle isn't working and the report says so. Built-in falsifiability. **Failure modes → mitigations** | Failure | Mitigation | |---|---| | Hallucinated counterfactuals (plausible, wrong) | Executable verification in sandbox where possible; JUDGE gate elsewhere; *dreams are verified before they're believed* | | Distillation reward-hacks the judge | Judge-of-Judges samples `source:dream` patterns at higher rate | | Cost runaway on a bad night | Hard `nightlyBudget` + `task_budget` self-awareness (§7 #14) — the dreamer knows its allowance | **Test plan** — failed-trajectory fixture produces a `source:dream` pattern · cluster dedupe collapses N same-class failures to 1 call · budget cap halts mid-pass cleanly · control-group split is honored · morning report renders. **Metrics** — next-day success delta (dreamed vs held-out classes), $/learned-principle, EWC++ retention of dreamed patterns at 7/30 days.
**Effort:** L · **Depends on:** trajectory verdicts flowing (already do), Sommelier envelope · **The poetry that's also engineering:** consolidation-during-sleep is how biological intelligence converts experience to skill without forgetting — ruflo has EWC++ *specifically* to prevent forgetting and has never had the replay loop that feeds it. This closes the loop. --- ## 🏗️ Blueprint 3 — The Credit Sommelier (cost-tracker: `frontier_credit_pool`) *Builds §7 #12. The post-June-22 survival plan, specified.*
Full spec — config · tools · envelopes · failure modes · tests · metrics **Config** ```jsonc "frontier": { "pool": 100.00, "resetDay": 1, // the Max bundled credits, monthly "rails": { "default": "subscription", "fable": "metered" }, "envelopes": { "court": 0.30, "dream": 0.20, "premortem": 0.20, "adhoc": 0.30 }, "gate": { "base": 1.0, "loosening": "linear from D-7, floor 0.25 at D-1" } } ``` **New MCP surface** ```ts frontier_quote({ task, signals }) // → { p_fail, regret, threshold_now, approved, envelope } frontier_ledger({ month }) // → envelope burn-down + per-institution spend + regret-avoided ``` **The three load-bearing policies** 1. **Dual-rail assertion at request time.** Everything ≤ Opus rides the Max subscription; *only* Fable touches the metered key. A `fable × subscription-rail` combination after June 22 is a hard error, not a silent fallback — rail misroutes are exactly the class of silent bug this issue's Finding A was. 2. **Departmental envelopes.** The court can't starve the dreamer: each institution draws from its reserve; unused reserves rebalance to `adhoc` at D-7. A central bank with departments, not a single slush fund. 3. **The expiring-budget theorem.** Credits have **zero salvage value** at month-end, so the optimal escalation gate *loosens as the reset approaches* — a budget that knows it expires should get braver, not thriftier. (This is the opposite of every throttling system ever shipped, and it falls straight out of the math.) **Failure modes → mitigations** — reset race across concurrent sessions → idempotent reset keyed on billing-month string · double-spend on parallel debits → claims-board lock on the pool · envelope starvation → D-7 rebalance + alert-ladder reuse (50/75/90/100%, already shipped). **Test plan** — rail assertion rejects fable-on-subscription · envelope debit + lock under parallel spends · loosening curve hits floor exactly at D-1 · idempotent double-reset · ledger reconciles to ADR-097 spend events. **Metrics** — pool utilization (target → ~100%: leftover credit is failure), spend mix by institution, **realized regret-avoided per dollar** (auditable via Judge-of-Judges sampling).
**Effort:** M · **Depends on:** #2358 merged (the metered rail must actually work) · **Why it's a positioning win:** no framework on earth models the subscription-vs-metered rail split. *"ruflo converts the credits you were already losing into exactly the thirty decisions that mattered most."* --- ## 📐 The regret gate, worked — three archetypes through the actual formula `escalate iff p_fail × regret > premium`, where `premium = costMult(fable) − costMult(opus) = 1.0`, regret in Opus-call-equivalents, signals from machinery that already ships (`analyze_file-risk`, `analyze_diff-risk`, `coverage-gaps`, reversibility class): | Task | `p_fail` (bandit posterior) | `regret` (risk × blast × coverage-gap × reversibility) | `p×r` | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---| | Fix a typo in README | 0.02 | 0.5 — trivially reversible, zero blast radius | **0.01** | Stay down-tier. (Haiku, honestly.) | | Refactor auth token rotation | 0.25 | 8 — high file-risk, coverage gap on the touched paths | **2.0** | **Escalate the *decision*, not the task**: Opus does the work, Fable pre-mortems the design (§7 #4). ~$1.10. | | Apply prod schema migration | 0.10 | 40 — irreversible, whole-system blast radius | **4.0** | **Court + pre-mortem**, witness-signed. The gate would pay 4× the premium; it pays 1×. | The middle row is the whole philosophy in one line: even when the gate fires, **Fable sees the contested decision, never the labor.** That's how 2× intelligence lands at a fraction of 1× cost. --- ## 🔬 The research horizon — the ruliology of intelligence economies Every institution above emits telemetry no other framework will have. Each bullet below is a paper (or a ruv-style flagship README section) waiting to be written *from data the architecture produces as a byproduct*: 1. **Precedent-graph science.** Court rulings cite prior rulings (`citations[]`). Run `pagerank-analyzer` over the citation graph: do swarm precedents develop the same power-law citation structure as human common law? Which rulings become *landmark cases*? First-ever dataset of machine jurisprudence — sitting in ReasoningBank. 2. **The Red Queen arena.** Seed `ruflo-arena` with Fable-designed attack strategies against aidefence; let defenses co-evolve. Publish a witness-signed **attack-resistance curve per release** — security posture as a measured, monotonic artifact instead of a claim. (Co-evolution under adversarial pressure is the literal Red Queen dynamic — arena was built for this.) 3. **Cross-platform judiciary.** ruflo's dual-mode already runs mixed Claude 🔵 + Codex 🟢 swarms. Seat Fable as the supreme court *over outputs it didn't generate*: every cross-model disagreement it adjudicates is a labeled datapoint in the first frontier-judged inter-model dispute corpus. Nobody has this data. 4. **Emergent specialization in the Exchange.** Under Vickrey dynamics with bidding-power audits (§7 #13), do agents develop stable *professions* — niches where their regret estimates are reliably accurate? Mechanism design meets swarm ruliology; the claims board is the petri dish. 5. **The amortization law.** Is `frontier_amortization_ratio`'s decay curve universal across installs — a *Moore's-law-of-distillation* with a measurable half-life per task-class? The Common Law federation (§7 #2) provides the multi-install dataset; ChangeLog-grade headline if the curve replicates. **The meta-point:** the research program costs nothing extra. Ship the institutions and the datasets accrete; the only thing rarer than frontier intelligence is *longitudinal telemetry of frontier intelligence governing a swarm* — and ruflo would be the only project on the planet generating it. --- *These are deliberately a gradient — the three blueprints are next-PR-ready, the worked math is merge-day policy, the horizon is where the trend line points. Keeping ruflo's innovation streak alive isn't about using the biggest model the most; it's about being the framework that uses it the most **cleverly** — and can prove it from its own ledger.* ✨ --- # 📜 Ready-to-adopt draft: ADR-148 > Written in the house ADR format (per ADR-147). Renumber to the next free slot; edit freely — this is a starting point, not a demand.
ADR-148 — Frontier Tier Routing (Claude Fable 5) # ADR-148 — Frontier Tier Routing (Claude Fable 5) **Status**: Proposed (draft contributed via #2357) **Date**: 2026-06-11 **Issue**: [ruvnet/ruflo#2357](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2357) **Related**: ADR-026 (3-tier model routing — extended by this ADR), ADR-142 (bucketed bandit priors — gains a `fable` key), ADR-143 (deterministic Tier-1 codemods — unaffected, stay at Tier 1), ADR-147 (nested subagents — consumer via critical-leaf promotion), ADR-097 (cost/federation spend events — rail for the credit pool) ## Context Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`, $10/$50 per MTok, 1M context) is a tier **above** Opus 4.8. The router cannot reach it: the selection axis is a normalized 0–1 complexity score and `opus` is hard-capped at `1.0` (`model-router.ts:563`, `Math.min(1, score * 1.5)`) — "stronger than Opus" is unrepresentable by construction. Separately, `callAnthropicMessages` sent `temperature` unconditionally, which the adaptive-thinking family rejects with a 400 (fixed in PR #2358). Timing matters: Max-plan Fable access ends June 22, after which Fable for Max users is API-credits-only (~$100/mo bundled). ## Decision Adopt Fable as an **opt-in frontier tier ("Tier 3+") that is never silently auto-selected**, in four phases: ### P1 — Reachability (ship before June 22) `fable` alias in `MODEL_MAP` → `claude-fable-5`; literal-ID pass-through (already works post-#2232); request-builder sampling-param guard (PR #2358). Explicit-only — zero routing-behavior change. ### P2 — First-class tier `'fable'` added to all three `ClaudeModel` definitions (and consolidated to one export); `MODEL_CAPABILITIES` entry (`costMultiplier: 2.0`); bandit priors incl. the three literal-key construction sites (`defaultBanditPriors`, `clonePriors`, `selectModel.sampledScores`); explicit-model allowlist so `model:"fable"` records `routedBy:'explicit'`. ### P3 — Gated escalation `opus → fable` as the final uncertainty-ladder rung, behind `config.allowFrontier` / `CLAUDE_FLOW_ALLOW_FABLE` (default **off**). Keeps the #2250 guards (`targetWorse` / `selectedTrusted`) unchanged. ### P4 — Criticality + credit economics Orthogonal `criticality` signal (from `analyze_diff-risk` / `coverage-gaps`) feeding a regret gate (`P(fail) × regret > premium`); monthly-resetting `frontier_credit_pool` in cost-tracker with dual-rail execution (subscription rail ≤ Opus, metered rail = Fable only) and a month-end-loosening spend curve. ## Consequences **Positive**: frontier capability with bounded, auditable spend; bandit learns where 2× pays off per complexity bucket; Max users convert expiring credits into high-leverage adjudications; distillation loop (gold trajectories → cheaper tiers) can reduce frontier dependence over time. **Negative**: a fifth model key touches every literal-key construction site (mitigated by P2 consolidation + tests); `allowFrontier` is one more config surface; regret signals need calibration before P4 is trustworthy. ## Alternatives considered - **`maxComplexity > 1.0` for Fable** — rejected: breaks the normalization invariant every downstream formula assumes; silently distorts confidence/uncertainty math. - **Always-escalate-on-uncertainty to Fable** — rejected: #2250 showed `uncertainty` is structurally ~0.6–0.7 on trivial routes; this would route trivial tasks to the most expensive model in the lineup. - **A separate frontier router** — rejected: duplicates bandit/persistence/state; `ClaudeModel` is already defined in three places and drifting — a fourth surface compounds it.
--- *Meta-footnote: fittingly, the innovation track above was brainstormed by **Claude Fable 5 itself** — running through Claude Code on a Max plan, inside the very free window described in Theme V. The model has reviewed the plan for its own employment and finds it sound.* 😄

title: fix(agent-execute): omit removed sampling params for Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 (#2357 Finding A)
body:
## What

`callAnthropicMessages()` always sent `temperature` (default `0.7`), but the adaptive-thinking family — **Fable 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7** — removed `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`. The API rejects the request:

```text
400 invalid_request_error: temperature: Extra inputs are not permitted
```

So `agent_execute` / `workflow_run` / the WASM-agent Anthropic path **cannot call any current frontier model** when an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. (Invisible on Claude-Max — no key → the provider check short-circuits before the fetch — fatal on a real key.)

**Part of #2357 (Finding A) — does not close the issue** (the Fable routing tier in #2357 §4–§6 is separate work).

## How

- New exported predicate `modelRejectsSamplingParams(model)` — prefix-matched (`/^claude-(fable-5|opus-4-8|opus-4-7)/`) so dated snapshots are covered.
- The Anthropic request body includes `temperature` **only** when the model accepts it. The `0.7` default for sonnet / haiku / opus ≤ 4.6 is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The Ollama / OpenRouter OpenAI-compat paths accept `temperature` and are untouched.

Net source diff: **+17 / −1** in `agent-execute-core.ts`, plus a vitest regression.

## Proof (mocked `fetch`, request body captured per model — no network, no real key)

**BEFORE — installed `3.10.42` dist (the shipping artifact):**
```text
claude-fable-5               temperature in body: YES (0.7)   ← would 400
claude-opus-4-8              temperature in body: YES (0.7)   ← would 400
claude-opus-4-7              temperature in body: YES (0.7)   ← would 400
claude-sonnet-4-6            temperature in body: YES (0.7)
```

**AFTER — identical harness, fix applied:**
```text
claude-fable-5               temperature in body: no          ✅
claude-opus-4-8              temperature in body: no          ✅
claude-opus-4-7              temperature in body: no          ✅
claude-sonnet-4-6            temperature in body: YES (0.7)   ✅ unchanged
```

## Tests

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/sampling-params-2357.test.ts` (follows the `validate-input-path-2352.test.ts` convention):
- predicate: rejects the frontier three + dated snapshots; keeps sonnet/haiku/opus-4.6
- request body via stubbed `fetch`: omits `temperature` for the frontier three (even when explicitly provided — it would 400); preserves the `0.7` default and explicit values for accepting models

**Run locally ✅:** the before/after dist-level harness above (full transcript), **plus the vitest regressions — 21/21 passing** across this file and #2359's (npm can't resolve the workspace's pnpm `workspace:*` protocol, so vitest was side-installed; the workspace sibling `@claude-flow/cli-core` resolved from the published 3.10.42 dist). Happy to iterate if CI flags anything.

## Risk

- Behavior-preserving for every model that accepts sampling params (the default path today).
- For the frontier three, the only behavior change is *removing* a parameter the API hard-rejects — there is no scenario where sending it succeeds.
- One judgment call: an **explicitly provided** `temperature` is also dropped for the frontier three (sending it can only 400). If you'd rather surface a warning instead of silently dropping, glad to add a `console.warn` — say the word.

title: Daemon self-terminating TTL + global status, honest HNSW/init footguns (carry-forward from pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref)
body:
## Summary

Carry-forward of the still-open, *fixable-in-ruflo* findings from **[pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref](https://github.com/pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref)** — a rigorous, reproduction-driven investigation kit by **@pacphi** that documents reliability and token-consumption problems in ruflo on modern Node (24/26) and the honesty of its self-learning/security surface.

🙏 **Huge thanks to @pacphi** for the depth here: root-cause docs, Docker reproductions, a held-out multi-seed statistical eval harness, and a cross-session token audit. Most of the kit's findings have *already* landed upstream (see the reconciliation table below); this issue tracks only what remains and is fixable in this repo.

A PR accompanies this issue.

## Already fixed upstream (no action needed — verified against 3.10.42 source)

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| `route feedback` never persisted (no `saveModel()`) | ✅ 3.10.6 (#2222, @pacphi credited) |
| Negative-reward inversion (`-r -1.0` parsed as `+1.0`) | ✅ 3.10.7 |
| Stale route cache hid learning / `--explore false` ignored | ✅ 3.10.8 |
| **#2219** Node 24/26 `better-sqlite3` silent WASM fallback → data loss | ✅ 3.10.6 (`better-sqlite3 ≥12.8.0` override) |
| **#2239 / F3** Q-state encoder collapse (keyword block discarded) | ✅ **3.10.11** (FNV-1a lossless fold) |
| `security defend` `.color` crash after detection | ✅ already guarded (`|| output.dim`) |
| `security cve --list` silent empty | ✅ already prints honest "no DB → use `npm audit`" |
| `.mcp.json` writes `ruv-swarm`+`flow-nexus` by default | ✅ default init writes only `claude-flow` (cloud is `--full`-only) |
| Fabricated Flash-Attention metric | ✅ removed 3.10.7 |

## Still open and fixable in ruflo (addressed by the PR)

### 1. Background daemon has no self-terminating lifecycle → multi-day token leak (primary)

The `daemon` runs interval workers (`audit` ~30m, `optimize`/`testgaps` ~60m, `map`/`consolidate`/…), each spawning a headless `claude --print` sweep. The daemon **never self-terminates** and `daemon status` only inspects the **current** workspace, so leaked daemons in other projects are invisible.

@pacphi's token audit traced a Max-plan quota burned in 1–2 days to **6 immortal daemons** (oldest **19 days**), and a later recurrence to **17** per-project daemons (**34,533** total worker runs) — ~94% of token spend was background Haiku/Sonnet machinery vs ~6% interactive. Evidence: [token-consumption-findings](https://github.com/pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref/blob/main/docs/usage/token-consumption-findings-and-mitigation-2026-06.md), [recurrence](https://github.com/pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref/blob/main/docs/usage/token-consumption-recurrence-and-cleanup-2026-06-11.md).

**Fix:** self-terminating TTL (default 12h) + opt-in idle shutdown inside the daemon process, a `--ttl` flag (`0` disables), and `daemon status --all` for a global, leak-surfacing view.

### 2. `neural status` falsely reports "HNSW Not loaded"

`getHNSWStatus()` reports availability off a lazy in-process singleton that `neural status` never warms, so it prints "Not loaded — @ruvector/core not available" even when the package is installed and exposes `VectorDb`. Cosmetic but misleading (it reads as real dormancy). **Fix:** report real capability (`@ruvector/core` resolvable) separately from in-process load.

### 3. `ruflo init` cloud-MCP + CLAUDE.md token footguns

`--full` still writes auth-gated cloud MCP servers (`ruv-swarm`, `flow-nexus`) into a committed `.mcp.json` (per-session MCP tool-def token cost). The generated per-project `CLAUDE.md` also still uses legacy `claude mcp add claude-flow -- npx -y @claude-flow/cli@latest`, inconsistent with the `ruflo@latest mcp start` the actual `.mcp.json` now emits. **Fix:** gate cloud servers behind an explicit `--cloud-mcp` even under `--full`; emit the `ruflo@latest` command and a note about the daemon's token cost.

## Tracked, but NOT fixable in this repo

### F4 — SONA learn→inference loop is a no-op stub (dependency-only)

The trained LoRA delta is never consumed in any decision (`deltaNorm` stays 0): `processInstantLearning` in the published `@ruvector/ruvllm` is an empty stub and `WasmSonaEngine::learn_from_feedback` is a no-op. This lives in **ruvnet/ruvector** ([RuVector#553](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/issues/553); #519 closed without a published fix), not here. ruflo consumes the API write-only (`intelligence.ts` `recordTrajectory`/`runBackgroundLoop`), so the loop comes alive automatically once the stub is replaced — **ruflo's only action is a future dep bump** of `@ruvector/ruvllm` in `v3/@claude-flow/providers/package.json`. No ruflo code change is useful until then.

> Separately worth noting: ruflo's *own* JS-fallback LoRA in `services/ruvector-training.ts` (`adapt_with_reward`) is a random perturbation rather than a real gradient on the WASM-unavailable path. Different code path from F4; can be tracked on its own if desired.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A daemon left running self-terminates after its TTL (default 12h; `--ttl 0` / `RUFLO_DAEMON_TTL_SECS=0` disables); optional idle shutdown.
- [ ] `daemon status --all` lists daemons across all workspaces with age + TTL and flags stale ones.
- [ ] `neural status` no longer prints a false "HNSW Not loaded" when `@ruvector/core` is installed.
- [ ] `--full` no longer writes cloud MCP servers unless `--cloud-mcp` is passed; generated CLAUDE.md uses `ruflo@latest`.
- [ ] F4 documented as a ruvector dependency item.

---
*Filed alongside a PR. All credit for the underlying investigation, reproductions, and the token-audit method belongs to **@pacphi** — https://github.com/pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref*

title: fix(daemon): self-terminating TTL + idle shutdown, global status --all, honest HNSW/init footguns
body:
## What & why

Carry-forward of the still-open, *fixable-in-ruflo* findings from **[pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref](https://github.com/pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref)**. Closes #2360.

🙏 **Thanks to @pacphi** — the investigation, Docker reproductions, multi-seed statistical eval, and the cross-session token audit that surfaced all of this are theirs. Most of that kit's findings already landed upstream (#2219, #2222, #2239 in 3.10.11, the security/MCP honesty fixes); this PR addresses what remained.

## Changes

### Daemon token-leak (primary) — `services/worker-daemon.ts`, `commands/daemon.ts`
The background daemon's interval workers each spawn a headless `claude --print` sweep, but the daemon had **no self-terminating lifecycle** and `daemon status` only saw the current workspace — so a forgotten daemon (observed: 19 days, 34k+ worker runs across 17 projects) leaked tokens invisibly.

- **Self-terminating lifecycle.** New `ttlMs` (default **12h**) + `idleShutdownMs` (opt-in) on `DaemonConfig`, sourced **constructor arg > `config.json` (`daemon.ttlSecs`/`daemon.idleSecs`) > env (`RUFLO_DAEMON_TTL_SECS`/`RUFLO_DAEMON_IDLE_SECS`) > default**. A monitor timer (checked every 60s, `unref()`'d) grace-shuts-down via `stop()` + `process.exit(0)`.
  - *Why `exit(0)`:* the foreground keep-alive is a **ref'd** `setInterval`, so `stop()` alone leaves a zombie — this mirrors the existing signal-handler path.
  - *Why a dedicated parser:* an explicit `0` **disables** the limit (preserves run-until-stopped), so the idiomatic `parseInt(x) || default` (which treats 0 as falsy) can't be used.
- **`--ttl` flag** on `daemon start`, validated and forwarded through the background fork; TTL surfaced in the status/start boxes.
- **`daemon status --all`** — global view across every workspace, reusing the same `ps`/`tasklist` scan as kill-stale, reading each workspace's `daemon-state.json` for age + TTL and flagging daemons past their TTL (or >12h).

### Honest `neural status` — `memory/memory-initializer.ts`, `commands/neural.ts`
`getHNSWStatus()` now reports **real capability** (`@ruvector/core` resolvable, cached sync probe) separately from in-process load, ending the false "HNSW Not loaded" that appeared whenever `neural status` ran in a fresh process. The render distinguishes Ready / Available / Not installed.

### `init` MCP/token footguns — `commands/init.ts`, `init/claudemd-generator.ts`
- Keep auth-gated cloud MCP servers (`ruv-swarm`, `flow-nexus`) **opt-in even under `--full`** via a new `--cloud-mcp` flag (they get committed into `.mcp.json` and add per-session tool-def token cost).
- Generated `CLAUDE.md` now emits `ruflo@latest mcp start` (matches the actual generated `.mcp.json`) instead of legacy `@claude-flow/cli@latest`, plus a note on the daemon's continuous token cost + TTL.

### Not in this PR (dependency-only): F4
The SONA learn→inference no-op (`processInstantLearning`) lives in `@ruvector/ruvllm` (ruvnet/ruvector, [RuVector#553](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/issues/553)). ruflo consumes it write-only, so the only ruflo action is a future dep bump — documented in the issue, no code change here.

## Tests
- `worker-daemon-resource-thresholds.test.ts`: TTL/idle defaults, env/config/constructor precedence, explicit-`0`-disables, invalid-value fallback, monitor arming/no-arming.
- `daemon-workspace-scope.test.ts`: `extractWorkspaceFromDaemonLine` (the helper behind `--all`), incl. spaces, trailing whitespace, legacy lines, round-trip.
- `memory-ruvector-deep.test.ts`: HNSW-status contract updated to assert the corrected `initialized` vs `available` separation.

Verified locally with vitest 4 (the version the CLI package declares): daemon + workspace suites **69 passed**, memory-ruvector **147 passed**, init-wizard **11 passed**. `tsc` introduces **no new type errors** (the pre-existing errors are an absent optional dep `@ruvector/learning-wasm` and an unbuilt sibling package, present on `main` too).

## Behavior change note
Daemons now self-terminate after **12h by default**. This is a deliberate default to stop the documented leak; it's fully configurable (`--ttl <secs>`, `RUFLO_DAEMON_TTL_SECS`, `daemon.ttlSecs`) and `--ttl 0` restores indefinite run.

---
*All credit for the underlying investigation belongs to **@pacphi** — https://github.com/pacphi/ruflo-machine-ref*

## Deep Dive Findings — Intelligence SOTA 2026

### SOTA Summary

| Finding | Source | Confidence |
|---------|--------|------------|
| Agent-native KG (Scholar-KG, 2.46M papers, 4B GRPO backbone) captures entity/claim/evidence/method-lineage edges; surpasses flat retrieval for multi-hop scientific reasoning | arXiv:2606.13669 (Agents-K1), June 11, 2026 | **B** — arXiv preprint, specific benchmark numbers not in abstract |
| Interleaved RL reasoning: +12.5% Pass@1, −37% reasoning length, −80% TTFT vs. think-then-act; consistent across PPO, GRPO, REINFORCE++ | arXiv:2505.19640, Jan 2026 update | **B** — multi-RL validation, preprint |
| AgentBeats: standardized reproducible multi-agent evaluation — 298 judge agents, 467 subject agents, 5-month open competition | arXiv:2606.13591, June 11, 2026 | **A** — large-scale, open, reproducible |
| EurekAgent: self-designed environment engineering achieves new SOTA 26-circle packing result for <$11 API cost | arXiv:2606.13662, June 11, 2026 | **B** — arXiv, single source |
| MemRefine: storage-budgeted LLM-guided memory compression meets budget while preserving downstream task performance | arXiv:2606.13177, June 11, 2026 | **B** — arXiv, single source |

### Gap vs Current Ruflo

| Capability | Ruflo v3.6.10 | SOTA 2026 | Gap |
|------------|--------------|-----------|-----|
| Knowledge retrieval | HNSW flat vector similarity (ReasoningBank) | KG graph traversal (Agents-K1, entity/claim/evidence edges) | **Critical — architectural** |
| Reasoning token interleaving | SONA adapts at trajectory end only | Interleaved think/act per tool boundary (arXiv:2505.19640) | **High — implementation** |
| Memory compression budget | None — all entries retained at full fidelity | Storage-budgeted LoRA compression (MemRefine) | **Medium — implementation** |
| Published eval harness | None | AgentBeats (298 judges, 467 subjects) | **Visibility gap** |
| KG infrastructure | `graph-backend.ts` wired for agent topology (ADR-087, `@ruvector/graph-node@2.0.3`) | Not extended to knowledge indexing | **Critical — infrastructure exists but unused** |

**Root issue**: A query like "which agent patterns are causally supported by evidence from method lineage X?" requires graph traversal — HNSW returns the nearest embedding but cannot hop through entity→claim→evidence chains. The fix does not require a new dependency; ADR-087 already installed `@ruvector/graph-node` with `kHopNeighbors()`.

### Recommended Action

**ADR-155 filed** (see PR): extend `v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/ruvector/graph-backend.ts` to index ReasoningBank entries as knowledge graph nodes (entity, claim, evidence types) with method-lineage and causal-support edges. Add `kg_query(entity, hops)` path to `UnifiedMemoryService` alongside existing HNSW path. Feature-flag `CLAUDE_FLOW_KG_ENABLED=true`. ~200 LOC across 3 files. No new dependencies.

---

## Scan Findings — Capabilities

- **Source:** arXiv:2606.13662 (EurekAgent, June 11, 2026)
- **Competitive signal:** EurekAgent achieves new mathematical SOTA (26-circle packing) at <$11 API cost by having agents engineer their own evaluation environments rather than using static test prompts. No competing framework (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK) ships environment engineering as a built-in capability.
- **Finding (Grade B):** Ruflo dispatches agents into fixed task descriptions with no mechanism to auto-generate or refine test environments. Capability gap is implementation-level: add an `environment_engineering: boolean` flag to Task spawn that, when true, runs a pre-task environment-refinement loop in SONA before executing the main task. **No ADR — implementation-level; aligns with SONA extension noted in ADR-006.**

---

## Scan Findings — Memory

- **Source:** arXiv:2606.13177 (MemRefine, June 11, 2026); arXiv:2606.12852 (WISE, June 10, 2026)
- **Competitive signal:** MemRefine's storage-budget enforcement ensures memory systems don't bloat unboundedly — a real production concern. WISE's causal event graphs enable robust memory recall under viewpoint changes (substantial improvement in long-horizon sparse task success).
- **Finding (Grade B):** AgentDB retains all memories at full fidelity with no budget enforcement. ReasoningBank's `consolidate()` step (EWC++) prevents forgetting but does not compress. Add `compression_budget_bytes: number` to `consolidate()` in `v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/graceful-retrieval.ts`, using the existing LoRA distillation step to compress low-frequency patterns. **No ADR — implementation-level; covered architecturally by ADR-006.**

title: [verification] HIGH: agentic-flow/transport/loader subpath removed in 2.0.13 — federation transport smoke broken
body:
## Summary

The ADR-104 federation wire transport smoke test (Check 8) failed on 2026-06-12. The `agentic-flow@fix` tag now resolves to `2.0.13`, which no longer exports the `./transport/loader` subpath. Any Ruflo code that imports `agentic-flow/transport/loader` (and the verification smoke test itself) will throw `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` at runtime. **This is a new regression — the same check passed on 2026-06-10 (reported 14ms send).**

## Impact

Any code path in Ruflo that uses `agentic-flow/transport/loader` to obtain a `WebSocketFallbackTransport` or `loadQuicTransport` will fail at runtime with a hard module resolution error. Federation transport between Ruflo nodes depends on this path per ADR-104.

## Expected

```
agentic-flow/transport/loader exports: loadQuicTransport, getTransportCapabilities, WebSocketFallbackTransport
WebSocket fallback available
Localhost send completes in 0 < dt < 5000ms
Script output: "Transport smoke: ok, sent in N ms"
```

## Actual

```
node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:314
  return new ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED(
         ^

Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './transport/loader' is not defined by "exports"
in /tmp/ruflo-verify/pkg/node_modules/agentic-flow/package.json
imported from /tmp/ruflo-verify/pkg/transport-smoke.mjs
    at exportsNotFound (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:314:10)
    at packageExportsResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:661:9)
ExitCode: 1
```

## Command output

```
# agentic-flow@fix install:
added 527 packages (fix tag → 2.0.13)

# agentic-flow@2.0.13 exported subpaths:
.
./orchestration
./sdk
./package.json
./reasoningbank
./reasoningbank/backend-selector
./reasoningbank/wasm-adapter
./router
./agent-booster
./transport/quic     ← present
./embeddings
# MISSING: ./transport/loader
```

## Relevant report section

Check 8 in `/tmp/verification-report.md`:
> Status: FAILED | Severity: HIGH | ExitCode: 1 | Duration: 46400ms
> NEW regression — Check 8 passed on 2026-06-10 with agentic-flow@fix (14ms send); now fails

## Commit SHA

`dfe1b9cf993c34571fa5f2d08f5772e0672c68ab`

## Timestamp UTC

`2026-06-12T07:04:55Z`

## Recommended fix

**Option A (preferred):** Restore `./transport/loader` to the `exports` map in `agentic-flow/package.json` in the upstream ruvnet/ruvector (or agentic-flow) package, republish, and update the `fix` dist-tag.

**Option B:** If `./transport/loader` was intentionally removed as an abstraction layer, update all Ruflo imports to use `./transport/quic` directly and update the verification smoke test accordingly.

**Option C (short-term):** Pin `agentic-flow` to the last known-good version in the verification runner and any Ruflo package that depends on it, until the upstream export is restored.

title: fix(plugins): make npm install/uninstall/upgrade work on Windows
body:
## Summary
On Windows, `PluginManager` failed every plugin lifecycle command with two distinct Node failure modes:

1. **`spawn npm ENOENT`** — `npm` on Windows is a bash shim with no `.exe`, so `execFile('npm', ...)` cannot resolve it.
2. **`spawn EINVAL`** — falling back to `npm.cmd` runs into CVE-2024-27980 (fixed in Node 18.20.2 / 20.12.2 / 21.7.3): the runtime refuses to spawn `.cmd`/`.bat` files directly.

This PR routes all three call sites (`install`, `uninstall`, `upgrade`) through a single `runNpm` helper that invokes `cmd.exe /d /s /c npm <args>` on Windows. `cmd.exe` is a real `.exe`, so neither failure mode applies, and Node's safe array-form argument escaping is preserved. POSIX path is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc` build clean — no new TS errors in `manager.ts` (8 unrelated pre-existing errors in other files)
- [x] Verified end-to-end on Windows 11 / Node 20:
  ```
  ruflo plugins install -n @claude-flow/security
  -> Installed @claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.10
  ```
- [ ] (Maintainer) verify Linux/macOS regression-free — POSIX branch is unchanged, but appreciated as a sanity check
- [ ] (Maintainer) verify same install on a fresh Windows host where it previously threw `spawn npm ENOENT` / `spawn EINVAL`

## Files
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/plugins/manager.ts` (+18 / −12)

| MemMachine: 3-tier store (short/episodic/profile), LoCoMo 0.9169 (GPT-4-mini), 80% fewer tokens vs Mem0 | arXiv:2604.04853 (Apr 2026) | **A** |
| MemMachine: LongMemEvalS 93.0%; gains from retrieval depth +4.2%, context formatting +2.0%, search prompt +1.8%, query bias correction +1.4% | arXiv:2604.04853 | **A** |

| Temporal decay / TTL per tier | ❌ None | MemMachine TTL per tier; LangGraph v0.4 TTL eviction; CrewAI v1.12 configurable | **Critical — architectural** |
| Episodic raw episode storage | ❌ HNSW embeddings only | MemMachine: raw episode objects alongside embeddings | **High — implementation** |
| Consistency verification on consolidation | ❌ None | SSGM: cosine coherence gate before episodic→long-term promotion | **High — architectural** |

| Published LoCoMo score | ❌ Not run | MemMachine 0.9169 (SOTA) | **Visibility gap** |

**Root issue**: AgentDB grows without bound. Stale embeddings surface at equal weight to recent ones, degrading retrieval precision and creating the topology-induced leakage risk identified by SSGM. Fix: `TemporalDecayController` (ADR-156) — new 19th AgentDB controller, ~205 LOC, feature-flagged off by default.

### Recommended Action

**ADR-156 filed** (see PR): add `TemporalDecayController` with TTL per memory tier (short: 7d / episodic: 90d / long-term: 365d / permanent: ∞), SSGM consistency verification gate (cosine coherence ≥ 0.7 before episodic→long-term promotion), and `episode_store` SQLite table for raw episode objects. ~205 LOC across 4 files. No breaking API change. Default off until ADR-088 LongMemEval baseline established.

---

## Scan Findings — Plugins

- **Source:** Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit (MIT-licensed, April 2026)
- **Competitive signal:** AGT exposes `PluginInterface` and `PolicyProviderInterface` allowing third-party tools to inject capability-attenuation and circuit-breaker policies into the runtime governance pipeline. Framework-agnostic integrations for LangGraph/AutoGen/CrewAI.
- **Finding (Grade B):** Ruflo's plugin system (ADR-015) registers tool handlers and semantic descriptions but has no `PolicyProviderInterface` — plugins cannot inject runtime governance behaviour (capability limits, circuit breakers). ADR-154 adds `RuntimeGovernancePlane`; the missing link is a plugin hook interface. **No ADR — implementation-level** extension to `@claude-flow/plugins/src/plugin-registry.ts`.

---

## Scan Findings — Automation

- **Source:** arXiv:2603.22386 (JudgeFlow); arXiv:2602.16873 (AdaptOrch)
- **Competitive signal:** JudgeFlow assigns block-level responsibility scores to failing logic blocks in multi-step workflows — enabling precise fault attribution. No production framework ships this natively.
- **Finding (Grade B):** Ruflo's `hooks post-task` records task-level success/failure but assigns no block-level score within a multi-step pipeline. When a 12-step automation fails, there is no mechanism to identify the causal block. Adding JudgeFlow-style scoring (~50 LOC) to `post-task` hook telemetry closes this debugging gap. **No ADR — implementation-level.**

title: Bug: detectExistingRufloMCP misses legacy 'claude-flow@alpha' key — users lose autopilot and newer tools
body:
## Summary

`ruflo init` (and `claude-flow init`) silently leaves projects stuck with an outdated `.mcp.json` that uses the `claude-flow@alpha` server key. Users who set up their project before the rename to `ruflo` never receive the updated config and cannot access tools added after v3.x — including all 10 `autopilot_*` tools.

## Affected versions

| Package | Version |
|---------|---------|
| `ruflo` (npm) | 3.10.45 |
| `@claude-flow/cli` | 3.10.45 |
| `claude-flow` (older local install that triggers the issue) | 2.7.35 |

## Root cause

`detectExistingRufloMCP()` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/executor.js` (line 754 in the dist) only recognises two server keys as "already registered":

```javascript
if ('claude-flow' in servers || 'ruflo' in servers)
    return candidate;
```

The old init templates (claude-flow ≤ 2.x) generated a different key — `"claude-flow@alpha"` — which is not in this list. This creates two failure modes:

**Scenario A — existing `.mcp.json` in project dir**
`writeMCPConfig()` sees the file already exists and skips it (`result.skipped.push('.mcp.json')`). The user is silently left with the stale config forever; `detectExistingRufloMCP` is never even called.

**Scenario B — stale key in a parent dir**
If `.mcp.json` does not exist in the project but a parent directory has `"claude-flow@alpha": {...}`, `detectExistingRufloMCP` walks the parents, doesn't match `claude-flow@alpha`, and writes a *new* `claude-flow`-keyed config. Both servers then run simultaneously under different prefixes (`mcp__claude-flow@alpha__*` and `mcp__claude-flow__*`), creating duplicate tool noise and potential confusion.

## Reproduction

1. Have an old project with `.mcp.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "claude-flow@alpha": {
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["claude-flow@alpha", "mcp", "start"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Run `npx -y ruflo@latest init` in that project.
3. Observe: init skips `.mcp.json`, no warning is shown.
4. Start Claude Code — `mcp__claude-flow__autopilot_*` tools are absent from the session.

## Impact

- All tools added after the `claude-flow@alpha` era are silently unavailable (autopilot, browser, wasm-agent, hive-mind, etc.)
- No error or warning is surfaced to the user
- Issue is hard to diagnose without inspecting the npx cache

## Suggested fix

1. Add legacy keys to the detection check:
   ```javascript
   if (
     'claude-flow' in servers ||
     'ruflo' in servers ||
     'claude-flow@alpha' in servers ||
     'claude-flow@v3alpha' in servers
   )
     return candidate;
   ```

2. When a stale key is detected, print a migration warning instead of silently skipping:
   ```
   ⚠ Found legacy .mcp.json with key 'claude-flow@alpha' at /path/.mcp.json.
     Your MCP server key is outdated. Run `ruflo init --force` to migrate.
   ```

3. `--force` mode should also rewrite a stale file (not just skip if it exists).

title: Bug: swarm.js error hint references deprecated 'claude-flow@v3alpha' package name
body:
## Summary

When `swarm_init` fails via MCP, the error recovery hint shown to the user references the deprecated dist-tag `claude-flow@v3alpha` instead of the current `ruflo@latest`. Following the hint installs the wrong package.

## Affected versions

| Package | Version |
|---------|---------|
| `ruflo` | 3.10.45 |
| `@claude-flow/cli` | 3.10.45 |

## Location

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/swarm.ts` → compiled to `dist/src/commands/swarm.js`, line 500.

## Current code (dist)

```javascript
// swarm.js line ~500
spinner.fail('MCP swarm_init failed — swarm metadata saved locally only');
output.writeln(output.dim(`  Error: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`));
output.writeln(output.dim(
  '  The MCP server may not be running. Start it with: ' +
  'claude mcp add claude-flow npx claude-flow@v3alpha mcp start'
));
```

## Problem

`claude-flow@v3alpha` is a stale dist-tag. The package has been renamed to `ruflo`. A user following this instruction will:
- Either install an old version of `claude-flow` that lacks current MCP tools
- Or get a confusing "package not found" / resolution warning from npm

## Suggested fix

```javascript
output.writeln(output.dim(
  '  The MCP server may not be running. Start it with: ' +
  'claude mcp add claude-flow -- npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start'
));
```

Note the added `--` separator and `-y` flag (forces fresh fetch, bypasses local stale installs).

title: Bug: ContainerWorkerPool spawns workers with deprecated 'claude-flow@v3alpha' package
body:
## Summary

`ContainerWorkerPool.buildWorkerCommand()` constructs the worker spawn command using the deprecated dist-tag `claude-flow@v3alpha`. Container workers may run an old, incompatible version of claude-flow that lacks current MCP tools and API surface.

## Affected versions

| Package | Version |
|---------|---------|
| `ruflo` | 3.10.45 |
| `@claude-flow/cli` | 3.10.45 |

## Location

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/container-worker-pool.ts` → compiled to `dist/src/services/container-worker-pool.js`, line 452.

## Current code (dist)

```javascript
// container-worker-pool.js line ~452
buildWorkerCommand(options) {
    // Use npx to run claude-flow daemon trigger
    return [
        'npx', 'claude-flow@v3alpha',
        'daemon', 'trigger',
        '-w', options.workerType,
        '--headless',
    ];
}
```

## Problem

- `claude-flow@v3alpha` is a stale dist-tag pointing to pre-rename versions of the package.
- Workers spawned with this tag may silently run a version from before autopilot, browser automation, wasm-agent, and other tools were introduced.
- Without the `-y` flag, `npx` may resolve to a locally installed `claude-flow` of any version (e.g. `2.7.35`), skipping the remote fetch entirely.

## Suggested fix

```javascript
buildWorkerCommand(options) {
    return [
        'npx', '-y', 'ruflo@latest',
        'daemon', 'trigger',
        '-w', options.workerType,
        '--headless',
    ];
}
```

The `-y` flag ensures npx always fetches/uses the latest published version rather than falling back to a locally installed stale copy.

title: [verification] HIGH: agentic-flow/transport/loader missing from @latest — Check 8 transport smoke fails
body:
## Summary

Check 8 (ADR-104 federation wire transport smoke) failed. `agentic-flow/transport/loader` is not exported by `agentic-flow@latest` (2.0.13). The patched `agentic-flow@fix` (2.0.12-fix.8) that contains the WebSocket fallback transport timed out during install (>60s). Any user installing `agentic-flow@^2` cannot reach the federation transport path.

## Impact

- Federation wire transport (ADR-104) is non-functional for users who install `agentic-flow@^2` (resolves to 2.0.13)
- `agentic-flow/transport/loader` subpath does not exist in the `latest` track
- The loader pattern (`loadQuicTransport`, `WebSocketFallbackTransport`) is gated exclusively behind `agentic-flow@fix` until upstream PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#153 merges
- Users following standard install instructions who do not pin to `@fix` will hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at federation transport initialization

## Expected

```
import { loadQuicTransport, getTransportCapabilities, WebSocketFallbackTransport }
  from 'agentic-flow/transport/loader';
// → resolves successfully
// → caps.webSocketFallbackAvailable === true
// → localhost send completes 0 < dt < 5000ms
```

## Actual

```
agentic-flow@fix install: Terminated (>60s timeout on this host)
agentic-flow@^2 → 2.0.13 installed (38s)

node transport-smoke.mjs →
  Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Package subpath './transport/loader'
  is not defined by "exports" in
  node_modules/agentic-flow/package.json
  
agentic-flow 2.0.13 only exports: main, reasoningbank

Exit: 10
Duration: 101s
```

## Command output

```bash
# agentic-flow@fix install (timed out):
npm install agentic-flow@fix --no-audit --no-fund
→ Terminated (exit SIGTERM after 60s)

# Fallback ^2 install:
npm install agentic-flow@^2 --no-audit --no-fund
→ added 522 packages in 38s, version 2.0.13

# agentic-flow dist-tags:
{
  "beta": "1.1.14-beta.1",
  "alpha": "3.0.0-alpha.2",
  "fix": "2.0.12-fix.8",
  "latest": "2.0.13"
}

# Transport smoke:
node transport-smoke.mjs
→ Transport loader not available.
  Error: Package subpath './transport/loader' is not defined by "exports"
  Fallback error: no transport export: main,reasoningbank
→ Exit 10
```

## Root cause

Upstream PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#153 (WebSocket fallback transport loader pattern) is still open and unmerged. `agentic-flow@latest` (2.0.13) does not include the `./transport/loader` subpath. The fix is only in the `agentic-flow@fix` patched dist-tag (currently 2.0.12-fix.8).

The federation plugin (`@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation`) imports `agentic-flow/transport/loader` in its plugin.ts initialization path. Any user who installs `agentic-flow@^2` without explicitly pinning to `@fix` gets the broken state.

## Recommended fix

**Option A (short-term):** Add `agentic-flow@fix` as a pinned dependency in `@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/package.json` instead of relying on the caller to install it.

**Option B (long-term):** Land upstream PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#153, cut a stable `agentic-flow@^2.x` release that includes the loader subpath, then re-pin from `@fix` to the stable release.

**Option C (defensive):** Add a graceful degradation path in federation plugin's `initialize()` so that when `agentic-flow/transport/loader` is unavailable, transport is disabled with a clear warning rather than a hard MODULE_NOT_FOUND crash.

## Environment

- Commit: `4cbcfc2671ad3f13ac9a648c1604c09fdb934248`
- Timestamp UTC: 2026-06-13T07:04:13Z
- Node: v22.22.2 / npm: 10.9.7
- OS: Linux 6.18.5 x86_64
- `agentic-flow@latest`: 2.0.13
- `agentic-flow@fix`: 2.0.12-fix.8 (exists, install timed out >60s)
- `@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@alpha`: 1.0.0-alpha.16

## Related

- ruvnet/agentic-flow#153 — upstream PR that adds the transport/loader subpath (unmerged)
- Issue #1877 — ADR-104 federation wire transport implementation (documents the `@fix` dependency)
- Check 8 report: `/tmp/verification-report.md`

title: fix: community bug batch — stale claude-flow@v3alpha references (#2369, #2370, #2371)
body:
## Summary

Three related community bugs reported by @dskarasev — all from the `claude-flow` → `ruflo` rename leaving runtime references to the deprecated `claude-flow@v3alpha` (or `claude-flow@alpha`) dist-tag. Each silently routes users / workers / detection at a pre-rename build that lacks autopilot, browser, wasm-agent, and other current MCP tools.

- **Closes #2369** — init's `detectExistingRufloMCP` missed legacy MCP keys, AND `writeMCPConfig` silently skipped existing local `.mcp.json` files with stale keys.
- **Closes #2370** — `swarm.ts` `swarm_init` failure hint pointed at the wrong package.
- **Closes #2371** — `ContainerWorkerPool` spawned workers with the deprecated dist-tag.

## Changes

| File | Fix |
|------|-----|
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/executor.ts` | `detectExistingRufloMCP` now recognises `claude-flow@alpha` and `claude-flow@v3alpha` in both the top-level `mcpServers` and project-scoped registration paths. `writeMCPConfig` now parses an existing local `.mcp.json`, and if it finds a stale-key entry, pushes a loud message naming the deprecated key and explaining how to fix it (delete + re-init, or `--force`). |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/swarm.ts` | MCP-down hint changed from `claude mcp add claude-flow npx claude-flow@v3alpha mcp start` → `claude mcp add claude-flow -- npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start`. The `--` separator avoids claude-mcp flag ambiguity; the `-y` forces a fresh fetch. |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/container-worker-pool.ts` | `buildWorkerCommand()` now returns `['npx', '-y', 'ruflo@latest', ...]` instead of `['npx', 'claude-flow@v3alpha', ...]`. `-y` prevents npx from silently falling back to a stale locally-installed `claude-flow`. |
| `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/stale-mcp-key-2369.test.ts` | New 10-test regression suite: pins all three runtime contracts (legacy-key recognition, hint string shape, ContainerWorkerPool argv shape, Scenario A warning message), plus a sanity sweep over the whole `cli/src/` tree (comment-stripped, legitimate legacy-key recognition lists excepted) so a future grep-and-replace can't silently re-introduce the deprecated dist-tag. |

## Test plan

- [x] New: `stale-mcp-key-2369.test.ts` — 10/10 tests pass
- [x] Existing `init-wizard-bugs.test.ts` — 11/11 still pass (no regression in surrounding init paths)
- [x] `npm run build` clean on `@claude-flow/cli`
- [ ] Repro check from each issue body:
  - #2369 Scenario A: `mkdir t1 && cd t1` with an `.mcp.json` containing `"claude-flow@alpha"` key → `ruflo init` now prints `existing file uses deprecated key 'claude-flow@alpha' — autopilot/browser/wasm-agent tools will be missing; delete .mcp.json and re-run, or re-run with --force to overwrite` instead of a silent skip

  - #2370: `npx ruflo swarm init` with the MCP server down → hint now shows `ruflo@latest`
  - #2371: container worker spawn → argv `['npx', '-y', 'ruflo@latest', 'daemon', 'trigger', ...]`

## Held / not in this batch

- **#2373** (HIGH verification: `agentic-flow/transport/loader` missing from `@latest`) — the federation plugin already caps its peer to `>=2.0.12-fix.8 <2.0.13` (PR #2364 / v3.10.44). The remaining issue is in the external verification harness that installs `agentic-flow@latest` directly; the actual fix is upstream PR `ruvnet/agentic-flow#153` to either restore the subpath in `@latest` or publish migration notes. Will comment on the issue.

title: fix(hooks): harden memory/hook helpers — real timeout, signal cleanup, truncation transparency, cross-platform slug
body:
﻿## Summary

Five hardening fixes to the `.claude/helpers` hook/memory scripts, all reproduced against current `main`. Each is small, isolated, and verified with Node's built-in test runner (no new deps).

### Fixes

1. **`runWithTimeout()` never enforced its timeout** (`hook-handler.cjs`). It called `fn()` then `clearTimeout(timer)` immediately, so an async `fn` returned a pending promise that resolved *through* the race — the timeout protected nothing (the intelligence-init guard for #1530/#1531 was inert). Reimplemented as a real `Promise.race` between the work and the timeout. Documented that a *synchronous* blocking callee can't be preempted in-process (the real guard there is the file-size cap in `intelligence.cjs`). Applied to both `hook-handler.cjs` copies (root + `v3/@claude-flow/cli`).

2. **Global silent swallow of unhandled rejections** (`auto-memory-hook.mjs`). `process.on('unhandledRejection', () => {})` hid *all* async failures process-wide. Kept exit-0 behaviour but log the reason under `RUFLO_DEBUG`/`DEBUG` so genuine bugs are visible.

3. **No SIGTERM/SIGINT cleanup** in db-touching helpers (`auto-memory-hook.mjs`, `context-persistence-hook.mjs`). A signal mid-write skipped `backend.shutdown()`, risking an unflushed SQLite WAL / stale `agentdb.rvf.lock`. Track the active backend and flush it on signal.

4. **Silent value truncation** (`intelligence.cjs`). Memory content was cut at 500 chars with no signal. Added a `clip()` helper that appends an ellipsis and warns under debug when it actually truncates.

5. **Cross-platform `projectSlug` bug** (`intelligence.cjs`). The slug used `cwd().replace(/^\//,'').replace(/\//g,'-')` — POSIX-only. On Windows it kept `:` and `\`, so it never matched Claude Code's real `~/.claude/projects/<slug>` dir and memory bootstrap silently found nothing. Now slugifies every non-alphanumeric to `-`, matching Claude Code's actual convention (verified: `G:\My Drive\...\ruflo-fix` -> `G--My-Drive-...-ruflo-fix`).

## Testing

- `node --test tests/hook-handler-runwithtimeout.test.cjs` — 5/5, including the decisive case: a slow async fn now resolves `null` at ~3s (old code returned the late value at ~5s).
- `node scripts/smoke-pre-bash-hook.mjs` — passes for both dispatcher copies (no regression).
- `node --check` on all 8 touched files.

title: [verification] HIGH: @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version hangs and times out (>60s)
body:
## Summary

`npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` hangs indefinitely and must be killed (SIGTERM) after 60 seconds with no output. The same hang affects `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha doctor`. This is user-visible breakage for anyone using the alpha CLI in a cold environment.

## Impact

Any user running `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha <anything>` on first invocation will experience a silent hang. The published alpha CLI is effectively unusable for cold-start invocations.

## Expected

```
@claude-flow/cli@alpha --version  →  prints version >= 3.7.0-alpha.20 within ~5s
```

## Actual

```
npm warn deprecated uuid@9.0.1: ...
npm warn deprecated glob@10.5.0: ...
[process hangs for 60s]
Terminated
exit code: 143 (SIGTERM)
```

`ruflo@alpha --version` works correctly (prints `ruflo v3.10.46`), so the hang is specific to the `@claude-flow/cli` startup path.

## Likely Root Cause

The CLI appears to block on ONNX model download or daemon initialization at startup, before it can answer simple flags like `--version`. The federation component doctor confirms the ONNX loader runs at startup:

```
Loading ONNX model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2...
Loading model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (23MB)
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/onnx/model.onnx
  Downloading: https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/resolve/main/tokenizer.json
ONNX embedder ready: 384d, SIMD: true
```

## Recommended Fix

Guard `--version`, `--help`, and other lightweight flag paths to skip ONNX/daemon init. Load embeddings and daemon connections lazily, only for commands that require them.

## Command Output

```
$ timeout 60 npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: ...
npm warn deprecated uuid@9.0.1: ...
npm warn deprecated glob@10.5.0: ...
Terminated
exit code: 143
```

title: [verification] HIGH: Witness manifests report 95–99 missing build artifacts (dist/ absent)
body:
## Summary

All three platform witness manifests (macOS, Linux, Windows) report 95–99 missing artifact entries and 6–8 drifted files when verified against the current source tree. The Ed25519 signatures themselves are cryptographically valid, but the compiled `dist/` output is absent — the TypeScript packages have not been built.

## Impact

- Release artifact integrity cannot be confirmed; the verification pipeline produces no trustworthy pass/fail for built output.
- Any developer cloning `main` and expecting local `dist/` files will find them absent.
- The witness check is a hard gate in the verification protocol; it cannot be marked passing with missing=95+.

## Expected

```
Ed25519 signature valid: yes
pass=N drift=0 regressed=0 missing=0
```
(for all three manifests)

## Actual

| Manifest | pass | drift | regressed | missing |
|----------|------|-------|-----------|---------|
| macOS    | 12   | 6     | 0         | 99      |
| Linux    | 10   | 8     | 0         | 95      |
| Windows  | 10   | 8     | 0         | 95      |

Ed25519 signatures: **valid** on all three.

## Sample Missing Artifacts

```
ADR-097-Phase2a  v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/dist/domain/entities/federation-node.js
ADR-097-Phase2b  v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/dist/application/federation-breaker-service.js
CAP-MCP-agent-tools  v3/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/agent-tools.js
CAP-MCP-memory-tools  v3/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/mcp-tools/memory-tools.js
ADR-104-transport  v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/dist/transport/midstream-aware-loader.js
... (95–99 total per manifest)
```

## Root Cause

The verification agent runs against a source-only checkout. No `npm run build` (or `npm ci && npm run build`) was run prior to invoking `verify.mjs`, so all `dist/` JS files are absent.

Additionally, the script could not even start on the first attempt due to a missing peer dependency:

```
verify.mjs: could not load @noble/ed25519 from any of:
  /home/user/ruflo
  /home/user/ruflo/v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation
  last error: Cannot find module '@noble/ed25519'
```
Root `npm install` resolved this, but `dist/` files require a build step.

## Recommended Fix

1. Add a prerequisite check in `verify.mjs` (or a wrapper script) that detects missing `dist/` and prints a clear error with instructions before attempting manifest comparison.
2. Document in `plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/witness/README` that `npm run build` must run before `verify.mjs`.
3. CI pre-verification step should always run `npm ci && npm run build` before calling `verify.mjs`.

## Environment

- Node: v22.22.2
- npm: 10.9.7

title: [verification] MEDIUM: npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha doctor full health check times out
body:
## Summary

`npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha doctor` (full health check with no component filter) hangs for >60s and is killed by SIGTERM. The targeted `doctor --component federation` succeeds in ~64s (ONNX downloads included). The hang blocks operators from using doctor to diagnose system health.

## Impact

Operators cannot run full system diagnostics via the CLI. Any automated health-check pipeline using `doctor` without a component filter will time out and report failure.

## Expected

```
doctor completes with no fail status within a reasonable time (<30s)
```

## Actual

```
$ timeout 60 npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha doctor
[60s pass]
Terminated (exit 143)
```

The component-scoped run works:
```
$ timeout 90 npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha doctor --component federation
Loading ONNX model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2...
...
✓ Federation Breaker: Federation plugin not installed (optional) — install only if you need cross-installation peering
Summary: 1 passed — All checks passed! System is healthy.
```

## Likely Root Cause

Same root cause as the `--version` hang (see related HIGH issue): ONNX model download blocks early in the CLI startup path before the full `doctor` command can begin parallel health checks. With the component filter, the check list is shorter and returns before a global timeout.

## Recommended Fix

1. Lazy-load ONNX embeddings — only initialize when a command actually requires them.
2. Add a `--timeout <ms>` flag to `doctor` so operators can control the deadline.
3. Add a `--no-embeddings` flag to skip ML init for lightweight environments.

- HIGH issue: `@claude-flow/cli@alpha --version` hangs and times out (filed same session)

File **ADR-159**: Implement multi-layer agent security stack — (1) MCP tool attestation, (2) indirect injection monitoring at hook chokepoints, (3) agent action audit trail with checkpointing. Target: raise coverage from ~34% to ≥80%.

No ADR — implementation-level note: OWASP ASI02 (Unauthorized Capability Escalation) partially covered by ADR-144; no new ADR needed for that gap alone.

---

## Scan Findings — Intelligence

**Source:** arXiv:2603.20639, arXiv:2506.20664 (Decrypto, June 2026)

Frontier reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B) exhibit emergent "society of thought" — multi-agent-like internal CoT without explicit training. Decrypto benchmark establishes multi-agent Theory of Mind (ToM) as 2026 evaluation standard. MARTI: +21.6% on AIME via RL coordination training (Grade B).

**Signal:** Ruflo's SONA/MoE routing has no ToM evaluation hooks; no Decrypto-style benchmark integration. Opportunity in `performance benchmark --suite all`.

## Scan Findings — Swarm

Google research: multi-agent coordination reduces performance 39–70% on sequential reasoning vs single-agent under equal token budgets. MARTI counters: +21.6% on AIME after RL convergence. Swarm Skills (arXiv:2605.10052): portable self-evolving multi-agent spec with Bayesian scoring but no quantitative conformance tests yet.

**Signal:** Ruflo's hierarchical default (6-8 maxAgents) correctly avoids the sequential-task penalty. RL-based coordination training (MARTI-equivalent) is a future differentiator gap.
