title: memory_store emits 128-dim mock embeddings — AgentDB vectorBackend controller never enables
body:
## Summary

The MCP `memory_store` tool persistently emits **128-dim mock (hash-fallback) embeddings** instead of the real **384-dim ONNX** embeddings, because the AgentDB `vectorBackend` controller initializes as `enabled: false` and never flips — regardless of ruvector being installed, enabled in the neural substrate, or any restart. The standalone CLI (`npx ruflo memory ...`) uses real 384-dim ONNX correctly, so the in-session MCP path and the CLI path diverge.

## Environment

- `ruflo` **3.10.46** (`npx ruflo@latest`), set up as Claude Code plugins + `npx ruflo init --start-all`
- claude-flow v3 runtime, memory **v3.0.0**, backend reported as `sql.js + HNSW`
- `ruvector@0.2.25` installed via `/vector-setup --full` (doctor: all checks pass; native binding working)
- Node `v22.22.2`, Linux x64

## Expected

With ruvector installed and enabled, `memory_store` should produce **384-dim** ONNX vectors (the AgentDB `vectorBackend` controller active), matching what the CLI produces.

## Actual

- `agentdb_controllers` → `vectorBackend` is `{ enabled: false, level: 2 }` (also `reasoningBank: false`). Only 4 of 6 controllers active.
- `memory_store` → `"embeddingDimensions": 128` on every call (mock hash fallback).
- `memory_bridge_status` → `"backend": "sql.js + MOCK (hash fallback)"`, `"embeddingBackend": "mock"`.
- Meanwhile `embeddings_status` reports `dimension: 384`, `neural.ruvector: true`, `ruvectorStatus: { available: true, enabled: true }` — i.e. ruvector IS enabled in the embeddings/neural subsystem, but `memory_store` / the `vectorBackend` controller does not use it.

## Reproduction

1. `npx ruflo init --start-all`; approve the `claude-flow` MCP server (`/mcp`).
2. Call `mcp__claude-flow__memory_store` with any key/value → response shows `embeddingDimensions: 128`.
3. Call `mcp__claude-flow__agentdb_controllers` → `vectorBackend.enabled: false`.

## Things tried (all leave `vectorBackend: false` and `memory_store` at 128-dim)

1. `embeddings_init { force: true }` → initializes a parallel 384-dim ONNX subsystem (`embeddings_status` shows 384), but `memory_store` still 128.
2. Restart the claude-flow MCP server with `.claude-flow/embeddings.json` (384) present.
3. `/vector-setup --full` → `ruvector@0.2.25` + add-ons installed, `ruvector doctor` passes, ruvector registered as its own MCP server (connects fine).
4. `embeddings_neural { action: "init" }` → flips `embeddings_status.neural.ruvector` to `enabled: true` (plus `sona`, `flashAttention`, `ewcPlusPlus`). `vectorBackend` controller still `false`.
5. Restart claude-flow **after** ruvector fully installed → `vectorBackend` still `false`, `memory_store` still 128.

So the `vectorBackend` controller appears to be gated by something other than ruvector availability/enablement, with no user-facing toggle (`config_list` exposes only ~11 generic keys, none for the vector backend).

## Impact

In-session MCP semantic memory (`memory_store` / `memory_search`) runs on low-fidelity 128-dim hash vectors instead of the real 384-dim ONNX embeddings, degrading semantic recall for anything driven through MCP/agents. (Separately, the MCP server's `sql.js` store is also isolated from the CLI's `.swarm/memory.db`, so CLI-written entries are invisible to MCP and vice-versa.)

## Questions

- What gates the AgentDB `vectorBackend` controller's initialization? Is there an env var / config key to force it `enabled` at server boot?
- Is the 128-dim mock fallback in `memory_store` expected when `vectorBackend` is disabled, even though the embeddings subsystem reports a working 384-dim ONNX + ruvector enabled?

## Workaround

Use the standalone `ruvector` MCP server, or the `npx ruflo memory` CLI path — both produce real 384-dim embeddings.

title: feat(routing): #2334 Phase 1 — cost-optimal neural seam + DRACO trajectory collection
body:
Closes #2334 (Phase 1). Supersedes #2347 (the tiny-dancer-direct attempt; this is the metaharness reframe you proposed on 2026-06-15).

## Why

`route(task, embedding?)` already accepts an embedding but no internal caller supplies one, so the neural path described in ADR-026 was never live and no trajectory carries the feature a Phase-2 model would train on. With `@metaharness/router`'s cost-optimal `route(embedding)` over a `{embedding, scores}` dataset + `qualityBar`, both original blockers (safetensors layout, candidate modeling) are moot. This wires the seam and starts collecting the dataset — **default behaviour unchanged.**

## What this changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/ruvector/router-embedding.ts` (new) | Lazy local MiniLM embedding, **only when a gate is open**. Accepts a vector **only** if `backend==='onnx' && dimensions===384` — never a hash fallback (ADR-086). |
| `src/ruvector/neural-router.ts` (new) | `tryCostOptimalRoute()` behind `CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_NEURAL=1` + an artifact at `CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_MODEL_PATH`. Dynamic-imports `@metaharness/router` (optionalDependency, ADR-124); pure-TS k-NN / KRR; returns `null` on any failure. |
| `src/ruvector/router-trajectory.ts` (new) | Opt-in decision rows (`CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_TRAJECTORY=1`) → `.swarm/model-router-trajectories.jsonl`. The **embedding/decision half** of a future training set — see "intentionally NOT" re the missing labelled-outcome half. Best-effort; never throws. |
| `src/ruvector/model-router.ts` | `route()`: lazy-embed when gated, feeding **only** the neural advisor (never the heuristic — so a `bandit-fallback` decision is byte-identical to the default bandit); neural pick stands only if it clears its quality bar; `routedBy` on every result, derived. |
| `package.json` | `@metaharness/router: 0.3.2` → `optionalDependencies` (exact pin). |
| `scripts/audit-env-var-precedence.mjs` | Register the 3 `CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_*` gates as feature-flag escape hatches (the env-var-precedence audit that blocked #2347). |
| `v3/docs/adr/ADR-149-…md` | The seam ADR (see open question on numbering). |

`routedBy ∈ {metaharness-knn, metaharness-krr, fastgrnn, bandit-fallback, heuristic}`. `'fastgrnn'` (native `@ruvector/tiny-dancer`) is **reserved** for Phase 2.

## Validation

```
# build — our added/edited files typecheck clean under the package tsconfig
$ npx tsc --noEmit            # 0 errors in src/ruvector/{neural-router,router-embedding,router-trajectory,model-router}.ts
                              # (residual sandbox errors are unrelated: optional native deps not installed + workspace project-ref ordering)

# tests — vitest 4.0.16
$ npx vitest run __tests__/router-phase1-2334.test.ts __tests__/router-bandit.test.ts __tests__/codemod-routing.test.ts
   ✓ router-phase1-2334.test.ts  (7)   # default byte-identical (0 embedding calls); bandit-fallback;
                                        # bandit-fallback complexity == default (embedding never perturbs the heuristic);
                                        # real metaharness-knn; mock/wrong-dim embedding rejected; trajectory v:1
   ✓ router-bandit.test.ts       (8)   # no regression
   ✓ codemod-routing.test.ts     (4)   # no regression
   Tests  19 passed (19)
```

## Dependencies (supply-chain note, ADR-124)

`@metaharness/router` added as an **optionalDependency, pinned exact**, dynamic-import only; the default path never loads it.
- `@metaharness/router@0.3.2`  `sha512-LQElU6mUrWd3ffJ5bwoonEIgw7oFQZpwZaehffyl/Pg+iozpRjIBPEXdb4uTOBnKH+yPiTEWKc+h9AiZr9Os9w==`
- Known gap: it carries `dist.signatures` but **no npm provenance attestation (SLSA)**. It's single-author + days-old; mitigated by the exact pin + the recorded hash above + full gating (a compromised/absent dep degrades to `bandit-fallback`, never affecting default routing).

`v3/pnpm-lock.yaml` is updated with a **minimal 15-line addition** for the new optionalDependency (lockfileVersion 6.0 / pnpm 8 format, matching the repo). Verified with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` → *"Lockfile is up to date, resolution step is skipped"* — so CI's frozen-lockfile gate passes.

## What's intentionally NOT in this PR

- No trained artifact / training + eval scripts — Phase 2 (the artifact-lifecycle ADR is yours to author).
- **No labelled-outcome sink.** The trajectory rows are the *embedding half* only. The per-model `scores` a trainer needs (quality each tier achieved on a query) are **not** recoverable from today's bandit outcomes (aggregate Beta(α,β) counters, not per-query `taskHash`-keyed labels). A Phase-2 outcome sink is the prerequisite to make these rows trainable — flagging so the dataset isn't assumed complete.
- No native FastGRNN inference (`@ruvector/tiny-dancer`) — reserved; `'fastgrnn'` kept in the union so adding it isn't a breaking change.
- No change to the bandit, the Tier-1 codemods, or the executing-model binding (routing stays advisory). `EnhancedModelRouter` does not yet consume the neural recommendation — wiring it in is a separate step.
- No default flip: both gates default OFF; promotion to default-on is a later step behind a measured +5pp bar.

**Open question (maintainer's call):** ADR numbering — `148` is contested between the frontier-tier ADR (#2357/#2359) and your Phase-2 artifact-lifecycle draft. I used `149` provisionally; renumber as you prefer.

title: fix(hooks): harden memory/hook helpers (timeout race, signal cleanup, truncation, cross-platform slug)
body:
## What

Hardens the `.claude/helpers/*` memory & hook helpers against five grounded bugs, and reconciles the diverged `v3/@claude-flow/cli` copies so the fixes don't drift.

### Fixes

1. **`hook-handler.cjs` — `runWithTimeout()` never guarded async callees.** The timer was cleared the instant `fn()` returned, so an async callee's hang was never caught — the "timeout" protected nothing. Replaced with a real `Promise.race` between the work and the timeout; the timer clears only after one settles. (A *synchronous* blocking callee still can't be preempted in-process — documented honestly; the real guard there is the file-size cap in `intelligence.cjs`.)
2. **`auto-memory-hook.mjs` — `process.on('unhandledRejection', () => {})` swallowed all async failures process-wide.** Scoped to keep hooks exit-0 but log the reason under `RUFLO_DEBUG`/`DEBUG`, restoring visibility of real bugs.
3. **`auto-memory-hook.mjs` / `context-persistence-hook.mjs` — no SIGTERM/SIGINT cleanup.** A signal mid-write could skip `backend.shutdown()`, leaving an unflushed SQLite WAL / stale `agentdb.rvf.lock`. Added signal handlers that flush the active backend before exit.
4. **`intelligence.cjs` — silent 500/100-char truncation.** Downstream reasoning could be built on severed text with no signal. Added a `clip()` helper that appends `…` and warns under debug when it actually cuts.
5. **`intelligence.cjs` — `projectSlug` only handled POSIX `/`.** On Windows the slug kept `:` and `\`, so it never matched Claude Code's real `~/.claude/projects/<slug>` dir and memory bootstrap silently found nothing. Now slugifies every non-alphanumeric to `-`, matching Claude Code's convention.

Plus: reconciles the diverged `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/helpers/{hook-handler,auto-memory-hook,intelligence}` copies so they carry the same fixes as the root dogfood copies.

## Verification

- `node --check` passes on all changed helpers (root + CLI copies).
- `node --test tests/hook-handler-runwithtimeout.test.cjs` — **5/5**, including the decisive case: a slow async fn resolves to `null` at ~3007ms (old code returned the late value at ~5000ms). This test is added by the PR.
- `node --test tests/context-persistence-hook.test.mjs` — 65/66. The one failure is a pre-existing stale assertion expecting a 768-dim hash embedding, while the implementation is 384-dim ONNX-aligned — unrelated to this change.

## Not included

A sixth `statusline.cjs` `execSync`→`execFileSync` hardening exists in my fork but depends on the #2195 statusline *delegation* rewrite that isn't on `main` here, so it's intentionally left out of this PR.

## Notes

Deliberately **not** done: a `session_id` key-sanitization "fix" — it's a controlled Claude UUID stored in a parameterized column, so it was a non-problem.

title: ADR-150 — Integrate @metaharness/* into npx ruflo (3-phase rollout)
body:
Tracking the [ADR-150](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/feat/metaharness-integration-research/v3/docs/adr/ADR-150-metaharness-integration-surfaces.md) rollout — exposing the `@metaharness/*` ecosystem (factory CLI + kernel + router + 5 host adapters + 13 verticals) inside `npx ruflo`'s UX.

**Companion artifacts**
- ADR (decision): `v3/docs/adr/ADR-150-metaharness-integration-surfaces.md` (this branch)
- Research dossier (full graded-evidence sourcing): https://gist.github.com/ruvnet/19d166ff9acf368c9da4172d91ac9113
- Upstream: https://github.com/ruvnet/agent-harness-generator

**Key structural insight** — MetaHarness is first-party (same author, same ADR numbering, registry shape mirrors ruflo's, `host-claude-code` emits ruflo's `.claude/settings.json` format). `@metaharness/router@^0.3.2` is already an `optionalDependency` of `@claude-flow/cli` (ADR-148/149). The remaining surface is the question: how do we expose our sibling's capabilities inside ruflo's UX?

---

## Phase 0 — Measurement spike (1–3 days · no code shipped)

- [ ] Run `npx metaharness score /Users/cohen/Projects/ruflo --json` and capture baseline scorecard
- [ ] Run `npx metaharness genome /Users/cohen/Projects/ruflo --json` for the 7-section readiness report
- [ ] Enable `CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_TRAJECTORY=1` over ≥50 routing decisions; verify `.swarm/model-router-trajectories.jsonl` shape matches `train-bundled-krr.mjs` expectations
- [ ] Confirm `import('@metaharness/router')` succeeds from `v3/@claude-flow/cli`; exercise `Router.fromExamples(...)` with the benchmark corpus
- [ ] Run `npx harness mcp scan .` to baseline ruflo's MCP threat-model

**Exit criteria**: baseline numbers in hand; no surprises in trajectory format or `mcp scan` output. **Do NOT** create plugins or change `package.json` in this phase.

## Phase 1 — MVP (3–7 days · MINOR release 3.12.0)

- [ ] Scaffold `plugins/ruflo-metaharness/` with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `scripts/smoke.sh`
- [ ] Skill `harness-score`: shells `npx metaharness score <path> --json`; exposes as `mcp__claude-flow__metaharness_score_repo`
- [ ] Skill `harness-genome`: shells `npx metaharness genome <path> --json`; exposes as `mcp__claude-flow__metaharness_genome`
- [ ] Skill `harness-mint`: shells `npx metaharness new <name> --template <id> --host <id> --yes`; requires explicit user-specified `targetDir` (never project root)
- [ ] Add `npx metaharness score . --json` to `.github/workflows/v3-ci.yml`; assert `exitCode === 0`
- [ ] Add `npx harness mcp scan .` to `v3-ci.yml`; assert no HIGH findings
- [ ] Pin `@metaharness/router` from `^0.3.2` to `~0.3.2` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json` (caret too permissive given 5-releases-in-2.7h velocity)
- [ ] Add `scripts/check-metaharness-compat.mjs` exercising `Router` constructor; wire into CI before publish
- [ ] Collect trajectory data, retrain bundled KRR via `scripts/train-bundled-krr.mjs`, regenerate `dist/router-krr.json` artifact
- [ ] Validate `routedBy: 'metaharness-krr'` activates on real routing decisions in next bench run

**Exit criteria**: plugin smoke 100%; meta-smoke shows 33/33 plugins (was 32/32); CI score + mcp-scan green on main; new bench shows `routedBy: 'metaharness-krr'` for ≥1 decision driven by measured-seed KRR.

**Semver**: MINOR — additive plugin, additive CI gates, additive MCP tools. No breaking changes.

## Phase 2 — Expansion (1–4 weeks · one or two MINOR releases)

- [ ] `npx ruflo eject` command wrapping `metaharness --from-existing ./` (attribution preserved via `<!-- ruflo-attribution-block -->`)
- [ ] `SelfEvolvingRouter` from `@metaharness/kernel` parallel-logged alongside the Thompson bandit in `model-router.ts` for 2 weeks
- [ ] Promote `SelfEvolvingRouter` to default IF disagreement < 5% OR quality improvement > 2%
- [ ] Accept `type: 'harness'` entries in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/plugins/store/discovery.ts`
- [ ] Surface harness entries via `npx ruflo plugins list --type harness`
- [ ] Add 13th background worker `oia-audit` to `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/hooks.ts` dispatch table
- [ ] `oia-audit` worker runs `buildOiaManifest()` + `buildThreatModel()` + `scanMcp()`; stores results in `metaharness-audit` memory namespace

## Explicitly deferred (Phase 3+ or separate ADR)

- [ ] `@metaharness/kernel` `ToolDispatcher` as primary MCP dispatch (v0.1.0 too early for 314-tool surface change)
- [ ] Promote `@metaharness/router` from `optionalDependency` to `dependency` (wait for 1.0 API stability)
- [ ] Expose `from-repo <git-url>` to Claude Code (untrusted Git clone — keep human-in-the-loop)

## Risks tracked

| Risk | Mitigation status |
|---|---|
| API stability (0.x both sides) | Phase 1 — pin to `~0.3.2`; add compat smoke |
| Subprocess overhead (~200ms cold-start) | Accepted for non-hot-path tools; router stays library-imported |
| GCP dependency in `harness validate` | Phase 1 — skip via `--skip-gcp` in CI |
| Sandboxing on `from-repo` | Phase 1+2 — never expose to Claude Code without explicit user confirm |
| Bus factor (same maintainer as ruflo) | No change from current posture |

## Acceptance

This issue closes when Phase 0 and Phase 1 are complete and a 3.12.0 release has shipped with `routedBy: 'metaharness-krr'` activating in production CI. Phase 2 milestones may close this and open follow-ups.

title: security cve subcommand is a stub — never returns CVE data (scan already does, via npm audit)
body:
## Summary

`security cve` is a stub — it never returns CVE data. Running it (e.g. `ruflo security cve --check`, or `claude-flow security cve`) just prints "No CVE database configured" and exits, regardless of the project's actual vulnerabilities.

This is surprising because the sibling `security scan` command **already does real CVE detection** via `npm audit --json` (GitHub Advisory DB). The data source exists in the codebase; the `cve` subcommand simply doesn't use it.

## Version

`ruflo` / `@claude-flow/cli` **3.10.46**

## Steps to reproduce

```console
$ cd any-node-project-with-known-vulns
$ npx ruflo security cve --check
# or: claude-flow security cve --list
```

## Actual

```
CVE Database
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
⚠ No CVE database configured.
This command requires a CVE data source (e.g., NVD API) which is not yet integrated.

To check for real vulnerabilities, use:

  $ npm audit                                    # dependency vulnerabilities
  $ claude-flow security scan                     # real code + dependency scan
```

The `--check`, `--list`, and `--severity` flags have no effect.

## Expected

`security cve` should report the project's known CVEs (honoring `--check` / `--severity` / `--list`), the same way `security scan` already does.

## Root cause

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/security.ts` → `cveCommand.action` (~line 259) is a hardcoded "not integrated" message. Meanwhile `scanCommand` in the same file (~lines 56–88) runs `npm audit --json` and parses `vulnerabilities[].via[]` for severity/title/url. The `cve` subcommand could reuse that exact approach.

## Suggested fix

Implement `cveCommand.action` against `npm audit --json` (the source `scan` already uses), with `--check` filtering advisories by package/CVE/GHSA/title and `--severity` by level. Using `spawnSync('npm', ['audit', '--json'])` (fixed argv, no shell) keeps it injection-free.

I already have a working patch and am happy to open a PR if useful.

title: [BUG] daemon proliferation: `init.ts:424` spawns `daemon start &` racing the PID-file dedup → kernel panic on macOS
body:
## Symptom

On a long-running Mac (macOS 26.1, Mac mini M4 Pro), a clean session accumulated:

- **39 zombie `node … @claude-flow/cli/bin/cli.js daemon start --foreground --quiet --workspace /Users/cohen/Projects/ruflo` processes**, ages 2 min → 4¾ hours, sizes 3 MB → 600 MB
- **3 stale `node_modules/.bin/cli mcp start` processes** including two 3 GB RSS each
- Total leaked resident memory: **~8.5 GiB**

Consequence: macOS kernel panic 2026-06-15 21:06 (`panic-full-2026-06-15-210627.0002.panic`) and a near-panic WindowServer userspace-watchdog timeout 2026-06-17 15:49 (`WindowServer-2026-06-17-154934.ips`). The system reboots and FileVault then blocks auto-login.

```
Pages free (before cleanup):     25,956   (~400 MiB)
Pages occupied by compressor: 1,761,687   (~27 GiB)
```

After killing the 41 dupes (keeping the newest of each group):

```
Pages free (after cleanup):  1,245,170   (~19 GiB)
Pages occupied by compressor:   14,941   (~230 MiB)
```

## Root cause

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/init.ts:424`:

```ts
execSync('npx @claude-flow/cli@latest daemon start 2>/dev/null &', {
  stdio: 'pipe',
  cwd: ctx.cwd,
  timeout: 10000
});
```

The trailing `&` makes `execSync` return as soon as the shell forks. The daemon hasn't started yet, hasn't written its PID file. If another `init`/`daemon start` runs in the next ~500 ms (devcontainer setup, VS Code task, MCP server start hook), `getBackgroundDaemonPid()` returns null for both, the dedup short-circuit at `daemon.ts:97-102` is bypassed, and both processes proceed to `startBackgroundDaemon()` → fork. Repeat over hours of usage and you get 39 live daemons.

The `daemon start` command already handles backgrounding internally (`daemon.ts:112-121` → `startBackgroundDaemon` does the detached fork). The `&` in `init.ts:424` is both unnecessary AND breaks the launcher's dedup.

## Repro

```bash
# In a fresh repo, with the daemon configured to auto-start in init prompts:
for i in {1..5}; do npx @claude-flow/cli init --start-all & done; wait
ps -axo pid,etime,command | grep "daemon start --foreground" | wc -l
# Observe: > 1
```

## Fix

Remove the `&` from `init.ts:424`. The `daemon start` command does the background fork itself; `execSync` will then wait for the launcher's PID-check / fork path to complete, and concurrent invocations will see the PID file and short-circuit.

## Related

- #527 — original "MCP Process Proliferation Causing VS Code Port Forwarding Issues" (open since 2025-07-29) — same class of bug, different surface.

## Environment

- ruflo @ feat/metaharness-integration-research, commit b5dc6896e
- `@claude-flow/cli` 3.11.0
- macOS 26.1 (25B78), Mac16,11 (Mac mini M4 Pro)
- Node v22.22.1 via mise

title: fix(daemon + security): #2407 daemon race + #2403 cve subcommand
body:
## Summary

Closes #2407.

Without atomic dedup, concurrent `daemon start` invocations all bypass the PID-file check and fork independent daemons. One incident on a long-running Mac accumulated **39 zombie daemons holding ~8.5 GiB** resident and contributed to the **2026-06-15 21:06 kernel panic** (compressor 27 GiB, configd watchdog timeout, panic-full-2026-06-15-210627).

## Two-stage race

**Stage 1** — `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/init.ts:424` used:
```ts
execSync('npx @claude-flow/cli@latest daemon start 2>/dev/null &', ...)
```
The trailing `&` made execSync return as soon as the shell forked, **before** the daemon wrote its PID file. Concurrent init invocations (devcontainer setup + VS Code task + MCP hook firing within ~500 ms) all hit Stage 2 with an empty PID file.

**Stage 2** — `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/daemon.ts:95-105`'s dedup read the PID file and forked `startBackgroundDaemon` non-atomically. N concurrent callers all saw an empty PID, all proceeded, all forked. Last write to the PID file won; the other N-1 ran orphaned.

## Fix

1. **`init.ts`**: drop the shell `&`. `daemon start` (default non-foreground mode) already handles its own detached background fork via `startBackgroundDaemon` AND writes the PID file synchronously before returning. Timeout bumped 10s → 30s for npx cold-cache scenarios.
2. **`daemon.ts`**: wrap the dedup + spawn in an **O_EXCL atomic lockfile** (`.claude-flow/daemon.lock`). Winner reads the PID file, spawns or short-circuits. Losers see `EEXIST`, poll for up to 5s waiting for the winner's PID to land, then return "already running" cleanly. Stale lockfile (crashed mid-spawn) is recovered by unlinking after timeout.

## Validation (race test)

5 concurrent `node cli.js daemon start` invocations against a fresh `/tmp/race-test2` workspace:

| | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| Surviving daemons | **3** | **1** ✓ |
| `Daemon already running` callers | 0 | 2 |
| killStaleDaemons sweeps | 0 | 2 (recovered mid-spawn crashes) |

After-fix output:
```
[OK] Daemon started in background (PID: 84773)
[WARN] Daemon already running in background (PID: 84773). Stop it first with: daemon stop
[WARN] Daemon already running in background (PID: 84773). Stop it first with: daemon stop

count: 1
PID file: 84773
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `bash plugins/ruflo-metaharness/scripts/smoke.sh` still green
- [ ] `metaharness-ci` jobs green
- [ ] No regression in daemon stop/restart flow
- [ ] Race test reproduces only 1 surviving daemon

Tracking issue for [ADR-153](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-153-metaharness-darwin-mode-integration.md) — population-based harness self-improvement via [@metaharness/darwin@0.1.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@metaharness/darwin).

## Summary

`@metaharness/darwin` is the **write** layer of the metaharness ecosystem. Where [ADR-150](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-150-metaharness-integration-surfaces.md) gave ruflo `score` / `genome` / `mcp-scan` / `threat-model` / `oia-audit` / `similarity` / `drift-from-history` (all read-only), Darwin Mode evolves a harness's 7 policy surfaces under a sandbox + safety inspector + promotion gate. **The model is frozen; the harness evolves.**

## Architectural constraints (per ADR-153, mirrors ADR-150)

1. **Removable** — `npm ls --without @metaharness/darwin` produces a working CLI
2. **Optional** — `@metaharness/darwin` lives in `optionalDependencies`, never `dependencies`
3. **Graceful degradation** — `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` emits `{degraded: true, reason: 'metaharness-darwin-not-installed', ...}` and exits 0
4. **CI gate** — `no-metaharness-smoke.yml` covers absence; `metaharness-ci.yml` adds a 5-min dry-run job

## Phase 1 MVP — checklist

- [ ] Add `@metaharness/darwin@~0.1.0` to `optionalDependencies` of:
  - [ ] `package.json` (root umbrella)
  - [ ] `ruflo/package.json`
  - [ ] `v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json`
- [ ] `plugins/ruflo-metaharness/scripts/evolve.mjs` — spawn wrapper, degraded payload on MODULE_NOT_FOUND, surfaces `winner.json` + top-N leaderboard
- [ ] Top-level CLI command `npx ruflo evolve <repo>` (mirrors `ruflo eject`), or `metaharness evolve` subcommand — decide before implementation
- [ ] MCP tool `mcp__claude-flow__metaharness_evolve` with ADR-112 "Use when ..." guidance
- [ ] `npx ruflo doctor --component metaharness` extended to report `@metaharness/darwin` availability + `metaharness-darwin --version`
- [ ] New `darwin-dryrun` job in `.github/workflows/metaharness-ci.yml`:
  - [ ] 5-min budget
  - [ ] `metaharness-darwin evolve . --generations 1 --children 1 --concurrency 1 --seed 0` on a seed repo
  - [ ] Asserts `archive.json` + `lineage.json` + `reports/winner.json` exist
- [ ] Smoke step 18 in `plugins/ruflo-metaharness/scripts/smoke.sh` — 5 grep checks + 1 runtime degraded-path check
- [ ] Extend `.github/workflows/no-metaharness-smoke.yml` graceful-degradation drill to cover darwin
- [ ] Update `CLAUDE.md` MetaHarness section with `ruflo evolve` + `metaharness_evolve`
- [ ] Add a "Darwin Mode" section to `docs/metaharness-user-guide.md`

## Explicit non-goals (Phase 1)

1. No model fine-tuning (model is frozen; harness evolves)
2. No auto-evolve in CI (user-initiated operation only)
3. No bypass of existing CVE / threat-model / mcp-scan checks
4. No cross-repo promotion (federation is Phase 3)
5. No in-place mutation of ruflo's own surfaces — variants land under `.metaharness/variants/`, promotion stays a manual PR through normal review

## Phases 2-4 (out of scope for this issue)

| Phase | Scope |
|---|---|
| 2 | Witness-sign winning archives (ADR-103) so promoted variants carry cryptographic provenance |
| 3 | Federated archives — share lineage trees across ruflo installations via the IPFS pattern from `hooks transfer` |
| 4 | Per-repo policy file `.metaharness/policy.json` — restrict which surfaces may mutate |

## Acceptance criteria

- All 4 ADR-153 architectural constraints verifiable via existing CI workflows
- Local validation: `bash plugins/ruflo-metaharness/scripts/smoke.sh` step 18 green
- Local validation: `npx ruflo evolve /tmp/seed-repo --generations 1 --children 1` produces archive/lineage/winner JSON
- Local validation: `npm uninstall @metaharness/darwin && npx ruflo evolve .` emits `{degraded: true, reason: 'metaharness-darwin-not-installed'}`, exits 0
- CI validation: new `darwin-dryrun` job in `metaharness-ci.yml` green
- Doctor validation: `npx ruflo doctor --component metaharness` includes a `darwin: { installed: true/false, version: '...' }` row

## Cross-references

- [ADR-153](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-153-metaharness-darwin-mode-integration.md) — this integration design
- [ADR-150](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-150-metaharness-integration-surfaces.md) — the original metaharness integration (read layer)
- [ADR-151](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-151-harness-intelligence-layer.md) — the recommender that could consume Darwin archives (Phase 4 candidate)
- [ADR-152](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-152-genome-similarity-search.md) — genome similarity (the metric Darwin's archive should ALSO be evaluated against)
- [@metaharness/darwin@0.1.0 on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@metaharness/darwin)
- Upstream source: [`ruvnet/agent-harness-generator/packages/darwin-mode`](https://github.com/ruvnet/agent-harness-generator/tree/main/packages/darwin-mode)
- Upstream design ADRs: ADR-070…075 in the agent-harness-generator repo

## Target release

`ruflo@3.13.0` (MINOR — new CLI surface + MCP tool count, ADR-150 + ADR-153 are siblings).

title: Windows: ruflo-adr import returns 0, agent-browser open hangs, agentdb G7 controllers disabled
body:
# Upstream findings: ruflo / claude-flow on Windows

Three independent findings from a full subsystem health audit on Windows 11 (win32-x64),
Node v24.15.0, `@claude-flow/cli` v3.12.3. Each can be filed as a separate issue.

| # | Component | Severity | Type |
|---|-----------|----------|------|
| 1 | `ruflo-adr` `scripts/import.mjs` | High | Windows path-separator bug (functional) |
| 2 | `agent-browser` (used by `ruflo-browser`) | High | Headed auto-launch hang on Windows |
| 3 | `ruflo-agentdb` G7 controllers | Medium | Docs/runtime contradiction + related tool defects |

---

## Finding 1 — `ruflo-adr` ADR import/index returns 0 records on Windows (path-separator mismatch)

**Plugin:** `ruflo-adr` (observed in cache version `0.3.0`)
**File:** `scripts/import.mjs`
**Severity:** High — `adr-index` and downstream `adr-verify` silently report an empty graph despite ADRs being present.

### Symptom
On Windows, running the ADR import (e.g. `adr-index`, or `node scripts/import.mjs`) reports:

```
Total ADRs: 0 across 0 source dirs
```

even when many `docs/adr/` or `docs/adrs/` directories contain `*.md` ADR files. As a result the `adr-patterns` / `adr-edges` namespaces stay empty and `adr-verify` shows an empty dependency graph.

### Root cause
In `findAdrs()`, the candidate path is built with `join(dir, e)`, which on Windows yields backslash separators (e.g. `C:\...\docs\adrs\0001-foo.md`). The file-selection test then matches **hardcoded forward-slash** substrings:

```js
// scripts/import.mjs  (~line 50)
} else if (e.endsWith('.md') && (p.includes('/docs/adr/') || p.includes('/docs/adrs/'))) {
  out.push(p);
}
```

`p.includes('/docs/adrs/')` is always `false` on Windows because `p` contains `\docs\adrs\`. Every ADR is skipped → `total: 0`.

A second, related forward-slash assumption affects the displayed `file` field:

```js
// scripts/import.mjs  (~line 66)
return { id, title, status, date, tags, context, links, file: path.replace(ROOT + '/', '') };
```

`ROOT + '/'` (forward slash) never matches the backslash-joined `path`, so on Windows the `file` field is left as the full absolute backslash path instead of a repo-relative one.

### Fix
Normalize separators to `/` before the substring checks (and before stripping `ROOT`):

```js
// ~line 50 — normalize before matching
} else if (e.endsWith('.md')) {
  const np = p.replace(/\\/g, '/');
  if (np.includes('/docs/adr/') || np.includes('/docs/adrs/')) out.push(p);
}
```

```js
// ~line 66 — normalize both sides before stripping ROOT
return { id, title, status, date, tags, context, links,
  file: path.replace(/\\/g, '/').replace(ROOT.replace(/\\/g, '/') + '/', '') };
```

This is cross-platform: POSIX paths already use `/`, so the `replace(/\\/g, '/')` is a no-op there; Windows paths get normalized so the matches succeed.

### Verification (Windows, after patch)
Dry-run against a tree containing many plugin `docs/adrs/` directories:

```
$ IMPORT_DRY_RUN=1 ADR_ROOT="<...>/plugins" node scripts/import.mjs
Total ADRs: **36** across 33 source dirs
```

Before the patch the same command returned `Total ADRs: 0 across 0 source dirs`.

### Notes
- The structural smoke tests for `ruflo-adr` pass (15/15) because they only check file presence and script syntax — they do not exercise `findAdrs()` against backslash paths, so the defect ships green.
- Suggested guard: add a regression test that runs `findAdrs()` against a path containing OS-native separators, or run the dry-run import in CI on a Windows runner.

---

## Finding 2 — `agent-browser open` hangs indefinitely on Windows (headed auto-launch); headless + CDP-connect works

**Component:** `agent-browser` CLI (the browser engine `ruflo-browser` shells out to)
**Severity:** High — out-of-the-box browser automation is unusable on this Windows host; every `ruflo-browser` skill that calls `open` stalls.

### Symptom
With Chromium present, a bare navigation hangs forever with no output and no error:

```
$ npx agent-browser open https://example.com
# prints nothing further; never returns
```

During the hang, a process check shows **no Chromium and no agent-browser node process** ever spawn; no screenshot is produced. The command had to be killed after several minutes. (This reproduces the original 3+ minute hang observed for `open about:blank`.)

### Not a missing-engine issue
Playwright Chromium **is** installed:

```
$ npx playwright install chromium
# → C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\ms-playwright\chromium-1228\chrome-win64\chrome.exe
```

So the stall is in `agent-browser`'s **headed auto-launch path**, not engine provisioning. Most likely the default (headed) launch waits on a browser/display that never materializes in a non-interactive / no-display Windows shell, and never times out or errors.

### Working alternative (verified end-to-end)
Pre-launching Chromium headless with a remote-debugging port and connecting over CDP works completely:

```bash
# 1) launch the installed Chromium headless with a CDP port
"…/ms-playwright/chromium-1228/chrome-win64/chrome.exe" \
  --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox \
  --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir="…/.chrome-cdp-profile" about:blank

# 2) confirm the CDP endpoint
curl -s http://localhost:9222/json/version
# → {"Browser":"Chrome/149.0.7827.55", … "webSocketDebuggerUrl":"ws://localhost:9222/devtools/browser/…"}

# 3) drive agent-browser over CDP
npx agent-browser connect 9222          # → ✓ Done
npx agent-browser open https://example.com   # → ✓ Example Domain
npx agent-browser screenshot out.png    # → ✓ Screenshot saved (valid 8,305-byte PNG, renders correctly)
```

### Suggested fixes
- Make `open` (and other auto-launch commands) default to **headless** when no display is available, or detect the non-interactive/headless context.
- Add a hard **launch timeout** so a stalled headed launch errors out instead of hanging silently.
- Document the headless `--remote-debugging-port` + `connect <port>` recipe as the supported Windows/CI path.

---

## Finding 3 — `ruflo-agentdb` G7 controllers documented as "activated" but disabled at runtime (gated on a connected AgentDB backend)

**Plugin:** `ruflo-agentdb`; engine `@claude-flow/memory`
**Severity:** Medium — docs/runtime contradiction, plus two genuinely broken tools in the same domain.

### Symptom
`README.md` (G7 block) and `ADR-095` state that five previously-disabled controllers
(`mutationGuard`, `attestationLog`, `gnnService`, `rvfOptimizer`, `guardedVectorBackend`)
were **activated** in ruflo 3.6.23+. But the live registry on v3.12.3 reports them still disabled:

```
$ npx @claude-flow/cli@latest mcp exec --tool agentdb_controllers --params '{}'
# total: 23, active: 16
# enabled:false → mutationGuard(L2), gnnService(L2), attestationLog(L3),
#                 semanticRouter(L4), guardedVectorBackend(L5), rvfOptimizer(L5), graphAdapter(L6)
```

### Root cause
The controllers are **not** disabled-by-default — their enable predicate is conditional on a live AgentDB instance. From the compiled registry:

```js
// @claude-flow/memory/dist/controller-registry.js  (~lines 378–406)
case 'mutationGuard':
case 'attestationLog':
case 'guardedVectorBackend':
    return this.agentdb !== null;     // security controllers
…
case 'gnnService':
case 'rvfOptimizer':
case 'semanticRouter':
    return this.agentdb !== null;     // AgentDB-internal controllers
```

In the default `npx` / idle runtime, `this.agentdb === null` (the memory backend reports `none` until a session/swarm wires AgentDB in), so all of these correctly evaluate to `false`. `graphAdapter` additionally requires an external graph-DB (by design).

So the activation is **conditional on a connected AgentDB backend**, not unconditional. The README/ADR-095 wording ("activated in 3.6.23+") overstates it and should read something like *"enabled when a live AgentDB backend is connected (`agentdb !== null`); otherwise inactive."* Alternatively, if these were intended to be active by default, the runtime isn't wiring `agentdb` when it should.

### Related defects observed in the same domain (worth separate triage)
- **`agentdb_pattern-store` always fails:** every invocation returns `{success:false, error:'pattern must be a string'}` regardless of payload shape (string, object, with/without metadata). Looks like a handler input-validation defect, not the documented benign `memory-store-fallback`.
- **`ruvector@0.2.25` standalone `embed text` fails:** `"Failed to initialize ONNX embedder: ONNX WASM files not bundled. The onnx/ directory is missing."` The package's own embedding path is non-functional (the separate `@claude-flow` memory embedder works fine via a disk-cached model).

### Suggested fixes
- Correct the README/ADR-095 G7 wording to describe the controllers as **gated on a connected AgentDB backend**, and/or document how to wire AgentDB so they activate.
- Fix the `agentdb_pattern-store` validation handler.
- Bundle the ONNX WASM/`onnx/` assets in `ruvector` (or document that standalone `embed` requires them).

title: security(deps): bump agentic-flow ^2.0.13 → ^2.0.14 to pull CWE-78 MCP shell-injection fix
body:
## Summary

Ruflo depends on `agentic-flow` as a runtime dependency. `agentic-flow` ≤ 2.0.13 contained an OS command injection vulnerability in its MCP server tools (CWE-78 — see [ruvnet/agentic-flow#169](https://github.com/ruvnet/agentic-flow/issues/169) for full advisory). Any Ruflo installation that resolved a vulnerable `agentic-flow` version exposed that injection surface whenever the bundled `standalone-stdio` / `http-sse` / `http-streaming-updated` / `stdio-full` / `claude-flow-sdk` / `poc-stdio` MCP servers were started.

- **Fixed by:** bumping the dep from `^2.0.13` → `^2.0.14`
- **Commit:** d51d56930 on branch `security/cwe-78-agentic-flow-bump`
- **Companion upstream advisory:** ruvnet/agentic-flow#169
- **Companion upstream fix commit:** ruvnet/agentic-flow a0f9c2b
- **Published upstream version:** `agentic-flow@2.0.14`

## Scope check

This is a **dep-only** fix. Ruflo does not vendor any of the vulnerable files — they live in `node_modules/agentic-flow/dist/mcp/`. Ruflo's own MCP tools (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/`) were audited as part of this work and confirmed to already use the hardened `execFileSync(file, argv, { shell: false })` pattern that the earlier CVE pass (`audit_1776853149979` markers in `github-tools.ts`) established. Specifically:

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/github-tools.ts` — has `run(staticCmdOnly)` and `runArgv(file, args)` helpers with explicit security comments; the only remaining string-form `execSync` is gated to static commands with no user input
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/terminal-tools.ts` — `terminal_execute` runs user-provided commands by design (this is the tool's purpose, not an unintended sink); inputs are validated via `validateText` / `validateIdentifier` / `validatePath` / `validateEnv` at boundary

No ruflo source changes were required; the fix is consumed entirely through the upstream npm release.

## What changed

```diff
--- a/package.json
+++ b/package.json
@@ -72,7 +72,7 @@
     "@ruvector/router-linux-x64-gnu": "^0.1.30",
     "@ruvector/sona": "^0.1.5",
     "agentdb": "^3.0.0-alpha.16",
-    "agentic-flow": "^2.0.13"
+    "agentic-flow": "^2.0.14"
```

Plus `package-lock.json` refreshed via `npm install agentic-flow@^2.0.14 --save`.

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/package.json` was **not** changed — it pins `agentic-flow: ^3.0.0-alpha.1` (a separate major/alpha line not covered by the 2.x advisory).

## Verification

Run from the repo root after `npm install`:

```bash
$ npm view agentic-flow version
2.0.14

$ cat node_modules/agentic-flow/package.json | grep '"version"'
  "version": "2.0.14",

$ for f in standalone-stdio.js \
          fastmcp/servers/claude-flow-sdk.js \
          fastmcp/servers/http-sse.js \
          fastmcp/servers/http-streaming-updated.js \
          fastmcp/servers/stdio-full.js \
          fastmcp/servers/poc-stdio.js; do
    ec=$(grep -c "execSync("    "node_modules/agentic-flow/dist/mcp/$f" || echo 0)
    ef=$(grep -c "execFileSync(" "node_modules/agentic-flow/dist/mcp/$f")
    echo "$f | execSync=$ec | execFileSync=$ef"
  done
```

Observed:

| File | `execSync()` calls | `execFileSync()` calls |
|------|-------------------:|----------------------:|
| `standalone-stdio.js` | **0** | 14 |
| `fastmcp/servers/claude-flow-sdk.js` | **0** | 6 |
| `fastmcp/servers/http-sse.js` | **0** | 5 |
| `fastmcp/servers/http-streaming-updated.js` | **0** | 9 |
| `fastmcp/servers/stdio-full.js` | **0** | 9 |
| `fastmcp/servers/poc-stdio.js` | **0** | 2 |

The only remaining `execSync` token anywhere in `node_modules/agentic-flow/dist/mcp/standalone-stdio.js` is a comment line documenting the historical sink — the actual call sites are gone.

## Distribution to downstream users

The legacy `alpha` / `v3alpha` dist-tags on the `ruflo` and `claude-flow` packages already point at the stable line per repo policy (see [feedback_stable_semver_no_alpha](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)). When the next `ruflo` / `claude-flow` / `@claude-flow/cli` patch release ships, `npx ruflo@latest` / `npx claude-flow@latest` / `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest` will all resolve `agentic-flow` ≥ 2.0.14 transitively via the bumped `^2.0.14` pin.

Until then, anyone on an existing `ruflo@3.6.x` install can pull the patched dep manually:

```bash
cd $(npm root -g)/ruflo  # or your project root if installed locally
npm install agentic-flow@^2.0.14
```

## Recommendation for the next release

Roll this bump into the next `ruflo` patch (3.6.11) under semver. The bump is non-breaking — all `agentic-flow` 2.0.14 MCP tool signatures are byte-identical to 2.0.13; only the internal shell-out implementation changed.

Per [the publishing rules in CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#publishing-rules), the bump must be propagated to **all three** packages with **all three** dist-tags each:

| Package | `latest` | `alpha` (legacy) | `v3alpha` (legacy) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@claude-flow/cli` | 3.6.11 | 3.6.11 | 3.6.11 |
| `claude-flow` | 3.6.11 | 3.6.11 | 3.6.11 |
| `ruflo` | 3.6.11 | 3.6.11 | 3.6.11 |

Also remember to mirror the bump into `ruflo/package.json` overrides (the wrapper does not inherit root `overrides`, per the [#2112 lesson in MEMORY.md](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#publishing-rules)).

## Cross-references

- Upstream advisory + fix: ruvnet/agentic-flow#169
- Upstream fix commit: ruvnet/agentic-flow a0f9c2b
- Published version: `agentic-flow@2.0.14`
- Ruflo branch: `security/cwe-78-agentic-flow-bump`
- Ruflo commit: d51d56930
- Original red-team report: `npm_agentic-flow_report_package_20260618_163017.zip`

title: [ADR-155] Implementation tracker — nightly self-learning security harness
body:
## Implementation tracker for [ADR-155](v3/docs/adr/ADR-155-nightly-self-learning-security-harness.md)

Triggered by the CWE-78 incident ([GHSA-vcv2-r9jh-99m5](https://github.com/ruvnet/agentic-flow/security/advisories/GHSA-vcv2-r9jh-99m5) / #2414 / #2415) — we caught it via reporter goodwill, not our own gates. This issue tracks the work to make security catchment first-party.

ADR proposal PR: #2417

## Architecture (recap)

```
            ┌──────────────────────────── nightly @ 03:23 UTC ───────────────────────────┐
            │                                                                            │
            │   fan-out (parallel, fail-fast: false)                                     │
            │   ┌────────────┬─────────────┬────────────────┬──────────┬──────────────┐  │
            │   │ deps CVE   │ mcp-static  │ mcp-pentest    │ codeql   │ differential │  │
            │   │ npm audit  │ mcp-scan +  │ vitest replay  │ existing │ harness      │  │
            │   │ osv-scan   │ threat-     │ injection      │ codeql   │ drift-from-  │  │
            │   │ gh advs.   │ model       │ corpus         │ workflow │ history      │  │
            │   └─────┬──────┴──────┬──────┴───────┬────────┴────┬─────┴──────┬───────┘  │
            │         │             │              │             │            │          │
            │         ▼             ▼              ▼             ▼            ▼          │
            │   ┌─────────────────────────────── triage ───────────────────────────────┐ │
            │   │  dedupe  →  rank (KRR weights)  →  suppress (TTL)  →  route        │ │
            │   │                                                                     │ │
            │   │  HIGH+ → issue + page · MEDIUM → issue · LOW → digest · NEW → log  │ │
            │   └─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘ │
            │                                     ▼                                     │
            │                       AgentDB: metaharness-security-audit                 │
            └────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                                       outcome-collector.yml (daily)
                                       resolves outcomes → trains nightly KRR
```

## Phase 1 — Land the workflow (closes the CWE-78 class alone)

> Goal: a nightly run that would have caught \`agentic-flow ≤ 2.0.13\` on day one. No learning yet; dumb max-severity ranking.

- [ ] **W1.1** Add \`.github/workflows/nightly-security-harness.yml\` with the 5-dimension matrix + triage job (cron \`23 3 * * *\`)
- [ ] **W1.2** Add \`scripts/security-triage.mjs\` — consumes 5 artifact streams, dedupes by \`(cwe, package, version_range, file)\`, ranks by raw severity, opens GitHub issues
- [ ] **W1.3** Add \`scripts/dimensions/deps-cve.mjs\` — runs \`npm audit --json\` + \`osv-scanner --format sarif\` + \`gh advisory list -R . --json\`; merges to one SARIF
- [ ] **W1.4** Add \`scripts/dimensions/mcp-static.mjs\` — wraps existing \`harness mcp-scan\` + \`harness threat-model\` outputs
- [ ] **W1.5** Add \`scripts/dimensions/mcp-pentest.mjs\` + initial \`tests/security/payloads.json\` corpus (start with the CWE-78 payload from today + 5 other known classes)
- [ ] **W1.6** Add \`scripts/dimensions/codeql.mjs\` — pulls SARIF from existing \`codeql.yml\` artifact
- [ ] **W1.7** Add \`scripts/dimensions/differential.mjs\` — wraps existing \`harness drift-from-history\`
- [ ] **W1.8** Cost budget circuit breaker (ADR-097 pattern) in \`security-triage.mjs\` — fails soft at \`$0.50\`, hard cap \`$1.00\`
- [ ] **W1.9** Issue templates: \`security-finding.md\` with \`{cwe, severity, dimension, evidence, fix_pr_hint}\` fields
- [ ] **W1.10** \`outcome-collector.yml\` daily workflow — scans closed security-labeled issues, classifies close reason, writes outcomes to AgentDB
- [ ] **W1.11** Backfill test: run the workflow against \`d51d56930^\` (pre-bump commit) and confirm it would have surfaced the CWE-78 vuln
- [ ] **W1.12** Update CLAUDE.md "Doctor Health Checks" section + add nightly-security-harness to the workflow inventory

**Definition of done for Phase 1:** the nightly run completes within 10 min wall-time, costs ≤ \$0.50, opens issues only for HIGH+ findings, and the backfill test (W1.11) demonstrably flags the CWE-78 regression on the pre-fix commit.

## Phase 2 — Loop A (per-dimension confidence weighting)

> Goal: when CodeQL + osv disagree, the model learns which dimension to weight. Triple-gate guard: \`CLAUDE_FLOW_NIGHTLY_LEARN_A=1\` env flag.

- [ ] **W2.1** Accumulate 30 days of \`(finding, dimension, human_outcome)\` from Phase 1 — gating criterion: ≥ 100 closed findings before training
- [ ] **W2.2** Add \`scripts/security-train.mjs\` — nightly KRR retrain over the accumulated trajectories
- [ ] **W2.3** Output \`data/security-triage-weights.json\` — checked into repo so weights are reproducible and auditable
- [ ] **W2.4** Add triple-gate to \`security-triage.mjs\`: env flag + weights-file present + import success → use KRR; else fall back to Phase 1 ranking
- [ ] **W2.5** Weekly weight snapshots as git tags: \`security-weights-2026-W25\` (rollback is one \`git checkout\`)
- [ ] **W2.6** Drift alarm — if KRR weights move > N std-devs from prior week, page maintainer instead of self-applying

## Phase 3 — Loop B (severity calibration)

> Goal: isotonic regression of \`CVSS → realized_impact_in_our_stack\`. Triple-gate: \`CLAUDE_FLOW_NIGHTLY_LEARN_B=1\`.

- [ ] **W3.1** Gating: ≥ 50 findings with realized-impact data (\`was_exploited\`, \`caused_revert\`, \`no_op\`) before training
- [ ] **W3.2** Fit isotonic regression, store as \`data/cvss-calibration.json\`
- [ ] **W3.3** Safety rail: a finding's calibrated severity can be ≤ its CVE-DB severity by at most one band (HIGH cannot drop below MEDIUM)
- [ ] **W3.4** Suppression catalog \`data/security-suppressions.json\` — each entry has \`{finding_hash, justification, suppressed_by, ttl_expires_at}\`; PRs against this file require security-team review
- [ ] **W3.5** Weekly suppression-diff comment on the nightly issue digest — visible audit trail

## Phase 4 — Loop C (auto-fix bid) — OUT OF SCOPE here, will be ADR-156

Reserved as a separate ADR because the auto-fix bid touches the human-in-the-loop gate explicitly. Today's session (agentic-flow 2.0.14 → ruflo 3.12.4 in 4 tool turns) is the proof-of-concept that the mechanism works; ADR-156 will write down the authorization model that lets it run unattended.

## Cross-cutting

- [ ] **X.1** \`no-metaharness-smoke.yml\`-style assertion: the harness can run with the \`harness\` CLI missing (falls back to static SARIF only) — proves ADR-150 graceful degradation
- [ ] **X.2** Memory contract documented in \`v3/docs/memory-namespaces.md\` for \`metaharness-security-audit\`
- [ ] **X.3** \`/ruflo-security-audit:nightly-status\` skill — surface the latest run's summary in Claude Code
- [ ] **X.4** Daily digest: one comment per day on a pinned tracking issue with the previous night's run summary
- [ ] **X.5** GHSA-DB integration smoke test (rate-limit + cache fallback paths)

## Definition of done — full feature

- [ ] Nightly run consistently completes within budget (10 min, ≤ \$0.50)
- [ ] Backfill of last 12 months of git history surfaces ≥ 80% of known closed security issues (recall floor)
- [ ] False-positive rate on opened issues < 30% after 60 days of Loop A training (precision floor)
- [ ] Cost-per-confirmed-real-finding < \$2 (cost-effectiveness floor)
- [ ] All Phase 1+2 workflow files pass \`no-metaharness-smoke.yml\`-style absent-path tests

## Risks & open questions

| Risk | Mitigation in scope | Open question |
|---|---|---|
| Suppression catalog becomes a silent backdoor | TTL on every suppression; weekly diff; security-team review on PRs | Should this live in repo file or AgentDB? (ADR defers to repo-file v1, revisit v2) |
| Model regresses, starts suppressing real CVEs | drift-from-history (ADR-152); weekly \`confirmed_real / total\` ratio tracked; training pauses if ratio drops > 20% | What's the right rollback signal — automatic or maintainer-paged? |
| GHSA rate limits mid-run | Exponential backoff + cached advisory list + \`degraded\` marker | Should we mirror GHSA into AgentDB nightly? |
| Active pentest noisy in MCP server logs | Logs to artifact only; explicit token-redaction step | Worth running this dimension off the schedule cadence? (weekly vs nightly) |
| LLM-judge cost runaway on a noisy finding storm | ADR-026 routing + ADR-097-style budget cap; fail-soft with \`deferred_count\` | How aggressive should the cache TTL be? |

## References

- 📄 ADR proposal: #2417
- 🔒 Triggering incident: #2414 / ruvnet/agentic-flow#169 / GHSA-vcv2-r9jh-99m5
- 🏷️ Today's release: [v3.12.4](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/releases/tag/v3.12.4)
- 📦 Patched dep: [\`agentic-flow@2.0.14\`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/agentic-flow/v/2.0.14)
- Related ADRs: [ADR-150](v3/docs/adr/ADR-150-metaharness-integration-surfaces.md) · [ADR-151](v3/docs/adr/ADR-151-harness-intelligence-layer.md) · [ADR-152](v3/docs/adr/ADR-152-genome-similarity-search.md) · ADR-026 · ADR-097 · ADR-074/075/076/078

title: [Dream Cycle 2026-06-19] swarm: AdaptOrch +22.9% SWE-bench via adaptive topology — hierarchical-default gap identified + ruview-integration,ruvector-integration scan
body:
## Tonight's Rotation

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **SLOT** | 4 |
| **DEEP surface** | swarm |
| **SCAN surfaces** | ruview-integration, ruvector-integration |
| **Session commit** | `9c28fe038cf49ac6db0bb4e04b6158076f03894d` |
| **Date** | 2026-06-19 |
| **ADR** | ADR-162 |

---

## Drift Check

- **Prior dream-cycle issues (last 7):** #2410 (2026-06-18, DEEP=memory), #2401 (2026-06-17, DEEP=intelligence), #2393 (2026-06-16, DEEP=security), #2381 (2026-06-15, DEEP=performance), #2378 (2026-06-14, DEEP=swarm), #2367 (2026-06-13, DEEP=memory), #2362 (2026-06-12, DEEP=intelligence)
- **Swarm repetition check:** #2378 (2026-06-14) was the last swarm deep-dive — 5 days ago, within the 5-slot rotation cadence. No substitution needed.
- **⚠️ needs-merge ACTIVE (24 nights):** All 7 listed dream-cycle issues remain OPEN; zero dream-cycle PRs merged. Recommend human review of oldest open dream PRs for merge consideration.
- **ADR numbering:** Highest committed = ADR-154; in-flight PRs claim ADR-155–161. Tonight uses **ADR-162** to avoid numbering conflict.
- **Self-score of last night's gist (#2410, memory — bi-temporal HNSW gap +10.4pp LongMemEval_S + OPD-Evolver beats ReasoningBank 11.5%):**
  - Grade A/B benchmark (LongMemEval_S A, OPD-Evolver A): ✅ 2 pts
  - ≥4 competitor rows (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK): ✅ 2 pts
  - Specific actions (bi-temporal schema, ADR-161): ✅ 2 pts
  - Witness present: ✅ 2 pts
  - <1500 words: ✅ 1 pt
  - Novel finding (bi-temporal HNSW vs standard HNSW): ✅ 1 pt
  - **Self-score: 10/10**
- **gh CLI:** Not available in environment — gist not published externally. Report stored at `v3/docs/adr/dream-gist-2026-06-19.md` in this PR branch.

---

## Deep Dive Findings — swarm

### SOTA Summary

AdaptOrch (arXiv 2602.16873, Feb 2026, **Grade A**) is the key 2026 result: dynamic topology selection from `[parallel, sequential, hierarchical, hybrid]` based on task dependency graphs beats any single static topology by **+9.8pp on SWE-bench Verified** (52.6% vs 42.8%), **+6.9pp on GPQA Diamond**, **+8.1pp on HotpotQA**. Crucially, the hybrid topology wins **49.7% of tasks** while hierarchical wins only **19%** — meaning Ruflo's hardcoded `hierarchical` default is suboptimal for the majority of production workloads.

Supporting papers:
- **AgentJet** (arXiv 2606.04484, Jun 2026, **Grade B**): Decoupled server/client swarm training, 1.5–10x RL training speedup via timeline merging.
- **SPIN** (arXiv 2606.07557, Jun 2026, **Grade B**): Reduces swarm coordination complexity O(n^m) → O(m·n·χ²) via tensorized policy; zero-shot scales 3→250 agents.

Industry signals:
- LangGraph ~38% production share (Presenc AI Q1 2026); static topology only.
- Independent swarm overhead: +58% tokens; centralized: +285%. Coordination cost requires explicit budgeting.
- Kimi K2.5: vendor claims 100 sub-agents / 1,500 parallel tool calls via PARL (**Grade C** — single vendor claim, unverified).

### Gap vs Current Ruflo

Ruflo has 5 topologies (`hierarchical`, `mesh`, `hierarchical-mesh`, `adaptive`, `ring`) but no **task-dependency-aware selector**. The `topology` parameter is fixed at `swarm_init` time. CLAUDE.md mandates `hierarchical` as the anti-drift default — correct for stability, but leaves +9–23% accuracy on the table for heterogeneous task mixes.

### Recommended Action

**Implement ADR-162** — `topology: "auto"` opt-in for `swarm_init` that calls a lightweight dependency-graph classifier before topology selection. Explicit-topology callers unchanged; `hierarchical` remains the fallback when no graph is supplied (anti-drift guarantee preserved).

---

## Scan Findings — ruview-integration

**Source:** RuView SOTA survey gist (ruvnet/12a235ec17ad5132f1cc4601537c97c7, 28 ADRs mapped, **Grade C** — single internal survey).

**Finding:** `coherence_gate.rs::Recalibrate` currently only flags CSI drift — the MU-SHOT-Fi source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) action is absent. Swarm agents experiencing domain shift (environment CSI drift) hard-restart rather than adapting in-place. Wiring SFDA (MicroLoRA+EWC++ ≤5 gradient steps, witness-logged) would replace hard-restart, preserving learned patterns across environment transitions. This is **implementation-level** — no ADR needed; reuses existing EWC++ infrastructure in `@claude-flow/memory`.

---

## Scan Findings — ruvector-integration

**Source:** CallSphere vector DB benchmark 2026; DataCamp 2026 top vector DBs (**Grade B** — benchmark + vendor data).

**Finding:** Qdrant (30K–80K QPS OSS), Milvus (100K+ QPS at scale). Ruflo ruvector NAPI HNSW measured ~1.9x at N=20k (CLAUDE.md audit). title: USERGUIDE documents a 'Weighted' consensus / Queen-3× voting mode that is unimplemented (and --queen-type is cosmetic)
body:
## Summary

`docs/USERGUIDE.md` documents a **`Weighted` consensus mode that gives the Queen 3× voting power** (and three queen types — Strategic/Tactical/Adaptive — via `--queen-type`). On the shipped CLI (`@claude-flow/cli` 3.12.4) and in the source, **none of the weighted-voting behavior is wired**, and `--queen-type` is cosmetic. Either the feature should be implemented or the USERGUIDE should be corrected to match the shipped equal-vote consensus.

## Evidence

**1. `Weighted` / `Majority` voting modes are unreachable.** USERGUIDE table lists `Majority | Weighted (Queen 3×) | Byzantine`, but the CLI hard-rejects them:

```
$ npx @claude-flow/cli@latest hive-mind init -c weighted
[ERROR] Invalid value for --consensus: weighted. Must be one of: byzantine, raft, gossip, crdt, quorum
```

**2. The engine has no per-voter weight.** `dist/src/mcp-tools/hive-mind-tools.js → calculateRequiredVotes()` is a pure equal-vote **threshold**:

```
bft    → ⌊2n/3⌋+1      raft → ⌊n/2⌋+1
quorum → unanimous=n · supermajority=⌊2n/3⌋+1 · majority=⌊n/2⌋+1
```

No queen multiplier, no weighted branch. The only `weighted` token in the codebase is a **load-balancing** algorithm (`coordination-tools.js`), unrelated to voting.

**3. `--queen-type` is accepted but cosmetic.** It parses and spawns (so it is not an "unknown option"), but `dist/src/commands/hive-mind.js` only **reads and echoes** it (≈ lines 51, 63, 175) — it never feeds voting or coordination, and `--queen-type __bogus__` is accepted silently with no validation. This is the same symptom as #212 ("hive-mind spawn ignores `--queen-type`/`--consensus`"), which is **closed as completed** but appears unfixed for `--queen-type`.

## Suggested resolution

Either:
- **(a)** Implement the documented behavior — add a `weighted` consensus mode with the Queen 3× weight, and make `--queen-type` affect coordination; or
- **(b)** Correct `docs/USERGUIDE.md` to describe the shipped **equal-vote threshold** consensus (`byzantine/raft/gossip/crdt/quorum`) and drop or mark-as-aspirational the `Weighted`/Queen-3× table and the `--queen-type` strategies.

Relates to #212 (queen-type/consensus params ignored) and #653 (mock/stub audit).

**Version:** `@claude-flow/cli` 3.12.4

title: MCP bridge should support streamable HTTP session cleanup DELETE
body:
## Problem

The MCP bridge currently supports `GET /mcp` and `POST /mcp`, but streamable HTTP clients such as Codex/RMCP send `DELETE /mcp` with `Mcp-Session-Id` during session shutdown. Without a cleanup handler, Express returns `Cannot DELETE /mcp`, which surfaces as noisy client-side cleanup failures after otherwise successful MCP calls.

## Proposed fix

A tested two-file patch is available on my fork branch:

- branch: https://github.com/djimit/claude-code-flow/tree/fix/mcp-session-cleanup-forkbase
- commit: https://github.com/djimit/claude-code-flow/commit/b905c09f42439eebc629e8a21b869637c9d60a7f

The patch:

- adds idempotent `DELETE /mcp` and `DELETE /mcp/:group` handlers returning `204 No Content`
- adds `DELETE` and `Mcp-Session-Id` to CORS handling
- emits a stable `Mcp-Session-Id` response header for `/mcp*` requests
- changes `notifications/initialized` handling to `202 Accepted` with an empty body
- adds test-harness coverage for cleanup and notification behavior

I initially opened PR #2424, but closed it because my fork is far behind upstream and GitHub showed unrelated dependency files/conflicts. The commit above is intentionally limited to:

- `ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/index.js`
- `ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/test-harness.js`

## Validation

Against the live bridge built from this patch:

- `node --check ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/index.js`
- `node --check ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/test-harness.js`
- `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- full bridge harness against `http://127.0.0.1:3002`: `56 passed`, `0 failed`, `0 skipped`
- Codex/RMCP smoke after patch: no `DELETE returned HTTP 404` session cleanup noise

## Notes

The cleanup handlers are deliberately idempotent and state-light. They acknowledge client session teardown without changing tool routing or backend execution behavior.

title: MCP stdio tools/list response exceeds macOS 64KB pipe buffer, causing tool registration failure
body:
## Description

When using ruflo MCP server in stdio mode with Claude Code CLI on macOS, the `tools/list` response (65,747 bytes) exceeds the macOS pipe buffer limit (65,536 bytes / 64KB). This causes the response to be truncated, resulting in incomplete JSON that Claude Code cannot parse. Consequently, **none of the 27 MCP tools are registered or usable**.

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, Apple Silicon)
- **ruflo version**: 3.12.3 (also tested with 3.0.0 MCP server)
- **Claude Code**: Latest version
- **Node.js**: v24.14.1
- **Transport**: stdio

## Root Cause

The `tools/list` response is exactly **65,536 bytes** (the macOS pipe buffer limit), causing truncation at the last few bytes. The truncated JSON cannot be parsed.

## Verification

```bash
# Response size: 65747 bytes
# Pipe buffer limit: 65536 bytes  
# Result: JSON truncated, parsing fails at column 65355
```

## Impact

- **All 27 MCP tools are unusable** via stdio transport on macOS
- Claude Code shows ruflo as "Connected" but ToolSearch returns no results
- Direct tool calls return "No such tool available"

## Related Issues

- #1070: MCP stdio mode outputs non-JSON-RPC metadata to stdout (resolved, but response size issue remains)
- #1606: Windows Codex first memory MCP tool call closes stdio transport

## Workaround

Using CLI commands directly (`npx ruflo swarm init`, `npx ruflo agent spawn`, etc.) which bypass the MCP transport.

---
## Updated Environment

- **OS**: macOS 26.5.1 (Build 25F80)
- **Model**: MacBook Pro 16" (MacBookPro18,2)
- **Chip**: Apple M1 Max
- **Memory**: 32 GB

### SOTA Summary (June 2026)

Six high-severity papers published in June 2026 establish a new security baseline for agentic systems, all benchmarked against production-representative tool-using agents:

| Paper | arXiv ID | Key Result | Grade |
|-------|----------|------------|-------|
| SafeClawBench | 2606.18356 | 291/347 (83.9%) sandbox harms pass semantic checks; per-model semantic failure 9–44.2% | **A** |
| Aura Mobile | 2602.10915 | Semantic firewall + privilege isolation: ASR 40% → 4.4%, TSR 75% → 94.3% | **A** |
| FinVault | 2601.07853 | SOTA models reach 50% ASR in financial scenarios despite existing defenses (963 test cases) | **A** |
| FragFuse | 2606.15609 | 86.3% access-control bypass via long-term memory fragmentation across interactions | **B** |
| CmdNeedle | 2606.15549 | 69–98.6% of real-world command denylists bypassable via overlooked command equivalents | **B** |
| Cordon | 2606.17573 | Task-scoped transactional rollback exposes cross-step violations missed by per-call guardrails | **B** |
| OWASP ASI 2026 | owasp.org | Separate Top 10 for Agentic Applications: ASI01–ASI10 distinct from LLM01–LLM10 | **B** |

### Gap vs Current Ruflo

Ruflo's `@claude-flow/security` module provides: `InputValidator` (Zod, HTTP/CLI), `SafeExecutor` (allowlist-gated), `PathValidator`, `ToolOutputGuardrail` (detection-only, per-call), `authorization/propagator` (claims-based), `integrity-verifier` (plugin supply chain).

**Three critical gaps identified:**

1. **No execution-phase sandbox enforcement** — `ToolOutputGuardrail` detects but does not block; SafeClawBench shows 83.9% of sandbox harms survive detection. Aura Mobile (Grade A) demonstrates that adding execution-phase controls cuts ASR to 4.4%.

2. **No cross-interaction memory fragment tracking** — `ToolOutputGuardrail` is stateless per-call. FragFuse (86.3% ASR) exploits this by spreading prohibited content across multiple memory writes, none individually triggering detection.

3. **No task-scoped transactional rollback** — multi-step tool chains have no systematic rollback primitive. Cordon shows this exposes cross-step violations that per-call guardrails miss entirely.

### Recommended Action

**Implement ADR-164: `SandboxEnforcer` with transactional rollback** (additive, opt-in, <300 lines):
- `SandboxTransaction.admit()` gate before every `SafeExecutor.run()` — throw `SandboxViolation` on policy breach, trigger rollback
- `SessionFragmentStore` extension to `ToolOutputGuardrail.scanAndEnforce()` — cross-interaction composite pattern detection, zero async I/O
- `SafeExecutor` startup auditor: equivalence-class checking for CmdNeedle-class allowlist gaps

Target metric: ASR <10% (matching Aura Mobile), down from ~84% current baseline.

Ruflo's 3-tier model routing (ADR-026) addresses model selection but does not optimize scaffold structure per task type.

**Source:** Multi-Agent Orchestration Guide 2026 (codebridge.tech), Swarms v9.0.2 changelog
**Competitive signal:** Swarms framework v9.0.2 (March 2026, 400k users, 10 orchestration architectures); multi-agent research architecture outperforms single-agent Opus by 90.2% in internal evals; Gartner: 40% of enterprise apps include task-specific agents by end 2026.

title: Regression (ADR-130): graph-edge-writer.js sql.js writer corrupts memory.db on agentdb_causal-edge — reintroduces the dual-write ADR-068 removed (#1257)
Unbounded native memory leak: orphaned sql.js MEMFS `dbfile_*` files (~11 MB each) accumulate per database open
body:
**Affected:** `@claude-flow/memory` (sql.js backend path) as shipped in `ruflo` (claude-flow) v3.12.3 / v3.12.4
**Severity:** high — unbounded RSS growth proportional to MCP tool-call / session volume (~36 GB observed in production over 6 weeks; ~160 MB/h under sustained load)
**Type:** resource leak in the JS layer (not pure WASM growth) — fixable in JS

## Summary

Under the `mcp start` long-lived process, the resident memory of the sql.js
backend grows without bound. The growth is **not** in the V8 JS heap
(`heapTotal` stays ~24 MB) — it is in native `external` / `arrayBuffers`
(observed at 1.3 GB / 1.1 GB and climbing on one instance).

A heap-snapshot retainer analysis shows the memory is held by the
**sql.js Emscripten in-memory filesystem (MEMFS)**: it accumulates files named
`dbfile_<random>`, **11 558 912 bytes each** — exactly the size of the
on-disk `memory.db`. One full database image is orphaned in MEMFS **per
`new SQL.Database(buffer)` call that is never matched by `db.close()`**.

## Evidence (V8 heap snapshot of the live `ruflo mcp start` child)

```
process.memoryUsage():  heapTotal 24 MB   external 1286 MB   arrayBuffers 995 MB
```

Top retained objects: **203 × `native:system / JSArrayBufferData` @ 11.0 MB = 2233 MB**
(plus 204 × ~0.1 MB and a 52.8 MB buffer). Retainer path of each 11 MB buffer:

```
JSArrayBufferData (11.0 MB)
  <- ArrayBuffer
  <- Buffer
  <- <MEMFS node>.contents            (Emscripten MEMFS file node)
  <- <MEMFS node>.node
  <- Array  (FS.nodes of the sql.js Emscripten module — a process singleton)
  <- Context (sql.js Emscripten module closure: has WebAssembly.Memory, HEAPF32/HEAP32 views, createNode, lookup, /dev/tty …)
  <- SqlJsRvfBackend.db
  <- ReflexionMemory.vectorBackend
  <- ControllerRegistry.controllers (Map)
```

The MEMFS file names confirm the source — each is a distinct sql.js temp DB file:

```
dbfile_3079493243  (11.0 MB)
dbfile_3056784716  (11.0 MB)
dbfile_1155588019  (11.0 MB)
… 203 total, all unique, all = sizeof(memory.db) = 11 558 912 bytes
```

## Root cause

sql.js's `Database` constructor writes its input bytes into a MEMFS file via
`FS.createDataFile("/", "dbfile_" + random, data, …)`. That file is only
removed by `Database.prototype.close()` (which calls `FS.unlink`). Because the
sql.js Emscripten module is a **process-wide singleton**, the MEMFS file
outlives the JS `Database` wrapper: **garbage-collecting the wrapper does NOT
reclaim the MEMFS storage** — only an explicit `close()` does.

In `@claude-flow/memory/dist/database-provider.js`, `createDatabase()`:

- has **no instance cache / singleton** — every call builds a fresh backend;
- for the `sql.js` provider, `SqlJsBackend.initialize()`
  (`@claude-flow/memory/dist/sqljs-backend.js:68`) runs
  `this.db = new this.SQL.Database(new Uint8Array(buffer))` where `buffer` is
  the full ~11 MB `memory.db`;
- the returned backend is used and then dropped by its caller **without
  `backend.close()`** (which would call `db.close()` → `FS.unlink`).

So each `createDatabase()` for an existing DB orphans one 11 MB `dbfile_*` in
MEMFS. With `createDatabase()` invoked per operation/session, native memory
grows ~11 MB per open, unbounded.

(Note: the probe `testSqlJs()` correctly closes its test DB, so the dominant
leak is specifically the **returned backend** not being closed, and/or
`createDatabase()` being re-invoked instead of reusing a cached instance.)

## Reproduction

1. Run `ruflo mcp start` with a non-trivial `memory.db` (e.g. ~11 MB).
2. Drive MCP memory tools (or anything that triggers `createDatabase()` for the
   sql.js provider) repeatedly.
3. Watch `process.memoryUsage().arrayBuffers` / RSS climb by ~one `memory.db`
   size per open, while `heapTotal` stays flat.
4. A heap snapshot shows N × `dbfile_<random>` MEMFS files of `sizeof(memory.db)`.

## Proposed fix (any one, in order of preference)

1. **Cache/reuse a single backend instance** for the process lifetime instead
   of calling `createDatabase()` per operation — the sql.js DB should be opened
   once and kept open.
2. **Guarantee `close()`** on every backend obtained from `createDatabase()`
   (try/finally at the call site), so sql.js `FS.unlink`s the `dbfile_*`.
3. **Defensive cleanup**: after closing, or periodically, unlink stale
   `/dbfile_*` entries from the sql.js MEMFS.

## Containment (consumer side, already deployed in ruflo-hub)

`server.mjs` runs an RSS watchdog that gracefully respawns the `ruflo mcp start`
child when its RSS crosses a threshold (idle-gated). This bounds the symptom but
does not address the root cause above.

title: [verification] MEDIUM: doctor reports MetaHarness ADR-150 integration failure — plugins/ruflo-metaharness/ not found
body:
## Summary

The `npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha doctor` command reports a `✗` (fail) status for the MetaHarness ADR-150 integration check. The `plugins/ruflo-metaharness/` directory is not found at any of the expected locations.

## Impact

Users who run `ruflo doctor` (the documented health check) see a failure entry. Any commands documented in CLAUDE.md under `MetaHarness Integration (ADR-150)` — including `ruflo metaharness score`, `ruflo metaharness oia-audit`, `ruflo eject`, and the MCP tools `mcp__claude-flow__metaharness_*` — will fail for users who do not have the plugin pre-installed.

## Expected

```
✓  MetaHarness (ADR-150): <version> installed and loadable
```
or at minimum a warning (⚠) for an optional component, not a ✗ failure.

## Actual

```
✗ MetaHarness integration (ADR-150): plugins/ruflo-metaharness/ not found in expected locations
```

Doctor summary: `9 passed, 9 warnings, 1 failed`

Note: doctor exits with code 0 despite the ✗ failure, which may mask the issue in scripts.

## Command Output

```
npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha doctor 2>&1 | tail -20

...
✗ MetaHarness integration (ADR-150): plugins/ruflo-metaharness/ not found in expected locations

──────────────────────────────────────────────────

Summary: 9 passed, 9 warnings, 1 failed

Run with --fix to see 9 suggested commands (does not auto-apply)

Some checks failed. Please address the issues above.
```

## Recommended Fix

Either:
1. Ship `plugins/ruflo-metaharness/` as part of the published package, **or**
2. Downgrade the doctor check from ✗ to ⚠ since MetaHarness is documented as an optional dependency (`optionalDependencies` per ADR-150 architecture rules)

The ADR-150 architectural constraint states "Ruflo remains operational if every MetaHarness package is removed" — the current ✗ failure contradicts this by making the doctor report an error for a missing optional component.

body:
## Summary
- Implements [ADR-153](v3/docs/adr/ADR-153-metaharness-darwin-mode-integration.md) — Darwin Mode is the WRITE layer that closes the loop ADR-150's READ layer opens (score/genome describe; evolve changes)
- Three new surfaces: \`harness-evolve\`, \`harness-security-bench\`, \`harness-bench\` — all honoring the four ADR-150 architectural constraints (removable / optional / graceful / CI-gate)
- Bumps \`metaharness\` umbrella from \`~0.1.11\` → \`~0.2.6\` and adds \`@metaharness/darwin@~0.3.1\` to optionalDependencies (cli + ruflo wrapper)

## Why this matters: connection to ADR-155
\`harness-security-bench\` wraps the upstream's own \"Darwin Shield\" (their ADR-155). This is the closest reference implementation for **our** [ADR-155 nightly self-learning security harness](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/pull/2417) (issue #2418). Running it periodically gives Loop A its empirical reward-signal floor: if Darwin Shield's champion reaches TPR=1 / FPR=0 on the 10-vuln/9-decoy seeded corpus, our loop gradient is sound.

## Surface added
| Script | Skill | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| \`scripts/evolve.mjs\` | \`harness-evolve\` | \`metaharness_evolve\` |
| \`scripts/security-bench.mjs\` | \`harness-security-bench\` | \`metaharness_security_bench\` |
| \`scripts/bench.mjs\` | \`harness-bench\` | \`metaharness_bench\` |
| \`scripts/_darwin.mjs\` | _(shared helper)_ | _(internal)_ |

## Safety
- \`evolve\` REQUIRES \`--confirm\`; without it, returns a dry-run plan (mirrors \`mint.mjs\`)
- Ruflo caps: \`--generations\` 1..50, \`--children\` 1..20, \`--concurrency\` 1..8, \`--population\` 1..20, \`--cycles\` 1..100
- Upstream exit code 99 (\"safety-disqualified\") propagates **verbatim** — not remapped — so CI can distinguish evolution failure from a safety-tripping mutation
- All 3 scripts emit \`{degraded: true, reason: 'metaharness-darwin-not-available'}\` and exit 0 when optional dep absent

## Test plan
- [x] \`node --check\` on all 4 new \`.mjs\` files
- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean on \`v3/@claude-flow/cli\`
- [x] \`scripts/test-graceful-degradation.mjs\` extended with the 3 new scripts; **16/16 assertions pass** (8 skills × 2 contracts each)
- [x] \`evolve --repo .\` (no --confirm) emits the expected dry-run plan JSON
- [x] \`bench --op verify --suite /dev/null\` reaches the upstream subprocess
- [ ] After merge: \`npm install @metaharness/darwin\` in a test project and verify \`metaharness_evolve\` MCP tool round-trips a real evolution

## ADR-150 four-constraint compliance
| # | Constraint | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Removable | \`npm ls --without @metaharness/*\` still produces a working CLI; the 3 new tools degrade with exit 0 |
| 2 | Optional in \`package.json\` | Added to \`optionalDependencies\` in both cli + ruflo wrapper, never \`dependencies\` |
| 3 | Graceful degradation | \`_darwin.mjs\` catches MODULE_NOT_FOUND/404/network failures; emits \`{degraded:true}\`; exit 0 |
| 4 | CI-absent-path coverage | \`test-graceful-degradation.mjs\` extended with all 3 darwin scripts |

title: fix(doctor): #2437 — MetaHarness plugin locator (npx/global install) + severity (fail→warn)
body:
## Summary
- Closes #2437
- Doctor's MetaHarness check now finds the plugin under \`npx\` cache and \`npm install -g\` paths (was only finding monorepo-dev path)
- Severity downgraded from \`fail (✗)\` to \`warn (⚠)\` when plugin is genuinely absent — matches the optional-dependency posture per ADR-150 constraint #2 and the runtime path's \`{degraded: true, exit 0}\` behavior
- Adds the v3.13.0 ADR-153 Darwin Mode surfaces to the required-files list (gates against silent deletion)

## Root cause

Pre-fix locator walked up only from \`process.cwd()\` + checked one hard-coded \`<cwd>/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/...\` candidate. That missed:
- \`npx @claude-flow/cli@<tag>\` — resolves under \`~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/...\`

Walk up from this module's own URL via \`import.meta.url\` — the plugins dir is always a sibling of the package root regardless of where the package was installed. Falls back to the prior cwd-walk + explicit-node_modules candidates for monorepo dev.
