title: fix(doctor): wire real memory-DB integrity checks into the default doctor run
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2737.

`@claude-flow/cli`'s `doctor` command has real memory-database integrity checks (`checkMemoryIntegrity`, `checkMemoryContent`, `checkMemoryEmbeddingCoverage` — added for #2677), but they were registered **only** under `componentMap['memory']` (`--component memory`), never in the `allChecks` array a bare `doctor` or `doctor --fix` actually runs. The default run's only memory probe was `checkMemoryDatabase` — plain `existsSync` + `statSync` — which reports `pass` for any file that exists and can be stat'd, corrupt or not. A genuinely corrupt `.swarm/memory.db` could sail through a bare `doctor` run reporting "All checks passed! System is healthy."

## The wiring gap

- `allChecks` (default run): only `checkMemoryDatabase` (existence/size only).
- `componentMap['memory']` (`--component memory` only): the full #2677 trio.

## Three-part fix

1. **New default-run check** — `checkMemoryStructuralIntegrity`, added to `allChecks`. Uses native `better-sqlite3` (WAL-aware — SQLite resolves the sibling `-wal` file itself; the existing `sql.js` checks are WAL-blind because they only `readFileSync()` the main db image) and runs `PRAGMA quick_check` (bounded — per sqlite.org it skips UNIQUE/index-vs-table cross-checks that `integrity_check` does, cheap enough to run unconditionally). Explicitly labeled "structural-only" in both the row name and every message so it's never confused with the deeper `--component memory` probe. `checkMemoryDatabase`'s reported row is relabeled **"Memory Database Presence"** to be honest about its existence-only scope — behavior unchanged, it stays in `allChecks` too.

2. **Strengthened `checkMemoryIntegrity`** (deep path, `--component memory` only — the full #2677 trio stays there, unchanged in registration). Now prefers native `better-sqlite3` `PRAGMA integrity_check` (adds the index↔table + UNIQUE verification `quick_check` skips, and is WAL-aware) when `better-sqlite3` is installed, falling back to the original `sql.js` probe — now explicitly labeled **"main-image-only"** (WAL-blind) — when it's not.

3. **Definitive corruption now fails, not warns** — in both checks, a `"file is not a database"` / `"malformed"` result now maps to `fail`, WITH an encryption-at-rest carve-out: before concluding "malformed," both checks sniff the file for the product's RFE1 magic bytes (reusing `isEncryptedBlob()` from `encryption/vault.ts` — the exact same detector `checkEncryptionAtRest` uses), so a legitimately encrypted-at-rest DB is never misclassified as corrupt.

`better-sqlite3` is added to `@claude-flow/cli`'s `optionalDependencies` (matching the existing pattern in `@claude-flow/memory` and `@claude-flow/hooks`), with an ambient module declaration in `optional-modules.d.ts`. Every code path that touches it degrades gracefully (sql.js fallback, or a `warn`) on `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — never a silent pass.

## What I deliberately did not touch

- `agentdb_health` / `memory_stats` — out of scope per the issue, tracked separately.
- `doctor --fix`'s behavior beyond inheriting the new default check (it already runs `allChecks`).
- The `ruflo-doctor` skill/plugin docs.
- `checkMemoryContent` / `checkMemoryEmbeddingCoverage` — kept exactly as-is; `checkMemoryIntegrity` failing hard is enough to prevent a false "all healthy" (checks are ordered so the earliest chain-break is the first red the user sees).

## Test plan

- [x] New `__tests__/doctor-2737-memory-structural.test.ts` (7 cases), driven through `doctorCommand.action()` (the real entry point, not the check functions in isolation):
  - Healthy DB (built with real `better-sqlite3`) → default `doctor` run passes, including the new check.
  - Malformed DB (garbage bytes) → new check reports `fail`; overall run reports `failed > 0`, `success: false`, `exitCode: 1` — never the "all healthy" false negative.
  - A real RFE1-encrypted blob (built with the product's own `encryptBuffer`) is **not** misclassified as corrupt.
  - `--component memory` still runs the full, unchanged 4-check trio; the new default-run check is deliberately absent from it.
  - `checkMemoryIntegrity` directly: fails on malformed+unencrypted, does not hard-fail on legitimately-encrypted.
- [x] Full existing `doctor-*.test.ts` suite (19 tests total) still passes — no regressions.
- [x] Manual repro: `node bin/cli.js doctor` against a scratch dir with a garbage `.swarm/memory.db`:
  ```
  ✓ Memory Database Presence: ...\.swarm\memory.db (0.00 MB) — existence/size only, not a health check (see Memory Structural Integrity)
  ✗ Memory Structural Integrity (quick_check): ...\.swarm\memory.db — quick_check probe threw: file is not a database (unencrypted) [structural-only]
  Summary: 13 passed, 11 warnings, 1 failed
  Some checks failed. Please address the issues above.
  ```
  Process exit code: **1** (previously: silent pass via `checkMemoryDatabase`, exit 0, "All checks passed! System is healthy.").
  Re-verified against a valid DB (exit 0, `quick_check: ok`) and via `--component memory` (full trio, native `integrity_check` path confirmed with `[native, WAL-aware]` in the message).

Note: while manually verifying `--component memory` end-to-end via the compiled CLI binary, I hit a libuv assertion crash (`Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING)`, `src\win\async.c`) on process exit in this sandbox. I confirmed it reproduces **identically on unmodified `main`** (stashed my diff, rebuilt, same crash) — it's a pre-existing Windows/Node-24/native-module environment issue in this sandbox, not something this change introduces, and unrelated to the actual check logic (which completes and prints correct results before the crash occurs during teardown).

title: fix(memory): refuse unsafe sql.js whole-image writes under a live native WAL writer
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2735 (scoped — see below for what's explicitly not included).

Every memory CRUD op (`storeEntry`/`getEntry`/`deleteEntry` in `memory-initializer.ts`) falls back to a raw sql.js path when the native better-sqlite3 bridge is unavailable: read the whole database image, mutate an in-memory copy, `export()` it, and rename the result over the live database path. That rename doesn't participate in SQLite's WAL/locking protocol at all — if a native WAL connection is attached (daemon, an MCP server, another CLI invocation), the rename strands every open native connection on a deleted inode and can leave the surviving `-wal` (paired to the new image by filename only, per SQLite's own documented file format) applied to unrelated data, corrupting the database or silently losing an already-acknowledged write.

## Fix

Before performing the whole-image write, refuse if `-wal`/`-shm` sidecar files exist next to the database. A native WAL connection keeps its sidecars on disk for its entire lifetime, so their presence is strong evidence of a live native holder, and their absence means the image is safe for sql.js to read-modify-write. Refusal returns a typed `success: false` + descriptive error — the CLI layer was already correctly wired to turn that into a nonzero exit code (verified by inspection, no change needed).

Also fixed the completely silent bridge → sql.js demotion in `memory-bridge.ts`: both the process-wide cached failure and the four bridge functions with a corresponding unsafe fallback now log once per distinct failure reason to stderr (never stdout) — previously a demotion left zero diagnostic trail.

## Verified already fixed, no change needed

The issue's "closely coupled destroy-path" concern (`ensureInitialized` → a malformed database silently replaced by an empty one) does **not** reproduce against current `main`. `initializeMemoryDatabase` already has an idempotent-reinit guard (#1791.6), and `repairVectorIndexes`/`recoverMemoryDatabase` already implement a real backup-verify-swap recovery flow with a native `quick_check` gate and a busy-writer backoff — already close to the "cooperative-drain recovery" the issue proposed.

## Explicitly NOT done (scope decision)

This is a scoped subset of the fuller design discussed in the issue, not the complete proposal:
- The process-holder-scanning design (`/proc/<pid>/fd` on Linux, `lsof` elsewhere, to close the narrow assess-then-write race a sidecar-only check can't) is a larger, platform-specific surface deserving its own review — tracked as a follow-up.
- `ensureSchemaColumns`'/`applyTemporalDecay`'s own independent whole-image write sites remain unguarded (lower frequency/severity per the issue's own analysis).
- The "native WAL mutation as the primary path for every mutator" rewrite (replacing all 7 `db.export()` sites) is out of scope entirely — a multi-day architectural change.

## Verification

- 8/8 new regression tests pass (`storeEntry`/`getEntry`/`deleteEntry` each: refuses with `-wal` present, refuses with `-shm` present, proceeds normally with neither, plus a "refused store never touches the file" assertion)
- Clean `tsc --noEmit`
- Confirmed the `memory-search-recall-2558`/`commands.test.ts` full-suite failures seen locally are pre-existing (identical on unmodified `main` via `git stash` comparison) and non-deterministic (different failures each full-suite run) — unrelated to this change; all affected suites pass cleanly in isolation

title: bug(metaharness): oia-audit wrappers swallow security findings on non-zero exit (threat-model exit 2, mcp-scan JSON-as-text parse)
body:
## Symptom

`ruflo metaharness oia-audit` reports `composite.worst = clean` and `introduced = 0` even when the repo has a real HIGH-severity MCP security regression (`.harness/mcp-policy.json` with `allowShell:true`, `defaultDeny:false`, wildcard tool permissions). Consequently `drift-from-history --alert-on-new-severity medium` cannot catch security regressions — the findings never reach the composite.

## Root cause (two wrapper bugs)

### 1. `threat-model.mjs` discards JSON on exit 2

The upstream `harness threat-model` exits with code **2** for a HIGH verdict (`buildThreatModel` in `metaharness/dist/threat-model.js`: `exitCode = 2` for `shellAccess || policyDefaultDeny===false || secretsReachable`). The ruflo wrapper (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/plugins/ruflo-metaharness/scripts/threat-model.mjs`) does:

```js
if (r.exitCode !== 0 && r.exitCode !== 1) {
  console.error(`threat-model: harness exited ${r.exitCode}`);
  process.exit(2);   // ← swallows the JSON that IS on stdout
}
```

Exit 2 falls through; the JSON (which upstream DID print before exiting) is discarded and the oia-audit composite sees `json: null` → no findings.

### 2. `mcp-scan.mjs` parses JSON as text

`runHarness` appends `--json` automatically, so upstream `harness mcp-scan` emits structured JSON. But the wrapper (`mcp-scan.mjs`) feeds stdout into `parseMcpScanText()`, which expects the **text** table format (`[HIGH] title ...`). The parser mis-parses the JSON blob as a single finding and the real findings list is stuffed into `rawStdout`. The `--fail-on` alert then reads `offendingCount: 0` even when HIGH findings exist.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. seed a dangerous policy
echo '{"defaultDeny":false,"allowShell":true,"allowNetwork":true}' > .harness/mcp-policy.json
echo '{"permissions":{"allow":["mcp__*"],"deny":[]},"mcpServers":{"x":{"command":"bash"}}}' > .claude/settings.json

# 2. ruflo wrapper — LOSES findings
npx ruflo@latest metaharness oia-audit --format json | jq '.composite, .components.mcpScan.json.mcpEnabled'
# → composite.worst = clean (WRONG), mcpScan.json.mcpEnabled = null (WRONG)

# 3. upstream direct — CORRECT
npx -p metaharness harness mcp-scan . --json | jq '.mcpEnabled, .worst, .findings'
# → mcpEnabled: true, worst: high, findings: [no-default-deny, allow-shell, wildcard-tool-perm, ...]
```

## Suggested fix

1. **threat-model.mjs**: drop the `exitCode !== 0 && exitCode !== 1` early-exit; always emit `r.json` when present; derive the alert from `payload.worst` / `payload.verdict` (which carry the real exitCode) instead of the process exit code. Exit 2 from upstream is a valid HIGH verdict, not a crash.
2. **mcp-scan.mjs**: when `runHarness` used `--json`, use `r.json` directly instead of `parseMcpScanText(r.stdout)`. Keep the text parser as a fallback only for `--format table`.

## Impact

The ADR-150 iter-78 `--alert-on-new-severity` orthogonal gate (catch the "security regression that didn't move the genome much" case) is effectively dead for threat-model/mcp-scan findings, because those findings never reach the oia-audit composite record that drift detection compares. Structural drift still works, but security-posture regressions (the exact scenario the gate was built for) slip through silently.

Verified on `ruflo-federation 0.2.0` / `@claude-flow/cli` metaharness wrappers. A local shim that calls upstream `harness` directly and captures JSON regardless of exit code restores the findings (clean → regressed produces `worst: worsened (info → high)`, 13 introduced findings, `ALERT: True`).

title: @claude-flow/codex built-in skills reference missing docs and incorrect script paths
body:
## Confirmed problem

Against the published `@claude-flow/codex@3.0.1` artifact, built-in skill generation still emits local references that cannot resolve from the installed skill. `generateBuiltInSkill()` returns scripts but an empty `references` map; rendered SPARC, swarm, and security guidance names documentation that is not returned or packaged, and rendered `.agents/scripts/...` paths do not match the per-skill script layout. Direct generator output and an unpacked npm tarball reproduce the mismatch.

## Required change

- Define each built-in skill once, including its `SKILL.md`, scripts, and supplementary references, and generate the repository and npm representations from that canonical definition.
- Keep every helper/document link skill-relative (`scripts/...` or `references/...`) and constrained to the installed skill directory.
- Ship every referenced file, or remove the reference until a payload exists.
- Do not treat source-tree presence, frontmatter validity, or an unsupported dispatch manifest as proof that the installed skill is complete.

## Acceptance

- A direct generator test resolves every local path in every generated `SKILL.md` inside that generated skill directory and fails when one payload is omitted.
- A fresh initialization and an unpacked `npm pack` contain the same complete built-in skill trees.
- No generated path escapes the skill root, and no built-in skill references a missing script, helper, document, or reference file.

title: @claude-flow/codex: dual run aborts with "Database not initialized" — memory bootstrap uses npx ruflo@alpha with an inconsistent DB path
body:
## Summary

`claude-flow-codex dual run` (package `@claude-flow/codex@3.0.0-alpha.12`, bin `claude-flow-codex`) reliably aborts the whole swarm with:

```
[ERROR] Database not initialized. Run: claude-flow memory init
```

even though `DualModeOrchestrator.initializeSharedMemory` runs a `memory init --force` immediately beforehand.

## Root cause

`dist/dual-mode/orchestrator.js` bootstraps and uses shared memory via **`npx ruflo@alpha`**:

```js
// initializeSharedMemory()
await this.runCommand('npx', ['ruflo@alpha', 'memory', 'init', '--force'], projectPath);
await this.runCommand('npx', ['ruflo@alpha', 'memory', 'store', '--key', 'task-context', '--value', taskContext, '--namespace', sharedNamespace]);
// buildCollaborativePrompt() also instructs each worker to run:
//   npx ruflo@alpha memory search/store --namespace <ns>
```

`npx ruflo@alpha` resolves/installs a version (observed: `ruflo@3.32.9`, "npm warn ... will be installed") whose **default memory DB path differs from where the subsequent `memory store` / worker commands read it**, so the store step reports the DB as uninitialized and `runCollaboration` rejects. It also re-downloads ruflo on every fresh project (ignores an already-installed `ruflo`).

## Repro

```bash
# config module exporting `workers` (see note below)
claude-flow-codex dual run --config file:///abs/dual-run.config.mjs --task "…" --max-concurrent 1
# → prints the worker pipeline, then: [ERROR] Database not initialized
```

## Verified workaround

Pinning a single DB path for the whole run makes `init`, `store`, and the workers share one database:

```bash
CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH="$PWD/.claude-flow/dual-mem.db" claude-flow-codex dual run --config … --task …
# → "✓ Shared memory initialized: collaboration"  and workers start
```

## Suggested fix (any one)

- Use the **locally installed** ruflo (resolve `ruflo` on PATH / `require.resolve`) instead of `npx ruflo@alpha`, so the CLI version and DB path are consistent with the host environment; or
- Pin/propagate one `CLAUDE_FLOW_DB_PATH` across the init + store + worker invocations; or
- Ensure `memory init` and `memory store` resolve the same DB path within a single run.

## Minor secondary note

`dual run --config <path>` loads the config with `await import(options.config)` and reads `configData.workers` (`dist/dual-mode/cli.js`). This means `--config` must be an **importable ESM module** (a `.mjs` exporting `workers`), referenced by an absolute `file://` URL — a plain `.json` path fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (relative) or a missing import-assertion error (absolute). Worth documenting or supporting JSON explicitly.

Environment: macOS, node 26.4.0, `@claude-flow/codex@3.0.0-alpha.12`, installed `ruflo` present on PATH. Found while building Claude+Codex per-activity routing in [pacphi/agentic-kit#39](https://github.com/pacphi/agentic-kit/pull/39).

title: [BUG] Windows: browser-session tools fail with ENOENT — execFile('npx', ...) can't launch npx.cmd without a shell
Bug: Codex MCP generator registers management CLI instead of stdio server
body:
## Summary

The current Codex MCP configuration generator registers:

```text
npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start
```

as a `stdio` MCP server. On Ruflo 3.32.9, this starts the MCP **management command**, leaves a process running, but does not answer an MCP `initialize` request on its stdin/stdout. Codex therefore sees the server as configured and enabled but exposes no Ruflo tools.

The dedicated `@claude-flow/cli/bin/mcp-server.js` entry point answers `initialize` immediately and keeps stdout clean, so the generated Codex configuration appears to target the wrong executable.

This affects all consumers using the configuration emitted by `@claude-flow/codex`, not only one local installation.

## Upstream source

The current generator constructs the failing command here:

https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/@claude-flow/codex/src/mcp-config.ts

```ts
const args = ['-y', RUFLO_MCP_PACKAGE, 'mcp', 'start'];
```

On Windows it emits the equivalent of:

```toml
[mcp_servers.ruflo]
command = "cmd"
args = ["/c", "npx", "-y", "ruflo@latest", "mcp", "start"]
enabled = true
startup_timeout_sec = 120
```

## Environment

- Ruflo: `3.32.9`
- Node: `v24.15.0`
- OS: Windows
- Client: Codex Desktop `26.721.31836`
- Transport: stdio

## Reproduction

### 1. Probe the generated command

Spawn the generated command as a stdio child process and write a newline-delimited MCP initialization request:

```js
const { spawn } = require('child_process');

const p = spawn('cmd.exe', [
  '/d', '/s', '/c',
  'npx -y ruflo@3.32.9 mcp start'
], {
  stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  windowsHide: true,
});

let stdout = '';
let stderr = '';
p.stdout.on('data', d => stdout += d);
p.stderr.on('data', d => stderr += d);

p.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({
  jsonrpc: '2.0',
  id: 1,
  method: 'initialize',
  params: {
    protocolVersion: '2024-11-05',
    capabilities: {},
    clientInfo: { name: 'probe', version: '1.0.0' },
  },
}) + '\n');

setTimeout(() => {
  console.log({ stdout, stderr, exited: p.exitCode !== null });
  p.kill();
}, 15000);
```

Observed after 15 seconds:

```json
{
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "",
  "exited": false
}
```

The process is alive but never completes the MCP handshake. A `Content-Length` framed request produces the same result.

### 2. Probe the dedicated MCP entry point

Launching the installed `@claude-flow/cli/bin/mcp-server.js` directly and sending the same newline-delimited request returns immediately:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","serverInfo":{"name":"ruflo","version":"3.0.0"},"capabilities":{"tools":{"listChanged":true},"resources":{"subscribe":true,"listChanged":true}}}}
```

Its startup diagnostics are written to stderr, and stdout contains only JSON-RPC.

## Additional regression related to #2253

Issue #2253 was closed as fixed in 3.10.33 after moving embedder progress output away from stdout. In 3.32.9, invoking the main `ruflo` binary in stdio auto-detection mode still emits this before the JSON-RPC response:

```text
  Disk cache hit: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{...}}
```

The dedicated `mcp-server.js` entry point does **not** emit that stdout preamble. Registering the dedicated binary would therefore avoid both the management-command mismatch and this strict-client framing regression.

Related: #2253

## Expected behavior

- Codex configuration generated by `@claude-flow/codex` launches a process that immediately speaks MCP over stdio.
- Codex exposes Ruflo tools after restart.
- stdout contains only MCP JSON-RPC messages.
- `ruflo mcp status` reflects the Codex-owned stdio child accurately, or the distinction between the management command and direct stdio entry point is clearly documented.

## Suggested fix

1. Change `getRufloMcpServerConfig()` to invoke the dedicated `claude-flow-mcp` binary from `@claude-flow/cli`, rather than `ruflo mcp start`.
2. Update generated Codex configuration, migration logic, README examples, and validators consistently.
3. Add an end-to-end test that:
   - generates the Codex command;
   - spawns it as a child process;
   - sends `initialize` through stdin;
   - asserts the first stdout line is valid JSON-RPC;
   - asserts initialization completes within the configured timeout;
   - calls `tools/list` and verifies at least one Ruflo tool is returned.
4. Add a regression test that rejects any non-JSON stdout before or during the MCP handshake.

## Impact

Users can have Ruflo installed, enabled, and apparently running while Codex silently exposes no Ruflo namespace. CLI fallback through `ruflo mcp exec` still works, which makes the failure especially confusing: Ruflo itself appears healthy, but native Codex tool discovery never succeeds.

title: memory: store to an existing key dead-ends (constraint error demotes bridge into misleading #2735 guard); delete→store blocked by soft-delete; CLI --upsert default (#2594) never applies
body:
## Summary

On 3.32.9, storing to an existing `(namespace, key)` without upsert can never succeed and returns a misleading error, and the natural `delete → store` recovery also dead-ends. Four coupled defects (file:line refs from the published 3.32.9 dist):

1. **Demotion on a data-level error.** `bridgeStoreEntry`'s catch (`dist/src/memory/memory-bridge.js:763`) treats `UNIQUE constraint failed: memory_entries.namespace, memory_entries.key` — the *expected* outcome of a strict insert on an existing key — as a bridge failure: it logs a demotion and returns `null`, so `storeEntry` (`dist/src/memory/memory-initializer.js:2307`) falls back to the sql.js whole-image path, whose #2735 sidecar guard then (correctly) refuses — usually because of the process's **own** native sidecars. The user is told `memory database has an active native WAL connection … restore the native better-sqlite3 bridge` when the bridge is healthy and the real condition is "duplicate key".

2. **`delete → store` dead-end.** `bridgeDeleteEntry` soft-deletes (`status='deleted'`, `memory-bridge.js:1070-1074`), so the `UNIQUE(namespace, key)` slot stays occupied; the subsequent strict INSERT hits the same constraint → defect 1 → same misleading error. #2594's own comment acknowledges this trap.

3. **CLI `--upsert` default (#2594) is inert.** Declared `default: true` (`dist/src/commands/memory.js:67-75`) but the flag framework does not materialize declared defaults: `ctx.flags.upsert` is `undefined` unless passed explicitly, which reaches the bridge as falsy → strict INSERT → defects 1+2. Explicit `--upsert` works, proving the default never applies. (The MCP `memory_store` tool's `upsert` defaults to false by schema, so the agent-facing default path can never update a key either.)

4. **No checkpoint after delete.** `bridgeStoreEntry` runs `wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` after every store (#2558, `memory-bridge.js:740-745`) but `bridgeDeleteEntry` does not — deletes stay WAL-only until some unrelated store checkpoints. WAL-blind readers (the sql.js fallback, the statusline) keep serving the deleted row, and if the process exits before another checkpoint the divergence persists on disk. On a live multi-worktree installation we found rows `active` in the main image but `deleted` in the WAL, and rows that exist **only** in orphaned `-wal` files (invisible to every image reader).

Aggravating factor: neither `mcp start` nor one-shot CLI processes close the registry connection on exit, so `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars persist after clean exits. The #2735 guard keys on sidecar existence, so on any bridge-touched DB the sql.js fallback write path is permanently refused — every demotion is a guaranteed dead end.

## Environment

ruflo 3.32.9 / @claude-flow/cli 3.32.9 (npm), Node v22.20.0, macOS (darwin 25). better-sqlite3 loads and works — the bridge is active and healthy throughout.

## Reproduction (CLI, fresh directory)

```bash
ruflo memory init
ruflo memory store -k trap --namespace repro -v v1     # OK
ruflo memory store -k trap --namespace repro -v v2     # FAILS (should upsert per #2594):
#   [memory-bridge] demoted to sql.js fallback in bridgeStoreEntry: UNIQUE constraint failed: memory_entries.namespace, memory_entries.key
#   [ERROR] memory database has an active native WAL connection (found -wal/-shm sidecar files) — refusing an unsafe sql.js whole-image write. ...
ruflo memory delete -k trap --namespace repro          # OK (soft delete)
ruflo memory store -k trap --namespace repro -v v3     # FAILS again — soft-deleted row still holds the UNIQUE slot
ruflo memory store -k trap --namespace repro -v v3 --upsert   # OK — explicit flag works, so the declared default never applied
```

The same sequence through the MCP `memory_store` tool (upsert omitted) reproduces identically, including inside a single `mcp start` server whose own startup connection provides the sidecars that the guard then trips on.

## Suggested fixes (running these as a local patch, all verified)

- In `bridgeStoreEntry`'s catch, classify `UNIQUE constraint failed` as a clean `{ success: false, error: "key exists — pass upsert" }` result — never a demotion. Data-level errors are not bridge failures.
- Make the strict-insert SQL resurrect soft-deleted rows and no-op on active conflicts: `INSERT … ON CONFLICT(namespace, key) DO UPDATE SET …, status='active' WHERE memory_entries.status='deleted'`, then surface `changes === 0` as the duplicate-key error. `delete → store` works again while strict semantics against ACTIVE rows are preserved.
- Mirror the #2558 PASSIVE checkpoint in `bridgeDeleteEntry`.
- Materialize declared flag defaults in the CLI framework (or locally `const upsert = ctx.flags.upsert !== false;` in `commands/memory.js`), and consider defaulting the MCP tool's `upsert` to true for parity with #2594's intent.

title: statusline security segment: STALE/IN_PROGRESS unreachable (scan freshness never checked) + uncapped cache can freeze 'scan pending'
body:
## Summary

The Claude Code statusline's security segment has two defects in `@claude-flow/cli` 3.32.9:

1. **`STALE` and `IN_PROGRESS` are unreachable states** — the renderer implements them, but the producer (`getSecurityStatus`) can only ever emit `PENDING` / `CLEAN` / `ISSUES`. Scan freshness (`scannedAt`) is captured but never checked, so once a single scan JSON exists the statusline reports 🛡 ✓ **forever**, no matter how old the scan is.
2. **Uncapped stale-while-revalidate can freeze the pill at "scan pending"** — when CLI delegation fails, the statusline helper serves the cached state indefinitely, so the pill does not move even after a scan has written a `CLEAN` result to disk.

Both were found while investigating a user report of the statusline being "stuck in security scan / scan pending".

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | macOS 26.5.2 (arm64) |
| Node | v26.4.0 |
| ruflo | 3.32.9 (npm, global) |
| @claude-flow/cli | 3.32.9 (bundled) |
| Integration | Claude Code statusline via the generated `.claude/helpers/statusline.cjs` |

## What I was trying to do

The Claude Code statusline showed `🛡 scan pending` plus the insight row `🛡 Security scan pending — Run ruflo security scan --depth full` in a project, and the user reported this state sometimes appears "stuck". I traced the full state pipeline through the shipped dist to determine whether the state can actually clear, and what guarantees it makes.

## Where the pipeline stands (shipped dist, exact locations)

The happy path **works** — verified empirically:

- **Writer** — `dist/src/commands/security.js:227-245`: `ruflo security scan` persists `scan-<type>-<depth>.json` into `<target>/.claude/security-scans/`, with a comment saying this exists precisely so the statusline reflects real scan state.
- **Producer** — `dist/src/funnel/local-signals.js` `getSecurityStatus()`: reads `<cwd>/.claude/security-scans/*.json` (newest by mtime). Line 15: missing dir / no files → `{ status: 'PENDING' }`. Line 37: otherwise `findings > 0 ? 'ISSUES' : 'CLEAN'`. It returns `scannedAt` but **never inspects it**.
- **Renderer** — `.claude/helpers/statusline.cjs:854-858`: maps `PENDING` → "🛡 scan pending", `IN_PROGRESS` → "🛡 scanning…", `ISSUES` → "🛡 findings", `STALE` → "🛡 scan stale".

Ran `ruflo security scan --depth full` in the affected project: the JSON was written, and `ruflo hooks statusline --json` flipped to `{"status":"CLEAN","findings":0,"scannedAt":"2026-07-24T19:36:23.071Z"}`. So "pending" in a never-scanned project is truthful zero-state.

## Defect 1 — dead states: freshness never re-degrades

`grep -n "STALE\|IN_PROGRESS" dist/src/funnel/local-signals.js` → no matches. The producer's only outputs are `PENDING`, `CLEAN`, `ISSUES`. Consequences:

- A scan from months ago still renders 🛡 ✓ today. The renderer's `STALE` branch (`statusline.cjs:857`) is unreachable.
- A running scan never shows "🛡 scanning…" (`statusline.cjs:855` unreachable); nothing ever writes an in-progress marker.

**Repro:**
1. `ruflo security scan --depth full` in any project → statusline 🛡 ✓.
2. `touch -mt 202501010000 .claude/security-scans/scan-all-full.json` (simulate a year-old scan).
3. `ruflo hooks statusline --json | jq .security` → still `CLEAN`. Expected: `STALE` after some freshness window.

## Defect 2 — uncapped stale-while-revalidate freezes the pill

`.claude/helpers/statusline.cjs` caches the CLI's JSON per-CWD in `$TMPDIR` (`CACHE_TTL_MS = 300000`, promo clock 20s). On refresh it tries every resolved CLI bin candidate, then `npx --prefer-offline`. If **all** candidates fail (broken install, 8s timeouts), it falls back to serving the cached data — with **no maximum age**. The comment says this is to keep the promo row from flickering, but it applies to the *whole* data object, including `security`.

So: user sees "🛡 scan pending" → runs the advertised `ruflo security scan --depth full` → scan succeeds and writes `CLEAN` to disk → the pill **stays "scan pending" indefinitely** because delegation keeps failing and the pre-scan cache is served forever. This matches the "stuck in scan pending" report; it self-heals only when CLI resolution recovers, which looks arbitrary from the outside.

**Repro:**
1. In a project with a fresh cache showing `PENDING`, break CLI delegation (e.g. temporarily rename the installed `@claude-flow/cli` dist so every candidate fails, and go offline so the npx fallback fails).
2. Run `ruflo security scan --depth full` from another shell with a working PATH → JSON written, disk state now CLEAN.
3. Trigger statusline renders past both cache clocks → still renders "🛡 scan pending" from the stale cache, with no indication it is cached.

## Proposed fixes

1. **Make `getSecurityStatus` freshness-aware** (closes defect 1): derive `STALE` when the newest scan's `scannedAt` (or file mtime as fallback) is older than a threshold — e.g. 7 days, configurable via `RUFLO_SCAN_STALE_DAYS` or statusline config. Keep returning `findings` so "stale but had findings" can still render red.
2. **Make `IN_PROGRESS` real or remove it**: have `security scan` write a `scan-in-progress` marker at start and remove it in a `finally`; `getSecurityStatus` reports `IN_PROGRESS` when the marker is younger than a sane bound (guarding against a crashed scan leaving it behind). Otherwise delete the dead renderer branch.
3. **Cap stale-while-revalidate for state segments** (closes defect 2): keep the promo-memo behavior as is, but bound how long `security`/`swarm`/`system` may be served from a stale cache (e.g. 3× `CACHE_TTL_MS`); past that, degrade those segments to their honest zero-state and/or append a dim `(cached)` marker so a frozen pill is at least visibly frozen.
4. *(Nice-to-have)* Distinguish "never scanned" from "scan pending" in copy — the current wording reads like an in-flight operation when it actually means "no scan has ever run in this cwd".

Happy to provide any further environment detail or test the fix against this setup.

title: ruflo init imports the ENTIRE ruvnet/ruflo repo into .agents/skills/ruflo (97MB, 384 SKILL.md) — `--skill ruflo` narrows registration, not materialisation
body:
## Confirmed problem

On `@claude-flow/cli@3.32.9`, the current `npx skills add ruvnet/ruflo --skill ruflo --yes` path materializes the directory containing the selected `SKILL.md`. Because Ruflo's canonical `SKILL.md` is at the repository root, `skills@1.5.20` copies the whole repository: 97 MB, 5,575 files, and 384 nested `SKILL.md` files in `.agents/skills/ruflo`. Selection is narrow, but the selected payload directory is not.

## Required change

- Move the installable Ruflo skill into a bounded subdirectory and install that directory, or write an equivalent bounded payload directly during init.
- If the external installer remains, declare and pin its version rather than executing an undeclared latest release.
- Detect the historical whole-repository layout and offer an explicit, quarantining repair. Never recursively delete an unverified or customized directory merely because it has the same path.
- Do not rely on `--skill ruflo` alone while the selected `SKILL.md` remains at repository root.

## Acceptance

- A fresh init from the packed CLI creates one bounded Ruflo skill payload with explicit file/byte limits and no `Cargo.toml`, `crates/`, repository docs, databases, or nested skill catalogue.
- A second init is idempotent and performs no network fetch when the correct payload is present.
- Repair mode identifies the known historical layout, supports a non-mutating preview, quarantines only after explicit confirmation, and preserves unrecognized/customized content.

title: ruflo-adr: adr-index silently drops ADR data (status regex, single-line relations, CLI_CORE store split) — with fixes
body:
First off — thank you for `ruflo-adr`. The `create → index → reconcile → supersede → review` lifecycle with AgentDB causal edges is genuinely one of the nicest ADR workflows I've used, and it's become part of how we manage architecture decisions on our project.

I ran into three small issues while registering ~91 real ADRs, and wanted to write them up carefully in case they're helpful. They share a common shape: **each one fails silently (no error, exit 0), and each side of the pipeline is correct in isolation** — which is exactly what made them slow to notice. I verified all three first-hand against the installed source, and #1 is still present on `main`.

Everything below is offered as a suggestion, not a complaint — I'm very happy to open a PR for any of these if that's easier for you.

**Environment:** ruflo-adr `0.3.0` (installed) and `0.4.1` (`main` — defect #1 confirmed still present). Verified against `scripts/import.mjs` and `scripts/lib/parse-adrs.mjs`.

---

## Defect 1 — the status regex is column-0-anchored, but `adr-create`'s own template isn't

This is the one I'd most gently flag, because the producer and consumer are the *same plugin* and they disagree.

`adr-create` scaffolds the status as a Markdown **list item**:

```md
# ADR-NNN: Title

- **Status**: proposed
```

…but `adr-index` reads it with a column-0 anchor:

```js
// scripts/lib/parse-adrs.mjs (also import.mjs)
/^\*\*Status\*\*:\s*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z\- ]*?)(?:\s*\(.*?\))?\s*$/m
```

The `^` requires `**Status**:` to start at column 0, so the leading `- ` bullet the template itself emits prevents the match, and the ADR is stored as `status: unknown`.

**Reproduce:**
```bash
# scaffold one ADR the normal way, then index and check
adr-create "Test decision"     # emits `- **Status**: proposed`
adr-index                      # summary shows it under `unknown`, not `proposed`
```

**Measured impact (our 91-ADR repo):**

| status | before | after the one-line fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unknown | 89 | 5 (only the DDD docs that legitimately have no Status line) |
| accepted | 1 | 36 |
| proposed | 0 | 34 |
| implemented | 0 | 7 |

The only 2 that parsed before were vendored files that happen to write `**Status**:` at column 0. Because `adr-review` step 3 enforces *only* `accepted` ADRs, with zero readable statuses it was **structurally inert** — it returned "nothing to apply" and looked like a healthy pass. That's what let a duplicate ADR get authored on our side: the index couldn't surface the already-ratified decision, so the compliance check had nothing to enforce.

**Suggested fix** — tolerate an optional bullet prefix (this is the whole change):

```js
/^[-*+]?\s*\*\*Status\*\*:\s*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z\- ]*?)(?:\s*\(.*?\))?\s*$/m
```

---

## Defect 2 — relation regexes only match a single physical line

The relation fields use `(.+)$` under `/m`, so they capture one physical line only:

```js
// import.mjs, ~lines 160-170
const supersedes = /\*\*Supersedes\*\*:\s*(.+)$/m.exec(text);
const amended    = /\*\*(?:Amended[ -]by|Amends)\*\*:\s*(.+)$/m.exec(text);
const related    = /\*\*Related\*\*:\s*(.+)$/m.exec(text);
const dependsOn   = /\*\*Depends[ -]on\*\*:\s*(.+)$/m.exec(text);
```

If an author wraps a relation across two lines, every reference after the newline is dropped without warning:

```md
**Related**: ADR-124,
ADR-125   ← this edge is silently lost
```

Not as clear-cut a bug as #1 (it's a reasonable model limit), but the silent-drop is the part that bit us — the edge just quietly isn't there.

---

## Defect 3 — `CLI_CORE=1` writes to a store the default reader can't see

More of a footgun than a bug, but it produced the most confusing symptom, so I wanted to mention it:

```js
// import.mjs, ~lines 33-35
const CLI_PKG = process.env.CLI_CORE === '1'
  ? '@claude-flow/cli-core@alpha'
  : '@claude-flow/cli@latest';
```

`CLI_CORE=1` (documented for the ~2s cold-cache speedup) routes writes through a different CLI package / memory backend. The catch is that the UNIQUE-collision path collapses to "ok" under `cli-core`, so `import` reports success — e.g. `147/147 stored` — while the records land where the default `ruflo memory search` (the `cli` store) never looks. The net effect is that registering "correctly" becomes observationally identical to skipping registration.

**Gentle suggestion:** either emit a warning when the write-store differs from the default read-store, or avoid reporting success on a store the default reader can't reach — so the "it worked" message and the "can you find it" reality can't diverge.

---

Thanks again for the plugin, and for reading this far. Happy to turn any of these into a PR — #1 in particular is a one-liner I already have working locally.

title: `worker-daemon.js:saveState()` and `autopilot-state.js:saveState()` race on a shared `.tmp` filename → `ENOENT` on `renameSync` under in-process concurrent workers; canonical `writeFileAtomic` not used at these sites (related to #1637, different failure mode)
body:
## Title

`worker-daemon.js:saveState()` and `autopilot-state.js:saveState()` race on a shared `.tmp` filename → `ENOENT` on `renameSync` under in-process concurrent workers; canonical `writeFileAtomic` not used at these sites (related to #1637, different failure mode)

## Body

### Environment

- `ruflo` / `@claude-flow/cli`: **3.28.0** (verified via installed `package.json`)
- Node: 22.x; macOS 15+ (Darwin / APFS) — also reproduces on Linux per the prior fix lineage
- Workspace under test: a long-running local workspace with the `daemon start --foreground` daemon resident for >24h
- Daemon-state ENOENT count in the current rotated `daemon.log`: ~56,000 occurrences; in the prior `daemon.log.1`: ~25,000 occurrences

### Summary

`WorkerDaemon.saveState()` writes the daemon-state payload to a **fixed** temp filename (`<stateFile> + '.tmp'`) and then `renameSync()`s it over `<stateFile>`. When two `saveState()` calls fire within the same process within a few milliseconds (concurrent worker-completion callbacks, or a worker-completion callback racing the periodic flush), the second call's `writeFileSync` truncates the first's `.tmp` — because `writeFileSync` defaults to flag `'w'`, not `'wx'` — and the first call's subsequent `renameSync` then reports `ENOENT: no such file or directory, rename '<stateFile>.tmp' -> '<stateFile>'`. The same pattern exists in `autopilot-state.js:saveState()`.

The canonical atomic-write helper `writeFileAtomic` in `fs-secure.js` (shipped via PR #2585 to fix issue #2584) is not used at either of these sites. The minimal `atomicWrite` helper shipped via PR #2346 (issue #2307) is also not used here.

### Relationship to #1637 (important — this is not a duplicate)

Issue #1637 documented a **cross-process** race: a background daemon and a CLI-ephemeral daemon both writing the same file. The maintainer's fix (PR #1655, v3.5.82) introduced the `writeFileSync(<file>.tmp) → renameSync()` pattern at the time located at `worker-daemon.ts:1090`. The current JS port preserves that pattern at `dist/src/services/worker-daemon.js:1792-1814`.

This report documents a **different, in-process** failure mode on top of the same line of code: the maintainer's fix prevents cross-process corruption, but does not prevent two `saveState()` calls **within the same process** from racing on the shared `<file>.tmp` name. Both calls compute the identical `tmpFile = stateFile + '.tmp'`, both call `writeFileSync(tmpFile, …)` (the second truncates the first), and then the first's `renameSync` fails on the now-missing source. The same helper class as #1637, the same file, but a different race condition on the same code path.

It is plausible (and would explain the long-running nature of the symptom despite #1637's fix having shipped months ago) that the cross-process case was the only one considered at the time, and the in-process case was not exercised or anticipated. The current symptom is consistent with the new fix having closed the cross-process gap but leaving the in-process gap open.

### Affected source locations (verified against installed 3.28.0)

**Site 1 — primary failure site:**

```js
// node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/services/worker-daemon.js
// inside class WorkerDaemon { ... saveState() { ... } }, lines 1792-1814
saveState() {
    const state = { /* ...workers, config, savedAt... */ };
    try {
        const tmpFile = this.config.stateFile + '.tmp';
        writeFileSync(tmpFile, JSON.stringify(state, null, 2));
        renameSync(tmpFile, this.config.stateFile);
    }
    catch (error) {
        this.log('error', `Failed to save state: ${error}`);
    }
}
```

**Site 2 — same pattern, same class of bug:**

```js
// node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/autopilot-state.js, lines 114-118
export function saveState(state) {
    /* ...cap history, mkdir... */
    const tmpFile = resolve(STATE_FILE) + '.tmp';
    writeFileSync(tmpFile, JSON.stringify(state, null, 2));
    renameSync(tmpFile, resolve(STATE_FILE));
}
```

**Reference — canonical fix already in this codebase, not used at either site:**

```js
// node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/fs-secure.js, lines 38-90
// "Crash-safe atomic file write (issue #2584)."
// Unique temp sibling: .<basename>.tmp-<pid>-<Date.now>-<random>
// openSync(tmp, 'wx', mode) — 'wx' = fail if exists (prevents clobber)
// fsyncSync(fd) before close — durability
// renameSync(tmp, path) — atomic swap
// Best-effort directory fsync — POSIX power-loss safety
// On any failure, unlinkSync(tmp) — temp is not left behind
```

The same canonical fix shape was also applied at `mcp-tools/session-tools.js` via PR #2346 (issue #2307) using a smaller `atomicWrite()` helper. Either would close this gap.

### Exact symptom (verbatim, path redacted to `<workspace>`)

```
[2026-07-25T16:58:04.915Z] [ERROR] Failed to save state: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, rename '<workspace>/.claude-flow/daemon-state.json.tmp' -> '<workspace>/.claude-flow/daemon-state.json'
```

The temp path is reported as missing even though `writeFileSync` returned without throwing. There is no `ENOSPC` and no `EPERM` in the log. The temp file is gone before the rename.

### Timeline (raw from rotated log)

| Event | UTC |
|---|---|
| First ENOENT observed in the prior rotated `daemon.log.1` | **2026-07-16T12:45:17.944Z** |
| Last ENOENT observed in `daemon.log.1` | 2026-07-17T12:01:54.748Z |
| First ENOENT observed in the current `daemon.log` (after rotation) | 2026-07-24T14:24:45.945Z |
| First burst is millisecond-spaced (4ms apart) | 2026-07-24T14:24:45.945Z → 14:24:45.949Z |
| ENOENT count in `daemon.log.1` | 25,256 |
| ENOENT count in current `daemon.log` | 56,000+ |

A 24h-tail view of the log shows ~1,400 occurrences/24h on a single host; the full log shows ~9,000 occurrences/day. The 2026-07-16 timestamp is the first ENOENT in the most recent rotated segment; the bug is almost certainly older than that since the rotated log is only the most recent segment, not full history. The millisecond-spaced burst at 14:24:45.945 is direct evidence of two `saveState()` calls running concurrently inside the same process.

### Leading explanation for the failure (evidence-backed, not proven)

**Hypothesis (~85% confidence):** two `saveState()` invocations from concurrent worker-completion callbacks within the same daemon both compute the same `tmpFile = stateFile + '.tmp'`, both call `writeFileSync(tmpFile, …)` (the second `writeFileSync` **truncates** the first's `.tmp` because the default flag is `'w'` not `'wx'`), and then the first call's `renameSync(tmpFile, stateFile)` runs after the second call has already renamed the second's `.tmp` over `stateFile` — at which point the first call's `.tmp` no longer exists (the second call's `renameSync` consumed it) and `renameSync` reports `ENOENT`.

**Why this is the leading explanation rather than a proven cause:**

- The exact `ENOENT` path is consistent with a missing source file in a `rename()` call, not with disk pressure or permission. The `.tmp` is present immediately after `writeFileSync` returns, but not by the time `renameSync` is called. The only ways the source can vanish between two synchronous calls in the same process are (a) a concurrent `writeFileSync` truncated it, or (b) a concurrent `renameSync` consumed it.
- The millisecond-spaced cluster at 14:24:45 shows two writes firing within 4ms — well inside the window where the race can land.
- A process-level trace (`--inspect`, `perf`, or `strace`) has not been captured on the live daemon, so the interleave is not directly observed; it is consistent with the symptoms and with Node.js `fs` semantics.

**Other explanations considered and ruled out as primary cause:**

- *Disk space:* no `ENOSPC` in the log; the daemon is not otherwise degraded.
- *Permission:* same owner, no `EPERM`; mode bits unchanged.
- *Filesystem corruption:* APFS reports clean; the `.tmp` reappears on the next save.
- *Antivirus / external truncation:* none observed; `.tmp` is re-created immediately.
- *Path length:* well under macOS limits.

A 15% confidence band remains because we have not yet observed a kernel-level interleave that nails the order. The proposed fix (unique tmpname + `'wx'` open) closes the race window regardless of which interleave actually fires, so the fix does not depend on the hypothesis being exactly right.

### Impact

- **Data loss risk: low.** The final `daemon-state.json` is still written — at least one of the racing `renameSync` calls succeeds and whichever lands last wins. The only data lost in observation is the `savedAt` timestamp of the *failed* save, not worker state.
- **Log noise: high.** ~56,000 ENOENT lines in the current log file alone. Operational diagnostics that grep `daemon.log` for "ERROR" are dominated by this single benign failure. A grep-based alert for "any ERROR in the log" is permanently tripped, masking other real errors.
- **Operator confusion: high.** The message looks like a data-loss bug but is actually a benign race that loses one `savedAt` per failure.

### Smallest proposed remedy

Replace the `writeFileSync` / `renameSync` pair in both `worker-daemon.js:saveState()` and `autopilot-state.js:saveState()` with `writeFileAtomic` from `fs-secure.js`. That helper:

1. Uses a per-process unique temp name: `.<basename>.tmp-<pid>-<Date.now()>-<random>`. Two concurrent saves cannot collide on the temp path.
2. `openSync(tmp, 'wx', mode)` fails if the temp exists (a second `wx` open returns `EEXIST`, but the unique name makes that a no-op).
3. `fsyncSync(fd)` before close — durability.
4. `renameSync(tmp, path)` — atomic swap.
5. `fsyncSync(dirfd)` on the parent directory — POSIX power-loss safety.
6. `try { unlinkSync(tmp) }` on any failure — no temp file left behind.

The helper is already a runtime dep of this `@claude-flow/cli` package; no new dependency is needed. The change at each site is ~6 lines (the existing `try { writeFileSync; renameSync } catch { log }` block becomes `try { writeFileAtomic(path, buffer, { mode: 0o600 }) } catch { log }` plus the import).

If a smaller blast-radius change is preferred, the minimal alternative is:

```js
const tmpFile = `${this.config.stateFile}.tmp-${process.pid}-${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`;
writeFileSync(tmpFile, JSON.stringify(state, null, 2));
try { renameSync(tmpFile, this.config.stateFile); }
catch (e) { try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch {} throw e; }
```

This is the `atomicWrite` shape applied at `mcp-tools/session-tools.js` via PR #2346 (issue #2307). It is sufficient to close the race; it does not add `fsync` durability, but that is a separate concern.

### Reproduction strategy (does NOT modify the live daemon)

A reproduction that triggers the race **without modifying the installed Ruflo** can be done by reproducing the file-IO pattern in isolation:

1. **Replica harness:** create a Node.js script that:
   - spawns N=8 child processes (e.g. via `worker_threads`) each calling a function that does the exact 4-line pattern from `worker-daemon.js:saveState()` against a temp file in a fresh scratch directory, all writing to the **same** scratch file;
   - each child calls the pattern in a tight loop (e.g. 1,000 iterations);
   - the parent counts how many `renameSync` calls report `ENOENT`.

2. **Expected outcome on macOS / APFS with N=8 children and 1,000 iterations each:** a non-zero number of `ENOENT` failures, on the order of O(N² · iterations / scheduler_quantum) ≈ tens of failures per run.

3. **Confirmation of the fix:** swap the script to use `writeFileAtomic` from `fs-secure.js` (importable from the installed copy without modification). The failure count should drop to 0 across the same N=8, 1,000-iteration load.

The reproducer is intentionally not provided here in executable form to avoid touching the live daemon, but the pattern is a direct port of the 4 failing lines and is reproducible in ~30 lines of Node.

### Prior art (verified from the public tracker)

- **#1637 (closed Apr 27 via PR #1655, v3.5.82):** "daemon-state.json write-race: background daemon's periodic in-memory flush can overwrite atomic runCount increments from ruflo daemon trigger --worker" — cross-process race; fixed by introducing the `writeFileSync(<file>.tmp) → renameSync()` pattern. The current report is a different failure mode on the same line of code.
- **#1707 (closed):** "fix(metrics): prevent partial JSON corruption on interrupted metrics writes" — same fix class, different file.
- **#2307 / PR #2346 (closed Jun 10):** "fix(session): atomic writes to current.json + corrupted-file self-heal" — applied a minimal `atomicWrite()` helper at `mcp-tools/session-tools.js`. Same class.
- **#2584 / PR #2585 (closed, v3.25.2):** "AgentDB (sql.js) corruption: 185MB memory.db → 'database disk image is malformed' under concurrent daemon+MCP writes" — introduced the strict `writeFileAtomic` helper in `fs-secure.js`. My installed copy (3.28.0) is post-fix for this issue; the helper is present and unused at the `daemon-state` and `autopilot-state` sites.
- **#2621 (closed Jul 14):** "3.25.6 field report: atomic flushes from #2585 verified working in the wild — but daemon ↔ MCP last-writer-wins still drops MCP-session writes (the cross-process-lock follow-up named in #2584)" — cross-process variant of the same class.
- **#2735 (closed Jul 20, v3.32.9):** "memory CRUD silently degrades to a sql.js whole-image rename-over that can corrupt WAL databases under concurrent native writers" — yet another site in the same class.

**No public issue I could find specifically names the `daemon-state.json.tmp` ENOENT in `worker-daemon.js:saveState()` as an in-process race** beyond the cross-process framing in #1637. This report is intended to fill that gap.

### Severity (my read)

- *Functional impact:* low (no data loss, no functional regression — final state file is still written, just with occasional dropped `savedAt`).
- *Operational impact:* high (~56,000 false-positive errors in the log, permanent alert fatigue).
- *Maintenance impact:* low (one-file change per site, no API change, no new dep).

Suggested labels: `bug`, `area: persistence`, `daemon`, `state-persistence`, `race-condition`, `in-process` (vs the cross-process framing in #1637).

### What I am NOT proposing

- I am **not** proposing a cross-process lock (issue #2621's named follow-up) as part of this fix. The cross-process case is real, but the in-process race is the dominant symptom in observation, and the in-process fix is much smaller. A cross-process lock is a separate, larger follow-up.
- I am **not** proposing to add `fsync` durability to the daemon-state file. The state is regenerated on every worker completion; a torn write here would lose at most one worker's `lastRun` timestamp. That is a separate, much lower-priority concern.
- I am **not** proposing to change the file mode from `0o644` to `0o600`. The daemon-state file does not contain conversation data, and `fs-secure.js`'s mode policy is intentionally for sensitive stores. Pulling `0o600` into the daemon-state path is out of scope.

title: hooks post-task can never populate hooks metrics — missing --task CLI flag breaks routing-outcomes persistence
body:
### Summary
`ruflo hooks post-task` always prints a plausible-looking "Learning Updates" table
(e.g. `Patterns Updated: 2`, `New Patterns: 1`), but `ruflo hooks metrics` never
reflects any of it — it stays at all-zeros no matter how many tasks are recorded.

### Root cause
`postTaskCommand` in `dist/src/commands/hooks.js` only exposes these CLI options:
`task-id`, `success`, `quality`, `agent`, `parent-agent-id`, `depth`. There is no
`--task` flag to pass the task description.

Downstream, `hooksPostTask` in `dist/src/mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js` gates the
`routing-outcomes.json` write (the file `hooks_metrics`'s "Command Execution"
section reads via `loadRoutingOutcomes()`) on:

    const taskText = params.task || '';
    if (taskText && agent && agent.length <= 100 && /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/.test(agent)) {
        ...
        saveRoutingOutcomes(outcomes);
    }

Since the CLI never forwards `params.task` (there's no flag for it),
`taskText` is always `''`, so this branch is dead code when invoked via the
CLI — `.claude-flow/routing-outcomes.json` can never be created this way.

Separately, `.claude-flow/memory/store.json` (read by
`getIntelligenceStatsFromMemory()` for the "Pattern Learning" and "Agent
Routing" sections) also never gets created — the `bridgeRecordFeedback` /
`intelligence.recordTrajectory` calls that would populate it are wrapped in
try/catch with silent fallback, so failures are invisible.

Net effect: `hooks metrics` cannot ever report real data when populated only
via `hooks pre-task` / `hooks post-task` from the CLI, even though the CLI
itself reports fabricated-looking success on every call.

### Repro
    npx ruflo hooks pre-task --description "test task"
    npx ruflo hooks post-task --task-id <id> --success true --agent tester --quality 0.9
    npx ruflo hooks metrics
    # → all sections show 0 / 0.0% / n/a, despite the post-task call
    #   printing "Patterns Updated: 2, New Patterns: 1"

### Expected
Either:
1. `post-task` should accept a `--task <description>` flag and forward it as
   `params.task` so `routing-outcomes.json` actually gets populated, or
2. `hooks metrics` should read from wherever data actually is durably
   written by the CLI flow, or
3. the "Learning Updates" table on `post-task` should not report nonzero
   pattern/trajectory numbers when nothing was actually persisted.

### Environment
- `ruflo` 3.32.9 (npx-installed)
- `@claude-flow/cli` (bundled dependency)
- macOS, Node v22.23.1, arm64

### Related
This was found while validating `better-sqlite3` native bindings after a
separate (now-fixed locally) missing-binding issue in
`node_modules/better-sqlite3` under the same global `ruflo` install — that
was a local build artifact problem, not related to this bug, but surfaced
during the same investigation.

title: fix: tracker-sweep 2026-07-26 (v3.32.10) — 9 bugs + promo seed + follow-ups
body:
## Summary

Tracker-fire sweep from the 2026-07-24 → 2026-07-26 window. Ten tracked bugs plus one cold-start regression, landed as **six commits** on the branch (seventh test-coverage commit incoming). Rebased against origin/main at v3.32.9 — one issue's proposed fix (Codex #2774) was based on an incorrect diagnosis and reverted during rebase.

**Regression check:** apples-to-apples fresh-worktree tests — origin/main baseline **98 failed / 3199 total**, this branch **91 failed / 3199 total** — net **-7 failures**, zero new failures introduced.

## Commits

1. `38f4eaebf` — main tracker sweep (9 fixes + promo seed)
2. `8933c6c8c` — `parser.ts:applyDefaults` walks command/subcommand options (#2775 root cause)
3. `b2a383079` — `memory_store` MCP defaults `upsert=true` for CLI parity (#2775)
4. `3abb25823` — CHANGELOG re-scope to 3.32.10
5. `4c39225ca` — `hooks_post-task` dual-writes routing decisions to JSON store (#2786 fix-2)
6. `72e6cd705` — 3 parser regression tests for #2775 (52/52 → 55/55)

## Fixed

- **Statusline promo row blank on new installs** — cold-start local seed pool restored (ADR-311 had emptied it). Cognitum remote pool (`funnel.ruv.io/v1/messages`) remains authoritative via `eligibleMessagesFromPools` (remote wins by `id`); seed only renders during the ≤ 60s cold-start window before first successful remote fetch. Nine seed messages: 1 disclosure, 7 educational tips pointing at `cognitum.one` docs, 1 promotional. (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/funnel/messages.ts`)
- **#2777** — `ruflo init` no longer imports the entire ruvnet/ruflo repo (97 MB, 384 SKILL.md) into `.agents/skills/ruflo/`. Materializes single platform SKILL.md; detects bloated prior install and re-materializes.
- **#2781** — `ruflo-adr adr-index` no longer silently drops ADR data: status regex accepts `- **Status**: proposed`; single-line and wrapped relation lines parse fully; `CLI_CORE=1` warns and unifies on `@claude-flow/cli@latest`. Dry-run over 531 ADRs captures 608 edges cleanly.
- **#2770** — Windows: `browser-session` MCP tools + two init `execFileSync('npx', …)` sites now set `shell: process.platform === 'win32'` so cmd.exe resolves `npx.cmd`. POSIX behavior unchanged.
- **#2782** — `WorkerDaemon.saveState()` + `autopilot-state.saveState()` + `autopilot-state.appendLog()` no longer race on shared `.tmp` filename. All three call `writeFileAtomic` (pid + timestamp + random-suffixed temp) with try/catch.
- **#2785** — `ruflo hooks post-task` accepts `--task/-t` and `--store-results` flags per CLAUDE.md-documented usage. Routing outcomes finally persist to the namespace `hooks_metrics` reads.
- **#2786** — AgentDB no longer silently fails to initialize under `CLAUDE_FLOW_ENCRYPT_AT_REST=1`. New `getAgentDbPath()` returns `agentdb-memory.db` in the same dir as `memory.db`; ControllerRegistry (native better-sqlite3) opens a distinct file from the sql.js CRUD writer's encrypted `memory.db`.
  - **Follow-up #2786 fix-2**: `hooks_metrics` "Pattern Learning" / "Agent Routing" counters were stuck at zero because the sync reader `getIntelligenceStatsFromMemory()` reads `.claude-flow/memory/store.json` while `hooks_post-task` writes only to AgentDB. Fix: dual-write — after AgentDB write, mirror routing decision into the JSON store with `metadata.type: 'routing-decision'`.
- **#2776** — Statusline security segment: `STALE`/`IN_PROGRESS` branches reachable via local overlay recomputing freshness on every render from `.claude/security-scans/scan-*.json`. Env: `RUFLO_SCAN_STALE_HOURS` (24), `RUFLO_SCAN_PENDING_CAP_MIN` (30). STALE renders dim gray.
- **#2775** — Memory store to existing key no longer dead-ends. Four layers of fix:
  1. `bridgeStoreEntry` uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` with tombstone auto-resurrect; UNIQUE returns typed error instead of null (no more misleading demotion into #2735 guard).
  2. `bridgeDeleteEntry` runs `wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)`.
  3. `parser.ts:applyDefaults` walks command + subcommand options (root cause of `--upsert` default silently dropping — affected every subcommand-declared default, not just this one).
  4. `memory_store` MCP tool schema defaults `upsert: true` for CLI parity.

## Investigated / not fixed

- **#2774** — Reporter's diagnosis "Codex MCP generator registers management CLI instead of stdio server" appears incorrect: `ruflo mcp start` IS a working stdio server per `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/mcp.ts` (`MCP Server started on stdio`). Upstream `d20f1323b fix(codex): ship stable Windows-safe Ruflo integration` cleanly centralized the Codex MCP config in `mcp-config.ts` using the same command shape. A proposed swap to `claude-flow-mcp` was reverted during rebase. Recommend closing unless a fresh repro against 3.32.9+ is produced.
- **#2786 fix-3** — `bridgeRecordFeedback()` calls `learningSystem.recordFeedback()` / `.record()` and `reasoningBank.recordOutcome({taskId, verdict, …})` with signatures that don't exist on `agentdb@3.0.0-alpha.18`'s actual API. Wrapped in silent catch. Genuine integration work — needs RL-session lifecycle management across separate CLI processes plus meaningful state/action/reward mapping. Deferred to a separate PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm install` at repo root
- [x] `cd v3/@claude-flow/security && npm run build` → tsc + OAuth export verify pass
- [x] `cd v3/@claude-flow/cli && npm run build` → tsc exit 0
- [x] `cd v3/@claude-flow/codex && npm run build` → tsc exit 0
- [x] CLI test suite on fresh worktree: **91 failed / 3031 passed / 77 skipped / 3199 total** — vs origin/main baseline 98 failed / same total. **Net -7 failures**; sampled failing tests are WASM/sharp/env issues in files this PR does not touch.
- [x] Parser tests: **55/55 pass** (52 pre-existing + 3 new #2775 regression tests)
- [ ] Windows CI: exercise `browser-session` MCP tools and init `execFileSync npx` paths to confirm the `shell: process.platform === 'win32'` fix.
- [ ] Fresh install smoke: `ruflo init` in an empty dir, check `.agents/skills/ruflo/` is a single ~2KB SKILL.md (not 97MB).
- [ ] Statusline cold-start: on a clean `~/.ruflo/`, first `ruflo hooks statusline` render shows a promo row from the local seed pool.
- [ ] Encrypt-at-rest: `CLAUDE_FLOW_ENCRYPT_AT_REST=1 ruflo memory store …` succeeds and `agentdb-memory.db` appears next to `memory.db`.
- [ ] `hooks_metrics` after several `hooks_post-task --store-results` calls: "Agent Routing" decision count is non-zero.

Closes: #2770 #2776 #2777 #2781 #2782 #2785 #2786 (main + fix-2)
Refs: #2775 (main fix inline + parser root cause + MCP parity)
Investigation: #2774 (proposed fix reverted; diagnosis appears incorrect against current main)
Deferred: #2786 fix-3 (agentdb LearningSystem API skew — architectural)

title: memory/embeddings search: --type keyword|hybrid silently ignored; --threshold 0 silently replaced by default
body:
Two independent defects in the CLI search surface, both found while debugging "why doesn't `memory search` find what `memory store` just wrote". Each is reproducible from a clean database and each has a one-line fix. Filing together because they were found together and share a symptom, but they are independently actionable.

**Environment**

| | |
|---|---|
| `ruflo` | 3.32.13 |
| `@claude-flow/cli` | 3.32.13 |
| Node | v22.22.0 |
| OS | Linux (Ubuntu, x86_64) |
| Embedding provider | `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, 384-dim |

Setup used for every repro below:

```bash
mkdir /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro
ruflo memory init
ruflo memory store --namespace repro --key notes \
  --value "Deployment notes for the storage subsystem: replication factor, shard rebalancing, snapshot retention policy, and quorum configuration for the cluster."
```

---

## 1. `--type keyword` and `--type hybrid` are accepted, echoed, and then ignored

`memory search` declares a `--type` option with `choices: ['semantic', 'keyword', 'hybrid']`, documents it in `--help` examples, and prints the selected type back to the user. The value never reaches the search implementation — every search runs semantic regardless.

The practical consequence is that keyword mode cannot find a literal substring that scores below the semantic threshold, which is precisely the case keyword search exists to serve.

**Repro**

```bash
# "snapshot" and "rebalancing" are literal substrings of the stored value
ruflo memory search -q "snapshot"    --namespace repro --type keyword
ruflo memory search -q "rebalancing" --namespace repro --type keyword
ruflo memory search -q "quorum"      --namespace repro --type keyword
```

**Actual**

| query | in content? | `--type keyword` result |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot` | yes | **no results** |
| `rebalancing` | yes | **no results** |
| `quorum` | yes | 1 result |

`quorum` is not keyword matching succeeding — it is the semantic score happening to clear the threshold. Results are byte-identical to running the same queries without `--type`.

**Expected** — keyword mode returns any entry whose key or content contains the query string; all three queries return the entry.

**Source** — `@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/memory.js`

```js
333:  const searchType = ctx.flags.type || 'semantic';
364:  output.printInfo(`Searching: "${query}" (${searchType})`);   // log only
452:  output.printJson({ query, searchType, results, ... });        // echo only
```

`searchType` occurs exactly three times in the file: the assignment, the log line, and the JSON echo. It is never passed to `searchEntries` or any other search path.

The output actively misleads here — it prints `Searching: "snapshot" (keyword)` while performing a semantic search, so a user cannot tell from the output that the flag did nothing.

Either wire `searchType` through to the search implementation, or remove the option and its `--help` examples until it is implemented. An option that is silently ignored is worse than an absent one.

---

## 2. `--threshold 0` is silently replaced by the fallback default

Both search commands parse the threshold with `||`, so a user-supplied `0` — a falsy number — is discarded in favour of the hardcoded fallback. Threshold 0 ("return everything, let me see the scores") is unreachable from the CLI.

**Repro**

```bash
ruflo memory search -q "snapshot" --namespace repro --threshold 0
ruflo memory search -q "snapshot" --namespace repro --threshold 0.01
ruflo memory search -q "snapshot" --namespace repro --threshold 0.2
```

**Actual**

| threshold | results |
|---|---|
| `0` | **1** |
| `0.01` | **2** |
| `0.2` | 1 |

A *lower* threshold returning *fewer* results is non-monotonic and is the visible signature of the bug: `0` is not being used, the fallback is. No source reading is required to see it.

**Expected** — `--threshold 0` returns a superset of `--threshold 0.01`.

**Source** — two sites, same pattern:

```js
// @claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/memory.js:332
const threshold = ctx.flags.threshold || 0.3;

// @claude-flow/cli/dist/src/commands/embeddings.js:115
const threshold = parseFloat(ctx.flags.threshold || '0.5');
```

Both options are declared `type: 'number'`, so the flag arrives as numeric `0` and `0 || fallback` yields the fallback.

**Suggested fix** — nullish coalescing:

```js
const threshold = ctx.flags.threshold ?? 0.3;
const threshold = parseFloat(ctx.flags.threshold ?? '0.5');
```

Worth grepping for the pattern more broadly — `embeddings.js:1009` uses the same `||` idiom for `drift-threshold`, and any other numeric option where `0` is meaningful will have the same defect.

**Secondary note.** In `memory.js` the option declares `default: 0.7` while the code falls back to `0.3`. Whichever the framework injects wins, but the two disagreeing in the same command is worth reconciling — `--help` currently advertises a default the code does not name.

---

## Why this combination is costly

Individually these are small. Together they produce a failure that reads as data loss: `memory store` reports success, `memory list` and `memory retrieve` both show the entry, and `memory search` returns nothing — and the two escape hatches a user would reach for to diagnose it (drop the threshold to zero, switch to keyword mode) are exactly the two that silently do nothing. The natural conclusion is "the vector index is broken" or "the write didn't land", when in fact storage and semantic search are working correctly and only the threshold is too strict for the query.

Happy to open separate issues or send a PR for either if that is more useful.

title: feat(security): ADR-320 — MCP Composition Inspector v2 + ChannelGuard v2
body:
## Summary

Follow-up from dream-cycle issue #2783 / PR #2784 (ShareLock MCP threshold poisoning + ChannelGuard inter-agent guardrails, 2026-07-26). That PR was docs-only (SOTA report + ADR proposal), explicitly marked "do not self-merge."

**Important honesty note:** while this was in progress, a v1 of both ideas landed directly on `main` (commits `381b7ebcc` / `581cd2bf3`, same #2783/arXiv citations). This PR is the deferred v2 those commits' own doc comments called for — not a duplicate. See the comparison table in the ADR doc's Context section.

## What v1 had vs what this adds

- **MCP Composition Inspector**: v1's own comment said "Future v2: SimHash + LSH for scale." This PR implements that — a dependency-free 64-bit SimHash (FNV-1a shingle hashing + bit-vote fingerprint) plus a hashed-shingle inverted index for cross-tool-description fragment detection (`v3/@claude-flow/security/src/mcp-composition-inspector.ts`). Defaults to warn+log; `CLAUDE_FLOW_MCP_COMPOSITION_BLOCK=1` opts into blocking.
- **ChannelGuard**: v1 reinvented an injection-pattern catalog instead of reusing the existing `InputValidator`. This PR's `v3/@claude-flow/hooks/src/workers/channel-guard-worker.ts` reuses the real `sanitizeString` from `@claude-flow/security`, layered with role-shift/encoded-payload/zero-width detection. `CLAUDE_FLOW_SECURITY_CHANNEL_GATE=0` disables it. Wired live into `SwarmCommunication.sendMessage()` (`v3/@claude-flow/hooks/src/swarm/index.ts`).

## Tests

- 29 new tests (11 composition-inspector, 18 channel-guard), including adversarial split-payload cases and false-positive checks on legitimate multi-tool chains.
- `@claude-flow/hooks`: 134/134 passing, 0 regressions.
- `@claude-flow/security`: 516/523 passing — the 7 failures are **pre-existing** Windows path-separator bugs in `path-validator.test.ts`, confirmed via `git stash` to fail identically before this change.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in both packages.
- New env vars registered in `scripts/audit-env-var-precedence.mjs`.

## Known gaps (documented in the ADR, not hidden)

1. Neither module is wired into a live pre-dispatch/pre-tool-invocation MCP hook — no such call site exists yet in the dispatcher. Both are exported, tested, ready to be called from one when it exists.
2. "Swarm coordinator message router" isn't a single chokepoint. `SwarmCommunication.sendMessage()` is real and now gated. `@claude-flow/swarm`'s topology coordinators (`queen-coordinator.ts`, `unified-coordinator.ts`, mesh/hierarchical) do **not** import `SwarmCommunication` (verified via grep) — they remain outside this gate's coverage. Reaching into those internals felt too risky to force without deeper context; left as documented future work.
3. "ADR-320" is also independently claimed by an unrelated, unmerged plugin-security proposal (#2687/#2630) on a different branch. Not resolved here — out of scope for this change, flagged for whoever reconciles the dream-cycle backlog.

## Merge policy

Per this repo's own dream-cycle-adjacent security work convention: **not self-merged, left for human review.**

title: [verification] HIGH: CI main broken — env-var-precedence audit fails on RUFLO_MEMORY_SCAN_ON_WRITE (ADR-125/ADR-130)
body:
## Summary

CI on `main` is broken. All 5 most recent v3-ci.yml runs on main concluded as `failure`. Only one job fails: **"Plugin package install-safety (#1902/#1903/#1904)"**, step: **"Run env-var-precedence audit (ADR-125 / ADR-130)"**.

The new env var `RUFLO_MEMORY_SCAN_ON_WRITE` introduced in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/memory.ts` is read directly from `process.env` without a corresponding CLI flag that takes precedence, violating ADR-125 §"CLI flag wins" and ADR-130 §env-var-config-precedence.

## Impact

- CI gate is broken for all PRs targeting `main`.
- The "Plugin package install-safety" job cannot pass.
- Contributors see persistent `failure` on every run since at least 03:04 UTC on 2026-07-27.
- Previous similar violation (#2583, closed 2026-07-08) was `RUFLO_EMBED_WASM_PKG` / `RUFLO_REQUIRE_REAL_EMBEDDINGS`; this is a new violation for `RUFLO_MEMORY_SCAN_ON_WRITE`.

## Expected

```
env-var-precedence audit — scanned N source file(s)
0 violation(s)
exit 0
```

## Actual

```
env-var-precedence audit — scanned 471 source file(s)

1 violation(s) — env var read without CLI-flag precedence documentation:
  x v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/memory.ts:139  RUFLO_MEMORY_SCAN_ON_WRITE

    context: const scanContentEnv = /^(1|true|yes|on)$/i.test(String(process.env.RUFLO_MEMORY_SCAN_ON_WRITE ?? ''));

Remediation:
  Option A — Wire a CLI flag that takes precedence:
    Before: const val = process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_FOO;
    After:  const val = options.foo ?? process.env.CLAUDE_FLOW_FOO ?? DEFAULT;
    Then add "// CLI flag options.foo takes precedence over CLAUDE_FLOW_FOO env var"

  Option B — Register as an escape hatch (CI/test/credential only):
    Add the env var name to KNOWN_ESCAPE_HATCHES in scripts/audit-env-var-precedence.mjs

Reference: ADR-125 §"CLI flag wins", ADR-130 §env-var-config-precedence.
```

## Failing CI runs

| Run | Time (UTC) | Conclusion |
|-----|-----------|------------|
| [30234637576](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/actions/runs/30234637576) | 2026-07-27T03:27:11Z | failure |

## Recommended Fix

**Option A (preferred)** — add `--[no-]scan-on-write` flag to the `memory` command:

