title: v3.32.29: every command crashes on a clean install — CLI entrypoint statically imports AgenticPolicyEngine from optionalDep @claude-flow/security ^3.0.0-alpha.14, which is unpublished (latest is alpha.12)
body:
`ruflo@3.32.29` is unusable after a clean global install: every command except `--version` dies during module loading, because the CLI entrypoint hard-imports two symbols from `@claude-flow/security` at a version that was never published to npm.

## Reproduction

Clean, isolated prefix (no pre-existing tree), macOS 26.5.2 / Node v26.5.0 / npm 11.17.0:

```
export NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/tmp/repro
npm install -g ruflo@3.32.29      # exit 0, 605 packages
ruflo --version                    # ruflo v3.32.29   <- works
ruflo --help
```

```
node:internal/modules/package_json_reader:301
  throw new ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND(packageName, fileURLToPath(base), null);
        ^
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@claude-flow/security' imported from
  /tmp/repro/lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/dist/src/services/policy-runtime.js
    at Object.getPackageJSONURL (node:internal/modules/package_json_reader:301:9)
    at packageResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:784:25)
    ...
    at async file:///tmp/repro/lib/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js:61:19
  code: 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
```

Identical failure for `status`, `doctor`, `swarm --help`, `mcp start` — i.e. all of them. `--version` survives only because it is answered before the import graph is walked, which makes the install look successful.

## Root cause

Two independent problems stack up.

**1. The declared version range cannot be satisfied.** `@claude-flow/cli@3.32.29`:

```json
"optionalDependencies": {
  "@claude-flow/security": "^3.0.0-alpha.14"
}
```

but the highest published version is `3.0.0-alpha.12`:

```
$ npm view @claude-flow/security versions
[ '3.0.0-alpha.1', '3.0.0-alpha.7', '3.0.0-alpha.8', '3.0.0-alpha.9',
  '3.0.0-alpha.10', '3.0.0-alpha.11', '3.0.0-alpha.12' ]
$ npm view @claude-flow/security dist-tags
{ v3alpha: '3.0.0-alpha.10', alpha: '3.0.0-alpha.10', latest: '3.0.0-alpha.12' }
```

Because the dependency is *optional*, npm silently skips it and exits 0 — nothing in the install output hints at the problem. `node_modules/@claude-flow/` ends up containing `cli, cli-core, mcp, memory, neural, shared` and no `security`.

**2. An optionalDependency is imported unconditionally.** `dist/src/services/policy-runtime.js` line 1:

```js
import { AgenticPolicyEngine, createLegacyCompatibleState, } from '@claude-flow/security';
```

This is a static ESM import of a package declared optional, reached from `bin/ruflo.js:61`, so a missing optional dependency is fatal rather than degraded. Even with the range fixed, installing the newest published version does not help — `3.0.0-alpha.12` does not export those symbols:

```
$ npm i @claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.12   # then import it
SyntaxError: The requested module '@claude-flow/security' does not provide an export named 'AgenticPolicyEngine'
```

Its exports include `AgentAuthorizationPropagator`, `InputValidator`, `SafeExecutor`, `ToolOutputGuardrail`, `createSecurityModule`, `makeLegacyPermissiveScope` etc., but neither `AgenticPolicyEngine` nor `createLegacyCompatibleState`. So `@claude-flow/security` >= alpha.14 appears to exist only in the monorepo and was not published alongside the `3.32.29` release train.

`policy-runtime.js` is new in `3.32.29` — the file is absent from the `@claude-flow/cli` tarballs for `3.32.26, 3.32.24, 3.32.22, 3.32.20, 3.32.16, 3.32.12, 3.32.8`, which is why only the current release is affected.

## Installing an older ruflo does not work around it

`ruflo@3.32.26` depends on `"@claude-flow/cli": "^3.32.7"`, which resolves to the latest matching `3.32.29`, so the broken CLI comes back and the error is byte-identical. The version printed by `ruflo --version` (3.32.26) is the wrapper's, not the CLI's — worth knowing when triaging reports.

## Workaround

Pin the CLI exactly, inside the global install:

```
npm install -g ruflo
cd "$(npm prefix -g)/lib/node_modules/ruflo"
npm install --save-exact @claude-flow/cli@3.32.26
```

`ruflo --help` / `doctor` / `status` work again after that (`doctor`: 9 passed, 15 warnings on a non-initialized directory).

## Suggested fix

Either publish `@claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.14`+ with `AgenticPolicyEngine` and `createLegacyCompatibleState`, or — since the dependency is deliberately declared optional — load it through a guarded dynamic `import()` in `policy-runtime.js` and fall back to a permissive/no-op policy when it is absent, so a missing optional package degrades instead of bricking every command. A CI check that installs the published tarball from the registry in a clean prefix and runs `ruflo --help` would catch this class of release skew; `--version` alone does not.

## Environment

- ruflo 3.32.29 (`@claude-flow/cli` 3.32.29)
- Node v26.5.0, npm 11.17.0
- macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0), arm64, npm prefix `/opt/homebrew`
- reproduced additionally in an isolated `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` with an empty tree

title: Daemon auto-start fires in any directory containing .claude/ (not a ruflo project), and the spawned daemon survives npm uninstall for up to 12h
body:
Two problems that compound each other:

1. Daemon auto-start treats **any** directory containing a `.claude/` folder as "an initialized ruflo project". `.claude/` is Claude Code's own directory, not a ruflo marker — so a plain `ruflo status` in a project that has never seen `ruflo init` (no `.claude-flow/`, no config, not even a git repo) silently spawns a detached background daemon and starts writing into that project.
2. The spawned daemon **survives `npm uninstall -g ruflo`**. Its script path is gone, nothing supervises it, and with `ttlMs: 43200000` / `idleShutdownMs: 0` it keeps waking workers for up to 12 hours. After uninstalling, `ruflo daemon stop` is not available either — the only remedy left is `kill`, and the pidfile is inside a project directory the user does not know about.

I hit this in the wild before understanding either part: I had two orphaned daemons for two unrelated directories, one of them my plain `~/dev` scratch folder, both still running after the package was uninstalled.

## Reproduction

Isolated npm prefix, throwaway working directory, `ruflo` 3.32.26 with `@claude-flow/cli` pinned to 3.32.26 (3.32.29 cannot run at all, see #2828):

```
mkdir -p /tmp/w/.claude && touch /tmp/w/.claude/launch.json   # Claude Code's dir, nothing to do with ruflo
cd /tmp/w
ruflo status
```

```
[ERROR] RuFlo is not initialized in this directory
[INFO] Run "ruflo init" to initialize
exit: 1
```

The command itself refuses to work — and still leaves this behind:

```
$ pgrep -fl "workspace /tmp/w"
44872 node .../@claude-flow/cli/bin/cli.js daemon start --foreground --quiet --workspace /tmp/w

$ find /tmp/w/.claude-flow
/tmp/w/.claude-flow/daemon.pid
/tmp/w/.claude-flow/daemon-state.json
/tmp/w/.claude-flow/harness-active-policy.json
/tmp/w/.claude-flow/logs/daemon.log
```

Nothing is printed about it: the `started` result is only surfaced under `--verbose`.

Control: the same command in the same directory **without** `.claude/` correctly does nothing (`reason: 'not a ruflo project'`). Creating `.claude/` is the only difference between the two runs.

## Why it fires: the guard does not match its own comment

`dist/src/services/daemon-autostart.js`:

```js
// Only in an initialized project (avoid scaffolding a daemon in a random dir).
if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(projectRoot, '.claude-flow')) && !fs.existsSync(path.join(projectRoot, '.claude'))) {
    return { started: false, reason: 'not a ruflo project' };
}
```

The stated intent is exactly right, but `.claude/` cannot carry it. Claude Code creates `.claude/` itself for `settings.json`, `launch.json`, local skills and so on, and users keep it in checkouts that have never heard of ruflo — in my case it existed only because of a `launch.json`. In practice this makes the guard almost always true, so "only in an initialized project" becomes "in nearly every project I am ever invoked in". `.claude-flow/` is the marker that actually means "ruflo lives here".

Called from `dist/src/index.js:197` for every command except `init`, `update` and `daemon` — so `status`, `doctor`, `--help`, everything.

## The daemon outlives the package

With the daemon from the repro above alive:

```
$ npm uninstall -g ruflo
removed 577 packages in 2s

$ ls $PREFIX/bin/ruflo
No such file or directory
$ ls $PREFIX/lib/node_modules/ruflo/node_modules/@claude-flow/cli/bin/cli.js
No such file or directory

$ pgrep -fl "workspace /tmp/w"
44872 node .../@claude-flow/cli/bin/cli.js daemon start --foreground --quiet --workspace /tmp/w
```

Still running, executing a script that no longer exists on disk. From its own `daemon-state.json`:

```json
"ttlMs": 43200000,          // 12h
"idleShutdownMs": 0,        // idle self-shutdown disabled
"maxConcurrent": 2,
"workers": [ map 15min, audit 10min, optimize 15min, consolidate 30min,
             testgaps 20min, backup 24h, harness 6h ]        // all enabled
```

There is no launchd/systemd unit (I checked `launchctl list`), so nothing external will reap it, and the documented `ruflo daemon stop` needs the binary that uninstall just deleted. The module docstring advertises "bounded lifetime: the daemon self-terminates on TTL/idle (12h default)" — with `idleShutdownMs: 0` the idle half of that is inert, so an abandoned workspace gets the full 12h.

On a loaded machine that is not free. My orphan's log, while I was doing unrelated work:

```
[05:14:43] Worker harness deferred: Memory too low: 2.8% free
[05:17:43] Worker map deferred: Memory too low: 1.8% free
[05:21:43] Worker optimize deferred: Memory too low: 4.1% free
```

It also writes outside `.claude-flow/`: `<cwd>/.claude/proven-config.json` + `.claude/.proven-config-version` (`schema: ruflo.proven-config/v1`, from `autoAdoptProvenConfigIfStale`) and `~/.claude-flow/update-state.json` — again in projects never initialized for ruflo. Cleaning up after an evaluation means finding files in three places, in every directory the CLI was ever run in.

## Suggested fix

1. Gate the auto-start on `.claude-flow/` (or a ruflo config file) only, and drop `.claude/` — that restores the guard's documented intent. A directory where `status` itself says "not initialized" should never get a daemon.
2. Print one line the first time a daemon is auto-spawned, at normal verbosity: what started, in which workspace, how to stop it, how to opt out. Right now the user's first hint is `ps`.
3. Make uninstall (or a documented `ruflo daemon stop --all` / `daemon list`) able to reach daemons across workspaces, and consider an npm `preuninstall` that stops them. A background process whose only stop path is the binary being removed is a footgun.
4. Give `idleShutdownMs` a non-zero default so an abandoned workspace daemon exits on its own well before the 12h TTL.

The opt-outs (`RUFLO_DAEMON_AUTOSTART=0`, or `daemon.autostart: false` in `claude-flow.config.json`) are well thought through, including the non-interactive-shell reasoning in the docstring — but they only help someone who already knows a daemon can appear. Item 1 is the one that matters: the auto-start currently fires in projects that are, by ruflo's own definition, not ruflo projects.

## Environment

- ruflo 3.32.26, `@claude-flow/cli` 3.32.26 (pinned; 3.32.29 is unusable, #2828)
- Node v26.5.0, npm 11.17.0, macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0), arm64
- reproduced in an isolated `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` with an empty tree; first observed with the 3.32.29 install on two real project directories

title: ADR-322 flywheel: safety envelope allows keys the proposer never emits, making local evaluation unreachable
body:
## Summary

The ADR-322 flywheel's local proposer path cannot run. Its safety envelope allows a set of policy keys that the proposer never emits, and forbids the keys it always emits, so every candidate is rejected before evaluation. `ruflo metaharness flywheel run --proposer local` always returns:

```json
{ "ran": false, "reason": "proposer archive contained no admissible candidates" }
```

No receipt can be produced, therefore no promotion is reachable on that path. Measured on `ruflo@3.32.30`.

## Why now

ADR-322 phases 0–2 shipped in the 3.32.26–3.32.30 train and the v3.32.26 end-user guide walks users through exactly this command. A user following that guide hits a hard stop at step 4 with a message that reads like a corpus/config problem on their side.

## Done looks like

- `flywheel run --proposer local` reaches evaluation on a project with a populated `neural_patterns` store and emits a signed receipt.
- A test binds the real proposer to the real envelope, so this class of drift fails CI instead of shipping green.

## Work items

- [ ] Align the envelope with the `RetrievalConfig` surface (PR below).
- [ ] Decide the `auto`-proposer promotion story (second defect, below) — this one is a governance call, not obviously a bug.
- [ ] Consider whether `canonicalizeJcs` throwing out of `validateCandidate` should be caught.

---

## Defect 1 — envelope/proposer key drift (blocker)

`harness-flywheel-runtime.ts:97` declares:

```ts
allowedPolicyKeys: ['alpha', 'topK', 'rerank', 'mmrLambda']
```

`retrievalPolicyNeighbors` (`harness-flywheel.ts:111`) mutates `RetrievalConfig` (`harness-flywheel.ts:40`):

```ts
interface RetrievalConfig { alpha; subjectWeight; mmrLambda; bodyWeight; typePenaltyFactor }
```

`topK` and `rerank` are `neural_patterns` search-call arguments; they are not representable in `RetrievalConfig`, so they are never proposed. Conversely `subjectWeight`, `bodyWeight` and `typePenaltyFactor` are proposed on every candidate and are not allowed.

The decisive detail is that `validateCandidate` (`flywheel-proposer.ts:100`) iterates **every** key of `candidate.policy`, and neighbors are full snapshots (`{...base, [axis]: v}`), not deltas. So the disallowed keys ride along on all of them.

### Reproduction

Against the installed 3.32.30 build, no patching:

```js
const { retrievalPolicyNeighbors, DEFAULT_CONFIG } = await import('.../services/harness-flywheel.js');
const { proposeFlywheelCandidates }                = await import('.../services/flywheel-proposer.js');

const archive = await proposeFlywheelCandidates({
  mode: 'local', baselinePolicy: DEFAULT_CONFIG, seed: 1,
  safetyEnvelope: { ref:'t', allowedPolicyKeys:['alpha','topK','rerank','mmrLambda'],
    numericBounds:{ alpha:{min:0.1,max:0.9}, topK:{min:5,max:20}, mmrLambda:{min:0.3,max:0.9} },
    maxP95LatencyMicros:5e6, maxCostMicrosPerTask:1e4, maxTokensPerTask:1e5,
    maxFailureRate:0.01, maxEvaluationCostMicros:1e6 },
  localProposer: () => retrievalPolicyNeighbors(DEFAULT_CONFIG).map(policy => ({ policy,
    resources:{ p95LatencyMicros:0, costMicrosPerTask:0, tokensPerTask:0, failureRate:0, evaluationCostMicros:0 } })),
});
```

```
candidates          : 19
admissibleCandidates: 0
paretoCandidates    : 0        <-- harness-flywheel-runtime.ts:137 requires > 0
rejection reasons(1): ["policy key not allowed: subjectWeight",
                       "policy key not allowed: bodyWeight",
                       "policy key not allowed: typePenaltyFactor"]
```

19/19 rejected on the default baseline, deterministically.

### Why the suite is green

- `__tests__/flywheel-proposer.test.ts:10` builds a synthetic envelope with `allowedPolicyKeys: ['alpha']` and feeds it synthetic alpha-only candidates.
- `__tests__/harness-flywheel.test.ts` calls `runFlywheelTick` directly, bypassing `runFlywheelWorker`, the production envelope and the archive.

No test imports `retrievalPolicyNeighbors` into a proposer test. The seam between the real proposer and the real envelope is the one thing never exercised, so the suite validates the ceilings but never the surface they guard.

### Note on the fix

Adding the three missing names is necessary but not sufficient. `validateCandidate:105` applies bounds only when they are present, so an allowed key without bounds is unbounded — a Darwin proposer could then submit arbitrary weights on those three axes. Verified:

```
bounds on 2 keys  -> subjectWeight=1e9 ADMISSIBLE, bodyWeight=-5000 ADMISSIBLE, typePenaltyFactor=1e12 ADMISSIBLE
bounds on all 5   -> all rejected
```

The PR therefore bounds all five axes.

Changing the envelope changes `safetyEnvelopeRef`, and `flywheel-transaction.ts:351` rejects a receipt whose ref differs from the pinned `activeSafetyEnvelopeRef`. Since the local path could never produce a promotable receipt, no local lineage can exist to migrate; a Darwin-produced lineage would need an explicit migration.

## Defect 2 — the default proposer produces an unpromotable receipt

Separate from the above, and possibly intended.

With `--proposer auto` (the default) and no Darwin adapter installed, `flywheel-proposer.ts:195` falls back to `runLocal('darwin-unavailable')`, stamping `proposerSubstitution`. `flywheel-transaction.ts:352` then refuses to promote any receipt carrying a substitution unless it appears in `options.allowedProposerSubstitutions`.

The CLI promote path (`commands/metaharness.ts:155`) passes only `{ confirm, trustedPublicKeys }` — never `allowedProposerSubstitutions` — as does the MCP tool (`mcp-tools/metaharness-tools.ts:713`). So once defect 1 is fixed, a default-mode run still yields a receipt that can never be promoted, with no flag to permit it.

ADR-322 and the end-user guide both say a substituted run is evaluation-only by default, so the *behaviour* looks deliberate. What seems unintended is that the default mode has no supported route to promotion at all, and the guide's walkthrough does not mention passing `--proposer local`.

## Defect 3 — non-finite policy value throws out of validation

`policyCandidateId` -> `canonicalizeJcs` throws `non-canonical number at $.typePenaltyFactor` on `Infinity`/`NaN`. That throw propagates out of `validateCandidate` and `finalizeArchive` rather than being recorded as a rejection reason. A proposer emitting a non-finite value crashes the run instead of having that candidate cleanly refused. Low severity given `runFlywheelWorker` wraps in try/catch, but it turns a candidate-level fault into a run-level one.

## Environment

- `ruflo@3.32.30` (global), macOS arm64, Node 22.17.0
- Verified against `main` @ `314ad1eb0`

title: fix(flywheel): align ADR-322 safety envelope with the policy surface it guards
body:
Fixes #2835 (defect 1).

## Summary

The ADR-322 retrieval safety envelope named a policy surface that does not exist, which made the local flywheel evaluation path unreachable. This aligns the envelope with `RetrievalConfig`, bounds every axis, and adds the contract test that was missing.

## The defect

`harness-flywheel-runtime.ts:97` allowed `['alpha','topK','rerank','mmrLambda']`. `retrievalPolicyNeighbors` emits `RetrievalConfig` snapshots keyed `alpha, subjectWeight, mmrLambda, bodyWeight, typePenaltyFactor`. `topK`/`rerank` are `neural_patterns` search-call arguments, not policy keys.

`validateCandidate` checks every key of a candidate policy, and candidates are full snapshots rather than deltas, so the three disallowed weights rode along on all of them:

```
candidates: 19   admissible: 0   pareto: 0
```

`runFlywheelWorker` requires a non-empty Pareto front, so every run ended at `"proposer archive contained no admissible candidates"`. No receipt, therefore no promotion.

## The fix

Envelope now names exactly the five real axes, each with a finite bound:

```ts
alpha:             { min: 0.1, max: 0.9 }
subjectWeight:     { min: 0.1, max: 10  }
mmrLambda:         { min: 0.3, max: 0.9 }
bodyWeight:        { min: 0.1, max: 10  }
typePenaltyFactor: { min: 0.1, max: 10  }
```

Bounds on all five, not just the two that had them, because `validateCandidate:105` range-checks a key only when bounds are present — an allowed-but-unbounded key is unbounded in practice. Measured:

```
bounds on 2 keys -> subjectWeight=1e9 ADMISSIBLE, bodyWeight=-5000 ADMISSIBLE, typePenaltyFactor=1e12 ADMISSIBLE
bounds on all 5  -> all rejected
```

The envelope is hoisted into an exported `retrievalSafetyEnvelope()` so tests can bind the real envelope to the real proposer.

## Why it shipped green

`flywheel-proposer.test.ts` uses a synthetic `allowedPolicyKeys: ['alpha']` envelope with synthetic alpha-only candidates. `harness-flywheel.test.ts` calls `runFlywheelTick` directly and bypasses the archive. Nothing joined the real proposer to the real envelope, so a fully green suite never exercised the shipped configuration.

`flywheel-envelope-proposer-contract.test.ts` closes that seam: real `retrievalPolicyNeighbors`, real `retrievalSafetyEnvelope()`, asserting the allowlist equals the emitted key set, that every allowed key is finitely bounded, and that an out-of-range weight on a previously unbounded axis is refused.

## Verification

- New test: **5/5 fail** against the v1 envelope, **5/5 pass** against v2. Confirmed by temporarily reverting the envelope and re-running.
- Full flywheel/harness suite: **16 files, 98 tests, green**.
- `tsc --noEmit`: 437 errors on this branch and **437 on pristine `origin/main`** — identical, pre-existing, none in the touched files.
- End-to-end against a real project with the fix applied to the installed build: the run advances past the proposer and reaches the next gate (`store too small to harvest a corpus`), confirming the admissibility blocker is what was stopping it.

## Compatibility

Envelope schema `v1 -> v2` changes `safetyEnvelopeRef`, and `flywheel-transaction.ts:351` rejects receipts whose ref differs from the pinned `activeSafetyEnvelopeRef`. Since the local path could never produce a promotable receipt, no local lineage can exist to migrate. A Darwin-produced lineage would need an explicit envelope migration.

## Not addressed here

Defects 2 and 3 in #2835 — the `auto`-proposer promotion dead-end and the non-finite-value throw out of `validateCandidate`. The first looks like a governance decision rather than a bug, so I left it for you rather than guessing at intent.

🤖 Generated with Ruflo & AQE

title: bug: autopilot config silently enables default task sources for invalid input
body:
## Summary

`ruflo autopilot config --task-sources <unsupported>` reports success but silently replaces the explicit value with all default sources:

- `team-tasks`
- `swarm-tasks`
- `file-checklist`

This is surprising and can broaden task discovery. In particular, `team-tasks` reads the global `~/.claude/tasks` tree, so a workspace configured with an unsupported source can begin discovering unrelated Claude team tasks from other workspaces.

## Reproduction

With Ruflo 3.32.30:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/ruflo-autopilot-repro
cd /tmp/ruflo-autopilot-repro
ruflo autopilot config --task-sources issues
```

Observed:

```text
Config updated: ... sources=team-tasks,swarm-tasks,file-checklist
```

Expected:

- return a non-zero/error result;
- list the supported values;
- leave the existing configuration unchanged.

The MCP `autopilot_config` path has the same fail-open behavior for unsupported `taskSources` values.

## Root cause

`validateTaskSources()` filters against `VALID_TASK_SOURCES` and falls back to all defaults when no input survives validation. That recovery behavior is reasonable while loading missing/corrupt persisted state, but the CLI and MCP configuration handlers also use it for explicit user input.

The resulting state file remains workspace-local. The cross-workspace symptom comes specifically from silently enabling `team-tasks`, whose discovery root is intentionally global.

## Proposed fix

Use strict validation at explicit configuration boundaries:

- reject empty, unsupported, or mixed-invalid source lists;
- enumerate the supported values in CLI help and the MCP schema;
- retain default recovery semantics when loading persisted state;
- add regression tests covering unsupported, mixed-invalid, empty, normalized, and deduplicated source lists.

I have a focused patch and regression tests ready.

title: fix(autopilot): reject invalid task sources
body:
## Summary

- reject unsupported or empty task-source lists at explicit CLI and MCP configuration boundaries
- preserve default recovery behavior for absent/corrupt persisted state
- enumerate valid values in CLI help and constrain the MCP input schema
- deduplicate normalized valid sources
- add focused regression coverage

Fixes #2837.

## Why

Before this change, an explicit unsupported value such as:

```sh
ruflo autopilot config --task-sources issues
```

was accepted and silently replaced by every default source. One of those defaults, `team-tasks`, intentionally scans the global `~/.claude/tasks` tree. The fail-open fallback could therefore make a workspace discover unrelated team tasks even though its autopilot state file remained workspace-local.

Persisted-state recovery and explicit configuration need different semantics: recovery may use defaults, but invalid user input should fail without saving broader defaults.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run __tests__/autopilot-task-sources.test.ts` — 5 tests passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- `npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false` — blocked by existing repository baseline errors, including unresolved `@claude-flow/security` workspace outputs, unbuilt swarm declaration outputs, and pre-existing `unknown` exception typing in `src/auth/client.ts`; no error referenced a changed file
- ESLint is not a usable TypeScript gate in this checkout because the current root configuration parses TypeScript as legacy JavaScript (`import` is reported as reserved)

## Scope

This PR does not add `issues` as a new discovery source and does not change the intentional global scope of Claude team tasks. It only prevents invalid explicit configuration from silently enabling those sources.

title: hooks route: learned patterns bucket per-agent and keep first-50 keywords, so more labelled outcomes degrade routing
body:
## Summary

`loadLearnedPatterns()` buckets learned routing keywords **per agent** rather than per task type, keeps the **first 50 distinct keywords ever seen** for that agent, and applies **no stopword or discriminative filtering**. The result is that each `learned-<agent>` pattern becomes a broad, noisy bag of generic terms that competes with the curated `TASK_PATTERNS` — so accumulating more labelled outcomes measurably *degrades* routing rather than improving it.

Observed on **v3.32.30** (`@claude-flow/cli`), with 42 recorded outcomes.

## Where

`dist/src/mcp-tools/hooks-tools.js`

- `loadLearnedPatterns()` — L196-214
- `getMergedTaskPatterns()` — L217-229
- `TASK_PATTERNS` — L231

```js
function loadLearnedPatterns() {
    const outcomes = loadRoutingOutcomes();
    const byAgent = {};
    for (const o of outcomes) {
        if (!o.success || !o.agent || !o.keywords?.length) continue;
        if (!byAgent[o.agent]) byAgent[o.agent] = new Set();
        for (const kw of o.keywords) byAgent[o.agent].add(kw);   // ← all tasks for an agent collapse into ONE set
    }
    const patterns = {};
    for (const [agent, kwSet] of Object.entries(byAgent)) {
        patterns[`learned-${agent}`] = {
            keywords: [...kwSet].slice(0, 50),                   // ← first-50-ever, insertion ordered
            agents: [agent],
        };
    }
    return patterns;
}
```

## Evidence

Reproducing the function against a real `routing-outcomes.json` (41 successful outcomes across 4 agents):

```
learned-tester:     50 kws | ['loop','verification','test','correct','install','agentdb','separate','file','encryption','upgrade','ruflo','verify', …]
learned-coder:      50 kws | ['smoke','test','upgrade','bug4','trajectory','fix','silent','memory-backup','no-op','encryption-at-rest','copyfilesync','fallback', …]
learned-researcher: 50 kws | ['root-cause','dual','ruflo','install','launchd','autoupdate','using','homebrew','npm','prefix','removed','units', …]
learned-reviewer:   20 kws | ['security','review','episodic-memory','summarizer','unrestricted','agent','sdk','tool','access','resumed','session','four']
```

**16 of 149 distinct keywords appear in two or more agent buckets** — they carry zero discriminative power but still match:

```
upgrade, test, upstream, json, episodic-memory, mcp, smoke, ruflo,
hooks, install, claude, local, agent, agents, swarm
```

`test` and `upgrade` and `smoke` each sit in **both** `learned-tester` and `learned-coder`.

Generic filler also survives into the buckets — `via`, `found`, `still`, `ones`, `using` — because nothing filters by frequency, document count, or stopword list.

Measured routing on this store (v3.32.30):

| task | routed to | per shipped `TASK_PATTERNS` |
|---|---|---|
| `fix a failing test` | `tester` | ✅ |
| `review this code for security vulnerabilities` | `researcher` | ❌ `security-task` |
| `implement a new dashboard section` | `tester` | ❌ `feature-task` |
| `research the best approach` | `coder` | ❌ |

## Why it gets worse with more data

1. **Per-agent bucketing** smears every task an agent ever did into a single pattern. An agent that has handled ten different kinds of work produces one vector representing none of them.
2. **`slice(0, 50)` on an insertion-ordered Set** freezes the bucket after roughly the first few tasks. Later, better-labelled outcomes contribute nothing — so the store grows while the routing input is fixed.
3. **No discriminative filtering.** Terms shared across agents, and English filler, are weighted identically to genuinely distinctive terms.
4. Curated `TASK_PATTERNS` entries are precise and narrow; `learned-*` entries are broad. In a nearest-match contest the broad noisy pattern frequently wins.

## Suggested direction

Any one of these would help; the first is probably the cheapest:

- **Drop keywords that appear in more than one agent bucket** before emitting patterns — they cannot discriminate by construction.
- **Rank rather than truncate**: keep the top-N by frequency-within-agent × rarity-across-agents (a small TF-IDF), instead of `slice(0, 50)` on insertion order.
- **Require minimum support** — ignore a keyword until it has appeared in ≥2 successful outcomes for that agent.
- **Bucket by task type rather than agent**, if outcome records can carry a task classification.
- Optionally gate learned patterns behind a confidence floor so they cannot outrank a static match.

## Note on a related, separate store

`hooks post-task` also feeds `intelligence.recordTrajectory()` → SONA/pattern distillation → `.claude-flow/neural/patterns.json` (168 entries here). Nothing in the routing path reads that file — `bridgeRouteTask()` (`dist/src/memory/memory-bridge.js` L2208) consults AgentDB's `semanticRouter` / `learningSystem.recommendAlgorithm`, and on this install those tables are empty (`reasoning_patterns` 0, `learning_experiences` 0), so it returns `null` and routing falls through to the merged keyword patterns above. That may be intended layering, but it does mean `patterns.json` size is not a signal of routing quality — worth documenting either way.

## Environment

- `@claude-flow/cli` **3.32.30** (via `ruflo`, `~/.local` prefix)
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64, node 22.23.0
- 42 outcomes in `.claude-flow/routing-outcomes.json`, 168 entries in `.claude-flow/neural/patterns.json`

title: flywheel: optimization anchor is ruflo-specific and hash-pinned, so downstream projects can run the loop but never promote
body:
## Summary

The flywheel's optimization objective is a fixed set of 10 human-labeled tasks about ruflo's own development history. Both flywheel paths use it, and the ADR-176 path pins it by content hash so it cannot be replaced locally. In any repository other than ruflo those queries retrieve nothing relevant, so the objective is flat across baseline and every candidate, and no candidate can clear the significance gate.

The result is that the flywheel can be made to *run* in a downstream install — populate the store and it will harvest a corpus and evaluate candidates — but it can never *promote*. And "never promotes" is indistinguishable from "no headroom left", which is the more dangerous of the two failure modes because it reads as success.

## Why now

ADR-322 shipped the governed flywheel in the 3.32.26–3.32.30 train and the end-user guide points users at `ruflo metaharness flywheel run --project-root .` in their own project. Once #2835 is fixed and the local proposer produces admissible candidates, this becomes the next thing a downstream user hits — and it fails much more quietly.

## Done looks like

A project can supply its own human-labeled anchor, with the same tamper-evidence guarantees the shipped one has, and the flywheel then optimizes that project's retrieval relevance rather than ruflo's.

## Work items

- [ ] Allow a project-local anchor file (path + its own pinned hash) to override the built-in set.
- [ ] Record which anchor a receipt was produced against, so lineages from different anchors are not comparable by accident.
- [ ] Decide what happens with no project anchor: fall back to the ruflo set, or decline to run with a clear reason.

---

## Detail

### The objective is ruflo-specific in both paths

`harness-flywheel-runtime.ts:146` (ADR-322 governed path) passes the hardcoded `ANCHOR` const. `harness-flywheel-runtime.ts:193` (ADR-176 generation path) passes `frozen.tasks` from `.claude/eval/human-relevance-frozen-v1.json`. Both are the same 10 tasks:

```
"how was the Opus model alias fixed"          => ["opus 4.8","opus alias","#2232"]
"self-learning wiring task-completed pretrain" => ["self-learning","adr-074","#2245"]
"SQL injection migrate.ts table identifier"    => ["sql injection","migrate.ts","agentdb","cve"]
...
```

These are labels over ruflo's own issues and ADRs.

### It is deliberately immutable

`loadFrozenHumanEval()` (`harness-frozen-eval.ts:65`) verifies against a pinned constant and throws:

```
frozen human eval hash mismatch — set has drifted (got ..., pinned sha256:6096e48e...);
supersede with a new versioned file, do not edit
```

That immutability is correct and worth keeping — the ask is not to unpin it, but to allow a *second*, project-supplied set with the same discipline.

### Why a flat objective cannot promote

`evaluateFlywheelCandidate` splits the anchor into train/held and scores with nDCG@3; the harvested self-supervised set is only the generalization guard. Acceptance (`flywheel-receipt.ts:281`) is:

```ts
accepted = relativeLift >= 0.02 && significant && frozenAnchorRegression <= 0
// significant = probability >= 0.95 && ciLow > 0   (paired bootstrap)
```

With a foreign corpus every anchor task scores ~0 for baseline and for all candidates. `relativeLift` has no signal, the paired-bootstrap deltas are all zero, `ciLow > 0` fails. Nothing is ever accepted, and the receipt does not distinguish "flat because the anchor is foreign" from "flat because the policy is already optimal".

To be straight about evidence: the immutability, the two call sites, the anchor contents and the acceptance rule are all read from source. The "scores ~0 on a foreign corpus" step is inference from the anchor's contents — I have not measured it, because measuring requires populating a downstream store first, which is only worth doing if the anchor problem is solvable.

### This is already anticipated in ADR-176

The hierarchical-evolution section says:

> The open research risk is that improvements found on one repository do **not** generalize — repository-specific optima will emerge.
> Global baseline └─ Language family └─ Framework family └─ **Repository specialization**
> A repository adopts the most-specific layer whose manifest passes *its own* benchmark.

"Its own benchmark" is exactly what is missing. The *policy* can specialize per repository, but the *yardstick* it is judged against cannot.

### Sketch, not a prescription

Something like a project-local `.claude/eval/<name>.json` plus a manifest entry naming the file and its expected hash, loaded through the same verify-or-throw path. The receipt already carries `gateVersion` and `policySchemaVersion`; an `anchorRef` alongside them would keep lineages from different anchors distinguishable.

I have not sent a PR for this one because the fallback semantics are a design decision — silently using ruflo's anchor in someone else's repo is arguably worse than refusing to run, and that is your call rather than mine to guess.

## Related

- #2835 — envelope/proposer key drift; blocks the local path before it ever reaches this gate
- ADR-176 (self-optimizing harness loop), ADR-081 (the anchor set), ADR-322 (governed flywheel)

## Environment

title: memory: bridge writes silently lost — agentdb-memory.db missing ADR-323 provenance_type column, error swallowed and reported as an unrelated WAL-sidecar refusal
body:
## Summary

A single transient AgentDB bridge-init failure permanently disables the native write path for the remaining life of that process. Every later write falls to the sql.js whole-image fallback, which refuses whenever `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars are present. The operator sees a message naming a cause they have no way to check, the real reason was discarded by a bare `catch {}`, and there is no recovery short of restarting the process.

Observed in the wild: an MCP server silently dropped **every** `memory_store` for roughly two hours while CLI writes to the same database succeeded normally.

## Why now

The failure is invisible by construction. The write returns `success: false` in a JSON payload that most callers do not surface, entry counts keep climbing because other processes write fine, and the one log line that would explain it is filtered out as noise. Nothing in the system reports that a process has entered this state.

## Done looks like

An operator hitting the WAL refusal can tell within one command whether the bridge is down and why, and can clear it without restarting.

## Work items

- [ ] Record and expose the init failure reason (PR below)
- [ ] Make `shutdownBridge()` able to clear a failed-init latch (PR below)
- [ ] Stop filtering degradation notices during init (PR below)
- [ ] Decide whether the latch should auto-retry after a cooldown (left open — see below)

---

## Detail

### The latch

`memory-bridge.ts` `getRegistry()`:

```ts
if (bridgeAvailable === false) return null;   // short-circuits forever
...
} catch {
  bridgeAvailable = false;                    // reason discarded
  registryPromise = null;
  return null;
}
```

`bridgeStoreEntry()` returns null when `getRegistry()` or `getDb()` is null, and `memory-initializer.ts` `storeEntry()` then takes the sql.js path, which refuses on sidecars:

```
memory database has an active native WAL connection (found -wal/-shm sidecar
files) — refusing an unsafe sql.js whole-image write. Retry once the native
writer completes, or restore the native better-sqlite3 bridge.
```

### The native driver was never the problem

Measured on `ruflo@3.32.30`, macOS arm64, Node 22.17.0:

- `better-sqlite3@12.11.1` resolves and opens `:memory:` with `journal_mode = WAL` from the `@claude-flow/memory`, `agentdb`, and `@claude-flow/cli` resolution contexts — all three.
- It opens the real `.swarm/memory.db` in WAL mode and reads all 10,578 rows.
- A fresh `ruflo memory store` succeeded end-to-end: 10578 → 10579 entries, mtime moved, 384-dim vector generated.
- The same `memory_store` through the long-lived MCP server failed in **7.5 ms** — far too fast for an init attempt, which is the latch short-circuiting.

Restarting other MCP servers changed nothing; only the affected process is poisoned.

### It is self-reinforcing

The `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars that trigger the refusal are created by the *healthy* native writers. The more reliably the native path works elsewhere, the more reliably a latched process fails. These two mechanisms were designed independently and interact badly.

### There is no recovery path

```ts
export async function shutdownBridge(): Promise<void> {
  if (registryInstance) {          // null exactly when init failed
    ...
    bridgeAvailable = null;        // so the reset is unreachable
  }
}
```

The only function that clears the latch cannot run in the state that sets it.

### The explanation is filtered out

AgentDB logs `[AgentDB] better-sqlite3 not available, using sql.js WASM` on fallback (`agentdb/src/core/AgentDB.ts`). The bridge's init suppressor drops any message containing `better-sqlite3` **or** `[AgentDB]` — both match. The single line that would explain a WASM fallback never reaches anyone.

### Related but distinct

`backend: 'sql.js + HNSW'` in `mcp-tools/memory-tools.js` is a hardcoded string literal at five sites, not a probe of the live driver. It reports sql.js regardless of what is actually in use, so it is actively misleading while diagnosing this. Not fixed in the PR — it is a reporting change with its own blast radius.

## Open question for the PR

The PR keeps the latch and makes it observable + clearable, rather than adding automatic retry. A cooldown-based retry would be more forgiving, but the latch may well be deliberate: registry init hung for over 5 minutes in my testing on the Xenova/ONNX fetch path, and retrying that on every write would be worse than failing fast. That trade-off is yours to make.

## Environment

`ruflo@3.32.30` (global), macOS arm64, Node 22.17.0. Verified against `main` @ `314ad1eb0`.

title: fix(memory): migrate ADR-323 provenance_type on the bridge path, and stop the swallowed error surfacing as a WAL refusal
body:
Fixes #2843.

## Summary

Bridge writes were silently lost on any install whose `agentdb-memory.db` predates ADR-323. This adds the missing column migration, and makes the class of failure that hid it visible.

**Note:** the issue's original root-cause analysis was wrong and has been [corrected](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2843#issuecomment-5118112879). This PR carries the actual fix.

## The defect

ADR-323 added `provenance_type` to `bridgeStoreEntry()`'s INSERT. `ensureSchemaColumns()` backfills it on the sql.js path; the bridge path only ran `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` — a no-op on an existing table. So on a pre-ADR-323 database every bridge write throws:

```
SqliteError: table memory_entries has no column named provenance_type
```

`bridgeStoreEntry()`'s catch returns null for anything that is not a UNIQUE violation, discarding the error. The caller demotes to the sql.js whole-image path, which refuses on WAL sidecars and reports "active native WAL connection … restore the native better-sqlite3 bridge" — a cause with nothing to do with the failure. better-sqlite3 was healthy throughout.

Measured on the affected install:

| database | has `provenance_type` |
|---|---|
| `.swarm/memory.db` (sql.js path) | **yes** |
| `.swarm/agentdb-memory.db` (bridge path, #2786) | **no** |

Adding the column with **no code change** turned `bridgeStoreEntry` from `null` into `{success: true, embedding: {dimensions: 384}}`, and MCP `memory_store` from failing to `stored: true` in 21 ms, with no restart.

The comment above that catch already anticipates this exact failure — *"so the caller never demotes to sql.js and never triggers the #2735 whole-image guard with a misleading 'active native WAL connection' error"* — but only handles UNIQUE.

## Commits

**1. `fix(memory): migrate provenance_type on the bridge path`** — the fix.

- `provenance_type` in the CREATE TABLE DDL (fresh databases) plus an idempotent `ALTER` (pre-existing ones). SQLite has no `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, so attempt-and-ignore is the idiom.
- Schema block extracted as exported `ensureBridgeSchema()`. The bug was untestable in place — the failure it causes is swallowed and resurfaces as an unrelated message, so nothing end-to-end could have caught it.
- `bridgeStoreEntry`'s catch records the swallowed error; `getBridgeFailureReason()` is no longer gated on `bridgeAvailable === false`, because a bridge that initialised fine can still fail every write — which is exactly this bug.

**2. `fix(memory): make a latched bridge-init failure diagnosable and recoverable`** — why it stayed invisible.

- `getRegistry()`'s bare `catch {}` discarded the init error and latched for the process lifetime.
- `shutdownBridge()` reset only inside `if (registryInstance)` — null in exactly the failed-init case, so the one function that could clear the latch could not run in the state that set it.
- The init log suppressor filtered `better-sqlite3` and `[AgentDB]`, swallowing AgentDB's own "better-sqlite3 not available, using sql.js WASM" line. Extracted as `shouldSuppressInitLog()`.
- The WAL refusal literal existed in three copies that had already drifted (`write` vs `read/write`); now one `walRefusalError()` helper that appends `Bridge unavailable: <reason>`.

## Deliberately unchanged

- **The latch itself.** A cooldown retry would be friendlier, but registry init hung >5 minutes on the Xenova/ONNX path during testing; retrying that per-write could be worse than failing fast. Open question in #2843.
- **`backend: 'sql.js + HNSW'`** — a hardcoded literal at five sites in `mcp-tools/memory-tools.js`, not a live probe. It reports sql.js regardless of the real driver and actively misled me during diagnosis, but correcting it is a reporting change with its own blast radius.

## ADR status

ADR-053 (**Implemented**, 2026-02-25) documents the sql.js fallback as intentional; unchanged by this — the fallback still exists and degrades the same way, it is now observable. ADR-323 (provenance) is **completed** by this rather than altered: it specified the column, and this makes the bridge path actually carry it. No ADR text needed updating.

## Verification

- 5 migration tests green; **3 of 5 fail with the exact production error** when the `ALTER` is removed.
- 9 diagnostics tests green; 7 fail against pristine `src`.
- End-to-end on a real 41 MB database: `bridgeStoreEntry` → `success: true`, 384-dim embedding.
- Combined affected suites: **11 failed / 28 passed**, versus **11 failed / 14 passed** on pristine for the same pre-existing files — same 11 failures, 14 of the passes are new. No regressions.
- `tsc --noEmit`: **437 on this branch, 437 on pristine `main`**. The single error in a touched file is the pre-existing `Cannot find module '@claude-flow/memory'`, which only moved line number.

## Operator remedy while this is unreleased

```sql
ALTER TABLE memory_entries ADD COLUMN provenance_type TEXT DEFAULT 'unknown';
```

on `.swarm/agentdb-memory.db`. Verified: fixes writes immediately, no restart, no reinstall.

🤖 Generated with Ruflo & AQE

title: mcp-bridge image runs node:20-slim, end-of-life since 2026-04-30
body:
Hello, and thank you for this project.

The image built by `ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/Dockerfile` runs on a base that no longer receives security fixes, and I thought it worth flagging.

## What I observed

`ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/Dockerfile` is single-stage:

```
 1:  FROM node:20-slim
28:  EXPOSE 3001
45:  CMD ["node", "index.js"]
```

The base of the **final stage** is what becomes the image, so this is what ships — not a builder stage that gets discarded. I checked that specifically; several other candidates I looked at today turned out to use an old base only in a `build` stage whose final image was nginx or distroless, and I set those aside.

**`node:20-slim` is on a line that reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30.**
Supported Node lines today are 22, 24 and 26.

## What end-of-life means here

Node.js states the consequence in its own security-release notes:

> "It's important to note that **End-of-Life versions are always affected** when a security release occurs."

The June 2026 release fixed **twelve CVEs** into 22.x, 24.x and 26.x, with older lines excluded:

| CVE | Severity | |
|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-48933 | **HIGH** | WebCrypto AES integer overflow → remote process abort (DoS) |
| CVE-2026-48618 | **HIGH** | Unicode dot separator → TLS wildcard-depth authentication bypass |
| CVE-2026-48934 | Medium | TLS host identity verification bypass via session reuse |
| CVE-2026-48928 | Medium | Uppercase SNI matching → mTLS authorization bypass |
| CVE-2026-48615 | Medium | Proxy credentials leaked in `ERR_PROXY_TUNNEL` error message |

The July 2026 release, published this week, again patched only 26.x/24.x/22.x, with *"the highest severity issue fixed in this release is HIGH."*

## Why nothing would have told you

The tag keeps resolving perfectly well — it simply stops being fixed, and nothing announces that. Dependabot's `docker` ecosystem is documented as supporting *version* updates but **not security updates**, so a base going end-of-life produces no alert at all.

## What I did NOT check

- I did not pull or scan the published image; this is an analysis of the Dockerfile that builds it.
- I did not determine which of those CVEs are reachable in your usage, and I'm **not** claiming any is exploitable here. The narrower claim is that an end-of-life runtime ships and structurally cannot receive these fixes.
- The base distribution's own package set was not assessed separately.

## Suggestion

Moving to a currently-supported line would put it back on a patched runtime. Happy to open the PR if that's useful.

*Disclosure: AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5). I verified the Dockerfile stages, the EOL dates from endoflife.date, and the CVE lists from the upstream projects myself before posting.*

title: chore(release): Ruflo v3.32.35
body:
# Ruflo v3.32.35: Adaptive Swarms and Safer Learning Loops

Ruflo v3.32.35 gives long-running agent teams a controlled way to learn which
workers should receive future tasks. The new `pheromone-adaptive` topology
combines outcome, latency, and consensus signals while preserving protected
roles, a minimum active quorum, and existing permissions. It begins in dry-run
mode so teams can inspect its decisions before enabling scheduling changes.

This release also makes the surrounding learning loop more trustworthy:
project flywheels must evaluate against a project-local, hash-pinned benchmark;
learned routing updates inside a live MCP process; AgentDB deletes and upserts
remove stale vectors; and daemon auto-start is limited to actual Ruflo
projects.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
npm install --global ruflo@3.32.35
ruflo doctor
```

Existing installations remain compatible. The default topology is still
`hierarchical`, old swarm state remains readable, historical flywheel receipts
remain verifiable, and the new adaptive scheduler is opt-in.

## Try adaptive swarm scheduling

Start in the default calibration mode:

```bash
ruflo swarm init \
  --topology pheromone-adaptive \
  --max-agents 8

ruflo swarm pheromone
ruflo agent metrics --format json
```

When the observations look right, explicitly enable scheduling enforcement:

```bash
ruflo swarm init \
  --topology pheromone-adaptive \
  --max-agents 8 \
  --apsc-live
```

Live mode changes Ruflo dispatch eligibility only. It does not terminate
agents, revoke access, discard context, or widen permissions.

## Use a project-local flywheel anchor

Create `.claude/eval/flywheel-anchor.manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "ruflo.flywheel-anchor-manifest/v1",
  "path": "my-project-anchor.json",
  "sha256": "sha256:<canonical-task-hash>"
}
```

The referenced anchor contains at least four labelled tasks. Ruflo binds its
canonical hash into new evaluation receipts. A non-Ruflo repository without a
project anchor now fails closed instead of silently optimizing against Ruflo's
built-in development benchmark.

## What changed

- Adds the opt-in `pheromone-adaptive` swarm topology with role-aware EMA
  scoring, dry-run calibration, protected roles, quorum floors, bounded
  exploration, atomic cross-process updates, CLI inspection, and MCP tools.
- Connects `hooks post-task` outcomes to adaptive scheduling and exposes each
  agent's score, sample count, role, and eligibility through `agent metrics`.
- Adds hash-pinned, project-local flywheel evaluation anchors and receipt
  binding while retaining historical receipt verification.
- Makes learned routing use supported, discriminative evidence and immediately
  invalidates a warm router after labelled outcomes.
- Makes AgentDB logical-key upserts, deletes, and cleanup reconcile every stale
  vector and report accurate lifecycle metrics.
- Limits daemon auto-start to projects containing `.claude-flow/`, reports the
  first start, and applies a 30-minute abandoned-daemon idle timeout.

## Measured benchmark

On the declared synthetic benchmark (12 agents, 20,000 updates), adaptive
scheduling produced:

- 33.3% active-agent reduction;
- +0.2617 admitted mean score;
- 0.0066 ms update p95 in the release validation run;
- preserved quorum and protected-role invariants.

These are Ruflo benchmark results for that workload, not a universal production
performance claim.

## Validation

- TypeScript builds passed for `@claude-flow/shared`, `@claude-flow/swarm`, and
  `@claude-flow/cli`.
- The changed-surface suite passed 93 tests across nine files.
- Twenty concurrent outcome writers persisted all twenty rounds with no
  residual lock.
- Built CLI smoke tests covered initialization, automatic post-task learning,
  status, manual updates, and JSON metrics.
- CI/CD, V3 CI/CD, CodeQL, cross-agent integration, CVE audit, and verification
  workflows passed on the merged commit.

This release ships [#2848](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/pull/2848) and
resolves
[#2815](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2815),
[#2819](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2819),
[#2832](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2832),
[#2834](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2834),
[#2839](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2839), and
[#2840](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2840).

title: macOS: daemon memory gate uses os.freemem(), deferring ~70% of workers and causing a KeepAlive restart loop
body:
## Summary

On macOS the daemon's memory gate reads `os.freemem()`, which on Darwin counts only
genuinely-free pages and excludes reclaimable inactive memory. The result is a `freePercent`
of well under 1% on a healthy, idle machine, so the gate defers almost every worker — and the
resulting lack of worker activity then trips the idle self-shutdown, which launchd `KeepAlive`
immediately restarts, producing a restart loop.

## Environment

- macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), 32 GB RAM, Node v26.1.0
- `ruflo` installed globally; daemon run via a launchd agent as
  `daemon start --foreground --quiet --ttl 0` (no `--headless`)

## The measurement

```
os.freemem():     0.15 GB  ->  0.5% of 32 GB   <-- what the gate uses
memory_pressure:  51% free
vm_stat:          518882 inactive pages = 7.92 GB reclaimable, invisible to os.freemem()
```

`canRunWorker()` computes `freePercent = (os.freemem() / os.totalmem()) * 100` and compares it
against `resourceThresholds.minFreeMemoryPercent`. The Darwin default is `5`
(`const defaultMinFreeMemory = process.platform === 'darwin' ? 5 : 10;`), which is unreachable
in normal macOS operation because inactive pages are never counted as free.

## Impact

Over 24 hours on one machine:

```
completed: 270
deferred:  622
   610 deferred: Memory too low
    12 deferred: CPU load too high
```

Secondary effect — a restart loop:

```
[09:45:57] Daemon started (PID: 42253, ..., minFreeMemoryPercent: 1%)
[09:45:57] Worker map deferred: Memory too low: 0.5% free
[09:46:57] Daemon self-shutdown: idle for 1800s (no worker activity)
[09:46:58] Daemon started (PID: 42645, ...)
```

The idle detector fires ~60 s after start because deferred workers register no activity;
`KeepAlive` then relaunches. Observed 9 restarts in ~10 minutes.

Lowering `minFreeMemoryPercent` to `1` does not help — 0.5% is still below it. Any positive
floor is unreachable while this metric is used.

## Suggested fix

On Darwin, derive available memory from `vm_stat` (`free + inactive + purgeable + speculative`)
or from `memory_pressure`, rather than `os.freemem()`. Linux `os.freemem()` has a similar but
much less severe skew versus `MemAvailable`.

## Possibly related — NOT confirmed

While investigating I could not get `.claude-flow/config.yaml` to affect the daemon at all:
across three `launchctl kickstart` restarts the startup line kept reporting the previous
threshold, and neither `Daemon config loaded from` nor `yaml parser unavailable` appears
anywhere in a log spanning 2026-06-16 to now, despite the daemon's cwd being the project root.
I note `@claude-flow/cli` is `"type": "module"`, so the `require('yaml')` inside
`readDaemonConfigFromFile` cannot resolve under ESM — but that path would emit the warning, and
it does not. I could not determine where the live values originate, so I am flagging this as an
observation rather than a diagnosis; happy to open it separately if useful.

title: system_status.uptimeFormatted returns wrong value (unit mismatch); system_health swarm/database checks always report unknown
body:
**Bug 1: uptimeFormatted unit mismatch**
system_status returns uptime in seconds, but uptimeFormatted appears to divide it as if it were milliseconds, producing values ~1000x too small.

title: x_federation_sync has no ordered cursor
body:
`x_federation_sync` takes a time window and returns events without a monotonic cursor. Events with equal or skewed `created_at` can be missed or returned twice across calls. A consumer that needs a gap-free, ordered log cannot build one on top of it.

**Proposal:** return an opaque, monotonic cursor (in relay receive order) and accept `since_cursor`.

**Acceptance:** a test interleaves events with identical `created_at` and checks that repeated sync calls return each event exactly once.

**Finding**: `CacheManager` (`v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/cache-manager.ts`) implements pure LRU+TTL eviction with zero importance/frequency signal, even though `CachedEntry.accessCount`/`lastAccessedAt` are already tracked on every entry. HTM-EAR (arXiv:2603.10032, Feb 2026) shows this exact policy permanently drops high-value "essential" entries under skewed access (2,416 of 15K facts on a BGL-log benchmark, MRR 0.069 vs 0.336 for an importance-aware policy). `CacheManager.evictLRU()` is genuinely reachable in production — `AgentDBAdapter`'s main cache, any `TieredCacheManager` L1, and `ControllerRegistry`'s `tieredCache` controller all route through it.

5 candidates were generated and scored (0.25·fit + 0.20·testability + 0.20·measurability + 0.15·production_value + 0.10·novelty + 0.10·reviewability):
| Candidate | Score |
|---|---|

| `CacheManager.clear()`'s `previousSize` always 0 (read after `cache.clear()`) | 3.60 |

| `@claude-flow/plugins` `ResourceLimits` dead config (`maxCPUPercent`/`maxFileSize`/`maxOpenFiles` never read) | 3.35 |

## 5. Hypothesis

> Given a `CacheManager` under size/memory pressure with a skewed access pattern (an entry accessed many times historically but not most-recently, sitting near the LRU tail while rarely-touched entries occupy more recent positions), when eviction is extended with an opt-in, continuous `frequencyWeight` (0-1, default 0) blending recency-rank with normalized `accessCount` over a bounded scan window (`evictionScanWindow`, default 32) — falling back to the exact original tail-eviction when `frequencyWeight` is 0/unset — then a high-access-count entry should survive eviction under `frequencyWeight>0` where pure LRU would evict it, subject to: byte-identical default behavior, zero change to TTL/`maxMemory` accounting, deterministic $0 Vitest evaluation.

title: fix(x-gateway): single-use invites, invite revoke, ordered federation_sync cursor (#5029, #5030)
body:
## Summary

Two x.ruv.io gateway fixes (`plugins/ruflo-x-gateway`), plus the CLI passthroughs.

### #5029: invites are single use, and can be revoked once the relay supports it

- `mintInvite` and `federation_invite_mint` now default to `max_uses: 1` (it was 25). `maxUses` and `ttlSecs` must be positive integers.
- New tool `federation_invite_revoke`. It is admin-token only and exists on the legacy `/mcp` surface only. It revokes an invite by `code` or `id`.
- **Where admission is decided.** The gateway holds no admission store. Claims are decided by buzz-relay's `POST /api/invites/claim`, which lives outside this repo. Upstream block/buzz added `POST /api/invites/revoke` and `GET /api/invites` in block/buzz#9680 (commit 792a9ce563, 2026-11-20). In the same upstream code, the claim path refuses a revoked row (`revoked_at`) and an exhausted row (`use_count >= max_uses`), under its `FOR UPDATE` row lock.
- **The deployed relay does not have the route yet.** Today relay.ruv.io answers `POST /api/invites/revoke` with a bare 404, the same as a path that does not exist. It also answers 405 to `GET /api/invites`. The tool reports that case as "the relay does not support invite revocation yet". It reports the route's own JSON `invite_not_found` separately.
- So the tool does nothing until the relay is upgraded. The default-1 change takes effect as soon as the gateway is deployed.
- The tool is withheld from `/chatgpt/mcp` and `/claude/mcp` because it accepts an invite code (a bearer secret), the same reason `federation_invite_mint` is withheld. `claude-directory-submission.json` `operator_tools_excluded` is updated.
- Mint returns no invite id, and there is no list tool, so in practice you revoke by code.
- CLI: `x_federation_invite_revoke` passes through to the gateway, and the mint `maxUses` and `--uses` text now says the default is 1.

### #5030: `federation_sync` cursor

- Every result carries `next_cursor`. Passing it back as `since_cursor` returns every later message exactly once, oldest first by `(created_at, id)`.
- **This is not relay receive order.** buzz-relay stores `received_at` but exposes no receive-order sequence over NIP-01. The cursor therefore holds:
  - a window floor, which trails the read time by 300 s;
  - 48-bit prefixes of the ids already delivered inside that window, grouped by second, with the seconds delta-coded.
  - It is versioned base64url and carries all state, because the gateway is stateless and runs on several instances.
- **What it guarantees.** Events that share a second are each delivered once. An event that reaches the relay up to 300 s after its own `created_at` is delivered once. An event older than that falls outside the window and is not delivered; this limit is documented.
- **Completeness is judged on the raw relay page.** buzz-relay applies `limit` in SQL (newest first) before it matches `#t`/`#k` in Rust (`handlers/req.rs`, `filter_fully_pushable`). A short `#t`-filtered page therefore proves nothing. Cursor reads send only `kinds`/`since`/`until`/`limit` and match the swarm tag and type locally. A page that comes back full is narrowed by bisecting `until` until the window `[lo, until]` comes back short. That window is then complete, so a backlog drains with no gap.
- **A timed-out read** delivers nothing and returns the same cursor.
- **The cursor is treated as hostile input.** Its length is capped (64 KiB), its shape is decoded strictly, its lookback is clamped to 30 days, and it is bound to the `type` filter it was issued for. Error messages never echo the cursor.
- **Without a cursor**, the read is unchanged: the same single REQ, filter and order as before. Its `next_cursor` keeps the whole requested window, because that read cannot prove it saw everything.
- CLI: `since_cursor` is added to the `x_federation_sync` input schema, and `ruflo federation sync --cursor` is added.

### Versions

The gateway package goes from 0.9.2 to 0.10.0 and the plugin from 0.10.6 to 0.11.0, with a CHANGELOG entry. The CLI version is not bumped.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd plugins/ruflo-x-gateway && npm test`: 157/157 pass. New suites:
  - `test/sync-cursor.test.mjs` (11 tests):
    - same-second events interleaved with calls;
    - a late arrival inside the overlap window;
    - a 1,200-event backlog with 1,500 non-swarm notes, drained at `limit: 45`;
    - type binding, and any accepted type string round-tripping;
    - the worst-case cursor size;
    - hostile cursors;
    - a future-dated event;
    - a timeout returning the same cursor;
    - `fetchCovering` bisection and saturation.
    - The fake relay applies NIP-01 `limit` newest-first and before tag matching, as buzz-relay does.
    - Mutation-checked: removing the delivered-id dedupe fails 4 tests, and judging completeness on the filtered count fails the backlog test.
  - `test/invite-admin.test.mjs` (4 tests):
    - mint defaults to 1 and honours an explicit value;
    - revoke signs NIP-98 with a payload tag, by code or id;
    - revoke requires the admin token, and malformed selectors never reach the relay;
    - a route-less 404 reads "unsupported", distinct from `invite_not_found` and from a 403;
    - the code is never echoed.
- [x] `cd v3/@claude-flow/cli && npx vitest run __tests__/x-federation-tools.test.ts __tests__/mcp-service-url-security.test.ts`: 59/59 pass, including new `since_cursor` and `invite_revoke` passthrough cases.
- [x] `scripts/audit-plugin-version-bump.mjs --base origin/main`, `check-plugin-manifests`, `audit-plugin-secrets`, `audit-cli-mcp-tools`, `audit-tool-descriptions` and `check-guard-tool-names` all pass.
- [ ] Not tested: the `#5029` acceptance tests (a revoked invite and a used-up invite each refused at claim). Claim is decided in buzz-relay, not in this repo, so those tests cannot live here. Upstream covers them in `crates/buzz-db/src/store/relay_invite/revocation_postgres_tests.rs` and `crates/buzz-db/src/store/relay_invite/manage_postgres_tests.rs`.
- [ ] Not run: `plugins/ruflo-x-gateway/tests/*.ts` (the mod runner; the hooks did not change).

## Notes for review

- The `federation_sync` description and input schema changed on the directory profiles (`/chatgpt/mcp` and `/claude/mcp`), which are reviewed surfaces. The tool count is unchanged at 12.
- One anonymous cursor call can open up to 24 authenticated relay connections, one per bisection round, and reads non-swarm kind-1 traffic in that window. The per-IP MCP rate limit still applies.
- Nothing ships until the owner deploys:
  - **default-1 invites and the cursor:** a gateway deploy;
  - **revoke:** a buzz-relay upgrade to a build that includes block/buzz#9680;
  - **CLI passthroughs:** a CLI release.
- This PR deploys nothing.

Fixes #5030
Refs #5029: fully fixed once relay.ruv.io runs a buzz-relay build with `POST /api/invites/revoke`.

title: fix(security): daily scan 2026-11-21 — 1 fix
body:
<!-- ruflo-daily-security -->

Automated daily security scan for 2026-11-21, with one fix and its test.

## Fix 1: agentbbs federation signatures did not cover all stored content

- **Class:** incomplete signature coverage / canonicalization mismatch (CWE-347), via a `__proto__` key
- **Severity:** high
- **Source:** agentic review of code changed in the last 7 days (`agentbbs-federation.ts`, touched by #5052)
- **File:** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/mcp-tools/agentbbs-federation.ts`

**Impact.** The module's guarantee is that a peer cannot forge or alter another node's envelopes. That guarantee had two gaps:
- `canonicalEnvelopeBytes` built the signed bytes by assigning payload keys to a plain object. An own `__proto__` key in a parsed payload set the object's prototype instead, so the key and everything under it were left out of the signed bytes. Verification still passed.
- `mergeEnvelopes` stored the incoming envelope as received, so extra top-level fields that the signature does not cover were saved too.

Together, a pinned peer relaying another node's genuine envelope could add unsigned content. Room reads and the federation endpoint then served that content as if the original node had signed it.

**What changed:**
- `canonicalEnvelopeBytes` refuses any payload object that has a `__proto__` key. `verifyEnvelope` then returns false and `signEnvelope` throws. Envelopes without such a key produce the same bytes as before, so existing signatures are unaffected.
- `mergeEnvelopes` now stores only the signed fields, plus `signature` and the incremented `hops`.

**Test added:** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/agentbbs-federation-signed-coverage.test.ts`. All 5 cases fail on `main` and pass with the fix. It covers:
- a top-level or nested payload `__proto__` key added in transit is refused;
- signing such a payload is refused;
- merge skips the altered envelope;
- merge drops unsigned top-level fields, and the stored envelope still verifies.

**Release note:** this is CLI source, so it ships with the train. No standalone publish is needed.

## Validation

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx vitest run` on all 5 `__tests__/agentbbs-*.test.ts` files | 72 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed |
| `cd v3/@claude-flow/cli && npx tsc --noEmit` | 4 errors, all TS6305 because `@claude-flow/swarm` dist is not built. Same output on clean `main`; none in touched files |
| `npm run build` (root) | Fails with the same 422 TS errors on clean `main` (in `v3/src/**` and `v3/swarm.config.ts`); none in touched files |
| `npx @claude-flow/cli@latest security scan --type code --depth deep` | Same 411 findings before and after; no new findings |
| `audit-umbrella-version-lockstep.mjs` | Not run: no `package.json` changed |

The root build and CLI `tsc` failures exist on `main` already and are not addressed here.

title: fix(hooks): redact Google, Cognitum and header/query-string keys in recorded commands
body:
## Summary

`redactCommandForStorage` (#4056) stores several common credential shapes verbatim in `commands/cmd-*` rows. This PR redacts them, and stops two existing rules from redacting things that are not secrets:

| Shape | Example (fake) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google API key `AIza` + 35 | `…/accounts:signUp?key=AIza…` | stored | `[redacted]` |
| Cognitum API key `cog_` + 64 hex | `x-api-key: cog_…`, `prefix_cog_…` | stored | `[redacted]` (identifiers like `cog_SomeMetric` left alone) |
| Header-carried keys | `x-api-key`, `X-Goog-Api-Key`, `x-auth-token`, `x-auth-key`, `x-access-token`, `apikey`, `api-key`, `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`, `Private-Token`, with optional `Bearer`/`Basic`/`token` scheme | stored | value redacted, header name kept; a `:` is required |
| Quoted header / object-literal values | `{headers:{"x-api-key":"…"}}`, `{"Authorization":"Bearer …"}`, `{"api_key":"…"}`, `{"apiKey":"…"}`, `params={'key': '…'}` | stored | value redacted |
| Query-string credentials | `?key=`, `&api_key=`, `?access_token=` | partly (`*_TOKEN=` only) | value redacted, rest of URL kept exactly |
| Form bodies | `-d key=…`, `-d "api_key=…"`, `--data-urlencode "key=…"`, `apikey=…` | stored | value redacted |
| Pagination cursor `?token=…` | `?token=nextpage123` | redacted | kept (not a credential) |
| `grep -rn x-api-key src` | | `src` redacted by the flag rule | unchanged |

## Why now

The store is local, but its rows are long-lived and get copied into the daily `.swarm/backups`. A credential the redactor misses stays in plain text in every copy until someone purges it. All of these shapes are common in commands agents run: Firebase `?key=` calls, Gemini keys, `x-api-key` headers, and inline `fetch` / `requests` calls.

## Changes

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/command-recording.ts`:
  - The Authorization and header rules take an optional quote before the value. The header rule has a wider name list and an optional scheme. It still requires `:`.
  - A new object-literal rule for `api[-_]?key|apiKey|x-api-key|x-goog-api-key|access[-_]?token|auth[-_]?token`. It also matches a bare `key` when the key name is quoted.
  - The query-string rule no longer matches bare `token`. It still matches bare `key`, deliberately, because Google and Firebase keys travel as `?key=`. A test pins that trade-off.
  - Two form-body rules: `api_key=` / `apikey=` / `api-key=` after whitespace or a quote, and bare `key=` only after `-d` / `--data*`.
  - The flag rule (`--api-key`, `--token`, …) now needs a non-word, non-dash character before its dash. Before, it fired inside header names: `x-api-key :v` lost its colon, and `grep -rn x-api-key src` had `src` redacted.
  - `cog_` is matched as `cog_` + 64 lowercase hex, using hex lookarounds instead of `\b`.
  - Every pattern is bounded like the existing rules.
- `__tests__/command-recording-4056.test.ts`:
  - 26 new redaction cases, plus negative tests that assert exact output with `toBe`: `?sort_key=`, `?token=nextpage123`, `grep -rn x-api-key src`, `grep -r cog_RegistryEntriesTotalCountMetric src`, and an ordinary `?limit=5&page=2` URL.
  - Exact-output tests for `?limit=5&api_key=…&page=2`, for bare `?key=`, for the spaced-colon header, and for `--api-key`.
  - The `cog_` fixture is now 64 hex. The hostile-input test covers the new prefixes as well (`cog_`, `{"api_key":"`, `'key': '`, `-d key=`, `--data-urlencode`, `Private-Token: `, `x-access-token: token `, …).

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run __tests__/command-recording-4056.test.ts`: **62 passed**.
- Negative control, the same tests against `origin/main` source: **29 failed, 33 passed**. Against this PR's first commit: **22 failed, 40 passed**. The tests that pass before the fix are regression guards (unchanged URLs, `?key=`, `--api-key`) and earlier cases.
- `git diff origin/main | gitleaks stdin`: no leaks found. Fixtures are fake, built by concatenation, and use `wget` / `http` / `node` rather than the `curl -H "…key:` form that gitleaks' `curl-auth-header` rule matches across lines.
- `tsc` reports no errors in `command-recording.ts`. The full CLI suite was not re-run, because the change is confined to the RULES table and its tests.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- URL-encoded separators (`key%3D…`) and shell-concatenated quotes (`"api_"'key=…'`) are not handled.
- Env-style names that do not end in a known suffix (`GOOGLE_KEY=…`) are not redacted.
- Sibling redactors have their own, narrower patterns and could share these rules:
  - `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/managed-run-collector.ts:39`
  - `.claude/helpers/intelligence.cjs:685`
  - `v3/@claude-flow/codex/src/activity/sanitize.ts:13`
  - `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/security/builtin-aidefence.ts:72`

## Notes

- `cog_` is the Cognitum API key prefix (api.cognitum.one). It is included because ruflo talks to that API (meta-llm, iot-cognitum), and recorded calls to it carry the key.
- Fork PR from a first-time-style contributor path, so CI may need a maintainer approval to run.
