title: fix(agentbbs): refuse symlinked state files
body:
## Problem

`.agentbbs` is the default project-local state directory, and it is not in `.gitignore`. A cloned repository can therefore ship `node-identity.json`, `peers.json`, `rooms.json`, or a `room-*.jsonl` entry as a symlink.

The AgentBBS read/write paths used path-following APIs (`readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`, `appendFileSync`), so a committed symlink could make:

- `federation_bbs_peer_add` / `federation_bbs_register` / `federation_bbs_publish` / `federation_bbs_sync` create or overwrite a file outside the project;
- `federation_bbs_watch` or `federation_bbs_serve` read a file outside the project;
- a dangling `node-identity.json` symlink make `getNodeIdentity()` create the symlink's target;
- a crash during `writePeers()` leave a truncated `peers.json`, which `readPeers()` treats as an empty, unpinned peer list.

This is the same class as #4746 (`.claude-flow` writes through symlinks), but a separate `.agentbbs` surface.

## Change

- Add `ensureAgentbbsDir()`: the base path must be a real directory; a symlink or non-directory is refused.
- Add `assertRegularStateFile()`: `lstat` the target and refuse a symlink or special file; a missing path is allowed.
- Apply it to `node-identity.json`, `peers.json`, `rooms.json` and every room log before read/write.
- `getNodeIdentity()` creates with `flag: 'wx'`, so a dangling symlink is refused rather than followed; an `EEXIST` race re-reads and validates the winner.
- `writePeers()` writes a temp sibling and renames it into place, so a crash cannot leave a truncated peer registry. The temp file is created with `wx`.
- `agentbbs-tools.ts` reuses the helpers before `nextSeq()`, `readEnvelopes()`, the `rooms.json` read/write, and both append sites.

Normal regular files and missing state paths behave exactly as before. A user who intentionally symlinked `.agentbbs` or one of its files must use the real path; the new behavior is fail-closed.

## Verification

Linux container, real symlinks in temp dirs:

- Four federation regression cases (`peers.json`, dangling `node-identity.json`, room log, symlinked base path) **fail against the pre-change source**:
  - `addPeer` overwrote the symlink target;
  - `getNodeIdentity` created the dangling target;
  - `mergeEnvelopes` appended to the victim room log;
  - a symlinked base path was accepted.
- The same four cases pass with this change.
- The `nextSeq()` symlink case passes with this change.

Local Windows:

- `agentbbs-federation` + `agentbbs-tools` targeted run: 63 passed, 9 skipped, 1 pre-existing failure (`stat.mode === 0o600`, Windows returns `0o666`; this suite runs on Ubuntu in `Test V3 Packages` and `Test Suite`).
- The symlink cases are `skipIf(win32)` because Windows requires a privilege for `symlinkSync`; Linux CI exercises them.
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` reports no errors in the changed files.

## Compatibility / scope

- No change to envelope signatures, peer pinning, origin checks, size/hop bounds, or the sync cursor protocol.
- State files are now `0600` when created by the atomic writers; existing regular files keep their content and mode unless rewritten.
- A symlinked state file now fails closed with a clear error instead of silently reading or writing outside the project.

title: fix(daemon): gate workers on available memory on macOS (#2935)
body:
This PR fixes [issue #2935](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2935).

## Why

On macOS, `os.freemem()` excludes reclaimable inactive memory. The daemon therefore sees far less usable memory than the system actually has, defers most workers, and can enter an idle-shutdown/launchd `KeepAlive` restart loop. PR #3000 fixed the separate stale-state restoration path, but the Darwin memory measurement is still wrong.

## What changed

- Added `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/available-memory.ts`, which measures Darwin available memory with `/usr/bin/vm_stat` as free + speculative + inactive pages using the reported page size. It clamps the result to total memory, caches readings for five seconds, coalesces concurrent probes, and falls back to `os.freemem()` if the one-second probe fails. Non-Darwin platforms continue to use `os.freemem()`.
- Updated `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/worker-daemon.ts` to use the available-memory reader for the worker gate and log fallback or invalid-measurement diagnostics once per daemon.
- Added parser, fallback, caching, concurrency, logging, boundary, and daemon-gate coverage in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/services/available-memory-2935.test.ts` and `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/services/worker-daemon-darwin-gate-2935.test.ts`.

## Tests

- GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`: the full base run passed 12,946 test occurrences with 0 failures, and the full candidate run passed 12,987 test occurrences with 0 failures, including 41 new tests.
- GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`, `macos-15`, and `windows-2022`: the focused daemon/configuration suites passed with 0 failures.
- GitHub-hosted `macos-15`: the Darwin probe reported `vm_stat` as the measurement source. GitHub-hosted `windows-2022`: the probe reported `os.freemem()`.
- Node 20 build, typecheck, and pack checks passed.

Fixes #2935

title: sql.js fallback at 3.56.1: memory_search and memory_search_unified still write store files (lock, hnsw.index, ruvector.db)
body:
Follow-up to #4570. Thanks for #3918. It works: on a current-schema store, the sql.js fallback no longer rewrites `memory.db` on every call. We re-measured on `@claude-flow/cli` 3.56.1 and found that the fallback search and list paths still write other store files. So for an operator who wants to grant these tools as read-only, they still aren't.

## What we ran

Each call ran in a fresh MCP server process (`mcp start`) on a copy of a test store. We traced it with `strace -f` and compared file and SQLite snapshots taken before and after the call. The fallback was forced three ways:

- **A:** `CLAUDE_FLOW_DISABLE_BRIDGE=1`, so `getBridge()` is unavailable.
- **B:** `bridgeSearchEntries()` returns `null`.
- **C:** `bridgeListEntries()` returns `null` (`memory_search_unified` only).

We ran each over five store shapes, four HNSW states (no index, empty, warm, stale), and with and without another connection holding `-wal`/`-shm` open. That came to 160 cells for `memory_search` and 120 for `memory_search_unified`.

## What we found

Every cell wrote at least one store file:

| Forcing | Writes seen in every cell |
|---|---|
| A (bridge disabled) | `.swarm/memory.db.lock` created (`O_CREAT\|O_EXCL`), written and unlinked by `withMemoryDbLock` in `ensureSchemaColumns`. `.swarm/hnsw.index` written (`pwrite64`), and created when absent |
| B (`bridgeSearchEntries` → null) | the same lock, plus `ruvector.db` modified |
| C, no other connection | the same lock, plus `ruvector.db` modified |
| C, sidecars held by another connection | no lock (the WAL guard refuses first, as the source suggests), but `ruvector.db` is still modified |

On stores with an older `memory_entries` schema (missing `status` / `provenance_type`), the calls also rewrite `memory_entries` rows. That happens under A and B with or without a held connection, and under C without one.

We saw no network activity from any of these calls.

## Ask

Make the search and list fallbacks fail closed before any write. Concretely: take no `memory.db.lock`, never create or write `hnsw.index` or `ruvector.db`, and never run schema changes or backfills. If they can't serve the call read-only, they should return an error.

The 3.42.4 → 3.56.1 diff suggests `withMemoryDbLock` and `getHNSWIndex` on this path are unchanged since #4570. We can share traces for any single cell if that helps.

title: SqlJsRvfBackend misreads Redb .ruvector stores as SQLite
body:
## Context

When multiple MCP stdio clients start against the same storage root, the first process holds a live SQLite WAL. A later `AgentDB.initializeDatabase()` call falls back to `SqlJsRvfBackend`, but that fallback tries to read the `.ruvector` file as SQLite even when the file is a valid Redb database.

This produces `file is not a database` and breaks `memory_store` even though the `.ruvector` file itself is valid.

## Observed evidence

- `agentdb-memory.db` is a valid SQLite database; `PRAGMA integrity_check` returns `ok`.
- `agentdb-memory.db.ruvector` has the Redb magic bytes `726564621a0aa90d`.
- Native `VectorDb` from `ruvector` opens the same `.ruvector` file successfully and returns `len()=0`.
- sql.js cannot open the same file because it is not SQLite.

## Proposed fix

Before using `SqlJsRvfBackend` on a `.ruvector` path, sniff the file magic bytes.

1. If the magic matches Redb, treat the file as a native Redb vector store or choose another `storagePath`.
2. Do not pass a Redb file to the SQLite/sql.js fallback.
3. Log which backend path was selected.
4. Keep the behavior explicit enough that a future RVF migration can replace the fallback cleanly.

## Related

- `ruvnet/ruflo#3143` — memory bridge ignores later explicit `dbPath` values.
- `ruvnet/ruflo#1242` — replacing sql.js with RVF is the long-term direction.

## Why now

We reproduced this on a real host while validating a single-owner MCP HTTP deployment. WAL checkpointing and one-owner HTTP fixed the immediate symptom, but the fallback remains fragile for any future multi-process startup.

title: fix(learning-loop): help/list runs are not verifiers; never store part of a secret (#5067)
body:
Fixes the in-PR items of #5067.

## Summary

The verified-outcome learning loop recorded **verified-success** for turns whose "test" only printed help or listed tests, and it could store part of a secret in task text or verifier evidence. This PR changes `plugins/ruflo-mods/hooks/loop/` (`verifier.ts`, `record.ts`, `taint.ts`, and a new `words.ts` shared bash word splitter) plus one guard in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/memory/verified-outcomes.ts`, and regenerates both `learning-loop.cjs` bundles, so the mod path and the classic-hooks path both get the fix.

**Before merge:** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/.claude/helpers/helpers.manifest.json` needs a re-sign for the new `learning-loop.cjs` bytes (`scripts/sign-helpers.mjs`, as #5037 did). I can't sign it as a contributor. The stable release workflow verifies the checked-in manifest before packing.

**CI state:** the red `guard`, `Test Suite (ubuntu-latest)` and `Test V3 Packages` jobs each fail only `helper-signing.test.ts` › *its hashes match the actual shipped helper files* (`learning-loop.cjs` integrity: new bytes vs the signed `33caa41c…`); Test V3 Packages is 1 failed / 12,647 passed. All three clear with the re-sign. `version-bump` is fixed in `c28a38691` (ruflo-mods **0.17.5**, CHANGELOG entry). Change the number if you slot it differently.

## Changes

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test --help`, `npm test -- --help`, `npx vitest --version`, `npx jest --listTests`, `pytest --collect-only`, `cargo test --no-run`, `go test -list .`, `npx vitest list`, `cargo nextest list` | passing **test** verifier, no taint | not a verifier, so the turn is not verified |
| `npx vitest run -t "prints --help text"`, `pytest -k 'help or --version'`, `npm test -- --reporter=list`, `pytest -v` | verifier | still a verifier (bash-accurate words; quotes group) |
| `npm run build # && npm test` | credited as **test**, but only the build runs | refused (a comment hides the rest) |
| `npm test -- --token=<github token>` | token kept as evidence and sent to SONA feedback, ledger and lessons | kind and outcome kept, evidence `[redacted]` |
| prompt with a key across the 300-char cut | `…xxx ghp_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNO` stored | `[redacted]` |
| prompt with a long JWT across the cut | partial JWT stored | `[redacted]`; any word the cut would split is dropped whole |
| 32M-character prompt | the whole prompt is normalised (~1.4 s with a full scan) | at most 64 KiB read (~6 ms) |
| `tsc -v`, `tsc --listFilesOnly`, `tsc -b --dry`, `eslint --env-info`, `make -n`, `go test -c`, `dotnet test -t`, `pytest --fixtures`, `npm test --if-present` | verifier | not a verifier (flags read for the program actually run, so `pytest -v` still verifies) |
| `npx tsc --ver\<newline>sion` | verifier (joined with a space) | not a verifier (bash joins with nothing) |
| key with a line separator or control character inside | stored (folding hid it from the screen) | `[redacted]` (screened as given too) |
| a task stored as `[redacted]` at ingest | trained SONA as `coder:redacted` | counted, never trained |
| `npx jest --pass"WithNoTests"` | no ADR-503 taint | `narrowed-verifier` taint (same shell words) |

## Tests

New cases in `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/mods/mods-learning-loop.test.ts`:
- no-run and list forms are refused, with a positive control of real runs whose arguments contain those words;
- evidence is redacted, including past the 80-character cut;
- an end-to-end mod run: an edit followed by `npm test --help`, `npx vitest list` or `npx jest --listTests` writes three records, none of them `verified-success`;
- task text with a split key, a long JWT, a far-away key, a word-boundary cut, and bounded reading of a huge prompt.

Local results, macOS, Node 22, mirroring `mod-guidance.yml` after a root `npm ci --ignore-scripts --legacy-peer-deps`:
- `node plugins/ruflo-mods/scripts/build-learning-loop-helper.mjs --check`: in sync.
- `tsc -p v3/@claude-flow/cli/tsconfig.mod-guidance.json`: passes.
- `bash plugins/ruflo-mods/scripts/smoke.sh`: 17 passed, 0 failed.
- `vitest run __tests__/mods/ --exclude '**/mods-cli-bin.test.ts'`: **668 tests passed** (658 on `main`). Six files fail to load **identically on unmodified `main`** in this local install, because `@claude-flow/cli-core/mcp-tools/types` is unbuilt (`commands`, `guidance-e2e`, `hardening`, `headless-worker-spawn`, `hive-mind-spawn-plugins`, `route`). CI should run them.
- Mutation check: each of the 12 guards was reverted on its own (per-program flags, program-aware `list`, `go test -c`, escaped-space comment, backslash-newline, raw evidence screen, raw task screen, key-header guard, SONA skip, `narrows()` words, word-boundary cut, prompt bound). Every revert fails at least one test. One of these tests found a real bug in the key-header guard, which is fixed here.
- Not run: `vitest.real-binary.config.ts` (needs a pinned Claude Code install).

Three Codex adversarial review rounds executed the cases above; the third was a fresh, unanchored review of the whole PR. Rounds 2 and 3 found the comment, quoted-subcommand, escape, per-runner, raw-screening and `[redacted]` gaps, all fixed here. Items that belong outside this PR are listed as follow-ups in #5067: verifying that a runner actually ran tests, screening at ingest and on file paths, head-matching false negatives already on `main`, differences between the mod and classic paths, and cleaning up existing records.

title: fix(memory): search and read-only list fallbacks never write the store (#5065)
body:
Part of #5065 (reported by @wrsmith108; thanks for the detailed trace matrix).

The sql.js fallbacks behind `memory_search` (`searchEntries`) and `memory_search_unified` (`listEntries`) wrote store files on every call. This PR makes them fail closed before any write.

**What changes**

| Write the report saw | Now |
|---|---|
| `memory.db.lock` created, written, unlinked (via `ensureSchemaColumns`) | A new `readOnlySchemaError()` reads `PRAGMA table_info` from the loaded image, with no lock. |
| Schema ALTER / backfill on older stores | Refused instead: `success: false` with an error saying the store is out of date and that any memory write (e.g. `ruflo memory store`) upgrades it. |
| `hnsw.index` created and written (`pwrite64`) | `searchEntries` only searches an HNSW index this process already opened (`existingOnly`), and otherwise uses the brute-force scan. |
| (not in the report) `rabitq.meta.json` written when a search builds the RaBitQ pre-filter | Built in memory only (`persistMeta: false`). |

`listEntries` gets an opt-in `readOnly` flag, which `memory_search_unified` passes. Its other callers (cleanup, export, the native mirror and the CLI) keep the migrating path. Their behaviour is unchanged.

**Behaviour change to note:** if the bridge is unavailable and the store predates the `status`/`provenance_type` columns, `memory_search` and `memory_search_unified` now return an error where they used to migrate silently. The first memory write migrates the store as before.

**Not covered here.** In the report, `ruvector.db` was modified under forcings B and C, where the AgentDB bridge is loaded. Nothing in the sql.js fallback opens that file. The fallback's last bridge call on this path, the brute-force cosine in `searchHNSWIndex`, is now skipped unless a local index is open. But I haven't traced whether the bridge's own initialisation in `getBridge()` writes `ruvector.db`, and that runs before any fallback. So this PR does not close #5065. A trace of one B cell on this branch would show what is left.

**Tests:** `__tests__/memory-search-fallback-readonly-5065.test.ts` hashes every file under the memory root before and after each call, and watches the directory with inotify. The watch catches a lock file that is created and deleted during the call.
- On `main`, all four main cases fail: the lock is seen every time, and the old-schema store is migrated.
- With the fix they pass.
- A fifth case covers the RaBitQ meta file and is skipped where `@ruvector/rabitq-wasm` cannot load. It is skipped in my local worktree, so CI is the first place it runs.

I also ran the 54 suites that touch the changed functions with and without the change, and got the same 19 failures both times. My checkout borrows symlinked `node_modules`, so those 19 are environment failures, and CI is the real check. Type-check is clean for the changed files.

title: fix(update): never load package files from the working directory (3.80.1)
body:
Security fix: the startup update checker could run code from the working directory.

`getInstalledVersion()` resolved `<pkg>/package.json` with `paths: [process.cwd()]` and loaded it with `require()`. A package's `exports` map can point `./package.json` at a `.js` file, so a `node_modules/@claude-flow/security` (or `embeddings`/`integration`/`testing`) committed to a cloned repository ran inside the CLI on the startup update check of nearly any command. Same class as ruvector GHSA-8pv4-hqq5-m2wv. Reproduced on published 3.80.0 with `npx ruflo@3.80.0 status`.

**Fix**
- Resolve from the CLI's own install only, and read the file with `JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))`, so nothing can be executed.
- `__tests__/update-checker-cwd-hijack.test.ts`: plants fake packages with an `exports` redirect in cwd; asserts nothing runs and the fake version is not reported. Fails before, passes after.
- `update-checker-opt-in-4755.test.ts`: its `createRequire` mock now also mocks the file read.
- Release 3.80.1: version fields bumped, helpers manifest re-signed (`verify-helpers`: ok).

**Validation**
- Release gate tests (cli gates + all update tests, codex, security, plugin-agent-federation, stage-internal-runtime-bundles): all pass.
- End to end with the built CLI: unfixed build writes the marker on `ruflo status`, fixed build does not.
- Swept `v3/@claude-flow/*/src` for other cwd-based or path-based dynamic loads: the rest resolve from the CLI's own install; codex `--config <path>` loads only a file the user names explicitly.

title: fix(policy): never leave an empty state.lock; say how to recover a stuck one
body:
## Problem
Every ruflo MCP tool call in Codex (`guidance_brain`, `memory_search`, …) failed with `Mcp error: -32603: … policy-state-lock-timeout`.

Root cause, observed on a real project: `.claude-flow/policy/state.lock` was a **0-byte file from Nov 17**, from a previous kernel boot. `acquireLock` created the lock with `O_EXCL` and wrote the owner record afterwards, so a process that died between the two steps (reboot, SIGKILL, OOM) left a lock that names no owner. The dead-owner reclaim deliberately refuses unidentifiable owners, so the project failed every call after a 5 s wait, with no hint about the cause, for five days.

## Fix
- **The lock is never visible without its owner.** The owner JSON is written to a private temp file and `link()` publishes it atomically. `link` returns EEXIST while the lock is held and never follows a symlink at the target. Windows and filesystems without hard links keep create-then-write, and that path now removes its own lock if the write fails.
- **A stuck lock explains itself.** A timeout against an owner that can never be identified (empty, unreadable, another host, an earlier boot, another PID namespace) now says which case it is, how old the lock is, and which path to remove. A live, identified owner keeps the bare `policy-state-lock-timeout`, which the console's `mcp-run` retries.
- Unchanged: unidentifiable owners are still never taken over automatically.

## Tests
`__tests__/policy-lock-dead-owner.test.ts` has 5 new tests. Against the old code, 3 of them fail, including a cross-process reader that **does observe an empty lock** during acquire/release. All of them pass with the fix. The lock, locked-json-store and ledger-durability suites pass: 75/75.

title: fix(hooks): keep Codex hook stdout valid JSON
body:
## Problem
In Codex: `Hook failed — hook returned invalid user prompt submit JSON output`.

Codex parses a hook's stdout as hook JSON when it starts with `{` or `[`. `hook-handler.cjs` reports in lines that start with `[`, such as `[INFO] Routing task …` (UserPromptSubmit), `[OK] Edit recorded` (PostToolUse) and `[OK] Task completed` (SubagentStop), so those hooks failed on every turn. #3163 fixed the same issue for auto-memory's Stop hook only.

## Fix
Under a Codex payload, detected by `turn_id` as in #3163, the handler collects everything it logs and writes it once at exit:
- for **UserPromptSubmit** and **SessionStart**, as `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName", "additionalContext"}}`, so the routing report still reaches the model;
- for every other event, on **stderr**, leaving stdout empty.

Claude Code payloads are unchanged, and `pre-bash` keeps its blocking protocol. The generated fallback (`generateHookHandler`) gets the same change. Both helper copies are byte-identical.

## Tests
`__tests__/hook-handler-codex-json-stdout.test.ts` runs the packaged helper, the dogfood copy and the generated fallback, under both a Codex and a Claude payload: 9 tests. The parity, #3163 and global-cli suites pass: 57/57.

title: doctor: Version Freshness compares against the frozen alpha dist-tag instead of latest
body:
`ruflo doctor` checks whether the CLI is current by asking npm for the `alpha` dist-tag, but releases now go to `latest` and `alpha` no longer moves (ADR-513, CLAUDE.md publishing section). Users who are behind the latest release are told they are up to date.

## Where

`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts`, `checkVersionFreshness()`:

```ts
// Query npm for latest version (using alpha tag since that's what we publish to)
const npmInfo = await runCommand('npm view @claude-flow/cli@alpha version', 5000);
```

The same check's fix advice installs `@claude-flow/cli@latest`, so it compares against one tag and recommends another.

## Registry today

`npm view @claude-flow/cli dist-tags`: `latest` is 3.80.1, `alpha` and `v3alpha` are 3.75.2.

## Effect

On any version from 3.75.2 to 3.80.0, `ruflo doctor` reports `Version Freshness: v3.7x.x (up to date)` and gives no update hint, although 3.80.1 is published.

## Expected

Compare against the `latest` dist-tag, the one the fix advice installs. The registry-failure warning, version parsing and fix strings can stay as they are (the branding of the fix strings is #1861).

title: fix(doctor): check version freshness against the latest dist-tag (#5079)
body:
This PR fixes [issue #5079](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/5079).

## Why

`ruflo doctor`'s Version Freshness check asks npm for the `alpha` dist-tag. Releases now go to `latest`, and `alpha` no longer moves (ADR-513), so the check compares against an old version. Today `latest` is 3.80.1 and `alpha` is 3.75.2: anyone on 3.75.2 to 3.80.0 is told they are up to date. The check's own fix advice already installs `@claude-flow/cli@latest`.

## What changed

- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts`: query `npm view @claude-flow/cli@latest version` instead of `@alpha`, fix the stale comment, and export `checkVersionFreshness` for the test. Version parsing, messages, fix strings, the 5 s timeout and the registry-failure warning are unchanged.
- `v3/@claude-flow/cli/__tests__/doctor-version-freshness-5079.test.ts`: puts a fake `npm` first on `PATH` that answers `999.0.0` for `@latest` and `0.0.1` for `@alpha`, and expects a warn with `latest: v999.0.0`. It goes through the real `runCommand` path. Skipped on Windows, like the other fake-PATH doctor tests.

## Tests

Local macOS arm64, Node 24.18.0, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the workspace build:

- New test: fails on main (`expected 'pass' to be 'warn'` once the function is exported; without the export it is not callable), passes with the fix.
- With the neighbouring `doctor-memory-version-3392` and `doctor-agent-browser-3166` tests: 15 passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli`: no errors.

## Not verified

The full suite, hosted CI, Node 20/22 and Windows were not run. No live registry call is made by the test.

Fixes #5079

title: fix(cli): let a subcommand's own --format choices shadow the global ones
body:
`validateFlags` (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/parser.ts`) checked a subcommand's `--format` against its own choices *and* the global ones (`text, json, table`), so subcommand-specific values always failed:

```
$ ruflo process monitor                 # own default is `dashboard`
[ERROR] Invalid value for --format: dashboard. Must be one of: text, json, table   (exit 1)
$ ruflo session export --format yaml    # also analyze dependencies --format dot, performance metrics --format prometheus
[ERROR] Invalid value for --format: yaml. Must be one of: text, json, table
```

Parsing and defaults already let the command's own option win; validation now does the same (a command option shadows the global option of the same name). Commands without their own `--format` still get the global choices (`status --format xml` is still rejected), and values outside a subcommand's own choices are still rejected.

Test: `__tests__/parser-subcommand-format-choices.test.ts` runs the real parser on `processCommand`/`sessionCommand`; 3 of its 5 cases fail on `main`, all pass with the fix. title: fix(embeddings): score the newest rows in `embeddings search`
body:
`embeddings search` (`v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/embeddings.ts`) reads `memory.db` directly with sql.js and loads candidate vectors with `LIMIT 1000` and no `ORDER BY`, so SQLite returns the oldest-inserted 1000 rows and anything newer is never scored, on every platform. This is #2982's root cause, already fixed in the memory bridge but not in this command. With 1100 embedded rows plus a newest "kubernetes ingress tls certificate rotation runbook" entry, `embeddings search -q "rotate TLS certs for k8s ingress" -t 0.3` printed `Found 0 matches`, while `memory search` found it at 0.87. With 900 rows it was found.

Fix: `ORDER BY updated_at DESC` and the bridge's own window (`resolveBridgeSearchWindow()`, 10000 by default, `CLAUDE_FLOW_SEARCH_WINDOW`), for both the namespace and `all` queries.

Test: `__tests__/embeddings-search-newest-rows.test.ts` seeds a real sql.js store and runs the real `search` action with a mocked embedder. The 1100-row cases fail on `main` and pass with the fix, and the 900-row case passes on both. Node 22: `pnpm typecheck` and CLI `tsc` are clean. The full v3 `vitest run` gave 12813 passed. Its failures are the same files that fail on `main` (ruvllm/agent WASM suites, flaky macOS memory-lock tests).

title: fix(system): report persisted swarm state in system_health
body:
This PR fixes [issue #2967](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/2967).

It covers bug 2, the swarm check (bug 1 was already fixed on main).

## Why

`system_health` always pushed a fixed swarm check, `unknown` / "Swarm connectivity not monitored", even right after `swarm_init` had persisted a running swarm that `swarm_health` reports as active.

## What changed

- The swarm check in `mcp-tools/system-tools.ts` now reads the persisted state through the existing `loadSwarmStore()` (the same reader `swarm_health` and `swarm_status` use).
- One or more running swarms: `healthy`, with the count and the most recently updated swarm id.
- No running swarm: still `unknown`, so it stays advisory and out of the score as before, with the message "No active swarm — run swarm_init".
- A corrupt swarm store (`loadSwarmStore()` throws): `warning` with the error message.
- The check now has a `latency` field like its neighbours.

Unchanged: the `database` check, which already probes a real file (the coordination store written by the `coordination_*` tools, not by `swarm_init`), the neural check, every other check and the score formula. The score itself can now change, because a running swarm counts as `healthy` and a corrupt swarm store as `warning`; with no swarm the check stays `unknown` and is excluded as before.

## Tests

- New `__tests__/system-health-swarm-2967.test.ts` runs the real `swarm_init` and `system_health` handlers in a temp project (`CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD`, same pattern as `mcp-untested-tools-4767.test.ts`). On base both cases fail (the check is always the fixed `unknown` message); with the fix 2/2 pass.
- `mcp-untested-tools-4767.test.ts` 19/19, `mcp-tools-deep.test.ts` 108/108, `task-summary-cancelled.test.ts` 1/1.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in `v3/@claude-flow/cli`: exit 0.

title: docs(readme): tag each ruPro link with its own campaign
body:
Implements the Ruflo side of cognitum-one/website#1536.

The two hero images, **Explore ruPro** and **Try the interactive demo** all pointed at untagged cognitum.one URLs, so a ruPro waitlist lead couldn't be traced to the link that brought it in. Each link now carries `utm_source=github`, `utm_medium=readme` and its own campaign:

| Link | `utm_campaign` |
|---|---|
| Neon sign | `ruflo-readme-rupro-neon` |
| Workspace tour | `ruflo-readme-rupro-workspace` |
| Explore ruPro | `ruflo-readme-rupro-explore` |
| Try the interactive demo | `ruflo-readme-rupro-demo` (tags placed before `#demo=welcome`) |

The neon link also moves from `/ruPro` to `/rupro`; the site's router is case-insensitive, so it lands on the same page.

Checked with `node scripts/readme-attribution.mjs --file README.md` from cognitum-one/website (all four ok), and each URL returns HTTP 200. Markdown only.
